text:
Lily and Sam went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look at the sea. The sea was big and blue and made a loud sound.

"Can we go in the water, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Not now, Lily. The sea is too cold and too rough today. Maybe later, when it is calm and warm," Mom said.

Lily and Sam felt sad. They wanted to swim and splash in the sea. They saw some other kids with buckets and shovels. They asked Mom and Dad if they could have some too.

"Sure, you can have some buckets and shovels. Let's go to the shop and see what they have," Dad said.

They walked to the shop near the beach. It had many things for the beach, like hats, sunglasses, towels, and toys. Lily and Sam looked at the buckets and shovels. They saw different colors and shapes. They wanted to order the ones they liked.

"I want the red bucket and the yellow shovel, please," Lily said.

"I want the blue bucket and the green shovel, please," Sam said.

The shopkeeper smiled and gave them the buckets and shovels they ordered. He said they were available and not too expensive.

"Thank you, shopkeeper," Lily and Sam said.

"You're welcome, kids. Have fun at the beach," the shopkeeper said.

Lily and Sam ran back to the sand with their buckets and shovels. They started to make castles and holes and bridges. They had fun at the beach, even if they could not go in the sea. They hoped the sea would be calm and warm tomorrow.

One day, Jane was walking through the woods searching for a place to take a nap. She had been walking for hours and was feeling very tired. All of a sudden, she spotted a tunnel. She thought it was the perfect place to take a nap and cautiously stepped inside. As soon as she sat down she felt a sense of calm and closed her eyes. Everything was peaceful until she heard a loud voice. 

"You can't take a nap here!", yelled a voice.

Jane opened her eyes and saw a squirrel standing in front of her. He continued speaking, "This tunnel is my home. You have to leave or else you will be stuck here forever." Jane was feeling frustrated but knew that the squirrel was right. She slowly began to stand up and as she stepped out of the tunnel, she thanked him for reminding her that she needed to find a better place to take her nap. 

The next day, Jane returned to the woods feeling determined to find the perfect place to take a nap. After a while, she noticed a small clearing in a nearby park. She happily ran over to the clearing and laid down in the soft grass. She quickly drifted off to sleep and felt content to have finally taken her nap in a nice and safe place.

Once upon a time there was a youth who loved to eat. Every day he would find something delicious to enjoy. One day he found a useful snack - it was a treat that was extra special. It tasted so good that the youth couldn't help but eat it all up.

The youth felt so full that he wondered if he could use the snack for something else. So he decided to save it for later. He put the snack in a special place where he could easily find it.

After a few days, the youth remembered it was there. He opened the box and it was still as fresh as the day he put it there. The youth then ate the snack and found it even more delicious than before! It had been a very useful snack indeed.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play and sing. One day, they find a big box in the garage. They open the box and see many funny clothes and hats. They want to try them on.

"Look, Ben, I am a princess!" Lily says. She puts on a long dress and a shiny crown. She twirls around and smiles.

"And I am a pirate!" Ben says. He puts on a striped shirt and a black hat. He holds a wooden sword and makes a scary face.

They laugh and clap. They pretend to be in a story. They sing loud and high. They think they are in an opera.

But they do not know that Mom and Dad are watching them. Mom and Dad are opera singers. They are proud of their twins. They think they are very cute and talented.

"Wow, they are amazing!" Mom says. She hugs Dad.

"Maybe they will be opera singers too!" Dad says. He kisses Mom.

They go to the garage and join the twins. They put on furry coats and masks. They pretend to be animals. They sing and dance with Lily and Ben. They have a lot of fun. They are a happy family.

Mommy was busy making dinner. She needed to mix some special ingredients together. She put them in a bowl. Then she stirred and stirred until everything was mixed up really well. 

When she was done, the bowl had a funny smell. Mommy tasted it and said "Mmm! Now that's a good mix!â€

But soon, Mommy felt a little bit of pain in her tummy. She forgot to add an important ingredient to her mix! She quickly got an apple and added it to the bowl. Now the smell was perfect! 

Mommy was happy with the mix, but she learned an important lesson: don't forget to add any ingredients when you mix!

Once upon a time, there was a battery who wanted to have fun. So he went outside and decided to spray water everywhere. He sprayed and sprayed, until his mom saw and got mad.

The mom said, "No! You must not spray like that!" Then, the battery felt ashamed.

So the battery stopped spraying and said he was sorry. His mom said, "It's okay. From now on, only spray when I say it is okay."

The battery was happy to hear that and was glad that he was forgiven. So he ran and played happily, and never sprayed without asking his mom first. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bear. The bear was walking through the woods when he heard a loud snap. He looked around and saw a curtain hanging down from a branch. He was curious, so he went to see what had made the noise. There, he found a little mouse. The poor mouse had gotten its tail caught on a twig and had snapped it off. The bear was very sad, he could tell the mouse was hurt. 

He looked around and found a soft leaf to wrap up the mouse's tail. He kept it safe until the mouse felt better. Then, he hung the curtain over a branch to make a cozy home for the mouse. The mouse thanked the bear and said goodbye as he scampered off into the woods. The bear was glad he was able to help the little mouse and make sure it didn't get hurt anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful queen who loved to be creative. She was kind and gentle, and she always wanted to make everyone happy. 
One day, the queen decided to unlock a secret box kept in her palace. She turned the key with a smile on her face and carefully opened the box. Inside, the queen uncovered a sparkly crown! She was so amazed and excited, she decided to show it to her kingdom. 

The queen put on the crown and set off on a parade around her kingdom. Everywhere she went, people cheered and clapped their hands. Everyone was so happy to see their queen looking so beautiful. She made them all smile. 

At the end of the parade, the queen declared that she was now the most creative and wonderful queen in the whole world. Everyone smiled and cheered even louder as she promised that she would use her creativity to make the kingdom a better place. 

The queen waved good-bye to her citizens, and thanked them for believing in her. With the secret box still in hand, she headed off to start making her kingdom even more wonderful. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little child named Timmy. Timmy was playing in his backyard when he saw a big truck. The truck was there to load some boxes. Timmy was curious about the boxes and went closer to see what was inside.

Suddenly, a loud noise scared Timmy. He looked up and saw a big forklift. The forklift was moving the boxes into the truck. Timmy was frightened and ran back to his house.

From his window, Timmy watched the truck drive away. He felt happy that he wasn't near the big forklift anymore. Timmy learned that it's important to be careful around big machines.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little boy named Tim. Tim loved trains and would watch them go by his house every day. One day, Tim saw a train that looked different from the others. It was a bright red train with a big smiley face on the front. Tim was very excited and jumped up and down with joy.

Suddenly, Timâ€™s mom called him for dinner. Tim was so excited about the train that he forgot to be alert and tripped on a toy. He fell down and started to frown. His mom quickly came over to help him up and asked him what was wrong. Tim told her about the red train with the smiley face and how he had tripped because he was so excited. His mom smiled and said, â€œDonâ€™t worry, Tim. We can go see the train together tomorrow.â€ Timâ€™s frown turned into a big smile and he was happy again.

Once upon a time, there lived an archer. He had a big bow and many arrows. He practiced shooting his arrows every day.

One day, he found a big tree that he wanted to practice shooting at. He set up his bow, aimed and let the arrow strike the tree. He smiled when the arrow reached the tree.

He pulled out another arrow and shot it too. But this time it flew and landed in a yummy looking pie on a window sill. He ran to the window to get the arrow. The pie smelled so yummy! He picked up the arrow and quickly ate the yummy pie. Yum! 

The archer had a really yummy snack and now he was ready to practice his archery again. He took out another arrow and tried to hit the tree again. He was confident that he could do it. 

He aimed, then shot and the arrow struck the tree! He was so proud of himself. He put away the arrow and the bow and went back home. He was happy he managed to hit the tree with the arrow.

Once upon a time, there was a big store. In the store, there was a pretty velvet dress. It was very expensive. A little girl named Anna saw the dress and wanted to have it.

Anna asked her mom, "Mom, can I have this pretty velvet dress?" Her mom looked at the price and said, "Sorry, Anna. It is too expensive. We cannot spend that much money on a dress."

Anna was sad, but she understood. She and her mom went home. The next day, Anna's mom had a surprise for her. She made a dress that looked just like the expensive velvet dress. Anna was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mom! I love you!"

Once upon a time there was a crab. The crab wanted to have a clean house. It would do many things to make it clean. The crab found some water and got its shell wet. Then it scrubbed and scrubbed until it sparkled. It also found some sand and dusted the floor of its house. Lastly, it found some leaves and put them on the floor.

The crab looked around and saw how clean its house had become. It smiled happily and said to itself, "My house is so clean!" Then it snuggled into a corner and went to sleep.

The end.

Once upon a time there was an ancient spot in the forest. A little girl named Molly took a trip to the spot to see what it was like. As she looked around, she saw that it was very old and seemed to be magical.

"What is this place?" said Molly to a nearby bird.

The bird chirped and then said, "This is an ancient spot. It has been here for many, many years."

Molly was interested in the spot so she decided to stand right in the center of it. Suddenly, she felt a tingle pass through her body.

"What was that?" said Molly, feeling a bit scared.

The bird said, "That was the magic of this spot. It will give you strength."

Molly was surprised, but also excited. She thanked the bird and then stood in the spot for a few moments more, feeling the strength it gave her. Then she waved goodbye and left the ancient spot.

Once upon a time, there was a toy. It was a perfect brick. Although it was small and plain, it was very special. Suddenly, a magical bird arrived in front of the brick. It waved its wings, and the brick began to move! It started to fly around the room.

When the tiny brick flew outside, it was amazed by the new world. Everything seemed so big and wonderful. The little brick wanted to explore a bit more and flew around the garden. Suddenly, the perfect little brick found a big red wall. And so it landed on it and stayed there.

The brick was so happy with its discovery that it decided to stay there forever. Its new home was the most perfect place in the world. From then on, the little brick was always happy whenever it arrived home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Penny who liked to explore the world.

One day, Penny was walking in the park when she saw something shiny. She leaned over and picked it up - it was a penny!

Penny smiled happily and put the penny in her pocket. She decided to taste it. It was metal and cold, but kind of sweet too.

Suddenly, Penny heard a voice. It was a little boy who came up to her and said, "Why are you tasting that penny?"

Penny was confused and didn't know what to say. After a moment, she simply replied, "I wanted to see what it tasted like!" 

The little boy smiled and said, "That sounds interesting. I think I'll try it too!"

They both tasted the penny. It was cold and sweet, but also a little bit sour. They smiled and laughed and decided to share the penny they had found.

Penny and the little boy shared the penny between them and enjoyed the taste. They were very happy with their discovery, and went off exploring the park together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary. She was three years old, and she wanted to find something special. So she went out on an adventure.

Mary looked under rocks and behind trees, but she couldnâ€™t find anything. Then, she heard a sound in the distance.

She ran to see what it was and saw a tall, clear post. She was happy and jumped up and down.

She ran around the post, eager to find out what was at the top. Sure enough, there was something special waiting for her. She found a big, red balloon tied to the post.

With a big smile, the little girl released the balloon into the air. She watched it soar away until it become a tiny speck in the sky. And so Mary's adventure was over. She went home with a smile and a special memory.

The little girl was walking in the woods. She was very alert, taking in all the sights and sounds. Suddenly, she heard a noise in the trees ahead of her. She stopped and questioned what it was.

The noise was coming from a small bird, its feathers sparkling in the sunlight. For a moment, the girl just stared in wonder. Then, she started to look around for its home.

Suddenly, she saw it! In the tree was a small hanger with two baby birds inside. They were cheeping and hungry for food. The girl quickly got her bag of birdseed and put some inside.

The babies ate hungrily and the girl was very happy. She stayed there until she was sure that the babies were safe and then she continued on her way. She felt very alert and happy that she had been able to help the babies.

True was a cheerful little girl and she loved to swim. She went to the beach all the time and enjoyed splashing in the waves. One day, True spotted a dolphin swimming close to shore. She was so excited she shouted to it, "Come and play with me!"

The dolphin nodded and smiled and was very friendly. They swam and raced around in the warm water. True was so happy that she laughed with joy and the dolphin joined in too.

When they were done, True waved goodbye and thanked the dolphin. Then she went back to shore, feeling cheerful and content. She would never forget the day she swam with the dolphin.

Once upon a time, there was a quiet baby bear. He had a very small mustache that he was very proud of. One day, the baby bear went for a walk in the forest. He was walking in the sunshine when he suddenly felt really thirsty.

He looked around and saw a river. The river was bubbling and glittering in the sunshine. The baby bear waded into the river and drank some of the fresh water. Then he sat on the banks and began to dry off in the warm sunshine.

He lay quietly in the sunshine, drying off, until he felt dry and comfortable. His little mustache was sparkling in the sunlight and he was so proud of it. He smiled and went on his way through the forest, feeling happy and content.

Once upon a time there was a small, special bird called a laser. He lived all alone in the blue sky and wanted to have a friend to share it all with.

One day he saw a small, colourful bird flying past and shouted, "Hello! Can we be friends?" The bird said, "Yes! Let's be friends!"

They flew high up into the sky and played together. They had so much fun and even made a game to see who could zoom the fastest around the clouds. Laser won every time.

After they had been flying together, they flew back down and Laser thanked the colourful little friend. "I had such a great time!" he said.

The colourful little bird said, "Me, too! I am so happy we are friends. I will come back to see you again soon."

And so they said goodbye, and the laser flew happily off into the blue sky with a big, happy smile on his face.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big kite in the sky. It is red and yellow and has a long tail.

"Wow, look at the kite!" Tom says. "It is so high and fast. I want to fly a kite too."

"Me too," Lily says. "Let's go and find one."

They run to the shed. They see a small kite. It is blue and green and has a star on it. They take the kite and a string. They go to the field.

They try to fly the kite. They run and run. But the kite does not go up. It falls to the ground.

"Why does it not fly?" Tom asks. "The wind is strong. It should fly."

"Maybe the string is too short," Lily says. "Or maybe the kite is too heavy."

They look at the kite. They see a problem. The kite has a hole in it. The wind goes through the hole. The kite does not hang in the air.

"Oh no, the kite is broken," Tom says. "How can we fix it?"

"Maybe we can use a patch," Lily says. "Or some tape. Or some glue."

They look for something to fix the kite. They see a big leaf. It is brown and dry. They think it can cover the hole.

They take the leaf. They put it on the hole. They use some grass to tie it. They hope it will work.

They try to fly the kite again. They run and run. The kite goes up. It hangs in the air. It moves with the wind. It looks like a bird.

"Yay, we did it!" Tom says. "The kite is flying. It is so pretty."

"Yay, we are so smart!" Lily says. "The leaf is a good patch. It is like a wing."

They laugh and clap. They watch the kite. They are happy.

But then, something bad happens. The wind gets stronger. It blows harder. It pulls the kite. The string breaks. The kite flies away.

"Uh oh, the kite is gone," Tom says. "The wind took it. We can't get it back."

"Uh oh, that is sad," Lily says. "The kite was ours. We liked it."

They are scared. They cry. They hug each other.

They see a man. He is walking in the field. He has a hat and a coat. He sees the kite. He catches it. He brings it to them.

"Hello, kids," he says. "Is this your kite? I saw it flying in the sky. It is a nice kite. But it has a hole in it. And a leaf on it. Did you do that?"

"Yes, sir," Tom says. "The kite was broken. We tried to fix it. But the wind was too strong. It broke the string. It flew away."

"Yes, sir," Lily says. "We were scared. We thought we lost it. We were sad. Thank you for finding it."

"You're welcome, kids," he says. "You are very clever. You used a leaf to patch the hole. That is a good idea. But you need a stronger string. And a smaller hole. Do you want me to help you?"

"Yes, please," Tom and Lily say. "We want to fly the kite again. We want to have fun."

"Okay, then," he says. "Let's go to my house. I have some tools and materials. We can fix the kite together. And then we can fly it again. How does that sound?"

"Good, good," Tom and Lily say. "Thank you, thank you."

They go with the man. They fix the kite. They fly it again. They are happy. The end.

Billy had a question for his aunt. She looked very worried and he wondered why. He decided to ask her to help him understand. 

â€œAunt, why do you look so worried?â€ he asked her. 

She carefully answered, â€œWhen we worry, it means we are concerned about something. Something might be wrong or might happen.â€ 

Billy thought about it for a moment and then asked, â€œCan I help make it better?â€

Aunt smiled and said, â€œYes, sweetheart, you can help by being supportive and understanding.â€ 

Billy hugged his aunt and said, â€œI will do my best to help.â€ She smiled and hugged him back. 

Billy was so glad he asked his aunt. He was relieved to know he could help make things better.

Lily was very happy. Today was her birthday. She had a big cake with candles and a lovely dress with flowers. She wanted to share her cake with her friends. She asked her mom if she could invite them to her house.

Mom said yes, but she had a surprise for Lily. She said Lily would meet someone new and get a special present. Lily was curious. Who could it be? What could it be? She hoped it was something fun and nice.

Mom took Lily to the car and drove to a big place with many animals. Lily loved animals. She saw dogs, cats, birds, rabbits, and more. She wanted to pet them all. Mom said they were here to adopt one of them. Lily was very excited. She could have a new friend!

Mom took Lily to a room where a lady was waiting. The lady smiled and said hello. She had a box in her hands. She said it was for Lily. She opened the box and Lily saw a small, fluffy, white kitten. The kitten looked at Lily with big, blue eyes and meowed softly. Lily gasped. She loved the kitten. She reached out and touched its fur. It was soft and warm. The kitten licked her hand and purred.

Lily hugged the kitten and thanked the lady. She thanked her mom too. She said it was the best present ever. She named the kitten Snowy. She said Snowy was her new best friend. She was very happy. She couldn't wait to show Snowy to her other friends and share her cake with them. She knew they would love Snowy too. It was a lovely birthday.

Once upon a time, there was a dragon who was very shy. He lived in a deep dark cave, far away from the rest of the world. He did not like it when people came too close, so he hid away in his cave. 

One day, the dragon heard something from outside. It was the sound of counting. He poked his head out of the cave to see what was happening. There was a little girl counting numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 and so on! 

The dragon liked the sound of the numbers, so he grew a bit braver and slowly crept out of his cave, step by step. He saw the girl and went closer. The little girl was so happy to meet the dragon, but he was still very shy. 

But the dragon eventually got used to the little girl, and they became friends. Every day, the little girl would come to the cave and they would play counting numbers together. The dragon was no longer shy, and they were happy friends. 

The End

Once upon a time, two friends wanted to unite. One day, they decided to play hockey. They never played before, so everything was unknown. They tried their very best and laughed together.

By the end of the day, they were very good at hockey! They could even practice together. The friends were so happy they united by playing hockey, and they decided to play every day. Every day, they discovered something new and had a wonderfully fun time.

The friends could always rely on hockey to unite them and make them happy. Whenever they felt sad, they knew they just had to pull out their hockey sticks and have a game to make everything better. The friends had fun and were united by hockey.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books with her mommy. One day, she was playing outside and fell down and hurt her leg. She cried and her mommy came to help her. "What happened, sweetie?" her mommy asked. "I fell and hurt my leg," Lily said. "Let's go inside and read a book to make you feel better," her mommy said. They went inside and read a little book about a happy puppy. Lily felt much better and her leg didn't hurt anymore.

Once upon a time there was a small bunny. He loved sweets, but his mom told him not to eat too many. One day, the bunny snuck out of the house and hopped over to the temple. It was a very special temple and the bunny was curious about what he might find.

When he arrived, he saw a delicate, white flower. He wanted to taste it, so he reached out and plucked the petals from the stem. To his surprise, it tasted like the sweetest honey he had ever tried!

The bunny should have listened to his mom, as it was not a good idea to take the flower. Suddenly, the bunny felt a strange feeling in his stomach and he ran all the way home.

He learned an important lesson that day; it is never a good idea to take something that does not belong to you. He happily listened to his momâ€™s advice and ate the sweets that she gave him. He was careful not to taste anything he wasn't supposed to!

Lily and Ben were bored. They wanted to play outside, but it was raining. They looked around the house for something fun to do. They saw a big box in the corner. It had a picture of a castle on it.

"Let's build the castle!" Lily said.

"OK!" Ben said.

They opened the box and took out the pieces. They were very cheap. They broke easily and did not fit well. Lily and Ben tried to make the castle, but it kept falling apart.

"This is no fun!" Lily said.

"Let's pretend we are in the castle!" Ben said.

They crawled inside the box and closed the flaps. They imagined they were a king and a queen. They had a crown and a dress and a sword. They had a lot of fun.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was their dog, Rex. He smelled them in the box. He wanted to play with them. He ran to the box and jumped on it. He ripped the flaps and bit the pieces. He barked and wagged his tail.

"Rex, no!" Lily and Ben shouted.

They tried to escape, but it was too late. Rex had made a big mess. He had torn the box and the pieces. He had scratched Lily and Ben. They had cuts and bruises. They cried and ran to their mom.

Mom was very angry. She saw the mess and the blood. She scolded Lily and Ben and Rex. She threw away the box and the pieces. She cleaned their wounds and gave them a hug.

She said, "You should not play with cheap toys. They are not safe. And you should not hide in a box. Rex did not know you were there. He thought it was a game. You are lucky he did not hurt you more. Next time, be more careful."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were bored. We wanted to have fun."

Mom said, "I know, but you have to be smart. You have other toys to play with. And you can read a book or draw a picture or sing a song. There are many ways to have fun inside. And when it stops raining, you can play outside. But no more cheap castles, OK?"

Lily and Ben said, "OK, Mom. We love you."

They hugged Mom and Rex. They learned their lesson. They never played with cheap castles again.

One day, Mommy put on her wide cloth and took Timmy to the park. He was so excited! When they got there, Timmy saw lots of kids playing. He ran over to a group of kids playing tag. He laughed and ran with them. 

Timmy also saw some big trees. He wanted to climb one and Mommy said it was ok. Timmy scrambled up the tree. He could see so far from up there. He could see all of the park. 

He stayed in the tree for awhile, but then it got dark. Mommy said it was time to go home. Timmy said goodbye to his friends and they waved. Then, he hopped down from the tree and ran over to Mommy. They held hands and walked home.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big bird in the sky. It was black and white and had a long neck. It was a swan.

"Look, Lily, a swan!" Tom said. "It can soar high and low. It has power in its wings."

"I want to soar like a swan," Lily said. "Can we do that, Tom?"

Tom thought for a moment. He had an idea. He took Lily's hand and ran to the swings. He helped her sit on one and pushed her gently. Lily felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She smiled and laughed.

"Tom, I'm soaring!" Lily said. "I feel like a swan!"

Tom smiled and joined her on the other swing. They swung higher and higher, back and forth. They felt free and happy.

They saw the swan fly over them. It honked softly and waved its wing. Tom and Lily waved back. They felt like they were friends with the swan.

They swung until they were tired. Then they slowed down and stopped. They got off the swings and hugged each other.

"That was fun, Tom," Lily said. "Thank you for helping me soar."

"You're welcome, Lily," Tom said. "You have power in your heart. You can soar anytime you want."

They held hands and walked back to their mom. She was sitting on a bench and reading a book. She looked up and smiled.

"Did you have fun, kids?" she asked.

"Yes, mom, we did," Tom and Lily said. "We soared like a swan."

Mummy was anxious. She couldn't find her special dress. She looked in her wardrobe, but it wasn't there.

"Please help, Daddy," she said.

Daddy smiled and reached into the wardrobe. He pulled out a toolbox and a brush.

Mummy's eyes lit up. "You can restore it?" she asked.

Daddy nodded. He worked carefully and when he was finished, the dress was shiny and beautiful.

Mummy smiled. She hugged Daddy and said, "Thank you, Daddy. You always make things better."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was eating her breakfast when she accidentally dropped her spoon on the floor. The spoon was delicate and broke into many pieces.

Lily's mom came to see what happened and asked, "What happened, Lily?"

Lily replied, "I dropped my spoon and it broke. I didn't understand why it was so delicate."

Mom said, "It's okay, Lily. We can get you a new spoon. Just be more careful next time."

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was playing in her backyard. She saw a bird flying in the sky and said, "Look, Mommy! A bird!" 

Her mommy replied, "Yes, Lily. Birds are good animals. They can fly high in the sky and sing beautiful songs." 

Lily asked, "Can we watch the bird together?" 

Mommy said, "Of course, we can watch the bird together. But did you know that there are many more things to watch in the universe? The universe is very big and has many stars and planets." 

Lily looked up at the sky and said, "Wow! The universe is so pretty. I want to watch it every day with you, Mommy." 

Mommy smiled and said, "I would love that, Lily. Watching the universe with you is one of my favorite things to do."

Jen and Tom were playing with their dolls in the living room. They liked to make up stories and act them out. Jen had a big doll with long hair and a pink dress. Tom had a small doll with a hat and a blue shirt.

"Let's go upstairs and set up a tea party for our dolls," Jen said. "We can use Mommy's cups and plates."

"Okay," Tom said. "But we have to be quiet. Mommy is napping upstairs. She is not feeling well. She is pale and has a sore throat."

They tiptoed upstairs with their dolls and went to Mommy's room. They saw Mommy sleeping on the bed. She looked pale and tired. They did not want to wake her up.

They went to the closet and found some cups and plates. They set them up on a small table in the corner. They pretended to pour tea and serve cookies to their dolls. They whispered and giggled.

"Would you like some more tea, Miss Doll?" Jen asked.

"Yes, please, Mr. Doll," Tom answered.

They had fun playing with their dolls. They did not notice that Mommy had opened her eyes and was watching them. She smiled and felt happy. She was glad that Jen and Tom were such good children. She loved them very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the land near his house. He would run around and laugh with his friends. 

One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help decorate the house for a party. Timmy was excited to help and started putting up balloons and streamers. However, his older sister was being very bossy and telling him what to do. Timmy didn't like it, but he didn't want to make her mad, so he did what she said. 

After they finished decorating, they went outside to play again. But while they were playing, they heard a loud crash. They turned around and saw that the decorations they had put up had fallen down and made a big mess. Timmy's mom was very upset and she scolded them for not doing a good job. 

Timmy felt very sad because he had tried his best, but his sister had been too bossy. He wished he had stood up for himself and done things his own way. From that day on, Timmy learned to be more confident and not let others be bossy to him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the hot sun. One day, her mommy told her that a big hurricane was coming soon.

Lily was scared and asked her mommy, "What is a hurricane?"

Her mommy explained, "A hurricane is a big storm with lots of wind and rain. We need to stay inside and be safe."

Lily was sad that she couldn't play outside anymore. But she knew it was important to be safe. When the hurricane came, she watched from the window as the wind and rain got stronger and stronger. Finally, the storm passed and the sun came out again. Lily was happy to be able to go outside again and release her energy by running and playing.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the rain and he loved to watch things grow. One day, Timmy's mommy took him to the museum. They saw lots of things like big bones and colorful paintings. Timmy liked the museum but he wanted to go outside and play. When they left the museum, it was very wet outside because it had rained. Timmy saw a flower growing in a puddle and he smiled. He loved to see things grow, even in the rain!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was holding her calendar and she accidentally dropped it on the floor. Her mommy heard the sound and asked, "What happened, Lily?" 

"I dropped my calendar," Lily said. 

Her mommy picked up the calendar and saw that it was cold outside. "It's a cold day today, Lily. We should wear our warm coats when we go outside," her mommy said. 

Lily nodded and put on her coat. They went outside and had a fun day playing in the snow. When they came back inside, they had some hot cocoa to warm up. Lily looked at her calendar and smiled. It was a great day! The end.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They saw a man with a big camera. He was taking pictures of the flowers and the birds.

"Mom, what is he doing?" Sara asked.

"He is taking pictures with his camera. A camera is a thing that can make a copy of what you see. Then you can look at the pictures later or show them to other people," mom explained.

"Can I try?" Ben said. He ran to the man and asked him if he could use his camera.

The man was very nice and said yes. He showed Ben how to hold the camera and press the button. Ben looked through the camera and saw a red balloon in the sky. He pressed the button and heard a click.

"Wow, I took a picture of the balloon!" Ben said.

"Good job, Ben. Can I see?" Sara said. She came closer to the camera and tried to grab it.

"No, it's mine!" Ben said. He pulled the camera away from Sara and made her fall.

"Ben, that's not nice. You have to share with your sister. And you have to say sorry to her," mom said.

"But I want the camera. It's fun," Ben said.

"It's not your camera, Ben. It belongs to the man. He was kind enough to let you use it for a moment, but you have to give it back. And you have to be kind to your sister too. She wanted to try the camera as well. How would you feel if she did that to you?" mom said.

Ben thought for a while. He felt bad for making Sara cry and for being rude to the man. He realized he was wrong.

"I'm sorry, Sara. I'm sorry, man. Here is your camera. Thank you for letting me use it," Ben said.

He gave the camera back to the man and hugged Sara. The man smiled and said it was okay. He gave Ben and Sara each a sticker of a red balloon.

"Thank you, man. You are very nice," Ben and Sara said.

They went back to their mom and showed her their stickers. Mom was proud of them for saying sorry and being kind.

The moral of the story is: you should share with others and be polite. You should also appreciate what others do for you and say thank you.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She had a smart cat named Whiskers who was very good at solving puzzles. One day, Lily found a square puzzle and asked Whiskers to help her solve it. 

Whiskers was an intelligent cat and he quickly figured out how to put the puzzle pieces together. Lily was very happy and said, "Thank you, Whiskers! You are so smart!" 

Whiskers purred and said, "Please don't mention it, Lily. I'm always happy to help you." From that day on, Lily and Whiskers solved many puzzles together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very curious and loved to explore.

One day, her mum decided to take her to the city to discover something new. They jumped on the subway and soon they were at their destination.

When they stopped, Lucy and her mum stepped out of the subway station, and in front of them was something amazing. It was a big sweet shop!

Lucy was so excited and ran inside. She looked around and discovered so many different kinds of treats. There were big lollipops, sweet candy apples and lots more.

â€œOh wow!â€ said Lucy, â€œThis is amazing!â€

Her mum smiled at her and said, â€œSee, I told you we'd discover something special.â€

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe. Joe wanted to buy a new toy, but he didn't have enough money. Joe asked his mom what to do.

His mom said, â€œJoe, if you want to buy a toy, you need to save your money.â€ So Joe started saving his money.

Each week, Joe put some pennies in a jar. After a few weeks, Joe had enough money to buy the toy. He was so happy!

He went to the store with his mom and saw the toy. The price was on a sign. It was very big and Joe was scared. His mom asked, â€œDo you think it's worth it?â€

Joe thought about it, and noticed that the toy looked a bit boring. But, he knew it would include lots of fun, so he decided it was worth it. He paid the price and left the store with his new toy.

From then on, Joe always tried to save his money for fun stuff. Nothing was too expensive and boring for Joe, because he knew his money could buy lots of fun!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Amy. She liked to explore the world around her.

One day, Amy was walking through a forest. Suddenly, she heard a loud ringing sound! She followed the sound and came to a big metal box with buttons. She was curious and pushed a button.

The metal box started to shake. A man with a grey hat came out. He said, "Hello Amy, I'll be happy to help you!"

Amy asked, "What's that box?" "It's an oxygen tank," the man replied. He showed her how it worked and how people use it to breathe clean air.

Then the man saw that the oxygen tank was very dirty. He smiled and said, "I think it needs cleaning. Would you like to help me?" Amy nodded and was very excited.

So Amy and the man worked hard to clean the oxygen tank. Finally, when it was all shiny and clean, they both gave a big smile and said together, "We did it!"

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were walking in the woods when they saw a turkey.

Jill was scared so she said, â€œNo. That turkey is too fast. We wonâ€™t be able to get it." 

Jack didnâ€™t give up and said, â€œI can get the turkey if I run fast." 

Jack ran fast, but the turkey ran faster. Then something amazing happened. Jack received help from a friendly animal! The animal ran after the turkey and caught it.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big dog named Max. Max was very frightened of everything. One day, Max was playing in the park when he saw a cat. The cat was sitting on a wall.

Max wanted to be friends with the cat, so he called out, "Hello, cat! Do you want to play?" The cat looked at Max and said, "No, I don't want to play with you. You are a big dog and you might hurt me."

Max was sad, but he knew the law said that big dogs should be careful with small animals. So, he walked away from the cat. But as he walked away, he tripped and fell. Max was hurt and cried out loud.

Nobody came to help Max because they were all too frightened of the big dog. Max was all alone, and he felt very sad. The bad ending made Max wish he was not so big and scary, so he could have friends to play with.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to catch bugs and put them in a jar. They wanted to see how the bugs lived and what they did. They thought bugs were a wonder.

"Look, Sara, I caught a big beetle!" Ben said, holding up his jar. "It has shiny wings and long legs. Do you think it can fly?"

"Wow, Ben, that is a nice bug!" Sara said, admiring the beetle. "But be careful, don't shake the jar too much. You might hurt it."

Sara and Ben found a shady spot under a tree and sat down with their jars. They watched the bugs crawl and wiggle inside. They tried to guess what the bugs were thinking and feeling.

Suddenly, they heard a loud bark. A big dog ran towards them, wagging its tail. It was Max, the spoiled dog from next door. Max liked to chase and bite everything he saw. He did not listen to anyone.

"Uh-oh, it's Max!" Sara said, grabbing her jar. "He will try to get our bugs! Run, Ben, run!"

Sara and Ben ran as fast as they could, but Max was faster. He jumped on them and knocked them down. He grabbed Ben's jar with his mouth and shook it hard. The jar broke and the beetle flew away.

"Max, no!" Ben cried, trying to get his jar back. "Bad dog, bad dog! You spoiled my bug!"

Max did not care. He licked Ben's face and wagged his tail. He thought he was playing a fun game. He did not understand why Ben was sad and angry.

Sara hugged Ben and tried to make him feel better. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. Max is a mean dog. He does not know how to share. But don't worry, we can catch another bug. Maybe we can find a butterfly or a ladybug. They are pretty and gentle. Do you want to try?"

Ben nodded and wiped his tears. He said, "OK, Sara. Thank you. You are a good friend. Let's go catch another bug. Maybe we can find a wonder."

Once upon a time, there was a big fat cat named Tom. Tom loved to play with his toys and eat lots of food. One day, something bad happen to Tom. He hurt his paw and couldn't walk anymore. His owner took him to the hospital, where the nice doctor helped him feel better. Tom was so happy to be able to walk again and play with his toys. From that day on, Tom made sure to be careful and not get hurt again.

Mummy had a jolly smile on her face when she put the violin in little Jack's hands. He held it carefully and looked up at Mummy, wondering what he was meant to do. She nodded and said, "Go ahead and play!"

Little Jack put the violin to his shoulder and willed himself to make a sound. After a few seconds the room was filled with a beautiful musical melody. Mummy's jolly smile grew even wider and soon she was tapping her feet along with the music.

Little Jack looked up, his eyes sparkling with joy. He put the bow up and down, faster and faster, as if he was trying to make all the music out of the world. The violin was singing and Mummy was singing and they were both laughing and smiling.

Little Jack put the violin down, still smiling. He felt so proud - he had made something so beautiful. And he knew that with a little bit more practice, he would be able to master the violin!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She was very excited because she was going to have an adventure. She put on her coat, grabbed her hat and marched to the park. When she got there she saw a big tree, then she saw a lime! She didn't know what it was but it looked very interesting. 

Sarah marched over to the lime and said, "Hello Lime. What are you doing here?" The lime didn't say anything! It just sat under the tree. 

Sarah was not sure what to do, so she asked the tree if it knew what the lime was doing. The tree said, "Why don't you pick the lime up and take it home with you? Then you can find out what it is!".

So Sarah picked up the lime and marched all the way home. When she got home, she cut the lime open and discovered it was full of tasty juice! She was very happy and she thanked the tree for giving her such an interesting adventure. 

The end.

Max was a curious 3-year-old boy. He liked to explore the world around him. One day, he was visiting his grandmother's house and he found a mattress in her bedroom. He wanted to touch it and it looked so soft, so he reached out and touched it. 

But the mattress was fragile and his touch made it crumble. His grandma shouted in surprise. Max felt worried and guilty. He had broken his grandma's mattress. 

His grandma knew that mistakes happen and was gentle with him. She hugged him and said, "Don't worry Max, accidents happen." His grandma then got him to help her find something that could be used to fix the mattress. They found a patch and his grandma showed him how to put it on.

Max was so proud that he had helped fix his grandma's mattress. He touched the patch and smiled. Now the mattress was good as new!

Once there was a little boy who loved being creative. He liked to take things and turn them into something new. One day, he saw a fountain and he wanted to take it. The little boy knew it was too big to fit in his pocket. But, he had a creative idea! 

He walked around the fountain and started taking tiny pieces. He grabbed a few rocks and some flower petals. He also found a little stick and some leaves. When he was done, he had taken a lot of things from the fountain. 

Then he started piecing them together. He chose the rocks to be the bottom of his project, then he built up with the flowers and leaves. The little stick he made into a flag to put on top. He was so happy with his fountain - he had made it himself!

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and their dog, Spot. Spot is a big, furry dog who likes to lick their faces and run with them in the yard.

One day, Anna and Ben are playing with their purple ball. They throw it to each other and to Spot. Spot runs fast and catches the ball in his mouth. He brings it back to them and wags his tail. Anna and Ben laugh and clap their hands.

But soon, they start to feel tired. They yawn and rub their eyes. Mommy comes and says, "It's time for a nap, my sweeties. Come on, let's go to your room." Anna and Ben nod and follow Mommy. They hug Spot and say, "Bye, Spot. See you later."

Mommy takes them to their room, where they have two beds with soft blankets and pillows. She tucks them in and kisses their cheeks. She says, "Sleep well, my loves. I'll be here when you wake up." She turns on a small lamp that makes a warm glow. She leaves the door ajar.

Anna and Ben close their eyes and snuggle with their teddy bears. They feel cozy and safe. They hear Spot's snores from the living room. They smile and drift into a nap. They dream of purple ball and Spot and Mommy. They are happy.

Once there was a little girl. She was three years old. Her teachers said she was bossy, but she loved to play outside with her friends.

One day she decided to go exploring, and she saw something really exciting. There was an open door! She had never seen it before. She thought this must be a special door.

She slowly walked inside the room and was amazed. There were toys everywhere! She had never seen so many exciting things.

Then she realized something. This was her very own room. It was her special room filled with her own toys. It was even more amazing to her than the open door.

She had so much fun playing in her room. She showed it to all of her friends, and they all thought it was very cool. She was so proud that she was bossy enough to explore and find her own special room.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. But one day, the sunshine went away and it became very dark and cloudy. Lily felt sad because she couldn't play outside anymore.

Lily decided to make her own sunshine. She got some paper and crayons and drew a big yellow sun. She taped it to her window and it made her room feel warm and bright. But when she went outside, it was still dark and cloudy.

Lily realized she couldn't make the real sunshine come back. She felt poor because she couldn't do anything about it. But then, she saw a rainbow in the sky. It was beautiful and made her feel happy again. Even though the sunshine was gone, she knew there were still good things in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the green grass. One day, she found a machine in the grass. The machine was big and shiny. Lily was curious about the machine and asked her mommy what it was. Her mommy said, "I recommend that you don't touch it because it might be dangerous." 

Lily listened to her mommy and stayed away from the machine. She played in the green grass with her toys instead. Later that day, Lily's daddy came home and saw the machine. He knew what it was and said, "This machine is used to cut the grass. It helps make the grass look nice and neat." 

Lily thought that was cool and asked if she could help use the machine. Her daddy said no because it was too dangerous for her. Lily was sad but knew that her daddy was just trying to keep her safe. From that day on, Lily played in the green grass and admired the machine from afar.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who lived in a big house with her family. One day, she went for a walk in the forest near her house. As she was walking, she noticed something shiny on the ground. It was an unknown object that she had never seen before. 

The girl picked up the object and looked at it closely. She couldn't figure out what it was or what it was for. She decided to take it home and show it to her family. 

When she got home, she showed the unknown object to her family. They were all very curious about it and tried to figure out what it was. After some time, they discovered that it was a rare gemstone that was worth a lot of money. The girl was very happy that she had found something so special in the forest.

Mummy was walking in the park with her little girl. Suddenly, the little girl saw a snake! She was scared and started to complain to mummy. But mummy said, "Don't worry, it's ok, the snake won't hurt us". Just then, an open door appeared near the snake. On the other side of the door was a big garden full of nice flowers and pretty birds. The little girl pointed to the door and said, "Let's go there, mummy!". Mummy said, "OK, lets go!" So the little girl and mummy opened the door and went through together. Inside the garden, there were no more snakes, only pretty things to look at. The little girl said, "I'm so glad we came here, it's much nicer!". And mummy smiled, happy to have made her daughter happy.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate machine. It was in a big room and it made lots of noise. Every day, the machine whirred and hummed, until one day it made a funny sound.

The machine was broken. Everyone was worried, so they called a nice man to help fix it. He opened the machine carefully and looked inside. He was careful and gentle, like if he was holding a delicate bird.

He fixed the machine and the funny noise stopped. Now, the machine worked better than ever! Everyone was so happy that they hugged the man, who was really happy too.

The machine was now like a big hug. It was quiet, so everyone could relax and be at peace. This machine was now special. Everyone was very glad it was fixed!

Once upon a time, there was a boy who was very sad. He had lost something very special - his sunglasses! He had been playing outside when the wind blew them away, and he couldn't find them anywhere.

He searched and searched, but couldn't find them, and he was getting very sad. But then, he had an idea. He put on his special hat and asked all his friends for help.

Everybody worked together, and finally, the boy gained back his special sunglasses! They had found them outside in the bushes, where the wind had blown them.

The boy was very happy and put on his sunglasses. Then, he noticed something strange - he could hear better with them on. His friends said that he had been deaf, but his special sunglasses had made him better!

The boy was amazed and thanked everybody for helping him to gain his special sunglasses back. He was happy to be able to hear now, and he was very happy to have his sunglasses back.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who liked to wander. One day, she found a hammer in an unknown place. Curious, she picked up the hammer and decided to explore with it.

The hammer was so heavy and the girl felt special because she had something to carry on her journey. Everywhere she went, the hammer made a loud thump as it bumped against the ground.

Under a big tree she found something interesting that she had never seen before. She used the hammer to knock on the round object and it made a strange sound. She kept knocking until the unknown object opened up and sprang to life!

She had discovered a tiny little bird! The bird flew up in the sky and the girl waved goodbye. She put the hammer back in her pocket and continued to wander - wondering what else she might find!

Once there was a modest mouse who lived in a chimney. Every night, the mouse would look out into the night sky and thought of all the places he would like to go. One night, he decided it was time to go exploring.

He set off into the night and after a while, he came to a big, old house. There was a crack in the chimney and the mouse crawled inside to stay warm.

Suddenly the mouse heard a voice. It came from inside the house and belonged to a little girl. "Please don't go!" She shouted. 

The mouse was surprised and he said, "Why should I stay?". The little girl said, "Because I am lonely. You can be my friend". 

The mouse knew he could also be brave and explore, so he decided to stay. The mouse found a cozy spot in the chimney and the two friends enjoyed many nights of stories and fun.

Sara and Ben are brother and sister. They like to play in the park. They swing, slide and run. They have fun.

One day, they see a big hill. They want to climb it. They hold hands and go up. They see many things. They see birds, flowers and clouds. They are happy.

But then, Ben slips. He falls down the hill. He rolls and rolls. He cries. Sara is scared. She runs after him. She wants to help him.

She catches him at the bottom. She hugs him. He is hurt. He has scratches and dirt. He is sad. Sara is sad too.

She helps him stand up. She wipes his tears. She says, "It's okay, brother. I am here. You are brave. We will go home. Mom will make you feel better."

They walk back to the park. They see their mom. She sees them. She is worried. She asks, "What happened?"

Sara says, "Ben fell down the hill. He is hurt. But he is okay. I helped him."

Mom says, "Oh, no. Poor Ben. You are a good sister, Sara. You are kind. Come here. I will hug you both. I will clean your wounds. I will give you a kiss. I love you."

Sara and Ben smile. They hug their mom. They love her too. They are glad. They are a family. They are ordinary. But they are special.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her hoop in the park. One day, while she was playing, she saw a boy with a big, disgusting bug on his shirt. Lily didn't like bugs, but she felt sorry for the boy. She went up to him and said, "Don't worry, I'll kiss the bug goodbye!" And she did! The boy was so happy that he gave Lily a big hug. From that day on, they became good friends and played with their hoops together every day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to a big building with her mom. They got in the elevator and went up, up, up. It was a very unusual elevator because it had buttons that glowed in the dark.

When they got out of the elevator, they saw a big room with lots of toys. Lily played with the dolls and blocks, but her mom had to go to a meeting. Lily had to remain in the room with the toys until her mom came back.

Lily waited and waited, but her mom didn't come back. She started to feel scared and sad. But then, she saw a friendly face - it was the security guard! He helped Lily find her mom and they all went home together. From that day on, Lily always remembered the unusual elevator and the kind security guard.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he found an ancient gear on the ground. It was rusty and old, but Timmy thought it was cool.

He took the gear home and showed it to his dad. His dad told him it was very old and special. Timmy wanted to keep it safe, so he put it in a box and locked it with a key.

But one day, Timmy's little sister found the key and opened the box. She played with the gear and accidentally broke it. Timmy was very sad that his special gear was broken and couldn't be fixed.

Timmy learned that sometimes things can't be fixed when they're broken, but he still had his toy cars and trucks to play with.

Sam and Jen were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. Sam had a red car that could zoom very fast. Jen had a pink bike that she could jog on. They had fun racing each other and making noises.

One day, they saw a big dog in the park. It was black and furry and had sharp teeth. It barked loud and ran after them. Sam and Jen were scared. They tried to get away, but the dog was faster. It caught up with Sam and bit his car. The car broke into pieces and stopped zooming. Sam cried and dropped his car. Jen stopped her bike and ran to him.

"Are you okay, Sam?" Jen asked. She hugged him and looked at his car. It was dead. It could not zoom anymore.

"I'm sorry, Jen. I should have listened to you. You told me not to zoom too close to the dog. But I wanted to win the race. I was silly and mean." Sam said. He felt bad and sorry.

"It's okay, Sam. I forgive you. You are my friend. But you have to be careful and kind. The dog was angry and scared. He did not like us zooming and jogging near him. He wanted to be left alone. We have to respect other animals and people." Jen said. She was wise and nice.

Sam and Jen learned a lesson. They said sorry to the dog and gave him a bone. The dog wagged his tail and licked their faces. He was happy and friendly. They played with him and their toys. They zoomed and jogged together, but not too fast or loud. They had fun and were safe.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big red strawberry on a green plant. They wanted to eat it, but it was too high for them to reach.

"Let's use a stick to get it," Ben said. He found a long stick and tried to poke the strawberry. But the stick was too heavy and he dropped it.

"Let's use a chair to climb up," Lily said. She dragged a small chair from the porch and put it near the plant. She climbed on the chair and reached for the strawberry. But the chair was too wobbly and she fell down.

"Are you okay?" Ben asked. He helped Lily get up and dusted off her dress.

"I'm okay, but I still want the strawberry," Lily said. She looked around and saw a butterfly. It was yellow and black and very graceful. It flew over the plant and landed on the strawberry.

"Look, a butterfly!" Lily said. She pointed at the butterfly and smiled.

"Maybe the butterfly can help us," Ben said. He had an idea. He whispered to Lily and they nodded.

They went to the butterfly and said, "Hello, butterfly. You are very pretty and graceful. We like you very much. Can you please share the strawberry with us? We are very hungry and we have no other fruit."

The butterfly looked at them and fluttered its wings. It was very kind and generous. It said, "Hello, children. You are very polite and friendly. I like you very much too. Of course I can share the strawberry with you. There is enough for all of us."

The butterfly moved aside and let Lily and Ben pick the strawberry. They thanked the butterfly and broke the strawberry in three pieces. They each ate a piece and gave the last piece to the butterfly. It was very sweet and juicy.

They all enjoyed the strawberry and became good friends. They played in the garden until the sun went down. They said goodbye to the butterfly and went home. They were very happy and grateful.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little girl called Daisy. Daisy loved her mummy and daddy very much, and she spent every day playing with them.

One day, Daisy went to play in the garden. While she was there, she found a beautiful crystal lying in the grass. It glittered in the sunshine and Daisy thought it was magical. She wanted to keep it for herself.

Daisy put it in her pocket and ran back to the house to show mummy and daddy. But when she got there, she saw that someone had disturbed the living room. Everything was in a mess and her parents were nowhere to be seen.

Poor Daisy started to cry. She was scared and she didn't know what had happened. She was so upset that she dropped the crystal and it made a loud noise when it hit the ground. 

At that moment, the bad robbers returned to the house. The crystal made them angry and they chased Daisy out of the house.

They never saw Daisy again. Her parents were so sad that she was gone. Daisy's chubby little face never returned to the house again.

Mummy and Daddy took their daughter to the beach. It was a lovely day. The little girl loved the clear blue sea, the white sand and the sunshine. 

Mummy and Daddy wanted her to try something new. "Let's buy a surfboard," said Daddy. So they found a big, colourful surfboard and bought it. 

The little girl had so much fun! She laughed as the waves carried her board forward and she felt the spray of the water on her face. 

When it was time to go home, the little girl hugged the surfboard. The sun was setting and it looked even more lovely than it had that morning. Mummy and Daddy smiled at each other. They were so happy that their daughter was having such a great time at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, while playing, Lily found a hidden treasure in the bushes. She was so excited and wanted to keep it for herself.

Lily's friend, Jack, saw her hiding the treasure and asked, "Can I see what you found, Lily?"

Lily hesitated for a moment, but then she let Jack see the treasure. Jack was very happy for Lily and said, "You will be rewarded for being so kind and sharing your treasure with me."

From that day on, Lily learned that sharing is caring and that when you let others see what you have, good things will come your way.

Once upon a time, there was a great cave deep in the forest. The entrance was surrounded by huge trees, and if you looked carefully, you could see a light in the darkness. Inside the cave, lived an old woman. 

Every morning, the old woman would walk out of the cave and into the forest. She would remind the animals that no matter the future, it was important to live together in peace and harmony. 

One day, the old woman's peacefulness was challenged. A strange creature, covered in dark fur and cold eyes, appeared in the forest. The creature threatened the old woman, saying that if the animals would not become its slaves, it would wipe out the entire forest. 

The old woman, however, refused to be afraid. She told the creature that in dark times like these, it was more important than ever to live in peace and unity. Reminding the creature of the importance of living together peacefully, the old woman bravely walked back to her cave.

So he went up to the people and said, "I'm selling my switch". He showed them the switch, and they liked it very much. They bought it and went away with a smile.

The man was so happy and proud. He had sold his switch, and he was feeling very good!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to explore. One day, Timmy went to a spooky house. He saw a skeleton and it scared him. He ran away and bumped into his friend, Sarah.

Sarah asked, "What's wrong, Timmy?"

Timmy said, "I saw a mysterious skeleton in the spooky house. It scared me!"

Sarah said, "Let's go back and see if it's still there. Maybe it's not so scary after all."

So, Timmy and Sarah went back to the spooky house. They saw the skeleton again but this time, they weren't scared. They realized it was just a decoration for Halloween. They laughed and continued to explore the mysterious house.

John and his mom were at the park. John wanted to play sports, so he ran across the grass. He saw a big, deep lake.

Mom: John, don't go too close!

John stopped, but he was so excited to play sports. He wanted to look for a sport he could do. Then he saw a sport he liked.

John: Mom, look!

Mom: What is that?

John: It looks like a sport I can do there.

Mom: Okay, but stay away from the deep water.

John smiled and ran over to the sport. He had so much fun playing and running around. He even got a little wet! John had a great time playing his sport and mom was happy he stayed safe.

Once upon a time there was a taxi. It was an amazing taxi. It could take people to lots of different places. It had lots of fun passengers and even prizes.

One day, a little girl wanted to go on the amazing taxi. She went inside and it started to move. She was excited!

The taxi included different games and lots of surprises. It made lots of noises and was really fun. Then, it brought the little girl to her destination.

It was an amazing journey that the little girl would never forget!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went to the park with her mom. They saw a big tree and Lily wanted to climb it. 

Her mom said, "Be careful, Lily. Don't hang from the branches." 

Lily climbed up the tree and found a little bird's nest. She gently opened it and saw three tiny eggs inside. She felt anxious because she didn't want to hurt the eggs. 

Suddenly, the mother bird came back and saw Lily. The mother bird said, "Please don't touch my eggs. They are very fragile." 

Lily apologized and climbed down the tree. She and her mom sat on the grass and watched the birds fly in the sky. They had a lovely day at the park. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a wild fireplace. It was big and it had lots of colors. Everyday, two children would cover it with fun things.

The first child was Bill. He liked to cover the fireplace with lots of blankets. He wanted it to be soft and comfy like his bed.

The other child was Sarah. She was very creative. She would cover the fireplace with pictures, flowers and feathers. That way it looked very pretty.

The two children would work together and have lots of fun. Every day the fireplace would look wild and bright. The children were very proud of their work.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a big white dog named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to play in the yard. The yard had green grass and a big tree.

One day, Fluffy saw a little boy named Tim. Tim was sad because he lost his ball. Fluffy wanted to help Tim. So, Fluffy looked for the ball in the yard.

Fluffy found the ball under the big tree. Tim was very happy. He said "Thank you, Fluffy!" Tim clapped his hands to applaud Fluffy. They played in the yard together and became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to dance. She would move her body to the rhythm of the music and twirl around the room. One day, Lily's mom signed her up for a dance class.

At the class, Lily met a boy named Max. Max was having a difficult time learning the dance moves. "I can't do it," Max said sadly. "It's too hard."

Lily smiled and said, "Don't worry, Max. I'll help you. We can practice together." So, Lily and Max practiced the dance together and soon they were both doing it perfectly. They even got to use scissors to cut out paper shapes for their costumes. At the recital, Lily and Max danced beautifully to the rhythm of the music and everyone clapped and cheered.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with pastel colors. Her mommy bought her a big box of pastels for her birthday. Lily was so happy that she hugged her mommy and said "I love you!"

One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. There were many children playing and it was very noisy. Lily didn't like the noisy sounds. She covered her ears and said "It's too noisy here!"

But then, Lily saw a little girl who was sad because she lost her toy. Lily wanted to help her. She gave the little girl her favorite pastel drawing and said "I love you, you can have this." The little girl smiled and hugged Lily. From that day on, Lily wasn't bothered by the noisy sounds anymore. She felt happy because she helped someone and she knew that love is more important than anything else.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a girl named Lucy. She loved to wear her favorite blouse. It was red with little flowers on it. One day, she saw a boy with an unknown toy. It looked like so much fun! Lucy wanted to play with the toy too.

Lucy asked the boy if she could play with his toy. The boy said no, but Lucy did not listen. She tried to push the boy to get the toy. The boy got very sad and started to cry. Lucy's mom saw what happened and came to help.

Lucy's mom told her that pushing is not nice. She said, "We should always be kind to others and share our toys." Lucy felt bad for making the boy cry. She said sorry to the boy and gave him a hug. From that day on, Lucy always remembered to be kind and share her toys. And they all played happily together.

Once upon a time, there was a rare bird with a special style. The bird had pretty colors and could sing beautiful songs. Everyone loved to watch and listen to the bird.

One day, the bird was flying high in the sky when it saw a little cat stuck in a tree. The bird wanted to help the cat. So, the bird flew down to save the cat.

The bird sang a soft song to make the cat feel better. Then, the bird gently picked up the cat with its strong feet. The bird flew down and put the cat safely on the ground. The cat was so happy to be saved by the rare bird with a special style. They became best friends and played together every day.

Lily wanted to buy a muffin from the bakery. She had saved some money from her piggy bank. She liked the muffins with chocolate chips and sprinkles. They looked yummy and sweet.

She walked to the bakery with her mom. She saw a big sign that said "Muffins: 2 for 5 dollars". She counted her money. She had 4 dollars and 2 pennies. She thought she had enough.

She went to the counter and pointed to the muffins she wanted. The lady behind the counter smiled and said, "That will be 5 dollars, please."

Lily gave her the money. But the lady shook her head and said, "Sorry, honey, this is not enough. You need 5 dollars, not 4 dollars and 2 pennies. These muffins are expensive."

Lily felt sad and confused. She did not understand why she could not buy the muffins. She started to cry. She felt embarrassed. She wanted to hide.

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. Don't cry. You made a mistake. It's not your fault. The sign is tricky. It means you have to pay 5 dollars for 2 muffins, not for 1 muffin. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She wiped her tears. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, lady. I thought I had enough money."

The lady said, "It's okay, sweetie. Don't be sorry. You are a smart and brave girl. You tried to buy something by yourself. That's very good. How about I give you one muffin for free? You can share it with your mom. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled. She said, "Thank you, lady. You are very nice. I like your muffins. They are yummy and sweet."

The lady gave her a muffin and a napkin. She said, "You're welcome, Lily. Enjoy your muffin. And don't forget to say thank you to your mom. She loves you very much."

Lily said, "Thank you, mom. I love you very much. Can we share the muffin?"

Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. I love you very much, too. And I love muffins. Let's share the muffin. And let's learn more about money and numbers. They are fun and useful."

They sat on a bench and ate the muffin. It was yummy and sweet. Lily felt happy and proud. She learned something new. She was not embarrassed anymore. She was a smart and brave girl.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big rubber ball that bounced very high. Ben had a small rubber duck that squeaked when he squeezed it. They were having fun, but they also wanted to try each other's toys.

"Can I play with your ball, Lily?" Ben asked politely.

"OK, but only for a little while. Then you have to give it back," Lily said.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very nice," Ben said. He took the ball and threw it in the air. It bounced on the floor and hit the ceiling. Ben laughed.

Lily watched Ben play with her ball. She felt a little jealous. She wanted her ball back. She looked at Ben's duck. It was yellow and cute. She decided to take it.

She walked over to Ben and grabbed his duck. She ran away with it.

"Hey, that's my duck! Give it back, Lily!" Ben shouted. He dropped the ball and chased Lily.

"No, it's mine now! You can keep the ball!" Lily said. She squeezed the duck and made it squeak.

"That's not fair, Lily! You are stealing my duck! That's very bad!" Ben said. He caught up with Lily and tried to take the duck from her.

They both pulled the duck and made it stretch. They heard a loud pop. The duck broke in half. They both gasped.

They looked at the duck. It was ruined. They felt very sad. They also felt very sorry.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I shouldn't have taken your duck. It was very rude of me," Lily said.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I shouldn't have played with your ball for so long. It was very selfish of me," Ben said.

They hugged each other and said they were still friends. They threw away the duck and shared the ball. They learned not to steal and to be polite.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. They enjoy the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They are playful and happy.

One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is brown and furry. It has a long tail and sharp teeth. The dog runs to Anna and Ben. It barks and growls. Anna and Ben are scared. They try to run away, but the dog is faster.

"Help, help!" Anna and Ben cry. "Go away, bad dog!"

But the dog does not go away. It jumps on Anna and Ben. It bites them hard. Anna and Ben scream and cry. They bleed and hurt.

No one hears them. No one helps them. The dog is hungry and angry. It eats Anna and Ben. They are gone.

The dog is full and happy. It enjoys the world. It is playful and bad.

Once there was a girl called Mary who had a cube. Mary liked to take her cube everywhere. But one day, when Mary was playing with her cube, it suddenly disappeared! Mary began to worry.

She searched high and low, but she couldn't find her cube. Then, all of a sudden, she heard a noise coming from behind the sofa. She rushed to see what it was, and there it was! Her cube was rolling across the floor, very fast.

Mary was so happy! She quickly picked up her cube and held it close. She didn't want it to run away again - so she made sure to put it away in a safe spot. And from then on, she never had to worry about it disappearing again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a big tree with lots of leaves. She climbed up the tree and sat on a branch. She looked up at the sky and saw some clouds. She wondered what they were.

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise. It was a branch breaking! She fell down from the tree and landed on the ground. It was a messy fall. She had some dirt on her clothes and a small cut on her knee. She cried and her mom came running to help her.

After her mom cleaned her up and put a band-aid on her knee, Lily started to question herself. She wondered if she should have climbed so high. She learned her lesson and promised to be more careful next time. From that day on, she played in the park but never climbed that tree again.

Emily was a little 3 year old girl. One day, she went outside to play. She looked up at the sky and it was a bright summer day. The sun was shining and it was very hot.

But then, Emily saw a fan. It was blowing the cool breeze around her. She loved to play in the cold air. She reached up and grabbed the fan. She smiled as she felt the air blowing on her face.

Emily looked around and saw that the other kids were enjoying themselves too. They were playing sports and having fun in the sun. But Emily was content just playing with the fan. It was just what she needed to stay cool in the hot summer weather.

Henry loved to learn about the world. He loved to watch people and see what they did. One day, Henry went for a walk and saw a smooth lake. He wanted to learn how to swim but he had some trouble. He kept trying, but he couldn't get the hang of it. 

After many attempts, he got frustrated. He felt like giving up. But he kept trying until he finally learned how to swim. He was so proud when he could swim smoothly. He learned that if he worked hard and kept trying, he could achieve anything. He learned a valuable lesson that day.

A fierce clock hung on the wall. Bob the Bunny was scared of it as it made a loud noise that scared him. He thought about how he could make it better.

Bob had an idea. He hopped over to the cupboard and took out a cloth. Then he hopped over to the clock. He wiped it gently and the clock felt better.

Suddenly, the fierce clock became calm and peaceful. Bob was so pleased that he hopped around the room, clapping his hands. The clock no longer made loud noises that scared him. 

Eager to show his friends, Bob hopped out the door. He couldn't wait to tell everyone how he had used the cloth to wipe the fierce clock and make it so much better.

Lily and Max were playing with a big ball in the park. They liked to kick the ball and run after it. Sometimes they threw the ball to each other. They had a lot of fun.

But then the ball rolled into the bushes. Lily and Max ran to get it, but they could not see it. They looked and looked, but the ball was gone. They felt sad and mad.

"Where is our ball?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe someone took it," Max said.

They heard a noise in the bushes. They saw a dog with the ball in its mouth. The dog was big and brown. It had a knot on its tail. It looked tough and mean.

"Hey, that's our ball!" Max shouted. He tried to get the ball from the dog, but the dog growled and ran away.

"Come back, dog! Give us our ball!" Lily cried. She ran after the dog, but the dog was too fast.

They chased the dog for a long time, but they could not catch it. They got tired and thirsty. They missed their ball.

They went back to the park. They saw a man with the dog. The man was nice and kind. He saw Lily and Max and smiled.

"Hello, kids. Are you looking for this?" He held the ball in his hand.

"Yes, that's our ball! The dog took it!" Lily said.

"I'm sorry. The dog likes to play with balls. He didn't mean to make you sad. He just wanted to have fun. Here, you can have your ball back," the man said. He gave the ball to Lily and Max.

"Thank you, mister. You are very good," Max said.

"You're welcome, kids. Have fun with your ball. And don't be afraid of the dog. He is not tough and mean. He is friendly and sweet. He just seems tough and mean because of his knot on his tail.
