He was born with it. He can't help it. He likes to play with kids. Do you want to pet him?" the man asked.

Lily and Max looked at the dog. The dog wagged his tail and licked his lips. He seemed nice and cute.

"OK, we can pet him. But only if he gives us our ball back," Lily said.

The dog nodded and dropped the ball. Lily and Max petted him and scratched his ears. The dog barked and wagged his tail. He was happy.

Lily and Max were happy too. They made a new friend. They played with the ball and the dog. They had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Ellie who was 3 years old. 
One day, Ellie was feeling chilly and cold so she decided to find something to keep her warm. She searched all around the house but couldn't find anything.

Suddenly Ellie had a super idea. She remembered seeing a blanket in the wardrobe a few days ago, so she opened it and grabbed it. She wrapped the blanket around her and felt its warmth. It was hot!

Ellie had solved her problem and she was very happy. She felt warm and cozy and had a big smile on her face.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to go to the gym with her mommy. One day, they were at the gym and Lily was getting impatient. She wanted to go home and play with her toys.

Her mommy said, "Lily, we can't go yet. I need to finish my workout."

Lily replied, "Mommy, can I cut the paper with my scissors while we wait?"

Her mommy smiled and said, "Sure, Lily. That's a great idea. Let's go get some paper." 

Lily happily cut the paper into little pieces while her mommy finished her workout. They both had fun at the gym that day.

One day, a little girl named Lucy found a long string in her room. She thought it was very fun to play with. She tied the string to her toy car and pulled it around the house.

As Lucy played, she saw her mom making a cake in the kitchen. Her mom poured something hot that looked like it could melt. "Mom, what are you doing?" asked Lucy. "I am melting chocolate for the cake," her mom said with a smile.

Suddenly, Lucy's pet cat, Whiskers, jumped up and tried to catch the string. But Whiskers got all tangled up in the string and made a terrible mess. Lucy and her mom laughed and helped Whiskers get free. They all had a fun day and enjoyed the yummy cake together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and sing songs. One day, Lily's mommy noticed that the sink in the kitchen was leaking. 

"Uh oh, we have a problem," said Lily's mommy.

"What problem?" asked Lily.

"The sink is leaking. We need to fix it," said her mommy.

Lily wanted to help, so she got her toy tool kit and pretended to perform a repair. Her mommy was so happy to see her trying to help. 

"Good job, Lily. You are such a helpful girl," said her mommy.

Lily was so happy to make her mommy proud. From that day on, whenever something needed fixing, Lily was always ready to perform her toy tool kit magic.

Once upon a time, there was a furry friend. He was round, like a ball, and he liked to roll around. He rolled around in the grass, and over pebbles. He even rolled up and down hills!

One day, the furry friend rolled right up to a hungry baby bear. The bear said, "I'm so hungry!" The furry friend said, "Let's be friends!"

The baby bear said, "But I don't have any food!" The furry friend said, "Don't worry! We can find some together!" They rolled and rolled and finally found a big bowl of honey.

The baby bear was so happy! He said, "Thank you, my furry friend!" They shared the honey, and had lots of fun.

The furry friend and the baby bear are still friends today. They like to go on adventures and roll around together.

Once there was a happy little boy named James. He liked to paint. One day he went to an office. There were lots of colors and he was so excited. He got out a paintbrush and started to paint. James painted a healthy sun and a green tree. He also painted a blue fish and a yellow duck.

He smiled as he looked at his paintings. He had done a very good job. Everyone in the office was very proud of James. Everyone laughed and cheered as he showed them his pictures. 

Then James put down his paintbrush and took a deep breath. He was so relieved that he had finished his painting. The office filled with love and joy. All the colors looked so bright and healthy against the white walls. 

James had made a masterpiece that day. Everyone agreed that his painting was beautiful.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a large dog with brown fur and a red bow on its neck. The dog is friendly and wags its tail.

"Hello, dog!" Anna says. "You are very pretty. Can I pet you?"

The dog nods and licks Anna's hand. Ben is scared of the dog. He hides behind a tree.

"Ben, don't be afraid," Anna says. "The dog is nice. Come and say hi."

Ben shakes his head. He does not want to go near the dog. He sees a shiny purse on the bench. The purse is pink and has flowers on it.

"Look, Anna, a purse!" Ben says. "Maybe it has something inside."

Ben runs to the bench and grabs the purse. He opens it and finds a cookie, a ball, and a whistle.

"Wow, this is a great purse!" Ben says. "I want to keep it."

The dog barks and runs after Ben. The dog wants the purse too. The dog jumps on Ben and knocks him down. The purse falls on the ground and the cookie, the ball, and the whistle roll out.

"Hey, stop it!" Ben cries. "This is my purse!"

The dog picks up the cookie with its mouth and eats it. The dog also plays with the ball and the whistle.

"Bad dog!" Ben says. "Give me back my things!"

Anna comes to help Ben. She sees a lady running towards them. The lady is wearing a blue dress and a hat. The lady is the owner of the dog and the purse.

"Spot, come here!" the lady says. "I'm sorry, kids, he took my purse. He likes to chew on things."

The lady takes the purse and the whistle from the dog. She gives the ball to Ben and the cookie to Anna.

"Here, you can have these," the lady says. "I'm sorry for the trouble. Spot is a good dog, but he is very curious."

The lady puts the bow back on the dog's neck and walks away. The dog wags its tail and says goodbye.

"Bye, dog!" Anna says. "You are very funny. Thank you for the cookie."

Ben is still angry. He does not like the dog. He does not like the ball. He wants the purse.

"Anna, let's go home," Ben says. "I don't want to play here anymore."

Anna nods and follows Ben. She likes the cookie. She likes the dog. She thinks the purse is too big for her. She is happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the forest near her house. One day, while she was walking, she found a mushroom. It was big and red, and it looked very yummy. She picked it up and smelled it, but she didn't know if it was safe to eat. 

Lily felt dizzy and didn't know what to do. She decided to ask her mom. "Mommy, can I eat this mushroom?" she asked. Her mom looked at it and said, "I'm not sure, Lily. Let's guess that it's not safe to eat. We don't want you to get sick." 

Lily was sad that she couldn't eat the mushroom, but she was happy that her mom helped her. From then on, she always asked her mom before eating anything she found in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a smart little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily's mommy told her they were going to the park in a few minutes. Lily was so excited! 

They got in the car and drove to the park. When they arrived, Lily ran to the swings and went really high. She had so much fun! 

After playing for a while, Lily's mommy said it was time to go home. Lily didn't want to leave, but she knew they had to go. They got back in the car and drove home. Lily fell asleep in the car and when she woke up, she was back in her own bed.

Tom and Amy are new friends. They live near the sea. They like to play on the sand and look at the water. Sometimes they see big boats and fish and birds.

One day, Tom and Amy find a big shell on the sand. It is shiny and smooth and has many colors. Tom picks it up and puts it to his ear.

"Listen, Amy, I can hear the sea!" he says.

Amy wants to hear too. She takes the shell from Tom and puts it to her ear.

"You are right, Tom, I can hear the sea too!" she says. "It sounds like waves and wind and bubbles."

They are very happy. They take turns to listen to the sea in the shell. They call it their sea shell. They decide to keep it and share it.

They run to their moms and show them their sea shell. Their moms smile and hug them.

"What a nice find, Tom and Amy!" they say. "You are very lucky to have such a new and beautiful sea shell. And you are very lucky to have each other as friends."

John and his mom went on a walk one day. As they walked, they saw a dull, old mailbox. John wanted to collect something so he asked his mom what was inside.

His mom laughed and said there was no way to tell without opening it. But then she had a bright idea. She said they should write a letter, put it in the mailbox and see if someone wrote back.

So John wrote a letter and put it in the mailbox. He waited patiently for a day, but nothing happened. He was getting bored so his mom suggested that they write more letters.

John and his mom wrote several letters and each time put them in the mailbox. After a few days, something wonderful happened - they started getting letters back!

John was so happy and he enjoyed collecting all of the letters in the mailbox. His mom said that was his special collection and he was proud of it.

Once upon a time, there was a man who liked to write. He would always sit quietly at his desk and scribble words on paper. One day, a little girl came to visit the man. She asked him, "What are you writing, Mister?"

"I'm writing a story," replied the man. "Would you like to help me?"

The little girl nodded her head and the man gave her a pencil and some paper. They both wrote together, quietly and happily. When they finished, the man read the story aloud and the little girl clapped her hands with joy.

From that day on, the man and the little girl wrote many stories together. They always sat quietly and enjoyed each other's company. The end.

Once upon a time, a child named Jane was playing with her marbles. She was so excited to print the beautiful colors on the ground. But something disgusting happened. The marbles started falling into a puddle nearby and their colors began to fade away. Jane thought she would never get them back. 

Suddenly, an old man appeared and he had a magical device in his hand. He explained to Jane that he can make all the colors of the marbles come back to life. Jane was so excited and asked the old man to print the colors of all her marbles. 

The old man waved his magical device over the puddle and the colors slowly started to come back. Jane was jumping and screaming with joy. The colors of the marbles were even brighter and more beautiful than before. 

From then on, Jane was always careful not to put her marbles in any disgusting puddles. She was very happy that the old man could make all the colors come back to life.

Sara was playing in the garden. She wanted to explore. She saw a red flower. She wanted to touch it. She carefully reached out her hand and touched the flower. Suddenly, something wet splashed on Sara's hand. Sara was unhappy. She didn't like the wet feel.

"What's that?" Sara asked.

Her brother came out of the house. He was laughing.

"That's water!" he said. "It came out of the water hose."

Sara thought for a moment. She wanted to touch the wet water. She cautiously reached out her hand and touched it. It was cold! Sara liked the feel. She smiled and laughed.

"I want to do this again," Sara said.

Her brother smiled. He showed her how to turn the water hose on and off. Sara was so happy! She was ready to explore more.

Sara was a princess who loved her crown. She wore it every day and never took it off. She liked how it sparkled and shone on her head. She thought it made her look pretty and special.

One day, she went to play with her friend Ben, who was a prince. They had fun running, jumping, and sliding in the garden. But Sara did not notice that her crown was getting dirty. It had mud, grass, and bugs on it. Ben saw it and said, "Sara, your crown is not clean. It is icky and yucky. You should wash it."

Sara was angry and sad. She said, "No, I don't want to wash it. It is my crown and I like it. It is not icky and yucky. It is pretty and special. You are mean and rude. Go away!" She ran away from Ben and hid behind a tree.

Ben was sorry and sad. He did not mean to hurt Sara. He just wanted to help her. He said, "Sara, please come out. I am not mean and rude. I am your friend. I care about you and your crown. I know it is pretty and special. But it will be more pretty and special if it is clean. It will sparkle and shine more. And it will not have mud, grass, and bugs on it. That is not good for your crown or your head. Please let me help you wash it."

Sara heard Ben and felt sorry and sad too. She realized that he was right. Her crown was not clean. It was icky and yucky. And that was not good for her crown or her head. She came out from behind the tree and said, "Ben, I am sorry. You are not mean and rude. You are my friend. You care about me and my crown. You are right. It will be more pretty and special if it is clean. It will sparkle and shine more. And it will not have mud, grass, and bugs on it. That is good for my crown and my head. Please help me wash it."

Ben smiled and said, "Sara, I am glad. You are my friend. I care about you and your crown. Come on, let's go wash it." They went to the fountain and washed the crown. It became clean and shiny again. Sara put it back on her head and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. I am happy." Ben said, "You are welcome, Sara. You are a good friend too. I am happy." They hugged and played some more.

The moral of the story is: Don't worry about your things getting dirty. You can always clean them. And don't be angry or rude to your friends who want to help you. They care about you and your things. Be thankful and kind to them. They will make you happy.

Ben and Lily were twins who lived in a big city. They liked to see many interesting things in the city, like tall buildings, colorful cars, and noisy trains. One day, they went to the park with their mom and dad. They saw a big pond with ducks and fish.

Ben and Lily wanted to feed the ducks and fish. They asked their mom and dad to give them some bread. Their mom and dad gave them some bread and told them to be careful and not go too close to the water. Ben and Lily nodded and ran to the pond.

Ben and Lily threw some bread to the ducks and fish. The ducks and fish came to eat the bread. Ben and Lily were happy and laughed. They wanted to see the ducks and fish better. They went closer and closer to the water.

But they did not listen to their mom and dad. They went too close to the water. They slipped and fell into the pond. The water was cold and deep. Ben and Lily were scared and cried. They could not swim. They called for their mom and dad.

Their mom and dad heard them and ran to the pond. They jumped into the water and tried to save Ben and Lily. But the water was too cold and too deep. They could not reach Ben and Lily. Ben and Lily sank to the bottom of the pond. They did not come up again.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to wear her pink belt with a shiny buckle. One day, Lily's belt got stuck in the washing machine and it started to rot. Lily was upset because she loved her belt so much.

Lily's mom saw that she was upset and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her about her belt and how it was rotting. Her mom said, "Don't worry, we can get you a new belt. Let's go to the store and pick out a new one."

Lily was happy again and they went to the store. They found a new belt with a sparkly buckle and Lily was overjoyed. She put it on and said, "Thank you, Mommy! I love my new belt!"

Once upon a time there was a modern tree. It had many branches and one special branch in the middle. Every morning, a bird would come and mark the branch with its beak. Every day the bird got bigger and bigger and every day the branch got shorter and shorter. The modern tree was very proud of the bird; it was the most special thing in the tree's life.

The bird's markings became a symbol of protection and love. Everyone in the forest knew that the modern tree was the bird's home and they respected it more each day.

One day a storm came and knocked down the modern tree. All the branches were broken except one, the marked branch remained intact and out of the storm's grasp. The bird had marked the branch with an extra bit of care and love. Thanks to that, the branch and the bird survived.

The branch was a symbol of hope and protection in the forest. It showed that love always prevailed and that it was strong enough toweather any storm.

Lily was in her classroom. She saw a large desk in the corner which was the teacher's. Although it was distant, she could see the colorful papers and objects on it. Lily was only three but she was learning a lot in school. She wanted to learn new things!

So one day, while her teacher was not around, Lily decided to walk to the desk. When she got there she looked carefully at all the things on the desk. She touched a pencil and pretended to write like her teacher did. She also looked at a book and pretended to be a scientist. Even though she couldn't read yet, she had fun pretending!

After a few minutes, Lily heard someone coming. It was her teacher. She quickly ran back to her seat. On her way she was very careful to make sure she didn't get caught.

The next day, Lily was very happy when the teacher asked her to come to the desk. She had learned that it was OK for her to explore and use her imagination. So, she went to the desk with a smile on her face, ready to learn something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, Timmy saw a big, scary dog. The dog barked loudly and scared Timmy. Timmy ran away and hid behind a tree until the dog went away.

After playing for a while, Timmy noticed that he had an itch on his arm. He scratched it and it felt better. But then, he noticed that his hands were messy from playing in the dirt. His mom always told him to wash his hands after playing outside, so he went to the bathroom to clean up.

Later that day, Timmy went home and told his mom about the scary dog and how it scared him. His mom hugged him and said that it was okay to be scared sometimes. She also noticed that Timmy had a messy shirt from playing outside. She helped him change into a clean one and gave him a big hug.

The little girl was standing on the side of the road, watching all the people and bright flags in the parade. She was so excited and wanted to join in. Suddenly, she saw a group of children in the parade wearing cool hats, dancing and singing.

"I want to join!" the little girl shouted happily.

One of the adults in the parade saw the little girl and gave her a big smile. "Come on" he said, diving into the parade, "Come join the fun!"

The little girl followed him and started to dance with the other children. Everyone was laughing and having a great time.

But soon the little girl became frustrated. She couldn't keep up with the other children, and they were all having more fun than her. But then one of the adults came over and said:

"Come on, let's show them how to dive in this parade."

With a big smile, the little girl followed the adult and started to dance and sing. Soon, she was singing and dancing just like the other children, and everyone was having a great time. The little girl was happy and no longer frustrated.

Once upon a time, there lived a cow called Moo. Moo was a selfish cow and did not care about anyone else around her. She would only look out for herself.

One day, right at noon, Moo decided to strike. She lifted her hooves and pawed at the ground, making a big fuss. All the other animals gathered around her, curious to find out what was going on.

Moo spoke up and said, "I am striking because I want more food and hay, so that I can be happy and content!"

The other animals were unimpressed and scoffed at her. "You are so selfish," said one of the other cows. "Don't you care about anyone else around you? We all want more, too!"

Moo realized she was being selfish and decided to drop her strike. Together with the other animals, they all worked together to find a solution. 

In the end, they could all be happy and content.

John was a 3 year old who loved sports. He was a very active child and always ready to play. One day, John's mom took him out to the park to play but when they arrived it started raining.

John looked up at the sky and said: "Mommy, why is it raining? I want to play."

Mommy smiled and said: "I'm sorry sweetheart, the rain is preventing us from playing today."

John sighed and said: "Aww, I thought we were going to have so much fun playing our favorite sport."

Mommy said: "I know. Maybe some other day. Let's go home and watch a movie so you can still have some fun!"

John liked this idea and was happy that his mom provided a solution. On the ride home, his mom spoiled him with snacks and treats.

John smiled and said: "Thanks Mommy. I love you!"

Mommy hugged him and said: "I love you too."

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Bob and Jane. Every day they would play in the park together, having lots of fun. One day, they decided to build something special, so they collected some logs and started to build a chair.

Bob found a nice and small log, just perfect for the back of the chair. When they finished building, they both decided to take a break. Jane looked around the park and suggested that they should have a picnic.

Bob nodded and started to go home to get what they needed for the picnic, but before leaving he said "Let's decide something. Whoever can do five somersaults in a row gets the small chair."

When Bob returned with the food and drinks. Jane had already got in position and she was getting ready to do the somersault. With determination, she did five somersaults in a row, and Bob had to admit defeated.

The two of them enjoyed their picnic in the chair, happy that Jane had won the small chair.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a big green apple on a tree. Lily wanted to eat it, but Ben wanted to throw it.

"Give me the apple, Lily. I want to play with it," Ben said.

"No, Ben. It is my apple. I want to eat it. It is yummy," Lily said.

They pulled the apple from each other. The apple broke in half. They both dropped the pieces.

"Oh no! We destroyed the apple!" Lily cried.

A bird flew down and picked up one piece. A squirrel ran and took the other piece.

"Look, Lily. The bird and the squirrel are happy. They like the apple," Ben said.

"Maybe they are hungry. Maybe we can share with them," Lily said.

They smiled and waved at the bird and the squirrel. They went to find more apples to share.

Once upon a time, there was a twin brother and sister. They both loved to swim in the big river. One day, the twin brother thought of an idea. He decided that he wanted to swim to the other side of the river. So, he jumped in the water and swam across the river.

As he swam, the water tasted bitter. But he kept going. The twin brother was determined to reach the other side of the river.

After a few minutes, he finally made it to the other side of the river. He was so proud of himself for making it across!

He swam back to the edge of the river and waved at his twin sister on the other side. She was so happy to see him that she started to jump up and down. Then the twins played in the river together until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time there was a cherry tree in a big field. One day, the tree was busy loading lots of big and juicy cherries. It was a mysterious sight to see! Everyone in the village wanted to get a cherry, but they were too high up the tree. 

The village men thought of a plan. They brought a ladder and tried to climb up the tree to get the cherries. But the ladder was too small and it didn't reach the cherries. 

Then a clever girl had an idea. She told the village men to get a long piece of string and tie it to the cherries. She then pulled the string until the cherries fell down from the tree. Everyone was so happy and the girl was very proud. 

The village men loaded all the cherries into a big basket and took them back to the village. Everyone had a wonderful time enjoying the delicious cherries. It was such a mysterious and wonderful day!

Once upon a time there were two friends â€“ Mike and Jack. They were always together and had lots of fun. One day Mike told Jack he had a goal. He wanted to fight the biggest bug he could find. Jack was a little upset but said he would help.

So they set off, walking through the woods, looking for bugs. Finally they spotted a big one! Mike was so excited, but Jack was a bit scared. Mike started to fight the bug, and Jack cheered him on.

Mike tried very hard to win and after a few minutes he did it! He had won the fight and achieved his goal! Jack was so proud of him and gave him a big hug.

Both Mike and Jack were very happy and couldn't stop smiling. From then on, they were always together and had lots of fun.

Tom had a red glove that he liked very much. He wore it every day when he went outside to play. But one day, his glove got a big hole in it. He was very sad and showed it to his mom.

Mom said, "Don't worry, Tom. I can fix your glove for you. But you have to be polite and say please and thank you." Tom nodded and said, "Please fix my glove, Mom. Thank you very much."

Mom took a needle and some thread and sewed the hole in the glove. She made it look like new. She gave it back to Tom and said, "Here you go, Tom. Your glove is fixed. Now you can play with it again."

Tom was very happy and hugged his mom. He said, "Thank you, Mom. You are the best. I love you and I love my glove." He put on his glove and ran outside to play with his friends. He was careful not to make another hole in his glove. He was a polite and good boy.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. They loved to play together every day. One day, Timmy found a toy that he really liked. Tommy also liked the toy, but Timmy didn't want to share it. Tommy started to worry that Timmy didn't want to be friends anymore.

Tommy asked Timmy, "Can I play with your toy too?" Timmy thought about it for a moment and then said, "Okay, we can share it." Tommy was happy and they played with the toy together.

After they finished playing, Timmy said to Tommy, "I'm sorry I didn't want to share before. I learned that it's important to share with my friends." Tommy smiled and said, "It's okay. It's rare to find such a good friend like you." They hugged and continued to play together happily ever after. The moral of the story is that sharing is caring and it's important to be a good friend.

Once upon a time, there was a small dog. He was all alone, so he decided to go on a search. He walked and he hopped, but he didn't find anything. Then, he came to a big, empty room.

Suddenly, a big, friendly cat popped out from behind a box! The cat said, "Hello! My name is Kitty. Would you like to be my friend?" The dog was so happy. He said, "Yes!" and he introduced himself.

Kitty and the dog became the best of friends. They played games, and sang songs and chased each other around the empty room! The room was now full of happiness and laughter! They were so glad they found each other. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toys on the floor. One day, she found a secret door on the floor. She opened it and found a treasure chest inside. She was so happy and excited to reveal the treasure to her family.

But then, a big, scary monster came out of the treasure chest. Lily was helpless and didn't know what to do. The monster started to chase her around the room. Lily tried to hide, but the monster found her. 

In the end, the monster caught Lily and took her away. Her family never saw her again. They searched everywhere, but she was gone forever. They were so sad and heartbroken. The secret door on the floor was never opened again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to explore. One day she found a bookshelf and wanted to find out what was inside. Her parents had warned her not to investigate bookshelves alone, but she decided to delay and open it anyways. When she got close, she noticed that the bookshelf was very dangerous. She found herself trapped and realized it was too late - she couldn't get out. From then on, the little girl always listened to her parents and never delayed doing the things they said.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the rain and jump in puddles. One day, her mommy gave her a present - a new umbrella with a gentle pink color. Lily was so happy and couldn't wait to use it.

The next day, it started to rain. Lily put on her raincoat and took her new umbrella. She went outside to play. She jumped in puddles and twirled around with her umbrella. But then, the wind started to blow harder and harder. Suddenly, Lily's umbrella turned inside out and she got very wet. She tried to run back inside, but she was already soaked.

Lily learned that sometimes presents can't protect you from bad things. She also learned that it's important to be careful when playing outside in the rain.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little bunny named Floppy. Floppy liked to hop around in the grass and play with his friends. One day, Floppy's friends wanted to play a game of tag. Floppy was too shy to join in at first, but then he decided to give it a try.

As Floppy was hopping around, he noticed that his feet were starting to hurt. His shoes were too small and didn't fit him anymore. Floppy's mom took him to the store to buy new shoes. They found a pair that fit him perfectly!

With his new shoes, Floppy was able to run and play without any pain. He loved the motion of running and jumping with his friends. Floppy was no longer shy and had a great time playing with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat candy, but his mom said it was bad for his teeth. One day, Timmy went to the barber with his dad. The barber had a sour face and didn't smile at Timmy. Timmy tried to make the barber happy by telling him a joke, but the barber didn't laugh.

After the haircut, Timmy and his dad went to the store to buy some candy. Timmy remembered what his mom said and decided to try not to eat too much candy. He only picked one piece and saved the rest for later. When they got home, Timmy's mom was proud of him for not eating too much candy. She told him that even though candy tastes good, it's important to take care of your teeth.

The moral of the story is that it's important to try new things and listen to your parents. Even if something tastes good, it's important to think about what's best for you in the long run. And sometimes, even if someone seems sour, you can still try to make them smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine and climb up high on the swing set. One day, her mommy asked her if she wanted to learn math. Lily didn't know what math was, but she trusted her mommy and said yes.

Her mommy taught her how to count to ten and Lily was so happy that she could do it all by herself. She felt so proud and high up in the sky like a bird. From that day on, Lily loved math and wanted to learn more.

Lily knew she could trust her mommy to teach her new things and help her grow. She loved spending time with her mommy and learning new things together. And every time she counted to ten, she felt like she was on top of the world.

Lily was playing with her dolls in her room. She liked to dress them up and make them talk. She had a big iron that she pretended was a phone. She put it to her ear and said, "Hello, this is Lily. How are you?"

She heard a loud sneeze from downstairs. It was her dad. He was sick and had to stay in bed. Lily wanted to make him feel better. She had an idea. She took her iron and ran downstairs.

She found her dad in his room, covered with a blanket. He looked tired and sad. Lily smiled and said, "Dad, I have a surprise for you. It will make you happy."

She gave him the iron and said, "This is a phone. You can talk to anyone you want. You can call Mom, or Grandma, or your friends. They will say nice things to you and make you laugh."

Her dad looked at the iron and tried to smile. He said, "Thank you, Lily. That's very sweet of you. But this is not a phone. This is an iron. It is for making clothes smooth. It is very hot and can hurt you. You have to be careful with it."

Lily did not understand. She thought the iron was a phone. She wanted to show her dad how it worked. She pressed a button on the iron and said, "Look, Dad, it makes a sound. It is ringing. Someone is calling you. You have to answer it."

She put the iron to her dad's ear. But the iron was not ringing. It was steaming. The hot steam burned her dad's ear. He screamed and dropped the iron. He was in pain. Lily was scared. She did not mean to hurt her dad. She started to cry.

Her dad hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. It was an accident. You didn't know. I'm sorry I yelled at you. I love you. You are a good girl. But please, don't play with the iron again. It is not a toy. It is dangerous."

Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, Dad. I love you too. I won't play with the iron again. I will play with my dolls. They are not dangerous. They are fun."

Her dad kissed her and said, "That's a good idea. You can play with your dolls. And maybe later, we can watch a movie together. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled and said, "That sounds good, Dad. I hope you feel better soon. Maybe the movie will make you happy."

Her dad smiled and said, "Maybe it will, Lily. Maybe it will."

Once upon a time, Benny was walking through the forest. He looked around and saw all sorts of things. Then suddenly, he spotted a mushroom. It was so big and round and it was a very strange color. He got closer, and then he noticed something. The mushroom was very dirty. Benny started to stare at it. He was so curious and wanted to know more about the mushroom.

He touched it, and the mushroom felt all squishy. He poked it, and the mushroom wobbled. Benny had so much fun discovering the mushroom. He wanted to stay and play longer, but he heard his mom calling him and so he said goodbye.

On his way home, Benny kept thinking about the mushroom. He wondered why it was so dirty and why it felt so squishy. He hoped to come back soon and learn more about the mysterious mushroom.

Once upon a time, there was a family. The family had a big dog named Max. Max liked to play outside in the yard. One day, Max found a ball. He picked it up in his mouth and brought it to the family. The ball was smooth and bouncy. The family played with Max and the ball all day long. They had lots of fun together.

Once there was a little girl called Mia who loved to jump. Everywhere she went, she jumped. When walking to school, she would jump on the sidewalk. At the park, she would jump into the sandbox.

One day Mia was at the supermarket and she saw something unusual. She saw a lawyer. Mia had never seen a lawyer before so it made her very curious. She wanted to know what a lawyer did and why he was so dressed up. So, Mia jumped right up to the lawyer and asked him.

The lawyer was very confused. He had never seen a little girl so eager to talk to him. He tried to explain but Mia kept on jumping and interrupting.

Soon enough the store manager got involved. He explained to Mia that it was not appropriate to engage with strangers and it was wrong to interrupt people when they were talking.

Mia was very sorry for her behaviour and decided to never do something like this again. She had learned her lesson that it is important to be respectful to all strangers.

One day, Tim went to play in the yard. He saw a mysterious box. It was big and blue. Tim was very curious.

He asked his mom, "What is in the box?" She said, "It's a surprise, but I will remind you later."

Tim played with his toys and forgot about the box. His mom came out and said, "Do you want to open the box now?" Tim was excited and said, "Yes, please!"

They opened the box together. Inside was a big, red ball. Tim was so happy. He played with the ball all day in the yard.

One day, a little boy named Ben saw a newspaper on the floor. He wanted to read it, but he could not. He only knew some letters and sounds. He asked his mom, "What is this?"

His mom said, "This is a newspaper. It has stories and pictures of things that happen in the world. Do you want me to read it to you?"

Ben nodded. He liked to hear stories. He sat on his mom's lap and listened. He saw a picture of a big dog. He pointed and said, "Dog!"

His mom said, "Yes, this is a dog. He is a hero. He saved a girl from a fire. He ran into the house and dragged her out. He is very brave and strong."

Ben said, "Wow! I like the dog. Can we have a dog?"

His mom said, "Maybe someday. But we have to take care of a dog. We have to feed him, walk him, and play with him. Do you think you can do that?"

Ben said, "Yes, I can. I can run with the dog. I can give him water and food. I can throw a ball for him. I can be his friend."

His mom said, "That's good. But we have to ask dad first. He might be allergic to dogs. And we have to find a dog that needs a home. Maybe we can go to the shelter and see if there is a dog that likes us."

Ben said, "Okay. Can we go now?"

His mom said, "No, not now. We have to finish the newspaper first. And then we have to do some chores. Maybe we can go tomorrow."

Ben said, "Okay. But can I keep the newspaper? I want to look at the dog again."

His mom said, "Sure. You can keep the newspaper. But be careful. Don't rip it or make it dirty. It is not a toy. It is a paper."

Ben said, "Okay. I will be careful. Thank you, mom."

He hugged his mom and took the newspaper. He put it on his bed and looked at the dog. He smiled and said, "Hello, dog. You are a hero. I hope you find a home. Maybe you can be my dog. I will run with you and be your friend."

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Joe. He was three years old and loved to write. He wrote stories about all sorts of things: animals, food, even the sky.

One day, Joe found a funny looking patch on the ground. It was a black patch and Joe knew he had to write a story about it. He ran and got his notebook, eager to start writing.

Just then, Joe's mom called out to him. She said, "Joe, what are you doing?"

Joe said, "I'm writing a story about this funny black patch!"

Joe's mom smiled. "That sounds really fun," she said.

So Joe went back to the black patch and started writing. He wrote and wrote until he had finished the story. When it was done, he was very proud of what he had written.

The End.

John had his own paint. He was very excited and happy to show it to his mom. He said, "Mommy, I own paint!" His mom replied, "That's great John, let's paint together!" So, they opened the paint and John started to draw with it.

After a while, John finished his masterpiece and it looked so beautiful to him. He said to his mom, "Look mommy, I own tight paint!"

His mom was surprised and said, "Wow John, that's very impressive. Let's hang it up!" But, before they could hang the painting, John had an accident and the paint got smeared all over the place. His mom tried to console him but John was devastated and sad. 

The bad ending had been foreshadowed ever since John opened his paint; his mom had warned him several times to be careful and not play around with the paint too much. But, inevitably, he went against his mother's advice and it cost him dearly in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. He was 3 years old. Jack collected many different kinds of rubber things - rubber ducks, rubber balls, and rubber monkeys. 

One day, Jack saw an ugly rubber toy in a shop. He wanted the toy so badly that he asked his mom if he could buy it. But his mom said no. She said it was an ugly toy.

"Why can't I have it?" Jack asked. He was very sad and he wanted the toy very much. 

His mom said, "It's ok. Let's record it so you can always remember it."

So Jack decided to record the toy. He looked at the toy and said, "That's an ugly one." And then he put it back on the shelf.

Jack was very happy that his mom suggested recording the toy. Now he had something to remember it by. It was a very special memory!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was nice and she loved to skip. Every day she would go outside and skip around her house. She would skip around her front yard, around the garden and even around the trees.

One day, a little bird came along and the girl decided to skip with him. They would skip together until the sun started to set. The little girl and the bird would skip in circles, hopping around and around until they were both tired and out of breath.

Then, the girl decided to make a game. She took a little round stone and put it in a circle on the ground. She and the bird took turns skipping around and around the stone, counting how many times they could skip around it in one go.

The girl and the bird laughed and played skipping games until it was very dark. Then, they said goodbye and the little girl went back inside. She was very tired, but smiled all the way home, happy that she had such a fun and special day.

Once upon a time, there was an infant who was very clever. He was always exploring and learning new things. One day, he wanted to recognize something. The infant went on a journey to find something he could recognize.

He searched high and low, but everywhere he looked he saw nothing he could recognize. Suddenly, he spotted something in the distance. He squinted and saw it was a fluffy orange cat! "Meow," said the cat. The infant recognized it, and his face lit up with joy! 

He went up to the cat and started petting it. The cat purred and rolled over for a belly rub. The infant was so pleased he had recognized the cat he had been searching for. They became fast friends. 

The infant and the cat would often go on adventures together. When they returned, the infant would always look forward to recognizing the cat again. They were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big castle. It was very old and had lots of stories to tell. The people who lived there were very rich and had lots of treasure. One day, a little girl came to visit the castle. She loved to hear stories, so she asked the king to tell her the history of the castle. The king was happy to oblige and told her all about the castle's past. The little girl was very happy and felt very lucky to have heard such a rich history.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful little mouse named Mimi. Mimi loved to play and run all day. One day, Mimi saw a big pocket on a chair.

Mimi wanted to see what was inside the pocket, so she entered it. Inside the pocket, Mimi found a small red ball. Mimi was very happy and started to play with the ball.

Mimi played with the red ball all day. She would roll it, toss it, and even hide it. Mimi was very happy with her new toy. And from that day on, Mimi and the red ball were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim liked to play with his toys, especially his toy pistol. One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. They sat on a bench and Tim put his pistol on the seat next to him. Suddenly, a bird flew down and took Tim's pistol! It was very unusual for a bird to take a toy. Tim was sad, but his mom hugged him and said they would get a new one. They went to the store and bought a new pistol. Tim was happy again and played with it on the seat next to him.

One day, a young girl named Sarah was playing in her backyard. She saw something shiny and started to dig it up. It was a gold crown! Sarah was so excited, she started dancing around in circles.

Suddenly, her neighbor called out from his porch. "What do you have there, Sarah?" 
He could barely contain his surprise when Sarah held up the crown.

The neighbor smiled. He pointed to the crown and said, "That looks like a special crown. It must be a very special treasure. It could be very valuable."

Sarah didn't understand what he meant, so she just smiled and continued to twirl around.

Days passed and Sarah continued to wear the crown proudly. One day when she was visiting her grandmother, the old woman said, "Sarah, I used to be a queen when I was young. That's why you have the crown. You must use it wisely." 

Sarah suddenly realized that the crown was more than just a toy. She carefully put it back in the box and made sure to take special care of it. She knew that one day it would be a reminder of her young queen days.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Jen. She loved to go fast. Every week she would go to the park with her bike and speed across the grass. She was the fastest in the park. 

One day, however, something terrible happened. Jen went too fast and fell off her bike. She bumped her knee and was hurt. She cried and cried. 

Her Mom came running over. She hugged Jen and helped her stand up. Mom took her home and made her a warm drink to make her feel better. 

Then, she let Jen have a rest. She stayed in bed all day and in no time she was feeling much better. 

She was ready to go out on her bike again the next week, but this time she made sure she didn't speed too much. Jen was careful and kept on the path. She had learned her lesson, and no longer wanted to go too fast.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went for a walk by the creek. She saw a frog and said, "Hello frog, are you happy?"

The frog nodded his head and said, "Yes, I am very cheerful today! Would you like to play with me?"

Lily was so happy to have a new friend to play with. They played together by the creek, jumping and splashing in the water. They had so much fun that they didn't even notice the time passing by.

When it was time for Lily to go home, she said goodbye to the frog and promised to come back and play again. As she walked home, she felt cheerful too, knowing she had made a new friend by the creek.

Once there was a girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved looking at animals. Lily loved going to the park and examining the animals that lived there.

One day, Lily saw an owl sitting on a tree. She was so excited. The owl was so pretty! With its white feathers, round eyes and pointy ears. She wanted to get closer to get a better look.

Lily slowly tiptoed towards the tree where the owl was perched on. The owl looked down at her but did not move. Lily was so close that she could even touch the owl. She looked carefully at all its features and examined every detail.

The owl was sitting so still and seemed happy that Lily was there. Lily smiled at it and said 'hello'. The owl didn't say anything. Lily said goodbye and thanked the owl for letting her examine it.

Lily left feeling very happy. She had seen a pretty owl and been able to get so close!

Once there was a baby who loved to play. One day, she was playing with her toys in the garden. Suddenly, she sneezed! It was a very loud sneeze! The baby felt something on her nose. She touched it and saw a thing. It was a small, hard thing.

The baby wondered what it was. She picked it up and looked at it more carefully. She saw that it was a small rock! She smiled and put it in her pocket.

From then on, the baby was very careful with her sneezes. Whenever she felt one coming, she closed her eyes tight and held her breath. And when she couldn't help but sneeze, she looked around for the hard things!

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went to a big building. He saw a tall elevator and went inside. The elevator went up and down and Timmy felt great. 

When Timmy got out of the elevator, he saw a big room with lots of toys. He played with the toys for a while, but then it was time to go. 

As he was leaving, Timmy saw a man part his hair. The man smiled at Timmy and Timmy smiled back. It was a great day at the big building.

John was sad. He had lost his friends when he went for a walk. The sky was very gloomy, but he kept on walking. Suddenly, something caught his eye - it was a deer in the woods! The deer seemed to be looking right at him. John was so excited. He slowly moved closer and closer to the deer. The deer revealed its beautiful antlers. John was so amazed at the beautiful sight. He wanted to stay and admire it, but he remembered that he had to find his friends, so he waved goodbye to the deer and it ran away. John continued on his way, happy to have seen such a beautiful creature.

Once upon a time there was a kind girl who loved to eat fruit. Her favourite was apples so she decided to go and pick some from the apple tree. The apples looked ripe and yummy. She was so excited she ran to get the apples but she slipped and fell! She tried again but she slipped a few more times. 

The girl was very frustrated and she was about to give up when she heard a kind voice. She looked up and saw a kind old man. He smiled and handed her a special basket to put the apples in. With the help of the basket the girl managed to pick lots of apples. 

When she got home, the girl shared all the delicious apples with her family. They were so happy and thanked the kind old man for helping her. The girl was very proud of herself. She had worked very hard to get all the apples and she enjoyed eating them with her family.

Once there was a boy who loved to compete with his friends. He was very competitive, and he always wanted to win in all the games they played. 

One day, he thought of a new game. He wanted to see if he could change the measure of something. He grabbed a ruler and measured his arm. Then he asked his friends to try and measure something bigger or smaller than him. 

At first, no one could succeed in changing the measure. But then his friend Jerry tried and measured his foot. It was bigger than the boy's arm! Everyone cheered for Jerry and the boy was impressed. 

From then on, the boy was always excited to play games with his friends. He was even more competitive, trying to change the measures of different things and see who could win!

Ben and Mia love to swim in the sea. They have big masks and tubes to see the fish. One day, they see a big boat near the shore. The boat has many boxes on it.

"Let's go see the boat," Ben says. "Maybe they have something fun."

"OK," Mia says. "But we have to be careful. The boat might be bad."

They swim to the boat and look at the boxes. They see words on them. They do not know what they mean. They see a hole in one box. They peek inside. They see many shiny things.

"Wow," Ben says. "These are pretty. Can we take some?"

"I don't know," Mia says. "Maybe they belong to someone."

They hear a loud voice from the boat. It is a man. He is angry.

"Hey, you kids! Get away from there! That's my supply of jewels! I stole them from the reef! They are very valuable!"

Ben and Mia are scared. They drop the shiny things and swim away. The man tries to catch them, but he is too slow. He is crazy.

Ben and Mia reach the shore. They are safe. They hug each other.

"That was scary," Ben says. "We should not go near the boat again."

"Yes," Mia says. "The boat is bad. The man is bad. The shiny things are bad. They hurt the reef and the fish."

They decide to swim in another place. They find a nice reef with many colors and shapes. They see many friendly fish. They are happy. They forget about the boat and the crazy man. They have fun.

Andy and his mom walked to the park. When they got there, Andy saw the most amazing thing: a modern yacht! It was big and white, with a room and a little pool.

Andy asked his mom if they could get on the yacht. She said no, but she promised to buy him something yummy at the ice cream shop.

Andy and his mom started to walk away, but then Andy decided to climb onto the yacht. He wanted to see what it was like inside.

Just when Andy was about to open the door, a mean man came out of the yacht. He said Andy couldn't be on the yacht because it was white and he was too dirty.

Andy and his mom walked away sadly. Andy didn't get to go inside the big, modern yacht and he didn't get ice cream either.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He was very curious about the world around him. 

One day, John went to a park to play. He saw a strange box full of junk. It was a big box of old items, like toys and blankets. 

John loved to poke things, so he started poking the box with his finger. Inside, he saw something funny. It was a stuffed toy! It was a bit silly looking, so John thought it was stupid.

He started poking the toy with his finger and it made a funny sound. He laughed and poked it again. Suddenly, the toy started moving and talking! John was so surprised and he jumped back.

The toy said, â€œHi John! My name is Pat. I am a talking toy. Want to be friends?â€ 

John was so happy he had a new friend! He nodded and hugged Pat. They were best friends, and every day John would go to the park to play with Pat and poke the junk in the box.

Jim was sad. He had been playing in the park all day and he was really tired. He sat down on the bench and started to complain. He said that the park was too dirty and he didn't like it.

Suddenly, a message floated down from the sky. It said "Hey Jim, why don't you come to the beach? It's clean and beautiful." Jim was excited and jumped up from the bench.

He ran all the way, but when he arrived at the beach, it was just as dirty as the park had been. Jim was even more angry than before and he started to complain again. He said "This beach is just as dirty as the park!"

But then he heard another message coming down from the sky. It said "Jim, just look around. There is so much beauty everywhere! See, there's a pretty tree, some birds and a nice big ocean. Everywhere you look there is love and beauty, you just have to see it!"

Jim looked around and he saw the beauty everywhere. He smiled and he knew that he had been wrong to complain about the dirty park and beach. From then on, he looked for beauty everywhere.

Sara liked to whistle. She whistled when she woke up, when she ate, when she played, and when she went to bed. She whistled loud and happy. She whistled songs and sounds. She whistled all the time.

But her brother Ben did not like her whistling. He said it was too noisy and annoying. He said it hurt his ears and head. He said it made him mad. He asked her to stop whistling many times. But Sara did not stop. She was persistent. She liked to whistle too much.

One day, Ben had an idea. He went to the kitchen and opened a can of tuna. He knew Sara did not like tuna. She said it smelled bad and tasted worse. She said it made her sick. He took the can of tuna and hid it under her bed. He thought it would make her stop whistling.

But he was wrong. Sara did not notice the tuna under her bed. She whistled as usual. She whistled when she woke up, when she ate, when she played, and when she went to bed. She whistled loud and happy. She whistled songs and sounds. She whistled all the time.

The next day, Ben was surprised. He smelled something bad in Sara's room. He looked under her bed and saw the can of tuna. It was open and rotten. It was full of flies and worms. It was gross and stinky. He felt sick and sorry. He realized his idea was bad and mean. He took the can of tuna and threw it away. He went to Sara and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I put tuna under your bed. I wanted you to stop whistling. But I was wrong. You can whistle if you want. I don't mind."

Sara smiled and hugged him. She said, "Thank you, Ben. I'm sorry, too. I know you don't like my whistling. But I like it. It makes me happy. Can we be friends?"

Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "Yes, we can be friends. And maybe you can teach me how to whistle. It sounds fun."

Sara was happy. She said, "Sure, I can teach you. It's easy. You just have to blow air through your lips. Like this." She whistled a tune.

Ben tried to whistle. He blew air through his lips. But he only made a funny noise. He laughed. Sara laughed. They laughed and whistled together. They were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a chicken who liked to hide all the time. He liked to hide under the bushes, and behind big rocks. One day, the chicken decided to hide in a scary cave. He was very brave and he didn't realize how fierce the animals in the cave were.

As the chicken walked further and further into the cave, he suddenly heard a loud voice. He looked around and saw a fierce lion, who said, "Why are you here? This is my cave!"
The chicken was scared and started to tremble. He said, "I'm just trying to hide, that's all."

The lion thought for a moment, then he said, "I will hide with you, if you want. I like to hide too." The chicken was so happy, and said yes. The chicken and the lion hid together, deep in the cave. The chicken felt much safer with his new friend.

The chicken and the lion are still hiding in the cave today. They have become very good friends and have lots of fun.

Lily was a shy girl. She liked to play with her dolls and books, but she did not like to talk to other kids. She was afraid they would laugh at her or be mean to her.

One day, her mom told her that they were going to a birthday party. It was for Anna, a girl from her preschool. Lily did not know Anna very well, but she knew she liked princesses. Lily liked princesses too, but she did not have a princess dress.

"Don't worry, sweetie," her mom said. "You can wear your pink skirt and your white shirt. You look very pretty. And maybe you can make a new friend at the party."

Lily nodded, but she felt nervous. She did not want to go to the party. She wanted to stay home and play with her dolls.

When they got to the party, Lily saw a lot of kids. They were running and jumping and laughing. They had balloons and hats and cake. Lily felt scared. She held her mom's hand and hid behind her.

"Look, there's Anna!" her mom said. "Let's go say hello."

Lily saw Anna. She was wearing a beautiful princess dress. It was purple and sparkly and had a big bow. She had a crown on her head and a wand in her hand. She looked very happy.

"Hi, Lily!" Anna said. "I'm so glad you came to my party. Do you like princesses?"

Lily nodded, but she did not say anything. She looked at the ground.

"Me too!" Anna said. "Do you want to play with me? I have a lot of princess toys. We can pretend to be princesses and have a tea party. Come on, I'll show you."

Anna took Lily's hand and led her to a corner of the room. There was a table with cups and plates and a teapot. There were also dolls and stuffed animals dressed as princesses and princes.

"Look, this is my favorite princess," Anna said. "Her name is Elsa. She has ice powers. And this is my favorite prince. His name is Jack. He likes to make snowmen. Who is your favorite princess?"

Lily looked at the toys. She saw a princess she liked. She had long blonde hair and a pink dress. She had a necklace with a heart.

"I like her," Lily said softly. "She is pretty."

Anna smiled. "She is pretty. Her name is Rapunzel. She has magic hair. Do you want to play with her?"

Lily nodded. She took the doll and held it gently.

"Great!" Anna said. "You can be Rapunzel and I'll be Elsa. And we can invite the other princesses and princes to our tea party. Do you want to do that?"

Lily nodded again. She felt a little less shy. She liked Anna. She liked playing with her. She liked being a princess.

"Okay, let's do it!" Anna said. "We are the best princess friends ever!"

Lily smiled. She agreed. She was happy. She was glad she came to the party.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Sunny went to visit her granny. Sunny was so excited to go! When she arrived, she gave her granny a big hug.

Granny smiled and said, "I have something I'd like to borrow from you, Sunny. Can you give me a hug too?" 

Sunny happily hugged granny tightly. After the hug, Sunny was feeling a bit tired from her visit. 

"Why don't you take a nap, sweetie?" Granny suggested.

"Ok," said Sunny, smiling. "You can borrow my sleepy head for a bit!" 

Granny laughed and put Sunny down for a nap. After a nice rest, Sunny felt refreshed and ready for a new adventure. She hugged granny goodbye and said, "Thanks for lending me your hugs, granny!"

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Spot found a smelly old sock in the yard. He liked the sock very much and played with it all day.

As the days went by, Spot noticed that the sock began to become even more smelly. He didn't care because he still loved to play with it. Spot's friends, the cat and the bird, didn't like the smelly sock. They told him to throw it away, but Spot didn't want to.

A whole year went by, and the sock was now very, very smelly. Spot's friends could not play with him anymore because of the smell. Spot felt sad and lonely. One day, he decided to throw the smelly sock away. His friends were happy, and they all played together again. From that day on, Spot never played with smelly things again.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl called Emily. She was only three years old and she loved to explore the world around her. One day, Emily was in the living room and she saw a big seat. She did not know what the seat was for, so she asked her mom.

"Mom, what is this seat for?" Emily inquired.

"It is for you, Emily! You can sit in it to watch your favorite cartoon," her mom explained.

Emily was so excited and ran over to the seat. She jumped into the seat and started to watch her favorite cartoon. She had so much fun and sat in the seat for a whole zero minutes! After that, Emily said goodbye to the seat and went to do something else. 

The end.

One day, a soldier was walking in the forest. He was tired and hungry. He saw a big apple tree with yummy apples. He tried to get one, but they were too high. He jumped and jumped, but he could not reach them.

A little boy saw the soldier. The boy wanted to help. He had a long stick. The boy used the stick to get an apple. The soldier was happy. He took a bite of the yummy apple.

"Thank you, little boy," the soldier said. The boy smiled. They became friends. They walked together and found more yummy things to eat. The soldier was not hungry anymore. They were both happy.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. Tom wants to go on the slide. Anna is scared.

"Come on, Anna, it is fun!" Tom says.

"No, Tom, it is too high!" Anna says.

Tom does not listen. He runs to the slide. He climbs up the ladder. He sits on the slide. He smiles at Anna.

"Look, Anna, I am brave!" Tom says.

But then, he sees a big dog. The dog is barking. The dog is running to the slide. Tom is afraid of dogs. He panics. He screams.

"Help, Anna, help!" Tom says.

But Anna does not hear him. Anna is deaf. She can not hear Tom. She can not hear the dog. She only sees Tom's face. He looks scared. She wonders why.

She runs to the slide. She sees the dog. She is not afraid of dogs. She likes dogs. She waves at the dog. The dog stops barking. The dog wags its tail. The dog likes Anna.

"Hi, dog, what is your name?" Anna says.

The dog licks Anna's hand. Anna pets the dog. She smiles.

Tom sees Anna and the dog. He is confused. He slides down the slide. He lands on the ground. He trips. He falls. He hurts his knee. He cries.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom says.

Anna hears Tom. She can read his lips. She sees his tears. She runs to Tom. She hugs him.

"I am sorry, Tom, are you okay?" Anna says.

Tom stops crying. He looks at Anna. He looks at the dog. He feels silly.

"I am okay, Anna, thank you," Tom says.

He pets the dog. The dog licks his face. He smiles.

"Hi, dog, you are nice," Tom says.

Anna smiles too. She is happy. She is proud of Tom.

"Tom, you are brave too," Anna says.

They are friends. They are happy. They play with the dog. They forget the slide. They forget the trip. They have fun.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Mary and Tom. Mary was very thoughtful and always tried to do nice things for Tom. One day Mary made Tom a special waffle for breakfast. Tom was so happy! He couldn't believe it! He smiled and thanked his friend.

From then on, every Saturday morning Mary would make Tom a waffle for breakfast. Tom always thought it was so thoughtful of her.

One Saturday morning Tom decided to surprise Mary by making breakfast for her. He made a delicious waffle! Mary was so surprised. She smiled and thanked Tom for being so thoughtful and for believing in their friendship. 

Tom and Mary enjoyed the waffles and their time together. They believed that their friendship would last forever.

Once upon a time there was a pretty house. Inside the house was a special room that was in the attic. It was a place for special things. One day, when the family was napping, something magical appeared.

The family had never seen anything so special and so strange. It was a sparkly, floating creature. It looked like a fairy and glowed in the dark. It had wings that made it look like it was swimming through the air.

The family was amazed. They wanted to see the creature up close. So they all ran up to the attic. But when they arrived, the fairy was gone.

The family thought they were dreaming. But then something appeared at the window. It was the fairy!

The beautiful creature flew in to the room and hugged the family. They were so happy that they wanted to keep the fairy forever.

The end.

Jill was on a special trip. She couldn't wait to explore and find new things. Jill saw something that was very exciting and unusual! 

It was something called yoga. She had never seen anything like it before. She wanted to learn more about it. 

Jill decided to try it and so she joined a warm room with lots of people. They all smiled and made her feel welcome. Everyone was doing the same poses and breathing in a focused way. 

Jill felt scares at first but with the help of her friends, she started to feel more relaxed. It was a warm experience and she felt the energy of the group. 

Jill came away from the experience with a smile on her face. She had found something special and new. She would always remember this day and the amazing thing she had found.

Once upon a time there was a little fish. He wanted to go for a swim but it was very hot outside. He looked around and saw a fan. He went over to the fan and it blew cool air. He was so happy! He jumped into the water and started to swim very slowly. He was having so much fun. He swam around and around and splashed around. He was laughing and feeling so happy. He swam until he was tired and the sun went down. He swam back to his home and said goodnight. He was so glad he found the fan which made his swim so much fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and go camping with her family. One day, her family set up a tent in the backyard for her to play in. 

Lily's little brother, Max, came outside and saw the tent. "I want to play in the tent too," he said. But Lily didn't want to share. "No, this is my tent," she said. 

Max got frustrated and started to cry. Lily felt bad and said, "Okay, you can come in my tent too." But then Max started to tease her by knocking down the pillows and blankets. Lily got upset and said, "Stop teasing me!" 

Their mom heard the commotion and came outside. She helped them work out their conflict and they all played together in the tent. They had so much fun that they even decided to sleep outside in the tent that night.

Once upon a time, there was a black zoo. It had lots of animals and it belonged to everyone in the town. Everyone could go to the zoo and visit all the animals.

One day, the people of the town wanted to bring a new animal to the zoo. So they put up a sign asking for help. Everyone looked but they couldn't find a new animal. 

Just as they were about to give up, a brand new, black zebra flew into town! Everyone was so excited and they hugged the zebra and gave it a big name: Zebby!

Zebby quickly became the pride of the zoo. Everyone loved watching Zebby running around the zoo and playing with all the other animals. From then on, everyone agreed that the black zoo would always own Zebby, and everyone in the town would take care of it forever!

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird had a bright yellow chest and loved to fly in the sky. One day, the bird saw a big plane zooming by and wanted to try it too. 

The bird flew up to the plane and tried to land on it. But the plane was too fast and the bird hit its chest on the plane's wing. The bird fell down to the ground and hurt itself badly. 

The other birds tried to help, but it was too late. The little bird's chest stopped moving and it went to sleep forever. The other birds were sad and missed their friend very much. They learned that it's not always safe to zoom around without being careful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily wanted to play with her favorite toy, but it was stuck under the bed. She tried to reach it, but she couldn't. She felt frustrated because she really wanted to play with it.

Lily's mom came into the room and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her that she couldn't get her toy. Her mom said she would help her and asked Lily to remove the pillows from the bed. They worked together and finally got the toy.

Later that day, Lily's grandma came to visit. She brought some cookies and they all sat down to eat them. Lily was so happy to see her grandma and they had a nice chat. After the visit, Lily hugged her grandma and said goodbye. She couldn't wait for her next visit.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong bear. The bear wanted to try some oat, but his friend the fox wanted to resist. The bear was very brave, but the fox was clever and brilliant.

The fox said to the bear, "Let's not eat oat. It's not nice!" But the bear was determined. He said "I won't resist! I will try the oat!"

So the fox knew he could not stop the bear. With a tiny bit of fear, he replied "Okay, but you might be sorry!"

The bear ate the oat and it was delicious. But suddenly, he started to feel very sick. He could not move, he was in so much pain. The fox was sad, he knew he was right to resist.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the big blue sea. One day, Nemo saw a shiny purse at the bottom of the sea. He was curious and wanted to know what was inside the purse. So, he got ready and took a deep breath. He dived into the water and swam towards the purse. When he reached the purse, he opened it and found a shiny pearl. Nemo was so happy and swam back to his home with the pearl. From that day on, Nemo would dive into the sea every day, looking for more treasures.

One day, Jack and his mom decided to visit a big park. The park was enormous, with lots of tall trees and lots of other children running around to play.

Jack's mom said, "Look at how big this park is, Jack! Shall we explore?"

Jack said, "Yes please!"

So they started walking through the park. After a while, they came to a big cross. It was made of wood and it was enormous.

Jack said, "Mommy, what's that big cross?"

Mom said, "That's a cross. It is a sign for people to remember that Jesus died for us and loves us very much."

Jack was very surprised. He said, "That's amazing! Thank you for showing me this."

Then they spent some more time playing in the park. It was a wonderful day!

Once upon a time, there was a small hippo. He loved to play in the sunshine. Every day, he would search for special things to play with.

One day, he found a delicate flower. He wanted to play with it gently. He touched the flower very carefully and it sparkled in the sun. The little hippo was so happy!

He kept playing with the flower all day. But as the sun went down, it was time for him to go home. He put the flower in the grass and said goodbye.

He has never forgotten the delicate little flower. And he still loves to play in the sunshine!

Once upon a time, there was a cute little puppy named Max. Max loved to play with his toys and run around in the yard. One day, Max's owner asked him to look for a switch in the kitchen. Max didn't know what a switch was, so his owner showed him. A switch is a little button that turns the lights on and off. Max thought it was very interesting! 

Max's owner asked him to press the switch to turn on the lights. Max pressed the switch with his cute little paw and the lights turned on! Max was so happy that he wagged his tail. From that day on, Max loved to play with switches and turn the lights on and off. He even found a new toy - a switch that he could press over and over again. Max was a very happy puppy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little girl. She was so curious about the world that everyday she would open the door to explore a new place. She found many wonderful things on her journey as she opened each door.

One day she opened a door and saw a huge garden full of colorful flowers. It was the most beautiful thing she had ever seen. She opened more doors and found a huge lake. It was sparkling in the sunshine. She opened another door and found a magical forest. She even saw a baby squirrel nestled among the trees.

The little girl opened the last door and was amazed to see a whole new world! It was a magical kingdom with beautiful castles, a bustling market and delicious smelling food stalls. She couldn't wait to explore this wonderful new place.

The girl explored this new world until it was late, and she had to go home. But she was happy and content, for she had opened a world of beautiful thing that day.

Once upon a time, there was a polite tiger. He lived in a big forest with lots of trees and animals. One day, the tiger got very dirty from playing in the mud. He decided to clean himself in the river. He splashed and played in the water until he was clean again. After that, he went back to his home in the forest feeling happy and fresh. The other animals were amazed to see how clean and shiny the tiger looked. From that day on, the tiger made sure to stay clean and tidy.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the kitchen. They have a big bowl, a spoon, and some flour. They want to make a cake.

"Let's stir the flour," Anna says. She holds the spoon and moves it around the bowl. The flour makes a cloud of white dust.

"Stir, stir, stir," Ben says. He helps Anna with the spoon. They laugh and cough.

Mom comes in the kitchen. She sees the mess. She is not happy.

"What are you doing?" she asks. She looks at the bowl, the spoon, and the flour.

"We are making a cake," Anna says.

"A cake?" Mom says. "Do you know how to make a cake?"

Anna and Ben shake their heads. They do not know.

Mom smiles. She has an idea.

"Let's make a quiz," she says. "I will ask you some questions. If you answer right, you can help me make a real cake. If you answer wrong, you have to clean up the mess. Do you want to play?"

Anna and Ben nod. They want to play.

"OK," Mom says. "First question: What do you need to add to the flour to make a cake?"

Anna and Ben think hard. They remember what they saw in the book.

"Eggs!" they say together.

"Very good," Mom says. "You are right. You can add some eggs to the bowl. Next question: What do you need to make the cake sweet?"

Anna and Ben think again. They remember what they like to eat.

"Sugar!" they say together.

"Very good," Mom says. "You are right. You can add some sugar to the bowl. Last question: How long do you need to bake the cake in the oven?"

Anna and Ben look at each other. They do not know. They guess.

"Five minutes?" Anna says.

"Ten minutes?" Ben says.

Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, that is too short. You need to bake the cake for a long time. Maybe thirty minutes or more. You are wrong. You have to clean up the mess."

Anna and Ben make a sad face. They do not like to clean up.

"Can we still have some cake?" they ask.

Mom nods. She says, "Yes, you can have some cake. But only after you clean up. And only if you say please and thank you."

Anna and Ben say, "Please and thank you." They start to clean up. They hope the cake will be yummy. They are still friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Alice. She was three years old and very obedient. 
One day, her parents took her to the beach. As they strolled along the shore, Alice spotted something shiny in the sand. She ran over to a spot and started to dig. 
She pulled out a silver key! She jumped up and down and shouted, "I've found a key!". 
Her parents laughed and asked her what she thought the key unlocked. 
Alice considered this and frowned. She then smiled and said, "Maybe it unlocks an adventure!" 
Her parents smiled and hugged her. They then all started out together, determined to discover the secret of the silver key.

Once there was a boy named Max. He was 3 years old and he loved to explore. One day, he decided to go for a walk. As he walked, he heard something very loud. He looked around and saw a tall bridge. He was so excited to see it. 

Max tried to reach it but it was too tall. He wanted to see what was on the other side of the bridge. Then he had an idea. He ran as fast as he could. He was so happy when he made it to the bridge.

Max looked at the bridge and wondered what was on the other side. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise coming from the bridge. It was a train! Max was so excited to see it. 

The bridge was very tall and strong and it crossed the river. Max ran across the bridge and saw what was on the other side of the bridge. It was a beautiful view of the town. Max was so happy to have explored the tall bridge.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She had a toy cell. It was her favorite toy. She played with it all the time. One day, her friend, Tim, came to play with her. Tim saw the cell and wanted to play with it too.

"Can you lend me your cell?" Tim asked Amy. Amy thought for a moment and said, "Yes, but you have to be nice to it." Tim promised to be nice, and Amy lent him her toy cell.

Tim played with the cell, but he was rude. He threw it and hit it. Amy saw this and felt sad. She knew she should not have lent her toy cell to Tim.

Amy went to Tim and said, "You are not nice to my cell. Give it back, please." Tim felt bad and gave the cell back to Amy. He said sorry for being rude. Amy forgave him, and they played with other toys.

From that day on, Tim learned to be nice to his friends' toys. Amy and Tim played happily ever after, and Amy knew that she should only lend her toys to friends who would be nice to them.

One day, John was playing outside in the rain. He splashed in puddles and kicked up mud. He was having lots of fun, and was almost completely soaked.

He went inside to tell his mom. "Mom, I'm ready to go play again," he said.

"Not so fast, John," said Mom. She pointed to John's muscles. "You have to dry off first before you go back out there, otherwise you'll catch a cold."
