John sighed. He didn't want to wait, but he knew his mom was right. He got ready and changed out of his wet clothes. He waited until the rain had stopped before going back outside.

When he stepped outside again, the sun was out and the sky was blue. John was so excited that he ran full speed and laughed with joy. He was happy he'd listened to his mom, and he'd stopped to get ready for the adventure ahead.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play the guitar, but his guitar was small. He wished he had a huge guitar to play with. 

One day, Tim went to the music store with his mom. He saw a huge guitar and said, "Mom, I want that guitar. It's huge!" 

His mom said, "We can't afford it, Tim. But we can support you by saving up for a bigger guitar." 

Tim was sad, but he practiced on his small guitar every day. He knew that one day he would have a huge guitar to play. 

Years later, Tim became a famous musician. He played his huge guitar on stage and remembered the support his mom gave him when he was just a little boy with a small guitar.

Once upon a time, there were two small boys, Jack and Sam. They were playing with furniture in their room. Then Sam found a big, long string. He held it and said "Let's tie this string around the furniture!"

Jack said "That's stupid! We can't tie it around the furniture".

But Sam didn't listen. He said "I know what I'm doing", and he started tying the string around the furniture.

But Sam kept tying the string until he was done.

Finally, Jack said "See, I told you it was a stupid idea". 

But it was too late. The string was tied around the furniture and there was no way to untie it.

The two boys had to learn their lesson that not all ideas work out.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah loved to explore the tidy forest near her home. She would spend hours exploring the different trees and collecting cute little rocks.

Once there was a bee named Benny. Benny was very obedient and always listened to his parents.

Benny landed on the fork and said, â€œHi there! Whatâ€™s your name?â€ The fork didnâ€™t answer.

Sara and Ben like to play outside. But today, the sky is gray and the rain is falling. Sara and Ben are sad. They want to have fun.

They look for a place to play. They see a big tree. The tree has many leaves. The leaves keep the rain away. Sara and Ben run to the tree. They find a hole under the tree. The hole is hidden by the roots. Sara and Ben crawl into the hole.

The rain stops. The sun comes out. Sara and Ben hear their mom calling. They crawl out of the hole. They run to their mom. They hug her and tell her about their adventure. Their mom smiles and listens. She is glad they had fun. She is glad they are safe. She is glad they are her children.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy loved to explore new places. She wanted to go on an exciting adventure. One day, she had an idea. She would build a secret sign so that only she and her friends would know where to go.

In the end, the secret sign worked! Lucy and her friends had a wonderful time exploring and discovering new places. Lucy was so proud that she had such a great idea. She now knew that if she ever needed to have another adventure, she would be safe with her secret sign.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to draw on the wide blackboard in her classroom. One day, Lily's teacher asked her to come up to the front and draw a picture for the class. Lily was so excited to enter the front of the room and draw her picture.

But as she was drawing, she accidentally broke the blackboard. The teacher was very upset and Lily felt very sad. She knew she had made a big mistake and didn't know how to fix it. Lily had to say sorry and go home without finishing her picture. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily was walking down the hall when she saw her big sister Emma. Emma was being bossy and telling Lily what to do.

Lily didn't like it when Emma was bossy. She wanted to play by herself. So, Lily decided to go to her room and play with her toys. She looked at her stuffed animals and picked out her favorite bear. She hugged the bear and felt happy.

Later, Lily went back to the hall and saw Emma again. This time, Emma wasn't being bossy. She asked Lily if she wanted to play together. Lily smiled and said yes. They played together and had lots of fun. The end.

One day, a small girl was walking through her garden. She saw a white oak tree standing tall and strong in the middle. She stopped and looked up at it in wonder.

The girl wanted to climb it so she carefully scaled the tree and soon found herself perched in a seat high up in the white oak. She was so happy with the view she had, she almost didn't want to come down!

But eventually, the girl tired and had to go. She climbed down carefully, never forgetting the wonderful white oak and the seat she sat in. From then on, she would visit the tree every day and be happy.

One day, a normal boy was outside playing in his garden. He saw a witch in his garden and he was scared. He wanted the witch to go away. He closed his eyes and wished for her to be gone. When he opened his eyes, she was still standing there. He got angry. He ran towards the witch and kicked her with all his might. She went flying away and landed in a nearby field. The boy was so happy. He smiled and went back to playing. He had saved his garden from the witch! He was proud of himself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, Lily and her friend Timmy were playing in the park when suddenly they heard a loud noise. "What was that?" asked Lily. "It's thunder," said Timmy. 

Lily looked up at the sky and saw dark clouds appearing. "It looks like it's going to rain," she said. "We should go home." 

As they were walking back, they saw a messy pile of leaves on the ground. "Let's jump in it!" said Timmy. "No, we shouldn't," said Lily. "It's too messy and we might get dirty." 

When they finally got home, Lily's mom asked, "Did you have fun playing outside?" "Yes," said Lily. "But we heard thunder and saw dark clouds appearing. And we saw a messy pile of leaves, but we didn't jump in it." "That's good," said her mom. "You don't want to get too messy before dinner."

Once upon a time, there was a little infant named Tim. He liked to play with his toys and watch the birds outside his window. Tim had a big, soft teddy bear that he loved very much.

One day, Tim's teddy bear was sad. Tim did not know why his teddy bear was sad. He tried to make his teddy bear happy by giving it a hug and a kiss.

Tim decided to take his sad teddy bear outside to watch the birds with him. They sat under a big tree and watched the birds sing and fly. Soon, the teddy bear was not sad anymore. Tim and his teddy bear were very happy watching the birds together.

One day, the mommy decided to take her three-year-old daughter to the park. When they arrived, the little girl was so excited. She couldn't wait to explore the grass, climb the trees, and run around. 

Mommy reminded her daughter not to go too far. Then she gave her a treat. It was a little cardboard box filled with sugary sweets. The daughter loved it! She was so happy! 

After that, they went for a walk around the lake. It was so charming. Mommy showed her daughter some ducks and birds. She reminded her daughter not to make too much noise when she saw them. 

Finally, it was time to go home. Mommy gave her daughter one last treat. It was her favourite ice cream. As a special treat, mommy added a little extra topping. The daughter grinned from ear to ear. It was the perfect end to a lovely day.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who lived in a castle. She had a tiny empty room with no one in it. One day, a magical perfume arrived in the room, and an amazing light shone in the empty walls. 

The princess was so excited, and she danced with joy. The magical perfume had a special power, it could unite people together. Everywhere the princess went, she spread the magical perfume and the people started to unite. 

Soon the world was filled with love and happiness. The princess was very happy and thanked the magical perfume. But all of a sudden, the magic perfume disappeared, and the princess was sad. 

But then the kind people who had been united by the perfume remembered it, and the magical scent filled the air again. Everyone celebrated and hugged each other, rejoicing in being united by the magical perfume. 

The princess was so happy and thanked the perfume for uniting everyone together. From then on, the princess spread the magical perfume wherever she went, uniting people together in love and joy.

Once upon a time, in a far away land, there lived a purple tree. The tree was very special because it kept everyone safe. All the people of this land loved the purple tree and made it their mission to protect it. They kept it safe from bad storms, animals and anything that would harm it. Every day, they would check the tree to make sure it was healthy and happy. And sure enough, the tree stayed strong and purple for many years.

Then, one day, something unexpected happened: there was a huge fire near the purple tree. The people were so worried about their beloved tree that they quickly ran to protect it. They put out the fire and made sure the purple tree stayed unharmed.

From that day on, the purple tree was loved and cared for by all the people of the land. It kept them safe and made them happy. And that's the story of the special purple tree.

Anna loves her kitten, Lily. Lily is very shy and likes to hide under the bed. Anna wants to play with Lily, but Lily is scared of loud noises and big people.

One day, Anna has a good idea. She finds a big box and some paper. She makes a present for Lily. She wraps the paper around the box and puts a bow on top. She writes "To Lily, from Anna" on the paper.

She puts the present under the bed and waits for Lily to come out. She hopes Lily will like her surprise.

Lily sees the present and is curious. She sniffs the paper and hears something inside. She scratches the paper and makes a hole. She peeks inside and sees a soft blanket and a toy mouse.

Lily is happy and climbs into the box. She wraps herself in the blanket and plays with the toy mouse. She feels warm and safe.

Anna hears Lily purring and smiles. She crawls under the bed and joins Lily in the box. She hugs Lily and says "I love you, Lily. You are my best friend."

Lily licks Anna's face and says "Meow". She is not shy anymore. She loves Anna too. They are both happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They look the same, but they are not the same. Anna likes to play with dolls and dress up. Ben likes to play with cars and trucks. Sometimes they share, but sometimes they fight.

One day, Mommy gives them a big box. She says it is a surprise for both of them. Anna and Ben are excited. They open the box together. Inside, they see a big teddy bear. It is brown and soft and has a red bow.

"Wow, it is so cute!" Anna says. She hugs the teddy bear. "Can I have it, Mommy?"

Ben shrugs. He does not like teddy bears. He thinks they are for babies. He looks for something else in the box. But there is nothing else. Only the teddy bear.

"Sorry, Ben," Mommy says. "There is only one teddy bear. You have to share it with Anna."

Ben is not happy. He does not want to share the teddy bear. He wants a car or a truck. He thinks Mommy does not know what he likes. He pouts and crosses his arms.

"Come on, Ben," Anna says. "The teddy bear is nice. You can play with it too. We can take turns."

Ben shakes his head. He does not want to play with the teddy bear. He thinks it is boring. He walks away from the box. He goes to his room. He finds his old car. It is blue and shiny and has four wheels. He likes his car. He plays with it on the floor.

Anna feels sad. She does not understand why Ben does not like the teddy bear. She thinks it is fun. She wants to play with Ben. She follows him to his room. She knocks on the door.

"Ben, can I come in?" she asks.

Ben does not answer. He pretends he does not hear her. He keeps playing with his car.

Anna opens the door. She sees Ben on the floor. She sees his car. She smiles. She has an idea.

"Ben, look what I have," she says. She holds the teddy bear. "It is not just a teddy bear. It is a driver. He can drive your car. He can go fast and make noises. Vroom, vroom!"

Ben looks up. He sees the teddy bear. He sees Anna's smile. He feels curious. He wonders how the teddy bear can drive his car.

"Really?" he asks.

"Really," Anna says. She puts the teddy bear in the car. She pushes the car. The car and the teddy bear move on the floor. They make noises. Vroom, vroom!

Ben laughs. He thinks it is funny. He thinks it is cool. He reaches for the car. He wants to try it too.

"Can I play with you?" he asks.

"Of course," Anna says. She gives him the car. She gives him the teddy bear. "You can play with them. We can share."

Ben smiles. He thanks Anna. He hugs the teddy bear. He hugs his sister. He thinks she is nice. He thinks she is smart. He thinks they are twins. They are the same.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to help their dad, who was a farmer. They liked to feed the chickens, milk the cows, and pick the apples. But they also liked to be playful and have fun.

One day, they decided to mix some things in a big bowl. They took some flour, some eggs, some milk, and some sugar from the kitchen. They also took some apples from the basket. They poured and cracked and stirred and chopped. They made a big mess, but they did not care.

When their dad came home, he saw the twins smiling and the oven on. He asked, "What are you two doing?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They hugged their dad and said, "We love you, dad!"

Once there was a boy called Paul. Paul was three years old and had a very precious wallet. Every time Paul saw it he felt so grateful.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit who loved to chew. He would spend all day nibbling away on different things. One particular day, he found himself at a mill. He started to chew on some of the grain, but it was too spicy for him! He started to feel a burning sensation in his mouth and he was very uncomfortable.

He tried to find something else to chew on, but there was nothing around in the mill. He looked up and down the mill, a bit desperate, but he couldn't find anything. He was really stuck and he started to get worried. 

Suddenly, at the other end of the mill, he spotted some juicy apples! He hopped over as fast as he could and started to chomp on one of them. The apples were just enough to take away the spiciness from the grain and he felt much better. 

The little rabbit was very happy to have found something to chew on, and went happily on his way.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a purple scooter that she loved to ride. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her scooter. She saw her friend Timmy and said, "Hi Timmy! Do you want to play with me?" Timmy said, "Yes, I want to play with you and your scooter."

Maybe we can play again tomorrow."

Once upon a time there was a small girl who loved playing outside. Every day she would gaze around the grassy fields of her garden and imagine the adventures she created. One day, she got very excited when she spotted a lady bug. She looked closer, and saw that it was very big. She wanted to catch it and make it her pet. 

She crept closer, but the bug flew away. She watched it go sadly, wondering if she'd ever catch it.

Mom and Dad love Jack very much. They love to kiss his little lips. Jack loves to give kisses too, but with a different lip. His top lip is bigger than his bottom lip.

Once upon a time, a bald dad was cooking dinner at his house. He stood in the kitchen and cooked the dinner with a big smile on his face.

When he finished, the fence was strong and Dad was happy. He had a good dinner and a nice fence â€“ he was very pleased.

"Look, we have a red pair and a blue pair and a yellow pair and a green pair," Lily said.

"Look, we have orange cars now," she said. She put the carrot and the cheese on the floor next to her yellow car.

"Wow, you're right. We have orange cars now," he said.

They looked for something purple. They saw a grape on the salad. Lily picked it up and broke it in half. She gave one half to Tom and kept one half for herself.

"Hey, what are you doing with my salad?" It was Mom. She was not happy. She saw the broken carrot and cheese and grape on the floor. She saw the toy cars next to them.

"No more playing with food. No more playing with cars. Go to your room. Now," she said.

Lily and Tom were very sad. They had to go to their room. They had no more salad. They had no more cars. They had no more colors. They had no more fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog. It lived in a pond with a big pipe. Every day, the frog would jump around and play.

It was very dark and scary inside the pipe. The frog wanted to go back home but it was too scared. So, it stayed and kept exploring.

Suddenly, the frog saw some light at the end of the pipe. The frog was so excited that it started to jump around! It kept jumping until it reached the end of the pipe and the light.

The frog was so happy to be free! It thanked the moon for being so patient and helping it find its way out of the dark pipe. From then on, it was very careful when jumping around in the pipe and it never stayed too long.

Once upon a time, there was an owl who lived in a large tree. The owl flew around the forest gracefully, and one day he saw two raccoons talking by the tree. They seemed to be discussing something very important.

As the sun went down, the owl flew back to his tree and went to sleep. He felt very proud to have been able to help his new friends.

Today, Emily and Mommy were very excited. They were going to decorate the living room together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat blueberries because they were her favorite fruit. One day, Lily's mom recommended that they go for a walk in the park. Lily was excited and happy to go on a walk with her mom.

The End

Once there was a small cat named Fred. Fred wanted to be comfortable, but he had a lot of trouble. Every day, he would try to find somewhere he could be safe and comfortable, but it seemed no matter where he went, trouble followed him.

Once upon a time there was a boy who liked to wander in the woods.

He stumbled across a meadow with the prettiest flowers he had ever seen. He could have stayed there all day. 
But soon, the wind started to blow and the boy decided it was time to go. He bid farewell to the birds and the butterflies and gracefully wandered back to his home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toys and running around outside. One day, Timmy and his friends decided to play a game of tag. The game was very fun, but also a little dangerous because they were running around so much.

Suddenly, Timmy's friend Johnny demanded to be "it" in the game. Timmy didn't want to be "it" anymore, so he said no. Johnny got upset and started to cry. Timmy didn't want his friend to be sad, so he decided to let Johnny be "it" instead.

As the game continued, Timmy's team started to win. They were getting closer and closer to victory. Timmy was so excited to win the game, but he didn't want to be too loud and scare his friends. Finally, after a few more minutes of playing, Timmy's team won! They all cheered and hugged each other. Timmy felt very happy that he helped his team win the game.

Once there was a boy named Tom. He was a very honest boy who always wanted to find where he belonged. One day, Tom went outside and it was raining really hard. Tom was scared because he saw that water was everywhere, flooding his street! 

Tom was so scared and didn't know what to do. He wanted to find somewhere safe to belong. Luckily, Tom's mom heard his cries and ran outside to help. She told Tom to hold her hand and she took him to a nearby shelter.

The shelter was warm and dry. Tom felt like he belonged there. He soon made lots of friends who played with him all day. They were all honest and kind, just like Tom. They had lots of fun playing until the rain stopped, and then it was time to go home.

Tom felt so happy. He realized that even though he had been scared of the flood, his mom had been there to help him and he had found a place where he belonged.

Once upon a time, there was a rug. It was so soft and fluffy. It lived in a cozy house called David's. David was a very nice boy who was only three years old. 

David liked to play on the rug all day long. He loved to feel its softness against his skin. He often had very sweet dreams while he was laying on it. 

One day, he started talking to the rug. He asked it if it minded him playing on it all day. Surprisingly, the rug replied back to him! It said that it loved having David play on it and that it felt a special bond with him. 

David then thanked the rug and made a promise to play on it every day. He then hugged the rug and thanked it for taking care of him. 

From that day onwards, David and the rug were the best of friends. They played together all day long and shared many sweet moments. David was so glad that the rug didn't mind him playing on it.

Tom and Anna are having lunch with Mom and Dad. They have soup and bread and cheese. Tom likes soup, but Anna does not. She makes a face and pushes her bowl away.

"Anna, you have to eat your soup. It is good for you," Mom says.

"I don't like soup. It is hot and wet and yucky," Anna says.

"Look, Anna, you can use your fork to eat the cheese. Cheese is yummy and soft and yellow," Dad says. He shows Anna how to cut the cheese with his fork.

Anna looks at Dad's fork. It is big and shiny and has four teeth. She likes Dad's fork. She reaches for it, but Dad stops her.

"No, Anna, this is my fork. You have your own fork. It is smaller and easier for you to hold," Dad says. He gives Anna her fork. It is not as big or shiny as Dad's fork. It has three teeth and a pink handle.

Anna looks at her fork. She does not like her fork. It is small and dull and has a silly color. She throws her fork on the floor and cries.

"Anna, that is not nice. You have to pick up your fork and say sorry," Mom says.

Anna does not want to pick up her fork or say sorry. She is angry and sad. She wants a big fork like Dad's. She thinks it is not fair.

Tom looks at Anna. He feels sorry for her. He likes his sister, even when she is silly. He has an idea. He picks up his fork and gives it to Anna.

"Here, Anna, you can have my fork. It is big and shiny and has four teeth, like Dad's. I don't mind. I can use my spoon to eat my soup," Tom says.

Anna looks at Tom's fork. She is surprised and happy. She takes Tom's fork and smiles.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother. I am sorry I was mean," Anna says.

Mom and Dad look at Tom and Anna. They are proud and happy. They hug their children and praise them.

"That was very kind of you, Tom. You are a good sharer. And that was very nice of you, Anna. You are a good apologizer. We love you both very much," Mom and Dad say.

Tom and Anna hug Mom and Dad back. They love them too. They eat their lunch with their forks and spoons. They are a happy family.

Lily and Tom were adventurous kids. They liked to explore the world and find new things. One day, they saw a big hole in the ground. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's go in and see!" said Tom.

"OK, but be careful!" said Lily.

They climbed down the hole and saw a dark tunnel. They walked along the tunnel, holding hands. They saw shiny rocks and strange bugs. They heard a loud roar.

"What was that?" asked Lily.

"I don't know, but it sounds scary!" said Tom.

They wanted to go back, but they could not find the way. They were lost.

"Help! Help!" they shouted.

But no one heard them. They remained in the hole, alone and afraid. They never saw the world again.

One day, a chubby cat named Kitty went to the park. Kitty saw a swing and wanted to play on it. Kitty climbed on the swing and started to move back and forth. Kitty was very happy.

A little boy named Timmy saw Kitty on the swing. Timmy said, "Hi Kitty! Can I play on the swing too?" Kitty said, "Yes, Timmy! Let's play together!" So, Timmy and Kitty took turns on the swing. They had lots of fun.

After playing for a while, Kitty and Timmy were tired. They decided to settle down under a big tree. They sat and talked about their fun day at the park. Soon, they both fell asleep, dreaming of more fun days on the swing.

Once there was a girl named Kate. She was three years old and very nosy. One day, she wanted to help her mom with a new task. Her mom asked Kate to sit still and rest while she finished the task. 

Kate thought about the task her mom was doing, but she was getting bored. She decided to go find something to do. She looked around the house for something fun but couldn't find anything. 

Then, Kate saw her mom again. She was still working on the task and Kate wanted to help. But her mom shook her head and said she needed to rest. Kate sighed and went to find a comfy spot to relax.

Kate found her mom's chair and settled into it. She closed her eyes and soon her mom's nosy task was forgotten. Kate slept until her mom was finished. She woke up feeling much better and was ready to help with the next task!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. Jack loved to play baseball with his friends. They would throw the ball and hit it with a bat. Jack was very good at it and he always had fun.

One day, Jack was feeling upset. He didn't know why, but he just felt sad. His mom noticed and asked him what was wrong. Jack told her that he was feeling upset and didn't know why.

His mom gave him a big hug and said, "It's okay to feel upset sometimes. Let's go outside and play some baseball. That always makes you feel calm and happy." Jack smiled and went outside to play with his friends. Playing baseball made him forget about feeling upset and he had a lot of fun. Jack realized that he loved playing baseball and it always made him feel better.

One day, a little mole went for a walk. The mole was very humble and kind. He liked to help his friends. The sun was shining and the sky was blue. The mole was happy.

As the mole walked, he saw a big tree. A small bird was hanging on a branch. The bird looked sad. The mole asked the bird, "Why are you sad?" The bird said, "I lost my nest. I have no place to sleep."

The humble mole wanted to help his new friend. He said, "I can help you find your nest!" They looked high and low. They looked near and far. At last, they found the nest. It was hanging on a branch in another tree.

The bird was very happy. "Thank you, mole!" said the bird. "You are a good friend." The mole smiled. He was glad he could help. They played together all day. And from that day on, the mole and the bird were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was an old dove. The dove had many friends. One day, the dove's friends came to visit. They wanted to have a party. 

The dove said, "Let's set up the party outside!" 

The friends agreed and they set up the party. They had cake, balloons, and toys. 

One friend said, "This is the best party ever!" 

The old dove smiled and said, "I'm glad you all had fun." 

And they all lived happily ever after. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl whose name was Jen. One day, Jen decided she wanted to bake something delicious. She asked her mom if she could use her mom's copper baking pan.

"Mom," asked Jen, "Can I use your copper baking pan to bake something?"

"Yes," replied her mother, "but be careful. It is an expensive pan, so please be careful when you use it."

Jen agreed and then went to work baking something delicious. She was very careful and eventually the baking was done. Everything smelled and looked amazing. It was so delicious that everyone wanted to try!

The moral of the story is that it is important to take special care of expensive things. Jen was very careful using her mother's copper baking pan, and her mom was very grateful. Jen was pleased that she could make something delicious and also help take care of something valuable.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with a lot of trees. They wanted to discover what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Lily!" Ben said. "Maybe we can find a treasure or a secret cave!"

"OK, Ben!" Lily said. "But be careful. It looks dark and spooky over there."

They ran up the hill, holding hands. They heard a loud noise. It was the wind. It was blowing hard and making the trees shake and the leaves fly.

"Wow, look at the wind, Lily!" Ben said. "It's so strong and fast!"

Lily felt scared. She did not like the wind. It made her cold and it made her hair go in her eyes. She wanted to go back to the park.

"Ben, I don't like the wind," Lily said. "Can we go back, please?"

Ben looked at Lily. He saw that she was scared. He wanted to make her feel better.

"OK, Lily," Ben said. "We can go back. But first, let's do something fun. Let's make a kite!"

Ben found a stick and a plastic bag. He tied the bag to the stick with a string. He gave it to Lily.

"Here, Lily," Ben said. "This is a kite. You can hold it and let the wind lift it up. It will fly like a bird!"

Lily took the kite. She felt curious. She wanted to try it.

"Thank you, Ben," Lily said. "How do I make it fly?"

Ben showed her how to hold the string and run with the kite. They ran down the hill, laughing and shouting. The kite flew high in the sky, dancing with the wind.

Lily felt happy. She liked the kite. She liked the wind. She was not scared anymore.

She hugged Ben and said, "You are the best, Ben. You made me discover something new and fun. I love you."

Ben hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are the best, too. You made me discover something new and sweet."

Once upon a time, there was a poor monkey. The monkey lived in a big forest with lots of trees. The monkey had no friends and was very lonely. One day, the monkey saw a group of children playing outside the forest. The monkey wanted to play too, so it decided to go and say hello. 

When the monkey got closer, one of the children poked the monkey with a stick. The monkey was scared and ran back into the forest. The monkey felt sad and alone once again. The next day, the monkey saw the children again and decided to try and make friends. But unfortunately, the children poked the monkey again and this time, they didn't stop. 

The poor monkey was hurt and couldn't move. The children ran away and left the monkey alone. The monkey lay there, hurt and lonely, until it eventually passed away. From that day on, the children never saw the monkey again, and they never knew how much they hurt it.

Once there was a little girl named Mary. She was three years old and loved to have a cup of coffee with her mom every morning.

One morning, her mom said, "Mary, let's go for a stroll and pick some beans from the garden". Mary was so excited, she felt like she was on top of the world!

So they went out and started picking beans. Mary picked deep blue beans, and her mom picked small, red beans.

Suddenly, Mary heard a voice, "Hey! Don't pick those beans!" It was Uncle Joe, who owned the garden. He looked so angry, and shouted at them, "I told you not to mind my garden! Now get out of here!"

Mary and her mum were so scared, they quickly ran away. But no matter how fast they ran, they never forgot how angry Uncle Joe was.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom told her they were going to prepare a surprise for her dad's birthday. Lily was so excited! They went to the store to buy some ingredients to make a cake. 

When they got home, Lily's mom asked her to help prepare the cake batter. Lily poured the flour and sugar into a bowl and mixed it with a spoon. Then, they put the cake in the oven and waited patiently. 

While they waited, Lily's mom noticed a patch on Lily's shirt. It looked uncomfortable, so she helped Lily take it off and put on a new shirt. Finally, the cake was ready! They put candles on it and sang "Happy Birthday" to Lily's dad. He was so surprised and happy that he gave Lily and her mom big hugs. The end.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play pretend. Today, they are playing store. Tom is the seller and Lily is the buyer.

"Hello, welcome to my store!" Tom says. "What do you want to buy?"

"I want to buy a cake," Lily says. "A big, yummy cake."

"OK, I have a cake for you," Tom says. He takes a pillow and puts it on a plate. "This is a famous cake. It is very good and sweet."

"How much is it?" Lily asks.

"It is five dollars," Tom says.

Lily takes some paper and gives it to Tom. "Here is your money."

"Thank you," Tom says. He gives Lily the plate with the pillow. "Be careful, the cake is heavy. It has a lot of weight."

Lily tries to lift the plate, but it is too heavy for her. She drops it on the floor. The pillow falls off the plate and rolls away.

"Oh no!" Lily says. "My cake is gone!"

Tom laughs. "Don't worry, Lily. It is not a real cake. It is just a pillow. We can play again."

Lily smiles. "OK, Tom. You are a good seller. And I am a good buyer. We have fun playing store."

Once there was a tidy girl named Amy. She had never had a hair cut. One day, her family decided to take her to a barber for the first time. 

When she got to the barberâ€™s, she felt scared and started to weep. She did not want her hair cut. But her family was very kind and talked to her gently. They explained that the barber was nice and he was only going to make her hair look nice. 

Finally, Amy calmed down and let the barber cut her hair. He was very gentle and finished quickly. When Amy looked in the mirror she was very happy. Her hair looked so tidy and pretty. 

From that day on, Amy was never scared to go to the barber.

Once there was a guard who was feeling very anxious. He had an important job to do, which was to look after the park. But one day something unexpected happened. A big, green car came zooming into the park at top speed! The guard was terrified and ran to tell the mayor. 

The mayor was very worried and they quickly got out their fastest police car to try and capture the driver. The police car zoomed after the big, green car, but it was too fast. Eventually the car disappeared in the distance and the mayor was very sad.

The guard was very relieved that the car had gone and no harm had been done. He was also very thankful that he could get back to work and guard the park again. From then on, he was always ready and alert, and never let anything near the park go unnoticed.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Star. Star was three and loved helping the people in her family prepare dinners.

One day, Star asked her Mum what she was making for dinner. Mum said she was making a very tasty cake. Star was so excited!

"Can I help?" Star asked.

Mum said, "Yes of course, what would you like to do first?"

Star said, "I want to measure the ingredients, I can do that with the scale!"

Mum smiled, "That's a great idea," she said.

So Star got the scale out of the cupboard and started to measure everything she needed. She was so proud of herself for helping.

Soon the cake was in the oven, and it was just a few minutes until dinner was ready. Star could smell how tasty it was going to be, and she couldn't wait to sample a piece.

Once upon a time, there was a popular oven. It had lots of friends that joined it every day. One day, the oven asked all it's friends if they wanted to join in a special game. Everyone was so excited and each of them wanted to join.

The first friend was a spoon. She waved her arms and ran around the oven. The oven cheered and clapped. Next, a banana joined in. He hopped around in circles and everyone laughed. Then, a carrot jumped in and started to twirl. Finally, a lemon shyly joined the fun.

The oven was so happy. It was the most popular oven in the whole town! All the friends celebrated by dancing in circles around the oven. Everyone had lots of fun and joined in the game. The oven was very pleased. They all agreed to join the oven often for more fun!

Once upon a time there was a young girl who lived in a small house. One day she decided to go for a walk in the woods near her house. While she was walking, she saw a small door in the ground. She used all her strength to push it open and saw some stairs that led up to an attic.

She went up the stairs and when she entered the attic, she saw someone. He was dressed in all black and he looked like he was in a hurry. He spoke to the young girl, "You should not be here. Hurry, go back the way you came".

The young girl was scared and she quickly ran back the way she had come. But before she could get very far away, the man chasing her appeared. He was coming closer and closer. 

The young girl started to cry and she ran faster, but she couldn't outrun the man. He quickly caught up to her and grabbed her. 

The young girl was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly bear named Bubba. Bubba lived in the forest with his friends, the birds and the squirrels. One day, Bubba found a tube in the river. The tube was big and yellow and Bubba thought it would be fun to play with.

Bubba tried to fill the tube with water from the river, but it had a hole in it. The water kept coming out. Bubba was sad because he wanted to play with the tube. But then, his friend the squirrel came up with an idea. They found some leaves and put them inside the tube. The leaves filled up the hole and now Bubba could play with the tube all day long.

Bubba and his friends had so much fun playing with the tube. They rolled it down the hill and even used it as a slide. Bubba was happy that he found the tube and even happier that his friend helped him fix it. From that day on, Bubba and his friends always looked for things to fill the tube with and play with together.

Once there was a girl called Julie. She needed to use a needle, so she asked her mom if she could lend it to her. Her mom said yes and showed Julie the needle. It was a pale needle, very thin and shiny. 

Julie was excited to use it. She carefully grabbed it with her fingers and started to show her mom what she wanted to do. Julie used the needle to make some new beautiful clothes for her doll. 

When she was finished, she asked her mom to lend her some brightly coloured thread too. Her mom got some from the drawer and Julie used it to sew the clothes together.

When Julie was done she smiled, happy that she could make something so nice with the needle and thread her mom had lent her. She hugged her mom and thanked her for the lend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a new telephone. She loved it very much and carried it around everywhere. One day, she was so excited that she was running around and her telephone fell out of her pocket and she lost it. She cried and looked for it all over the place, but she just couldn't find it. She asked her mum to help her and then her mum called a new telephone for her.

The little girl was so happy to get the new telephone that she made sure to keep it safe with her this time. She kept it by her side all the time just to make sure she wouldn't lose it again. From that day onwards, she was careful to always keep her telephone safe.

Once upon a time, there was a very cheerful little sock. Every day, he would race around the house, bringing smiles and laughter with him wherever he went!

One day, he decided to go outside and play. He quickly skipped and jumped around the garden. But then his foot got very dirty, making the once happy and cheerful sock look sad.

Not wanting to stay dirty for long, the sock quickly ran back inside. There, he saw a big, soft cloth lying by the door. The sock smiled. He knew what to do!

So the sock grabbed the cloth and began to wipe his foot. The soft cloth's touch was just like magic; it made the sock's foot clean again!

Happy and cheerful once more, the sock thanked the cloth and went on his merry way, ready to bring smiles and laughter once again!

Mama and baby were in the car. They were going to the grocery. Mama was tired, but baby was excited. They drove to the grocery and Mama got out of the car with baby. They went into the grocery and baby saw lots of fun things.

Mama and baby walked around the store and picked out some food. Baby wanted lots of treats, but Mama said no. Mama and baby finished shopping and they went back to the car.

They drove home and Mama put away the groceries. Baby was tired from all the fun at the grocery, so Mama put him in bed. Mama tucked him in and kissed him goodnight. Baby fell asleep and Mama finished cleaning up the kitchen.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and toys, but she didn't like to share them with her friends. One day, Lily's mom gave her a beautiful bracelet to wear on her hand. Lily loved it so much that she didn't want to take it off, not even when she went to bed.

That night, Lily had a dream about a fairy who told her that if she didn't start sharing her toys, she would lose her pretty bracelet forever. The fairy also said that if she prayed and asked for forgiveness, she would be able to keep her bracelet and make new friends.

When Lily woke up, she remembered her dream and started to think about what the fairy had said. She realized that sharing was important and decided to invite her friends over to play with her toys. They had so much fun together, and Lily felt happy because she knew she had done the right thing. She also prayed before going to bed, thanking the fairy for her advice.

From that day on, Lily always shared her toys with her friends, and her bracelet stayed on her hand, reminding her of the lesson she had learned. She knew that praying and being kind to others was the best way to keep her pretty things and make new friends.

Once upon a time, there lived two friends, Jack and Jane. They always went to the park together to run around and have fun.

One day, as they were walking in the park, they saw a weird wink. They could not quite figure out what it was. Jack thought it was funny while Jane thought it was strange.

Jack: "Let's go closer and have a look," he said.

Jane was a bit scared but she followed Jack anyway. As they slowly passed by, the wink slowly moved away. It was so weird!

Jack and Jane ran back to tell their parents about the weird wink. It was the most exciting thing ever!

Their parents listened to them carefully and smiled. They were so proud of their children for being brave enough to pass by the weird wink. That was the end of their story!

Once upon a time, there was a honest chimney sweep who loved to store away his beloved tools. His tools were very important for his work, so he wanted to make sure he kept them all in one safe place. 

One day, he set off with his tools and headed for the nearest town. But soon after he left, he started to wonder - had he remembered to store everything away properly?

The chimney sweep returned home and looked around but he couldn't see his tools anywhere. He sighed and said to himself, "I must have forgotten to store away my tools!".

Suddenly, he heard a little voice. "Don't worry share, I stored everything away safely in my room!" It was the chimney sweep's three-year-old daughter! She had remembered to put all his tools away safely. 

The chimney sweep was overjoyed. He thanked his daughter for being so honest and for making sure his beloved tools were safe and sound. And from that day, the chimney sweep never forgot to store away his tools in the same place. The end.

Lila liked to make things with string. She had many colors of string in her box. She could make bracelets, necklaces, and pictures with string. She liked to show her things to her friends and family.

One day, she had an idea. She wanted to make something unusual with string. She took a long piece of green string and tied it to a stick. Then she took a short piece of red string and tied it to the green string. She made a loop with the red string. She had made a string bow.

She found a thin piece of wood and made it sharp at both ends. She tied a yellow string to it. She had made a string arrow. She was very proud of her string bow and arrow.

She went to the garden and looked for a target. She saw a big pumpkin. She put the arrow on the bow and pulled the string. She let go of the string and the arrow flew. It hit the pumpkin with a thud.

Lila was very happy. She had hit the pumpkin with her string arrow. She ran to the pumpkin and picked up her arrow. She saw her mom and dad watching her from the window. They smiled and clapped their hands. They applauded her for her unusual string bow and arrow. Lila waved at them and smiled. She felt very good. She loved to make things with string.

Little Jack was a bright and curious 3 year old. Every day he asked questions and explored the world around him.

Today, Jack and his mommy went to the post office. Jack was excited! He watched as mommy put letters in the mail. Jack loved to watch the post man take the letters away.

Once they were done mailing the letters, mommy and Jack went home. Jack noticed two soft little toes sticking out from under the couch. He quickly peeked under the couch and saw a kitten!

Jack was so happy that he had found a new playmate! The kitten's fur was soft and when it meowed Jack felt a little flutter in his tummy. He knew this would be a fun day! He and the kitten quickly became the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Alex. He wanted so much to eat some chocolate but his mom said he had to wait. Alex was very impatient. 

He asked his mom, "Can I have it now?" 

His mom said, "No, sweetheart. You need to work for it." 

So Alex worked very hard and waited. He put away his toys, brushed his teeth and ate all his dinner. At last, his mom gave him the chocolate he wanted.

He was so happy. He said to his mom, "Thanks for the chocolate!" 

His mom smiled and said, "You worked very hard for it. I'm glad you like it!"

Once upon a time there was a small boy called Jack. He had a neighbor called Bill. Jack and Bill didn't always get along as Bill could be quite grumpy. 

One day, Jack had a great idea. He was going to have a competition with Bill to see who could win! All the kids on the street were invited to join in the challenge.

Jack and Bill faced each other and each of them was given an orange. The challenge was to see who could squeeze the most juice out of their orange the fastest. 

The kids all cheered as Jack started to squeeze his orange with all of his might. Jack was squeezing so hard that the orange couldn't take it anymore and his orange exploded! 

"Hooray!" all of the kids cheered. Jack was declared the winner and Bill had to grumble and accept defeat. 

Afterwards when Jack went home, he grinned a big smile. He had won the challenge and was so proud of himself!

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was very obedient and always listened to his owner, a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and Spot went for a walk in the park. Suddenly, Spot saw a little bird in trouble. The bird had fallen from its nest and couldn't fly. Spot knew he had to rescue the bird quickly.

"Quick, Lily! Come see the bird," Spot barked. Lily came over and saw the bird. "Oh no! We have to help it," she said. Spot carefully picked up the bird in his mouth and brought it back to its nest. The bird's family was so happy to see their baby bird safe and sound.

"Good job, Spot! You are such a brave and helpful dog," Lily said. Spot wagged his tail happily. From that day on, Spot and Lily were known as the heroes of the park.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and his favorite toy was a red car. One day, Timmy's friend came over to play. 

"Wow, I like your car! Can I play with it?" asked Timmy's friend.

"Yes, you can play with it. But please be careful with it because it's my own car," replied Timmy.

Timmy's friend was very happy and played with the car for a while. Suddenly, he saw a flag on the floor. "Look, Timmy! What is this flag for?" he asked.

"That's my dad's flag. He is a dependable soldier and he always carries it with him," Timmy explained.

Timmy and his friend played together for a long time and had a lot of fun. When it was time for his friend to go home, Timmy said, "Thank you for playing with me and taking care of my own car. Let's play again soon!"

Tom and Mia are playing with their toys in the living room. Tom has a big truck and Mia has a doll. They are having fun, but they are also making a lot of noise.

"Tom, Mia, it's time to clean up!" Mom calls from the kitchen. "You have a task to do before dinner."

Tom and Mia groan. They don't want to stop playing. They are grumpy.

"Why do we have to clean up?" Tom asks.

"Because it's your job to keep your toys tidy," Mom says. "And because I have a surprise for you."

"A surprise?" Mia says. "What is it?"

Mom smiles. "You'll see. But first, you have to finish your task."

Tom and Mia look at each other. They are curious. They wonder what the surprise is. Maybe it's a new toy, or a cake, or a movie.

They decide to clean up their toys quickly. They put them in their boxes and baskets. They help each other. They are not grumpy anymore.

"Good job, Tom and Mia!" Mom says. "You did your task very well. Now, are you ready for your surprise?"

"Yes, yes, yes!" Tom and Mia say.

Mom leads them to the backyard. She covers their eyes with her hands. She walks them to a big box. She lets go of their eyes.

"Surprise!" She says. "Reveal!"

Tom and Mia open their eyes. They gasp. They see a big tent. It has pillows, blankets, books, and lanterns inside. It looks cozy and fun.

"A tent!" Tom says. "Wow!"

"A campout!" Mia says. "Yay!"

Mom hugs them. "Do you like it?" She asks.

"We love it!" Tom and Mia say. "Thank you, Mom!"

They run to the tent. They want to explore it. They are happy.

Mom smiles. She is happy too. She did a good job. She made a surprise for her kids. She made them happy.

Once upon a time, there was a strong boy named Tom. He liked to play outside with his friends. One day, while he was playing, he saw a big tree. Tom wanted to climb the tree, so he did.

As he climbed the tree, he met a magic bird. The magic bird said, "I can give you one wish, but you must help me." The bird had lost its nest and needed a new one. Tom said, "I will help you find your nest."

Tom and the magic bird looked high and low for the nest. They had a hard time finding it. But they did not give up. They kept looking until they found it. The bird was very happy and said, "Thank you, Tom. What is your wish?"

Tom thought for a moment and said, "I want to be strong so I can help my friends." The magic bird granted his wish. From that day on, Tom was the strongest boy in the town. He helped his friends and everyone was happy.

One morning, Emily and her mom went outside to play. The sky was bright and sunny. It was pleasant outside.

Mom looked down at Emily and said, â€œLetâ€™s share some bubbles. Take these bubble wands and try to make some big bubbles in the air.â€ So, Emily and her mom each had a bubble wand and tried to make the biggest bubbles they could.

They had lots of fun until suddenly, a flood came and knocked over the bubbles. Emily was sad and cried for a little bit, but Mom said, â€œDonâ€™t worry Emily, maybe the bright sun will come back and help us make more bubbles.â€

So, they waited and watched the sky, hoping for a sign from the sun. Finally, after a few moments the sun peeped out from the clouds and the sky was bright once again. As Emily and her mom shared their happy feelings, little bubbles started to form in the air. They cheered and laughed, thankful for the bright sun's help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a little boy who was sad. 

Lily went over to the boy and asked him what was wrong. He said he lost his gold toy car and couldn't find it. Lily wanted to help the boy, so she looked around the park with him. They searched high and low, but they couldn't find the gold car. 

Lily didn't want the boy to be sad anymore, so she gently hugged him and said she would support him in finding the car. They searched some more and finally found the gold car under a tree. The little boy was so happy and gave Lily a big hug. From that day on, they became good friends and played together at the park every day.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy cow called Daisy. Daisy was always getting herself into all sorts of trouble. One day she found a box of powder at the end of a rainbow. She sniffed the powder and it made her sneeze.

Suddenly, Daisy's feet began to get bigger and bigger and bigger. Soon, Daisy was so big she could not even fit through the doorway.

Laughing, Daisy shouted to her friends, â€œLook, look at me now!"

But her friend, a tiny mouse, said, "Oh no, what have you done?"

Daisy was puzzled and replied, "I don't know, I only sniffed the powder!"

The mouse said, "Well I think you must have eaten some of the powder, it appears to have caused you to increase in size!"

Daisy quickly ran back to the end of the rainbow and put the box of powder away. She was very careful never to touch it again. 

And so, Daisy stayed the perfect size, living happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was an old house. It was so old that it had leaks in the roof when it rained. One day, a little girl saw the leaks and told her mommy. Her mommy replied, "We should fix it soon." 

The little girl wanted to help, so she got her toy hammer and tried to fix the leak herself. But it was too big for her to fix. She asked her mommy for help and her mommy replied, "Let's call a repairman to fix it."

The repairman came and fixed the leak. The little girl was happy that the old house was fixed. She thanked the repairman and he replied, "You're welcome!"

Tommy loves rockets. He has many rockets in his room. He plays with them every day. He makes them fly and zoom and blast off. He pretends he is an astronaut.

One day, Tommy gets a new rocket for his birthday. It is big and shiny and red. It has a button that makes it light up and make noises. Tommy is very happy. He says, "Thank you, Mommy and Daddy! This is the best rocket ever!"

He runs to his room to play with his new rocket. He puts it on his bed and presses the button. The rocket lights up and makes noises. Tommy smiles and claps. He says, "Wow, this is so cool!"

But then, something bad happens. The rocket falls off the bed and hits the floor. It breaks into pieces. The light and the noise stop. Tommy is very sad. He says, "Oh no, my new rocket! It is broken!"

He picks up the pieces and tries to fix them. But he can't. He starts to cry. He says, "I want my new rocket back! It was so fun!"

Mommy and Daddy hear Tommy cry. They come to his room and see the broken rocket. They hug Tommy and say, "We are sorry, Tommy. Your new rocket was an accident. It is not your fault."

They help Tommy clean up the pieces. They say, "We can get you another rocket, Tommy. Or maybe you can play with your other rockets. You have many rockets, Tommy. You are still an astronaut."

Tommy stops crying. He says, "Thank you, Mommy and Daddy. You are right. I have many rockets. I am still an astronaut."

He smiles and hugs them. He says, "I love you, Mommy and Daddy. And I love rockets."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy went to the park with his mom and dad. They sat on a bench and watched the other kids play. It was a cool day, so Timmy wore his jacket. 

After a while, Timmy's mom said it was time to go home. Timmy had a surprise for his dad, so he ran ahead to their car. When they got to the car, Timmy asked his dad to help him unpack his backpack. 

Inside the backpack, there was a toy car that Timmy wanted to show his dad. His dad thought it was really cool and they played with it together. Timmy was so happy to share his surprise with his dad.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim wanted to build something special for his mom's birthday. He thought and thought about what to make. Then, he had an idea! He would build a big present for her.

Tim was worried. He didn't know if he could build the present all by himself. He asked his dad for help. Together, they found some big boxes, pretty paper, and a big bow. They worked together to make the present look nice.

When Tim's mom saw the present, she was so happy! She gave Tim a big hug and thanked him for the special gift. Tim felt proud that he could build something so nice for his mom. And he was no longer worried.

Billy was a curious three year old. He liked going for a jog in the park every day. One day, he was jogging around the lake, when he spotted something strange. It was a big net, all tangled up. He went closer to take a look.

Billy was curious about the net and he accidentally stepped in it. He stumbled, but then felt something soft. Something fluffy was in the net! Billy was puzzled and decided to untangle the net.

When he opened the net, he found out it was full of little birds. They were scared and flapping their wings. Billy smiled and slowly freed all the birds from the net. They were grateful and happily flew away.

Billy finished his jog and went home, feeling proud that he had helped the birds. He wouldn't forget his curious adventure.

Jimmy saw a strong man in the park. The strong man was playing a flute. Jimmy liked the sound of the flute. He wanted to try it too.

The man gave Jimmy the flute. Jimmy tried to play it but it was too hard. The strong man showed Jimmy how to move his fingers to make music with the flute. Jimmy practiced and practiced until he could make music too.
 
Jimmy was very happy. Every time he went to the park he would see the strong man and play the flute with him. They made lots of beautiful music together.

Once there was a little girl called Milly. Milly was very eager to learn something new. She decided to learn how to shake her body. She began to move around in her bedroom, shaking her arms and legs. Then she began to shake her head. She shook it very fast, up and down. Milly was so excited that she forgot to close her mouth. Her little teeth began to make a funny noise called chatter. Milly couldnâ€™t stop smiling. When she finished her dance, she felt very proud of herself. Milly was eager to show her friends her new dance. She canâ€™t wait to start shaking her body again!

Robbie was a little bunny. He was feeling hungry so he hopped through the garden, looking for something to eat. He found a sweet carrot! He hopped closer and sniffed it. It smelled so good.

Robbie asked the carrot, "Are you yummy?"

The carrot didn't answer but Robbie was sure it was yummy. He nibbled a tiny bit. It tasted so sweet that Robbie wanted to eat the whole thing. He asked the carrot, "Can I eat the whole thing?"

The carrot was silent, so Robbie decided to eat it. He ate the whole carrot and felt very satisfied. He hopped away, feeling happy he had asked the carrot his question so he could enjoy a sweet snack.

Once there was a boy who loved to talk. He talked all the time and his family called him chatty. One day he went to the store to buy a crayon. He was really busy running around the store, looking for just the right one. He picked up a bright red crayon and was so excited that he immediately started to talk about it. He talked about how pretty the color was, and what he was going to draw with it. 

When he got home he set up his paper and crayon. He drew a picture of his house but it was a bit wobbly. He showed his Mom and she said that was ok. She was proud of him for being so creative with just a crayon. He smiled because he was proud of himself too. 

He used the crayon to make more pictures. Sometimes he used other colors too. But he always loved the bright red one because it always made him feel so happy and talkative.

Lisa loves to skip. She skips in the park, she skips in the school, she skips in the mall. She likes to skip because it makes her happy and fast. She can skip faster than her brother Tom, who likes to run.

One day, Lisa and Tom go to the mall with their mom. Mom says they can watch a movie. Lisa is excited. She likes movies. She skips to the movie place. Tom runs after her. Mom walks behind them.

At the movie place, they see a big sign. It says "Modern Popcorn". Lisa and Tom wonder what that means. They ask mom. Mom says it is a new kind of popcorn. It has different colors and flavors. It sounds fun. Mom buys some modern popcorn for them to share.

They go inside the movie room. It is dark and big. They find their seats. Mom gives them the popcorn. Lisa and Tom look at it. It is very pretty. It has red, blue, green, yellow, and pink pieces. They smell good too. They taste them. They are sweet and salty and sour and spicy and fruity. They are yummy. Lisa and Tom like modern popcorn.

They watch the movie. It is funny and scary and sad and happy. They laugh and scream and cry and smile. They eat their popcorn. They skip some pieces to each other. They have fun. They love movies and modern popcorn. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy cat named Tom. Tom liked to look at everything and everyone. He would look at his friends, the birds, and the fish in the pond.

One day, Tom saw a dish with yummy food. He wanted to eat the food, but it was not his dish. Tom did not care, he was too nosy. He went to the dish and started to eat the food.

Suddenly, a big dog named Max came. Max saw Tom eating from the dish. Max did not like that. Max walked up to Tom and gave him a big slap. Tom learned his lesson and never ate from someone else's dish again.

One day, Mama took her little boy to the park. He felt so glad! Everywhere he looked he saw so many things to explore. He played on the swings and ran around the grass.

When he got tired, Mama brought out a special lunch for him. It was delicious! He ate it all up and was so content.

Before they left, Mama took her boy for a special shower. The water was warm and it felt so nice. He played and splashed and was so happy.

Finally, after he was fed and washed, they said goodbye to the park. Mama was glad she had such a fun day with her little boy. He smiled and held her hand as they walked home.

Once upon a time there was a famous jungle. All the animals that lived there were often amazed by how many interesting things they could explore.

One day, an elephant wanted to find a way to cover the whole jungle. He started by gathering branches and leaves to make a big blanket. All the animals got involved, making sure that every part of the jungle was covered. The elephant was very pleased with the result.

The animals were happy because the blanket kept them safe and the heat of the sun away. They could now roam around the jungle and enjoy it.

The famous jungle was now covered by the cozy blanket. And the animals had a peaceful and safe place to live.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful deer. The deer loved to play in the big green woods. One day while playing, she saw a small round stone. She thought, "I will come back to kick this stone later."

The next day, the deer went back to the stone. She wanted to kick it very far. But when she tried to kick it, she did not see a big tree root. The deer did a big stumble and fell down. She felt sad and her leg hurt a little.

A whole year went by, and the deer was now more careful. She went back to the stone and tried again. This time, she looked around and saw the tree root. She did not stumble and kicked the stone very far. The deer was happy and learned to always look before she played.

Once there was a friendly little girl named Susie who lived near a big lake. One day, Susie went out to the lake to go fishing. She had a rod with a hook and some bait. She also had a little bucket filled with gold.

Susie cast her line into the water and waited. Soon, she felt something pull on it. She smiled and pulled the line up and saw that she had caught a fish.

"Oh, hello!" said Susie to the fish. She put her hand in the water and carefully tried to pick it up.

But the fish bit her hand! "Ouch!" yelled Susie.

But then, she noticed that the fish had a piece of gold in its mouth! Susie carefully grabbed the gold and smiled.

Susie learned a valuable lesson that day: be careful when trying to pet friendly animals!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a pet bird named Blue. Blue was a very patient bird. He liked to sit on Sue's shoulder and sing songs.

One day, Sue found a message in a bottle. She opened the bottle and read the message. It said, "Help me escape!" Sue wanted to help, so she asked Blue to fly and find who needed help.

Blue flew high and low, searching for the person who needed help. He finally found a little boy named Tim stuck in a tree. Blue helped Tim escape the tree, and they became friends. Sue, Blue, and Tim played together every day, and they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a bulb. He was feeling very anxious. He wanted to have a friend, so he looked around.

Suddenly, he saw a bee. He waved to the bee and asked if it wanted to be his friend. The bee said yes, and the bulb was so happy.

Every day, the bulb and the bee had lots of fun. They would fly around together, play games, and go on adventures.

One day, they decided to go exploring. They found a beautiful garden with lots of flowers. They stayed there, playing games and exploring, until the sun went down.

The bulb and the bee were the best of friends, and their friendship made them both very happy. They'll always be together, no matter what.

Once there was a little girl who loved to try new things. She had a frame that her grandpa had given her. Every day she would spend hours looking at it.

One day she decided that she wanted to try to make a picture for the frame. She looked around for something that would work and she found a box of little crayons.

She sat down with the crayons and tried her best to make a pretty picture. She made wiggly lines and swirls and stars, but it didn't look quite right.

She decided that she would try again the next day. So she put the crayons away and put the little frame back in its spot on the shelf. The next day she tried again and this time the picture looked much better!

She was so excited, she ran to show her grandpa the picture. He smiled and said it was beautiful! She was so proud of her work and the frame now had a beautiful picture in it that she had created.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little boy called Ryan. He loved to explore the beach and collect shells. 

One day, Ryan met a kind surfer. He showed Ryan how to ride the waves. Ryan was so excited and wanted to do it again. 

But then the surfer warned Ryan to look out for the tide. He said it would come in and release the surfers back to shore. 

So Ryan watched the tide come in. He saw it carry the surfers up the beach and away. He thought to himself, "I must remember to watch out for the tide next time". 

And so the nosy little boy played happily at the beach, while always keeping a careful eye out for the tide.

Jill and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a shiny gem on the ground. It was red and sparkly and looked very pretty. They both wanted to have it, but there was only one gem.

"I saw it first!" Jill said. "It is mine!"

"No, I saw it first!" Ben said. "It is mine!"

They started to pull the gem from each other, but it was very hard and slippery. They pulled and pulled until the gem flew out of their hands and landed in a bush.

"Oh no!" Jill and Ben said. "Where is the gem?"

They ran to the bush and looked for the gem, but they could not find it. They searched and searched, but the gem was gone. They felt very sad and angry. They started to weep and blame each other.

"It is your fault!" Jill said. "You pulled too hard!"

"No, it is your fault!" Ben said. "You pulled too hard!"

They wept and wept until they heard a soft sound. It was a furry kitten who was hiding in the bush. The kitten had found the gem and was playing with it. The kitten looked at Jill and Ben and meowed.

"Look!" Jill said. "There is the gem!"

"And there is a kitten!" Ben said. "It is so cute!"

They forgot about their fight and went to the bush. They gently took the gem from the kitten and petted its fur. The kitten purred and licked their hands.

"Can we keep the kitten?" Jill asked. "It is so nice!"

"Yes, let's keep the kitten!" Ben agreed. "It is so fun!"

They hugged the kitten and smiled at each other. They realized that the gem was not as important as having a friend. They learned to share and be kind. They named the kitten Gem and took it home. They lived happily ever after.

Once there was a small village full of people and animals. But the village was so dull. Nothing ever happened there. All the animals and people were bored.

One day, a mysterious carriage rolled into the village. Everyone was so excited and they all stopped to look at it. Inside the carriage was a zebra with a very special power - it could zip!

The zebra used its special zip power to make the village much more fun. Suddenly the streets were full of exciting activities and bright colours! Everybody was thrilled and started to cheer. 

The zebra left the village with a big smile on its face. But it left something behind â€“ the feeling of excitement and happiness that it had brought to the village. From then on, the village was always cheerful and full of life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite teddy bear named Mr. Fluffy. One day, Lily was eating a chocolate bar and accidentally got some on Mr. Fluffy's fur. 

"Oh no, Mr. Fluffy is dirty!" Lily exclaimed. 

"Don't worry, we can wipe it off," said Lily's mom. 

Lily's mom got a wet cloth and wiped the chocolate off of Mr. Fluffy's fur. 

"Good as new!" said Lily. 

Later that day, Lily and Mr. Fluffy went outside to play. Mr. Fluffy's tie kept falling off, but Lily was persistent and kept tying it back on. They had so much fun playing together!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. One day, Tom lost his key. He looked everywhere, but he could not find it. He was very sad and embarrassed because he knew he should have taken better care of it.

Tom's mom saw him looking sad and asked what was wrong. Tom told her about the lost key. His mom said, "Sometimes, when we need help, we can pray and ask for it." So, Tom closed his eyes and prayed for help to find his key.

The next day, Tom found his key under his bed. He was so happy! He thanked his mom for teaching him to pray. From that day on, Tom always prayed when he needed help and took better care of his things.

Sammy and his mommy were going on a special trip. They had never been to a camp before, but Sammy was very excited to go on this journey. 

On the way there, Sammy could feel the car going up and down the hills. His mommy pointed out the sky and told him it was bright blue, just like the ocean. 

When they finally arrived at the camp, Sammy was so happy to see the other children playing. He noticed how everyone was being so thoughtful and sharing their things with each other. 

Sammy was having so much fun, and his mommy was happy to see him playing with all the other kids. She wanted to make sure he was having the best time and was there to support him every step of the way. 

The time went by so fast. Later on, as they drove home, Sammy was very tired but still smiling, thinking of all the fun he had at the camp. He was grateful for the thoughtfulness of his mommy and all the people he had met.

Once there was a pup who was feeling very sick. His mom said he needed to see a veterinarian. So they set off on their way.

The veterinarian was so kind. He spoke to the pup in an gentle voice. He readied a big syringe filled with medicine. It looked harsh but the pup knew it was going to help him get better.

He had to take the medicine every day. Every morning and night the pup would take it. Slowly the pup started to feel better. After a few weeks the pup was completely better!

The pup was very happy and thanked the veterinarian for making him all better. The veterinarian said it was his pleasure.

Once upon a time, there was a big garden. In the garden, there was a rake. The rake was very useful to clean up the leaves. One day, a fierce wind blew and many leaves fell on the ground. The garden owner took the rake and started cleaning. It seemed like a lot of work, but the garden looked better when the leaves were gone. The rake was happy to help!

Once upon a time, there was a wild bear. He liked to play in the forest with his friends. One day, he found a shiny rock and he wanted to make it shiny more. He went to his friend's lab and asked for help. His friend gave him a cloth and said, "You can polish the rock with this." The bear took the cloth and polished the rock. It became so shiny that he could see his reflection in it. The bear was happy and his friend was proud of him. From that day on, the bear loved to polish shiny things.

One day a little girl named Lily went with her mommy to the park. As they walked, Lily picked up many pretty things - a flower, a stone and a feather. Her mommy smiled and said "What a wonderful collection!"

When they reached the playground, Lily saw a swing and asked to try it. She grabbed the chains and started to swing high. When she stopped, she saw another girl sitting nearby.

Lily asked the other girl if she would like to play. The girl replied softly "No, thank you". Lily asked why, but the girl did not answer.

Lily felt uncomfortable so she said goodbye and played on the slide. She thought about how uncomfortable the girl must be, but she didn't know why.

As they were leaving, Lily's mommy said "Let's find a word to describe how she felt". Lily thought for a moment and said, "Picked".

Her mommy nodded and smiled. "Yes, she felt picked."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and go on adventures with her dog, Max. One day, they went on a walk in the woods and it started to rain. Lily's clothes got all wet and she was sad.

But then, they found a big tree with a dry spot underneath it. They sat down and waited for the rain to stop. Suddenly, the sun came out and the light shone through the trees. Lily felt happy again.

She looked up at the sky and saw a beautiful rainbow. She felt adventurous and wanted to follow it. Max barked and wagged his tail, so they went on an adventure to find the end of the rainbow. They walked and walked until they found a pot of gold. Lily and Max were so happy and they danced in the light of the sun.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird called an ostrich. The ostrich had long legs and a big body. One day, a little girl saw the ostrich and wanted to give it some yummy food. She tried to reach the ostrich with her hands, but it was too far away. 

The little girl thought hard and came up with an idea. She went to get a long stick and used it to reach the ostrich. The ostrich was happy to get some yummy food and ate it all up. 

From that day on, the little girl would visit the ostrich and bring it yummy food. She would use the stick to reach the ostrich and they became good friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was an old earth. It was very beautiful and full of life. Everyone on the earth had something to pay for. Everyone paid for the things they needed. Whether it was food, clothes or toys, everyone always paid for the things they wanted.

One day, a little boy wanted a toy elephant. He had saved for it for a long time, and he was ready to pay. He used his allowance and bought the elephant. He was so excited to take it home to play with.

When he got home, he hugged his elephant very tightly. He knew he had paid for it, and he was so excited to have it. He liked to play and cuddle with the old earth. He kept it safe, and took it everywhere he went.

Every day, the little boy and his new elephant played together. They went on adventures and had lots of fun. The little boy learned to care for his elephant, and he knew that he had paid for it with his allowance. He was so happy to have it. 

The little boy and his old earth were best friends. They had many adventures and made lots of memories together. He thought it was the best thing he had ever paid for.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She wanted to bake something, so she grabbed a pen and a big note. She drew a picture of a cake to help her remember what she wanted to make. She asked for help from Mom and Dad, and they were very happy to help her.

Together, they grabbed all the ingredients from the kitchen. Jane put in a cup of sugar, while Mom added some butter, and Dad cracked the eggs. With a little help, they stirred and mixed the ingredients until it was ready. Jane was so happy.

When the cake had finished baking, it smelled so delicious. Jane grabbed the plate and took it to the table with Mom and Dad. Together, they enjoyed the yummy cake. Jane was very proud of her baking and everyone was very happy and thankful.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a gentle crane. The crane had many friends. One day, the crane's best friend, a tiny mouse, came running to him. The mouse was sad.

"Help me, crane!" said the mouse. "A big cat took my food. I have nothing to eat and I am hungry."

The gentle crane wanted to help his friend. So, he went to the big cat and asked, "Please give the food back to the mouse. He is very hungry."

The big cat laughed and said, "No, I will not give it back. I will eat it all."

The gentle crane had an idea. He told the big cat, "If you give the food back, we will celebrate with you. We will have a big party!"

The big cat liked the idea of a party. So, he gave the food back to the mouse. They all had a big party together and celebrated. The mouse was happy, and they all became friends.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. They had to be careful not to lose the ball or hit someone with it.

One time, the ball went too far and landed near a lady who was sitting on a bench. She had a big hat and a book. She looked up and saw the ball. She smiled and picked it up.

"Hello, children," she said. "Is this your ball?"

"Yes, it is," Tim said. "We are sorry. We did not mean to bother you."

"That's all right," the lady said. "You can have your ball back. But please be careful where you kick it. There are other people and animals in the park. You don't want to hurt them or make them angry."

"OK, we will," Lily said. "Thank you, lady."

The lady gave them the ball and they said goodbye. They ran back to their spot and decided to play a different game. They agreed to settle for catch instead of kick. They threw the ball to each other and caught it with their hands. They had fun and were careful not to let the ball go too far again. They liked the lady and hoped to see her again.
