Once there was a dry pie. Princess Jane wanted to take a picture of it. She asked her friend, Tommy. Tommy said, "Sure!" The two of them went to Tommy's house.

When they got there, Tommy pulled out a big, black machine. Princess Jane said, "What is that?" Tommy laughed and said, "It's a printer. It takes a picture and prints it out." 

Princess Jane was very excited. She smiled and said, "Let's print the pie!" Tommy put the picture in the printer and pressed a few buttons. After a few moments, the printer spat out a picture of the dry pie. Princess Jane clapped her hands and said, "Yay! That looks great!" 

They both held up the picture and smiled. Then, they enjoyed eating the dry pie. It was delicious!

Once upon a time, there was a selfish king. He lived in a magnificent castle with lots of his servants.

Every morning he would get up and dress himself in his finest clothes. He loved to show everyone how rich and important he was.

The king was very mean to his servants. He made them do all the work and never said 'thank you'.

One day, a fairy appeared to the king. She said that he was being too selfish and had to change his ways.

The king listened to the fairy and started being kind to his servants. He shared his food with them and thanked them for all their hard work.

The king was very happy when he saw how much better his kingdom was because of his kindness. From then on, he was always sure to dress in his finest clothes, but also act with kindness and generosity.

Once upon a time there was a spot. It was a lonely spot, all by itself. One day it decided to move. It felt scared so it moved slowly and carefully. 

As it moved, the spot became a little less fearful. Soon, it started to move faster and faster. It kept going until it reached a new spot. It was a much better spot than the old one. 

The spot was so happy that it began to dance. It was a fun spot and it was no longer scared. It was happy to have moved and it was ready to meet new friends. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Phoebe who liked to explore. Every day, she would wander around her house and the garden, looking for new things. One day, she heard a strange noise coming from the garden and wondered what it was. She paused and had a little look.

Inside a tree, she found a dragon! The dragon was singing a magical spell. It began to glow and a rainbow glittered in the sky. Phoebe was so excited!

The dragon asked if Phoebe would like to play with it. She said yes, and the dragon gave her a flexible wand made out of a twinkle. With the wand, Phoebe could make the spells come true.

The magical spells were so much fun, and soon Phoebe and the dragon were laughing and playing for hours. What a lovely day it was!

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play and have fun. They are very happy because they are going on holiday with Mum and Dad. They pack their bags and toys and get in the car.

The car goes very fast on the road. Lily and Tom look out the window and see many things. They see cows and sheep and trees and houses. They tell each other what they see and make up stories. They sing songs and laugh.

After a long time, the car stops at a big house. Mum and Dad say this is where they will stay for the holiday. They get out of the car and take their bags and toys. They go inside the house and look around. It is very nice and cosy.

But there is a problem. The house has a smelly smell. It smells like old socks and cheese and fish. Lily and Tom do not like the smell. They cover their noses and say yuck. Mum and Dad do not like the smell either. They say sorry and look for the source of the smell.

They find it in the kitchen. It is a big bin full of rubbish. Someone forgot to take it out before they left. Mum and Dad take the bin outside and throw it away. They open the windows and spray some perfume. The smell goes away and the house is fresh and clean.

Lily and Tom are happy again. They say thank you and give Mum and Dad a hug. They unpack their bags and toys and choose their rooms. They are ready to enjoy their holiday. They hope to see more cows and sheep and trees and houses. They hope to have more fun and make more stories. They hope the house does not get smelly again.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lila. She was three years old and very curious. She had heard about attics and wanted to explore one for herself.

One day, Lila followed her dad upstairs and he opened the door of an attic. The attic was filled with fascinating things. There were old boxes and toys with bright colors. Lila couldn't believe her eyes! She ran around, touching everything and picking up treasures to keep.

Soon, Lila's brother noticed all the exploring she was doing. He became very jealous and began to follow her around the attic. He wanted to see what she was going to find next.

Even though her brother tried to follow her, Lila still managed to find incredible things. By the end of the day, Lila had discovered a secret the attic.

From then on, Lila came back to the attic often. She was glad she'd found a special place to explore. And she was even happier that her jealous brother couldn't follow her there!

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were always fighting. They would scream and yell and push each other over. When both friends were upset, nothing would make them happy.

One day, one of the friends had an idea. Instead of fighting, why not give each other a massage?

The friends thought this was a great idea and started doing it regularly. They would trade massages and talk to each other instead of fight.

The friends quickly learned that massage was far better than fight and they started to become the best of friends.

The moral of the story is that good things come when you find a way to work together and be kind. Sometimes it takes courage to do something different, but it's worth it in the end.

Lily liked to study. She liked to look at books and pictures and learn new things. She had a big drawer in her room where she kept her books and papers and crayons. She liked to open the drawer and take out what she wanted to study.

One day, Lily wanted to study about animals. She opened the drawer and looked for a book with animals. She saw a book with a lion on the cover. She wanted to see the lion and learn its name. She reached for the book, but she was clumsy. She pulled too hard and the book fell out of the drawer. Then the drawer fell out too and all the books and papers and crayons spilled on the floor.

Lily was scared and sad. She made a big mess and she did not see the lion. She started to cry. She did not know what to do.

Then she heard her mom come in. Her mom saw the mess and Lily crying. She did not get angry. She hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, honey. You were trying to study, but you were clumsy. That happens sometimes. Let's clean up together and then we can look at the book with the lion. Do you want to do that?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, mom. I want to study the lion. Thank you for helping me." She and her mom picked up the books and papers and crayons and put them back in the drawer. Then they sat on the bed and opened the book with the lion. Lily learned that the lion was called a king of the animals and that it made a loud sound called a roar. She liked the lion and she liked to study. She was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named John. He was very young and full of joy. One day, John was playing in the park when he fell down. He started to cry as he looked up to the sky.

Suddenly, an old man appeared. He was kind and very compassionate. The old man told John, "Don't worry. Everyone falls down sometimes."

John rolled over and looked at the old man. He asked, "Who are you?"

The old man smiled and said, "I am your youth. I never leave your side, even when you fall. Know that I will always be with you."

John smiled, feeling better now. He thanked the old man and the old man disappeared.

John then stood up and went back to playing in the park. He remembered the old man's words, knowing that no matter what, his youth would never leave him. He had found comfort in the old man's compassionate words.

Once there was a little girl called Steph. Steph was three years old and wanted to choose the perfect table for her room. She thought about it for a long time. She wanted something special.

One day, she went with her parents to a furniture shop. There were lots of tables to choose from. She looked at them all, but none of them seemed perfect. Just when she thought she wouldn't find one, she saw it. It was a beautiful wooden table with a big smile on it. She knew it was the one!

So, Steph chose the perfect table. She brought it home and it made her very happy. Every evening, she would sit at her table and draw or colour. And when she was finished, she'd put the things away neatly, just like her mum and dad had taught her.

The table was perfect. It was just what she needed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved puppies very much. One day, she saw a puppy in the park. The puppy was so cute!

Lily went to the puppy and said, "Hi, little puppy! Can I pet you?" The puppy wagged its tail and licked Lily's hand. Lily was so happy!

Suddenly, a boy came up to Lily and said, "That's my puppy! You can't have it!" Lily replied, "I don't want your puppy. I just want to borrow it for a little while." The boy said, "No way! That's a fake puppy. It's not real." 

Lily looked at the puppy and realized that it was indeed a fake puppy. She laughed and said, "Oh, silly me! I don't want to borrow a fake puppy. I'll just look for a real one." The boy smiled and said, "Good luck finding one!" Lily said goodbye to the boy and the fake puppy, and went on her way to find a real puppy to play with.

Tom and Lily are playing in the park. They like to slide, swing and run. They are having fun. But then, Tom sees a big dog. The dog is brown and has a long tail. Tom likes dogs. He runs to the dog and says, "Hello, dog. Can I pet you?"

The dog is friendly. He wags his tail and licks Tom's face. Tom laughs and pets the dog's ear. The ear is dry and soft. Tom says, "Your ear is dry, dog. Do you need water?"

Lily sees Tom and the dog. She is scared of dogs. She thinks they are loud and mean. She calls Tom and says, "Tom, come back. The dog might bite you."

Tom says, "No, Lily. The dog is nice. He likes me. Look, he lets me touch his ear."

Lily says, "But Tom, we have to return. Mom said we have to be home soon. It is getting dark."

Tom says, "Okay, Lily. I will return. But can I say goodbye to the dog first?"

Lily says, "Yes, Tom. But hurry up."

Tom hugs the dog and says, "Bye, dog. You are a good dog. I hope I see you again."

The dog barks and wags his tail. He is happy. He likes Tom too.

Tom and Lily run back to their mom. She is waiting for them at the gate. She says, "There you are. Did you have fun?"

Tom and Lily nod and smile. They tell their mom about the dog. She says, "That sounds nice. But next time, be careful. Not all dogs are friendly. And always ask the owner before you pet a dog."

Tom and Lily say, "Okay, mom. We will."

They go home and have dinner. They are tired and happy. They dream of the dog and his dry ear.

Molly and her family were sitting in the living room. Her mom and dad were on the couch and Molly was sitting on the floor. They were looking around the room, wondering what to do.

Then, Molly had an idea. She said, "Let's watch TV!" Everyone thought it was a good idea and so they decided to do it.

Molly's family looked around the room until they saw an old TV in the corner. It hadn't been used in a long time, but Molly's mom decided to plug it in and turn it on.

The TV made noises and lights came on. Molly was so excited and ran to the couch with her mom and dad. They all watched the show together and had a lot of fun.

At the end of the night, everyone said they had a great time. They thanked Molly for deciding to watch the old TV.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide-and-seek with her friends. One day, she was hiding behind a curtain and her friend couldn't find her. 

"Where are you, Lily?" her friend asked.

"I'm behind the curtain!" Lily replied.

Her friend was surprised and said, "Wow, that's a creative hiding spot!" 

Lily giggled and said, "I can see you, but you can't see me!" 

Her friend laughed and said, "You're right! You're really good at this game!" 

From that day on, Lily's friends always looked behind the curtain when they played hide-and-seek. And Lily always had fun hiding in creative places. The end.

Joey was so excited when he saw the horse. It was pink and he thought it was so pretty. He wanted to get close to it to see it better. He reached out and touched the horse's pink fur. It felt so soft and smooth. 

The horse nickered softly and made Joey feel happy. He thought it was so nice to pet the pink horse. Joey wished he could take it home but he knew that wasn't possible. 

Joey gave the horse one more pat before saying goodbye. He hoped to see the pink horse someday again. He smiled and waved as it trotted away and he walked back home, feeling happy.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl called Molly. Molly was very brave, so one day she decided she wanted to explore a cave. 

Molly found the cave and she yawned as she looked inside. She was very excited because she knew it was a rare cave. Molly had never seen a cave like this before, and she was eager to find out what was inside. 

Molly shrugged, took a deep breath and entered the cave. She was surprised to find that it was very dark, but she kept exploring and soon she saw something. It was a small sparkling rock. Molly's eyes widened with excitement. She had never seen a rock so rare before. 

Molly was so tired from exploring the cave, so she yawned and decided to take the rare rock home with her. Molly was so happy she had found such a special stone. She thanked the cave for the adventure, and she smiled on her way back home.

Johnny was walking by a river. He heard a loud noise and stopped to listen. Suddenly, a big, dangerous shape jumped out from the water. Johnny was so scared he hid behind a tree. He stayed there for a long time trying to figure out what the shape was. 

Suddenly, Johnny heard a friendly voice coming from the shape. He listened carefully and realized that the shape was an animal, looking for its lost home. Johnny recognized the animal as an elephant and knew he had to help. 

He slowly came out from behind the tree and approached the dangerous animal. He showed the elephant the way to his home and told him to be careful. In return, the elephant thanked Johnny for his help. Johnny walked home with a smile on his face, proud that he had helped the lost and dangerous shape.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. She was troubled, because she didn't have anyone to play with. Then one day, she saw a purse! Inside was a note with a surprise; it was an invite!

It was from her friend, Bob. He wanted her to come over and play. Anna was so happy! She put on her shoes and raced outside.

When she got to Bob's house, there were all sorts of toys. They laughed and played for hours. They invited some of their other friends and had a huge party. Everyone had so much fun playing together!

Anna was no longer troubled. She was so glad Bob had invited her over. They became the best of friends.

Maggie wanted to buy something special. She went to the store to look around. The store was full of things that caught her eye. She saw a math book that she liked. It was bright, colourful and very exciting!

Maggie asked the shopkeeper if she could buy the book. Thankfully, the shopkeeper said yes. But when she opened it up, it was filthy and covered with dirt. She was so upset.

Maggie asked the shopkeeper why the book was so filthy. He told her that it had come from a dusty warehouse. He said he had cleaned it up a bit, but some of the dirt had stayed.

Maggie decided to buy it anyway. She was so excited to learn about math! She took the book home and carefully wiped away the dirt. She was happy to see the clean pages of the math book. Maggie and her math book have been inseparable ever since.

Lila and Tom were playing with their toys in the garden. Lila had a big doll that she liked very much. Tom had a small car that he liked very much. They were happy and shared their toys.

But then, a big dog came and saw the toys. The dog ran and grabbed the doll with its mouth. Lila was scared and cried. "No, no, that is mine! Give it back!" she shouted. Tom tried to help her and threw a stick at the dog. But the dog did not care and ran away with the doll.

Lila and Tom ran after the dog. They saw the dog go into a house. They knocked on the door. A lady opened the door. She saw the dog with the doll. She saw Lila and Tom. She was angry and ashamed.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry, this is my dog. He is naughty and likes to carry things. He did not mean to hurt you. Here, take your doll back. And here, have a cookie. I'm very sorry," she said.

Lila and Tom took their doll and their cookie. They thanked the lady and went back to the garden. They hugged their toys and each other. They were happy again. They learned to be careful with their toys and to forgive others.

Mia and Jack were best friends. They liked to do everything together. One day, Mia and Jack decided to spend the day in the park. It was an icy day, but they were excited to play.

They found a pile of junk by the pond, so they ran over to it. Mia and Jack started to look through it.

They found a toy boat and an old ball. They made a path of rocks across the pond and put the boat in it. They watched as the boat drifted away. Then they kicked the ball back and forth until they got tired.

Before they left, they decided to spend some time watching the ducks swim in the pond. It was so fun to watch the ducks and to see the icy water glisten in the sunlight.

Mia and Jack had such a great day, and were happy that they got to spend it together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom gave her a ball of yarn to play with. Lily loved the yarn and started to play with it. She wrapped it around her toys and made a big mess.

Suddenly, Lily's cat, Mittens, came into the room and scared her. She managed to grab the yarn and ran out of the room. But the yarn was tangled and Lily couldn't untangle it. She was sad and didn't know what to do.

Then, Lily's mom came to help her. She managed to untangle the yarn and Lily was happy again. They both worked together to clean up the mess and put the yarn away safely. From that day on, Lily learned to be careful with the yarn and not to get scared of her cat.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky lived in a pond with his family and friends. One day, Ducky saw a bright and shiny object in the water. It was a raft! Ducky had never seen a raft before, so he climbed on it and started to play.

But suddenly, the raft started to move! Ducky tried to get off, but he couldn't. He was scared and didn't know what to do. Luckily, Ducky's mother saw him and quickly came to his rescue. She helped him escape from the raft and brought him back to safety.

From that day on, Ducky learned an important lesson. He realized that sometimes things that look fun can be dangerous. He promised to always be careful and listen to his mother's advice. And whenever he saw a bright and shiny object, he would remember to think twice before playing with it.

Once upon a time, there was a careless boy who stayed out at night. One night, his mom found out and she was really mad. She told the boy that he had to pay for his actions. The boy was scared and he promised he would never stay out at night again. His mom smiled because she knew her son would be more careful. The end.

There was a house and two friends who lived in it. One was named Jack and the other was named Jill. 

One day, Jack and Jill were playing in the house when they heard a loud noise. They both looked up and saw a big tough man. He said, "I'm looking for the toughest kid around. Who's the toughest?" 

Jack and Jill looked at each other in surprise. Jack smiled and said, "I'm the toughest one here." The tough man looked at Jack carefully, then he laughed and said, "No, that's not true. I think Jill here is the toughest one."

Jill smiled and said, "That's not true either. We're both tough." 

The tough man laughed even harder. He said, "You're both very tough. But I think you should joke around more often."

Jack and Jill smiled. They both liked to joke. They played games and laughed for hours. They both agreed that being tough was great, but it was even better when you could joke about it.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to read books. He would read them all day long. One day, Timmy's mom asked him if he wanted to help her make dinner. Timmy said yes and they went to the kitchen. Timmy's mom gave him a small potato to peel. Timmy peeled it very carefully and then they cooked it for dinner. After dinner, Timmy read his favorite book before going to bed. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emma. She was three years old, and she was really excited because she had just got a new scooter. As she walked out of the shop carrying the scooter, she realized that she had no idea how to ride it.

She asked her Dad to show her, and he smiled and said: "Let's give it a try". Emma sat down on the scooter, and her Dad held onto it, running alongside as she tried to scoot away. She was feeling a bit scared, but she pushed herself off the ground with her feet, and soon she was scooting away.

It felt so exciting and a bit crazy! Emma couldn't believe that she was actually riding a scooter. She flew down the streets, and felt like the wind was blowing through her hair. Her Dad ran behind her, cheering her on. 

Soon Emma was riding her scooter with ease, and she realized that it was the most fun she had ever had. She knew that she would treasure this moment forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her dolls. One day, Lily's mom told her that they were going to visit her grandma. Lily was so excited because she loved her grandma very much.

When they got to her grandma's house, Lily saw a beautiful vase on the table. Her mom told her that it was very fragile and she should be careful around it. Lily promised to be careful and not touch it.

Later that day, Lily's grandma recommended that they all go for a walk in the park. Lily loved going for walks so she turned to her mom and asked if they could go. Her mom agreed and they all went for a lovely walk in the park. When they got back to her grandma's house, Lily was very tired and went straight to bed. She dreamed of all the fun she had that day and couldn't wait to visit her grandma again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to count. She could count up to ten all by herself. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. They saw a tall tree and Lily said, "I want to stand under the tree." Her mom said, "Okay, but be careful not to climb it."

Lily stood under the tree and counted the leaves. Suddenly, she saw a bird fall from the sky and land on the ground. She ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, the bird is dead!" Her mom said, "Let's go see if we can help it." They went to the bird and saw that it was not moving. 

Lily's mom explained to her that sometimes animals get hurt and can't be helped. Lily said, "I will count the leaves on the tree for the bird." She counted all the leaves and said, "I hope the bird can be happy in heaven." Her mom smiled and said, "That was very kind of you, Lily."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to bake cookies with her mom. One day, Lily's mom put on a modern apron with bright colors and asked Lily to help her mix the cookie dough.

Lily nodded her head and said, "Yes, Mama!" She loved helping her mom in the kitchen. As they mixed the dough, Lily's mom said, "You are such a good helper, Lily. You are going to be a great baker one day!"

Lily smiled and said, "I love baking with you, Mama." They finished making the dough and put it in the oven to bake. As they waited for the cookies to be done, Lily's mom asked, "What kind of cookies do you want to make next time?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Chocolate chip cookies, please!" Her mom nodded and said, "Sounds good to me!" They hugged each other and waited for the cookies to finish baking. When they were done, they enjoyed eating their delicious cookies together.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big rainbow in the sky. It has many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.

"Wow, look at the rainbow!" Lily says. "It is so pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Ben says. "Do you think we can touch it?"

Lily and Ben run to the rainbow. They want to hold it in their hands. But the rainbow is too far away. They cannot reach it.

"Maybe we need a ladder," Lily says.

"Or a rocket," Ben says.

They look around. They do not see a ladder or a rocket. They only see a tree, a swing, and a ball.

"Maybe we can make a rainbow," Lily says. "We can use the ball and the swing."

"How?" Ben asks.

Lily has an idea. She takes the ball and throws it in the air. The sun shines on the ball. The ball makes a little rainbow on the ground.

"Look, Ben, a rainbow!" Lily says.

Ben sees the rainbow. He is glad. He runs to the rainbow. He tries to hold it in his hands. But the rainbow is too small. It disappears.

"Oops, it is gone," Ben says.

Lily throws the ball again. The ball makes another rainbow. Ben tries to hold it again. But the rainbow is gone again.

They do this many times. They have fun. They laugh and giggle.

They do not need a ladder or a rocket. They have a ball and a swing. They have each other. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a deaf, three year old girl. She loved going to the library every day and read books.

One day, while she was reading, she came across a big book about history. She was curious and wanted to read it, even though she was scared of its size. 

The librarian saw the girl and smiled. She said, â€œDo you want to read more about history?â€ The girl nodded and the librarian said, â€œThatâ€™s great! You can learn so much from reading history books.â€

The girl smiled and took the book home. She read the book every day, and soon she knew a lot of facts about the past.

The girl was very proud when she showed her parents what she had learnt from reading history. Her parents smiled and said, â€œYouâ€™re so clever!â€ She felt so proud - she had achieved something all by herself, even though she was deaf!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sally. Sally was very careful when she did things. One day while she was playing outside, Sally spotted a strange powder. Sally's mommy had taught her to be careful, so she knew that she couldn't touch it.

Sally went back inside and asked her mommy what it was. Her mommy told her that it was a special kind of powder, and she needed to be very careful. Her mommy grabbed a special cloth and some gloves, then went outside to remove the powder.

Sally watched as her mommy carefully removed the powder using the cloth. Once all of the powder was gone, her mommy threw away the cloth, much to Sally's relief.

Sally smiled as she watched her mommy clean up the powder. She was so happy that her mommy was so careful. She knew that, with her mommy around, she would always be safe.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was an enormous tree. Many animals lived near the tree. One day, a little squirrel named Tim found a sharp rock. He had a worry in his heart. He did not want anyone to get hurt by the sharp rock.

Tim decided to hide the sharp rock. He knew that the big tree had a hole in it. He thought that the hole would be a safe place to put the rock. But he had another worry. What if someone found the rock in the tree?

Tim asked his friend, a wise old owl, what to do. The owl told Tim to put the rock in the river. The river would make the rock smooth and not sharp anymore. Tim liked this idea. He took the sharp rock to the river and threw it in.

After some time, the rock became smooth. Tim's worries went away. He knew that no one would get hurt by the sharp rock now. All the animals in the forest were safe and happy. Tim learned that it was good to ask for help when he had a worry.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big hole in the ground. They wanted to know what was inside.

"Let's go and look," said Tom.

"No, it might be dangerous," said Lily.

But Tom did not listen. He jumped into the hole. Lily was scared. She called for Tom, but he did not answer.

Tom went deeper and deeper into the hole. It was dark and cold. He heard a loud growl. He saw a big bear. The bear was grumpy. He did not like visitors in his home.

"Who are you? What are you doing here?" the bear roared.

Tom was very afraid. He wished he had listened to Lily. He said, "I'm sorry, Mr. Bear. I was curious. I wanted to know what was underground. Please don't hurt me."

The bear looked at Tom. He saw that he was a small boy. He felt sorry for him. He said, "You are lucky, boy. I'm not hungry today. But you should not come here again. This is my home. You belong above the ground. Go back to your friend. And remember, curiosity can be dangerous."

The bear helped Tom out of the hole. Tom ran to Lily. He hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. You were right. I should have listened to you. I met a grumpy bear underground. He was scary, but he let me go. I learned my lesson. I will not be so curious again."

Lily was happy that Tom was safe. She said, "I'm glad you're okay, Tom. I forgive you. But next time, please be careful. There are many things to know and explore, but some things are better left alone."

Tom and Lily went home. They told their parents what happened. Their parents were proud of them. They said, "You are brave and smart, Tom and Lily. You learned a valuable lesson today. Curiosity is good, but it must be balanced with caution and respect. Knowing when to stop is also important. We love you very much."

Once upon a time there was a small boy. His name was Tom. Tom was very polite. One day he wanted to have a nap. He went outside and saw a beautiful leaf. He thought it looked so cozy that he decided to lay down and have his nap there. He closed his eyes and started to dream. He dreamt of the leaf and how polite it was.

When he woke up, he picked up the leaf and lightly blew it away. The leaf flew away far into the sky. He watched it with a smile on his face. He was so happy he had been able to nap with the nice leaf. He thanked it before heading home with a happy skip in his step.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little girl called Cathy. Cathy always wanted to be a success but she felt too shy to try new things. Every day she watched her friends explore and try new things. One day, Cathy asked her mum if she could join her friends and try something new.

Her mum smiled and said, "Of course you can, Cathy! You should never be too scared to be brave and try something new." 

Cathy felt scared but excited at the same time. She took a deep breath and started walking towards her friends. When she saw them, Cathy stepped back. She was too shy to say hello.

Suddenly her friend Lisa called out, "Cathy! Come join us! We're playing hide and seek." 

Cathy smiled. She took another deep breath and ran towards Lisa. Before she knew it, she was having the best time!

Cathy was so happy and proud of herself for being brave. She had taken the first step to success!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Timmy found a bow and arrow. He wanted to try it out. 

Timmy pulled back the arrow and let it go. The arrow flew through the air and split a tree in two. Timmy was amazed! 

Suddenly, Timmy's mom called him in for dinner. "Timmy, come inside now. It's time to eat," she said. 

Timmy went inside and saw that his mom had made his favorite meal. "Wow, mom! This looks so tidy!" he exclaimed. 

After dinner, Timmy went to bed with a smile on his face. He couldn't wait to play with his bow and arrow again tomorrow.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the snow. One day, they see a big hill. They want to slide down the hill on their sled.

But Mom says, "No, it is too icy. You might get hurt. Stay here where I can see you."

Lily and Ben are cross. They think Mom is no fun. They wait until Mom is busy. Then they sneak to the hill with their sled.

They go very fast down the hill. It is fun, but scary. They scream and laugh. But then they see a big rock. They cannot stop. They hit the rock and fall off the sled.

Lily and Ben are hurt. They cry and bleed. Mom hears them and runs to them. She is very worry. She hugs them and says, "I told you it was too icy. Why did you not listen to me?"

Lily and Ben are sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We were bad. We wanted to have fun. But we were wrong. We love you, Mom."

Mom says, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. But you have to be careful. I do not want you to get hurt. Come on, let's go home and clean your wounds."

Lily and Ben nod. They hold Mom's hand and walk home. They are still cross, but they are also glad that Mom is there. They learn a lesson. They will not sneak to the icy hill again.

Once upon a time there was a big white body that floated in the sky. It was so big and white that it seemed to stretch out forever. Every day the body created beautiful things like clouds and rainbows.The body was so amazing that everyone wanted to see it. One day a girl who was three years old decided to go explore it. She climbed and climbed for what felt like forever. Finally, she found the white body and she couldn't believe her eyes! All around her, there were things she had never seen before. She sat on the white body and watched the sun go down as the body created amazing new things. The girl was so excited. She spent the rest of the night dreaming of all the things the white body would create.

Jill and Ben like to play in the garden. They have a big bucket and a small scale. They fill the bucket with soil and put it on the scale. They want to see how much the soil weighs.

"Look, Ben, the scale says ten!" Jill says. "That is a lot of soil!"

"Let me try!" Ben says. He takes some soil out of the bucket and puts it in his hands. He puts his hands on the scale. "Now the scale says eight. I have two soil in my hands!"

Jill and Ben laugh. They think it is fun to weigh the soil. They take turns putting soil in and out of the bucket and the scale.

But then Mom comes out of the house. She sees the mess they have made. She is not happy.

"Jill and Ben, what are you doing?" Mom says. "You have spoiled the garden! The soil belongs in the flower beds, not on the scale. And look at your clothes, they are dirty!"

Jill and Ben feel sorry. They did not mean to spoil the garden. They only wanted to play.

"Sorry, Mom," they say. "We will clean up the soil and the scale. And we will change our clothes."

Mom smiles. She knows they are good kids. She helps them clean up the garden. She tells them they can play with the soil again, but only in a sandbox. She also tells them they can weigh other things, like toys or books or fruits. She says weighing is a good way to learn about numbers and sizes.

Jill and Ben nod. They like to learn new things. They hug Mom and say thank you. They are happy to play in the garden.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make sounds like vroom and beep when they move the cars.

One day, they find a big car in the garage. It is red and shiny. It has four wheels and a steering wheel. Tom and Sam want to try it. They climb inside the car and pretend to drive.

"Let's go to the park!" Tom says.

"OK!" Sam says.

They turn the key and the car starts. It makes a loud noise. Tom and Sam are happy. They push the pedals and the car moves. They turn the steering wheel and the car goes left and right.

But they do not know how to stop. The car goes faster and faster. They see a tree in front of them. They are scared.

"Stop! Stop!" Tom shouts.

"I don't know how!" Sam cries.

They look for a button or a lever that can stop the car. They see a word on the dashboard. It says reverse. They do not know what it means, but they think it might help.

"Push it! Push it!" Tom says.

Sam pushes it. The car makes a beep sound and changes direction. It goes backwards. It goes away from the tree. Tom and Sam are relieved.

But they do not see the fence behind them. The car hits the fence and breaks it. The car stops. Tom and Sam are shocked. They hear a voice.

"Hey! What are you doing with my car?" It is the owner of the car. He is angry. He comes out of the house and sees the damage.

Tom and Sam are sorry. They get out of the car and say sorry to the owner. They say they were playing and did not know how to stop.

The owner is still angry, but he sees that they are just kids. He tells them that the car is dangerous and they should not touch it. He tells them to go home and tell their parents what they did.

Tom and Sam nod and run away. They are sad and scared. They say they will never play with cars again. They say they will play with something else. Something that has rhythm and is not dangerous. Like drums.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big box. She was very eager to open it. 

Lily's mom asked, "What's in the box, Lily?" 

"I don't know," said Lily. "Let's watch and see!" 

Lily opened the box and inside was a toy car. She was so happy and played with it all day. 

The next day, Lily's friend came over. "Can I watch you play with your car?" asked Lily's friend. 

"Sure!" said Lily. "Let's play together!" 

They had so much fun playing with the toy car. Lily was very happy to share her toy with her friend.

Once upon a time, there was a monster who loved to bite. Everywhere he went, he looked for things to bite. He even bit people who were not so nice! 

One day, the monster bit a truth. It was a surprise because the monster thought the truth would be sweet. But, it was sour! The monster was so surprised that he started to cry. 

The monster was sad because he did not want to hurt the truth. But, he had already bitten it. Luckily, he found a way to make it better. 

He took the truth and made it into a big hug for everyone in the world. It was his way of saying sorry for biting the truth. And everyone was happy because the truth was now a hug. 

The end.

Once there was a little girl who really wanted to go on the slides at the park. She asked her mom and dad if she could go but they said no. The little girl was very sad. 

She decided to have a plan to try and go on the slide even though her parents said no. She had an idea. She ate three bowls of oatmeal and went to the park. 

When she got to the park she ran to the slide. She felt very fit and strong. She ran up the stairs and looked down the slide. It was big but she thought she was big enough too. 

The little girl was very excited but then she heard her parents calling. She felt her stomach drop. She covered her ears and made her decision. She decided to go down the slide because she thought she was fit enough and she wanted to do it. 

So she went down the slide! She screamed the whole way and when she got to the bottom she was very proud of herself. The little girl knew that she made the right decision.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big box. They pretended the box was a spaceship, a castle, a boat, and many other things.

One day, their mom said she had to mail some letters. She asked Lily and Ben to help her put the letters in the box. Lily and Ben were happy to help. They took the letters and put them in the box. But then, they had an idea.

"Let's mail ourselves!" Lily said.

"Yeah, let's go on an adventure!" Ben agreed.

They climbed into the box and closed the lid. They giggled and whispered to each other.

"Where do you think we will go?" Lily asked.

"Maybe to the moon, or the jungle, or the sea!" Ben said.

They waited and waited, but nothing happened. They started to feel hot and bored.

"Mom, we're ready to go!" Lily shouted.

"Mom, open the box!" Ben yelled.

But mom did not hear them. She had gone to the kitchen to make some tea. She did not know that Lily and Ben were in the box.

Soon, dad came home from work. He saw the box and the letters on the table.

"Looks like mom has some mail to send," he said. He picked up the box and carried it to the car. He did not know that Lily and Ben were in the box.

Lily and Ben felt the box move. They were scared and confused.

"Dad, stop!" Lily cried.

"Dad, we're in here!" Ben screamed.

But dad did not hear them. He had turned on the radio and was singing along. He did not know that Lily and Ben were in the box.

He drove to the post office and parked the car. He got out and took the box to the counter. He did not know that Lily and Ben were in the box.

"Hi, I have some mail to send," he said to the lady.

"Sure, let me weigh it for you," the lady said. She put the box on the scale. She was shocked. The box was very heavy.

"What's in here?" she asked.

"Just some letters," dad said.

The lady looked at him suspiciously. She shook the box gently. She heard some noises.

"Help!" Lily and Ben shouted.

The lady opened the box. She was shocked. She saw Lily and Ben in the box.

"What are you doing here?" she asked.

"We wanted to mail ourselves," Lily and Ben said.

The lady looked at dad. He was shocked. He saw Lily and Ben in the box.

"How did you get in there?" he asked.

"We put ourselves in," Lily and Ben said.

Dad was angry. He took Lily and Ben out of the box. He apologized to the lady. He took the letters and the box and went back to the car. He did not know what to say.

Lily and Ben were sorry. They realized they had made a big mistake. They did not want to mail themselves anymore. They wanted to go home.

"Mom, we're sorry!" Lily and Ben said.

"Mom, we love you!" Lily and Ben said.

Mom was shocked. She saw Lily and Ben in the car. She hugged them and kissed them. She was glad they were safe.

"What happened?" she asked.

"We'll tell you later," dad said.

He drove them home. He explained what had happened. He was not happy. He said they had to be more careful and listen to mom. He said they had to share their toys and play nicely. He said they had to be fair.

Lily and Ben nodded. They agreed. They learned their lesson. They did not want to mail themselves again. They wanted to stay with mom and dad. They loved them very much.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. She had a big basket of apples and was so excited to give them away as presents.

Anna set off on her journey and soon arrived at her best friend's house. Her friend was very surprised to see her and her basket of apples. 

"Thank you for the apples, Anna!" said her friend.

"You're welcome!" said Anna and she handed over the basket with a big smile. 

Anna and her friend had a great time playing with the apples. They counted them, rolled them, smelled them and even tasted a few. 

Anna suddenly realised that she had to go, so she gathered up the last few apples and said goodbye to her friend. 

"Thank you for coming Anna," her friend said.

"You're welcome!" said Anna happily, with a big wave.

Anna was a bit worried on the way home, but she felt better when she saw her house. She put the last few apples in her basket and said a big thank you. 

Anna was so happy she had been able to give her friends such a lovely surprise.

Once upon a time, there was a stable. Inside the stable were two ponies. The ponies were happy and enjoyed jumping around their home.

One day, one of the ponies made a mistake and knocked over a bucket. The other pony got mad and started to yell.

The yelling frightened the other pony. He ran outside and didn't come back. The pony inside the stable knew he had made the other one angry and he felt very sorry.

For days and days, the pony was alone. He missed his friend and hoped that he would come back. Then one day, he heard a familiar voice. It was his friend!

It turned out his friend had been looking for new places to play. The two ponies were so happy to be together again and they hugged each other and jumped around the stable. From then on, the two ponies stayed together and were never scared or mad at each other again.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to go on an adventure. He found a pin lying in a nearby park. The pin was very shiny and he was so proud to have it. He invited his friends to come and join him in exploring. Everyone was excited and they quickly followed him.

They came across a stream with a rainbow in the sky. The little boy was so proud of the pin because it made the rainbow look even more beautiful. His friends could not believe how amazing it was.

Soon they reached the top of a hill where they had an amazing view of the world. They all sat together and ate ice cream. Everyone was so excited and happy to be on the adventure and the little boy was proud to have found the pin.

At the end of the day they said goodbye and the little boy went home. He was so proud of his pin and the wonderful adventure he had.

Once upon a time, there was a man with a big, hairy beard. He loved to design things with his hands. One day, he decided to make an axe. He worked hard on it for many days until it was perfect.

The man was so happy with his axe that he decided to show it to his friend. But on the way, he tripped and fell. The axe flew out of his hands and hit his friend. His friend was hurt very badly and had to go to the hospital.

The man felt very sad and guilty. He realized that he should have been more careful with his axe. From that day on, he never designed anything dangerous again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She loved to spin around and around. Every night she would spin until the sun went down.

One night, the little girl was spinning when suddenly the sunset was the prettiest sight she had ever seen. She stopped spinning and watched the colors of the sky change from yellow to purple. It was so beautiful.

The little girl knew that sunsets were important, so she promised to always take time to stop spinning and watch the sunset together.

From then on, every evening she would spin until the sun started to go down, and then she would stop and watch the sunset. The little girl felt lucky to be able to enjoy such a beautiful sight.

One day, Little Bear and his Mommy went for a visit. She took him to a place he had never seen before. It was an icy place with lots of snow. As they walked around, Little Bear heard some music. It came from something his Mommy called a radio. It made Little Bear smile. 

When Little Bear asked his Mommy about it, she said it was called a radio and that it played music. 

Little Bear said, "Can I make music with it too?"

Mommy said, "Yes, Little Bear, you can make your own music too. Let's try it together."

So Little Bear and Mommy made music together with the radio. Little Bear was so happy. It was an amazing visit!

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She had a special mission; to collect doves. Everyday she would put on her brightly coloured dress and her sparkly shoes and go out collecting. Every morning she would walk to the park and then look to the sky. Then she would spot a dove and try to catch it in her hands.

Today was a sunny day, and the little girl was feeling very sleepy. She found a big tree to sit under as she watched the doves up in the sky. Suddenly she noticed a dove land on a branch close to her. Gently, she reached out to try and catch it. "Coo-Coo!" the dove said.

The little girl was suprised. She had never heard a dove talk before!

"Hi, little dove" the little girl said. "My name's Daisy. And I'm here to collect doves".

"Well, you caught me!" the dove said. "Let's be friends!"

Daisy was so happy. She had found a special friend and could share her dove collecting mission with him.

Together Daisy and her dove friend went on many adventures and caught lots of doves. Every night before bedtime, Daisy would give her doves a big hug before they flew up to the sky.

That was Daisy's life collecting her special doves, and it was just perfect.

Tom and Mia liked to play in the park. They saw a big tree with many branches. The tree was very old and had many holes. Tom and Mia wanted to make a house in the tree.

They found some wood and some rope. They tied the wood to the branches with the rope. They made a floor and a wall and a door. They were very happy with their house.

"Look, Mia, we have a house in the tree!" Tom said. "We can pretend we are birds or squirrels or pirates!"

"Yes, Tom, this is fun!" Mia said. "But we need a roof. What if it rains?"

They looked around for more wood and rope. They saw a man with a big hat and a long beard. He was sitting on a bench. He had a book and a stick. The book and the stick looked very old.

"Hello, children," the man said. "What are you doing?"

"We are making a house in the tree," Tom said. "But we need a roof. Do you have any wood or rope?"

The man smiled. He opened his book and showed them a picture. The picture was of a tree with a house. The house had a roof made of leaves.

"This is an ancient house," the man said. "People used to live in trees like this a long time ago. They used leaves to make roofs. You can do the same. There are many leaves on the ground. You can tie them together with your rope."

Tom and Mia thanked the man. They liked his book and his stick. They picked up some leaves and tied them together. They made a roof for their house. They invited the man to come and see their house. The man was very proud of them. He gave them his book and his stick as a gift.

"Thank you, sir," Tom and Mia said. "You are very kind. We like your ancient book and your ancient stick. They are very special."

The man hugged them. He said goodbye and left. Tom and Mia played in their house for a long time. They read the book and pretended to be ancient people. They had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Julie. She was a very brave and adventurous girl who loved doing new things. One day, Julie was walking through a dark and scary forest. She was scared, but she kept walking. As she walked, she heard a strange noise. It sounded like some one was talking.

Julie slowly moved closer and closer to the noise until she spotted a man sitting in the shadows. She couldn't see his face, but he was speaking.

"I'm so thirsty," the man said, "I wish I had some of that nice smelling perfume." He laughed.

Julie felt scared, but she was also curious. She thought to herself, "Maybe I should give him some perfume." 
Julie slowly moved closer and closer, but before she could reach the man, he suddenly jumped out of the shadows and grabbed her by the arm.

"Give me your perfume!" he shouted. Julie was so scared, but she still tried to speak.

"Please, let me go," she managed to say. But the man was too angry and wouldn't listen.

He grabbed the perfume from her and ran away, leaving her alone in the dark forest. Julie never saw him again, and that was the last time she ever felt brave enough to do something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very thirsty and wanted some milk. He asked his mommy, "Mommy, can I have some milk please?" His mommy said, "Sure, Timmy. Let me get you a glass of milk."

Timmy was very impatient and wanted his milk right away. He said, "Mommy, I want my milk now!" His mommy said, "Timmy, you need to be patient. The milk is coming."

While Timmy was waiting for his milk, he saw his toy gun on the table. He picked it up and pretended to shoot his mommy. His mommy said, "Timmy, we don't shoot people. That's not nice."

Finally, Timmy's milk arrived and he drank it all up. He was happy and no longer impatient. He said, "Thank you, mommy. I love you." His mommy replied, "You're welcome, Timmy. I love you too."

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a big bow in her hair that she loved to wear every day. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and played on the swings. But when she got off the swing, she noticed her bow was missing! She looked everywhere for it but couldn't find it.

Lily was sad because her bow was her favorite. Her mom promised to buy her a new one, but Lily wasn't sure if it would be as pretty or reliable as her old one. She didn't want it to spoil easily like some of her other bows.

The next day, Lily's mom surprised her with a new bow. It was just as pretty as her old one and Lily was so happy! She put it in her hair and played all day without worrying about it spoiling. Lily realized that even though her old bow was gone, she could still find joy in new things.

Once upon a time there was a rich girl who liked to dress up in fancy clothes. One day, the girl was getting ready to go out and grabbed her favourite umbrella. She ran out and opened it up, ready to fly away.

Suddenly, a child nearby saw her and asked, "What is that?"

The girl smiled and said, "It's an umbrella! I use it to keep me dry if it's raining."

The child was very curious and asked, "Can I try it out?"

The rich girl was more than happy to share and said, "Sure! Here you go!"

The child started to run around with the umbrella, twirling it around and laughing. The girl laughed with her and enjoyed watching the child's joy. When it was time to go, the girl packed up her umbrella and thanked the child for a lovely dress-up day.

Once there was a fat cat named Sebastian. He was always hungry and wanted to eat something tasty.

One day, he saw a luxury rock in the garden. He walked over and started to rock it back and forth. As he rocked, he found a bowl of yummy treats inside.

Excitedly he started to eat from the bowl. Suddenly, a voice said â€œHey Sebastian, what are you doing?â€ It was Sebastianâ€™s best friend Lucy.

Sebastian said â€œI found a luxury rock and there are yummy treats inside it!â€ 

Lucy laughed and said â€œLetâ€™s eat the treats together.â€

Sebastian and Lucy rocked the luxury rock and ate the yummy treats until their tummies were full. After that, they went off to play and had lots of fun.

Lily and Sam are friends. They like to play in the yard. They have a ball, a bike and a doll.

One day, Lily sees a big dog in the yard. The dog is black and brown. It has a long tail and sharp teeth. Lily is scared of the dog. She runs to Sam and hugs him.

"Sam, Sam, there is a big dog in the yard! It looks mean and hungry. What do we do?" Lily says.

Sam is not scared of the dog. He is strong and brave. He thinks the dog is lonely and wants to play. He has an idea.

"Let's offer the dog our ball. Maybe it will like it and be our friend. Come on, Lily, don't be afraid. I will hold your hand," Sam says.

Sam and Lily walk slowly to the dog. They hold the ball in front of them. The dog sees the ball and wags its tail. It barks softly and sniffs the ball. It takes the ball in its mouth and runs around the yard. It looks happy and playful.

"See, Lily, the dog is not mean and hungry. It is just a big puppy. It likes our ball. Can we play with it?" Sam says.

Lily smiles and nods. She is not scared of the dog anymore. She thinks the dog is cute and funny. She and Sam follow the dog and throw the ball for it. The dog brings the ball back and licks their faces. They laugh and hug the dog.

They have a new friend in the yard.

Pete and his mom were in the kitchen. Pete's mom had a bowl full of dough on the counter. "We are going to make cookies, Pete," she said.

Pete touched the dough. It felt rough between his fingers. He didn't like the feeling. "Mom, can we make the dough smooth?" he asked.

His mom smiled. "Yes, Pete. We can use the rolling pin to make the dough smooth. That will improve it."

Pete helped his mom roll out the dough. Together their efforts made the dough nice and smooth.

"We did it!" said Pete happily.

His mom laughed. "Now, let's make some cookies!"

Once upon a time, there was a man. He was very nice and always gave things to people. One day, he had a white cross. He wanted to give it away. So he found a little girl and brought the cross to her.

The little girl was so happy and she said, "Thank you!" But, when the man left, the cross started to feel heavy. The little girl tried to take it off, but it wouldn't move. It was stuck.

The little girl began to cry and she tried to ask for help, but no one came. Finally, she had to carry the cross everywhere she went. No matter where she went, the white cross was always with her.

The little girl never found a way to get rid of the cross. She was stuck with it forever. And that's the bad ending to the story.

One day, a little girl called Lucy was playing in her garden. She was having lots of fun looking at the bees and helping her mum tend the flowers. Suddenly, she saw a stranger. He came closer and closer. Lucy felt scared and helpless. She didn't know what to do.

Lucy ran inside and found her mum. She told her about the stranger and her mum said not to worry. She quickly called Grandma who lived nearby. Grandma came quickly and she and Lucy's mum went to the garden to see what was going on.

When they got there, Grandma shooed the stranger away. Lucy was so relieved. Grandma said it was important to always be careful when strangers go near. Lucy nodded and gratefully thanked Grandma for coming to help. From then on, Lucy was always very careful when strangers came close.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jane. She was spreading candy around with her friends. Everyone was having so much fun; they couldn't stop laughing.

Suddenly, John came over to the group and saw everyone with the candy. He felt envious that he didn't have any.

Jane happily offered John a piece of candy. "It's okay," she said, "We'll share."

John couldn't believe how kind Jane was. He accepted the candy and enjoyed it together with the other children. 

Moral: Sharing brings people closer together and can make everyone happy.

Once upon a time, Tinker the musician was in the forest playing her flute. She played a beautiful, kind melody when suddenly a magical bird flew past. Tinker was so surprised that she accidentally snapped her flute!

Tinker started to cry. "What am I going to do?" she asked herself.

Just then, an elf appeared. "Don't worry, Tinker," the elf said. "I can fix your flute."

Tinker smiled. "Really?" she asked.

The elf nodded. "But," he said, "you have to do something for me first."

Tinker agreed and they soon found themselves in front of an audience of birds and animals. The elf handed Tinker a new flute and said, "Play a kind melody and all will be fixed."

Tinker nodded. She closed her eyes, took a deep breath and began to play. The beautiful, kind melody gently filled the air. Tinker snapped her fingers when the song was done, and suddenly the magical bird flew back past! Her flute had been fixed!

Tinker thanked the elf and went back to playing her flute in the forest. She was the happiest musician ever!

Once upon a time there lived a friendly cat. The cat loved to work. Every day it worked to get food for itself, and then it would go for a walk in the garden.

One day, the cat was working in the garden when it heard a voice. 
"Mew! Mew!" said the voice. 
The cat looked up and saw a little girl. 
"Hi there!" said the girl. "What are you doing?"

The cat purred and said, "I'm working. I'm getting food." 
The little girl smiled and said, "That's cool. Can I help?" 

The cat nodded and said, "Sure! You can help me get food." They worked together, and the cat showed the little girl all the spots it liked to get food from. Soon enough, they had enough for a meal. 

The cat and the little girl were now good friends. They worked together every day in the garden, and the cat always showed the little girl where to get the best food. 

The end.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to make them zoom on the grass and the dirt. They had many cars of different colors and sizes.

"Look at my orange car!" Ben said. "It is very fast and loud. Zoom, zoom, zoom!"

Lily looked at Ben's car and wanted to play with it. She reached out her hand and grabbed it. "I want to play with the orange car!" she said.

Ben was angry. He did not like to share his car. He pulled it back and shouted. "No, it is my car! You have your own car. Give it back!"

Lily was angry too. She did not want to give back the car. She held it tight and cried. "No, it is mine now! You have many cars. I only have one!"

They both started to tug and yell. They did not hear their mom calling them from the house.

"Ben, Lily, what is going on?" mom said. She came to the garden and saw them fighting over the car. She was not happy. She took the car from them and put it on the table. "You two need to learn to share and be nice. No one can play with the car until you say sorry to each other."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They felt bad for making mom angry and for hurting each other. They said sorry and hugged. Mom smiled and gave them a hug too. She gave them each a cookie and a glass of milk. She said they could play with the car together if they promised to take turns and be kind.

Ben and Lily agreed. They thanked mom and went back to the garden. They played with the car and their other toys. They made them zoom and laugh. They were happy and had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was always ready for an adventure. One day, she had a feeling that something special was going to happen. 

So Lucy grabbed her coat and hopped up and down with excitement. Suddenly, a big fat bee flew past her and left a warm trail of chocolate behind. Lucy followed the bee and the sweet smell of chocolate lead her to a secret garden. 

The garden was full of amazing things. Trees shone in the sun and the grass was full of bright colours. But Lucy's eyes were on the chocolate. She couldn't believe her luck! 

Lucy picked one of the chocolates and she was ready to eat it when the bee flew back and lead her to a special corner of the garden. There, she saw a big pile of chocolates waiting for her. 

She couldn't believe her eyes. All the chocolates were for her! She ate all the chocolates until her tummy was full up and ready for a nap. 

Whenever she got bored, Lucy would go back to the secret garden and follow the big fat bee. It would always lead her to wonderful surprises.

Once there was a little boy named John. John was three years old and loved to explore the world. One day, John decided to test the drawer in his bedroom. He opened the drawer and looked inside. It was disgusting. All the drawer had was old, moldy food and cobwebs. John quickly closed the drawer and looked around his room to find something else to explore.

Lily and Ben were playing in their room. They had a big box of toys and a candle. The candle was for when it was dark and they wanted to make shadows on the wall. They liked to pretend they were animals or monsters or fairies.

But today, their mom said they had to stop playing soon. She said they had to go to the dentist. Lily and Ben did not like the dentist. He made their teeth hurt and gave them a bad taste in their mouth. They wanted to delay going to the dentist as long as they could.

"Let's hide under the bed," Lily said. "Maybe mom will not find us."

"OK," Ben said. "But we have to take the candle. It is too dark under the bed without it."

They took the candle and crawled under the bed. They lit the candle and held it carefully. They made funny faces and noises and laughed. They forgot about the dentist for a while.

But then, they smelled something bad. They saw smoke coming from the bed. The candle had burned the sheet. They were scared and dropped the candle. The fire grew bigger and bigger.

"Help! Help!" Lily and Ben shouted. "Fire! Fire!"

Mom heard them and ran to their room. She saw the fire and grabbed a bucket of water. She threw the water on the fire and put it out. She was angry and worried.

"What were you doing with the candle?" she asked. "You could have burned the whole house down. You could have hurt yourselves. You know you are not supposed to play with fire."

Lily and Ben were sorry. They cried and hugged mom. They said they were sorry and they would not do it again. They said they were trying to delay going to the dentist.

Mom sighed and hugged them back. She said she was glad they were OK. She said they still had to go to the dentist, but she would buy them ice cream afterwards. She said they had to be more careful and listen to her.

Lily and Ben nodded. They got ready to go to the dentist. They hoped he would be nice and gentle. They hoped the ice cream would be yummy. They learned their lesson. They would not play with fire or candles again. They would not delay doing what mom said. They would be good kids.

Once upon a time, in a thick forest, there lived a squirrel named Sam. Sam loved to find acorns and play with his friends. One day, Sam found a big acorn under a tree. He was very happy and wanted to show it to his friend, Bunny.

Sam went to Bunny's home and said, "Bunny, look at my big acorn! Let's play with it." Bunny looked at the acorn and said, "Wow, that's a nice acorn! But first, let's pay the tree a 'thank you' for giving us the acorn." So, Sam and Bunny went to the tree and said, "Thank you, tree!"

Sam and Bunny played with the acorn all day. They rolled it, threw it, and even pretended it was a ball. They had so much fun and were very tired. At the end of the day, they put the acorn back under the tree and said, "Thank you, tree, for letting us play with your acorn."

The next day, Sam and Bunny went to find more acorns in the thick forest. They found many acorns and shared them with their friends. And every time they found an acorn, they remembered to pay the tree a 'thank you.'

From that day on, Sam, Bunny, and their friends always said 'thank you' to the trees for giving them acorns to play with. The trees were happy, and the forest was filled with laughter and fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play on her couch all day long. One day, her mom told her that she could not play on the couch anymore because it was getting dull. Lily was very sad and started to cry.

Her mom saw how sad she was and asked her, "Why are you crying, Lily?" Lily replied, "I want to play on the couch, but you don't permit me to." Her mom smiled and said, "I didn't say you can't play on the couch, Lily. I just said it's getting dull. Let's make it fun again!"

Lily was very happy and helped her mom decorate the couch with colorful pillows and blankets. Now, the couch was not dull anymore and Lily could play on it all day long. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for permitting me to play on the couch again!"

Once there was a girl called Annie. One day, she wanted to make something special.

She went to the shop to buy some thread but the thread was so tangled. Annie tried to untangle it but it was too hard.

So she asked her mom for help. Together, they cleaned the thread. Then she made a beautiful dress with the thread.

She also added some spicy-smelling flowers to her dress, to make it even more special. Everyone was so surprised with her new dress!

Annie was very happy and she wore it everywhere she went!

Tom and Sue like to play with paint. They have many colors of paint and big papers to make prints. They dip their hands in the paint and press them on the papers. They excite to see the prints of their hands.

But they do not listen to Mom when she tells them to be careful. They splash the paint everywhere. They make the floor, the walls, and the furniture dirty. They also make their clothes and faces dirty. They do not think about the mess they make.

Mom comes back and sees the paint all over the house. She is not happy. She is angry. She tells Tom and Sue to clean up the mess. She says they cannot play with paint anymore. She says they have to learn to respect the house and the things in it.

Tom and Sue are sad. They do not like to clean up. They do not like to lose their paint. They say they are sorry to Mom. They say they will be more careful next time. They say they will only make prints on the papers.

Mom hugs them and says she loves them. She says she is glad they are sorry. She says they can play with paint again, but only if they follow the rules. She says the rules are to wear aprons, to use a mat, and to clean up after themselves. She says the rules will help them have fun and keep the house nice.

Tom and Sue agree to follow the rules. They thank Mom for giving them another chance. They promise to be more responsible. They learn that playing with paint is fun, but it also needs respect.

Once there was a bear named Gray. He was very dull and didnâ€™t like to play. Every morning he would just sit and rest. No other bear played with him, he was the only one who was so unrest. 

But one day a special bear came to Gray. This bear had a very bright smile and twinkle in her eye. She said, â€œHey Gray! Letâ€™s go rub this big tree!â€ 

Gray was so happy! He decided to rub the tree with the special bear. As they both rubbed the rough bark, Gray felt so happy and alive. The special bear smiled and said, â€œSee, youâ€™re not so dull after all!â€ 

They rubbed the tree together until the stars came out. Now they play together every day, and Gray loves it!

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but they do not share them well. Sometimes they fight over the toys and make a lot of noise.

One day, their mom says, "Lily and Ben, I have a surprise for you. Come and see." She takes them to the living room, where she has a big table. On the table, she has displayed many books, puzzles, and games. "These are for you to play with," she says. "But you have to follow some rules. You have to take turns, and you have to ask before you touch anything. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nod. They are very excited. They see many things they like. Lily sees a book with animals. She loves animals. She asks, "Mom, can I touch this book?" Mom says, "Yes, you can. But you have to let Ben look at it too, when he wants to." Lily says, "OK." She picks up the book and opens it. She sees a picture of a lion. She says, "Look, Ben, a lion! It is big and yellow and has a mane."

Ben sees a puzzle with cars. He loves cars. He asks, "Mom, can I touch this puzzle?" Mom says, "Yes, you can. But you have to let Lily help you too, when she wants to." Ben says, "OK." He picks up the puzzle and starts to put the pieces together. He sees a picture of a red car. He says, "Look, Lily, a car! It is fast and shiny and has four wheels."

Lily and Ben play with the books and the puzzles for a while. They take turns and ask before they touch. They show each other what they find. They have fun. Mom is happy. She says, "You are playing very well. You are being fair and kind. I am proud of you." Lily and Ben smile. They hug their mom and say, "Thank you, mom. We love you."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very nervous. He had lost his toy razor. He loved to pretend to shave like his dad. Every day, he would play with his toy razor. But now, it was gone.

One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. He thought maybe he left his toy razor there. He looked and looked, but he could not find it. Tim was very sad. He missed his toy razor so much. He wanted to find it and play with it again.

Then, Tim saw a girl playing with a toy. He looked closer and recognized it. It was his toy razor! Tim was so happy. He went to the girl and told her that it was his toy. The girl was nice and gave it back to him. After that, Tim was not nervous anymore. He had his toy razor back and could play with it again. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a family who had a very hot day. The mother said to the father, "It's so hot, can you help and get me a fan?"

The father said, "Yes, I will help you." He went outside and searched for a fan. After a while he found one, it was quite old but he thought it would do the job.

He took it home and plugged it in. It started to work but it made a very hard noise. The mother said, "Oh dear, the fan is a bit hard."

The father said, "Not to worry. I can help you." So he worked very hard fixing the fan until it was perfect. The noisy stopped and the house was cool and comfortable.

The family was so happy with the fan. They thanked the father for his help. Moral of the story: It's always a good thing to help.

Billy was an adventurous 3-year-old who dreamed of something wild. One day, he decided to take a walk in the park. He looked around and saw a big tree with a big hole. He looked closer and saw something furry inside! It was a mouse!

Billy leaned in and said, "Hi, little mouse. What are you doing here?" 

The mouse was very excited. "I'm looking for a place to call home!" the mouse replied. 

Billy smiled. He reached into his pocket and pulled out a set of building blocks he had been carrying with him. "I have just the thing for you," he said as he placed the blocks in the hole. 

The little mouse was delighted! He built a small house in the hole and settled in for the night. 

Billy laughed as he watched the mouse settle into his new home. "Good night, little mouse," he said before he walked away, still dreaming of something wild.

Cory was a curious three-year-old. He wanted to explore the world around him and find out what he could see.

One day Cory was playing in the garden and he noticed there was an ugly bug on the ground. He wanted to take a closer view and see what it was, so he asked his mum:

"Mum, can I supply a view?"

Mum smiled and said, "Yes, of course you can, my darling. Just go ahead and take a look."

So Cory carefully bent down and looked closely at the bug. It had lots of legs and antennae! He watched it scuttle along the ground before flying away.

He ran back to his mum, excited and amazed what he had seen.

"Mum, did you see the ugly bug?" he asked.

Mum smiled and said, "Yes, I did. It was quite an interesting view!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. Every day Mia went for a walk with her mom. One day, Mia and her mom were walking when they saw two dogs fighting. Mia was scared and hid behind her mom. "It's okay, Mia," said her mom, "Those two dogs are just fighting." 

Mia looked at the dogs and saw one was white and the other was brown. She wanted to help. "Mom, what can I do?" She asked. 

Her mom said, "We can do something to help the dogs. Let's make a clear saltwater solution." Mia was excited. She grabbed the bowl and filled it with water, while her mom added some salt. Mia stirred it until it was all mixed up. 

The mom poured the clear salt water between the two dogs. It helped stop the fight. Mia smiled and hugged her mom. It was a happy ending!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad. One day, her mom asked her to go to the park and play. Lily was very happy and ran to the park.

At the park, Lily saw a wide tree. She went to the tree and saw a faucet. She turned the faucet and water came out. Lily was thirsty, so she drank some water. Then, she saw a little boy who was also thirsty. Lily said, "Hi, I am Lily. Let's be friends!" The little boy smiled and said, "Hi, I am Tom. Nice to meet you!" They both drank water and played together.

Lily and Tom played and had fun all day. They learned that it is good to share and help others. When they went home, they told their moms and dads about their new friend. Lily and Tom were happy because they learned that sharing and helping others makes everyone happy.

Once upon a time, little Henry was excited for winter. As he lay in bed, he thought about all the fun he would have when the snow came.

Henry's mom asked him what he thought about winter and Henry said, "I like winter because I can play in the white snow!" Henry smiled widely and his mom smiled back.

Then, Henry asked his mom if he could plan a special winter day. Mom said yes and told him to think of a plan!

Henry thought and thought, then announced, "Let's make a snowman!" Henry's mom said it was a great plan and that they would have so much fun the day they made the snowman.

So, Henry continued to think of other things they could do, like make snow angels, have a snowball fight, and go sledding. Finally he said, "We will be so happy this winter!" 

His mom agreed and said, "Yes, we will have a wonderful winter!" 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear. The bear liked to play in the woods. One night, the bear saw the moon in the sky. It was big and bright. The bear liked the moon because it was gentle and calm. 

The bear wanted to touch the moon. So, the bear climbed up a tree. But, the bear lost its balance and fell down. The bear was okay, but it couldn't touch the moon. 

The bear was sad, but then it saw that the moon was still there. The bear smiled and went back to playing in the woods. The end.

Bob was a little boy who had a shiny red bike. He loved riding it around in his backyard. But one day, his bike's pedals wouldn't move. He pushed and pulled and tried to move them, but they wouldn't budge. His daddy tried to help, but he couldn't get them to move either. They both were frustrated and angry.

Then, Bob's daddy said, "My little buddy, we will have to get someone to fix your bike so it can pedal again." But Bob refused. He was determined to get his bike pedaling again, and he didn't want help. He took a deep breath, and he tried pushing the pedals slowly. Finally, he could feel them starting to move. With a big smile, he rode his bike around the backyard. 

Bob had figured out how to make his bike pedal again! He was so proud of himself. Now he could ride the bike really fast again, just like he liked.

Jill and Jack were best friends. They would play together each day.

One day, Jill had to leave for a little while. "Don't worry Jack," she said. "I will be back soon."

Jack felt very worried. He didn't know what to do while Jill was gone. Suddenly, he had an idea! He ran to the kitchen and grabbed a bottle of wine.

Jack smiled as he opened it. He took a big sip and bubbles tickled his nose. He felt a lot better. Suddenly, he had another idea! He would make a necklace with the cork from the wine bottle.

When Jill returned, she was surprised to see Jack wearing the necklace. "It's so unique," she exclaimed.

Jack smiled and felt no more worry. He was happy to share his unique creation with his best friend.

Once there was a wise old lady. One day she went outside her house and saw a board lying in the grass. She seemed to think it was a special board. She took it inside and put it in the corner of her living room.

The next day when the old lady awoke, the board seemed to be glowing. She was so excited. She picked up the board and walked outside. She shouted, "This board is magical!"

The old lady soon found out what the board could do. When she held it up high and sang, wonderful music seemed to play from it. The old lady was so happy and sang all day.
