The old lady was wise and she knew it was important to share this special board with others. So she decided to let all the kids in the neighbourhood play with the board. They sang and danced to the magical music. Soon everyone was having fun!

The old lady and the kids smiled at each other. It seemed like the magical board brought them all together. They shared many stories and laughed a lot. It was a happy day!

Sara and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big bowl of fruit on the table. Sara wanted to try a lemon. She picked one up and smelled it. It smelled sour.

"Can I eat this?" she asked Ben.

Ben shook his head. "No, it is not good. It will make your face funny."

Sara did not believe him. She wanted to see for herself. She bit the lemon. It was very sour. She made a face and spit it out. She did not like it at all.

"See, I told you," Ben said. He laughed at Sara's face.

Sara was angry. She did not like being laughed at. She picked up the lemon again and slapped Ben with it. Ben was surprised. He felt the lemon juice on his cheek. It stung.

"Ow, that hurts!" he cried. He rubbed his cheek.

Sara felt bad. She did not mean to hurt Ben. She just wanted him to stop laughing. She said sorry to Ben.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I did not mean to slap you. I was just mad."

Ben forgave Sara. He said sorry too.

"I'm sorry, Sara. I did not mean to laugh at you. I was just joking."

They hugged and made up. They decided to play with something else. They left the lemon on the table.

An elderly lady came into the kitchen. She saw the lemon on the table. She wondered who left it there. She picked it up and smelled it. It smelled sour.

She smiled. She liked lemons. She squeezed the lemon into a glass of water. She added some sugar and stirred it. She drank it. It was sweet and sour. She liked it a lot.

She said thank you to the lemon. She did not know who slapped it. She did not care. She was happy.

Once upon a time there was a man who lived all alone. He never had anyone around to talk to or play with. He was sad and lonely. That was until one day, when he heard a voice. It suggested he go out into the woods and find some friends. He was curious so he chose to follow the voice.

The man walked through the woods and soon he heard the sound of laughter. The voice had suggested he find some friends and now he had. They were all animals that lived in the woods--a bear, a rabbit and a fox. The man spent his days playing and talking with his new friends.

Even though the man was happy, he still felt something was missing. One day, the bear suggested a campfire. The man thought it was a great idea. They started a fire and gathered around it in a circle.

At first, the fire was empty, but soon stories and songs filled the air. As the group sang and laughed, the man felt truly happy for the first time. He was no longer alone. He was part of a community. And the voice in the woods had made it all possible.

Once upon a time, there lived a bad ostrich. All the other animals in the jungle admired it because it was so beautiful. Every day, the ostrich would go for a stroll in the jungle and it was very happy.

One day, an elephant wanted to admire the ostrich too. So it started following the ostrich while it walked around the jungle. The ostrich did not know why, so it started running away. The elephant kept trying to catch up with the ostrich, but it was too slow.

Just then, the ostrich saw a small bird. It flew so fast and it was so pretty. The ostrich was so amazed that it stopped running. The elephant was happy too and it stopped following the ostrich. 

The ostrich and the small bird admired each other for a little while before flying away in different directions. The ostrich felt so much better now that it was away from the bad elephant. It knew that it was back to its old self again.

One day, a girl named Sue went to her mom's kitchen. She saw her mom kneel down to get a cup. The cup was for coffee. Sue thought coffee was dull. She liked juice better.

Sue's mom said, "Sue, I have a surprise for you later." Sue was excited. She thought about the surprise all day.

In the afternoon, Sue's mom called her to the kitchen. There was a big, bright cup with a straw. Sue's mom said, "Here is your surprise, Sue! It's a new cup for your juice!" Sue was so happy. She knew her mom's coffee cup was dull, but her juice cup was the best.

Once upon a time there was a fierce hut that lived on the edge of a big forest. The hut was made of sticks and was so fierce that it scared away the animals.

One evening when the sun was about to set, a brave little girl remembered where she had seen the hut before. She took a deep breath and started walking towards it. The little girl wasn't scared.

When she finally reached the hut, the little girl looked inside. Although the hut was small, it was filled with lots of warm blankets and food.

The little girl brought her friends to the hut the next day and they all laughed and played there. They decided to make it their secret club house and the fierce hut became their happy hideaway.

From then on the brave little girl remembered how she had found the hut and the adventures she and her friends had there. The little girl had made a true friend in the fierce hut.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Pete. He was three years old and liked to shout when he played.

One day, Pete was running around in his backyard. It was getting dark, so his mom called to him, "Pete, it's time to come inside!" Pete was having so much fun that he didn't hear her at first. So, his mom shouted louder and said, "Pete, come inside now!"

Pete ran inside hoping it wasn't too late. He saw a big, yellow sun in the sky, and he shouted with glee. He was so excited to see the sun and thought it was a sign that it was safe to go out and play again. 

When Pete looked out the window again, he noticed it was getting darker. He glanced up at the yellow sun and wished that it could stay and play with him longer. Pete sighed and said goodbye to the yellow sun, knowing that it was time to go to bed.

Tim likes trains. He has many trains at home. He plays with them every day. He makes them go fast and slow. He makes them stop and go. He makes them say choo-choo.

One day, Tim goes to the park with his mom. He sees a big train on the tracks. He wants to ride the train. He asks his mom, "Can we ride the train, please?"

His mom says, "Yes, we can. But we have to wait. The train is not available now. It is busy. It will come back soon. Then we can ride it."

Tim waits with his mom. He is excited. He watches the train go by. He counts the cars. He waves to the people. He hears the whistle.

After a while, the train comes back. It stops at the station. The conductor says, "All aboard! The train is available now. Come and ride with us!"

Tim and his mom bring their tickets. They get on the train. They find a seat. They look out the window. They see the trees, the flowers, the animals, and the other trains. They enjoy the ride. Tim is happy. He loves trains.

Once upon a time in a big forest there lived a tiny caterpillar. He was so small and fragile that he could barely move around. He had never seen another caterpillar like him.

One day while he was crawling along, he heard a voice. It was a magical voice that said, "Hello, little caterpillar!" The caterpillar was so happy and he spoke back to the voice. The voice told him, "I'm a fairy and I can help you find other caterpillars like you!"

The fairy helped the tiny caterpillar find a big group of caterpillars. There were so many of them! The little caterpillar was so excited he couldn't speak. He made a lot of new friends that day! Every day, the caterpillar and the other caterpillars would gather together to eat and play.

The little caterpillar was so happy to have found his friends. He knew he had to be careful and delicate as he was still so fragile, so he moved around very gently. He made sure to take good care of himself and he had the best time with his new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved fashion. She spent all of her time imagining what it would be like to have the perfect outfit for her. Every day, she would go searching for new clothes that she could wear.

One day, she found the most perfect dress. It was her favourite colour, and it fit her perfectly. She was so excited, she decided to wear it that same day.

When she got to school, all the other students crowded around to admire her dress. She was so proud and happy. She knew that it was the best choice she had ever made.

But then her teacher told her she couldn't wear it. The dress was too fancy, too 'fit' for school. She felt so sad and embarrassed. Tears ran down her face, and she had to go home without her perfect dress.

The little girl was never able to wear her dress again. She still remembers it with sadness. She never imagined it would end this way.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named John. John was healthy and strong. He loved to go exploring. One day John decided to go to the park.

As he was walking in the park, he stumbled on a big pile of leaves. He got very excited as he kept exploring. He stumbled again and saw something shiny. It was a little wake! John was so happy.

He took the wake and showed it to his mom. His mom said that it was very special and it showed how healthy he was. Then she said he needed to go to bed, as he had to get up early the next morning to go to school.

John put the wake under his pillow and went to bed. He had lots of sweet dreams. In the morning, he remembered the exciting adventure he had with the little wake he found in the park. He smiled, feeling healthy and happy.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy named Jimmy. One cold day, Jimmy was playing with a knife in his yard. He thought it was fun to use the knife to cut things. 

Out of the corner of his eye, Jimmy saw his dad, who said to him, "Jimmy, knives are not toys. You must be very careful with them, or you could get hurt!"

Jimmy was scared and put the knife away. From then on, he was more careful whenever he was holding a knife.

The moral of the story is that we should always increase our care and caution when using sharp objects like knives.

Once there was an elderly man who lived by himself. He was sad because he had no one to keep him company. One day, he went for a walk and noticed something odd on the ground. It was a mitten! He picked it up and gained a little hope. He looked around for whoever lost the mitten but couldn't find anyone. So, he decided to go home with the mitten and have it as a companion. 

He took care of the mitten and named it Mitt. Mitt was a great listener and the elderly man found joy in talking to it. After a while, the elderly man realized that the mitten had brightened his day and he was no longer alone. 

The man and Mitt continued to spend their days together and the elderly man even gave Mitt a warm bed to sleep in. The man was happy and thankful that he had gained a special new friend.

Mama was having a lot of trouble with her car. It wouldnâ€™t start, and the engine made funny noises.

â€œWhatâ€™s wrong mama?â€ asked the 3 year old child.

â€œMy car is broken,â€ replied mama.

â€œCan you repair it?â€

Mama smiled. â€œI sure can, with some help.â€

The little girl helped mama take the broken pieces of the car to the repair shop. They worked together to get the car fixed.

Finally, after a few days, mama got the car back in working order.

â€œHey look mama! The car is fixed!â€ the little girl said excitedly.

Mama gave her a big hug. â€œYes, we fixed it together. Now we can go anywhere we want!â€

Katy was a three year old who loved flowers. She looked at them with her big eyes while they fluttered in the wind, and the beautiful colours captivated her.

One day, Katy's dad took her to the garden centre to pick out a new flower for the family's garden. She skipped along happily, admiring the flowers around her.

Katy admired one beautiful yellow flower especially. "This is it, Daddy!" she said as she pointed at the flower.

"Are you sure, Katy? Does it make you feel comfortable?" her dad asked, wanting her to be sure. 

"Yes, Daddy," Katy said. She knew that this flower would be special, and she had great value for it. 

"That's great," her dad said, giving her a hug. Together, they bought the flower and planted it in the garden. 

Every day, Katy would go to see it and admire it. The flower's beauty never faded, and she held it in great value.

John was a little boy. He liked to play in his garage. One day, John was in the garage when he heard a strange sound. He went to see what it was and saw a wild animal. It was a fox! It jumped around the garage and then ran away. John was very excited and ran to tell his mom. Mom said that foxes like to play in garages sometimes. John was happy he got to hear a wild animal!

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful dog named Spot. Spot had a toy gun that he loved to play with. He would run around the yard and pretend to be a hero. Spot was very happy.

One day, Spot met a new friend named Fuzzy. Fuzzy asked, "Can I play with your gun?" Spot thought about it and decided to trust Fuzzy. They played with the gun together and had lots of fun.

Later, Spot and Fuzzy saw a big ball stuck in a tree. Spot had an idea. He used his toy gun to knock the ball down. Both friends were so happy. They knew that trusting each other was good, and they played together every day after that.

Once upon a time, there was a fragil clock. It was made of very thin glass and was very special. Every day, the clock would make a chiming sound at exactly the same time. It was so nice that the whole house enjoyed the singing of the clock.

One day, the clock stopped making the chimes. Everyone became sad because they missed the singing. So the mom went to find a special man to fix the clock.

The man was a clock expert. When he saw the clock, he knew he could help. He gently touched the clock and asked it to start singing again. He repeated his words over and over and finally the clock began to chime again. 

The whole family was delighted that the clock was singing once more. From then on, they took better care of the fragile clock, making sure that it was securely placed and never dropped. The clock repeated its chimes every day and the family was very happy.

The little girl had a thick coat on her back. Everywhere she looked there were people trading things. One man traded shoes for coins, another were swapping hats for bread. She watched with wide eyes as the trades were made. 

Soon she was asked to trade too. She was asked to give her coat in exchange for some vegetables. After much thought, she decided to do it. 

As soon as she completed the trade she dreamt of having a thick coat again. She dreamt of a big, warm coat that would keep her safe from the cold. 

The next day she headed back to the market. There she saw a coat hanging outside one of the shops. It was thick and warm just like in her dreams. She traded some of the vegetables she had gotten earlier and the coat was hers. 

The little girl happily walked home wearing her new warm and thick coat.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the kitchen with Mom. Mom is making soup for lunch. She tells Sara and Ben to be careful. The soup is very hot and spicy.

"Spicy means it will make your mouth burn," Mom warns. "Do not touch the pot or the spoon. And do not taste the soup until it is cool."

Sara and Ben nod. They promise to listen to Mom. They play with their toys on the floor. But Ben is curious. He wants to know how spicy the soup is. He sees Mom go to the phone. He thinks she is not looking.

Ben sneaks to the stove. He reaches for the spoon. He dips it in the soup. He brings it to his mouth. He takes a sip.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Ben cries. He drops the spoon. He runs to the sink. He turns on the water. He drinks from the faucet. His mouth is on fire.

Mom hears Ben. She runs to the kitchen. She sees the spoon on the floor. She sees the soup on the stove. She sees Ben at the sink.

"Ben, what did you do?" Mom asks. She is angry and worried.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Ben says. He is still drinking water. "I wanted to try the soup. But it was too spicy. It hurt my mouth."

Mom hugs Ben. She is glad he is not hurt. But she is also disappointed. "Ben, you broke your promise," she says. "You did not listen to me. You were not careful. You could have burned yourself."

"I know, Mom," Ben says. He feels bad. He looks at Sara. Sara is shaking her head. She is not happy with Ben.

"Ben, you have to be more obedient," Mom says. "Spicy things are not for little kids. They are for grown-ups. Next time, you have to wait until I say it is okay."

"Okay, Mom," Ben says. He is sorry. He wants to make Mom happy. He wants to make Sara happy. He wants to make a new promise. "I will not do it again. I will be a good boy. I will listen to you. I will be careful."

Mom smiles. She kisses Ben. She is proud of him. She is proud of Sara. She loves them both. She says, "That's a good promise, Ben. I believe you. Now, let's clean up this mess. And then we can have some soup. But not too spicy. Just right for you and Sara."

Lila and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw some big kids coming. The big kids looked mean and angry. They wanted to take Lila and Tom's toys.

"Give us your toys, or we will hurt you!" one of the big kids shouted.

Lila and Tom were scared. They did not want to lose their toys. They did not want to get hurt. They hugged each other and held their toys tight.

"No, these are our toys! Go away!" Tom said.

The big kids laughed. They moved closer to Lila and Tom. They reached out their hands to grab the toys.

"Stop! Leave them alone!" a voice said.

Lila and Tom looked up. They saw Sam, their older brother. Sam was strong and brave. He came to the park to protect them. He stood in front of Lila and Tom and faced the big kids.

"These are my sister and brother. You cannot take their toys. You cannot hurt them. Go away, or I will make you go away!" Sam said.

The big kids did not laugh anymore. They saw that Sam was stronger than them. They did not want to fight him. They did not want to start a war. They turned around and ran away.

Lila and Tom were happy. They thanked Sam for saving them. They gave him a hug and a kiss.

"You are the best brother ever!" Lila said.

"You are our hero!" Tom said.

Sam smiled. He hugged them back. He was glad he could protect them.

"Let's go home and have some cookies," Sam said.

Lila and Tom nodded. They picked up their toys and followed Sam. They felt safe and loved. They were a happy family.

Once upon a time, there was a little boat that loved to sail on the big blue sea. The boat was made of wood and had a white sail that would catch the wind and take it wherever it wanted to go. Suddenly, Grandma put down the scissors and hugged grandpa. She kissed his forehead and said that she still loved him, even when he was naughty. Grandpa smiled and was relieved that he was not in trouble anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. It was her birthday and she was very excited! Her mommy made a huge cake with lots of frosting and candles on top.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. They were very playful and happy.

But then a big dog came and took their ball. The dog ran away with the ball in its mouth. Tim and Lily were sad and scared. They did not know what to do.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny. The bunny was walking through the forest when he saw a funny-shaped stone. He hopped over to look at it more closely. The bunny touched it, and suddenly the stone began to roll away. The bunny tried to chase the stone, but it rolled faster than he hopped.

The bunny followed the stone until it rolled down into a deep, dark hole. Unfortunately, his foot got stuck and he couldn't get it out!

The bunny started crying, when suddenly he heard a voice. "Don't cry, little bunny," the voice said. "I can help you!"

It was a tiny green frog who hopped out of the hole. "See this rope?" the frog asked, pointing to a rope near the hole. "You can climb out if you grab hold of the rope and pull." 

The bunny was so happy that he thanked the frog and grabbed hold of the rope. He pulled, and he pulled, until finally he was out of the hole. 

The bunny looked at the stone and said, "I'm glad I didn't get hurt, like that stone did." He hopped off, happy to be back on solid ground.

Once there was a little boy, he was three years old. He saw a trunk by the shore which was very deep and he decided to open it. He asked the trunk what was inside, but it chose to ignore him. He kept asking and the trunk kept ignoring him.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy had a favorite cup. It was a big, red cup. She liked to drink from it every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Ben. He was so restless that he could hardly sit still.

One day, Ben's mom brought him to the park. She said he could play for as long as he wanted.

So he ran and jumped and had lots of fun! When it got too dark, Ben's mom said it was time to go.

But Ben was not done having fun and he didn't want to go. He pleaded with his mom to stay a bit longer.

"Mom, please!" Ben said.

His mom smiled and said, "If you pass this test, I will give you a special reward. All you need to do is sit still for one minute without moving."

Ben quickly agreed, and he sat still and quiet for the whole minute. When it was over, his mom gave him a big hug and a special reward.

Ben was so happy and proud of himself. He had passed the test, and he was rewarded with love. From then on, Ben never felt so restless again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to taste new foods. One day, Tim went to a big fair with his mom. There were many fun things to see and do at the fair. Tim saw a big, light balloon in the sky. He wanted to get one for himself.

Once upon a time, there was a playful bee. He loved to fly around the meadow and play. One day he decided to visit a nearby flower. 

As he arrived, he noticed the flower had a strange smell. He was curious, so he wanted to learn more. He buzzed around the flower and started to sniff it.

Mommy was packing up the car. She was very tough and she had to do it all by herself. She put bags and boxes in the car. Then she called to daddy, "Daddy, can you please help me with the dishwasher?"

Once upon a time, there was a big bean. It was the biggest bean in the garden. All the other beans were small. The big bean was very proud.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Billy. He was a very curious boy, and one day he decided to go somewhere special. He put on his shoes and grabbed his hat, and off he went! He walked and walked, until he came to a big hill. It was too big for him to climb, so he sat down on the ground and thought.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy cart. He would push it around the house and fill it with his favorite toys.

Lila and Ben are twins. They like to play outside in the sun. They have a big ball and a small bike. They share them and have fun.

One day, it is very hot. The sun is bright and makes them sweat. They drink some water and look for some shade. They see a big tree with thin branches. They run to the tree and sit under it.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, called Sam and Ryan. Sam loved playing hockey and would skate on the frozen pond with his friend Ryan. Sam would pick up the hockey stick and hit the frozen puck around the pond.

Once upon a time, there was a family who wanted to do something fun. They all decided to go to the hockey rink. When they arrived, it was very exciting. Everyone was wearing different things. There were some people wearing red shirts, blue pants and green shoes.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play and have fun all day long. One day, Benny was hopping through the forest when he saw a big oak tree. Benny thought the oak tree was very important because it was so big and strong.

Once, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty, pale dress. Lily loved her dress very much. She also had a small, friendly cat named Tom. They played together all day.

A little boy named John was walking down a street one day. He saw a big barrel near the side of the street. He wondered what was inside the barrel.

Once upon a time, there was a playful bunny named Benny. He loved to hop and play all day long. One day, Benny met a little girl named Lily. They became friends and played together in the park.

Once upon a time, in a little house, there lived a girl named Lily. Lily had a big, original mirror that she loved. She would look into the mirror and make funny faces every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved winter because he could play in the snow. One day, Timmy went outside to play, but he saw a fierce snowstorm coming. The snow was blowing everywhere and it was very cold.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emily. She was three years old and loved to explore the world around her.

"Ha ha, you're not a dancer, you're a wet rat!" the boy laughs.

"Apologize to Anna right now. You don't pour water on people. That's rude and mean." Anna's dad says.

Anna feels better. She smiles and says thank you. She decides to forgive the boy. She asks him if he wants to dance with her. The boy nods and says yes. They dance around the fountain together. Once there was a little girl named Lily who was three years old. She was a very fair girl with lots of curiosity. She wanted to understand everything around her.

Sammy was very excited. He was going to go see his grandmother and he couldn't wait. When he arrived, he saw a shiny bunch of ash on the ground. It sparkled in the sun and Sammy couldn't resist. He picked up the ash and ran off.

Sammy's grandmother was in the garden, but when she saw Sammy running with the ash, she got angry. She shouted, "No Sammy, you must not steal!" Sammy was scared so he put the ash down where he found it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her mommy gave her a package to examine. It was a big, brown package with a silly smiley face on it.

Once upon a time, Annie had a diary. It was bright pink and shiny. Every day, she would write silly things in it. Things like her favourite animals and her best friends names. Whenever Annie had a secret, she would write it down in her diary.

Jim had a whistle. He loved to whistle with it. One day, he saw something in the sky. It was bright and loud. It was a helicopter! Jim was very excited. He wanted to make the helicopter come down. So he whistled with his whistle. The helicopter came down and surprised Jim.

Jack and Jill were playing chase in the hall. Jack was running and jumping and having lots of fun. Jill got a bit careless and tipped over a flower pot. It made a crash and a mess!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved winter and playing in the snow. One day, she went outside to build a snowman. Her mommy said, "Be careful, Lily. Don't get too cold."

Lily replied, "I'm not cold, Mommy. I'm proud of my snowman." She set the carrot nose and the coal eyes on the snowman's face. Suddenly, the wind picked up and it started to snow harder.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She was very excited when she heard the bell. It was big, noisy and bright. Jane wanted to see what was making all of the noise. She ran out her front door and to the end of the street. 

She saw a big truck with a big bell on top. It was so exciting for Jane. She waved and shouted to the driver of the truck, "Hey, can I ride in your truck?" 

The truck driver smiled and said, "Yes, of course! Hop on in." Jane was so thrilled to get a ride in the noisy but fun truck. She waved goodbye to her family and went off with the truck driver. 

The truck drove around the town and beeped the bell every time it stopped. Jane was so happy and excited to see all the wonderful things the town had to offer. Every time the bell sounded it made Jane happier and louder. 

The truck driver dropped Jane off at her house, honking the big bell goodbye. Jane thanked the driver and ran inside to tell her parents all about her exciting ride in the noisy bell truck.

Once upon a time, there were two chambers. They were far away from each other. Each chamber had a smart creature living inside. The creatures were so intelligent. They decided to work together to help each other.

One day, they noticed that the chambers were starting to separate from each other. They knew they needed to keep their chambers together. So, they worked together and figured out a way to keep the chambers close.

They put together a long, strong string and tied one end to each chamber. Then, the smart creatures held on the other ends and kept the chambers together.

Then, each chamber stayed close and the two intelligent creatures never had to worry about separating again.
The end!

Once upon a time there was a wise old squirrel. He was ancient, and incredibly clever.

Every day, the wise old squirrel would try to win something special. He spent many days looking for something amazing to win.

One day, he found a really big prize. It was hidden inside a big tree. The squirrel was so excited, he ran to get it.

The squirrel was the first to find it. He was so happy, he had won! He was so excited, he ran back to his family and told them the good news.

Everyone celebrated the wise old squirrel's win. He was very proud of himself for winning the big prize.

Once upon a time, there was a lively little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her kite. Lily's kite was very special because it had brightly coloured streamers that would blow in the wind. 

One day, Lily took her kite to the park to have fun with it. But as she was getting ready to fly it, it suddenly flew away!

Lily was so sad. She ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, my kite flew away!" 

Her mom smiled and said, "It's okay, sweetheart. We can find the kite and go back to the park to fly it again."

So, Lily and her mom drove back to the park. When they got there, Lily's kite was still flying in the sky!

Lily's mom hugged her and said, "You forgive the kite for flying away and now it can forgive you for letting it go. That's why it stayed."

Lily was so happy! And from then on, whenever Lilly flew her kite, she always remembered to forgive it for occasionally flying away.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They also like to run and chase each other.

One day, Lily has to go to the doctor. She is sick and has a fever. She cannot play with Tom. Tom is sad. He misses Lily a lot. He does not want to play alone.

He goes to the park and sees a boy. The boy is bigger than Tom. He has a ball. Tom wants to play with the ball. He asks the boy, "Can I play with you?"

The boy says, "No, this is my ball. Go away." He kicks the ball hard. The ball flies in the air and lands on the roof of a house. The boy is angry. He says, "Now look what you did. You made me miss my ball. How will I get it back?"

Tom says, "I'm sorry. I did not mean to make you miss your ball. Maybe we can get it back. There is a ladder over there. We can climb it and reach the roof."

The boy says, "No, that is too hard. The ladder is very high. I am afraid of heights. You go and get it. You are smaller. You only need to climb an inch."

Tom says, "No, that is not fair. You are the one who kicked the ball. You should get it. It is not easy to climb a ladder. It is dangerous. We should ask for help."

The boy says, "No, I don't want to ask for help. I don't want anyone to know that I lost my ball. You have to do it. Or I will tell everyone that you are a baby and a coward."

Tom says, "No, you are the baby and the coward. You are mean and selfish. You don't know how to share or be nice. You are not a good friend. I don't want to play with you. I want to play with Lily. She is kind and fun. She knows how to miss someone. She is a good friend."

Tom leaves the boy and goes home. He hopes that Lily will get better soon. He wants to see her and play with her again. He learns that it is better to have a good friend than a bad one. He also learns that it is not good to miss something that you can't have. He is happy with what he has. He is happy with Lily.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to find twigs and make things with them. Tom made a sword and Lily made a crown. They were having fun.

Then they saw a big twig on the ground. It was long and thick and had many branches. It was unique. They both wanted it.

"Look, a big twig!" Tom said. "I want it for my sword!"

"No, I want it for my crown!" Lily said. "It is pretty!"

They ran to the twig and grabbed it. They pulled and pulled. They did not want to share.

"Let go!" Tom said.

"No, you let go!" Lily said.

They were angry and sad. They did not play anymore.

Then they heard a voice. It was their friend Ben. He was walking his dog.

"Hi, Tom and Lily!" Ben said. "What are you doing?"

"We are fighting!" Tom said.

"We want this twig!" Lily said.

Ben looked at the twig. He had an idea.

"Why don't you share the twig?" Ben said. "You can both use it for your things. It has enough branches for a sword and a crown. And you can play together."

Tom and Lily thought about it. They liked Ben's idea. They let go of the twig.

"Okay, let's share the twig!" Tom said.

"Yes, let's share the twig!" Lily said.

They smiled and hugged. They thanked Ben. They used the twig for their sword and their crown. They played together. They were happy.

Once there was a dancer named Lily. She was very cheerful and always smiled when she was dancing. One day, she wanted to enter a special dance contest. But no one wanted to accept her to join in.

Lily was sad when nobody accepted her. She slowly walked away from the group of dancers, feeling a bit lonely. Suddenly, she heard a voice. It was a friendly fairy! The fairy said she wanted to help.

The fairy cast a spell, and suddenly the other dancers cheered. They said they would accept Lily to be part of the dance contest. Lily smiled and thanked the fairy. She twirled around and was so happy to be accepted.

Lily danced her way to the center of the stage and wowed the audience with her moves. In the end, Lily won the dance contest and everyone cheered for her! She was so happy and cheerful.

One day, a small boy named Tim went for a walk with his mom. They saw a big automobile on the street. It was red and shiny. Tim liked the automobile very much. He wanted to touch it, but his mom said no.

They kept walking and found a warm, soft ball on the ground. Tim picked it up and gave it a big squeeze. It made him happy. But then, a girl named Sally came running. She said the ball was hers and wanted it back.

Tim did not want to give the ball back. He liked it too much. But his mom said he had to share. Tim felt sad but gave the ball back to Sally. Sally smiled and asked if Tim wanted to play with her. They played together with the warm ball, and Tim felt happy again.

Once there lived a sweet family. The family was made up of a mom, dad and their daughter. Every season they set aside time to do something special together.

One Spring, the daughter was feeling very selfish. She wanted to do fun things with only herself and refuse to have any fun with her family. So when her family asked her to join them for a picnic, she said no!

"We love spending time with you as a family," said her mom.

"But I don't want to come," said the daughter, "I want to be alone!"

But her parents didn't give up. They kept asking, and finally her dad said, "We'll make it fun for you. You can pick the food and games you want to bring."

This motivated the daughter to come along. She set up the picnic, picking her favorite foods and games. Together, the family enjoyed the picnic season. They laughed and had a lot of fun, and the daughter was no longer so selfish.

Once upon a time there was a kind man. He wanted to have a parade. So he went out and rang the bell. All of his friends heard the bell and came running. They had all kinds of fun things for the parade. They had flags and candy and balloons! Everyone was in the parade, even the animals! The parade was so much fun. They laughed and sang and danced all day. When the parade was over, the kind man thanked everyone for coming. They all said goodbye and wished him well. That was the best parade ever!

One morning, Tim and his mom went to the park. They saw a big tree with a cat in it. The cat was very high up and needed help to get down. Tim wanted to help the cat, so he asked his mom if they could remove the cat from the tree and make it safe.

Tim and his mom took the cat home. They gave it some food and water. The cat was happy and safe with Tim and his mom. They played with the cat all day and had lots of fun. Tim was glad that they could help the cat and make it safe.

Once upon a time in a land far away, there lived a young girl. Her name was Sarah and everyday she would wake up in her beautiful bedroom. She would look out the window and see bright birds, green trees and blue sky. One morning, Sarah woke up and decided she wanted to explore the world.

The young girl was in awe and said, "This place is so beautiful". She spent the rest of the day playing and discovering the world around her. At night, she went back home, dreaming of all the beautiful things she'd seen.

One day, a tall man went for a jog. He liked to run in the park. The sun was bright and the sky was blue. While he was jogging, he saw a little girl. The little girl was looking up at the sky.

The little girl said, "I want to catch a star." The tall man looked up and saw many stars in the sky. He wanted to help the little girl catch a star. So, he tried to jump high to reach a star. But he could not jump high enough.

The tall man and the little girl tried many times to catch a star. They jumped and jumped, but they could not reach the stars. They were very sad. The stars were too high in the sky. In the end, they could not catch a star, and they went home with no star.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to hop around and play with his friends in the forest. One day, Benny's friend, a chipmunk named Charlie, saw a beautiful velvet ribbon on the ground. Charlie was enthusiastic and said, "Wow, this is so pretty!" 

Benny replied, "I worry that someone might be looking for it. We should try to find the owner." 

Charlie didn't want to listen and kept the ribbon for himself. The next day, they saw a sad deer looking for her lost velvet ribbon. Benny remembered what he said and told Charlie that they should return the ribbon to the deer. 

Charlie realized his mistake and apologized to the deer. The deer was happy and thanked Benny and Charlie. Benny felt proud that he did the right thing and helped someone in need. The moral of the story is that it's always better to do the right thing, even if it's hard.

Once upon a time there was a boy who only wanted one thing - a big TV. Every day he asked his mom and dad for an enormous TV, but they would just tell him, "No!" 

One morning he woke up and ran to the living room. He couldn't believe his eyes, there in front of him was a huge TV! He jumped up and shouted, "Yay! I get a TV!" 

The boy ran over to the TV and tried to turn it on, but it didn't work. He shook it and shook it and then he heard a voice. He quickly stepped back in surprise. 

The voice said, "Hello, little boy! I'm the TV genie! You get a wish for my TV and I'll make it come true!"

The boy thought for a moment and then he said, "I want the TV to make me happy and play games all day!"

The TV genie said, "Your wish is granted! Enjoy your enormous TV!" 

The boy was so excited and he played games all day long with his enormous TV! The End.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl called Mandy. Mandy loved to play and explore and one day, she found a pair of scissors. She thought they were so cool and was so cheerful!

Mandy was so thirsty, she gulped and gulped until she was all done. She went back to playing and was having the best day ever! She brought her scissors and kept finding new, exciting things to do. 

Mandy was so cheerful, she even caught a fish with her scissors. She was so proud of herself and went home to tell her mom. Her mom was so proud of her and gave Mandy a big hug. 

And that was the end of Mandy's exciting day!

Once upon a time, there was a bossy bird named Betty. Betty lived in a big nest in a tall tree. She loved to tell the other birds what to do.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom had a toy named Zipper. Zipper was a hard toy car. Tom loved to play with Zipper every day. They had lots of fun together.

Tom and Sue decided that Zipper and Daisy should marry. They had a big party with cake and juice. Zipper and Daisy were now married and they played together all the time. Tom and Sue were happy that their toys were friends, just like them. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and chase butterflies. One day, she saw a beautiful butterfly with tight wings fluttering around her garden. She ran after it, but it flew away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to swing on the playground. She would go higher and higher until she felt like she was flying. From that day on, Lily would swing every day and think about her dream world. She knew that even though she couldn't visit it in real life, she could always go there in her imagination while swinging on her favorite purple swing.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved yogurt, especially the tasty strawberry kind. One day, Timmy's mommy bought him a big container of strawberry yogurt.

Later that day, Timmy and Sally decided to race outside. Timmy was very fast, but Sally was faster. Suddenly, Timmy tripped and fell. Sally ran over to him and asked if he was okay. Timmy said he was fine, but he realized that sharing with his sister was more important than having all the yogurt to himself. So, he offered Sally some of his tasty yogurt and they both enjoyed it together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, he went to the park with his mom and saw a beautiful statue. It was big and shiny and Tim wanted to touch it.

His mom said, "Don't touch the statue. It's very old and fragile. We don't want to break it."

Sam was a 3 year old boy and he loved playing outdoors. One nice day he went outside and saw something exciting. His dad was showing him two purple tires. Sam was so excited - he had never seen anything like it before! 

His dad explained that these were special tires made for a bike. Sam was so happy he was about to get a new bike with these tires. He couldn't wait to take it for a ride. 

The next day, Sam was ready to go for a ride with his new bike. He put on his helmet and his dad helped him get on. As he started to pedal his bike, he felt so happy as the purple tires carried him along. 

Sam had so much fun zooming around the neighborhood with his new bike. He felt so much freedom and joy with the purple tires. He was one happy 3 year old!

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly high in the sky and sing songs. One day, Tweety saw a big zigzag in the sky. Tweety didn't know what it was, so he asked his friends. They guessed it was a storm coming.

Tweety decided to fly away from the zigzag, but he got lost. He flew and flew, but he couldn't find his way back home. He was scared and sad. But then, he remembered something his mom had told him: "If you ever get lost, just follow the sun and you will find your way back home."

So, Tweety followed the sun and it led him back home. He was so happy to be back in his perfect little nest. Tweety learned that sometimes it's okay to guess, but it's always better to ask and learn. And if you ever get lost, just remember to follow the sun.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a red hat that he loved to wear every day. One day, Timmy and his mommy went to the store to buy some candy. Timmy was so excited to get some candy! 

When they arrived at the store, Timmy's mommy noticed that his hat was too tight. She helped him take it off and they went inside. Timmy saw all the candy and his eyes got big. He picked out his favorite candy and his mommy paid for it. 

As they left the store, Timmy put his hat back on. It felt much better now that it wasn't too tight. Timmy was so happy to have his candy and his hat back on his head. They walked home and Timmy ate his candy with a big smile on his face. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a baby bird who lived in a tree. He was a small bird, and very lonely. He wanted a friend to play with, but he had nobody.

Once there was a dad, a mom, and a little boy named Max. They all wanted to go on an adventure. So, they packed up their things and headed off.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to go for walks in the forest with his mommy. One day, they found a trail that they had never seen before. It looked scary, but Timmy wanted to explore it.

Lily liked to watch yoga on TV. She saw people bend and stretch and breathe. She wanted to try yoga too. She asked her mom if she could join her.

"Sure, Lily, you can do yoga with me. But first, we need to eat breakfast. What do you want?" Mom said.

"I want toast and jam and juice," Lily said.

Mom made toast and jam and juice for Lily. She gave her a plate and a cup. Lily took a big bite of her toast. She made a face. "Yuck! This jam is sour!" she said.

Mom tasted the jam. She frowned. "Oh, no, you're right. This jam is bad. I'm sorry, Lily. Let me get you some honey instead," she said.

She went to the kitchen and looked for honey. She did not see it on the shelf. She opened the cupboard. She saw a big mess. The honey jar was broken. There was honey everywhere. And there was a bear. A big, brown bear. It was licking the honey. It looked at Mom. It growled.

Mom screamed. Lily heard her scream. She ran to the kitchen. She saw the bear. She was scared. She grabbed her mom's hand. They ran out of the house. They called for help.

The bear finished the honey. It was full. It was sleepy. It saw the TV. It saw yoga. It liked yoga. It went to the living room. It lay down on the mat. It did yoga. It bent and stretched and breathed. It was happy. It snored.

Once upon a time, there was a wise bear. He had a spear given to him by a great king. The bear was so wise that he used the spear in special ways. He could use the spear to help him find food!

One day, the bear was looking for something special to eat. He found a special fruit. The bear liked it so much he wanted to have it all for himself. But, the fruit was starting to rot and the bear knew he had to share. 

So, he called upon his animal friends. He said, "Come help me! I have found a special fruit, but it is starting to rot. I wish to share it with all of you."

His friends were so very thankful! They ate the fruit and shared stories until it was gone. The bear felt so wise for sharing the fruit, and it made him happy to see his friends happy too.

Simon was a small boy. He looked up at the sky. He admired the roof of the house. There was a tree in the yard. The leaves were all dead. They weren't moving like when the wind blew. Simon didn't understand why.

His dad came outside and said, "When the leaves fall from the tree, it means that it is getting colder outside." Simon looked confused. His dad said, "The leaves get stiff and die, like when you take a rest from running around."

Simon looked up at the roof of the house and then at the leaves on the ground. He wanted to admire the leaves and the roof, but he now knew that they were dead. Maybe someday the leaves would come back. Simon thought that was a wonderful thing to imagine.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her soft teddy bear and go on adventures. One day, Lily and her mommy went to the lake to row a boat. They had so much fun rowing and looking at the fish in the water.

After they finished rowing, Lily wanted to go on another adventure. She saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. But her mommy said it was too dangerous and they should go home. Lily was sad but listened to her mommy.

On the way home, they saw a big dog. Lily wanted to pet the dog but her mommy said it was not safe. The dog was not friendly and might bite her. Lily listened to her mommy and did not use her hand to pet the dog.

When they got home, Lily was happy to see her daddy. But he was not feeling well. He had a fever and was very sick. Lily's mommy called the doctor but it was too late. Daddy passed away and Lily was very sad. She hugged her soft teddy bear and cried.

Sam had a watch that he liked very much. It was blue and shiny and it made a tick-tock sound. He wore it every day and showed it to his friends. He felt mighty with his watch.

One day, a man came to his house. He had a big bag full of toys and books. He said he wanted to sell them to Sam and his mom. He saw Sam's watch and said, "What a nice watch you have! Do you want to trade it for something in my bag?"

Sam looked at the bag and saw many things that he wanted. He saw a red car, a yellow ball, a green dinosaur, a brown bear, and a big book with pictures. He thought they were all very fun and cool. He said, "Yes, I want to trade my watch for something in your bag. What can I have?"

The man smiled and said, "You can have anything you want, but only one thing. Choose wisely, because you can't change your mind later." He opened the bag and let Sam see all the things inside.

Sam thought hard. He liked his watch, but he also liked the toys and books. He wanted to have them all, but he knew he had to pick one. He looked at the red car, the yellow ball, the green dinosaur, the brown bear, and the big book. He wondered which one he would play with the most. He wondered which one would make him feel mighty.

He decided to trade his watch for the big book. He liked books because they had stories and pictures that he could look at and read. He thought the book would make him learn new things and have new adventures. He said, "I want the big book, please."

The man nodded and said, "Okay, here you go. Give me your watch and take the book. It's a fair trade." He took Sam's watch and gave him the book. He said, "Thank you, Sam. Enjoy your book. Goodbye." He left with his bag and Sam's watch.

Sam opened the book and saw many pages with words and drawings. He felt happy and excited. He said, "Mom, look at my book! It's so big and nice! Can you read it to me?"

His mom smiled and said, "Sure, Sam. I'm glad you like your book. It looks very interesting. Let's sit down and read it together." She hugged him and said, "You are a mighty boy, Sam. You made a good choice."

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Joe and Molly. Joe and Molly loved to play together. One day, Joe said to Molly, "Let's go get pizza!" Molly clapped her hands and was very happy. 

So, Joe and Molly went to the pizza shop. When they arrived, Molly chose a big piece of pizza and Joe chose a small one. But when Molly tried it, she said, "This pizza is bad!" Joe laughed and said, "Maybe you just don't like pizza!" 

Molly thought and then said, "Maybe I do like pizza, but this one is bad!" Joe shrugged and ate his pizza anyway. Molly was sad, but Joe said, "Let's go somewhere else. I bet they'll have better pizza!" 

So, they went to another pizza shop and this time, Molly liked her pizza a lot. She smiled and said, "This pizza is good, Joe!" Joe smiled back and said, "I told you it would be better!" And then the two friends ate their yummy pizzas and had a wonderful time.

Once there was a little furry kitten. She was so tiny and cute that everyone wanted to hold her. One day she became curious and went off to explore. 

Soon, she came to a place with lots of tall grass. She decided to go in and play. Suddenly, she felt something sharp on her paw. It was a cut!

The little kitten was scared, but soon she saw something amazing. It was a big, furry rabbit! He had lots of soft fur and she wanted to snuggle up to him. The bunny saw the kitten's cut and used his paw to rub it gently. Suddenly the cut was all better!

The kitten was so happy and the bunny too. They became the best of friends and played together all the time. Whenever the kitten had a problem, she knew the bunny would always be there to make it better.

Once upon a time, there was a prince. He was on a mission to find a magical treasure. On the way, he stumbled upon a mountain. As he looked upon the mountain, he saw a precious gem drop down from the top. It was sparkling in the sunlight!

The prince was so excited that he ran up the mountain to get the gem. Just as he was about to reach it, a giant eagle flew down and snatched it up. The prince was so envious!

He shouted out, "Hey eagle! Please give me back my gem!"

The eagle laughed and replied, "Go away prince! I see this shiny treasure and I want it for myself! You're not getting it back!"

The prince was very sad, but he didn't give up. He thought of a plan. He shouted out, "Wait, eagle! I could give you something even better!"

The eagle didn't believe the prince, but he asked anyway, "What could you possibly give me that's better than this gem?"

The prince replied, "I could give you something even shinier and more precious. Do you want to find out what it is?"

The eagle was intrigued and said, "Yes, show me!"

The prince then reached beneath his cape and pulled out a beautiful diamond necklace. The eagle was so amazed that it dropped the gem and flew away with the necklace.
