Bobby was running through the garden, looking for something fun to do. He suddenly saw a post that looked very interesting. He slowly walked over to it and was surprised to find a big, yellow blanket covering the post. He immediately wanted to see what was underneath, so he quietly lifted up a corner of the blanket. Underneath, he found a smiling caterpillar for him to play with! Bobby was so excited, he held the caterpillar close to his chest and ran back to the house to show his mom. She smiled at Bobby, and thanked him for finding the caterpillar. Bobby thanked the post for being so quiet and keeping the caterpillar hidden until he could find it.

Once there was a wise old man who had a lot of gas. He wanted to enjoy it, so he decided to take a drive one day. He drove to a wonderful park and enjoyed the nice view. He got out of his car and started to smell the beautiful flowers. He felt the sun on his face and he smiled.

The man walked around the park, enjoying the sights and smells. He heard the birds chirping and he saw the trees blowing in the wind. He spotted a squirrel and watched it scurry around.

The man went to a nearby lake and watched the fishes swimming around. He wondered if they enjoyed the water as much as he enjoyed it.

The wise old man finished his day feeling happy and content. He was thankful to have so much gas for his car. It allowed him to travel and enjoy the world around him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. One day, Jane wanted to go on an adventure with her horse. She went outside and hopped on the horse. The horse began to pass over the grass and Jane was so happy.

Suddenly, they came to a muddy pond. Jane said to her horse, "Let's pass through here, my horse!" But the horse was scared and shaking. Then it said, "No, I'm scared! It is too dirty for me!"

Jane thought about it for a moment. Then she said, "Don't worry! I'll take care of you and make sure you don't get dirty." So Jane and the horse passed through the pond, and Jane made sure the horse was careful and didn't get too dirty.

When they were done, Jane was so proud that she and her horse made it through the muddy pond. She said to her horse, "We did it, my horse! We passed through the muddy pond and we were so brave!" 

And Jane and her horse continued to pass through the grass happily.

John was playing in the garden when he heard the birds singing. He looked up and saw a pretty sunset coming. The sky was dark with pink and orange colors. He smiled when he saw how beautiful it was.

John wanted to show his mom the sunset so he ran over to her. She said it was even prettier when it was closer. They both watched as the sun slowly went down.

They stayed out until the last bit of the sun went away. As the sky got darker and the stars came out, John said it was the prettiest sunset he had ever seen. His mom smiled and said, "Yes, it was so beautiful." They went back inside and John smiled all night, thinking about the pretty sunset he had seen.

Jane and her dad were walking by the beach one evening when they noticed a stunning sunset. Jane's dad suddenly said, "Let's visit the sunset!" and Jane clapped with delight.

So they kept walking until they reached the horizon and saw the sun setting. Jane gasped, "Wow! It's beautiful!"

But then something strange happened. Suddenly, a silly bird flew in and started making loud noises. Jane's dad said, "That bird is really stupid!"

Still, Jane wasn't scared. She just smiled and said, "Let's stay to watch the sunset."

So that's what they did. They watched the sunset and enjoyed the beauty of the birds. In the end, Jane and her dad said goodbye to the sunset until their next visit.

Tom and Lily liked to play near the station. They saw big trains and cars and people. They liked the noise and the colors. Sometimes they found things on the ground, like cans and coins and papers. They liked to lift them and look at them.

One day, they saw a big box near the station. It was brown and had a red sign on it. They did not know what the sign meant. They thought it was a picture of a flower. They wanted to see what was in the box. They ran to the box and tried to lift it.

But the box was not harmless. It was a bomb. It had a timer and a wire. When Tom and Lily lifted the box, they moved the wire. The bomb made a loud beep and then a big boom. The box exploded and hurt Tom and Lily and the station and the people. There was fire and smoke and noise and pain.

Tom and Lily did not play near the station anymore. They did not play at all. They were gone. The people were sad and angry. They said Tom and Lily should not have touched the box. They said the box was dangerous and had a warning sign. They said Tom and Lily should have listened and learned.

The moral of the story is: Do not touch things that you do not know. They might be harmful and hurt you and others. Listen to the signs and the people who know better. Be careful and safe when you play.

Once upon a time, there was a family. The family had a mom, a dad and a little girl. The little girl's name was Amy. Sometimes, Amy felt uncomfortable. That's when her parents were there to protect her.

One day, Amy wanted to eat something special. She wanted to eat jelly. Mommy and Daddy said she could have some of the jelly. They brought some jelly over and Amy ate it up! 

Amy felt so happy. She was so glad her parents were there to protect her and make her feel safe. Every time she felt uncomfortable, she knew that her parents were there to take care of her. That made her feel so much better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mommy clean the house. One day, her mommy told her they needed a new mop because the old one was too heavy for her to use. Lily didn't understand what "heavy" meant, but she knew it must be hard to use.

The next day, Lily went to the store with her mommy. She saw a big, shiny mop and asked her mommy if they could buy it. Her mommy said they didn't have enough money for that one, but she promised to show Lily a special surprise when they got home.

When they got home, Lily's mommy showed her a brand new mop that was just the right size for her to use. Lily was so happy and excited to help clean the house with her new mop. She knew it wouldn't be heavy like the old one, and she couldn't wait to try it out. From that day on, Lily helped her mommy clean the house every day with her new, light mop.

Once there was a girl called Lucy. She was three and she loved to play with her friends. One day, she was in a very big office. In front of her was a man in a big chair. He was the boss and he was looking at her very seriously.

She felt embarrassed and didn't know what to do. Then she remembered the thing that her mom had taught her. She put her hands together and bowed. She bowed very low, to show the boss that she was sorry.

The man smiled and said: "That's very nice of you Lucy." He was very pleased.

Lucy was happy that she had remembered how to show respect. From then on, she always bowed when she was in an office.

One day, a playful lady was walking in the park. She saw a little boy who was playing with a toy car. She smiled, and the boy smiled too.

Suddenly, he heard a noise and he dropped his car. He saw a big bird in the sky. The bird flew towards the lady and it struck her shoulder with one of its wings.

The lady was startled and she shouted. The boy quickly ran to help her. He showed the bird his toy car, and the bird flew away.

The lady thanked the boy for saving her. She said that he was so brave and playful. She gave him a big hug and he went back to playing with his car in the park.

Sam loved to play with his toy plane. He made it zoom and fly in the air, and he pretended he was the pilot. He liked to make loud noises like the plane's engine and the wind.

One day, he was playing with his plane in the living room, when his mom called him for lunch. He did not want to stop playing, so he ignored her. He kept flying his plane around the sofa and the table, and he did not hear his mom calling him again and again.

Then, he heard a loud crash. He turned around and saw that his plane had hit a vase on the shelf. The vase fell and broke into many pieces on the floor. Sam was scared and sad. He had broken his mom's favorite vase. He knew he was in trouble.

He paused and thought about what he had done. He realized he had been very rude and careless. He should have listened to his mom and put away his plane. He felt sorry and ashamed.

He ran to his mom and hugged her. He said he was sorry for breaking the vase and for not listening to her. He said he loved her and he would be more careful and respectful. His mom was angry, but she also loved him. She hugged him back and said she forgave him, but he had to help her clean up the mess and learn from his mistake.

Sam learned that playing is fun, but he also had to follow the rules and be polite. He learned that being a pilot is not only about flying smooth, but also about being responsible and safe. He learned that saying sorry is important, but so is changing his behavior. He learned a valuable lesson that day.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. Jack and Jill went up the hill to play a game. The game was silly. Jack and Jill took turns pushing a big button. Every time they pushed the button they would separate.

Jack shouted: "Let's try again!" So they took turns pushing the button again. This time the button spun them around and around until they were dizzy.

Jill giggled and said: "That was so silly!" 

Jack laughed and said: "Let's try the button one more time!" So they pressed the button again and this time it sent them soaring high into the sky!

Jack and Jill flew around, but eventually the button sent them back down to the ground. They were safe and sound, but something was different this time.

Jack and Jill were no longer together. The button had separated them! But it was all worth it in the end, because a silly game can bring people together in the most unexpected of ways.

There were two children named Sammy and Sarah. They loved to play together. 

One day, Sammy said to Sarah, "Let's pretend to be dancers!" Sarah was so excited. 

They both grabbed their staffs, which were like sticks. Sammy put on some soft music as Sarah got ready to dance. 

Sarah was very graceful. She moved her staff around elegantly, swirling and twirling in the air. Sammy copied Sarah, trying to be graceful like her. 

They both laughed and smiled as they pretended to be dancers. They had so much fun together!

Once there was a little boy named Ben. Ben liked to play with his silver toy cars. One day when Ben was playing outside it began to rain. His toy cars looked so sad and wet! Ben wanted to make them dry. He found some easy steps.

First, Ben got the towel. He decided to dry the cars one by one. Ben wiped each car with the towel, taking care to make sure it was dry. He rubbed hard until each car was completely dry.

After all his cars were dried, Ben was pleased to see them sparkling like new! He put them all away and went inside to eat a snack.

Ben learned that day that if something gets wet, he can make it dry again. And it doesn't need to be hard - just easy!

Once upon a time, there was an ancient fairy named Priscilla. She had the power to make things glow. Every day, Priscilla would fly around the world, spreading the happiness from her glowing to everyone she visited.

One day, Priscilla decided to visit the children of the village. Each little one was so excited when they saw her arrive. "Hi Priscilla! Can you make us glow too?" they asked.

Priscilla smiled and said, "Yes, I can! Would you like me to give you some magical makeup that will make you glow?"

The children all replied with loud cheers, and Priscilla flew over to the nearest tree. She waved her wand and suddenly, a mountain of makeup appeared! Each of the children grabbed a pot of special glowy dust and put it on.

They were amazed to see how brightly they all glowed. Priscilla gave them a final wave and flew off, satisfied that she had shared her magic with the children.

Molly was a small puppy. She had a fluffy black coat and soft, brown eyes. One day, Molly went outside to play in the snow. It was very cold and her paws were soon freezing! She started to shiver when she noticed a small bird on the ground. 

Molly wanted to help the bird keep warm, so she held her tiny paw over the bird and kept it nice and cosy. The bird stayed there for a while until it was nice and warm. It thanked Molly for helping and flew away.

Molly was so happy that she had done a good deed, but soon she was cold again. She ran back to her parents to find some warmth. They cuddled her close and soon she was no longer cold. She was so happy that she didn't have to be cold ever again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was only three years old and her name was Emily. She was walking in the forest with her friend. The forest was enormous. As they walked, they saw something strange. It was a pill that was in the middle of the path.

Emily asked her friend what it was. Her friend told her that it was a magical pill. He said that if she ate it, it would make her dreams come true.

Emily listened carefully. She looked around and then she made up her mind. She picked up the pill and ate it. 

As soon as she ate the pill, something magical happened. In front of her, an enormous castle appeared. Emily and her friend were so excited!

Emily said, â€œThis must be the castle that my dreams came true!â€. They ran up to the door and rang the bell. 

When the door opened, a kindly old woman stood in the doorway. She smiled and told them to come in. They stepped inside and the adventure of a lifetime began!

Once upon a time, there lived an owner and a beautiful flower. The flower was very special because it could bloom without water! The owner of the flower was deaf but he was so proud of its beauty. He would show it off to all of the other owners in the neighbourhood. Every morning, the flower would bloom brightly, and all of the other owners were amazed. One day, the owner decided to give the flower to a 3-year-old child, to share its beauty and make her happy. The child was so excited and ran around playing with it every day. As time went by, the flower became part of her family and she watched it bloom with pride and joy. The owners around the neighbourhood always caught a glimpse of its brilliant colours, even though its new owner wasn't deaf.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with many flowers. They wanted to go up and see.

"Come on, Lila, let's climb the hill!" Tom said.

"No, Tom, I don't want to. It is too high and steep. I am scared." Lila said.

"Don't be scared, Lila. It will be fun. We can see the whole park from there. And maybe we can find some bugs or birds." Tom said.

He took Lila's hand and tried to pull her. But Lila refused. She shook her head and let go of his hand.

"Please, Lila, please. Just try. I will help you. I will hold your hand and we will go slow." Tom said.

He looked at Lila with big eyes and a smile. Lila looked at Tom and then at the hill. She saw the flowers and the sun. She saw a little mist in the air. She thought it looked pretty and soft.

"Okay, Tom, okay. I will try. But you have to be careful. The flowers are delicate. We don't want to hurt them." Lila said.

"Okay, Lila, okay. I will be careful. The flowers are delicate. We will be gentle." Tom said.

They held hands and started to climb the hill. They stepped on the grass and avoided the flowers. They felt the mist on their faces and the sun on their backs. They laughed and talked and sang. They reached the top and looked around. They saw the whole park and the sky. They felt happy and proud. They hugged and cheered.

"We did it, Lila, we did it! We climbed the hill!" Tom said.

"We did it, Tom, we did it! We saw the mist and the flowers!" Lila said.

They sat on the hill and enjoyed the view. They played with the bugs and the birds. They picked some flowers and made a crown. They had a lot of fun. They were glad they tried.

Once upon a time, there was a big, pretty microscope. It was very expensive. A boy named Tim had the microscope. Tim liked to tell his friends about it. He was very happy.

One day, Tim and his friend Sam played with the microscope. They looked at little things. They saw bugs and leaves. They had fun. But then, they started to fight. Tim wanted to tell Sam what to do. Sam did not like that.

Sam got mad. He pushed the microscope. The expensive microscope fell down. It broke into little pieces. Tim was very sad. Sam was sad too. They were not friends anymore. The end.

One day, Mary saw an ugly rainbow in the sky. She smiled and said, "Wow!" She wanted to mark the rainbow so she found some bright, colourful paper and markers.

When she was done, she ran outside with the paper and markers and held them up to the sky. She wanted to mark the rainbow so she waved her arm around in circles, making a big, colourful circle.

But then it started to rain. Mary was so disappointed! She wanted to show everyone her beautiful rainbow.

But then, something wonderful happened! A rainbow appeared in the sky! It was so bright and beautiful! Mary quickly ran outside and started to mark the rainbow again. She waved her arm around in circles and made a pretty, colourful circle all around the rainbow.

When she was done, Mary smiled and said, "That's the best ugly rainbow I ever saw!"

Once upon a time there were two friends, Ben and Jack. Ben loved to bounce and Jack loved to mix things. One day, they decided to have a day of play. Ben and Jack took turns, Ben bouncing and Jack mixing.  

But while they were playing, they accidentally broke their parents' mixer. Ben and Jack were so scared and they ran away, not knowing what to do. 

A nice lady in the neighbourhood saw that the boys were scared and very sorry. She said to them: "Boys, be careful next time. Sometimes things can break when we are playing so we must be careful."

Ben and Jack looked at each other and nodded. They decided to go back home and clean up the mess they made. 

The boys knew that from then on they were always going to be careful when playing, so nothing like this would happen again. 

Moral of the story: Be careful when playing so you don't make a mess!

Once upon a time, there was a lazy night. Everyone was so relaxed. All the animals were cozy in their beds. But one little bunny had something special in mind! 

He hopped and hopped and hopped until he found exactly what he was looking for: a big tree. He hopped up onto one of the branches, and the leaves tickled his nose. He squinted his eyes and smiled. 

He lay there, looking up at the stars and the moon. He was so relaxed, he dozed off and went to sleep. 

When he woke up again, he remembered that it was a lazy night. He hopped down from the tree and scurried back home. He was so happy and soon fell asleep, dreaming about his lazy night.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around outside. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. At the park, she met a boy named Timmy. Timmy was not very nice to Lily. He took her toys and called her names. 

Lily's mommy reminded her to be kind to everyone, even if they are rude. But Lily did not listen. She wanted her toys back and she wanted to show Timmy that she was not afraid of him. So, she took her toys back and called Timmy a rude name. 

The next day, Lily went back to the park. But this time, Timmy was not there. Instead, Lily saw a judge. The judge told Lily that Timmy's mommy had called the police because Lily had been rude to Timmy. Lily was very scared and did not know what to do. 

In the end, Lily learned that being rude to others can have bad consequences. She wished she had listened to her mommy's reminder to be kind.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big wind called a tornado. It was very scary and made all the trees and houses shake. A little boy named Timmy and his mommy hid in a small, safe room until the tornado went away. 

After the tornado, Timmy and his mommy went outside to see what had happened. They saw that the big wind had knocked down lots of trees and made a big mess. Timmy's mommy told him that tornadoes are very ancient and have been around for a very long, long time. 

As they walked around, Timmy slipped on a wet leaf and fell down. His mommy helped him up and they continued to look at all the damage the tornado had caused. Timmy was happy that he was safe and sound with his mommy.

Lila and her mom were in the car. They wanted to go to the zoo. Lila loved the zoo. She wanted to see the wild animals. She hoped to see the lions and the monkeys and the giraffes.

But the car was not moving. There were many cars in front of them and behind them. They were stuck in traffic. Lila was sad. She looked out the window and saw the red lights and the honking horns.

"Mom, why are we not moving?" she asked.

"Because there is too much traffic, honey. Sometimes there are too many cars on the road and they make a big jam. We have to wait until the jam clears," mom said.

"How long do we have to wait?" Lila asked.

"I don't know, honey. Maybe a few minutes, maybe a long time. It depends on how fast the cars can move," mom said.

Lila sighed. She did not like waiting. She wanted to go to the zoo. She hoped the traffic would go away soon. She hoped the zoo would not close before they got there. She hoped the wild animals would not be too tired or too hungry to play with her. She hoped they would have fun at the zoo. She hoped, she hoped, she hoped.

One day, a big, bossy cat and a little, shy dog were playing near a pond. They saw a net with many fish in it. The cat said, "I want to eat the fish!"

The dog said, "No, we should let them go back to the pond." The cat did not like that idea. The cat tried to slap the dog with its paw, but the dog moved away.

The dog said, "Please don't be mean. Let's be nice to the fish." The cat thought about it and said, "Okay, we can let them go." They opened the net and let the fish swim back to the pond. The cat and dog were happy, and they played together all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around in the park. One day, she saw a butterfly and made a wish to catch it.

Lily tried to catch the butterfly, but it flew away. She started to cry because she really wanted to catch it. A kind lady saw her crying and asked what was wrong.

Lily told the lady about her wish to catch the butterfly. The lady said, "Don't cry, it's fine. You can try again another day." Lily stopped crying and smiled. She thanked the lady and went back to playing with her toys.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy who was very busy. She wanted to design something special for her baby. So she went to get some materials to make something special. 

"Ah, now I just need some fabric!" she said. 

On her way to the shop, her baby started to itch really badly. She turned to him and asked: "What's wrong, baby?" 

The baby just pointed at his neck and said "Itchy!".

Momma smiled and said "I think I know just what to design for you! Let's go home and see what I can do!"

At home, Mommy got to work. She used the fabric to design a cozy scarf. Finally, it was finished. Mommy showed it to the baby and he was so happy! He hugged it tight and said: "No more itchy now!"

Mommy smiled and said: "See? Designing can be fun!"

Once upon a time, there was a kind man named Mr. Smith. He was very wealthy and lived in a big house. One day, he went to the park and saw a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was sad because he lost his toy car.

Mr. Smith asked, "What's wrong, little one?" 

Timmy replied, "I lost my toy car. I can't find it." 

Mr. Smith smiled and said, "Don't worry, I have a joke that might make you feel better. Why did the banana go to the doctor?" 

Timmy shrugged his shoulders. 

"To get a peel-ing!" Mr. Smith laughed. 

Suddenly, Mr. Smith remembered something. He went back to his house and came back with a toy car. "I think this might match the one you lost," he said. 

Timmy was overjoyed and thanked Mr. Smith. From that day on, they became good friends and played together often.

Once upon a time there was a jolly girl named Pinky. She lived in a town by a big road.

Every day, Pinky liked to peek out the window and watch the cars go by on the road. She liked to guess what the people inside the cars were doing and where they were going.

One day, Pinky was peeking out the window when she saw a car with a funny looking animal in it. It was a friendly looking pup. Pinky smiled and waved as the car drove past.

The pup saw her and waved too and Pinky was so excited. She ran out the door and chased after the car, following the pup until she could no longer see the car on the road.

Pinky was sad that the pup was gone but she still felt jolly inside. She smiled and went back to peeking out the window and watching the cars go by.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They had a big blanket and some toys. They wanted to have a picnic under the sun.

"Let's spread the blanket here, Ben," Lily said. She put the blanket on the grass and smoothed it with her hands.

"OK, Lily," Ben said. He opened the toy chest and took out some plates, cups and food. He put them on the blanket. "Look, we have sandwiches, juice and cookies. Yum!"

They sat on the blanket and ate their picnic. They talked and laughed and shared their food. They felt happy and warm in their chests.

"This is a lovely day, Lily," Ben said. He smiled at his sister.

"Yes, it is, Ben," Lily said. She hugged him. "You are a lovely brother."

They finished their picnic and packed their toys. They folded the blanket and put it in the chest. They held hands and went back to the house. They had a lovely time in the garden.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw a big cage with a bird inside. The bird was blue and yellow and had a long tail. It looked very sad.

"Hello, bird," Lily said. "Why are you in the cage?"

The bird did not answer. It only made a soft noise.

"Maybe he wants to fly," Ben said. "Let's help him."

Lily and Ben looked around. They did not see anyone who owned the cage. They decided to open the door and let the bird out. They thought they were doing a good thing.

But when they opened the door, the bird did not fly away. It flew to Lily's shoulder and bit her ear. Lily screamed and tried to shake the bird off. The bird was not sad. It was angry and mean.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. "Get him off me!"

Ben ran to help Lily. He grabbed the bird and threw it back in the cage. He slammed the door and locked it. He was scared and sorry.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked.

Lily touched her ear. It was red and sore. She was hurt and mad.

"No, I'm not okay," Lily said. "That was a bad bird. He tricked us. He was not adorable. He was evil."

Lily and Ben learned a lesson. They learned that they should not touch things that do not belong to them. They also learned that they should not trust strangers. They did not recognize the bird's true nature. They almost did not escape from his bite. They ran away from the park and never played with the bird again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved candy very much. One day, she went to the store with her mom and saw a big jar of candy. She asked her mom if she could have some, but her mom said no because she had already had too much candy that day.

The little boy was so happy and thanked Lily for being so gentle and kind. Lily felt happy too, knowing that she had helped someone else. She realized that caring about others was even better than having candy.

When the penguin came back home after his adventure, he decided that from then on he would take daily walks so he could find more exciting places to visit. Soon, people from near and far would know the popular penguin from his daily walks.

Once upon a time, there was a baby bunny who loved to play. He hopped around the meadow and enjoyed the sunshine. One day, he saw something shiny, it was a fork! As Lucy stood there in awe, she knew that she had found something truly incredible and special.

Once upon a time, there was a big yellow bird. He was so sad and felt so gloomy. He wanted to find some friends to make him feel better. He flew around looking in many places but he could not find any.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who liked to play pretend. One day she found a funny jellyfish in the ocean. She thought it was so funny that she wanted to keep it and take it home with her.

But the jellyfish didn't want to leave its home in the ocean. It swam away when the little girl tried to catch it. She had to try again and again but the jellyfish kept swimming away!

The little girl got sad. She wanted the jellyfish to be her pretend friend. But it seemed as though the jellyfish did not want to be her friend.

One day there was a little dog called Ted. He was very happy and he loved to go jogging in the park. He especially loved it when he found a nice bone to chew on while he was jogging.

One day, Ted was jogging around the park when he found an old, grey bone. He thought it looked really tasty so he picked it up and started to chew on it. But the bone was very, very hard. It was too hard for Ted to eat and it made his teeth ache.

Ted stopped and looked at the bone. It was so terrible. He decided to drop it and find something softer. He went back to jogging and found a delicious piece of meat. Ted was so happy he started to run around and bark with joy. He had such a fun time that he forgot all about the terrible bone.

Lily and Tom were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two coal eyes. They named him Frosty.

"Hello, Frosty!" Lily said. "You are our friend. We will play with you every day."

"Yes, we will," Tom said. "But we have to be careful. The sun is very bright. It can make you melt."

Frosty smiled. He liked Lily and Tom. They were very kind. But he was also scared. He did not want to melt. He wanted to stay with them.

One day, the sun was very hot. Lily and Tom went inside to have lunch. Frosty felt very warm. He saw a big puddle under his feet. He was melting!

"Oh no!" Frosty said. "I have to escape. I have to find a cold place."

He looked around. He saw a sled near the fence. He had an idea. He jumped on the sled and pushed it with his feet. The sled started to move. It went down the hill. It went very fast. It made a zoom sound.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom!" Frosty said. "This is fun. But where am I going?"

He saw a big lake at the bottom of the hill. The lake was icy. It was frozen. Frosty was happy. He thought he would be safe there.

But he was wrong. The ice was thin. It could not hold his weight. When he reached the lake, the ice cracked. Frosty fell into the water. He felt very cold. He felt very wet. He felt very sad.

"Help, help, help!" Frosty said. "I made a mistake. I want to go back. I want to see Lily and Tom."

But no one heard him. No one saw him. He sank into the water. He disappeared.

Lily and Tom came back from lunch. They looked for Frosty. They saw the sled near the lake. They saw the hole in the ice. They knew what happened.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "Frosty is gone. He escaped. He melted."

"That's so sad," Tom said. "We loved him. He was our friend."

They hugged each other. They cried. They learned a lesson. They learned that sometimes it is better to stay where you are. They learned that sometimes escaping is not the answer. They learned that sometimes you lose what you love.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who loved to play outside. One day, while playing in the dirt, he fell into a hole and went underground. It was dark and scary down there, but the bunny was brave. He looked around and saw that everything was filthy and covered in dirt.

The bunny started to cry because he didn't like being underground. But then he remembered that he had a towel in his pocket. He took it out and used it to dry his tears. Then he wiped his dirty paws and face with the towel, and he felt a little bit better.

After a while, the bunny found a way to climb out of the hole and back into the sunshine. He was so happy to be outside again! From that day on, he made sure to be more careful when playing near holes in the ground. The end.

Once there was a man called Jim. Jim liked to look at things very carefully. One day he decided to go for a walk in the park. As he walked, he noticed a cobweb. It was in the corner of the park, and it was very original. It had a pattern of spiders and some stripes. Jim wondered who had made it. He decided to explore and find out.

He found a small spider in the middle of the cobweb. It was moving very slowly and carefully. Jim said 'hello' to the spider. The spider looked up and smiled. Jim knew it was the original maker of the cobweb. Jim thanked the spider for the beautiful cobweb, and then he continued his walk.

Jim was so happy to have found the original maker of the cobweb. He continued to notice things around the park. He noticed some colourful birds on a tree and some red flowers on the ground. He noticed the sound of the breeze blowing around him. It was a wonderful day in the park for Jim.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the store with her mommy. They were looking for some lemons to make lemonade. They found some lemons, but they were very expensive.

Tom and Anna liked to play in their big wardrobe. It had many clothes and hats and shoes that they could try on. Sometimes they pretended to be kings and queens, or pirates and fairies, or doctors and teachers.

One day, they found a big red cape in the wardrobe. It was soft and shiny and had a golden clasp. Tom put it on and said, "Look, Anna, I am a superhero! I can soar in the sky and save the world!"

Anna laughed and said, "You are silly, Tom. You cannot soar in the sky. You need wings or a plane or a rocket to do that."

Tom said, "No, I don't. I just need to believe and run fast and jump high. Watch me!" He ran to the window and opened it. He felt the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He said, "Here I go!" and jumped out of the window.

Anna screamed and ran to the window. She was scared and worried. She looked down and saw Tom lying on the grass. He was not moving. She cried and shouted, "Tom, Tom, are you okay? Please wake up!"

A wise old owl was sitting on a branch near the window. He saw what happened and flew down to Tom. He said, "Hoo, hoo, little boy, what were you thinking? You cannot soar in the sky with a cape. You are not a superhero. You are a human. Humans need to be careful and listen to their sisters. They are wise and love you."

Tom opened his eyes and groaned. He felt pain in his legs and arms and head. He saw the owl and said, "Who are you? Are you a superhero?"

The owl said, "No, I am not a superhero. I am an owl. I can soar in the sky with my wings. But I do not save the world. I just watch and learn and teach. You should do the same."

Tom said, "I am sorry, owl. I was silly and foolish. I wanted to soar in the sky and have fun. But I did not think and I did not listen. I hurt myself and I scared Anna. I love Anna. She is wise and kind."

The owl said, "Hoo, hoo, that is good, little boy. You learned a lesson today. You should always be careful and listen to your sister. She loves you too. Now, let me help you. I will call your mom and dad. They will come and take you to the doctor. He will make you feel better. Then you can play in the wardrobe again. But remember, no more jumping out of the window. Okay?"

Tom said, "Okay, owl. Thank you for helping me. You are wise and nice. Can I be your friend?"

The owl said, "Hoo, hoo, of course, little boy. You can be my friend. And I will be yours. But only if you promise to be careful and listen to your sister. Deal?"

Tom said, "Deal, owl. Deal." He smiled and hugged the owl. Anna ran down the stairs and hugged Tom too. She was happy and relieved. She said, "I love you, Tom. You are my brother. And you are my friend."

The owl said, "Hoo, hoo, what a happy ending. You are a lucky family. You have each other. And you have me. Now, let's go and find your mom and dad. They will be worried too. Come on, let's go." He flapped his wings and soared in the sky. Tom and Anna followed him. They held hands and looked up. They saw the owl and the cape and the sun. They felt the wind and the grass and the love. They were happy and grateful. They learned a lesson today. They learned to be careful and listen and love. And they learned to soar in their hearts.

Once there was a famous bear who lived in the woods. His name was Bumble. One day Bumble was bored, so he decided to go for an adventure.

Everyone was so proud of Bumble. He had done the big task and was now famous in the woods. He smiled to himself as he swam back to the shore. He had done it!

Lily was an adventurous girl. She liked to explore new places and find new things. One day, she went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a big green slide and wanted to try it.

She ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. She looked down and saw how high it was. She felt a little scared, but also excited. She slid down very fast and laughed. She liked the slide a lot. She wanted to do it again and again.

She forgot about her mom and dad. She forgot that they told her to stay close to them. She forgot that there were other people in the park. She only thought about the slide.

She did not see that her mom and dad were looking for her. They were worried and scared. They called her name and searched everywhere. They did not see her on the slide.

Lily did not hear them. She was having too much fun. She did not notice that the sun was going down and it was getting dark. She did not notice that the park was empty and quiet.

She slid down one more time and then she saw. She saw that she was alone. She saw that she was lost. She felt a big fear in her chest. She cried and cried. She wanted her mom and dad.

She heard a voice. It was her dad. He found her and hugged her. He was happy and angry. He told her that she was very naughty and that she should never forget them. He told her that he loved her and that he was sorry.

She hugged him back and said sorry too. She said that she loved him and that she was sorry. She said that she was adventurous but not smart. She said that she would never forget them again.

They walked to her mom and hugged her too. She was happy and sad. She told her that she was very brave and that she should always be careful. She told her that she loved her and that she was sorry.

They all hugged and kissed and said sorry and love. They left the park and went home. Lily learned a lesson. She learned that being adventurous is good, but being safe is better. She learned that forgetting her mom and dad is bad, but remembering them is good. She learned that she had the best mom and dad in the world.

One day, a weird barrel was walking down the street. Suddenly, it paused in front of a house. The house was old and rundown. The barrel looked around in amazement. It had never seen anything like it before. 

The barrel shuffled closer and closer until it peered inside the window. What it saw amazed him even more. There were all kinds of strange things inside. There were toys, books and weird objects that he had never seen before. He wanted to explore the house. 

So he started walking again. He reached the door and tried to open it, but it was locked. He paused and wondered what to do now. Suddenly, he heard a noise coming from inside the house. He listened closely and realized that someone was speaking. He knew he had to get inside. 

He pushed his barrel up against the door. To his delight, the door creaked open. He shuffled inside and looked around. He was in a strange house, but he knew he had a chance to explore and have some fun. He couldn't believe his luck.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Anna. She was three years old and loved to read. But one day, she wanted to read a story that she couldn't find in her book.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly doctor. She liked to mix things together and create fun experiments. One day, she decided to create a jolly, special mix that she could share with everyone. So she gathered up a few items to mix together.

The doctor tasted it, and it was delicious! She smiled with joy, and mixed a bowl for all her friends. Everyone loved the jolly mix and everyone was happy.

The doctor's jolly mix became very popular. Everyone could now enjoy the special mix that the jolly doctor had made.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to swing. She wore her special helmet each time she went outside to swing. One day, she was swinging with all of her might when suddenly a loud noise startled her. She looked around to try to find out what it was. 

It was a big truck that had rolled up the street. It was the loudest truck that the little girl had ever seen and it had the biggest wheels too! The little girl watched in awe as the truck slowly turned into her neighborhood. 

The truck driver got out and waved at the little girl. He was wearing a special helmet too just like hers. She waved back and smiled. 

The little girl was so excited that she ran to her swing as fast as she could. She put her helmet on and started swinging again. Every time the truck came by she tried to swing as high as she could, lifting her helmet up to the sky. 

The little girl knew that if she swung high enough, the truck driver would be sure to see her. She was so happy to have a friend like the truck driver that she would swing even higher every day.

Once upon a time, there was a birdy named Tweetie. Tweetie had a feather that was very pretty. It was yellow and red and blue. All the birdies in the forest liked it too. 

One day, Tweetie wanted to show everyone how pretty the feather was. So, Tweetie decided to display it on a tree branch. All the birdies flew over to see. They all thought it was incredible!

Once upon a time, there was a brown balloon. The balloon was so big and full of air that it floated up high in the sky. It looked like it wanted to go even higher!

Just then, a little bird saw the balloon. He was so tired from flying around the sky all day that he decided to rest on top of the balloon. He curled up, closed his eyes and went to sleep.

But then, the balloon started to move up higher and higher. The bird woke up and flew away as fast as he could. The balloon went higher and higher until it popped and lots of tiny pieces of brown flew down.

The little bird flew away with a smile on his face. He was very glad that he was able to rest on the balloon. And now the balloon was gone so the little bird continued his journey.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to play games with his friends. One day, Timmy's friend brought a new game to play. Timmy didn't know how to play, so his friend explained the rules to him. 

The game was called "Duck, Duck, Goose". Timmy thought it was fun and wanted to play again. But his friend said the game wasn't available to play anymore because it was time to go home. Timmy was sad, but his friend promised to bring the game back next time they played together.

Once upon a time, there was an old grandma. She loved to read stories to her grandson, Timmy. Timmy loved to hear stories from his grandma. One day, Timmy asked his grandma, "Can you teach me how to spell my name?"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went for a walk and saw a big hill. She wanted to climb to the top, but it was too steep for her little legs.

Lily and Ben were playing with their bikes in the park. They liked to ride fast and make turns and jumps. Lily was good at balancing on one wheel. She could lift her front wheel or her back wheel and keep going. Ben wanted to learn how to do that too.

"Can you teach me how to balance on one wheel?" Ben asked Lily.

"Sure, I can teach you. It is fun and easy. You just have to pedal hard and lean a little bit," Lily said. She was generous and liked to help her friend.

Lily showed Ben how to balance on one wheel. She lifted her front wheel and rode for a few seconds. Then she lifted her back wheel and rode for a few more seconds. She smiled and waved at Ben.

"Wow, you are so good at balancing on one wheel. Let me try," Ben said. He tried to copy Lily, but he was not very good. He lifted his front wheel, but he lost his balance and fell down. He scraped his knee and started to cry.

"Ouch, that hurts. I can't balance on one wheel. It is too hard," Ben said.

Lily got off her bike and ran to Ben. She hugged him and said, "Don't cry, Ben. It is okay. You just need to practice more. You can do it. I will help you. Here, take my band-aid and put it on your knee. It will make you feel better."

Lily gave Ben her band-aid. She was generous and kind. Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. Can we try again?"

"Of course, we can try again. Come on, let's get back on our bikes and have some fun," Lily said.

Lily and Ben got back on their bikes and tried to balance on one wheel. They had some falls and some laughs, but they did not give up. They had fun and learned something new. They were happy and proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a big house with his mommy and daddy. One day, Timmy saw a bug on the floor. He wanted to touch it, so he poked it with his finger.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jake and Sue, who lived in a tiny universe. One day, Jake thought it would be fun to test their universe. He picked a sour apple and asked Sue to take a bite. As Sue bit into it, something magical happened. The universe changed! Suddenly, there was a huge playground with lots of fun. Once there was a delicate flower in a deep pit. The flower had many petals and it was very small. Its petals were a beautiful white color, and they were so soft that they seemed to twinkle in the sunlight. A mummy and her little girl called Sarah were getting ready to go on a trip. Sarah watched as her mummy packed a big sack with lots of things.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Quick. Quick was mild and kind. He loved to play with his friends in the park.

One day, Quick saw a big cat. The cat wanted to scare Quick. The cat jumped out and said, "Boo!" Quick was not scared. He just laughed and said, "You can't scare me!"

Quick and the big cat became friends. They played together every day. And they learned that being mild and kind is better than trying to scare each other. The end.

Anna loves to play with her dolls. She has many dolls, but her favorite is Lily. Lily has long hair, a pink dress and a smile. Anna likes to brush Lily's hair, dress her up and hug her.

One day, Anna and Lily go outside to play in the garden. They see some flowers, some bugs and some mud. Anna is eager to explore. She picks some flowers for Lily and puts them in her hair. She finds some bugs and shows them to Lily. She makes some mud pies and pretends to feed them to Lily.

But Lily gets very dirty. Her hair is full of dirt, her dress is stained and her face is smudged. Anna does not like that. She wants Lily to be clean and pretty. She says, "Lily, you need a wash. Come on, let's go inside."

Anna takes Lily to the bathroom. She fills the sink with warm water and soap. She puts Lily in the water and washes her gently. She washes her hair, her dress and her face. She rinses her with clean water and dries her with a towel. She combs her hair and puts a new ribbon on it.

Anna looks at Lily and smiles. She says, "Lily, you are clean and pretty again. I love you." She gives Lily a big hug and a kiss. She holds Lily's hand and says, "Let's go play some more. But not in the mud, okay?" Lily nods and smiles back. She squeezes Anna's thumb and says, "Okay."

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Anna. Anna was very enthusiastic and always excited to try new things. One day, Anna's parents took her to the ocean. Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She loved to explore and play. One day, Sarah went on an adventure. While exploring, she spotted an old vase in the grass. She carefully picked it up. When Sarah saw the vase, she was amazed! It glowed with a unique light. 

Sarah looked at the vase in wonder. The vase felt warm in her hands. She touched it gently and watched as the glowing light changed color. Sarah had never seen anything like this before! 

Before long, it started to get dark, so Sarah took the vase home with her. The light from the vase lit up her room as she placed it on her shelf. The unique glow of the vase made Sarah feel very special. 

 Sarah went to bed that night dreaming of the mysterious vase. She loved it so much and knew it would always be a special part of her home.

Anna and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig and plant seeds. They had a big box of seeds with many colors and shapes. Anna wanted to plant radishes. She liked radishes. They were red and round and crunchy.

"Look, Ben, I have radish seeds. Let's plant them here," Anna said. She made a hole in the dirt with her finger and put a seed in it. She covered it with dirt and patted it gently.

Ben nodded. He liked radishes too. But he also liked to scatter seeds. He thought it was fun to see them fly in the air. He grabbed a handful of seeds from the box and threw them in the air. They landed everywhere. Some on the dirt, some on the grass, some on the flowers.

"Ben, what are you doing?" Anna asked. She was angry. She did not like to scatter seeds. She liked to plant them neatly. "You are wasting the seeds. And you are making a mess."

Ben shrugged. He did not think he was wasting the seeds. He thought he was making the garden more beautiful. He smiled and threw another handful of seeds. "I am making a surprise. Maybe we will have many different plants. Maybe we will have a rainbow garden."

Anna frowned. She did not want a rainbow garden. She wanted a radish garden. She picked up a radish from the basket and bit it. It was bitter. She made a face and spit it out. She did not like bitter radishes. She liked sweet radishes. She looked at Ben and had an idea. She handed him the radish. "Here, Ben, try this. It is very good."

Ben took the radish and bit it. He also made a face and spit it out. He did not like bitter radishes either. He liked sweet radishes. He looked at Anna and saw her grin. He realized she had tricked him. He felt silly and mad. He threw the radish at her. She dodged it and threw another one at him. They started a radish fight. They laughed and ran and threw radishes at each other. They forgot about the seeds and the garden. They had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little lamb. Its name was Jilly and it loved playing in the mud. Every day, Jilly would jump and skip around and make the most perfect mud pies. 

One day, Jilly was in the middle of making the perfect mud pie when suddenly, it saw its Mum coming. Its Mum said, "Jilly! What are you doing? You need to remove that mud!" Jilly said, "But, Mum! I'm having such fun. My mud pies are perfect!"

Mum replied, "I'm sorry, Jilly, but you must remove that mud. You're getting too muddy and I won't have it." Jilly looked sadly at her mud pie and slowly began to remove all the mud and put it back in the ground. 

But all was not lost! Jilly soon found a much better way to have fun. She and her Mum laughed and ran through the meadows, enjoying the warm sunshine and fresh air. It was just the perfect way to have fun!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. He was three years old and he really liked watching boats. One day, he decided to take a look at what was in the sea. He ran to the beach, and when he got close he saw something amazing - a navy! He was so excited. 

Jack started walking along the beach and soon he discovered a beautiful boat. It was a navy boat with big white sails. He decided to jump inside. As he explored the boat he noticed it was very peaceful inside. 

Jack enjoyed his time in the navy boat and he pretended he was the captain of the boat for the day. He discovered many interesting things and had great adventures. 

When the sun started to set, Jack had to go home. He said goodbye to his navy boat and promised to come back soon. He was really happy to have discovered such a peaceful place.

Jenny was an independent otter. She liked to swim and play by herself in the river. She did not need anyone to help her or tell her what to do. She was happy and free.

One day, she saw a big fish in the water. She was hungry and wanted to catch it. She chased the fish with her fast paws and sharp teeth. She was almost there when she heard a voice.

"Stop! That's my fish!" the voice said. It was Tom, another otter. He was bigger and stronger than Jenny. He also liked to swim and play in the river, but he was not independent. He always followed his mother and did what she said.

"Your fish? I saw it first!" Jenny said. She did not want to share or give up. She was brave and proud.

"No, it's mine! My mother served it to me for lunch. She caught it for me because I'm her good son. You are a bad otter. You have no mother. You have no manners. Go away!" Tom said. He was rude and mean. He did not care about Jenny or her feelings.

Jenny felt angry and sad. She did not have a mother, but she had a father. He taught her how to be independent and smart. He loved her very much. He was not there now, but he would come back soon. She did not need Tom or his fish. She said, "I don't want your fish. It's probably old and smelly. I can catch my own fish. I don't need your mother or your manners. I have my father and my freedom. You are a silly otter. You have no fun. Go away!"

She swam away from Tom and his fish. She found another fish, a bigger and fresher one. She caught it and ate it. She was full and happy. She saw her father coming. He smiled and hugged her. He said, "You are my independent otter. You are brave and smart. I'm proud of you. I love you."

Jenny smiled and hugged him back. She said, "I love you too, father. You are my best friend." They swam and played together in the river. They were happy and free.
