"It is a big shaking that happens sometimes," said the owl. "We all need to be careful when it happens!" 

Chloe thanked the owl for teaching her something new and, after that day, she liked to be extra careful whenever she heard rumbling in the ground.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Lucy and Amy. They were both very poor and they struggled to find food every day. 

Amy and Lucy decided to go in search of something to eat. But as they walked around the village, they just couldn't find anything. They were so hungry and so tired. 

Then, they saw an exit at the end of the village. They decided to go through it to try and find food. Amy and Lucy struggled to make their way through the exit, which was very dark and scary. 

Eventually, they made it to the other side. To their surprise, they found lots of food and water. They had finally found something to eat! They filled their tummies and felt so relieved and happy. 

Amy and Lucy looked out at the village, feeling thankful and content. They were no longer poor or hungry, and they had found a way to survive.

The sky was dark and it started to rain. But little Sarah wasn't scared. She couldn't wait to go outside and splash in the puddles!

Sarah put on her raincoat and headed out. Suddenly, she heard a honking sound and saw a goose. It was flapping its wings and moving its neck. Sarah was very scared and wanted to run away.

But then her mom said it was ok â€“ the goose was just saying hello. So Sarah stayed and waved back. She even tried to talk to it!

After a while, Sarah was no longer scared. She and the goose played together in the rain until the sun came back out.

One day, a happy fish named Fin wanted to raise a big rock. Under the rock was a pretty scale. The scale was shiny and blue. Fin wanted the scale to make his home look nice.

Fin asked his friend, a strong crab named Claw, to help him. Claw said, "Yes, I can help you raise the rock!" They worked together to lift the rock. It was heavy, but they did it.

When the rock was raised, Fin took the shiny scale and put it in his home. Fin and Claw were very happy. They swam and played together all day. Fin's home looked so nice with the pretty scale.

One day, there was a girl who wanted to play in her room. She had a big, soft carpet which was perfect for playing. She was happy.

Suddenly, she had an idea and started running around the carpet. She was having lots of fun. 

As she ran around, she accidentally splashed water on the carpet. She felt embarrassed. 

The girl was worried, but then she remembered something. She ran to the kitchen, grabbed a towel and started to dry the carpet. 

Soon, it was all dry and she was happy again. She had learned her lesson and promised to be careful the next time.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved playing soccer and would always kick the ball around in his backyard. One day, Timmy's dad took him to a big stadium to watch a soccer game. Timmy was so excited to see all the players and hear the crowd cheering.

As they were walking to their seats, Timmy's dad said, "Be careful not to run too fast or you might trip and fall." Timmy listened and walked slowly to his seat. 

During the game, Timmy saw one player who was very good. He scored many goals and the crowd cheered loudly for him. Timmy thought, "I want to be like him when I grow up." 

After the game, as they were leaving the stadium, Timmy's dad said, "Remember, it's important to be humble even if you're really good at something." Timmy nodded and said, "I will remember." He also remembered to stop and look both ways before crossing the street.

Once upon a time there was a mechanic. He had a long day because he had to fix a lot of cars. He was so tired, he decided to take a break. So he went outside and dug a hole in the ground. He put a blanket in the hole and he lay down inside it. He buried himself in the ground. He enjoyed the feeling of being buried because it was warm and cozy. 

The next day, the mechanic got up, brushed himself off and continued to work on the cars. He was so proud of himself for finding a way to relax after such a long day. He told all his mechanic friends what he had done and they thought it was a great idea. From then on, whenever they had a long day, they would bury themselves in the ground and relax. 

The End.

Sara and Tom are brother and sister. They like to play in the garden. Sara is four and Tom is three. They have a big ball and a small car.

One day, they see a hole in the fence. They are curious. They want to know what is on the other side. They crawl through the hole. They see a big dog. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a red collar.

"Hello, doggy!" Sara says. "Do you want to play with us?"

The dog wags its tail. It likes Sara and Tom. It runs to them and licks their faces. They giggle. They throw the ball and the dog fetches it. They push the car and the dog chases it. They have fun.

But then they hear their mom calling. "Sara! Tom! Where are you? It's time to come in and have a bath!"

They look at each other. They are dirty. They have mud on their clothes and their faces. The dog has mud on its fur and its collar.

"Uh-oh," Tom says. "We have to go, doggy. Bye-bye!"

They crawl back through the hole. They run to their mom. She sees them and gasps.

"What have you been doing?" she asks. "You are not clean at all! You need a bath right now!"

Sara and Tom nod. They are sorry. They hug their mom. They say goodbye to the dog. They hope they can play with it again. They go inside and have a bath. They wash the mud off. They become clean again. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, Lily heard about a club where all the cool kids went to play. She wanted to join the club so badly, but she didn't know how.

Lily asked her friends how to join the club, but they didn't know either. Then, she saw a fierce-looking boy who was in the club. She thought he must know how to join. So, she went up to him and asked him how to join. The boy said she had to do something really mean to someone else to join.

Lily didn't want to do something mean, but she really wanted to join the club. So, she did something mean to her little brother. She thought she would finally be able to join the club, but when she went back to the boy, he told her that the club was only for mean kids. Lily realized that being mean was not worth it and she felt very sad. The moral of the story is that it's better to be kind than to be in a club that makes you do mean things.

Once upon a time there was a class. In this class there was a group of kids. They liked to play together and have fun. One thing they did not like was their teacher. She was very mean, and always said mean things. She even made them do disgusting things.

One day they decided they wanted to make a plan. They wanted to make the teacher include them in something fun. So they came up with an idea. They decided to hide in the classroom and steal all the teacher's books. When the teacher came back she was very angry!

The kids laughed and said the teacher needed to include them more. They said if she did, the things she made them do wouldn't be so disgusting. The teacher looked at them and thought for a moment.

The next day the teacher came to class with a smile on her face. She said that her plan was to include the kids in her next lesson. They were very happy and played together until it was time to start the lesson. 

The lesson turned out to be some of the most fun they had ever had in class. It was so much better than doing disgusting things! From then on, the teacher always made sure to include the kids in everything.

Once upon a time there was a big elephant. He wanted to know how much he weighed, so he asked the wise old animal doctor.
The animal doctor said he needed something to weigh the elephant, so they found a reliable wooden box. The elephant carefully stepped into the box and the animal doctor carefully weighed the box.

The animal doctor said, "You weigh a lot! You're the biggest elephant I've ever seen!"
The elephant was so happy and jumped up and down, but then he slipped and fell on his knee. He was very sad and began to cry.

But the animal doctor promised the elephant he would always be there to help him. The elephant was so relieved to know that the animal doctor was reliable. 
From then on, the animal doctor weighed the elephant every week, and the elephant's knee was never hurt again!

Mummy and Daddy were very happy. They had a new car and were going for a drive. They opened the door and got into the car. Suddenly, Mummy said: "Oh no! I forgot the brush!" Daddy said, "It's ok. We can get it later."

But Mummy was not happy. She said: "No, I need the brush right now!" So they got out of the car and went back into the house to get the brush.

When they got back to the car, they saw that someone had taken it! Daddy was angry and tried to find the car thief, but he was gone.

Mummy and Daddy were very sad. They had lost the car they were so happy to get, and they didn't know what to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to talk and play with her friends, but one day she met a boy who spoke a different language. Lily didn't understand what the boy was saying and felt sad because she couldn't talk to him.

Lily's mommy told her that everyone speaks a different language, but that doesn't mean they can't be friends. Lily didn't want to be stupid, so she decided to learn the boy's language. She practiced every day and soon she could understand him.

One day, Lily and the boy were playing when another kid came up and said mean things about the boy's language. Lily stood up for her friend and told the mean kid that it's not stupid to speak a different language. The mean kid felt bad and apologized.

From that day on, Lily and her friend played together every day, and Lily felt proud that she could understand his language. The end.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to travel with his mom. He was very excited. He took his toy car, his teddy bear, and his thermometer. Tim was a persistent little boy.

On their way, Tim saw a big dog. Tim said to his mom, "Look, a big dog!" The dog looked at them and wagged its tail. Tim's mom said, "Yes, it's a big and friendly dog."

Tim and his mom walked and walked. Tim looked at his thermometer. It was hot. He said, "Mom, it's hot. Can we rest?" His mom said, "Sure, let's rest under that tree."

They sat under the tree and had a snack. Tim was happy he could travel with his mom. He knew being persistent helped him have a fun day.

Mama and Baba laughed when they saw Jack. He was wearing an ordinary outfit, but he had put his shoe on the left foot. Mama said it didn't matter, but Baba said it was wrong. Jack was sad and went to sit in the corner.

Mama told Baba that it wasn't wrong, that it was just a little mix-up. Baba shook his head and said no. He said it was wrong and he didn't want Jack to do it again. Jack was very sad, he had very mixed-up feelings inside him.

Mama saw that Jack was sad. She knelt down beside him and said that it was ok, that babies make mistakes sometimes. Baba heard this and felt bad for what he said. He laughed and came over to hug Jack, saying that it was ok and that his shoe looked funny.

Jack laughed too and hugged his parents. He smiled and was happy again. Baba said that they could make a game of it, to help Jack remember to always put his shoe on the right foot. The family spent the afternoon playing the game and in the end, Jack always remembered to put his shoe on the right foot - no matter what.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big teddy bear. They called him Mr. Fluffy and gave him many hugs every day.

One day, their mom took them to the doctor for a check-up. The doctor was a nice lady who smiled and talked to them. She looked at their eyes, ears, and mouth, and listened to their heart and lungs. She said they were very healthy and brave.

But then, she took out a needle and said they needed a shot. Lily and Ben did not like needles. They were scared and cried. They did not want a shot. They wanted to hug Mr. Fluffy.

"Please, don't cry," the doctor said. "The shot will only hurt a little bit, and then it will be over. It will help you stay healthy and strong. You can hug Mr. Fluffy after the shot, okay?"

But Lily and Ben did not listen. They ran away from the doctor and hid under a table. They hugged Mr. Fluffy and said they did not want a shot. They were very grumpy and did not listen to their mom or the doctor.

The doctor and their mom tried to find them and calm them down, but they could not. They were too fast and too loud. They knocked over a lamp and a chair and made a big mess. They made the doctor and their mom very angry and sad.

They did not get their shot, but they also did not get to go home. They had to stay in the doctor's office until they said sorry and behaved. They missed their lunch and their nap. They were hungry and tired and still scared. They wished they had listened to the doctor and their mom. They wished they had been brave and not grumpy. They wished they had a better day.

Once upon a time there was a chubby dog. He had a collar with a number on it. He liked to go for walks in the park and play with the other dogs. 

One day, on his walk, he met a little girl. She was only three years old.

The girl smiled and said, "Hello! What is your number?"

The dog wagged his tail and said, "bow-wow! My number is 16!"

The girl clapped her hands and said, "That is a nice number! Would you like to play with me?"

The dog barked happily and the two of them ran off to the sandbox. They played until it was time to go home. 

The chubby dog thanked the little girl before running off. He knew that they would be friends forever now!

Mum and Dad were busy packing for their holiday.

"Look at all these things!" shouted Dad.

Mum smiled at him. "We have to stay here until it's all ready," she reminded him.

Dad nodded. He went over to their little girl and asked, "Can you help us? We need to stay focused and get it all done."

The little girl smiled and nodded. She started looking around the room, trying to work out the best way to help. Suddenly she spotted her favourite teddy bear.

"Teddy can stay here with me!" she said happily.

Mum and Dad smiled at each other. "Yes, that's a good idea," said Mum. "You can stay here with Teddy and look after him, while we get ready for the holiday."

The little girl hugged Teddy close and nodded. She watched happily as Dad and Mum continued their busy packing.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with blocks and make patterns. One day, they visit Ben's grandma. She lives in a big house with a garden.

"Hello, Anna and Ben," grandma says. "Do you want to see my flowers?"

"Yes, please," Anna and Ben say. They follow grandma to the garden. There are many flowers of different colors and shapes. Grandma tells them the names of the flowers.

"This is a rose. It is red and has a nice smell. This is a sunflower. It is yellow and very big. This is a daisy. It is white and has a circle in the middle."

Anna and Ben look at the flowers. They see patterns in the petals and leaves. They try to make patterns with their blocks.

"Look, grandma," Anna says. "I made a pattern like a rose. It has red blocks and green blocks."

"That's very pretty, Anna," grandma says.

"Look, grandma," Ben says. "I made a pattern like a sunflower. It has yellow blocks and brown blocks."

"That's very clever, Ben," grandma says.

Grandma smiles and hugs them. She is happy to see them. She gives them cookies and milk.

"Thank you, grandma," Anna and Ben say. "We like your flowers and your cookies."

"You're welcome, Anna and Ben," grandma says. "You are very good and sweet. I love you very much."

Anna and Ben love grandma too. They have a fun time visiting her. They make more patterns with their blocks and flowers. They are not serious. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the lake. Every day, Ducky would swim in the lake and play with his friends.

One day, Ducky saw a big cloud in the sky. He knew that it would rain soon. Ducky didn't want to get hurt by the rain, so he went to his home. Ducky waited for the rain to stop.

After the rain stopped, Ducky went back to the lake. But something was different. The lake had changed. The water was higher and it looked different. Ducky realized that the rain had made the lake change. But he was happy to be back in his favorite place to swim.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Bob who loved to wander. One hot summer morning, Bob hopped along a path that led to a pine forest. Bob sniffed the air and was so excited! 

When Bob reached the forest, the big pine trees were refreshingly cool and shady. He hopped around the trunks, running and exploring happily. Suddenly, Bob stopped and looked around. He was lost!
 
Bob started to worry. He wondered how he would ever find his way out of the forest. Just then, a friendly starling flew down and landed on a branch next to Bob.

"Excuse me," Bob said. "Can you help me get out of this pine forest?"

The starling smiled, "I sure can! Just follow this path and it will take you home." 

Bob thanked the kind bird and hopped away. He kept his eyes on the path until he reached the other side of the forest. Finally, he made it back home in time for dinner.

Once upon a time there was a horse that liked to hop. Every day it hopped around the farm, over fences and through the fields. All the other animals thought it was weird that the horse liked to hop instead of running like the other animals.

One day, a little girl came to the farm. She was only three years old. She saw the horse hopping and thought it was so much fun. She started to hop too, and the horse started to hop beside her.

They hopped around the farm together, over the fences and through the fields. They hopped faster and faster, spinning around and jumping higher and higher. The little girl laughed and laughed. 

At last, the two were so tired that they had to stop. They laid down on the grass and watched the clouds in the sky. The horse was no longer weird; it was just having fun. And the little girl made a new friend too.

Once upon a time there was an orange leak. The leak was always getting bigger and bigger. Until one day it split. The orange leak split into two. Each part of the orange leak was still leaking and getting bigger. Soon the two orange leaks had spread across the floor. But then something surprising happened. A big sunny ray of light came down from the sky and filled the two orange leaks with sunshine. The orange leaks smiled and started to jump and dance in the sunshine. From that day on, the orange leaks never split again and always stayed together.

One day, a little girl named Jane found a small plant. The plant was tough and did not grow well. Jane wanted to help the plant. She asked her mom, "How can I help the plant?"

Her mom said, "Give it water and sun." So Jane did that. But the plant still did not grow. Jane was sad. She wanted her plant to be big and strong.

One day, a big dog came to play. The dog ran and jumped near the plant. Jane was scared. She said, "No, dog! You will hurt my plant!" The dog stopped and looked at Jane. Then, the dog bowed to Jane and walked away.

The next day, Jane saw that her plant had grown a little. She was happy. The plant was getting stronger. Jane knew that her love and care helped the plant grow. And the dog learned to be careful too.

John was playing in the park when he noticed a fire. He had never seen fire before and it scared him. He was fearful and wanted to run away. But then he noticed a man. The man was holding something that made a loud noise. He was using it to put out the fire. John was so relieved and now he wasn't scared anymore. He watched carefully as the man put out the fire. It was amazing! John felt proud of how he had been brave and overcome his fear.

Once upon a time, there were two races; one was mighty and strong while the other was small and weak. Neither race wanted to be separated from the other. 

The mighty race wanted to stay together and help the small race become stronger. But the small race kept wanting to leave, as they were scared of being too weak.

One day, the two races faced each other in a big race. They both wanted to win but neither wanted to separate. The tiny races ran fast and the mighty race ran powerfully. 

The race was so close that it was impossible to tell who had won. In the end, they came to a happy agreement where they would stay together and never be separated. 

The small race helped the mighty race reach their goals, and the mighty race helped the small race feel stronger and more confident. From then on, they never separated and always worked together happily.

Once there was a tiny kitten named Tim. He was the best kitten in the whole world. He had soft fluffy fur and bright green eyes. 

One day, Tim felt something strange in the air. Suddenly, the ground started shaking. Tim had never felt anything like it before. He was so scared and felt very miserable.

Just then, Tim's mommy came running into the room. She picked him up, held him close and said "It's alright Timmy, it's just an earthquake. Don't worry, I love you."

Tim meowed a tiny meow and nuzzled against his mommy's chest. He felt so safe and happy, knowing his mommy was there.

As the earthquake stopped and everyone started to calm down, Tim thought to himself "I love my mommy, she always makes me feel so safe."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a village with her mommy and daddy. The village was very calm and peaceful.

One day, Lily went to the park in the village. She saw a boy playing with a ball. She wanted to play too, so she asked him if she could play with him. The boy said yes, and they started playing together.

After a while, Lily's mommy and daddy came to the park. They saw Lily playing with the boy and they were happy. They clapped their hands and said, "Good job, Lily! You made a new friend!"

Lily was very happy that her mommy and daddy were proud of her. She smiled and clapped her hands too. She loved living in the calm and peaceful village with her family.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Mittens. Mittens liked to sleep all day and never did any work. One day, Mittens received a present from his friend, a glowing ball of yarn. Mittens was so happy and played with the ball of yarn all day and night.

But one day, Mittens lost the ball of yarn and couldn't find it anywhere. Mittens was sad and realized that he should have taken better care of his present. He learned that being lazy and not taking care of things can have consequences.

From that day on, Mittens became a responsible cat and took care of all his presents. He learned that it's important to appreciate and take care of the things we have.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named George. He was excited to have a special day with his family.

They all went to the museum to see the skeletons. George was so excited when he saw all the bones!

George rubbed his hands on the bones. They felt so smooth and shiny. He rubbed the rib bones, the tail bone and the head bone.

He was having so much fun! He couldn't believe the skeleton felt so nice to touch. His family laughed at George and they were happy to see him so excited.

The day ended, and they all got ready to go home. George hugged the skeleton before they left and waved goodbye. He was so happy to have gotten to rub the skeleton.

Once upon a time, Jack wanted to learn. He knew he had to go to school to do that, but he was scared. He asked his mom, "Will school help me learn?"

"Yes, Jack," his mom said. "School is a safe and reliable place for you to learn."

So Jack went to school. He was nervous at first, but gradually he started learning things. He learned how to count, how to write his name and how to draw a picture. Jack even made some new friends along the way.

Before long Jack wasn't scared of school anymore. He looked forward to going each day because he knew that school was a reliable place where he could learn new things.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Benny. He loved to play in the garden and eat carrots. One day, Benny saw a carrot that was too high for him to reach. He tried to jump, but he couldn't get it.

Then, Benny saw a piece of string on the ground. He had an idea! He tied one end of the string to the carrot and the other end to a stick. He pulled the stick and the carrot came down. Benny was so happy and ate the carrot.

Later that day, Benny saw a playful squirrel. The squirrel wanted to play with Benny, but Benny was too busy eating carrots. The next day, Benny saw the playful squirrel again. This time, Benny put down his carrots and played with the squirrel. They had so much fun together! From that day on, Benny and the playful squirrel were best friends.

Tom and Jen are playing in the yard. They have a big shovel and a bucket. They want to dig a hole and bury something.

"What can we bury?" Tom asks Jen.

"Let's bury this can," Jen says. She shows Tom a can with a picture of a car on it. "It has oil inside. Oil is good for cars."

"OK," Tom says. He takes the can and puts it in the bucket. He follows Jen to a spot under the tree. They start to dig.

They dig and dig until they make a deep hole. Tom is about to put the can in the hole when he hears a loud noise. He looks up and sees a big truck coming down the road. The truck is red and has a sign that says "Danger".

"Look, Jen, a danger truck!" Tom says.

Jen looks up too. She sees the truck and gasps. She knows what the sign means. The truck is carrying something dangerous. Something that can explode.

"Tom, we have to stop!" Jen says. "We can't bury the can. The can has oil too. Oil and danger don't mix. They can make a big boom!"

Tom drops the can and runs to Jen. They grab the shovel and the bucket and run away from the hole. They hide behind the fence and watch the truck pass by.

They are scared, but they are also glad. They learned something new today. They learned that oil is good for cars, but not for burying. They learned that some things are dangerous and should be left alone. They learned to be careful and listen to each other.

They hug and smile. They are safe and happy. They decide to play something else. Something less risky. Something like tag or hide and seek.

The pretty shield was a very special toy for Jack. It was light blue, with sparkles all around it. He liked to play knight with it and pretended it protected him from dragons. 

One day, Jack wanted to show his shield to his friend Mary. But, when Jack tried to lift his shield, it was too heavy. He tried and tried but he couldn't move it. He struggled and struggled to pick it up, but he just couldn't do it. 

Suddenly, his Mom came in the room. She saw Jack struggling and she smiled. "Here, let me help," she said. She picked up the shield and it became light. Then she gave it to Jack. 

Jack smiled and gave his Mom a big hug. He was so happy he had his pretty shield again. He thanked Mom and ran off to show it to Mary.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who grew big, red radishes. He loved to plant them in his garden every year. One day, he found an ancient seed that he had never seen before. He decided to plant it and see what would happen.

After a few days, a small plant grew from the ancient seed. The farmer took care of it every day, watering it and giving it sunlight. Finally, the plant grew into a big, beautiful radish. The farmer was so happy that he completed his collection of radishes.

He took the ancient radish to the county fair and won a blue ribbon for the biggest and most beautiful radish. The farmer was very proud and he knew that his hard work paid off. From that day on, he always looked for ancient seeds to plant in his garden.

Once there was a little girl named Becky who loved to play outside. All of her favorite things to do were running, jumping and playing hide-and-seek.

One day, when Becky was playing outside, it started to get really cold. The air was so still, it felt like it was frozen. Suddenly, all the leaves on the trees stopped moving and everything around Becky was quiet. She had never seen anything like it!

Becky was so curious that she started to move really slowly, hoping not to make a sound. She crept to the edge of the garden and spotted a door, it looked like it was the exit! She slowly opened the door, it was icy cold. Inside, there was a room filled with spoiled food. Becky couldn't believe her eyes!

When the door shut behind her, Becky realized that she was in trouble. She tried to open the door three times but nothing happened. She was frozen in the room, unable to escape!

Fortunately, Becky's mom and dad soon realized that she was missing. They quickly followed her trail and found her inside the cold room. Once she was free from the exit, Becky hugged her mom and dad and thanked them for finding her!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, she saw a flame in the fireplace and it scared her. She asked her mommy to blow it out, and her mommy did.

After that, Lily was tired and wanted to rest. She went to her room and saw that it was messy. She decided to tidy up her toys before taking a nap. She put all her dolls in one place and her blocks in another. Her room looked so tidy and nice.

Lily laid down on her bed and closed her eyes. She felt so cozy and warm. She was happy that she had a tidy room and that the flame was gone. She fell asleep and had a sweet dream. The end.

Once there was a zip. It was long and white, like a thread. It was rough to the touch. One day, the zip blinked. It saw a red bird fly across the sky. It was so beautiful. 

The zip was excited and blinked again. This time it saw a big elephant walking across the field. It was so big and strong. The zip was amazed and winked once more.

This time it saw a big caterpillar crawling up a tree. It was colourful and slimy. The zip stared in wonder at all these creatures. It was a truly magical day. 

The zip blinked one last time and it was back in its place. But it had a new feeling. It was so excited to see all the wonderful animals around it. It would never forget the magical afternoon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He was so excited because his mommy was taking him to see a witch. He had heard lots of stories about witches and he was so eager to meet one.

When they arrived, the witch was so welcoming. She offered Tom a sweet treat and he was delighted. She showed him all her magic tricks and Tom was speechless. Everywhere he looked, he saw magic!

The witch then offered Tom a very special gift. She gave him a magic wand. Tom was so excited. He could not believe that he was the proud owner of a magic wand. He twirled it around in his hands and he felt magical.

Then it was time for Tom to say goodbye and head home. He thanked the witch for the magical gifts and waved goodbye. She gave him one last gift, a hug. Tom was so surprised and so excited that he hugged the witch right back. 

He couldn't wait to show his mom and his friends all the magical things the witch had offered him.

Once upon a time, there was a family. Tom, the dad, wanted to get a pet for his three year old son, Joe. But Joe had a very special request - he wanted an attractive pet. 

Tom said, "What kind of pet do you want?"
Joe replied, "I want a puppy, Daddy. I want it to be attractive!"
Tom smiled, "I'll see what I can do."

The next day, the family went to the pet store. As soon as Tom opened the door, Joe was excited. He saw so many furry, cute puppies! 

He ran up to one and hugged it, saying "Daddy! I want this one! It's so attractive!" Tom thought the puppy was perfect for Joe and brought it home. 

Since then, Joe and his puppy have been the best of friends. Joe and his puppy go everywhere together. Everywhere Joe goes, his attractive puppy is right by his side!

Mommy was careful. She took Jack to the doctor and the doctor said he needed an x-ray. Jack was a bit scared but Mommy held him tight.

The doctor put a special machine over Jack and said, "We need to take a picture. This machine takes a special x-ray. It will be over soon."

Mommy smiled and hugged Jack. The doctor said, "We need to take a few x-rays and we will replace them. That means we will take one and put another in so we can see how Jack is doing."

After the x-rays were taken Jack was feeling a bit better. The doctor said that Jack was going to be all better very soon. Mommy and Jack hugged and they were so happy.

Once upon a time there was a furry blueberry. It was soft and round and had thick, fuzzy fur. It sat atop a big hill all alone and sighed with sadness. 

Suddenly a friendly creature appeared. It was a small creature with two eyes, two legs, and two arms. The furry blueberry smiled.

The creature and furry blueberry played together all day long. They rolled around and giggled. They danced and sang silly songs. 

Before the sun went down, the furry blueberry hugged the creature goodbye. It had been so much fun, that both of them sighed with happiness. The furry blueberry waved with its tiny paw, and the creature disappeared into the night. 

The furry blueberry sat back atop the hill and gazed up in the starry sky, happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mom went for a walk in the park. They saw a bird struggling to fly. "Look, Mommy! The birdie can't fly high!" said Lily. Her mom replied, "Yes, sweetie. It seems like the birdie is having a hard time." 

As they continued their walk, Lily saw a butterfly. "Mommy, look! A butterfly! It's so pretty!" exclaimed Lily. Her mom said, "Yes, it's a beautiful sight." 

Suddenly, Lily's mom sneezed. "Achoo!" Lily said, "Bless you, Mommy. Do you have a cold?" Her mom replied, "No, it's just a mild allergy." They continued their walk and enjoyed the rest of the day together.

The chubby copper set was sitting in the corner of the room. It belonged to the little boy who lived there. One day he found the set and decided it was his very own. He was so excited! He took it outside to the garden, where he set it up with four chairs.

The little boy was so proud of his new set. He decided he would have a picnic in the garden. He ran inside and grabbed some food. He put it all on the table and went to find some friends to join him.

He found his big brother, so they sat together on the chubby copper chairs, eating their food and chatting away. After they finished their meal, they played games together and laughed until they were too tired and had to go inside. 

The little boy had so much fun with his lunch set. He couldn't wait to invite his friends to play with him again. He knew his set was the best one in the garden!

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his friends in the park. One day, while playing, Spot saw a cable on the ground.

A big bird came and tried to steal the cable. Spot barked, "No, bird! Don't steal!" The bird looked at Spot and said, "I'm sorry, I didn't know it was yours."

Spot and the bird became friends, and they played together in the park. They shared the cable and had lots of fun. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a big, unusual animal came to the town. It had long legs and a long neck. The kids in the town had never seen an animal like this before. They all wanted to play with the new animal.

A little boy named Tim said, "Let's have a race with the new animal!" All the kids and the animal got ready to race. They lined up at the start line. Tim counted, "One, two, three, go!" And they all started to run as fast as they could.

The unusual animal was very fast. It used its long legs to run faster than all the kids. The kids laughed and cheered as they watched the animal win the race. After the race, they all became friends with the unusual animal and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in the forest. One day, she found a beautiful dragon who was lost. "Are you lost?" Lily asked the dragon. "Yes, I belong in the mountains," the dragon replied. 

Lily wanted to help the dragon find its way home, so she decided to go on an adventure with the dragon. They walked and walked until they finally found the mountains. But when they got there, they saw that the charming castle where the dragon lived was being attacked by mean knights. 

Lily and the dragon knew they had to save the castle. "We have to help!" Lily said. The dragon breathed fire and scared away the knights. The king of the castle was very grateful and said, "You both belong in this castle now. You are both very brave and charming." Lily and the dragon were very happy to have found a new home and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom bought a new rug for their living room. It was red and soft. Lily loved it.

But then, Lily's little brother came running in with muddy feet. He jumped on the rug and made it dirty. Lily's mom was angry and said, "We need to change this rug now!"

Lily helped her mom take the rug outside to shake off the dirt. While they were doing that, Lily saw a big, fierce dog walking down the street. She said to her mom, "Look at that fierce dog! I'm glad he's not in our house." 

After they cleaned the rug, Lily's mom put it back in the living room. It looked as good as new. Lily was happy to have her soft, red rug again.

Once upon a time, there was a chimney. The chimney was always tidy and neat. Every day, the chimney permitted a little boy named Billy to take a nap inside the chimney. One day, the chimney said to Billy, "Why don't you go outside and play in the sunshine?"

Billy said, "But I like taking naps here in the chimney. It's so cozy and warm."

The chimney smiled and said, "It's nice to take naps here, but don't you want to go outside and play for a while? There's so much to do out there!"

Billy thought about it for a moment, then said, "Okay, I guess I'll go outside and play!" He waved goodbye to the chimney and went out to play in the sunshine. He had so much fun, and when he was done, he came back to the chimney, all tired and happy.

The chimney smiled, and said, "See, I told you it would be fun! Come back anytime, Billy. I'm always happy to permit you to take a nap here."

And they both lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was an orange dancer. She liked to paint. One day, she talked to a friend and said, "I want to paint a picture today of something special."

The friend said,  "What do you want to paint?" 

The orange dancer smiled, "I want to paint a picture of me dancing." 

So the orange dancer set out to find colors to paint with. She found lots of colors including red, blue, yellow, and pink. She also found some orange paint and this made her happy. 

She started to paint her picture. She mixed some of the colors together and used them to make new colors. As she painted she started to dance, and her friend laughed.

When she was done, the orange dancer was very happy with her painting. She said, "This painting is so special. It looks like me dancing." 

Her friend said, "Yes, you are a very special orange dancer.

Sara likes to read books. She has many books in her room. She reads them every day. She reads about animals, and cars, and stars.

One day, Sara finds a new book in her room. It is a big book with a shiny cover. She opens it and sees many pictures. She sees a picture of a chain. A chain is a long thing with many round parts. She reads the words under the picture. The words say: "A chain can be used to pull, to lock, or to make noise."

Sara wants to try the chain. She looks around her room. She sees her toy box. She sees a lock on her toy box. She thinks: "Maybe I can use the chain to open the lock." She takes the chain and puts it around the lock. She pulls the chain hard. The lock does not open. She pulls harder. The lock still does not open. She pulls harder and harder. The chain breaks. The lock falls to the floor. Sara is sad. She says: "Oh no, I broke the chain. Now I can't read the book anymore."

Sara hears a noise. She turns around. She sees her mom. Her mom is smiling. She says: "Sara, what are you doing? I brought you a new book. It is a book about chains. I thought you would like it." Sara is surprised. She says: "Mom, this is the book I was reading. I found it in my room. I tried to use the chain to open the lock, but I broke the chain. I'm sorry, mom." Her mom hugs her. She says: "It's okay, Sara. The chain was old and weak. It was not a good chain. I have a new chain for you. It is a strong chain. You can use it to play, but not to open locks. And you can still read the book. The book is not broken. It is a good book. I love you, Sara." Sara smiles. She says: "I love you too, mom. Thank you for the book and the chain. Can we read the book together?" Her mom says: "Of course, Sara. Let's read the book together. It is a warm day. We can read the book in the garden. Come on, Sara. Let's go." Sara takes the book and the chain. She follows her mom. She is happy. She likes to read books. She likes to learn new things. She likes to be with her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going for walks in the forest with her mommy. One day, they found a big, red mushroom. Lily thought it looked funny and she started to laugh.

"Mommy, look at this mushroom! It's so big and red!" Lily said.

Her mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it's a mushroom. But be careful, some mushrooms can be spicy and make you sick."

Lily listened carefully and promised to never eat a mushroom without her mommy's permission. From that day on, every time they went for a walk in the forest, Lily would look for mushrooms and they would both laugh at the silly ones they found.

Once there was a little bird who wanted to win a race. All the other birds were ready and excited for the race, but the little bird was nervous. He just wanted to do his best and was hopeful for success. 

The race began and the little bird flew with all his might. He felt happy and blew through the wind with joy. He worked very hard and was determined to win. 

The little bird had almost made it across the finish line when he began to slip and fall behind. He looked sad and tired, but he did not give up! With one last burst of energy, the little bird flew over the finish line and won the race!

Everyone was so glad the little bird had won. Bird friends cheered and celebrated with him. The little bird was filled with accomplishment and joy. He had achieved success and was proud. 

The little bird was glad he had won the race and happy he could make all his bird friends proud. It was a special moment he would never forget.

Once upon a time, there was a huge bear. He was walking around in the woods looking for a friend. He wanted someone to play with.

He came across a little rabbit hopping around. The bear asked the rabbit, â€œDo you want to play with me?â€

The rabbit answered, â€œYes! Letâ€™s play tag!â€

The bear and the rabbit started running and jumping around the woods. The bear was so big and the rabbit was so small that the bear had trouble running around.

Then the rabbit said to the bear, â€œCan you fold your foot? You will be able to run faster!â€ The bear tried and he could move faster and better. 

The bear and the rabbit laughed and continued playing and running around until they were both too tired. They said goodbye and went on their way.

Once there was a little boy called Tom who was three years old. His dad, Mike, was teaching him to understand a new game.

Tom asked, "Daddy, what is this game called?"

Mike smiled and said, "It's called golf, Tom. It's a game where you put a ball into a bright cup."

Tom was very excited and said, "Can I play too?"

Mike said, "Yes of course, you can try. I will help you understand how the game works."

Tom was happy and he went off with Mike to have a go. In no time Tom was having a great time and was getting quite good at the game.

At the end Mike said, "Well done Tom! You really understand golf now!"

Tom smiled and said, "I had fun!"

Once upon a time, there was a kangaroo named Joey. Joey was a big kangaroo who liked to hop and play all day. One day, Joey got lost in the forest and he was confused. He didn't know which way to go to find his way back home.

Joey sat down and started to plan. He thought about the way he came and tried to remember the trees and bushes he saw. After a while, Joey figured out the right way and started to hop towards home. 

When Joey finally made it back home, all his kangaroo friends were so happy to see him. They asked him where he had been and Joey explained that he got lost but he made a plan to find his way back. From that day on, Joey was known as the smartest kangaroo in the forest.

Once upon a time, there lived an eager little mouse. He loved to explore the world and see all the wonderful things the world had to offer. One day, he was exploring an old barn when he saw an unusual trap. He wanted to see what it was, but his mother had always warned him about such traps. But the little mouse was too curious and he couldn't help himself. He carefully poked his little nose closer and closer, until it was just inches from the trap. Suddenly, the trap snapped suddenly shut, trapping the poor little mouse inside. 

The little mouse was so scared and sad. He called out for help, but no one heard him. Suddenly, he heard a noise outside the barn, and it was his mother! She had been searching everywhere for him, and when she heard him, she quickly came to the rescue. She carefully opened the trap and the little mouse was freed. 

The mouse was so happy to be back with his mother. She told him sternly, "I warned you about traps, but you didn't listen! Next time, you better listen to me." the little mouse promised he will never do it again, and he was more careful from then on.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty bird. This bird was very attractive. It had many friends. They all lived in a big tree. The tree was in a park. The park had a pit. The pit was not deep.

One day, the attractive bird went to the pit. It wanted to play. But the pit was full of mud. The bird did not like the mud. It started to complain. It said, "I don't like this pit. It is dirty."

The bird's friends heard it complain. They came to the pit. They saw the mud. They did not like it either. They all complained. They said, "We want a clean pit."

A kind man heard the birds complain. He came to the pit. He saw the mud. He cleaned the pit. The birds were happy. They thanked the kind man. They played in the clean pit. They did not complain anymore. And they all lived happily in the big tree.

Once there was a cool mine. It was filled with glittering treasures. One day, three little birds flew in. They loved the mine so much! They started to sing. Their sweet songs echoed through the tunnels. Everyone in the mine could hear them.

The birds sang louder and louder, filling the air with their happy sounds. Everyone in the mine was so glad to have them. They loved the birds and their singing.

Everyone worked together to make the mine even cooler. They used the treasures they found to build staircases and bridges. Everyone had laughter and fun in the mine.

The three little birds were happy too. They flew around the mine, singing proudly. They were so thrilled that the treasures were now part of their home.

And from then on, the birds could sing and the mine stayed cool.

Diana was bouncing on her trampoline. She was so happy to be outside playing. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise from the sky. She looked up and she saw something that confused her. It was a bird, tightly squeezing something in its beak. Diana was curious but she was also scared.

The bird flew right over her and gently dropped the item it was holding onto the trampoline. Diana was a bit scared but she was also adventurous. She slowly approached the item to see what it was. To her surprise, it was a bottle with a tightly sealed lid. 

She cautiously opened the bottle and found a small message inside. The message was sealed in an envelope and it was labelled â€œfor Dianaâ€. Diana was astonished but also a bit worried. She wanted to know what was inside so she decided to open it. 

Inside the envelope, there was a beautiful drawing. It was of a trampoline and beneath it were two words: â€œYield Joyâ€. Diana smiled and laughed with joy. She knew what those two words meant. It was a message to keep playing and enjoy every moment outdoors. 

Diana happily yielded to the joy of playing with her trampoline. She smiled and enjoyed every moment of it.

Once upon a time, there was a little monkey named Bongo who lived in the jungle. Bongo loved to swing from tree to tree and play with his friends. One day, Bongo saw an adorable baby bird who had fallen out of its nest. Bongo wanted to help the baby bird.

"Hello, little bird," said Bongo. "What's wrong?"

"I fell out of my nest," said the baby bird. "I can't fly yet."

"Don't worry," said Bongo. "I will help you." Bongo picked up the baby bird and sprang up to the nest. The mama bird was very happy to see her baby back in the nest.

"Thank you, Bongo," said the mama bird. "You are very kind."

Bongo smiled and swung off to play with his friends. He was happy to have helped the adorable baby bird.

Amy and Tim were standing in the garden. Amy had a big box and Tim had a small one. Tim was very excited and said: "Let's race!" 

Amy opened the lid of her box and took out two labels. "You can have the blue one and I'll have the red one," she said and gave one to Tim. 

The two of them ran about in the garden. They raced around a tree, then up and down the path. It was so much fun!

But soon, the garden was very messy. Leaves and twigs and little stones were scattered all around. 

Amy and Tim stopped running. "We had better tidy up," said Amy. 

So they both began to collect the labels and put them back in the box. After a few minutes the garden was tidy again. 

Amy smiled and said: "That was a great race!"

Mummy and Timmy were in the kitchen. On the table was a plate with a fork in the middle. Mummy said to Timmy, "It is time to settle down and eat your dinner."

Timmy looked up at Mummy and said, "I no like that. I don't want to eat that food." Mummy said, "It's fine. It's your favourite food. Come and try it."

Timmy slowly walked up to the table and looked at the plate. He saw the fork on the plate and he said, "What's that?" Mummy replied, "That is a fork. It is what you eat your dinner with."

Timmy smiled and reached out his hand towards the fork. He grabbed it and smiled. He said, "I like the fork mummy." Mummy smiled and said, "Now settle down and eat your dinner."

So Timmy ate his dinner with the fork and was very happy. Mummy was pleased too because Timmy had eaten all his dinner. It was a fine end to the evening.

Once upon a time, a little girl had a puppy. The puppy was very cute and fluffy. One day, the little girl and her puppy went for a walk in the park. They saw a man sitting on a bench. The man looked sad and he sighed.

The little girl asked, "Why are you sad?" The man replied, "I lost my puppy. I don't know where he went." The little girl felt sorry for the man and said, "Don't worry. We will help you find your puppy."

So, they searched for the man's puppy. They looked everywhere, but the puppy was unknown. The little girl didn't give up and she kept looking. Finally, they found the puppy hiding behind a tree. The man was very happy and he thanked the little girl and her puppy. They all went home with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a funny dog named Spot. Spot loved to play all day long. In the evening, when the sun went down, Spot would go home to his family.

One day, Spot's mom told him to behave when they went to visit their friends. Spot promised to be a good dog. He wagged his tail and barked happily.

At their friend's house, Spot played with the other dogs. They all had so much fun. Spot remembered to behave and was a good dog. In the end, everyone had a great evening.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived in a small town. One day, she went out to the park to play. As she skipped around, she spotted a red ball. With a squeal of delight, she ran towards the ball and began to bounce it.

"Look at me, Mommy! I'm bouncing the ball!" the little girl exclaimed. 

Her mom smiled. "Yes, you are! You look so happy!", she said.

The girl kept bouncing the ball until she got too tired. All of a sudden, she felt guilty. She had taken the ball without asking.

"Mommy, I'm sorry. I took the ball without asking," she said softly.

Her mom smiled. "It's okay, sweetheart. Let's take it back to the park tomorrow and let someone else have a turn," she said kindly.

The little girl smiled and hugged her mom. She felt much better now that she had taken responsibility for her actions. 

The moral of the story is that it's important to take responsibility and not to feel guilty when we make mistakes.

Once upon a time, there was a green frog named Freddy. Freddy loved to hop around and catch flies for lunch. One day, he met a little girl named Lily.

"Hi, I'm Lily. What's your name?" the little girl asked Freddy.

"My name is Freddy. Nice to meet you," replied the green frog.

Lily wanted to catch Freddy and keep him as a pet, but Freddy didn't permit it. "I'm sorry, Lily. I don't want to be your pet. I like hopping around in the pond," said Freddy.

Lily understood and let Freddy go back to his pond. From that day on, they were friends and would visit each other often.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Andy. He was only three years old, but he had a big curiosity. One day, he saw a safe with a big, red handle just outside his house. It looked very clear and he wanted to open it. 

Andy tried to open the safe but it was locked. He looked for a key, but there was none. He began to cry and tear. He was very sad he couldnâ€™t open the safe.

Suddenly, Andy heard a voice. He looked up and saw his grandma. She had a big smile on her face and said, â€œDonâ€™t worry, Andy. I have the key to the safe. But it is only for special occasions.â€ She winked at him and then put the key in the handle. 

The safe suddenly opened. The biggest surprise was revealed! Andy started cheering and jumping with joy as he saw his birthday presents inside the safe. He hugged his grandma and thanked her. She just smiled and said, â€œI told you itâ€™s only for special occasions.â€

Andy now knew the secret of the safe and shared the key with his sister and brother. Now all of them could open it whenever they want for special occasions. He was very clear about this and carefully kept the key safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play her flute. She would practice every day and dream of playing in a big concert. One day, she saw a very attractive flute in a store and begged her parents to buy it for her.

Her parents said no, but Lily didn't listen. She took the money from her piggy bank and bought the flute herself. She was so happy and played it all day long.

But then, something bad happened. Lily accidentally broke the attractive flute. She was scared of punishment from her parents, but instead of getting angry, they helped her fix it. From then on, Lily learned to be responsible and take care of her things. And she continued to practice her old, but still beautiful flute, dreaming of the day she would play in a big concert.

Lily and Ben like to play pretend. They have a big box of dress-up clothes and toys. One day, they decide to play car drivers. They find hats and sunglasses and keys and a license. The license is a card with a picture and some letters. Lily says it is her license and she can drive any car she wants.

Ben says no, that is not fair. He wants to drive too. He says he can change the license to make it his. He takes a crayon and draws on the card. He makes a new picture and some new letters. He says now it is his license and he can drive any car he wants.

Lily is angry. She says Ben is crazy. He cannot change the license like that. He ruined it. She says he cannot drive any car he wants. He can only drive a toy car. She takes the keys and runs to the toy car. She gets in and drives away.

Ben is sad. He says he is sorry. He says he just wanted to play. He says he will make a new license for Lily. He takes a paper and a crayon and draws a new card. He makes a nice picture and some nice letters. He says now it is Lily's license and she can drive any car she wants.

Lily sees Ben. She sees the new license. She smiles. She says thank you. She says Ben is not crazy. He is nice. She says he can drive with her. She gives him the keys and invites him to the toy car. They get in and drive away. They have fun. They are happy.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play together. One day, they want to act like teachers and students. Tom is the teacher and Mia is the student.

Tom says, "Mia, do you have your pencil?"

Mia says, "Yes, I have my pencil. Here it is."

Tom says, "Good. Now, write your name on this paper."

Mia tries to write her name, but the pencil is too harsh. It makes a loud noise and breaks the paper.

Mia says, "Oh no, the pencil is harsh. It hurts the paper. I can't write my name."

Tom says, "Don't worry, Mia. It's not your fault. The pencil is bad. We need a new pencil. Let's go and find one."

Tom and Mia go to look for a new pencil. They find a soft pencil that is nice to the paper. They go back to their game and write their names. They are happy. They act like teachers and students. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly chicken. The chicken wanted to try new things! So it hopped out the door and started exploring.

First it tried flying, but it was too high! It tried swimming but it got too wet. It tried walking but it was slow.

Then it saw a juicy, red strawberry. It tried to eat it but it was too sour. So it hopped away to find something else.

It spotted some juicy, sweet melon. This time it tried to peck it and it was able to eat it! It was so delicious that the friendly chicken had a great time.

It hopped back home, excited that it had tried something new. From then on, it always looked for new things to try!

Once upon a time there was a rat. His name was Peter and he was very brave. One day, Peter started to explore the world outside his house. He came across a bottle full of a strange liquid. Peter sniffed it and it smelled bad. He thought it was poison.

Though he was scared, Peter decided to drink a drop. Suddenly, the poison tasted sweet! Peter was so surprised that he dropped the bottle and it broke. From the poison spilled out a rare gem.

Peter was so excited that he started jumping up and down. A nearby rabbit watched him curiously.

The rabbit asked, "What happened? Why are you so happy?"

Peter smiled and said, "I found something very special. It's a rare gem that I found in the bottle of poison I drank!"

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Jack. Sam liked to fight and Jack liked to itch. One day, the sky was gloomy and Sam wanted to fight. Jack was itchy and he didn't want to fight. Sam said he would take an itch break and fight first.

Jack and Sam started to fight in the grass. Sam was bigger but Jack was faster. Sam was throwing punches like a robot. Jack was trying to dodge and run away. But Sam was too fast for him! 

Jack was getting scared, so he started shaking. Suddenly, his whole body started to itch. He knew if he scratched his itches, Sam would get the upper hand in the fight. So, Jack kept moving and tried to ignore the itches. 

At last, Sam got tired and stopped fighting. Jack was relieved - he had won! Although he was itchy all over, he was happy to have won the fight. He and Sam hugged and they decided they wouldn't fight again any time soon.

There was a fisherman who wanted a boat for fishing. He went to the store and saw the boats. He wanted the most expensive one so he bought it. The boat blinked on the water and it was so cool. The fisherman held his rod, went in the boat and started fishing. He cast his line out in the water and waited. He saw a tiny fish swimming, but it was too fast for him to catch. Then the fisherman caught a big fish! He blinked and smiled when he saw it. He was so proud of himself. He put the big the fish in the boat and brought it back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. They played on the swings and the slide. Lily loved to swing high in the sky.

Suddenly, Lily's mommy saw a wire on the ground. She said, "Lily, we need to leave now. There is a wire on the ground and it's not clean." 

Lily asked, "What is a wire?" 

"It's a thin, long thing made of metal," her mommy replied. 

Lily said, "Oh, we don't want to touch that. Let's go home and play with my toys." 

So, they left the park and went home to play with Lily's toys. They had a fun day together.

Once upon a time, there was a brave lion. He was the bravest lion in all the land. Everywhere he went, he would roar so loudly that everyone could hear him. 

One day, the lion decided to take a walk. He found a mop and decided to use it like a broom. He was so creative, he kept walking and using the mop over and over. 

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. He stopped walking and looked around. He saw a big, angry tiger coming towards him. The tiger roared at the lion and was ready to fight. The lion bravely roared back, protecting his mop. 

The lion used his mop and fought the tiger. He was so brave and creative, he quickly managed to win the battle. The lion was happy and proudly roared in the air. 

From then on, the lion was known as the bravest and most creative lion in all the land.

One day, a sleepy boy named Tim went to play a sport. He liked to play with a ball. His friend, Sam, came to play too.

"Let's play!" yelled Sam. But Tim was too sleepy to play well. Sam got mad and yelled, "You are not good today!"

The sky got dark and it looked like rain. Tim felt bad and wanted to go home. Sam threw the ball one more time. Tim tried to catch it, but he fell down.

In the end, Tim got hurt and went home sad. Sam felt bad too. They should have stopped playing when Tim was sleepy.

Once upon a time, there were two little brothers, Mark and Tom. Every day, Mark and Tom played together happily. One day, Mark wanted to mix a special potion. He asked Tom to help him. But Tom was worried about the potion, so he said no.

Mark was sad, but he still wanted to mix the potion. So he decided to go ahead and mix it all by himself. He took some water, some leaves and a few other things.

The potion smelled strong and strange. Suddenly, a bright light surrounded Mark and the room. When the light disappeared, Mark had vanished!

Tom was so scared that he ran away. He looked for an exit and managed to escape.

The moral of this story is that one should be thoughtful and think before doing something. Just because something is fun or exciting doesn't mean it's a good idea. Sometimes it brings bad consequences.

Mommy was so excited to take Lily to the park. They hopped in the car, and drove to the park. When they got there, Lily squealed with excitement, and ran around the park. They took out some snacks, and shared them with the ducks! 

Lily wanted to explore the playground, so Mommy followed her from slide to slide. Suddenly, she watched Lily jump into a big drain, filled with dark water. Lily's face lit up, but Mommy shouted "No!", and she looked very scared. 

Mommy quickly ran to pull her out, but she regretted not watching Lily closer. They had a strong hug, and Mommy explained why this was dangerous. Lily nodded her head, and said "Okay". 

After that, Mommy made sure to always keep her close, and keep an eye out for dangers. They had more fun, and left the park with lots of smiles!

One day, Mommy and Baby were walking in the park. Baby saw a cat with a soft, velvet fur and said "Mommy, I like it!" Mommy said, "It sure is soft!" Baby said, "It's weird too!" 

Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it's a bit weird. But God made it and we can thank him for it." Baby said, "Thank God for weird velvet cats!" 

Just then, a dog ran up to the cat and started barking. Baby got scared, but the cat seemed happy. He purred and rubbed against the dog. Baby said, "Mommy, that's weird!" 

Mommy smiled again and said, "Yes, that's a bit strange. They look like they're friends. It's nice that they can be so kind to each other. Let's thank God for that." 

Baby smiled and said, "Thank you God for weird velvet cats and kind dogs!"

Ben and Mia were playing with clay. They liked to make shapes and animals with the clay. They had a big box of clay and many tools to cut and roll and squeeze the clay.

"Look, I made a snake!" Mia said, holding a long green clay snake. "It can bite you!"

"No, it can't!" Ben said, laughing. "It's just clay. I made a lion. It can roar and eat your snake!"

He showed Mia his clay lion, which had a big mouth and a mane. He made it roar and moved it towards Mia's snake.

Mia was scared. She did not like Ben's lion. She did not want it to eat her snake. She grabbed a tool that looked like a measure. It had numbers and a pointy end. She wanted to poke Ben's lion and make it go away.

"Stop it, Mia!" Ben said, seeing what she was doing. "That's not a toy, that's a measure. You can hurt me or the lion with that!"

But Mia did not listen. She was angry and afraid. She poked Ben's lion with the measure. The measure went through the clay and hit Ben's hand. Ben screamed. It hurt a lot. Blood came out of his hand.

Mia dropped the measure. She saw what she had done. She felt sorry and scared. She started to cry.

Ben's mom heard the scream and the cry. She ran to the room. She saw Ben's hand and the measure and the clay. She was very angry and sad. She picked up Ben and took him to the bathroom. She wrapped his hand with a cloth. She called the doctor.

She looked at Mia with a harsh face. She said, "Mia, you did a very bad thing. You hurt Ben with the measure. You could have hurt him more. You are not allowed to play with clay or tools anymore. You have to go home now. I will tell your mom what you did."

Mia felt very bad. She wanted to say sorry to Ben and his mom. But they did not want to talk to her. She had to go home with her mom. She did not have any friends to play with. She did not have any clay to make shapes and animals. She was very sad and lonely. She wished she had not poked Ben's lion with the measure.

Jim was sad. He wanted to play with his friends but they had all gone. Jim thought of a plan - he would make a promise. He would put the promise in a box and save it for his friends when they returned. 

He all made the promise. He put it in the box and locked it. He hoped his friends would remember it when they came back. 

But soon after that bad things started happening. The box got bigger and bigger, and soon it was bigger than Jim. He couldn't open it because it had grown so big. 

One day the box began to shake and rumble. Jim knew it was too late, he had made the wrong promise. It was a sad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She wanted to have a picnic with her friends. So, she asked her mom to help her get ready for the great picnic day. Her mom said yes and helped her pack the yummy food.

On the day of the picnic, Lucy and her friends went to the park. They found a nice spot under a big tree. Lucy started to examine the food her mom packed. She saw apples, sandwiches, and cookies. Lucy and her friends ate and played all day. They had lots of fun.

At the end of the day, Lucy saw some trash on the ground. She remembered that her mom told her to always clean up after herself. So, she and her friends picked up all the trash and put it in the trash can. They learned that it is good to take care of the park and keep it clean for everyone to enjoy. And that was the moral value of their great picnic day.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big velvet bear. The bear was soft and cuddly, and they named him Ted.

One day, Sara and Ben had a fight. Sara wanted to play with Ted, but Ben wanted to play with him too. They both pulled on Ted's arms, trying to take him away from each other.

"Let go of Ted! He is mine!" Sara shouted.

"No, he is mine! I found him first!" Ben yelled.

They pulled and pulled, until Ted's arms ripped off. Sara and Ben gasped. They looked at Ted, who had no arms left. They felt very sad and sorry.

They looked at each other, and saw tears in their eyes. They realized they had been very mean and selfish. They hugged each other and said, "I'm sorry, I love you."

They decided to unite Ted's arms with some thread and a needle. They worked together, and soon Ted had his arms back. They hugged Ted and said, "We're sorry, we love you too."

They learned to share and care for their toys and each other. They never fought over Ted again. They played with him every day, and he was happy. They were happy too. They thought Ted was the best toy ever, and not boring at all.

Once upon a time there was a boy who had a very bad day. He was sad because he had lost his toy. No matter how hard he looked, he couldn't find it. He was so upset that he started to cry. 

Suddenly, he saw a hand reach out to him. He looked up and saw his friend. She smiled and said, "Don't worry. I'll rescue you!" She grabbed his hand and together they looked for the toy. 

They searched everywhere, but they still couldn't find it. He started to cry, again. But then his friend said, "I know how to make you feel better. Come with me!"

She took him to her house and gave him a new toy. He was so happy and hugged his friend. She smiled and said, "I'm glad I could rescue you!" 

From that day forward, the boy knew he had a true friend who would help him when things got bad. He was never scared to ask her for help because he knew she was always there to rescue him.

Lily and Tom are playing with their toys in the garden. They have cars, dolls, blocks and balls. They are having fun, but they are also making a big mess. The toys are everywhere, and some of them are dirty or broken.

"Look, Lily, I have a big truck!" Tom says, as he drives his toy truck over the grass and the flowers.

"That's nice, Tom, but be careful. You are hurting the plants. They are part of the world, and we have to take care of the world," Lily says, as she picks up a doll with a torn dress.

"What do you mean, take care of the world?" Tom asks, as he stops his truck and looks at Lily.

"The world is everything around us. The sky, the sun, the moon, the stars, the trees, the animals, the people. The world is beautiful, but sometimes it can be broken. Like when there is too much trash, or too much smoke, or too much noise. Then the world is sad and sick, and we have to help it," Lily explains, as she shows Tom a picture book with images of the world.

"How can we help the world?" Tom asks, as he looks at the pictures.

"We can help the world by being kind and gentle. By not wasting water, or electricity, or food. By not throwing things away, but recycling them. By not breaking things, but fixing them. By not making a mess, but cleaning it," Lily says, as she puts the doll in a basket.

"Cleaning? But cleaning is boring. I don't like cleaning. I like playing," Tom says, as he grabs his truck again and starts to drive it over the toys.

"Tom, stop! You are making more mess. You are breaking more toys. You are not helping the world. You are hurting it," Lily says, as she runs after Tom and tries to stop him.

"No, I'm not. I'm just playing. You are being bossy. You are not fun. You are mean," Tom says, as he pushes Lily away and drives his truck faster.

Lily and Tom start to argue and fight. They are not happy. They are not friends. They are making the world more broken.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play games with his uncle. His uncle was very fun and always made Tim laugh. One day, they played a game to see who could win.

Tim's uncle said, "Let's play a game. If you win, I will buy you a toy from the cheap store." Tim was very excited and wanted to win the game. They played and played, and Tim tried his best to win.

Finally, Tim won the game! He was so happy and proud. His uncle took him to the cheap store and Tim picked out a toy. They went home and played with the toy all day. Tim loved his uncle and the fun times they had together.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sophie. She loved playing with her toys. One day, she was playing with her favourite toy - a big red truck. She was pushing it around and making engine noises with her mouth.

However, she didn't understand that her toy was too big. She accidentally bumped into her Dad's leg and the toy hurt him.

He said "OUCH! That toy hurt me!" Sophie felt sad. She didn't mean to hurt her Dad.

Her Dad smiled and said "It's OK, sweetheart. I know you didn't mean it". He hugged her and said "I know you love this toy. Just remember to be careful next time, okay?". 

Sophie nodded and said "Yes, Daddy". From then on, Sophie tried to understand where she was playing her toys, and she made sure she didn't hurt anyone ever again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and eat yummy snacks. One day, Lily saw her mommy putting on makeup and she wanted to try it too. 

Lily's mommy warned her that makeup was only for grown-ups and it wasn't safe for little children. But Lily didn't listen and she pulled her mommy's makeup off the table. She put on the lipstick and eyeshadow, thinking she looked pretty.

But when Lily's mommy saw her, she was very upset. She explained that pulling things without permission was wrong and that makeup wasn't for little kids. Lily felt bad and apologized. From then on, she learned to always ask before taking things and to wait until she was older to play with makeup.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a brave girl named Lucy. She had a soft, velvet dress that she loved to wear. Lucy was very good at helping her mom and dad.

One day, Lucy's mom asked her to organize her toys. Lucy was happy to help. She put her dolls in one box and her cars in another box. She felt proud of her work.

Lucy wore her velvet dress when she finished organizing. She felt brave and strong. Her mom and dad were very happy. They all hugged and had a fun day together.

Once there was a poor man who needed help. He wanted to count the stars in the night sky, but he couldn't reach them. He tried and tried but he just couldn't do it.

One day, he had an idea. He decided to put an ashtray on the ground. 

He looked up and started to count the stars one by one. Everytime he counted one, he put a pebble in the ashtray. After counting all the stars, he had a big pile of pebbles in the ashtray.

The poor man was so happy. He had managed to count the stars! Now he could count the stars whenever he wanted.

Annie was playing in her classroom. She loved to play in the mild sunshine that shone through the windows. Her teacher had asked her to stay in the classroom until it was time for their lunch break. Annie tried very hard to stay but she was so excited that she couldn't help but jump around and giggle with her friends. They ran around the classroom and had lots of fun. 

Whenever Annie felt like she was going to get too carried away, her teacher would remind her to stay. Annie got the message and slowed down, but inside she was still bursting with joy! She would stay in the classroom with her friends until lunchtime arrived. 

Finally, it was time for lunch. Annie was so happy to leave the classroom and enjoy some lunch outside. The time she spent in her classroom was still so much fun and she couldn't wait to come back again the next day.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Bob. He was three years old and he loved to play. One day Bob's mommy said, "Let's go to the cold maze!". So off they went.

The maze was big and twisty. Bob got lost! He couldn't find his mommy. He was so scared. He shouted, "Mommy!" But she couldn't hear him. He started to miss her.

But then he saw a friendly lady. She said, "Do you want help finding your mommy?" Bob was so happy. She helped him find his way back.

At last, Bob found his mommy. She was so glad to see him. She said, "I missed you so much!". Bob smiled and said, "Me too!" And they all lived happily ever after.

Tim and Liz liked to play with their toys. They had a big box of toys in their room. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a scale. It had a round thing that could spin and show numbers. Tim and Liz did not know what the numbers meant, but they liked to spin the round thing.

They took the scale to the living room and put it on the floor. They took turns to stand on the scale and spin the round thing. They laughed when the numbers changed. They did not see their mom come in. She was worried when she saw them playing with the scale. She knew the scale was not a toy. It was a special scale that their dad used for his work. It was very expensive and delicate.

She shouted at Tim and Liz to stop playing with the scale. She ran to the scale and tried to take it away from them. But Tim and Liz did not want to give up their toy. They pulled the scale from their mom. They pulled too hard. The scale broke. The round thing fell off and the numbers stopped. The scale was ruined.

Their mom was very angry and sad. She scolded Tim and Liz for breaking the scale. She told them they had to go to their room and stay there. She said they had to pay for the scale with their allowance. She said they had no more toys to play with. Tim and Liz cried. They were sorry for breaking the scale. They wished they had not played with it. They wished they had listened to their mom. They had no fun. They had a bad day.

Once upon a time there was a nice red couch. On the couch sat a boy. His nose started to tickle and he had to sneeze! He put his hand to his face and said, "Ah-choo!" All around him, everyone laughed. It was fun to sneeze!

The boy liked the red couch. He liked to sit on it and look around the room. He noticed a plush toy on the couch and picked it up. He hugged it and grinned. Then, he sneezed again! "Ah-choo!" He laughed and put the toy down.

The boy kept looking around the room. Everything was so nice and colourful. Then, he sneezed one more time, saying, "Ah-choo!" He looked around and laughed again. It was funny to sneeze! He loved his red couch and the funny feeling that came with it when he sneezed.

Sara and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat a muffin. They saw a big muffin on the table. It looked yummy.

"Can we have the muffin?" Sara asked Ben.

"Let's discuss it," Ben said. "Maybe we can share it."

Sara nodded. She liked to share with Ben. They were good friends.

They went to the table and grabbed the muffin. They broke it in half. They each took a bite. It was sweet and soft.
