But they did not see the note on the table. It said: "Do not eat the muffin. It is for Mommy's birthday. Love, Daddy."

They also did not see the dog. The dog was hiding under the table. He smelled the muffin. He wanted to eat it too.

He jumped out and barked. He scared Sara and Ben. They dropped the muffin. The dog ate it. He made a big mess.

Sara and Ben cried. They were sorry. They made a mistake. They ruined Mommy's birthday.

Daddy came in and saw the mess. He was angry. He yelled at Sara and Ben. He said they were naughty. He said they had to go to their room.

Sara and Ben felt bad. They wished they had not eaten the muffin. They wished they had read the note. They wished they had seen the dog.

They learned a lesson. They should always discuss things before they do them. And they should always look around them. Or they might get into trouble.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his blocks. He would stack them up high and make different shapes. One day, Timmy's mommy asked him to help her measure the length of a piece of string. Timmy was so excited to help! 

He grabbed his ruler and carefully measured the string. "Wow, mommy! This string is incredible! It's so long!" exclaimed Timmy. His mommy smiled and praised him for doing such a good job. 

Later that day, Timmy went back to playing with his blocks. He decided to make a tower in the shape of a triangle. He stacked them up and measured how tall it was. "Look, mommy! I made a triangle tower!" Timmy said proudly. His mommy was amazed at how smart and creative her little boy was.

Once there was a little girl called Lilly. Lilly was three years old and loved adventures. But one night Lilly had a nightmare. She was scared and started to cry. She ran to her parents and knelt down beside her mum and dad.

Her mum said, "Don't worry Lilly, we're here to look after you."

Lilly felt much better but she was still scared of the nightmare. So she decided to take matters into her own hands. She ran to her dad and said, "Let's make a nightmare catcher!â€ 

Her dad got some thin sticks and bent them into an arch. Then he tied them together with some string. He said, â€œThis will catch any nightmares that come too close to you.â€

Together they hung the nightmare catcher over Lilly's bed and with a smile she said, "Goodnight."

Lilly felt much better and brave enough to go to sleep. She fell asleep safe in the knowledge that any nightmare that tried to enter her room would be caught up in the nightmare catcher.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. Jack was so proud of his shiny body. He loved to bathe everyday with lots of bubbles. All of Jack's friends were so envious of him!

One day, the wind blew in a special new kind of bubble. It was pink with twinkly stars inside. As Jack jumped in the bath, the special bubble floated around him. Jack was so excited!

The bubble started to float up and down Jack's body. As it touched Jack, he was filled with happiness and felt clean and special.

After his bath, Jack's body felt so soft and clean! His friends were even more envious of him. Every day, Jack would take a special bath in the twinkly pink bubble. It made him feel so happy. The End.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends: Jack and Jill. Every day Jack and Jill played together in their garden.

One day, Jack had a special surprise for his best friend. He had made her a wonderful costume! It was a bright pink tutu with matching frilly sleeves. Jill was delighted and gave him a big thank you hug.

Jack and Jill decided to take the costume to their neighbour Suzie's house and show her. Suzie was just as excited when she saw the costume. She said they should have a fancy dress parade.

Jack and Jill began to stir. They collected anything they could find like hats, buckets and ribbons. They asked around the neighbourhood until they had enough things to make a costume for everyone.

When the parade was ready, Jack and Jill led the way. People cheered and clapped as the children went around the neighbourhood. Jack was so reliable and everyone knew he had organised the whole parade with Jill.

At the end, everyone had a great time and Jack and Jill promised to do it again next week.

Once upon a time, there was a little pig. He lived on a farm with his family. The pig had a hidden spot he liked to play in. It was behind the big red barn. He loved to hide there and play with his toys.

One day, the little pig found a small seed in his hidden spot. He thought it would be fun to grow something. So, he dug a hole with his little pig feet and put the seed in the ground. He covered it up and gave it some water.

Every day, the pig went to his hidden spot to check on the seed. He gave it water and talked to it. Soon, a tiny green plant began to grow. The pig was so happy! He watched as the plant grew bigger and bigger. The little pig had grown a beautiful flower in his hidden spot. He was so proud of his flower and loved to sit by it every day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lily. Lily was full of surprises. Every morning, she woke up feeling very lively.

One morning, Lily had an idea. She wanted to mix all her favourite ingredients together to make a special surprise. She eagerly ran to the kitchen and started to roll up her sleeves.

First, she took some flour, sugar and milk and put them in a bowl. Then, she added some blueberries and a pinch of cocoa powder. 

Lily started stirring her mixture, and very soon it smelt delicious. When it was ready she called out to her parents: "Mama, Papa! Come here! Look at my surprise!"

Her parents came into the kitchen, amazed by the delicious smell in the air. They tried some of Lily's mixture and they could not believe how good it tasted.

"Oh Lily, this is wonderful! What did you make?" her parents asked.

Lily looked up at them with a big smile and replied: "I made a tasty and lively surprise! I mixed everything together, just like you taught me".

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Bella. She was very adventurous and loved to try new things. One day, Bella decided she wanted to bury her suit in the ground. Her mom said no, but Bella had a bright idea.  

Bella gathered all the tools she could find and started digging a big hole. She was determined to bury her suit and have an adventure. But when Bella put the suit in the hole, something else came out - a giant bird!    

The bird had a loud voice and said, "What are you doing? That is my home!" Bella was so scared that she ran away. She didnâ€™t know what to do.  

The bird chased Bella all the way home. When they arrived, the bird said, "I want my home back!" Bella was scared. But then she had a bright idea. She said, "I will exchange my suit for your home!"

The bird thought about it, and decided to agree. Bella was happy, and the bird was happy. Everybody was happy and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, they were playing hide-and-seek when a big, white fog came rolling in. Timmy and his friends couldn't see each other anymore, and they were scared. But then, Timmy had an idea. He said, "Let's hold hands so we don't get lost in the fog!" 

Timmy's friends thought that was a great idea, and they all held hands tightly. They walked slowly and carefully through the fog, and eventually, they found their way out. Timmy felt proud that he had helped his friends gain confidence in the scary fog. 

After that day, Timmy's friends started calling him "Timmy the Wise" because he knew what to do in a scary situation. Timmy was happy that he could help his friends, and he didn't feel ignorant anymore.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mommy. They saw many kids flying kites in the sky. Lily wanted to fly a kite too. Her mommy bought her a beautiful kite with a rainbow color.

Lily held the kite and ran with it. The wind blew the kite up high. Lily was so happy to see her kite flying in the sky. She wanted to touch the clouds with her kite.

The park was peaceful and quiet. Lily and her mommy sat on the grass and watched the kite flying. They felt so happy and relaxed. They enjoyed the peaceful moment together.

Once upon a time there was a wild pirate. He wanted to find an adventure and explore the world. So one day he asked a fish if he knew of any good places to explore.
The fish said, "No, but why don't you ask the bird? He might know something."
So the wild pirate flew up to the sky to ask the bird. The bird told him, "Yes, there is a place you can explore. It is a far away island with many exciting things to see!"

The wild pirate was excited and thanked the bird. He flew to the island and was amazed at all the wild places to explore. He swam in the deep blue sea and climbed the tall trees. He found so many interesting things, he didn't want to leave. 

But after a while, the wild pirate decided it was time to go home. He thanked the bird and fish for their help and sailed off in search of more adventure.

Once upon a time there was a jail. It had big walls, high fences and lots of guards. It was very reliable, so nobody could escape!

One day, something new happened. A big sign appeared above the jail. It said 'The jail will close!' Everyone was very shocked.

The jail was shut and no one was allowed in. All the prisoners had to find a new place to live. They were happy to be free!

The guards found new jobs and the jail closed for ever. Everyone was happy because nobody was in jail anymore. They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a strong boy named Tim. Tim liked to collect things. He had many toys, rocks, and sticks in his room. One day, Tim was playing outside with his friends. They were running, jumping, and laughing.

Tim saw a pretty rock on the ground. He wanted to collect it. But when he bent down to pick it up, Tim fell and hurt his knee. It was bleeding. Tim started to cry. His friends ran to get help.

Tim's mom came outside with a bandage. She put the bandage on his knee. Tim felt better right away. His mom told him that he was very strong. Tim smiled and went back to play with his friends. They all had a fun day together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to the zoo with his mommy and daddy. They saw lions, tigers, and bears! Oh my! 

One day, Timmy woke up feeling very dull. He didn't want to go to the zoo. But his mommy and daddy said they would buy him a big ice cream if he went. That made Timmy happy! 

At the zoo, Timmy saw a big elephant. It was so big and strong! Timmy loved watching the elephant eat peanuts. He was happy he woke up and went to the zoo.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who had the most unique belt. It was the most special belt she had ever seen.

Every morning, the little girl put her belt on to get ready for the day. She remembered how happy she felt wearing it.

One day the little girl was playing in the garden with her best friend. The two of them were having a lot of fun, but at the end of the day she forgot to take her belt off.

When the little girl realized she had left her belt in the garden she was so sad. She was afraid she would never see it again.

But the next day, to her surprise, the belt was back in her room waiting for her. It was just like she remembered it. She was so happy she remembered to put it on every morning from then on.

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Benny. Benny loved to eat sweet honey from the beehive. One day, Benny saw a file on the ground. He picked it up and wondered what it was for. 

Benny decided to ask his friend, a rabbit named Rosie. "Rosie, what's a file for?" he asked. Rosie replied, "It's a tool to make things smooth." 

Benny thought about this and decided to use the file on the beehive to make it easier to get the honey. But when he tried, the beehive broke and the bees got angry. 

Rosie came to help and said, "Benny, you need to yield to the bees. They need their home to stay safe." Benny realized his mistake and apologized to the bees. From that day on, Benny and Rosie enjoyed sweet honey together, but Benny never used a file on anything without asking for help first.

Once upon a time there was a big promise made to a three year old. She was promised a surprise if she weighed the same each day.

She was really excited and couldnâ€™t wait to see what her surprise was, so she weighed herself each morning.

One day, she jumped onto the scale and noticed that she weighed more than the day before. She was a little scared to look at her surprise and stepped off the scale.

Her mom was there to reassure her.

â€œItâ€™s ok, honeyâ€, she said. â€œIt doesnâ€™t matter if the numbers change a little. I promised you a surprise and I still want to give it to you.â€

The little girl smiled, stepped back onto the scale, and weighed herself. And when she finished, she got the surprise she had been waiting for - a big, delicious ice cream cone!

Once upon a time there was a happy little boy named Dan. He was always loyal to his family, friends and neighbors. One day, Dan wanted to find something special to do, so he took his pet pup and headed out to explore the village.

As Dan walked along, he noticed an old man playing a violin. The old man was sad and lonely, and Dan wanted to help. He smiled and took his pup up to the old man. The man smiled back and handed Dan his violin. Dan was so excited and he said goodbye with a hug.

The pup and Dan went home and Dan took out the violin. He and the pup played it together and it sounded so nice. But the pup was tired, so Dan put the violin away in his bedroom.

The next morning, Dan woke up and saw that the violin was gone! Someone had stolen it during the night. Dan was so sad, but he didn't give up hope. He and the pup went back to the old man's house and told him what had happened.

The old man was so thankful and said they were the most loyal friends he had ever met. He said he would find a way to get the violin back.

The old man and Dan searched everywhere, but they couldn't find who had stolen the violin. Even so, they were determined to bring it back. Finally, after weeks of searching, the old man and Dan found the violin.

Mommy and baby brother went to the store. Inside, they saw lots and lots of toys. Mommy asked, "What do you want baby brother?" Baby brother said with a big smile, "Please birthday!" Mommy answered, "Well, that's a great choice!" 

They looked around the store and found a great birthday present. Mommy asked, "How about this!" She held up a box with a bright and organized birthday toy inside it. Baby brother smiled and said, "Yes! Please!" 

Mommy and baby brother headed home to plan a birthday party. They invited all of baby brother's friends and it was so much fun. There were games, cake and presents - it was the most organized birthday ever!

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to draw with crayons. They had many colors of crayons, but they both loved orange the most. They always wanted to use the orange crayon for their pictures.

One day, they found only one orange crayon in their box. They both reached for it at the same time. They pulled and tugged, but neither of them would let go.

"Give me the orange crayon!" Tim said. "I saw it first!"

"No, I did!" Sam said. "It's mine!"

They started to yell and fight over the orange crayon. They did not seem like friends anymore.

Their teacher saw them and came over. She was not happy. She took the orange crayon from them and said, "You two need to learn to share. If you can't share, you can't play with the crayons at all."

She put the orange crayon away and gave them each a different color. Tim got a blue crayon and Sam got a green crayon. They looked at their crayons and felt sad. They missed the orange crayon.

They looked at each other and felt sorry. They realized they had been silly and mean. They decided to say sorry and make up.

"I'm sorry, Sam," Tim said. "You can have the orange crayon next time."

"I'm sorry, Tim," Sam said. "You can have it now. I like green too."

They hugged and smiled. They started to draw with their crayons. They made a picture of a sun with the orange crayon and a grass with the green crayon. They added a sky with the blue crayon. They wrote their names on the picture and gave it to their teacher.

Their teacher was proud of them. She said, "That's a beautiful picture. And you know what? You two are beautiful friends. You learned to share and be kind. That's more important than any color."

Tim and Sam nodded and agreed. They learned that sharing is caring. And that orange is not the only color.

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin. The penguin was very lonely because it had no friends. One day, the penguin went outside to play and found a spray bottle. The penguin started to spray water everywhere and it was so much fun! Suddenly, another penguin saw what was happening and came over to play. The two penguins sprayed water and played together all day long. From that day on, the lonely penguin was never lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a little mule named Momo. Momo had a big orange ball. He loved to play with his ball all day.

One day, Momo saw a big pot. He wanted to stir the pot. But his ball fell into the pot. Momo was sad. He wanted his ball back.

Momo tried to get his ball. He asked his friends for help. His friends helped him stir the pot. The ball came out. Momo was happy again. They all played with the orange ball together.

Once upon a time there was a small pup named George. He was a curious pup who liked to explore the world. One day, George came across a very strange object. It was a big box with buttons and a digital screen.

George was very confused and didn't know what to do. Then a voice came from inside the box. "Hello George," said the voice. "This is a weigh machine. It can tell you how much you weigh!"

George was still confused, but he was excited too. He stepped onto the machine. The voice spoke again. "You weigh 8 kilos," it said.

George was so surprised. He jumped off the machine with a smile. He didn't understand what had just happened, but he was proud that he had learned something new.

The next day, George went to school. The teacher was talking about the weigh machine and George decided to share his story. When he was done, all his classmates were just as surprised and confused as he had been.

The teacher smiled. "You've completed your lesson today," she said. "Now you all know what a weigh machine is and how it works." 

George was very proud. He felt like he had been much more than just a pupil for that day.

Once there was a poor little girl named Mary. Mary loved to kick around circles in the dirt. One day, Mary went to the park, kicked the circles around for a while, and got very tired. She decided to take a nap.

While Mary was sleeping, a beautiful fairy flew down from the sky and she said, "What a beautiful little girl! Here, I will give you a special present." She waved her magic wand and a big circle appeared.

Mary woke up, saw the big circle and asked, "What is this?"

The fairy said, "It's a magic circle. It will give you whatever you want. All you have to do is to kick the circle three times, and something special will happen." 

So Mary kicked the big circle three times, closed her eyes and when she opened them again, she was filled with joy! The magic circle had given her a bag of money, a beautiful house and a pet dog.

Mary looked up to the sky and thanked the fairy from the bottom of her heart. Now Mary was no longer poor, and she could enjoy kicking circles in the park for hours and hours!

Lila and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big orange cat. The cat is graceful. It walks on the fence and jumps on the tree.

"Wow, look at the cat!" Lila says. "It is so pretty and fast!"

"I want to pet the cat," Tom says. "Maybe it is friendly."

They run to the fence and call the cat. "Here, kitty, kitty! Come to us!"

But the cat does not come. It looks at them and meows. Then it runs away.

"Bye, cat!" Lila and Tom say. "Maybe we will see you again."

They are not sad. They are happy. They have seen a big orange cat. They have had fun. They go to the slide and slide down. They laugh and smile. They are friends.

Tommy was having a nice day. He stepped outside and saw the event. It was a modest event with lots of smiling people. He tried to join them, but he stumbled and fell! He brushed himself off and joined the event. Everyone around was so happy and he had a wonderful time. He felt like he was part of something special. Finally, the event ended and Tommy fell asleep in his bed, dreaming of the modest event.

Sara was a big sister. She had a baby brother named Tom. Sara loved Tom very much, but sometimes she was jealous. She wanted to play with Mom and Dad, but they were busy with Tom.

One day, Sara saw Tom sleeping in his crib. She had an idea. She took her doctor kit and went to examine Tom. She put a stethoscope on his chest, a thermometer in his mouth, and a band-aid on his arm. She said, "I am a doctor. I will make you better, Tom."

But Tom did not like Sara's game. He woke up and started to cry. He spit out the thermometer and pulled off the band-aid. He was scared and hurt. He wanted Mom and Dad.

Mom and Dad heard Tom's cry and ran to his room. They saw Sara and her doctor kit. They were angry and worried. They said, "Sara, what did you do to Tom? You should not play with him like that. You could hurt him or make him sick. He is a baby. He needs love and care, not games and toys."

Sara felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I am sorry, Mom and Dad. I wanted to play with you, but you were busy with Tom. I wanted to examine him, like you do. I wanted to be intelligent, like you are."

Mom and Dad hugged Sara and said, "Sara, we love you very much. You are a big sister and a smart girl. You can play with us and with Tom, but you have to be gentle and kind. You can examine him, but only with your eyes and your words. You can ask him questions, like how he feels, what he likes, and what he learns. You can help him grow and learn, too. That is how you show your intelligence and your love."

Sara smiled and said, "Thank you, Mom and Dad. I understand. I will be a good sister and a good doctor. I will love Tom and play with him nicely."

She went to Tom's crib and said, "Hi, Tom. I am sorry I scared you. I love you. Do you want to play with me?"

Tom stopped crying and looked at Sara. He smiled and reached for her hand. He said, "Yes, Sara. I love you, too. You are my sister. You are intelligent."

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very nervous because it was her friend's birthday party and she didn't have a gift. She didn't know what to do.

Lily's mom saw that she was sad and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her that she was nervous because she didn't have a gift for her friend's birthday party. Her mom told her not to worry and that she would help her find the perfect gift.

They went to the store and looked at all the toys. Lily's mom helped her pick out a beautiful doll that she knew her friend would love. Lily was so happy and grateful for her mom's help.

At the party, Lily gave her friend the gift and she was so happy. Lily learned that it's okay to ask for help when you need it and that giving gifts can make others happy.

It was time for the lecture to begin. Little Tom was excited to come to the high school and learn something new. When he arrived, he was amazed at the big space filled with many people.

The teacher started his lecture. He spoke with a voice that was calming and wise. Tom listened carefully and learned many new things. He began to feel a strange feeling in his heart.

Tom asked the teacher, "What is this feeling inside my heart?"
The teacher smiled and said to him, "It's the feeling of healing. When you learn something new, your heart can heal and grow stronger."

Tom smiled and felt happy. He knew that the lecture would help him to heal and feel better. He thanked the teacher for his wise words and ran off to tell the other children the good news.

Lily was a wise girl who liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She knew how to wash the fruits, stir the soup and set the table. One day, her mom let her make a salad for lunch. Lily was very happy and proud.

She took a big plate and put some lettuce, tomatoes, carrots and cheese on it. She added some salt, pepper and oil and mixed everything with a spoon. She tasted a bite and smiled. It was yummy and healthy. She carried the plate to the table and put it in the middle.

"Look, mom, I made a salad!" she said.

"Wow, Lily, you did a great job!" her mom said. "You are a very wise and helpful girl. Thank you for making lunch for us."

Lily's mom gave her a hug and a kiss. They sat down and enjoyed the salad together. Lily felt very happy and proud. She liked to help her mom in the kitchen.

Anna and Ben were twins who loved to play outside. They had a big garden with many flowers and trees. They also had a small patch where they grew some vegetables, like carrots and lettuce. Their favorite vegetable was the pumpkin, because it was big and round and orange. They liked to make faces on the pumpkins and pretend they were their friends.

One day, their mother told them that they could pick one pumpkin each for Halloween. They were very happy and ran to the garden. They looked at all the pumpkins and tried to find the best ones. Anna saw a huge pumpkin that was almost as big as her. She thought it would make a great lantern. She ran to it and tried to lift it, but it was too heavy. She asked Ben to help her.

Ben was looking at a smaller pumpkin that had a funny shape. He thought it would make a funny face. He liked it very much. He heard Anna calling him and turned around. He saw the huge pumpkin and said, "Wow, that's a big pumpkin! Do you want it?"

"Yes, please help me take it to the house. It's too heavy for me," Anna said.

Ben hesitated. He wanted to keep the smaller pumpkin, but he also wanted to help his sister. He remembered that their mother always told them to share and be kind to each other. He decided to help Anna. He said, "OK, let's take it together. But can I have the smaller pumpkin? I like it too."

Anna smiled. She said, "Sure, you can have it. Thank you for helping me. You are a good brother."

They lifted the big pumpkin together and carried it to the house. Their mother was waiting for them. She praised them for their choice and said, "You have picked two beautiful pumpkins. I'm proud of you for working together and sharing. Now let's clean them and carve them."

They followed their mother to the kitchen. They washed the pumpkins and cut off the tops. They scooped out the seeds and the pulp. They were surprised when they saw what was inside the big pumpkin. It was rotten and spoiled. It smelled bad and had worms and bugs in it. They felt sick and dropped the pumpkin. It splashed on the floor and made a mess.

They looked at the smaller pumpkin. It was fresh and sweet. It had no worms or bugs in it. It smelled good and looked happy. They felt happy too. They said, "We like this pumpkin better. It's not spoiled. It's perfect."

Their mother nodded. She said, "Sometimes, the biggest things are not the best things. Sometimes, the smallest things are the most precious things. You have learned a valuable lesson today. Don't judge a book by its cover. Don't be greedy or selfish. Be grateful and generous. That's what makes you happy."

Anna and Ben hugged their mother. They said, "We're sorry for the mess. We're glad for the lesson. We love you, Mom."

They cleaned up the mess and carved the smaller pumpkin. They made a funny face on it and put a candle inside. They placed it on the porch and admired it. It glowed in the dark and smiled at them. It reminded them of their love and their joy. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly boy named Tim. He loved to read books. One day, he went to the library to find a new book. The library was big and full of books. Tim was very happy.

In the library, Tim met a girl named Sue. Sue did not like the library. She would complain about the books. She said they were boring. Tim wanted to help Sue. He showed her fun books to read. But Sue did not want to try.

One day, a big storm came. The wind blew and the rain fell. The library started to flood. Tim knew what to do. He put the books up high so they would not get wet. Sue did not help. She just complained.

The library was saved, but Sue's house was not. All her things got wet and ruined. She was sad. Tim tried to help, but it was too late. The moral of the story is to not complain and try to help others.

Once upon a time there was a furry little dog called Richard. He loved to explore the world around him and go on long hikes with his owner.

One day, Richard went for a walk and found an exciting trail to explore. He was so excited and set off following the trail with his owner.

As Richard walked, his owner saw a furry spider ahead. "Look, Richard! It's a hairy spider!" she said. Richard was scared and started to bark, his little tail wagging quickly.

Richard's owner smiled at him and said, "It's okay, Richard. I'm here to support you." She held his paw and said, "Let's keep going, the trail is full of surprises!"

So Richard and his owner carried on, exploring the trail and having adventures. Whenever Richard got scared, his owner was there to support him and help him see that his fears did not need to be so scary.

And they lived happily ever after.

Lily was a lazy girl. She often didn't want to do anything. Everything felt like too much effort. But one day, something inside of her changed.

She found a paintbrush and some paints lying around. As she looked at them, she felt excited. She began painting on the wall next to her.

She painted all sorts of things. She painted the sky, trees, and flowers. She really brought the painting to life!

When she was finished, she stepped back and looked at what she had created. She was so proud of herself. She realized that if you put your mind to it, you can do anything. 

From then on, Lily never felt lazy anymore. Painting had made a huge difference in her life, and she was so happy!

Peter was a little rabbit. One day he was feeling hot so he decided to do some exercise. He hopped up the hill. As he hopped, he felt the warm sun on his back. It was so hot!

He hopped faster and when he reached the top he was panting. He took a deep breath and hopped around. He leaped and skipped in the open field. The sun was shining very bright and everything was hot. Peter hopped for a long time. He felt happy and strong.

When the sun started to go down, Peter stopped to rest. He lay down in the warm grass and laughed. He had had so much fun exercising. Peter hopped home happily. He was tired but he had enjoyed himself. He was ready for bed.

Once there was a chubby little girl named Jane. Jane wanted very badly to learn how to play the piano. Every day she heard the piano music coming from her neighbor's house, and it made her want to learn even more. However, her parents did not permit her to learn. They said she was too young and it was too expensive.

Jane was determined to change her parents' minds, so she hatched a plan. She practiced very hard on an old piano that was in her grandmother's attic. When her parents came to visit, she asked them if she could play them a song. To Jane's surprise, they said yes!

As Jane played, her parents were so amazed. They finally let her take piano lessons. Jane was so happy that she could finally learn how to play the piano she had been dreaming about.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their toy jets. They liked to make zooming noises and pretend they were flying in the sky. Sometimes they would strike each other's jets and say "Boom!" or "Crash!"

One day, a big jet flew over the park. It was loud and fast and shiny. Lily and Ben looked up and saw it. They were amazed and excited. They wanted to see it better.

"Let's follow it!" Ben said. He ran after the jet, holding his toy. Lily followed him, but she was worried. She did not want to go too far from the park. She did not want to get lost.

"Ben, wait!" Lily called. "We don't know where it's going. We should go back."

But Ben did not listen. He kept running and running. He wanted to catch the jet. He did not see the road or the cars or the people. He only saw the jet.

Lily ran after him, but she could not keep up. She was scared and tired. She wanted to go back to the park. She wanted to find their mom.

"Ben, stop!" Lily shouted. "We're in trouble. We need to go back."

But Ben did not hear her. He was too far away. He was too busy chasing the jet. He did not see the red light or the big truck. He only saw the jet.

Lily saw the red light and the big truck. She saw Ben running into the road. She screamed and dropped her toy. She wanted to save Ben. She wanted to strike the truck. She wanted to make it stop. But she could not. She was too small and too late. She only saw the jet.

It was the day of the big show. All the instruments were ready and the artist had his guitar in hand. He was a musician, ready to work.

The crowd was loud and full of excitement. The artist made his way on stage and stepped up to the mic. He strummed his guitar and began to play. The sound was clear and the audience was mesmerized.

The musician performed a number of beautiful songs that left the entire crowd speechless. He was at the top of his game.

After a few thunderous applause, the musician wished everyone a good night and walked off stage.

He had worked hard and the payoff was precious. Everyone was very impressed by the artist's clear and passionate performance.  The man was pleased and filled with joy. He had finally shown everyone what he was truly made of.

Once upon a time, there was a vegetable in a garden that nobody could see. It was hidden. But the vegetable was very happy, no matter what. Until one day, when a giant monster came along and tried to destroy it. 

The monster was big and strong, and the vegetable was scared and weak. The vegetable tried to run, but it was too late! The monster caught up and started to pull and smash the vegetable. 

But then something magical happened. A brave fairy appeared, and with a wave of her wand, she made the monster disappear!

The vegetable was saved! The fairy smiled and flew away, and the vegetable smiled too as it went back to its secret hiding place.

Spot was a dog who liked to play with his friends. He had a ball, a bone and a rope. He was happy when he shared his toys with other dogs. But one day, he saw a new dog in the park. The new dog was very tall and had long hair. Spot was afraid of the new dog.

"Who are you?" Spot asked the new dog.

"I am Fluffy. I just moved here with my family. Can I play with you?" Fluffy said.

Spot did not want to play with Fluffy. He thought Fluffy was too big and too different. He wanted to keep his toys for himself. He growled at Fluffy and ran away with his ball, his bone and his rope.

Fluffy was sad. He did not understand why Spot did not like him. He wanted to make friends and have fun. He followed Spot and tried to talk to him.

"Please, Spot, don't be mean. I just want to be your friend. Can I have one of your toys?" Fluffy said.

Spot did not listen to Fluffy. He was angry and scared. He screamed at Fluffy and bit his tail.

"Go away, Fluffy! You are not welcome here! These are my toys and you can't have them!" Spot said.

Fluffy yelped in pain and ran away. He cried and looked for his family. He felt lonely and hurt.

Spot was proud of himself. He thought he had scared Fluffy away. He had his toys and his park. He did not need anyone else. He played with his ball, his bone and his rope. But soon, he got bored. He looked around and saw no other dogs. He had no one to play with. He felt lonely and sad.

He realized he had made a mistake. He had been rude and selfish. He had hurt Fluffy's feelings. He had lost a chance to make a new friend. He felt sorry and ashamed.

He decided to look for Fluffy and apologize. He hoped Fluffy would forgive him and play with him. He learned that being kind and sharing is better than being mean and greedy. He learned that being different is not bad. He learned that everyone needs a friend.

One day there was a little girl and she wanted to go out and play. She asked her mom if she could go out in the yard and mom said yes.

The little girl ran out onto the modest lawn. She saw a big old tree with one perfect branch that was just the right size for her to swing on. She grabbed onto the branch with both hands and started to swing back and forth. She went higher and higher and she could feel the wind on her face.

The little girl felt so happy as she swung and she laughed out loud. Big grownups looked over the fence and smiled at her. Eventually the little girl stopped jumping because she was getting tired.

But the next day she couldn't wait to go out into the yard and swing on the tree again.

One Tuesday, a little girl was feeling sad. She didn't know why, but she wanted to go outside and find some fun. She entered the park and saw lots of children playing. She said hello, but nobody answered her. She felt even more sad.

But then she spotted a big slide. She entered the slide, excited to have some fun. She smiled as she went around and around, faster and faster. After that, she entered the sandbox, giggling as she played. She found some friends and together they made beautiful sandcastles.

The little girl was no longer sad. She had so much fun that she forgot all about why she was feeling sad in the first place. Her day at the park on Tuesday had been the best.

Jack was a 3-year-old boy and he loved to bounce. He liked to bounce so much, he even bounced when he walked down the street. One day, he reached a park with a big rubber bounce house. He was so excited to jump inside. 

Jack hopped in and started to bounce. He said to himself, "This is so much fun! I'm going to bounce until I can't anymore!" He kept jumping around and laughed as he flew high into the air. 

Suddenly, he heard his mom calling him from outside. 

"Time to go home, Jack!" said mom.

Jack did not want to leave so he asked his mom.

"Mom, can we come back tomorrow?" 

His mom smiled and said, "Sure thing. Now let's go home and have some yummy dinner!" 

Jack happily ran outside and saw his mom with a dictionary and a big smile on her face. 

"What's that dictionary for?" asked Jack.

"I want to check up on something," said his mom with a twinkle in her eye.

Jack and his mom went home, and he enjoyed his yummy dinner. He was eagerly waiting for the next day so he could visit the bounce house again!

Once upon a time there was a generous fireman. He was always out and about, helping people in need. One day, the fireman was travelling around town when he spotted a little 3 year old boy. The boy was sad and alone. The generous fireman wanted to make the boy feel better, so he asked if he could sign. The 3 year old nodded and followed the fireman to an open field.

The fireman reached into his pocket and pulled out a piece of paper. He started to trace a big smiley face on the paper, and when he was done the boy laughed. He was so happy that the fireman had taken the time to make him smile.

The 3 year old boy thanked the generous fireman and pointed to the sky. The fireman lifted his head and saw a bright rainbow stretching across the sky. The fireman smiled back and waved goodbye as he made his way off into the sunset. The little 3 year old boy watched him go, and he smiled, knowing that he had been helped by a generous fireman.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was named John and the other was called Mary. John and Mary had come to a special party.

When they arrived, they had to unpack all the things they had brought to the party. After everything was unpacked, they looked around and saw that the party was full of peace.

John and Mary had a lot of fun talking and playing games. But suddenly, John became very selfish. He wanted to do everything by himself and wouldn't share his things with Mary.

Mary was so sad and soon enough, the peace of the party had gone away. But instead of getting angry, Mary shared some of her own toys with John. When John saw how kind Mary was, he changed his mind.

John and Mary spent the rest of the party together and they were both happy. The party was once again full of peace!

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big ball. They liked to kick the ball, throw the ball, and bounce the ball.

One day, they found a pack of gum in their mom's purse. They had never seen gum before, but they thought it looked yummy. They each took a piece and put it in their mouths. They liked the sweet taste and the soft feel of the gum.

They decided to play with the ball and the gum at the same time. They kicked the ball, threw the ball, and bounced the ball. But they also chewed the gum, blew the gum, and stretched the gum.

Soon, they had a problem. The gum got stuck to the ball, to their hair, to their clothes, and to each other. They tried to pull the gum off, but it was very difficult. The more they pulled, the more the gum stretched and stuck.

"Help!" they cried. "We can't get the gum off!"

Their mom heard their cries and came to see what was wrong. She saw the mess they had made and was very angry. She took the ball, the gum, and the scissors. She cut the gum off the ball, their hair, their clothes, and their bodies. She threw the gum in the trash and the ball in the closet.

She scolded them for taking the gum without asking and for making a mess. She told them that gum was not a toy and that they should never play with it again. She said that gum could prevent them from talking, breathing, and eating properly. She said that gum could also hurt their teeth and their stomachs.

She made them wash their hands, their faces, and their mouths. She gave them a glass of water and a hug. She told them that she loved them, but that they had to be more careful and listen to her.

Tom and Lily felt sorry for what they had done. They said they were sorry and that they would not take the gum again. They learned their lesson and never played with gum again. They still liked to play with the ball, but only when their mom said it was okay.

Lily and her mom went to the market. Lily liked the market. She saw many pretty things. She saw fruits, flowers, toys and books. She wanted to touch everything.

"Mom, can I have this?" Lily asked. She pointed to a red ball. It was shiny and bouncy.

"Maybe later, sweetie. We have to buy some food first," her mom said. She took Lily's hand and walked to the next stall.

Lily was sad. She really wanted the ball. She saw a man selling balloons. He had many colors. Lily liked the pink one. It had a smiley face on it.

"Mom, can I have that?" Lily asked. She pointed to the balloon.

"Not now, honey. We have to hurry. The market will close soon," her mom said. She pulled Lily's hand and walked faster.

Lily was angry. She did not like to hurry. She wanted to have fun. She wanted the ball and the balloon. She did not want to go home.

She let go of her mom's hand. She ran back to the ball. She grabbed it and hugged it. She smiled.

"Hey, that's mine!" the seller shouted. He tried to take the ball from Lily.

Lily did not want to give the ball. She screamed. She screamed very loud. She screamed so loud that everyone in the market heard her.

Her mom heard her too. She turned around and saw Lily. She saw the seller. She saw the ball. She was shocked.

"Lily, what are you doing?" her mom asked. She ran to Lily. She took the ball from her. She gave it back to the seller. She said sorry.

Lily did not say sorry. She was still screaming. She wanted the ball. She wanted the balloon. She wanted everything.

Her mom was upset. She picked up Lily and carried her. She left the market. She did not buy anything.

Lily cried all the way home. She did not have a good day. She learned a hard lesson. She learned that she cannot have everything. She learned that she has to listen to her mom. She learned that screaming is not nice.

One day the sky was grey. It was starting to rain. It was so silly!

The rain started to pitter-patter on the ground. The trees were dripping with water. All the people outside ran for cover.

Nancy was watching from her bedroom window. She saw the funny sight of people running away from the rain. It made her giggle.

But she didn't mind the rain too much. She ran outside and twirled under the raindrops. It felt so cool and refreshing.

The rain eventually stopped and the sun came out. Everything was so sparkly and colourful. What a silly sight! Nancy smiled, happy to be outside again.

Anna was a very cheerful girl. She especially loved playing outside. One day, while Anna was playing in the garden, her mum came and called her inside.

Anna said, "Mum, why? I'm having so much fun!"

Mum smiled and said, "Anna, I need you to help me lift a blouse out of the cupboard. Will you come and help?"

Anna was very excited to help, so she followed her mum inside. Mum lifted the blouse from the cupboard and showed Anna.

"Now," said Mum, "Can you help me lift the blouse on my bed?"

Anna was eager to help, so she reached up and together with her mum, they lifted the blouse onto the bed.

When it was done, Anna said, "There!", feeling very proud of her work. 

Mum smiled and said, "Well done, Anna. You did a great job."

Anna was very cheerful as she gave her mum a big hug. She was so glad she had helped.

Once upon a time, in a peaceful forest, there lived a little bird named Blue. Blue loved to sing and fly all day long.

One day, Blue found a small box. He was very curious about what was inside. He opened the box and found a tiny creature. The creature said, "Please release me, and I will give you a special gift." Blue opened the box and let the creature out.

The creature thanked Blue and gave him the gift of time. Now, Blue could enjoy his peaceful forest even more. He could fly and sing all day, and never run out of time. Blue was very happy and grateful for his new gift.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to eat radishes that grew in the garden. One day, Benny saw a big red radish that he wanted to eat. He said, "I want to eat that big red radish!" But his mom said, "No, you can't eat that one. It's not ready yet."

Benny was sad, but he listened to his mom. The next day, Benny went back to the garden and saw that the big red radish had a tear in it. He said, "Mom, look! The big red radish has a tear in it. Can I eat it now?" His mom said, "Yes, you can eat it now. It's ready."

Benny was so happy that he got to eat the big red radish. It was the best radish he ever had. From that day on, Benny always waited until the radishes were ready to eat.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lucy went to the park with her mom. They brought a big bag full of toys to play with. When they got to the park, Lucy's mom sat down on a bench and said, "Lucy, let's unpack the toys now."

Lucy started to unpack the toys from the big bag. She found a red ball, a yellow plastic shovel, and a blue teddy bear. Lucy wanted to play with the red ball first, but the ball was very stubborn and did not want to roll.

"Please, ball, roll for me!" Lucy said. The stubborn red ball did not want to roll, but when Lucy asked nicely, it finally started to roll. Lucy was very happy to play with her red ball, the yellow plastic shovel, and the blue teddy bear.

After playing for a long time, Lucy and her mom packed up the toys and went home. Lucy was tired but happy from playing with her toys at the park. The stubborn red ball, the yellow plastic shovel, and the blue teddy bear were happy too, because they had a fun day with Lucy.

Once upon a time, in a peaceful forest, there lived a little lizard named Lizzy. Lizzy was green and loved to play with her friends. One day, she saw a big tree and wanted to climb it.

Lizzy tried to climb the tree, but she could not. She tried again and again, but she could not succeed. She felt sad and sat down. Her friend, a small bird named Billy, saw her and asked, "Why are you sad, Lizzy?"

"I want to climb the tree, but I can't," said Lizzy. Billy wanted to help her friend. He said, "Don't worry, Lizzy. Let's try together." So, Lizzy and Billy tried to climb the tree together.

With Billy's help, Lizzy was able to climb the tree. She felt very happy and said, "Thank you, Billy!" They both smiled and played together in the tree. From that day on, Lizzy and Billy were best friends, and they knew they could succeed in anything if they helped each other.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Tom and Jane. Tom and Jane were both three years old and liked playing together.

One day, Tom wanted to go on an adventure. Jane was worried but Tom told her he would be all right. So off they went.

As they explored, Tom noticed something shiny and sparkling in the grass. Tom reached for it and realized it was a sparkling stone. He held it in his hand and showed it to Jane.

Once upon a time there was a boy. His name was Timmy. Timmy was three years old.

One day Timmy went outside to play. He saw a big hill and decided to climb it. He was so happy to get to the top!

But then Timmy saw a creek. The creek was so deep, he thought he could never cross it. But then he noticed a log. Timmy decided to climb along the log. He was careful not to fall in the creek.

At last Timmy made it across the creek! When he looked back, he felt very successful. He had climbed the hill and crossed the creek. He was so proud of himself.

Timmy smiled and said, " I did it! I'm the best climber ever!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to build things with his hammer. He would hammer and hammer until he made something new. 

One day, Tim's friend came over and requested to use Tim's hammer. Tim said yes and gave his friend the hammer. But his friend got angry and broke the hammer. Tim was sad because he loved his hammer so much.

Tim's parents tried to fix the hammer, but it was broken beyond repair. Tim was so upset that he didn't want to build anything anymore. He lost his passion for creating things and never wanted to share his toys again.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who wanted to go on a row. He believed that if he was small enough he could fit in a row. He asked his mom if he could join the small row. His mom said yes, and the little boy was so excited. 
He picked out a small row and got in it. Without thinking he started to row. He realized he was going too fast and tried to slow down, but he couldn't. He kept going faster and faster until he crashed into a rock. He was very scared but luckily he was fine.
His mom came to the rescue and helped him get out of the row. She brought him back home and hugged him tight. From that day forward, he never tried to row again. 
But he still believed in the power of the small row. He was determined to try it again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play his guitar. He would strum it every day and make great music. One day, Timmy's little sister came into his room and tried to pinch his guitar strings. Timmy got mad and told her to stop. But then he showed her how to play a song and they made great music together. From that day on, Timmy and his sister played guitar together every day and had lots of fun. The end.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck. The truck has a picture of a cone with cream on it. Lily and Tom love cream. They run to the truck.

"Hello, kids. Do you want some cream?" the man in the truck says.

"Yes, please!" Lily and Tom say.

The man gives them each a cone with cream. Lily and Tom are happy. They lick their cream. It is sweet and cold.

But then, a boy comes. He is bigger than Lily and Tom. He has a weird hat. He looks at their cream.

"Hey, that's my cream!" he says. He tries to grab Lily's cone.

"No, it's not! It's mine!" Lily says. She holds her cone tight.

The boy laughs. He is teasing Lily. He tries to grab Tom's cone.

"No, it's not! It's his!" Tom says. He holds his cone tight.

The boy laughs. He is teasing Tom. He tries to grab both cones.

"Give me your cream!" he says.

Lily and Tom are scared. They don't like the boy. They don't like his weird hat. They don't like his teasing.

They look at each other. They have an idea. They lift their cones. They throw their cream at the boy.

"Splat!" The cream hits the boy's face. The boy is surprised. He is angry. He is messy.

Lily and Tom giggle. They are not scared anymore. They are brave. They are clever.

They run away from the boy. They find a new place to play. They don't need cream. They have fun.

Once, there was a little girl named Jane. She was 3 years old and very friendly. One day, a magical angel came to visit her. The angel was wearing a shiny white gown, with silver wings on her back. Jane was so excited. She wanted to remember the angel forever, so she took a picture.

The angel gave Jane a special bag with lots of fun things inside. There was a toy car, a teddy bear, and a storybook. Jane was so happy, she said thank you to the angel and waved as she flew away.

Jane loves to look at the picture of the angel sometimes. She remembers what the angel looked like and what was in the bag. Jane smiles when she remembers her friendly angel.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who lived in a big meadow. She was playing with her friends when suddenly the sun disappeared from the sky! The bunny was scared and asked her friends: "Where did the sun go?"

Her friends all said they didn't know, so the bunny had to go look for it. She hopped around the meadow, but couldn't find the sun anywhere. Suddenly she saw a rare rainbow in the sky!

"I know!" she shouted. "The sun must have gone past the rainbow!"

So she hopped towards the rainbow, but as she got closer, the sun disappeared behind a cloud. The bunny was sad and thought she had lost the sun forever.

Just then, a warm breeze touched her face and the cloud slowly moved away. There it was! The sun was there, shining brighter than before! The bunny was so happy and the meadow lit up with its warmth. From that day on, the bunny never lost the sun again.

Lily and Ben love to watch the parade. They see big balloons, loud drums, and funny clowns. They wave and cheer with their mom and dad.

But Lily wants to see more. She sees a big red fire truck at the end of the parade. She likes fire trucks. They are shiny and fast and reliable. They help people when there is a fire.

She tugs on her mom's hand and says, "Mom, can we go closer to the fire truck? Please, please, please?"

Her mom smiles and says, "Okay, Lily, we can go closer. But we have to be careful and stay with dad and Ben. The fire truck is very big and loud. It might scare you."

Lily nods and says, "I'm not scared, mom. I'm brave. Thank you, mom."

They walk to the end of the parade, where the fire truck is parked. Lily sees a friendly fireman sitting on the truck. He waves and says, "Hello, little girl. Do you like the fire truck?"

Lily nods and says, "Yes, I do. It's very pretty and strong. Can I see it closer?"

The fireman smiles and says, "Sure, you can. But you have to ask your mom and dad first. They have to say yes."

Lily looks at her mom and dad and says, "Mom, dad, can I see the fire truck closer? Please, please, please?"

Her mom and dad look at each other and say, "Okay, Lily, you can. But you have to be careful and listen to the fireman. He knows how to keep you safe."

Lily says, "Thank you, mom. Thank you, dad."

The fireman helps Lily climb on the fire truck. He shows her the hose, the ladder, and the siren. He lets her wear his helmet and jacket. He tells her stories about his job and his friends.

Lily is very happy. She thinks the fire truck is the best thing in the parade. She thanks the fireman and gives him a hug. She says, "You are very nice and reliable. You are my hero."

The fireman says, "You are very welcome and brave. You are my friend."

Once upon a time, there were two little birds who lived in a tree. One was called Brownie and the other was called Bluey. They were both very enthusiastic and liked to play games together.

One day, the birds were playing hide-and-seek and Brownie found the perfect hiding spot. It was behind a big twig! Brownie used his wings to muster around the twig, stirring it ever so lightly. After a few minutes, Bluey found Brownie and they both giggled with joy.

After that, the birds started to build a nest together. Brownie picked up the twig he was hidden behind and he used it for their nest. They stirred up some leaves and put the twig in the middle to hold everything together.

When the nest was finished, the birds were so pleased. They both hugged each other happily and Brownie said, "I'm so enthusiastic that we did it!" And Bluey said, "Me too!" 

And they both flew off together into the sky, happy to be with each other.

Once there was a little girl named Lily who loved the rug in her bedroom. She could cuddle up on the rug and feel safe. On this special day, Lily couldn't find her rug. She looked everywhere in her room, but she couldn't see it! She started to tremble, feeling scared and confused.

Suddenly, Lily heard a voice coming from beneath her bed. It said "Here I am, Lily! I'm hiding under your bed!". Lily crawled onto her bed and looked over the edge, and she spotted her rug tucked away in a hidden corner.

Lily smiled and said "Oh rug, why did you hide from me?". The rug replied by saying "I was feeling lonely and thought maybe if I hid, you'd come and find me. Now I'm happy you're here!".

Lily smiled even wider and said "I'll never let you be lonely again rug!". Then she stretched out on top of the rug and cuddled into it. Suddenly, the rug didn't feel lonely anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a swan named Lily. She was very pretty and had feathers as white as snow. One day, Lily went to the pond to swim but she saw that it was very dirty. She didn't like it at all. 

Lily decided to organize a group of ducks to help her clean the pond. They worked hard, but suddenly a mean alligator appeared. He wanted to eat Lily and her friends. 

But Lily was very brave and used her strong wings to scare the alligator away. She saved all her friends and they continued to clean the pond until it was sparkling clean. As a reward, they all shared a juicy orange that they found near the pond. From that day on, Lily and her friends knew that they could always count on each other to solve any problem.

Once there was a little girl who loved to splash. Everywhere the girl went, she would get the chance to splash, whatever it may be. One day the little girl went to the bathroom and saw a mirror. She noticed how shiny it was and wondered what would happen if she splashed it. So, she decided to try it!

She grabbed a cup, filled it with water and splashed it on the mirror. The splash was even bigger than the girl thought it would be! The mirror was now very messy and the girl had to clean it up. She used a towel and wiped the mirror until it was clean like before. The little girl happily ran off, ready to splash near her mum!

The little girl got on the bus. It was very busy inside. She was excited to go on the journey and have an adventure.

The bus driver smiled at her and gave her a ticket. She put her ticket in her pocket and watched as the bus drove away.

She looked out of the window and saw lots of things. There were people walking in the street and cars driving. She saw some children playing in the park and a cat chasing a bird.

The little girl was so busy watching the world go by that she didn't realise when the bus had already arrived at her stop. Luckily, the bus driver saw her and stopped the bus. She thanked the bus driver and happily stepped off the bus with her ticket in her hand. 

The little girl was so excited about the adventure she had on the bus. She knew she would never forget the things she had watched.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Bill. He was three years old and he was very happy.

One day, his parents asked him to do something very special and difficult. He had to put away all the toys in his room. Bill worked hard and he was perfect.

When he finished, his parents gave him a big reward. It was a big box of chocolates! Bill was very excited.

Bill ate some of the chocolates and saved the rest for later. He was very happy and it was a perfect day.

The day ended and Bill was tired. He lay down in bed, happy and full of joy.

Once upon a time, there was a poor rhinoceros who was looking for some food. He searched high and low, but he couldn't find anything!

"Oh dear," said the rhinoceros, feeling discouraged. "It seems like I will never find anything to eat!"

Just then, a friendly unicorn trotted over. "Don't worry, Rhinoceros!" The unicorn said. "I can help you find something to eat!"

The rhinoceros looked up, hopeful. The unicorn took the rhinoceros to a nearby pond where there were some tasty water plants. The rhinoceros quickly ate his fill.

"Thanks, Unicorn!" The rhinoceros said, feeling much better.

"You're welcome, Rhinoceros," the unicorn said with a smile.

And after that, the poor rhinoceros was never hungry again!

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their new toy. It was a big red ambulance that could spin and make noises. They took turns pushing it on the grass and watching it spin around.

"Look, Lily, it's spinning so fast!" Ben said.

"It's so fun, Ben, can I try again?" Lily asked.

"Okay, but be careful, don't let it go too far," Ben said.

Lily pushed the ambulance with all her might and it spun faster and faster. But it also went farther and farther, until it hit a big rock and flew into the air. Lily and Ben gasped as they saw the ambulance crash on the ground and break into pieces.

"Oh no, our ambulance!" Lily cried.

"It's okay, Lily, don't cry, we can fix it," Ben said.

He ran to the ambulance and picked up the pieces. He tried to put them back together, but they didn't fit. The wheels were bent, the siren was broken, and the soft red paint was scratched.

"It's not okay, Ben, it's ruined, we can't fix it," Lily said.

She hugged the ambulance and sobbed. Ben felt sad too. He hugged Lily and the ambulance and said,

"I'm sorry, Lily, it was an accident, I didn't mean to break it. Maybe we can get a new one, or play with something else."

Lily looked at Ben and saw that he was sorry. She wiped her tears and said,

"It's okay, Ben, I'm sorry too, I pushed it too hard. Maybe we can get a new one, or play with something else."

They smiled at each other and put the ambulance in their backpack. They decided to play on the swings instead. They still had fun, even without the ambulance. They learned to be careful with their toys and to share them with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy old man. Every day he would ignore the people around him and be angry with everyone. One day he went to the market, and saw a big and delicious potato. He couldn't resist it and took the potato without asking.

Once upon a time, there was a big theater in a small town. The theater was rare because it was very old and special. People from all over came to see the shows there.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He went to a new restaurant with his mom and dad. They sat down at a table and looked at the menu. Timmy saw some yummy food he wanted to try.

Once upon a time there was a fluffy puppy. The puppy was very soft and had a gentle texture. He loved to run and play in the park. One day, while playing, he hurt his paw. He yelped in pain and his puppy friends ran to see what was wrong.

The sun was shining and the sky was blue. All the animals were playing in the meadow and the birds were singing.

Suddenly, it started to rain and the meadow began to soak. The animals were so sad; all of their fun had stopped.

Ben and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big dog. The dog has a medal on its neck. It is shiny and red.

"Wow, look at that dog!" Ben says. "It has a medal. It must be rich."

Sam nods. He feels bad. He says sorry to the dog and its owner. The owner is nice. He says it is okay. He says the dog is not mean. He says the dog was scared. He says the medal is a reward. The dog is a hero. The dog saved a child from a fire.

"Wow, really?" Ben says. "That is amazing. The dog is a hero. The medal is special."

"Yes, it is," the owner says. "Do you want to pet the dog? He is friendly. He will not bite you if you are gentle."

Ben and Sam pet the dog. The dog licks them. They smile. They are happy. They learn a lesson. They do not touch other people's things. They respect the dog and its medal. They make a new friend. The end.

Mama and Jack were very excited. They had just moved into a new house. Jack was only three so he couldn't help much, but he watched as Mama unpacked all their boxes. He saw clothes and toys, books and games. When Mama asked him what he was most excited about, he smiled and said, "I'm excited to make friends here!"

But when they opened up one of the boxes, he saw something strange - it was a stiff, white jacket. Jack was confused. "What is this thing?" he asked.

Once upon a time, there was a messy room. Toys were everywhere, and it was hard to walk without stepping on something. A little girl named Lily didn't want to clean it up, so she just stared at the mess.

Anna likes dogs. She nods and smiles. She walks to the lady and the dog. She pauses. She is a little scared. The dog is bigger than her.

The lady says, "Don't worry. Rex is very friendly. He likes children. He won't bite. He just wants to say hello."

Anna reaches out her hand. The dog sniffs it. He licks it. He wags his tail. Anna giggles. She pets the dog. She feels happy.

The lady says, "You are very brave. Do you want to join us for lunch? I have some sandwiches and cookies. Rex has some bones and water."

Anna says, "Yes, please. Thank you. Can I call my mom first?"

The lady says, "Of course. Where is your mom?"

Anna says, "She is at home. She is working. She said I can play in the park until noon."

The lady says, "OK. Let's go to that bench. You can use my phone to call your mom. Then we can have lunch together."

Anna says, "OK. Thank you. You are very nice. And Rex is very cute."

The lady says, "You are very welcome. And you are very sweet. I'm glad we met. Maybe we can see each other again."

Anna says, "Yes, maybe. I hope so. Maybe Ben can come too. He is my friend. He likes dogs too."

The lady says, "That would be nice. Maybe we can be friends too."

Anna says, "Yes, we can. Friends are good."

They walk to the bench. They call Anna's mom. They have lunch. They talk and laugh. They are not lonely anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a quiet wagon. The wagon was old and grey. One day, a little girl saw the wagon. She wanted to play with it.

The little girl jumped into the wagon. She laughed and smiled as she pushed the wagon around in circles. She jumped in and out of the wagon with delight.

Suddenly, her mom called her for dinner. The little girl said goodbye to the wagon and ran off. The little girl never forgot her quiet wagon.

The End

Joe was a boy who loved to play. One day, he wanted to play with a hoop. However, he only had an orange hoop. Joe and his mom went to the store together, but Joe started to complain when he didn't see the kind of hoop he wanted.

Mom said to Joe, "What kind of hoop do you want, sweetheart?". Joe replied, "A blue one, mommy, not an orange one". His mom laughed and said, "I think an orange hoop is lovely, and it will look really nice in your room, right?". 

Joe thought about it, and then nodded his head in agreement. The two went home with the orange hoop, and Joe smiled all the way. Joe's mom was so happy to see Joe so happy and content. So, Joe played with his hoop for hours, and he never complained anymore.

Lily was a shy girl who liked to play with puzzles. She had many puzzles with animals, cars, and flowers. She could solve them very fast and make nice pictures.

One day, she got a new puzzle from her grandma. It was a big puzzle with a zoom. A zoom was a thing that could fly in the sky and make loud noises. Lily had never seen a zoom before. She was curious and excited.

She opened the box and took out the pieces. She tried to find the corners and the edges. She looked at the picture on the box. It was a zoom with red and blue stripes. It had wings and a tail and a nose.

Lily started to solve the puzzle. She found the pieces that matched the colors and the shapes. She worked hard and had fun. She did not notice that her brother Max came into the room.

Max was not shy. He liked to play with balls and cars and trucks. He saw Lily's puzzle and wanted to play too. He grabbed some pieces and tried to fit them in. He did not look at the picture. He did not care about the zoom.

Lily was angry. She said, "No, Max, that is not right. You are messing up my puzzle. Go away and play with your own toys."

Max did not listen. He said, "I want to play with the zoom. It is cool. Let me help you."

He pushed some pieces and broke the puzzle. Lily cried. She said, "You are mean, Max. You ruined my puzzle. I don't want to play with you."

Max felt sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to hurt you. I just wanted to play with you. Can we fix the puzzle together?"

Lily stopped crying. She said, "OK, Max, but you have to be careful and follow the picture. The zoom is not easy to solve. It has many pieces and details."

Max nodded. He said, "OK, Lily, I will be careful and follow the picture. The zoom is hard to solve. But it is also fun and pretty."

They hugged and smiled. They worked together and solved the puzzle. They made the zoom fly in the sky and make loud noises. They were happy and proud. They showed their puzzle to their grandma and said, "Look, grandma, we solved the zoom. It is a gift from you. Thank you, grandma."

Grandma smiled and said, "You are welcome, my dears. You did a great job. I'm glad you solved the zoom. And I'm glad you played together. You are a good team."

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful princess who wore a veil on her head. The veil was like a pretty scarf that covered her hair. The princess loved her veil because it made her feel special and pretty.

One day, the princess was going to a big party. She needed a dependable horse to take her there. She asked her friend who had many horses to supply her with one. Her friend gave her a strong and dependable horse that would take her to the party safely.

As the princess rode on the horse, her veil fluttered in the wind. She felt happy and excited to go to the party. When she arrived, everyone admired her beautiful veil and the dependable horse that brought her there. The princess had a wonderful time and was grateful to her friend for supplying her with such a great horse.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Bun Bun. Bun Bun loved to jump on the rug in his cozy burrow. One day, while he was jumping on the rug, he heard a loud noise outside. Bun Bun was scared and didn't know what to do. He hopped to the door and peeked outside. 

Suddenly, a big, scary fox jumped out from behind a tree. Bun Bun tried to run, but his feet got tangled in the rug. The fox caught him and took him away. Poor Bun Bun was never seen again.

Lily and Tom are playing in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. Lily wants to give the snowman a glove, but she only has one. She looks for the other glove, but she cannot find it.

"Tom, do you have my glove?" she asks.

"No, I have my own gloves. See?" Tom says, showing his hands.

"Maybe we can ask Mom for another glove," Lily says.

They run to the house and knock on the door. Mom opens the door and smiles.

"Hello, my little snowflakes. What do you need?" she asks.

"Mom, can we have another glove for the snowman? We only have one," Lily says.

"Sure, let me see what I have. You can come in and warm up for a bit," Mom says.

She goes to the closet and finds an old glove that she does not use anymore. She gives it to Lily and says, "Here you go. This glove is very helpful. It can keep the snowman's hand warm and cozy."

"Thank you, Mom. You are very helpful too," Lily says.

She hugs Mom and runs back to the snowman with Tom. They put the glove on the snowman's other hand and smile.

"Look, we finished the snowman. He looks very happy," Tom says.

"Yes, he does. And he has two helpful gloves," Lily says.

They clap their hands and dance around the snowman. They are very happy too.

Once there was a tank. Inside the tank lived a fish. His name was Shake. He liked to explore and have adventures. One day he decided to head out of his tank to explore the world outside.

As he swam around, he noticed something very interesting! Nearby, he saw a big tree. Shake was so excited and wanted to go explore it. He swam closer to have a better look.

As he swam nearer, Shake heard a friendly voice. It said, â€œHello, Shake! Iâ€™m Sam. What are you doing here?â€ Shake was a bit scared, as he didnâ€™t know who Sam was. He said, â€œIâ€™m exploring the big tree. It looks so interesting!â€ 

Sam laughed and said, â€œYou know what? I think you can make it to the top of the tree!â€ Shake was sure he couldnâ€™t, but Sam kept encouraging him. Finally, he decided to try it. He wiggled his tail furiously and shook his way up to the top of the tree. He was so excited that he made it! 

The view from the top of the tree was amazing. Shake was so happy he decided to explore the world outside of his tank. He waved goodbye to Samuel, thanked him for his help, and happily swam back to his tank.

Once upon a time there was a young boy called Tom. One day Tom wanted to go on a special adventure. He decided to enter a nearby forest with his kayak.
Tom was so excited as he paddled through the forest. Everything was so quiet! Suddenly he spotted something very unique. It was a shiny beetle with blue wings. Tom was mesmerized by the beauty of the beetle. 
He wanted to take the beetle back home with him. He carefully picked it up with his hands and put it in his kayak. Then Tom paddled away and went back to his house.
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a group of animals who were all friends. One day, the bunny asked the bear, â€œHey friend, what do you want to do today?â€ The bear replied gently, â€œLetâ€™s watch a peaceful firework show!â€ The bunny smiled and said, â€œLetâ€™s go!â€

So they hopped and ran until they reached the best spot to see the firework show. â€œOh wow!â€ the bunny shouted when all the colorful firework lit up the night sky. It was so pretty!

The bear smiled, wrapped his arms around his friend, and said, â€œIsnâ€™t it beautiful?â€ The bunny nodded and replied, â€œItâ€™s so peaceful!â€ The animals watched the firework show until the sky turned dark again. They said goodbye and went home, their hearts feeling full and happy.

Once there was a boy named Bob. He loved to look at the big bright blue sky. One day, he decided to go for a walk in the park.

He looked around and noticed a pond. As he walked closer, he could see a big fish swimming around. He was so excited, he had never seen anything like it before!

The fish was very gentle and the boy could tell that it was a tuna. Bob looked into the water and watched the tuna swim around. It was so beautiful!

Bob suddenly noticed a bird flying above the pond. He looked up and watched as the bird circled around. Then it swooped down and landed right next to the tuna!

Bob was so surprised that he didn't even move. The bird looked around and then flew away with the tuna still in its beak.

Bob was amazed. He could hardly believe that he had just seen a bird with a tuna in its beak! He couldn't wait to tell everyone about his adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to a park with her mom and dad. When they arrived, Lily looked around and saw lots of trees, flowers, and kids playing.

Lily saw a staff member and she got excited. She ran up to him and asked, "Can I have a balloon, please?" The staff member smiled and said, "Of course, which color do you want?"

Lily picked a pink balloon and held it tightly. She was so excited that she ran to her parents and said, "Look, I got a balloon!" They smiled and said, "That's great, Lily. Let's go play on the swings." They all had a fun day at the park and Lily was happy with her new balloon.

Once upon a time there was a troubled boy. He was so sad he couldn't think of anything that could make him feel better. He sat outside and looked around him sadly.

Suddenly he heard music. He looked up and saw a group of people dancing. They were happy, and the boy couldn't help but smile.

The boy laughed and began to dance too. He moved his feet around in circles and jumped up and down. He felt much better.

But soon there was a loud noise and the boy stopped to listen. A big animal was making angry noises and coming closer and closer. The boy was scared and ran away as fast as he could.

The animal seemed to follow him though, and the boy ran harder and harder. He didn't know what was happening! The boy tried to remember what his mommy had taught him: in tough times, just keep dancing.

So the boy started to dance. He moved his feet around in circles and jumped up and down. The animal stopped to watch the boy's silly dance. And after a few moments it walked away, just like that! 

The boy was no longer scared. He was relieved and he laughed as he danced. He was sure he had faced the threat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to draw and color. One day, she drew a picture of a silly monster. She showed it to her mom and said, "Look at my creative monster!"

Her mom laughed and said, "That's a funny joke, Lily!"

Lily was happy that her mom liked her drawing. Later that day, Lily's dad came home from work. Lily showed him her monster picture too.

Dad said, "Wow, Lily! You're so creative! What's the result of your monster's silly joke?"

Lily giggled and said, "He tickles people with his monster arms!" Everyone laughed and Lily felt proud of her silly monster drawing.

One day, Jane wanted to go on a ride. She got into her daddy's big, red car. It was so big that it looked like it would never fit in the tiny garage. But somehow, it got in and the garage door closed. 

 Jane and her dad drove to a bright park. When they got there, they saw a tall slide. Jane screamed with delight! She put on her helmet and raced over to the slide. "Whee!" she yelled as she rode down. 

Her dad watched, smiling. When she was done, he said, "Let's go find a shelter for lunch." Jane nodded eagerly. They walked until they found a nice, sun-filled spot beneath a big tree. Dad put out a blanket and Jane munched on her lunch. 

After lunch, Dad said, "Let's go for another ride!" Jane clapped her hands and raced off to find another slide. She could hardly wait to go down it!

Mum was anxious. She had many things to do and the day was flying by. But she decided to take a moment and relax with her little daughter. So they sat together on the couch, snuggled up close.
