Mum hugged her daughter and kissed her thumb. "Time for a nap, little one," she said.

The little girl rubbed her eyes and stretched. She opened her mouth wide and let out a big yawn. Mum smiled and hugged her again. She was so sweet and tired.

Soon, the little girl was sound asleep. Mum stayed close and stroked her daughter's head. All was peaceful and calm.

Mum was so grateful for the quiet moment. It was the best way to relax and feel less anxious. Even a few minutes could make a difference. It was amazing what a yawn could do.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named John. John lived in a big house with a distant armchair. Every day, he liked to bounce on the armchair.

One day, John's mom said, "No bouncing on the armchair!" John didn't want to listen, so he kept bouncing until suddenly the armchair broke!

John was very sad, but he knew he had to fix it. He ran and got a tool box, but the tools were too heavy to use.

John thought and thought, and he had an idea. He got two pillows and put them under the armchair. Then he bounced on them until they were just right.

John's mom was so happy to see the armchair fixed. From then on, whenever John wanted to bounce, he would put the pillows under the armchair.

Once there was a kitty called Dotty. She was a small, fluffy, cute kitty. Dotty loved to go outside and explore her garden that was so wide.

One day when Dotty was outside something made her sneeze. She didn't know what it was. She started to sneeze and sneeze until all of a sudden, a tiny paw touched her nose. It was a mouse! She was so startled that she jumped up very high!

The mouse was so scared too. It was scared that Dotty would hurt it with her paw. But instead Dotty did something very unexpected. She went up to the mouse and gently licked it with her tongue.

The mouse was even more surprised. It started to purr and Dotty gave it a big hug! From that day on, Dotty and the mouse became the best of friends. They explored the wide garden together and sneezed when something tickled their noses.

The bell rang loudly. Trudy the happy girl heard it and smiled. She loved ringing the red bell. 

Trudy was very fond of plants. She was very careful with them too. She watered them every day and talked to them.

One morning, Trudy saw a careless boy near her plants. He was picking the flowers off her pretty plants. Trudy asked, "Why are you doing that?"

The careless boy shrugged and said, "I'm just having fun." 

Trudy shook her head. She said, "My plants are very special to me. Please don't pick them again."

The boy was sorry for his careless mistake. He promised he would never pick Trudy's plants again. Trudy smiled and rang the bell.

Once, Bob saw a tall pool. He wanted to stay inside it. So, he hopped in.

Bob was happy to feel cool in the pool. He swam around and got a lot of splashes! 

"Can I play too, Bob?" asked his sister Helen.

"Yes!" shouted Bob, and he quickly showed Helen how to swim.

The two of them stayed in the tall pool for hours and hours. They were having so much fun that they forgot how late it had gotten!

Mom came to the pool and called out, "Come on. It's time to go home now!" 

So Bob and Helen reluctantly stayed out of the big pool, and went home to bed.

Once upon a time, there was a Huge spaghetti that stretched from one mountain to the other. Two little children, Jack and Jane, were standing by the spaghetti. 

"Let's twist it!" said Jane. 

"We can't," said Jack. "It's too Huge."

Jane kept insisting, but Jack refused. 

Suddenly, an old lady came walking by. She had a kind face and she was wearing a shawl. "What are you trying to do?" she asked the children. 

"We want to twist the Huge spaghetti," said Jane.

The old lady smiled and shook her head. "It's too Huge for you to twist. But if you work together and never give up, you can do it," she said.

Jack and Jane worked very hard, and eventually they managed to twist the Huge spaghetti. As they enjoyed the view of their accomplishment, the old lady smiled.

The moral of the story is to never give up! No matter how Huge the task may seem, if you work together you can accomplish anything.

Once upon a time there lived a girl called Emma. One day, Emma got an invite to the a birthday party. She was very excited. She quickly put on a pretty dress and rushed to the party.

When she got there it was very big. She couldn't believe it! It was enormous. Everything was so colourful and there were so many people there.

The party had lots of fun things to do. Everyone was eating cake and playing games. But Emma couldn't join in. Her tooth was very sore and it caused her pain. She tried to cope but it was too much and she started to cry.

Everyone was so kind and wanted to help her. They got some ice cream and put it on her tooth. It was cold but it felt better. Soon, she was able to join in with the party and she had lots of fun.

Ben and Lily wanted to play dress up. They found some old costumes in the attic. Ben put on a pirate hat and a sword. Lily wore a fairy dress and a wand. They pretended to be on a ship, sailing to a magic island.

"Arr, matey, I see the island ahead!" Ben said. "There must be treasure there!"

"Maybe, but we have to be careful. There might be monsters, too!" Lily said. She waved her wand and made some sparkles.

They climbed down the stairs and went to the backyard. They saw a big tree that looked like a ship. They ran to it and climbed on the branches.

But they did not see the dog next door. The dog was big and loud. He did not like strangers. He saw Ben and Lily and barked. He jumped over the fence and ran to the tree.

"Roof, roof, roof!" The dog said. He wanted to catch them.

Ben and Lily were scared. They did not know what to do. They looked for a way to escape.

"Quick, jump to the swing!" Ben said. He saw a swing hanging from another branch. He grabbed his sword and swung to it.

"Help, I can't reach it!" Lily said. She was too small. She held her wand and hoped for a miracle.

Then, they heard a voice. It was their mom. She came out of the house and saw the dog. She was compassionate. She did not want the dog to hurt them.

"Hey, boy, calm down. It's okay. They are just playing." She said. She walked to the dog and petted him. She gave him a treat and a toy. The dog stopped barking. He wagged his tail and licked her hand.

"Mom, you saved us!" Ben said. He jumped off the swing and hugged her.

"Mom, you are a fairy godmother!" Lily said. She flew down from the tree and kissed her.

Mom smiled and hugged them. She looked at their costumes and laughed.

"You two are very creative. But next time, be careful of the dog. He is not a monster, but he is not a friend, either."

She took them inside and gave them some cookies and milk. They told her about their adventure. They were happy and safe. They learned a lesson. They did not need a magic island. They had a magic mom.

Marc was a young boy who was always looking for fun. One day, he saw a girl playing by herself and he thought it would be nice to join her. He asked her if he could play with her and she said yes. 

They started talking and Marc quickly realized how boring the girl was. He told her he valued her, but he didn't really mean it. 

The girl noticed that Marc wasn't really listening to her, so she asked him what he valued. Marc was too impatient to really explain it properly and said, 'I value things that are interesting'. 

The girl felt hurt and ran away crying. Marc tried to apologize, but it was too late. He realized it was his own fault for not valuing her properly and he felt sad because he had hurt the girl's feelings. Unfortunately, it was too late to fix the situation and Marc was left with a dull and boring day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in her garden. One day, she found a big, sour lemon and decided to eat it. But as soon as she took a bite, she made a funny face and sighed because it was too sour.

Suddenly, she felt a pain in her lung and started to cough. She realized that she had accidentally swallowed a lemon seed and it got stuck in her lung. She tried to cough it out, but it wouldn't come out.

Lily was scared and didn't know what to do. She went to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom took her to the hospital, where the doctors helped her get the seed out of her lung. From that day on, Lily learned to be more careful when eating things and to always ask for help when she needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and curious little girl called Rose. She lived in a small cottage in the middle of a dark and mysterious forest. Rose was always asking her parents lots of questions. One day, she asked them what lay beyond the forest. Her parents told her that beyond the forest was a beautiful beach with crystal clear waters. 

The next morning, full of excitement, Rose packed some lunch and set out on an adventure. As she wandered through the forest, she noticed the ground getting wetter and the air becoming very smelly. Soon she noticed that instead of the beach, she'd found a big bog.

Rose was so disappointed. But, she was determined to not lose her sense of adventure. She decided to take a closer look, so she stepped closer to the bog. Suddenly, Rose heard a voice calling out to her, â€œHelp me!â€.

It was a small animal that had become trapped in the bog. Rose thought and thought about what to do. She eventually decided to reply to the animal, â€œI am here to help you!â€. 

Rose then used some nearby sticks to slowly pull the animal out of the bog. The animal thanked Rose for her kind and courageous act. 

The moral of the story is: a kind heart and courageous spirit will always help you find a way out of any difficult situation.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved playing with his toys and going on adventures. One day, Jack's mom asked him to go to the store to buy some milk. Jack was excited to go on this adventure all by himself.

As Jack walked to the store, he saw a man in a black mask running away from a store with a bag in his hand. Jack knew something was not right. When Jack arrived at the store, he saw that the man had stolen a toy from the store. The store owner asked Jack if he saw the man's number plate. Jack remembered the number and told the store owner.

When Jack returned home, he saw the man in the black mask walking down the street. Jack felt guilty for not telling his mom about the man earlier. Jack quickly ran to his mom and told her everything. His mom was proud of Jack for being brave and for helping the store owner. From that day on, Jack always made sure to zip his lips and tell his mom if he saw anything suspicious.

Once upon a time there was a green frog who was helpless and alone. He looked everywhere but couldn't find anyone to play with. He hopped along, feeling sad, until he suddenly heard music coming from a nearby pond. When the frog got closer, he saw two fish happily swimming together and singing sweetly. He was so excited that he quickly joined them in the pond! 

The frog found that he had the most fun when he was swimming and dancing with his new fish friends. They partied together all day and night, playing games and laughing the whole time. The frog was so happy he never wanted to leave the pond. 

The next morning, the sun came up and the friends knew it was time to part. The fish waved goodbye and the frog said a sad goodbye too. But as he hopped away, the frog felt hopeful. He knew his new friends wanted to play with him again soon, and he was excited for their next playdate!

Once upon a time, there was a cat named Whiskers. Whiskers was very tired because he had been running and playing all day. He decided to take a nap in the sun. 

While Whiskers was sleeping, a bird came and left a message for him. The message said that there was a mouse in the garden. Whiskers woke up and saw the message. He got up and went to the garden to catch the mouse.

When he got there, he saw that the mouse was already gone. Whiskers started to frown because he really wanted to catch the mouse. He went back home and went back to sleep.

Once upon a time, there was a mummy and a daddy who were bossy. One day, they were going to a special place. They were hoping that their little girl would receive a new language. 

When they reached the special place, the little girl was so excited! She saw lots of new people, and she heard lots of new sounds. There were lots of people and they were all speaking different languages. The little girl was amazed! 

The mummy and daddy had arranged for the little girl to learn the language of the people at the special place. They spent time listening and talking together.

At the end of the day, the little girl received a new language. She couldn't wait to show it to her mummy and daddy. She spoke it to them and they were so proud of her! 

The little girl was so happy, she had received a new language!

Once there was a little girl. She was always sad and one day she started to cry. The tears were running down her red cheeks. She had been crying for a long time and she did not know why.

Suddenly, she saw a small pebble. It was very smooth and sparkly. It looked like it was just waiting for her. She picked it up and held it in her hands. It felt warm, like it was a little friend.

The little girl stopped crying. She started to feel much better. Her sorrow melted away when she saw the pebble. Now she had something shiny and available to make her happy.

Once upon a time there lived a mighty warrior. He was very brave and strong and didn't know fear. One day he set off on a quest, for he wanted to capture a most magical prize. 

He searched far and wide and finally he found it - an old bathtub! He was so happy and ready to bring home his wonderful new prize. But he was soon stopped in his tracks by an old wizard. He warned the warrior that the bathtub contained a great power, and that soon it would have to be returned. 

The warrior was undaunted and he saw no reason to return the bathtub, as he had found it after all. But the wizard insisted and before the warrior knew it, the bathtub was returned to the wizard and the warrior was left with nothing. 

But the warrior realised that it was his own brave and mighty heart that had made the journey worthwhile and that he would treasure that forever.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a modern phone. Every day he would urge his friends to come and play. One day, he decided to call them all on his phone. He tried to reach them one by one, but no one was answering. He felt so sad and did not know what to do. 

Then, he had an idea. He decided to go to his friendsâ€™ houses, to urge them in person. He started running so he could reach them quickly. He ran and ran until he finally reached each of their houses. He looked through the window of one friend and urged him to come outside and play. His friend smiled and said yes!

He went to all of his friendsâ€™ houses, urging them all to come out and play. Finally, he had all of his friends together and it was time to play. They all had the best day ever and enjoyed each otherâ€™s company. 

From that day forward, the boy always remembered his urge to call his friends and go to them in person. He learnt that he should never give up because, in the end, his urge was worth it!

Tommy did not like meat. He thought it was disgusting. It smelled bad and tasted worse. He did not want to eat it for dinner.

But his mom said he had to eat some meat or he would not get any dessert. She put a big piece of meat on his plate. Tommy felt sad and angry.

He looked around the room. He saw his dog, Spot, under the table. He had an idea. He picked up his fork and pretended to eat the meat. But he did not put it in his mouth. He removed it from his plate and threw it under the table. Spot was happy. He ate the meat in one bite.

Tommy smiled. He thought he was clever. He asked his mom for dessert. But his mom was not fooled. She saw what he did. She was not happy. She said he had to eat another piece of meat or he would get no dessert and go to bed early.

Tommy felt sad and angry again. He did not like meat. He thought it was disgusting. He wished he had a different dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal bean who lived in the forest. One day, a fierce wind blew through the trees. The loyal bean was scared, so he started to call out to anyone who could help him. 

Suddenly, he heard a booming voice coming from the top of a tall tree. It was a brave bear who said, "I will protect you little bean!"

The bear stretched out her arms and caught the loyal bean in her giant paws. She snuggled him close, and the loyal bean felt safe. 

The brave bear nuzzled the loyal bean and said, "You can count on me to always keep you safe." The loyal bean smiled and thanked the brave bear for protecting him. 

The loyal bean and the brave bear became best friends, and the bear always kept the loyal bean safe from the fierce winds. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old. She loved to play in the garden, swing in her swing and be independent.

One day, Amy had an exciting adventure. She went for a ride in a funny vehicle. She had never seen anything like it before! It was bright and colourful. She loved the feeling of being inside of it and exploring.

The vehicle took her to a big park. She saw so many things: trees, flowers, birds and other animals. She felt excited and wanted to remember it all.

When the ride was over, Amy thought back to the fun she had. She remembered how much she enjoyed the vehicle and being independent. She knew she'd never forget her adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He had a big toy box where he kept all his toys. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to tidy up his toys and put them back in the toy box. Timmy didn't want to tidy up because he wanted to keep playing.

But then, Timmy's little sister came in and wanted to play too. She wanted to play with Timmy's favorite toy car, but she couldn't find it because all the toys were scattered around the room. Timmy saw that his sister was sad, so he decided to cover her with a blanket to make her happy.

After that, Timmy realized that he couldn't play with his toys if they were all over the place. So, he decided to slide all his toys back into the toy box. It was hard work, but he felt good when he was finished. Timmy's mom was very happy that he tidied up and he got to play with his sister and his toys again!

One day, a lively cat named Tom went to the park. He saw his friend, a dog named Max. Max was playing with a measure. Tom was curious and asked, "What are you doing, Max?"

Max said, "I am measuring the length of this stick. I want to show you how long it is." Tom was excited to learn. They both looked at the measure and saw the numbers. Max showed Tom how to use the measure.

They had so much fun measuring different things in the park. They measured the slide, the swings, and even the trees. They laughed and played all day. Tom was happy that Max showed him something new.

Once there was a young girl who loved to play. Every day she would go out and use her imagination to create adventures. One day, she found a heart in her garden and she was filled with joy. She embraced the heart in her hands as she ran outside to show it to her friends.

The little girl and her friends played with the heart all day long. In the morning they ran around it, in the afternoon they skipped over it, and in the evening they sang songs around it. It felt like a magical time and the girl's young heart filled up with happiness.

As the sun began to set, the little girl gently placed the heart back into the garden. She took one last look at it and smiled, knowing that it would keep her happy for many years to come.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to go on adventures in the forest near her house. One day, she woke up early and decided to go on a walk. She put on her coat and went outside. 

As she walked, she saw a thin mist in the air. It looked like a cloud that was really close to the ground. Lily thought it was magical. She decided to follow the mist and see where it went. 

The mist led her to a clearing in the forest. In the middle of the clearing was a tree with a swing hanging from one of its branches. Lily was so happy she had followed the mist. She spent the whole morning swinging and having fun. She decided it was the best adventure she had ever been on.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play outside. One day, Timmy went on an adventure in the woods with his blue flashlight. He walked and walked until he found a big ice cream cone. Timmy was so excited to eat it, but it was too cold outside and the ice cream started to melt. 

Suddenly, a mean bear appeared and growled at Timmy. "Give me your flashlight!" the bear demanded. Timmy was scared and didn't want to give up his favorite toy. But the bear was very big and Timmy was very small. So, he gave the bear his blue flashlight. 

Timmy was sad and started to cry. He wished he had never gone on his adventure. He walked back home without his flashlight and without his ice cream. When he got home, his mom asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her everything that had happened. His mom hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. We can buy you a new flashlight. But always remember to be careful when you're outside."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a big smile and two thumbs. One day, Lily spun around and around until she got dizzy. She fell down and her thumb hurt. Her mom gave her a kiss and a band-aid, and Lily felt better. From then on, Lily was careful not to spin too much and make herself dizzy again.

Lily was playing with her ball in the park. She liked to kick it and watch it fly. She saw a big tree and wanted to hit it with her ball. She ran and kicked the ball hard. But the ball did not hit the tree. It hit a bird.

The bird fell to the ground. Lily was scared. She ran to the bird and saw that it was not moving. She felt sorry for the bird. She picked it up and hugged it. She wanted to help it.

She ran to her mom and showed her the bird. Her mom was sad too. She said they had to go to the vet. The vet was a person who helped animals. They got in the car and drove to the vet.

The vet looked at the bird. He said it had a broken wing. He said he had to take an x-ray. An x-ray was a picture that showed the bones inside the body. He took the bird to a room and put it on a table. He turned on a machine and took the x-ray.

He came back with the x-ray. He showed it to Lily and her mom. He pointed to the wing. He said there was a crack in the bone. He said he had to fix it. He said he had to put a bandage on the wing. He said the bird would be okay.

Lily was happy. She thanked the vet. She said she was sorry for hitting the bird. She said she would be careful next time. The vet smiled. He said it was an accident. He said he was glad Lily brought the bird to him.

He gave the bird back to Lily. He said she could keep it until it got better. He said she had to feed it and keep it warm. He said she had to be gentle with it. He said he would see them again in a few weeks.

Lily nodded. She held the bird close. She said she would take good care of it. She said she would be its friend. The bird looked at her with its clear eyes. It made a soft sound. Lily smiled. She said she loved the bird.

Tiny was walking in the park when she noticed a big spring. It was so big and shiny, it made her jump! She ran over to it and touched it with her finger. The spring moved, so she touched it again. She laughed and started to bounce up and down on it.

When she looked up, she saw a boy. He was a little older than her, around five or six.

"Hi!" said Tiny.

"Hello," said the boy.

"What are you doing?" asked Tiny.

"I'm looking for something important," said the boy.

"What is it?" asked Tiny.

"It's a special spring," said the boy. "It's magic and it can make wishes come true."

Tiny was excited. "Do you think this is it?" she said, pointing to the big spring.

The boy smiled and nodded. "Yes, I think this is the one. Thank you so much for finding it," he said.

Tiny beamed. She was so happy to have helped the boy find something important. Then, she watched as the boy started to make his wish on the spring. When he was done, the spring glowed and a puff of magic sparkled in the air.

Tiny smiled. She was so glad she had helped the boy find such an important spring.

Sam wanted a haircut. He heard his mom and dad talking about going to a barber. He asked if he could go, too. His mom said yes, and off they went.

At the barber, the barber said that he was available. Sam was excited to get his haircut. The barber put a cape around him and began cutting his hair. It felt funny, but soon it was all finished. 

Sam looked in the mirror and he was so happy. He looked so grown up with his new haircut! His mom and dad said it looked great. 

Sam thanked the barber and he gave him a big smile and a wave goodbye. He couldnâ€™t wait to show all his friends his new look.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who lived in a small village. One day, there was a big earthquake that shook the ground and made everything wobble. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. His dad told him that everything will be okay and that they just need to be careful.

After the earthquake, Timmy saw that his friend Billy's house was destroyed. Billy was crying and sad because he lost all his toys and clothes. Timmy wanted to help his friend, but he didn't know how. He asked his dad what he can do to make Billy feel better.

His dad told him that sometimes, the best thing we can do is just be there for our friends and accept them for who they are. Timmy didn't understand what his dad meant by "accept", but he knew that he wanted to help Billy. So, he went to Billy's house and sat with him. They talked about the earthquake and how scary it was. Timmy made Billy laugh by doing silly faces and making funny noises.

Timmy learned that being there for someone is important and that we should never judge others for their mistakes. His dad told him that it's foolish to think that we are better than others just because we have more things or because we didn't experience the same things they did. Timmy promised himself that he will always be there for his friends and accept them for who they are.

Lily was a little girl who liked to draw and paint. She had a tutor who came to her house every week to teach her new things. The tutor was very nice and patient, and Lily enjoyed learning with her.

One day, Lily wanted to show her tutor her new picture. She had drawn a huge flower with many colors and shapes. She was very proud of it and ran to get it from her room. But when she came back, she saw that her baby brother had found her picture and was tearing it into pieces. Lily was very sad and angry. She shouted at her brother and tried to take her picture back.

"Stop it, Max! That's my picture! You are bad!" Lily cried.

"No, no, no! Mine, mine, mine!" Max said, holding the torn pieces tightly.

The tutor heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily and Max fighting over the picture and tried to calm them down.

"Lily, Max, don't fight. It's not nice to tear other people's things. Max, can you say sorry to Lily? Lily, can you forgive Max? He is still very small and doesn't know better." The tutor said.

Max looked at the tutor and then at Lily. He saw that Lily was crying and felt sorry. He gave her the pieces of the picture and said, "Sorry, Lily. Me no tear."

Lily looked at the pieces of the picture and then at Max. She saw that he was sorry and felt better. She gave him a hug and said, "It's okay, Max. Me forgive."

The tutor smiled and said, "That's very good, Lily and Max. You are both very kind. How about we make a new picture together? I have some paper and crayons. We can draw a huge flower again, or anything you like."

Lily and Max nodded and smiled. They followed the tutor to the table and started to draw. They had fun and learned to share. They forgot about the torn picture and made a new one. They were happy.

Once there was a boy named Joe. He was 3 years old and loved to explore. One day, he saw a watch in his dad's room. He asked his dad if he could pass it. His dad said yes, and handed him the watch.

Joe was very excited to have the watch. He played with it all day long. The watch was very easy to use. He pressed buttons, turned the knobs and saw it light up. He was even able to change the time!

At the end of the day, Joe was very happy with his new watch. He liked it so much that he decided to take it with him everywhere. He passed the watch all around his neighborhood and showed it off to all of his friends. They were very impressed by it!

This was the best day ever for Joe, now he was the proud owner of a colorful watch. Joe happily passed the watch around for everyone to see every single day!

Tim and Anna liked to play with their wagon. They would fill it with toys and pull it around the yard. Sometimes they would take turns riding in it. They were very enthusiastic about their wagon.

One day, they saw a big hill near their house. They thought it would be fun to go down the hill with their wagon. They did not ask their mom or dad if they could go. They just took their wagon and ran to the hill.

They put the wagon at the top of the hill and climbed in. Tim held the handle and Anna held the toys. They were ready to go. They pushed the wagon and it started to roll down the hill. It went faster and faster. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laughed and shouted.

But the hill was too steep and the wagon was too fast. They could not control it. They saw a big rock at the bottom of the hill. They tried to steer away from it, but it was too late. The wagon hit the rock and flipped over. Tim and Anna flew out of the wagon and landed on the grass. The toys scattered everywhere. The wagon was broken.

Tim and Anna were scared and hurt. They cried and called for their mom and dad. Their mom and dad heard them and came running. They saw the wagon and the rock and the toys and the children. They were angry and worried. They picked up Tim and Anna and checked them for injuries. They had some scratches and bruises, but nothing serious. They hugged them and told them they were glad they were okay.

But they also told them they were very naughty. They said they should not have gone to the hill without permission. They said they could have been seriously hurt or lost their wagon. They said they had to punish them for their bad behavior. They took away their wagon and their toys for a week. They said they had to stay in their room and think about what they did.

Tim and Anna were very sorry. They said they were sorry to their mom and dad. They said they were sorry to their wagon and their toys. They said they would never do it again. They went to their room and felt sad. They wished they had listened to their mom and dad. They wished they had been more careful with their wagon. They learned their lesson.

Tim and Sam were two squirrels who liked to play in the park. They had a big tree where they stored their nuts for winter. One day, they decided to organize their nuts by size and color. They made piles of big nuts, small nuts, brown nuts, and green nuts.

"Look, Tim, we have so many nuts!" Sam said. "We are very smart and hard-working."

"Yes, we are, Sam. And we are very lucky, too. No one can take our nuts away from us," Tim said.

But they did not see that a naughty crow was watching them from another tree. The crow was hungry and greedy. He wanted to eat their nuts. He waited until Tim and Sam went to look for more nuts. Then he flew down and started to peck at their piles.

"Yum, yum, these nuts are delicious!" the crow said. "I will eat them all and leave nothing for the squirrels."

But Tim and Sam came back soon. They saw the crow eating their nuts. They were very angry and sad.

"Hey, you, stop that!" Tim shouted. "Those are our nuts! We worked hard to find them and organize them!"

"Too bad, squirrels. I am bigger and stronger than you. I can eat whatever I want," the crow said. He laughed and pecked at another nut.

Tim and Sam did not know what to do. They were too small to fight the crow. They needed help. They looked around and saw their friends, the rabbits, the mice, and the birds. They called them and told them what happened.

"Help us, please! The naughty crow is stealing our nuts!" Tim and Sam said.

Their friends were kind and brave. They came to help them. They made a loud noise and scared the crow away. They helped Tim and Sam pick up their nuts and put them back in their tree.

"Thank you, friends. You are very good and helpful," Tim and Sam said.

"You are welcome, squirrels. We are happy to help you. We are all friends in the park," their friends said.

Tim and Sam learned a lesson. They learned that it is good to organize their nuts, but it is also good to share them with their friends. They learned that being greedy and selfish is naughty and wrong. They learned that being kind and generous is good and right. They learned that friends are more important than nuts.

Once upon a time, there was a strong muscle man. He had muscles so mighty that he could lift anything he wanted! One day, the muscle man was feeling restless. He wanted to let out his power so badly that he started to snap his fingers.

When the muscle man snapped his fingers, a magical thing happened! A fairy appeared, waving her wand and casting a spell. "You have been granted one wish," the fairy said.

The muscle man smiled. "I want to be the strongest man in the land," he said.

The fairy nodded and snapped her wand. Instantly, the muscle man grew bigger and stronger. He laughed and twirled around with joy!

From then on, the muscle man was the strongest man in the land. He could lift anything he wanted and never got tired. He had found the rest he wanted and he was able to use his muscles to help out his fellow villagers. Everyone was happy and lived happily ever after!

Tony was proud every week because he got to see his mom. He loves her so much. His mom visits him every Saturday for a few hours. Tony thinks it's the best day of the week.

His mom is the best! He loves to give her lots of hugs. He loves to play with her. He loves to show her all the new things he learned since the last time she visited. She is always so proud of him.

When it is time for her to go, Tony gives her a big hug. He hopes that she comes back soon. Tony loves his mom so much! She is the best!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a helpful dancer named Lily. She loved to dance and show her friends all her fun moves. Lily was always happy and kind to everyone.

One day, Lily met a new friend named Tim. Tim was shy and didn't know how to dance. He said, "Lily, I want to dance like you, but I don't know how." Lily smiled and replied, "Don't worry, Tim! I will show you how to dance."

Lily and Tim spent the whole day dancing together. Lily showed Tim all her moves, and Tim tried his best to copy them. Soon, Tim was dancing just like Lily. They laughed and had so much fun. From that day on, Lily and Tim became best friends, and they danced together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, Lily's mom gave her a big teddy bear to play with. Lily was so happy and proud of her new toy.

Lily loved to rub the teddy bear's soft fur. It made her feel so cozy and warm. She played with the teddy bear all day long, giving it big hugs and kisses. 

When it was time for bed, Lily held onto her teddy bear tightly. She felt so proud to have such a special toy. As she drifted off to sleep, she dreamed of all the fun adventures she and her teddy bear would have together.

The little girl was proud. She wore a beautiful dress, and wanted to show it off. She went to the park and sat on the grass. 

She smiled as she looked around the park. The trees were green and the flowers were blooming. She could hear the birds singing. The air was fresh and the sun was shining. 

Suddenly, the little girl saw something. It was a beautiful butterfly, sitting in the middle of a bright red flower. It made the little girl very happy. 

Then spring came, and the little girl was so proud. She saw all the new buds on the trees, and heard the chirping of the birds. She felt like she was part of the beautiful scenery. She smiled and sat in the park, watching the world around her in awe.

Once upon a time, there was a player. He was an ordinary player, but he was good at the game. One day, he decided to practice extra hard. He grabbed a stick, and sharpened it. Then he started to practice.

He practiced and practiced until finally, he got very sharp. He hit the ball with the stick, and it flew far and fast!

His friend watched in awe. "That was amazing!" his friend said.

The player smiled. "Thanks," he replied. "But I think I can do even better." 

He stepped back, and started to practice some more. He swung the stick, and again and again, the ball flew even further. He had become really sharp!

His friend was very impressed. "Wow!" his friend said. "Now you're the best player ever!" 

The player smiled, and nodded in agreement. He was the sharpest player in town!

Once upon a time, there were two special friends. One was named Ben and the other was named Bob. Together, they shared lots of wonderful things.

One day, Ben spotted something very incredible outside. "Bob, look! What is that?" asked Ben.

Bob looked outside and smiled. "That's a big, bright rainbow! It's so wondrous," said Bob excitedly.

Ben smiled too. "Let's share this amazing sight with everyone else," he said.

So the two friends brought their friends outside to share the incredible rainbow. Everyone gasped in wonder when they saw it. It was truly amazing.

The friends clapped and cheered. They were so happy to share the incredible wonder of the rainbow.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lucy. She was very excited because it was her birthday. It was a sunny day, so she rushed outside to play in the garden.

In the garden, she saw a word. It was a dry word and it was very charming. She liked the way it looked and wanted to take it home. So Lucy put the word carefully in her pocket and brought it inside.

She decided to use the dry word to make a birthday card for herself. She cut a beautiful shape out of a piece of paper and then glued the word on it. It looked perfect!

She put the card on the kitchen table and waited for her parents to come home so they could see it. When they arrived they were so charmed by her card that they gave her a big hug and told her they were very proud of her.

Lucy hugged her parents back and was so happy to have a beautiful, dry word to make her birthday card.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the snow. They make a snowman and a snow fort. They throw snowballs at each other. They laugh and have fun.

But soon they feel cold and hungry. They want to go inside and have some hot chocolate. They put on their hats and gloves and scarves. They say goodbye to their snowman and their snow fort. They march to the door of their house.

Mama is waiting for them. She has a big smile and a warm hug. She has two cups of hot chocolate on the table. She puts some marshmallows on top. She says, "Here you go, my sweeties. Drink this and you will feel warm and cozy."

Lily and Ben sit down and sip their hot chocolate. They feel the heat in their mouths and their bellies. They say, "Thank you, Mama. This is yummy." They look out the window and see their snowman and their snow fort. They are icy and white. They say, "We will play with you again tomorrow."

Once upon a time, in a wild forest, there was a kind bunny named Bobo. Bobo had many friends in the forest. One day, Bobo found a bottle of lotion. He did not know what it was, but he took it with him.

Soon, Bobo met his friend, Toto the turtle. Toto had dry skin and felt sad. Bobo showed Toto the lotion and said, "Let's try this on your skin!" They put the lotion on Toto's skin, and it felt much better. Toto was very happy and said, "Thank you, Bobo!"

From that day on, Bobo and Toto shared the lotion with all their friends in the wild forest. Everyone felt better and thanked Bobo and Toto for their help. They all played and had fun together, and they lived happily ever after.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play together. One day, they found a big ruler in the garage. It was a measure that could show how long things were. They decided to use it to measure themselves and see who was taller.

"Look, I am taller than you!" Tom said, standing next to the measure. He was very proud of his height.

"No, you are not!" Lily said, standing on her toes. She wanted to be as tall as Tom.

They both tried to stretch themselves as much as they could, but they were still the same height. They got angry and started to push each other.

"Stop it, you two!" Mom said, coming into the garage. She saw them fighting and took the measure away. "This is not a toy, it is a tool. You could hurt yourselves or break something. And it does not matter who is taller, you are both my children and I love you the same."

Tom and Lily felt ashamed of their behavior. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They realized that being friends was more important than being taller. They learned to be happy with who they were and not to compare themselves to others.

Mom smiled and gave them a cookie each. She was glad that they made up. She told them to go and play outside, but to be careful and not to be clumsy. She did not want them to fall or scrape their knees.

Tom and Lily nodded and ran outside. They found a ball and a hoop and had fun playing together. They forgot about the measure and their height. They were happy to have each other as friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved winter. She loved to play in the snow and make snowmen. One day, she was playing outside when she saw her friend Jack.

"Hi Jack!" said Lily.

"Hi Lily!" said Jack. "I don't like winter. It's too cold and the snow is too thick."

Lily felt sad because she wanted Jack to like winter too. "Why don't you try to accept winter, Jack? It can be fun!" she said.

Jack thought about it and decided to give winter another try. He put on his warm coat and went outside to play with Lily. They made a big snowman together and had so much fun. Jack realized that winter wasn't so bad after all.

Once, there was a girl. She had a garage. Inside the garage she kept her toys.

One day, the girl noticed something was wrong with her toys. She went in the garage and saw that they had broken.

She decided she would repair them and make them as good as new. She made sure to wash them all so they were nice and healthy.

Then she took some glue and fixed all the toys until they looked perfect. She was very pleased with her work.

When she was done, the girl could play with her toys again and have lots of fun. She was very happy.

Ben and his dad went to the office. Dad had to work on his computer. Ben wanted to play with dad's toys. Dad had a lot of toys on his desk. He had a car, a plane, a ball and a phone.

"Can I play with your toys, dad?" Ben asked.

"Sure, you can play with some of them. But be careful, okay? Don't break them or lose them," dad said.

Ben picked up the car and made vroom-vroom noises. He drove the car on the desk and on the floor. He had fun with the car. Then he saw the plane. He wanted to fly the plane. He put the car down and grabbed the plane.

He threw the plane in the air and watched it soar. He clapped his hands and laughed. He ran after the plane and caught it. He threw it again and again. He did not see where the plane was going.

The plane flew out of the window and landed on the street. Ben gasped and ran to the window. He saw the plane on the ground. He saw a big truck coming. He saw the truck run over the plane and smash it. He saw the plane break into many parts. He felt sad and scared.

He started to cry. He ran to dad and hugged him. He told him what happened.

"I'm sorry, dad. I broke your plane. It flew out of the window and the truck smashed it. It has many parts now. I'm sorry, I'm sorry," Ben sobbed.

Dad looked at the window and saw the broken plane. He felt angry and sad. He loved his plane. It was a gift from his friend. He wanted to yell at Ben. But he saw Ben's tears and heard his sorry. He felt sorry for Ben too.

He hugged Ben and stroked his hair. He said, "It's okay, Ben. I know you didn't mean to break it. It was an accident. Accidents happen sometimes. I'm not mad at you. I still love you. But you have to be more careful next time, okay? You have to watch where you throw things. You have to respect other people's things. Do you understand?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, dad. I understand. I'm sorry. I love you too."

Dad smiled and kissed Ben's cheek. He said, "Let's go home and have some ice cream. How does that sound?"

Ben smiled and said, "That sounds good, dad. Can we get chocolate?"

"Sure, we can get chocolate. Come on, let's go," dad said.

He picked up Ben and his bag. He said goodbye to his bald boss, who was watching them from his office. He said, "Sorry, boss. I have to go. My son had a little trouble with my plane."

His boss nodded and said, "No problem, dad. I understand. Kids will be kids. Have a good day."

Dad and Ben left the office and went to the car. They drove to the ice cream shop and got chocolate ice cream. They ate their ice cream and talked about their day. They forgot about the broken plane and the parts. They were happy.

Ben was restless. He did not want to nap. He wanted to play with his cars and trucks. But Mom said he had to nap. She put him in his bed and gave him a kiss. She said she would make tuna for lunch. Ben liked tuna.

But Ben did not sleep. He tossed and turned. He kicked his blanket. He looked at his cars and trucks on the shelf. He wanted them. He got out of his bed and tiptoed to the shelf. He reached for his red truck. But it was too high. He stretched and stretched. He lost his balance and fell.

He hit his head on the floor. It hurt. He screamed. He screamed loud. Mom heard him. She ran to his room. She saw him on the floor. She saw the blood on his head. She was scared. She picked him up and hugged him. She said it was okay. She said she would take him to the doctor.

Ben cried. He did not want to go to the doctor. He wanted his red truck. He wanted his tuna. He wanted his mom. He was restless. He screamed.

Mum and dad took Sally to the market. They wanted to buy some food. As they were walking around, Sally saw something she wanted. It was a bright, red lip! She begged mum and dad to buy it for her. Eventually they agreed and Sally was so happy. 

The lip was really big so Sally had to carry it around the market. Everyone could see it, and as she walked around, some of the other children asked if they could have a turn playing with it. Sally was so proud to have it, she didnâ€™t want to share it! 

Soon the children started getting competitive. They all wanted to buy their own lips, so they could show them off. Some of the parents were forced to buy their children lips, just to keep them happy. 

Sally hugged her lip tightly and hugged her parents. She was so glad she had been the first one to buy a lip!

Once upon a time, there were two friends called David and Emily. They lived near a big park and love to play there.

One day, Emily said to David: "Let's go to the park! It is so fair there."
David said: "Yes, let's go!"

When they arrived, they saw that some animals were in the park. Emily said: "Let's feed the animals!" 
David agreed and they found some food in their bag.

They fed the animals. Then David said: "Look, the birds are so happy now!"
Emily smiled and said: "Yes, we made them very happy."

They hugged each other and went home feeling very fair.

Lily liked to play in the pond. She saw many fish, bugs and frogs. She liked frogs the most. They were green and wet and made funny sounds. She wanted to catch one and make it her friend.

One day, she saw a big frog sitting on a rock. She ran to it and said, "Hello, frog. Do you want to play with me?" The frog looked at her and said, "Ribbit, ribbit. I am not a frog. I am a prince. A witch turned me into a frog. If you kiss me, I will turn back into a prince."

Lily was surprised. She had heard stories about princes and princesses, but she had never seen one. She wondered what a prince looked like. She thought he might be handsome and kind and have a crown. She wanted to see him. She said, "OK, I will kiss you. But you have to be nice to me and play with me."

She leaned over and kissed the frog on his nose. There was a flash of light and a puff of smoke. The frog turned into a boy. He had brown hair and blue eyes and wore a shirt and pants. He did not have a crown. He smiled at Lily and said, "Thank you, thank you. You broke the spell. You are very brave and sweet. I am a prince, but I don't have a kingdom. I ran away from home because I did not like the rules. Can I stay with you and be your friend?"

Lily looked at him and thought he was not very funny. He was not a frog anymore. She liked frogs better. She said, "No, thank you. You are not a frog. You are a boy. I don't want to play with you. I want to play with frogs. Goodbye, prince." She ran away and looked for another frog to catch. She hoped it would not turn into a boy. She liked frogs the way they were.

Ben and Lily went to the park with Mom. They saw a huge pond with many ducks. Ben and Lily liked ducks. They wanted to feed them.

"Mom, can we give them some bread?" Lily asked.

"Sorry, sweetie, we don't have any bread. But we have some olives. Do you think they will like olives?" Mom said.

"Let's try!" Ben said. He took an olive from Mom's bag and threw it into the pond. A duck saw the olive and swam to get it. It picked up the olive with its beak and ate it.

"Yay! The duck likes olives!" Ben cheered.

"Me too! Me too!" Lily said. She took another olive and threw it into the pond. Another duck swam to get it. It also ate the olive.

"Wow! The ducks love olives!" Lily said.

"Can we swim with the ducks, Mom?" Ben asked.

"No, honey, the pond is too deep and cold for you. And the ducks might not like it. They need their space. But you can watch them swim and quack. They are very happy." Mom said.

"Okay, Mom. We will watch them. They are very cute." Ben said.

"Yes, they are. And you are very kind to share your olives with them." Mom said.

Ben and Lily smiled. They sat on the grass and watched the ducks swim and eat olives. They had a lot of fun at the park.

Once there was a tall boy. He was trying to decide what he should do. He thought and thought but he just couldn't make up his mind.

Suddenly he had an idea. He decided to get his knife. With the knife he knew he could do many things. He figured solving his problem would be easy.

So he took the knife and went outside. He started cutting a tree with it. After a little bit, he had enough wood to build something. He made a tall house on the ground.

He was very pleased with his work. He had decided what he wanted to do and he had made it happen. It was his special tall house and he was proud.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was playing in her garden and found something very special, a pin! It was a beautiful pin with lots of sparkly colours. She was so excited and wanted to keep it forever, so she put it in her pocket.

Later that day, the little girl wanted to show her pin to her friends, but when she looked inside her pocket, it was gone! She was very sad, so she search everywhere but still could not find it.

The next morning she awoke and went back outside to look for the pin again. As she was searching, she heard a gentle voice. The voice said, "Stay here and you will find it." The little girl stayed and sure enough, there it was, her beautiful pin! She was so happy and knew that the voice was right. 

From then on, she would always listen to the voice when she was looking for something special.

Once upon a time, in a distant land, there was a big hedge. A little boy named Tim wanted to see what was on the other side of the hedge. He thought it must be something very fun and exciting. So, Tim decided to try to climb over the hedge.

Tim tried and tried, but he could not reach the top of the hedge. A friendly bird saw Tim and said, "Hi, Tim! What are you doing?" Tim replied, "I want to see what's on the other side of the hedge. Can you help me?" The bird agreed to help Tim and carried him up and over the hedge.

When they got to the other side, Tim saw that it was just a big field with nothing fun or exciting. Tim was very sad and started to cry. The bird tried to cheer him up, but Tim was too sad to smile. In the end, Tim learned that sometimes, what we think is exciting is not always as fun as we imagine.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and swing. They saw a stream with water that sparkled in the sun. They wanted to go near it and splash.

"Look, Lily, a stream!" Ben said. "Can we go there?"

"Yes, let's go!" Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Mommy said not to go too close to the water."

They ran to the stream and saw some white stones and some fish. They picked up some stones and threw them in the water. They made a big splash and laughed.

"Look, Ben, a white fish!" Lily said. "It is so pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Ben said. "It reminds me of the white cat we saw at the pet shop. Do you remember?"

"Yes, I do!" Lily said. "It was so soft and fluffy. I wanted to pet it, but Daddy said no."

They watched the white fish swim away. They heard Mommy calling them.

"Lily, Ben, it's time to go home!" Mommy said. "Come on, let's go!"

"OK, Mommy!" Lily and Ben said. They ran to Mommy and gave her a hug. They told her about the stream and the white fish.

"That sounds like fun!" Mommy said. "But you have to be careful around water, OK?"

"OK, Mommy!" Lily and Ben said. They got in the car and went home. They were happy and tired. They dreamed of the stream and the white fish.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jack. Jack was three years old and he loved to make new friends.

On this particular day, Jack wanted to introduce himself to his new neighbor. He was very excited so he grabbed a yummy candle and knocked on the neighbor's door.

A lady called Mrs. Smith opened the door. Jack smiled and said, â€œHello. I'm Jack. Would you like to be my friend?â€

Mrs. Smith smiled and said: â€œYes, I'd love to! Here, why don't we light this yummy candle together and make a wish for our new friendship?â€ 

Jack and Mrs. Smith lit the candle, made a wish and enjoyed the yummy smell of the candle. From that day on, Jack and Mrs. Smith were the best of friends!

Once upon a time, there was a man who wanted to build something. He worked hard every day until he made something special. It was an expensive machine that he could speak into. He tested it and the machine made a voice that sounded like a real person. He was so happy, he wanted everyone to hear. So he showed it to all his friends. They were amazed! It was one of the most expensive machines they had ever seen. Everyone loved it and wanted one of their own. The man was so proud of what he built. He knew that his hard work and creativity had paid off.

Once upon a time, there was a snowman. He had eyes made of coal and a hat upon his head. One day, the snowman wanted to look his best for the winter festivities. So he went in search of a razor.

The snowman trudged through the icy snow until he found a furry creature. 'Do you have a razor?' the snowman asked. The furry creature nodded and quickly gave the snowman a shiny razor.

The snowman was so happy! He thanked the furry creature and began to carefully shave the snow around his face. The snowman looked so handsome!

But then he heard a voice. 'What do you think you're doing? That's my razor!' said a voice. An icy wind blew, and the snowman saw a large polar bear.

The snowman quickly answered, 'I'm sorry, I just wanted to look nice for the party!' The polar bear looked him over and saw how handsome he looked. The polar bear smiled and told the snowman he could keep the razor. 

The snowman was so happy! He thanked the polar bear and danced all the way to the winter party. He arrived looking his best and everyone at the party was so impressed!

The snowman lived happily ever after, with his icy razor.

"Look, mommy!" said Jerry as he gazed at the muffin in the bakery window. The muffin was a work of art - it was a swirl of different colors, and had a chocolate chip to top it off. Jerry was in awe.

"It's beautiful, isn't it?" said Mom. "Would you like to have one?"

Jerry nodded eagerly, and Mom bought him the muffin.

As he took his first bite, Jerry savored the sweet taste of the muffin. As he continued to gaze at it, he had an idea.

"Mommy," he said excitedly, "can we make creative muffins like this one at home?"

Mom smiled. "Yes, of course we can," she said. "We can make any kind of muffins you want!"

Jerry grinned, pleased that Mom was just as excited about making muffins as he was. He couldn't wait to get home and start making his imaginative creations.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat blueberries. One day, she went for a walk in the forest and found an ancient tree. The tree was very big and had lots of branches. Lily climbed up the tree and found lots of blueberries. She picked them all and put them in her basket. 

Suddenly, it started to rain. Lily was getting wet, so she used her basket to cover her head. She climbed down the tree and ran home. When she got home, she made a blueberry pie with all the blueberries she had picked. It was delicious! From that day on, Lily went back to the ancient tree every week to pick more blueberries and make more pies.

Once upon a time, there was a clay figure who lived all by itself. It had a long body and little arms, but no eyes, nose, or mouth. Each day the clay figure stood in the same spot, lonely and alone. 

One day, a little girl noticed the lonely clay figure. She smiled and said, "Hello!" The figure just stood there. 

The girl asked, "Can you show me something cool?" To her surprise, the figure started dancing around! She clapped and cheered, amazed by the display. 

The girl asked the clay figure to dance for her every day. Soon, the figure was no longer lonely. Every day, the little girl and the clay figure would display something special for each other. Together, they were the best of friends. 

The end.

Once there was a kitten named Tom. Tom loved to go on adventures. Today, he wanted to visit the forest. So, he went!

When Tom arrived in the forest, he met an old lion. The lion had big eyes. He was very bossy. 

Tom was scared. He didn't know what to do. 

The lion said, "What are you doing here?"

Tom said, "I wanted to explore the forest."

The lion replied, "You need oil for your journey." 

At first, Tom didn't know what the lion meant. But then the lion gave him a bottle of oil. 

Tom said, "Thank you very much!" He filled his pockets with the oil and went off to continue his adventure. 

Tom had a lot of fun exploring the forest with his oil. And he never forgot how kind the old lion was.

Once upon a time, there was a quick little girl who loved to dance. Every day, she would hurry off to her dance class with her organized group of friends. She would practice her moves, twirling and leaping around the room with her friends.

It was so much fun to practice dancing, and the little girl grew better and better. Soon, she was able to do more complicated moves. The teachers were very pleased with her progress.

Finally, it was time for the big dance recital. All the students danced their best, especially the little girl who was quick and organized. Everyone clapped as she finished her dance. She felt so happy and proud of herself.

The little girl's parents watched with love in their eyes. It was such a special moment. It felt so good to be able to dance and show off her hard work. From then on, the little girl kept dancing, and she continued to get better and better.

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to visit their grandpa. He is a great man. He has a big house with a garden. He tells them stories and plays with them.

One day, they go to visit grandpa with their mom. They knock on the door. Grandpa opens it and smiles. He hugs them and says, "Hello, my little ones. I'm so happy to see you. Come in, come in."

They go inside and see a big cake on the table. It has candles and frosting. Grandpa says, "It's my birthday today. I made a cake for us. Do you want some?"

Sara and Tom clap their hands and say, "Yes, please. Happy birthday, grandpa. We love you."

They sit down and eat the cake. It is yummy. They sing a song for grandpa. He blows out the candles and makes a wish. He says, "My wish is to have more days like this. You are the best gift I ever had."

Sara and Tom hug him and say, "You are the best grandpa ever. We are glad you are our grandpa."

They spend the afternoon playing and talking. They have a lot of fun. They are happy to visit their grandpa. He is a great man.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, Timmy went on an adventure to find his missing pants. He looked high and low, but he couldn't find them anywhere.

As he continued his search, he saw a dangerous snake slithering towards him. Timmy was scared, but he remembered that his mom had taught him how to record animals with his phone. He quickly took out his phone and recorded the snake. 

Feeling proud of himself, Timmy continued his search for his pants. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise and saw a big truck coming towards him. He tried to run, but he tripped and fell. The truck hit him and he was hurt badly. 

Timmy's mom found him lying on the ground and rushed him to the hospital. Sadly, Timmy didn't make it. His mom was heartbroken and wished she had never let him go on that dangerous adventure. She watched the video of the snake that Timmy had recorded and cried, knowing that it was the last thing he ever did.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a big house with lots of furniture. He had a modest bed, a small table, and a big chair. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but one day he had to hurry and clean up his room before his mom came in.

Timmy picked up all his toys and put them away in their proper place. He dusted off his modest bed and fluffed up his pillow. He even straightened out the furniture in his room. Timmy was so proud of himself for hurrying and cleaning up his room all by himself.

When Timmy's mom came in, she was so happy to see how clean and tidy his room was. She gave him a big hug and told him how proud she was of him. Timmy felt so happy and proud of himself too. From that day on, Timmy learned that it's important to hurry and clean up his room so he can make his mom happy.

Once, there was a man who loved to bring things home. One day he had brought home some ink.

"What have you brought home?" asked the little three year old girl.

"I brought some ink, it'll be fun to draw with," the man said. 

The little girl was excited and ran to get her pencils and paper. But when she opened the jar of ink, she was surprised. It was a bad colour!

"This ink is bad!" said the little girl sadly.

The man was sorry to learn that the ink was bad and decided he would go back out and find some more ink in a better colour.

"I'll bring back some better ink so you can draw with it and have fun," he said. 

The little girl smiled and waited for the man to come back. He eventually returned with some ink in a great colour, and the little girl was so happy! She made the most beautiful pictures with the new ink. And that's how the bad ink was brought home and changed for the better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in nature. One day, she saw a beautiful red flower. She picked it and showed it to her mom.

"Lily, that's a pretty flower," her mom said. "Let's sort it with the other flowers."

Lily and her mom sorted the flowers by color. They put the red flower with the other red flowers. Lily was happy to see all the pretty colors. She said, "Nature is so pretty!" 

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, it is."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the big green grassy field near her house. One day, she saw a red ball bouncing towards her. She caught the ball and started to play with it. She kicked the ball, then she threw it, and then she rolled it. But suddenly, she needed to take a step back and pause. She saw a little bird with a broken wing on the ground. She gently picked up the bird and took it to her mommy. Her mommy helped the bird and soon it was able to fly again. Lily was very happy that she helped the little bird.

Once upon a time there was a nosy staff member. He worked in a store and asked a lot of questions. He was always asking people if they needed help and what they were looking for.

One day, a customer wanted to buy something and the nosy staff member asked lots of questions. The customer was getting frustrated. She wanted to be left alone.

The customer asked the nosy staff member to close the store, so she could buy something in peace. But the nosy staff member refused. He said it was against the store rules.

The customer was annoyed, so she walked away. But the nosy staff member followed her and kept asking her questions. In the end, the customer was so mad that she had to close the store herself! She was very happy when the store was finally closed and she could buy what she needed in peace.

Once there was a bad monster that liked to scatter things. One day it scattered all the toys in the house. The toys were all over the place. Great mess!

But then, the monster noticed something under the couch. It was a little toy car. The monster wanted to take the car, but it was under the couch. He tried to reach it, but couldn't.

The monster decided he had to scatter the couch. He pushed and pushed and finally, the couch was scattered all over the room. He reached under the couch and grabbed the toy car.

But, what he didn't know was that an even bigger monster was watching him. The bigger monster was very angry. He roared and roared and the bad monster ran away, scared.

The bigger monster gathered all the scattered things and put them back in the house. He saved the day!

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was very hungry. She wanted to eat something. The girl saw a box of cereal on the kitchen table. It looked yummy, and it smelled spicy.

The girl opened the box, and she tried some of the cereal. It was delicious! She ate a big bowl.

When she was done, the girl wanted more, but the box was empty. She sighed, wished she had more cereal, and went to do something else.

Later that day, the girl went back to the kitchen. To her surprise, the cereal box was full again! She took a bowl and tried some of the cereal. It was even better than before! It tasted so spicy!

The girl thanked her mom and dad for leaving more cereal. She was so happy to have a full bowl to enjoy. The girl smiled, ate the cereal, and went happily on her way.

Once upon a time, there was a compassionate dog named Buddy. Buddy liked to help his friends. One day, Buddy and his friend, a little bird named Tweet, went on an adventure to find a treasure.

They walked and walked until they found a big tree. Buddy and Tweet looked up and saw the treasure box in the tree. Buddy climbed the tree and got the treasure box. They were so excited!

It was getting late, so Buddy and Tweet decided to sleep under the tree. They were tired from their big adventure. As they slept, they dreamed about the fun they had finding the treasure. And they knew they would always remember this special day.

Once upon a time, there was a bear who was very jolly. He loved to run and play in the forest. One day, he was running and teasing when he came across an animal he had never seen before. It was a funny little creature. The bear thought it was so funny that he laughed and laughed. The funny creature laughed too. They both had so much fun they decided to be friends. From that day onwards they were the best of friends. They would play and tease each other every day and the bear always felt so jolly.

Once upon a time there lived a small boy. His name was James. He was very ordinary.

One day, James found a puzzle. It was beautiful and it had many pieces. James was curious and wanted to put it together.

He worked very hard and very carefully. He tried to balance all the pieces. He knew it was important to balance them carefully in the right shape and spot. 

After a few hours of hard work, James finally finished the puzzle. He was so proud and excited! 

He showed it to his mum and dad. They were so happy and proud of him. James smiled and was happy too. 

The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. They saw a lizard on a rock. It was green and brown and had a long tail.

"Wow, look at the lizard!" Lily said. "It is so cool. Can we touch it?"

Ben was scared of the lizard. He thought it might bite or scratch them. He shook his head.

"No, Lily, we can't touch it. It is not a toy. It is a wild animal. It might run away or hurt us."

But Lily did not listen to Ben. She wanted to see the lizard up close. She had an urge to touch it. She moved slowly towards the rock.

"Come on, Ben, don't be a baby. It is just a lizard. It is not a lion or a snake. It is cute and small. I want to pet it."

Ben tried to stop Lily. He grabbed her arm.

"Lily, stop! You are being silly. The lizard does not want to be petted. It wants to be left alone. You are scaring it. Come back here!"

But Lily pulled her arm away from Ben. She reached out her hand to the lizard. The lizard did not like Lily's hand. It felt threatened. It opened its mouth and showed its teeth. It hissed and jumped at Lily.

"Aaaah!" Lily screamed. She was surprised and scared. She fell back and dropped her hand. The lizard ran away and hid under a bush.

Ben ran to Lily. He hugged her and checked her hand. She had a small scratch on her finger. It was bleeding a little bit.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked. "Did the lizard hurt you?"

Lily nodded. She was crying. She felt sorry and stupid.

"Yes, Ben, I am okay. But the lizard hurt me. It was angry at me. I should have listened to you. You were right. I was wrong. I was silly. I am sorry, Ben."

Ben smiled and kissed her cheek. He took her hand and wrapped it with a leaf.

"It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. You are not silly. You are curious. But you have to be careful. Some animals don't like to be touched. They need their space. Next time, we can look at the lizard from far away. Okay?"

Lily smiled and nodded. She hugged Ben and said thank you.

"Okay, Ben. Thank you for being my friend. You are very smart and brave. And tall. I like you."

They walked back to the house. They saw their mom and dad. They told them what happened. Their mom and dad were glad they were okay. They gave them a hug and a cookie. They said they were proud of them for being honest and kind. They said they loved them very much.

Once upon a time there was a very clean little machine. It was a very special machine that only one person could manage.

One day, a young girl named Sally saw the machine. She was very curious and asked her dad, "What is it?"

Her dad smiled and said, "It's a very important machine. Someday when you're bigger, you'll be able to manage it."

Sally was very excited. She asked, "Can I manage it now?"

Her dad laughed and said, "Not yet, but soon."

From then on, Sally kept looking at the machine, wondering when she'd be big enough to manage it. 

Finally, when Sally was old enough, she was allowed to manage the machine. She was so proud of herself! She worked hard and was very successful.

Sally had managed the machine and it was now very clean! She was so happy that the hardwork had paid off.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous cactus. Its spikes were as sharp as thorns, and it's green body reached far into the sky.

One day, a three year old came across the cactus. She was walking in the desert and noticed how big it was. She got close to the enormous cactus and called out to her mom, asking to pick it.

Her mom quickly told her to keep away. She said, "No no. You can't miss that cactus." 

But the three year old was very stubborn and she ignored her mom and reached out for the cactus. As soon as she touched it, she was hurt by the sharp spikes.

She began to cry loudly and felt a lot of pain. Her mom quickly came to help her. The three year old felt very sad and she had to go to the doctor.

Sadly, the three year old had to miss playing outdoors and visit the doctor often, because of the enormous cactus.

Lily and Ben like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They like to match their cars with the same color or the same size. They say, "This car is red, and this car is red. They match!" or "This car is big, and this car is big. They match!"

One day, they find a box of powder in the kitchen. They do not know what it is, but it looks like snow. They think it is fun to play with. They take some powder and sprinkle it on their cars. They say, "This car is white, and this car is white. They match!"

But then, their mom comes and sees the mess. She is not happy. She says, "What are you doing? This is not snow, this is flour. You made a big mess in the kitchen. You have to clean it up!" She is bossy and angry.

Lily and Ben are sorry. They do not like to make mom angry. They say, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know it was flour. We just wanted to play and match our cars." They help mom to clean up the flour. They use a broom and a dustpan. They say, "This broom is yellow, and this dustpan is yellow. They match!"

Mom sees that they are sorry and that they are trying to help. She is not angry anymore. She says, "Thank you, Lily and Ben. You are good helpers. Next time, ask me before you play with something you do not know. And remember, flour is for baking, not for playing." She gives them a hug and a kiss. She is not bossy, she is nice.

Once upon a time, there was a fireman who was so nice and clean. He always wanted to help people. One day, he saw something glow in the night sky. He knew he had to help, so he grabbed his fire gear and ran. When he arrived, he saw the fire and it was big and orange. He began to work quickly and bravely. He put out the fire and sprinked the ground with water to make sure it was clean. The fireman smiled with happiness, for he had saved the town from the fire. He knew he was helping and it made him feel good.

Once upon a time, there was a big green forest. In the forest, there lived a little bunny who loved to eat dessert. One day, the bunny was hopping around when he saw a big tree with lots of green leaves. He thought it would be a good place to find some dessert.

As he got closer, he saw something appear on the tree. It was a big, juicy apple! The bunny was so happy and started to nibble on it. But then, he heard a noise and turned around to see a big bear coming towards him.

The bunny was scared and ran away as fast as he could. He didn't want to share his dessert with the bear! From that day on, the bunny was more careful when looking for dessert and always kept an eye out for any animals that might appear.

Once upon a time there was an ugly rod. It was old and rusty. Every day it stood by itself at the bottom of a ditch. One day, a little 3 year old girl called Sarah walked by. She saw the rod and was interested in it. She bent down and picked it up. It felt funny and cold, like it had been in the ditch for a long time. 

Sarah was excited and wanted to take the ugly rod home with her. She thought it would be fun to draw and colour on it. Sarah stood back up and put the rod over her shoulder. She ran all the way home, passing through fields and over bridges, with the rod very securely held in her hands. 

Back at home, Sarah put the rod in her bedroom. Every time she saw it she felt so happy and excited because she knew she was the only person who had it. She was amazed at how ugly and yet special it was all at the same time. She could not believe she had found this amazing rod. 

The rod lay in Sarahâ€™s bedroom for a long time and she still stands by it every day. She knows that the ugly rod is part of her and she will never forget it.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They loved nature and all the animals and plants they could see. Sometimes they would make up games and challenges for each other. They would dare each other to do things that were fun or scary.

One day, they saw a big tree with a hole in it. They wondered what was inside. Lily dared Ben to put his hand in the hole and see what he could feel. Ben was not afraid. He said he would do it if Lily did it too. They agreed and walked towards the tree.

But they did not know that someone else was living in the hole. It was a grumpy old owl who did not like visitors. He was sleeping when he heard the twins coming. He opened his eyes and saw two small hands reaching into his home. He was very angry and decided to teach them a lesson.

He waited until Ben's hand was close enough and then he bit it hard. Ben screamed and pulled his hand out. He saw blood and a big mark on his finger. He cried and ran to his sister. Lily was shocked and scared. She hugged Ben and said she was sorry. She did not dare to put her hand in the hole.

The owl watched them from the hole. He was satisfied and went back to sleep. He hoped they would never come back. He liked his peace and quiet. He did not like nature's games.

Once upon a time, there was a green structure. It was tall and had many levels, and it looked shiny in the sunlight.

One day, a group of friends appeared at the green structure. They were excited to explore and waved hello as they started to explore.

The first level was a room full of games and puzzles. They played together for a long time.

Next, they went up to the second level of the green structure. It had a beautiful garden and a place for them to have a picnic.

At the top of the green structure, a surprise appeared. It was an ice cream shop! The friends ate sundaes and laughed together.

They had a lot of fun and all agreed the green structure was the best place to play!

Once upon a time, there was a little fairy. She was eager to restore her magical powers. One day, she asked a 3 year old child for help. 

"Please help me restore my magic," she said.

The child was eager to help. "I'll look for the magical items," he said. 

The child and the fairy began their search for magical items. Soon, they found a special bracelet, a sparkling wand and a shiny crown. With these items, the fairy's magic was fully restored! 

The fairy was so happy. "Thank you for your help," she said as she hugged the child. 

The child was so excited. He had helped restore a real fairy's magical powers and that made him happy!
