Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very restless and couldn't stay in one place for too long.

One day, when she was walking along, she stopped to stare at a strange object on the ground. It was a big, round rock. She tilted her head and opened her mouth, not knowing what to say.

Just then, her big sister appeared. She bent down, placed her hand on the little girl's back, and said to her, "Remember, you must be careful when walking!"

The little girl nodded and smiled. She looked up into her big sister's eyes, and said, "I remember!"

The big sister smiled back. "That's my brave girl," she said.

The little girl beamed with pride. She was so happy to have her big sister to remind her to be careful. She knew she could always trust her big sister to keep her safe.

Once upon a time, there was a big orange cat named Kitty. Kitty lived in a small house with a nice family. Kitty loved to play with her toys and her family.

One day, Kitty's favorite toy went missing. She looked all around the house, but she could not find it. Kitty's family saw her looking for her toy and they wanted to help. So, they all decided to join in the search for Kitty's toy.

They looked under the beds, behind the couch, and even in the kitchen. After a long time of searching, Kitty's little brother found the toy under a chair. Kitty was so happy to have her toy back, and she was even happier that her family joined her in the search. They all played together with the toy and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was very organized and loved to keep things neat. One day, she was playing with her toys, when something strange happened. She felt a pinch on her shoulder. She looked around and saw a bug! She quickly snatched it up with her hands and released it outside. She was so happy that she hadn't been pinched again! She went back to her toys and started to organize them in her special way. The girl smiled, feeling proud that all of her toys were very organized.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Lily and Max. They were playing in the garden outside of Lily's house. Lily's garden was so rich and colorful, with big green trees and red, yellow, and orange flowers.

Max looked around and noticed something. He asked Lily, "Do you recognize that thing in the garden?" Lily wasn't sure what he was talking about. Max pointed to a spot in the garden and said, "That big yellow thing is special."

Lily walked closer and then she recognized it! It was a huge yellow butterfly! She said, "Wow! It looks so pretty." The butterfly flew over to a nearby flower and started to drink the nectar.

Max and Lily watched the butterfly for a long time. Eventually, the butterfly flew away but Max and Lily never forgot about it. They will always remember their special moment in the rich garden.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big cage in the park. They go to look at the cage.

Inside the cage, there is a lion. The lion is very big and has a lot of hair. The lion looks sad. Tom and Lily feel sorry for the lion.

"Hello, lion," Tom says. "Why are you in the cage?"

The lion does not answer. He just lies on the ground and sighs.

"Maybe he is hungry," Lily says. "Let's give him some food."

Tom and Lily find some bread and apples. They throw them into the cage. The lion does not eat them. He just looks at them and sighs.

"Maybe he is lonely," Tom says. "Let's be his friends."

Tom and Lily go closer to the cage. They smile and wave at the lion. The lion does not smile or wave back. He just looks at them and sighs.

"Maybe he is bored," Lily says. "Let's do something fun."

Tom and Lily think of something fun. They decide to do a show for the lion. They sing and dance and tell jokes. They hope the lion will like their show.

The lion watches their show. He does not laugh or clap. He just looks at them and sighs.

Tom and Lily are sad. They do not know how to make the lion happy.

"Maybe he does not like us," Tom says.

"Maybe he does not like the cage," Lily says.

They look at the cage. The cage is very small and has no toys or plants. The cage is not a good home for the lion.

"Maybe he wants to go home," Tom says.

"Where is his home?" Lily asks.

The lion hears their question. He lifts his head and roars. He points his paw at the sky. He shows them a picture in his mind. The picture is of a big land with many trees and animals. The land is his home.

Tom and Lily understand. The lion misses his home. He does not belong in the cage. He belongs in the land.

"We are sorry, lion," Tom says. "We wish you could go home."

"We are sorry, too," Lily says. "We hope you will be happy someday."

Tom and Lily bow to the lion. They say goodbye and leave the cage. They hope someone will help the lion go home. They hope the lion will find his happiness.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sally. Sally liked to laugh, but had a hard time understanding the language of the people around her. One day, Sally was walking around her neighborhood when she saw a great big tree. She ran up to the tree and started to jump around it, laughing.

Suddenly, a little bird flew down from the tree and landed on a nearby branch. The bird looked at Sally and spoke in a strange language that Sally didn't understand. Sally was very surprised and just stared at the bird. 

The bird noticed Sally's confusion, so he started speaking in a different language. He said, "Why do you look so sad? Let's have a laugh!"

Sally was excited and she clapped her hands in joy. She looked at the bird and began to laugh. The bird laughed too. It was a bitter laugh, but Sally thought the bird was funny and kept laughing. 

After a while, Sally was able to understand some of the little bird's language. They became best friends and chatted all the time, laughing together. From that day on, they were the happiest friends in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a hunter who lived in a big forest. Every day, he went looking for animals to hunt and he always ended up finding something. One day, he was feeling extra lucky and decided to take a walk further into the forest.

As he ventured into the woods, he heard a funny noise coming from high up in a tree. When he looked up, he saw a crazy monkey who was eating bananas and laughing. The hunter thought the monkey was so funny that he decided to marry it.

He bought the monkey sweets and they shared them while they talked. The hunter asked the monkey if it would like to marry him and it agreed!

The two were so happy together and moved into a new tree near the hunter's house. From then on, they were the happiest and craziest married couple living in the forest.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the beach with her family. They brought a cooler filled with yummy snacks like apples and crackers. Lily loved the beach because she could build sandcastles and play in the water.

One day, Lily saw a crab walking towards her cooler. She didn't want the crab to eat her snacks, so she yelled, "Stop!" The crab didn't listen and kept walking towards the cooler. Lily's dad saw what was happening and gently picked up the crab and moved it away. He told Lily that the crab was harmless and just wanted to explore.

Lily was happy that her snacks were safe and she could continue playing at the beach. She even saw some dolphins jumping in the water and it made her smile. She had a great day at the beach with her family. The end.

One day, Sam and Susie were playing near a beach. They saw the tide washing in and out. Suddenly, Sam had an idea. He said, "Let's build a sandcastle!" Susie thought it sounded like fun.

They started digging and using sticks to make a castle. But the tide kept coming in and washing away the sand castle. Sam was getting frustrated. Then, he had a new idea. He said, "Susie, I have a request. Can you help me find something foolish that will help us keep the tide away?"

Susie thought was a great idea! She searched around and soon she found a big rock. It was perfect! She brought it over and helped Sam put it in front of the sandcastle. The rock kept the tide away and their castle was not washed away! Sam and Susie were very happy and clapped their hands.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and run around in the park. One day, she went to the park and saw a boy crying. 

"What's wrong?" asked Lily. 

"I lost my way home," replied the boy. 

Lily felt sad for the boy and wanted to help him. "Don't be ashamed to cry," said Lily. "Let's find your way home together." 

The boy smiled and together they walked around the park until they found his house. The boy was happy and thanked Lily for helping him. Lily felt proud of herself for being a good friend. From that day on, Lily and the boy became good friends and played together in the park every day.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went on a walk with his dog. They followed a creek that had lots of water in it. Timmy liked to throw rocks in the water and watch the splashes. But then, he started to feel uncomfortable. His feet were wet and his socks were squishy. 

Suddenly, Timmy's dog ran away. Timmy called for him, but the dog didn't come back. Timmy was sad and scared. He didn't know what to do. He decided to follow the creek to try and find his dog. 

As he walked, the creek got bigger and bigger. The water was moving fast and it was hard to walk. Timmy slipped and fell in the water. He tried to stand up, but the water was too strong. Timmy was swept away by the creek and he never found his dog. The end.

Once upon a time there was a naughty cowboy called Jake. Jake lived on a ranch and he loved to ride his two horses, Buzz and Fire.

Every morning, Jake would get up early, have breakfast, and then bathe the horses. He would fill a big bucket with water and give each horse a big bath. They both loved it!

One morning, as Jake was bathing Fire, the horse said, "Mmmm, this feels so nice! You are the best cowboy! Can I have my breakfast now?"

Jake laughed and said, "Yes, of course you can. You deserve it after all that bathing!" 

The naughty cowboy and the two happy horses lived happily ever after on their ranch. The End.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved nature. She was always so excited to discover new sights and sounds of nature. One day, she went on a special adventure with her mom to a nearby forest. 

The little girl was so excited to explore the forest for the first time. She and her mom wandered through the tall trees and splashed in the babbling brook. While climbing a hill, the little girl noticed a smelly smell - it was coming from a nearby cave!

The little girl asked her mom, â€œWhatâ€™s smelly?â€ Her mom replied with a smile, â€œThat is the smell of a skunk!â€ The little girl was curious and wanted to explore further, but her mom said it was best to stay away. â€œWe canâ€™t get too close - skunks can be dangerous!â€ 

The little girl waved as the skunk scurried away and vowed to remember the smelly smell of the skunk. She and her mom continued to explore the beautiful nature of the forest and the little girl thought to herself, â€œI canâ€™t wait to come back here soon and explore some more!â€

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the store with her mom. They needed to buy food for dinner. Amy wanted to act smart and help her mom. She held her mom's hand and walked with her through the store.

In the store, Amy saw her friend Tom. Tom was with his dad. Tom said, "Hi Amy! I am helping my dad too. We are buying food for dinner." Amy smiled and said, "I am helping my mom. I want to be smart like you." Tom and Amy felt happy to be smart helpers.

Amy's mom told her about value. She said, "Amy, when we buy things, we look for good value. That means we get more for our money." Amy nodded and tried to find good value things for dinner. She and her mom bought food and went home. Amy was proud to be a smart helper and learned about value that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside with her friends, but she was scared of the dark. Every night, she would have a nightmare about monsters under her bed. 

One night, Lily's mommy tucked her into bed and said, "Don't worry, Lily. There are no monsters under your bed. Just close your eyes and go to sleep." 

Lily tried to sleep, but she couldn't stop thinking about the monsters. She decided to look under her bed to make sure. She found nothing but some toys and a thick blanket. 

But when she crawled back into bed, she heard a voice say, "I'm not a monster, Lily. I'm your nightmare." Lily was so scared that she screamed and woke up her mommy. 

From that night on, Lily never looked under her bed again. She learned that sometimes, it's better not to find out what's hiding in the dark.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sally. Sally went to the woods with her mommy, who was looking for a mysterious statue. Sally loved exploring, so she ran ahead and looked everywhere.

She soon saw the statue in a clearing. It was so tall and shiny, like a giant gold teddy bear. She wanted to touch it.

Sally tugged and tugged, but she couldn't move the statue. â€œHere, Sally! Let me show you!â€ her mom said.

Silly and her mommy pulled really hard, and the statue started to wobble. Finally, it jumped up and Sally giggled with delight. â€œWow! It's so mysterious" she said. 

On the way home, Sally stretched her arms around the statue and dragged it in the sunshine. She already had most of the answers to her questions, but she knew she would find out more during her next adventure!

Anna and Ben are playing in the garden. They see an aeroplane in the sky. It is big and white and makes a loud noise.

"Where is the aeroplane going?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. Maybe to another country," Ben says.

They watch the aeroplane until it is very small and far away.

"Let's pretend we are flying too," Anna says. She runs and spreads her arms like wings. Ben follows her.

They run and jump and laugh. They feel the wind on their faces and the sun on their backs.

They see a lemon tree near the fence. It has yellow fruits that look like balls.

"Can we pick some lemons?" Ben asks.

"OK, but be careful. They are sour," Anna says.

They pick two lemons and peel them. They take a bite and make a funny face.

"Yuck! They are very sour!" Ben says.

"They make my mouth hurt," Anna says.

They spit out the lemons and drink some water from the hose.

They look at each other and giggle.

"That was a bad idea," Anna says.

"Next time, let's pick apples. They are sweet," Ben says.

They agree and go back to playing. They forget about the sour lemons and the aeroplane. They are happy.

Once upon a time in a far away land, there was a painter named Jack. Jack was kind and loyal, and always thanked everyone that he met. One day, Jack was feeling especially kind and he decided to give a gift to all the people in his town. He went to the store and he bought some big buckets of bright colors. He gathered all the townsfolk together, and he said, â€œToday I am thanking each and every one of you! I am giving you all a wonderful present: paint! I want you to use it to make something beautiful!"

Everyone was so excited and began taking the paint. Then, one by one, they used the paint to make something special. They created pretty pictures and colored the walls of their homes. When they were done, they thanked Jack for his kind gift.

Jack was so happy to see how loyal and thankful everyone was! He knew he had made the right decision by giving his gift. From that day forward, Jack was known as the loyal painter who gave the best gifts.

Geoffrey was measuring his bedroom when something went crazy. He stopped and looked up. An olive was spinning around, faster and faster. He could hear it laughing. 

He looked around his bedroom, but nothing else seemed unusual. He thought it was very strange that an olive would be spinning around like that.

He asked the olive, "What are you doing?"

The olive said, "I'm measuring too! I'm measuring how long I can spin around."

Geoffrey thought for a moment, then he said, "That's crazy! But why are you measuring in my room?"

The olive smiled and said, "Because I like it here. I like to measure in your room."

One day, Mommy brought home a new bathtub. It was big and white. Sammy was a shy three year old and so he was a bit scared at first.

Mommy showed Sammy how to get in the bathtub and fill it with warm water. Sammy quickly learned that taking a bath in the new bathtub was fun. He always felt so clean afterwards and he could splash the water around and make bubbles.

Mommy loved to bring Sammy in the bathtub with her. They would sing and play together and Sammy felt happy and special.

Every night before bed, Mommy brought Sammy to the bathtub and they would snuggle together until it was time to get out. Sammy never felt shy when he was in the bathtub with Mommy. He knew he was safe and loved.

Lily loved nature. She liked to look at the birds, the flowers, and the trees. She wanted to help nature and make it happy. One day, she saw a big truck near the park. The truck had a big saw and a big sign. The sign said: "We will cut the trees and make a mall here."

Lily was sad and angry. She ran to the truck and shouted: "Stop! You cannot cut the trees! The trees are nature's friends! They give us air and shade and homes for the birds! You are bad and mean!"

The truck driver saw Lily and laughed. He said: "Go away, little girl. You don't know anything. The mall will be good for the city. It will have shops and games and food. The trees are old and useless. I will cut them and make money."

Lily did not go away. She said: "No, you are wrong. The mall will be bad for the nature. It will make noise and trash and smoke. The trees are not useless. They are beautiful and important. I will not let you cut them. I will save them!"

Lily climbed on the truck and took the saw. She threw it away and ran to the trees. She hugged them and said: "Don't worry, trees. I am here. I will protect you. You are my friends."

The truck driver was angry and scared. He called the police and said: "Help! There is a crazy girl on my truck. She took my saw and ran to the park. She is trying to stop me from cutting the trees. Come and get her!"

The police came and saw Lily and the truck driver. They asked them what happened. Lily told them her story. The truck driver told them his story. The police listened and thought. They said: "Lily, you are brave and kind. You care about nature and you want to save it. But you cannot take things that are not yours and you cannot climb on trucks. That is dangerous and wrong. You have to be careful and respectful. Truck driver, you are greedy and rude. You don't care about nature and you want to destroy it. But you cannot cut trees that are not yours and you cannot laugh at children. That is harmful and mean. You have to be responsible and respectful."

The police took the saw and the sign from the truck driver. They said: "We will not let you cut the trees. The trees are part of the park and the park is for everyone. The park is a place where nature and people can live together and be happy. You have to find another place for your mall. And you have to say sorry to Lily and the trees."

The truck driver was ashamed and sorry. He said: "I am sorry, Lily. I am sorry, trees. I was wrong and selfish. I will not cut you. I will find another place for my mall. And I will plant more trees there."

Lily was happy and proud. She said: "Thank you, police. Thank you, truck driver. I am glad you changed your mind. I hope you will be nice to nature from now on. And I hope you will visit the park and see how beautiful it is."

The police and the truck driver left. Lily stayed with the trees. She sang to them and played with them. The birds and the flowers and the other animals came and joined her. They thanked her and praised her. They said: "You are a hero, Lily. You saved the trees and the park. You are a friend of nature. You are famous!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big box. In the box, he had many grapes. He liked to keep them organized. He put the green grapes on one side and the purple grapes on the other side. Tim loved his grapes very much.

One day, Tim's friend Sam came to play. Sam saw the box and asked, "Can I have a grape?" Tim said, "No, I own all these grapes. They are mine." Sam felt sad but he still wanted to play with Tim.

They played with toys and had fun. But Sam still wanted a grape. When Tim was not looking, Sam took a grape from the box. He ate it very fast. Tim saw him and got very mad. He yelled, "You took my grape!" Tim did not want to be friends with Sam anymore. Sam went home feeling sad, and Tim was left alone with his grapes.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were walking together through a big, huge park. Suddenly, they saw an enormous hill.

"Wow!", they both said, looking up at the hill.

"Do you think we can climb up there?", asked Jack.

"Yes, we can!", said Jill.

So they both grabbed hands and started walking up the hill. Soon they reached the top and saw a huge, long pass.

"This looks like a lot of fun!", said Jack.

"Let's go down the pass and reverse!", said Jill.

So they both ran down the pass, going faster and faster. At the end, they both made a big jump and glided through the air in reverse!

They both landed on the soft grass and laughed. That was such a fun day!

Once upon a time there was a lively little girl. She was playing with her toy gun and pretending to shoot anyone who came near.

Suddenly, she shot herself by accident. She started crying and her mom saw what had happened. Her mom quickly grabbed a bandage and put it on her. 

The bandage was bright and colourful and it made the girl feel happy. She stopped crying as soon as she saw the beautiful bandage. Her mom gave her a big hug and told her to be careful while playing.

From that day forward the little girl had learned her lesson and never played with her toy gun again. She always remained lively, but now she was even more careful.

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play together. Sometimes they play with toys, sometimes they play with balls, sometimes they run and jump.

One day, they decide to play exercise. They want to be strong and healthy. They find a big rope in the yard. They think it is fun to pull the rope.

Sam says, "I will pull this end, and you pull that end. We will see who is stronger."

Mia says, "OK, let's do it. But be careful, don't pull too hard."

They start to pull the rope. They pull and pull and pull. They feel their arms and legs working. They laugh and smile.

But then, something happens. The rope breaks. It snaps in the middle. Sam and Mia fall down. They are surprised and scared.

They look at the rope. It is old and thin. It is not reliable. It is not good for exercise.

Sam says, "Oh no, the rope is broken. It is not a good rope. It is a bad rope."

Mia says, "Yes, it is a bad rope. But we are OK. We are not hurt. We are still friends."

They hug each other. They are happy. They decide to find another game to play. They look for a reliable toy. They find a ball. They think it is fun to kick the ball. They play exercise with the ball. They are strong and healthy.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the garden. One day, they find a big bottle of soap. They want to make bubbles.

"Look, Tom, I have soap!" Lily says. She opens the bottle and pours some soap on her hand.

"Me too, me too!" Tom says. He grabs the bottle and pours some soap on his hand.

They blow on their hands and make bubbles. The bubbles are big and shiny. They laugh and clap.

"More, more!" Tom says. He pours more soap on his hand. He blows harder and harder.

"Stop, Tom, stop!" Lily says. She sees something bad. The soap is going in Tom's ears. "The soap will make you deaf!"

But Tom does not hear Lily. He blows more and more. The soap fills his ears. He can't hear anything.

"Tom, Tom, can you hear me?" Lily says. She shakes Tom's arm. She is scared.

But Tom does not answer. He does not hear Lily. He does not hear anything. He is deaf.

Lily cries. Tom cries. They are sad. The soap is bad. The end.

One day, a little girl named Amy was playing with her red brick. She liked to build towers with her bricks. She was trying to make a very tall tower, but it kept falling down. Amy felt frustrated.

Amy's big brother Tom saw her and asked, "What's wrong, Amy?" She told him, "I want to make a tall tower, but it keeps falling." Tom wanted to help his sister, so he had an idea. "Let's save the tower with a strong base," he said.

Tom and Amy worked together to make the tower. They put many bricks at the bottom to make the strong base. Then, they carefully added more bricks to make the tower taller and taller. Finally, the tower was very tall and did not fall down. Amy was so happy, and she thanked Tom for his help. They played with the brick tower all day and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was three years old and his name was Sam. One day Sam went out for a walk with his mom. 

As they walked, they came across a field with lots of pumpkins. Sam said, "Mom, can I find a pumpkin?".

His mom smiled and said "Yes, of course, you can find a pumpkin."

So Sam started searching through the field and soon found the perfect pumpkin that he wanted. It was big and round, and had a funny face on it. 

When Sam picked up the pumpkin to show his mom, he noticed that it was sour! He wrinkled up his nose and asked his mother, "Is this the type of pumpkin I can keep?" 

His mom laughed and said, "No, Sam. This pumpkin is sour. We can't put it in our home. But, let's look around and try to find a sweet pumpkin for us to keep!"

Sam laughed and got back to looking for a pumpkin. With his mom's help, he soon found the sweetest pumpkin in the whole field!

Sam was so happy and put it into his cart. He waited patiently to bring it home and carve a funny face into it. It was going to be the best pumpkin ever!

One day, there was a little boy named Jimmy. He was only three years old. He wanted to go outside to play and thought it would be fun to go for a run. So he put on his shoes and started to run in the grass. 

He saw a big apple tree and noticed that there were lots of juicy apples hanging in the branches. He was so excited and wanted one of them. He started to run towards it, but suddenly he felt something wet on his feet. He looked down and saw that he was standing in a big puddle of mud. 

Jimmy was worried and soiled his shoes. He quickly ran back home to get a towel and a fresh change of clothes. After he had cleaned up the mud, he went back to the tree and picked a big red apple. He tasted it and it was so sweet! 

Jimmy was very happy with his big red apple, but he was very careful not to get dirty again. He stayed in the grass and ran around having all kinds of fun. That day, he made sure to always keep an eye out for puddles!

Once upon a time there lived a little girl. Her name was Daisy and she loved to play. One day she found an old video in the attic. She was very curious and decided to watch it. 

The video was about a mysterious land Full of strange creatures. Daisy couldn't believe what she was seeing.

Daisy decided to go and explore the land but her mum said it was too dangerous. She was so sad and angry.

"Why can't I go?" Said Daisy, "I want to see the creatures!"

"It's too harsh sweetheart," said Daisy's mum.

Daisy was disappointed but she trusted her mum and stayed home. She still believed that the world in the video really existed, somewhere.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah who loved to sleep. Every night she would snuggle up in her bed, close her eyes and dream wonderful dreams. 

One night was very different, however. Sarah was very sleepy but she couldn't seem to go to bed. She just kept looking out of her bedroom window at the dark night sky. 

Suddenly her mom appeared in the doorway with a calendar in her hand. She said to Sarah, "It's time for bed, sweetheart. Look, you can see the crescent moon on the calendar!" 

Sarah gasped as she spotted the crescent moon in the bottom corner of the calendar. She said to her mom, "I'm so sleepy now. I'll go to sleep now mom." 

Her mom smiled, kissed her on the forehead and said, "Goodnight sweetheart." 

Sarah closed her eyes and went to sleep. She slept soundly throughout the night and dreamt wonderful, wonderful dreams.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was so excited because it was her birthday! All of her friends were there and they had cakes, candy and presents.

But Sarah was feeling sad. She wanted to play with the other kids but she felt too heavy.

"What's wrong Sarah?", her Mom asked.

"I'm too big", she replied.

Her Mom hugged her. "That's ok Sarah. You can still play. You can try to move your body - it will help make you feel lighter," she said with a smile.

Sarah was excited! She started wiggling her arms and legs and soon she was running around and laughing with the other kids. She felt so light and happy.

The party was so much fun and Sarah was thrilled that she was able to join in. She was no longer sad - she was happy and full of excitement!

Once upon a time, there was a little lizard. The little lizard lived in a tiny house. The house was in a big forest with many trees and flowers. The little lizard loved to play with his friends, the birds and the bugs.

One day, the little lizard saw a big fire in the forest. The fire was very close to his tiny house. The little lizard wanted to prevent the fire from burning his house. He thought very hard about what to do.

The little lizard had an idea. He asked his friends, the birds, to help him. The birds flew to the river and brought water in their beaks. They dropped the water on the fire. The little lizard and his friends worked together to prevent the fire from burning his house. They were all very happy and proud of what they did.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside, but he didn't like when mosquitoes buzzed around him and bit him. One day, Timmy's friend Sally came to play with him. Sally saw that Timmy was getting bitten by mosquitoes and wanted to help him. 

Sally told Timmy that if he wore bug spray, the mosquitoes wouldn't bother him anymore. Timmy was happy that Sally wanted to help him and he put on the bug spray. They played outside for a long time and no mosquitoes bothered them. 

After they finished playing, Timmy thanked Sally for her help. Sally was happy to help her friend and they promised to play together again soon. From then on, whenever Timmy played outside, he made sure to wear bug spray to keep the mosquitoes away.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a big tree with many branches. Lily wanted to climb the tree and see the birds. Ben was scared of heights and said no.

"Come on, Ben, it will be fun!" Lily said. "The tree is smooth and easy to climb. You can hold on to the hose that hangs from the branch. I will go first and show you."

Lily climbed the tree with the help of the hose. She reached the top and saw a nest with three eggs. She was happy and called Ben to join her.

Ben was still afraid, but he did not want to disappoint Lily. He tried to climb the tree, but he slipped and fell. He hurt his knee and cried.

Lily heard Ben's cry and climbed down quickly. She ran to him and hugged him. She said she was sorry and that she should not have pushed him.

Ben stopped crying and hugged her back. He said he was sorry too and that he should have told her how he felt.

They learned that they should respect each other's feelings and not force each other to do things they don't like. They decided to play something else that they both enjoyed. They were happy and stayed friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on adventures and exploring new places. One day, she heard about a big castle that was nearby. She decided to go and check it out.

As she walked towards the castle, she saw a man with a sour face. He looked like he didn't want to be bothered. Lily smiled at him and said hello, but he didn't say anything back. She thought to herself, "I hope I don't meet anyone else like him at the castle."

Finally, she arrived at the castle and was amazed by its size and beauty. As she explored the castle, she met many friendly people who showed her around. She even met a prince who invited her to a big party that night. Lily was so excited to go and couldn't wait to see what other adventures awaited her at the castle.

Bobby and his Mommy went to the park. Bobby was so excited to go outside and have a picnic! He wanted to bring his toy dog too, so that he could play with it in the park.

Bobby and his Mommy packed their picnic bags and headed to the park. When they arrived, there was a big park guard standing at the gate. 

"Good morning, everyone!" said the park guard. "Welcome to the park!"

"Thank you!" said Bobby's Mommy.

Bobby and his Mommy walked through the gate with their picnic bags. They had a successful picnic in the park and played lots of fun games with Bobby's toy dog. 

When it was time to leave, the park guard said goodbye. 

"Goodbye, everyone!" said the park guard. "Have a wonderful day!"

Bobby and his Mommy waved goodbye and walked away, smiling.  Bobby had a successful day in the park with lots of fun.

Mommy was supplying lovely clothes for Amy. She had lots of clothes to choose from â€“ pretty dresses, colorful jammies and lots of t-shirts. Amy tried them all on, but she loved the blue dress the best. She twirled around in it and said, "Look, Mommy! I'm beautiful!" Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, you look lovely darling."

Amy skipped and jumped around the room in her new dress. She couldn't wait to wear it the next day. Mommy had supplied Amy with lots of lovely clothes and she was so happy.

Amy hugged her Mommy and said, "Thank you for the pretty clothes. I love them so much!" Mommy smiled and said, "I love you too sweetheart." Amy hugged her tight and said, "I love you too!"

One day, a little girl was playing in the garden. She felt safe and peaceful, like nothing could hurt her. Suddenly, she heard a sound. It was a shark!

The little girl started to crawl away, but it was too late. The shark was getting closer, ready to attack. The little girl tried to stay quiet and still, hoping the shark would go away, but it didn't work.

The shark came closer and closer, until suddenly it lunged forward and bit the little girl. She screamed in pain as the shark dragged her away.

The little girl never returned, and was never seen again. Her peaceful day in the garden ended in tragedy.

Lily was deaf. She could not hear what the teacher said in the classroom. She could not hear what the other kids said to her. She felt sad and lonely.

One day, a new kid came to the classroom. His name was Ben. He was deaf too. He could use his hands to talk. He showed Lily how to do it. Lily was happy. She had a friend.

They played together at recess. They shared their toys and snacks. They learned new words with their hands. They had fun.

But some kids were mean. They did not like Ben and Lily. They said bad things about them. They laughed at them. They took their toys and snacks. They pushed them and hurt them.

Lily and Ben tried to tell the teacher. But the teacher did not understand. She did not know how to use her hands to talk. She did not help them. She said they had to grow up and stop being silly.

Lily and Ben felt angry and scared. They did not want to go to the classroom anymore. They did not want to learn anymore. They did not want to play anymore. They lost their happiness.

Once upon a time there was a messy room. Toys were all over the floor and the bed was a mess.

A young boy named Timmy wanted to tidy up the room. He began to pick up the toys and put them on the shelves. He took all the pillows off the bed and made it look neat and tidy.

When he was finished, a feeling of peace came into the room. Timmy smiled and laid down on the bed. He was so happy to have finished tidying the room.

Then Timmy's mom came in and praised him for making his room look so neat and clean. Timmy smiled even wider. He was sure glad to have finished tidying up his messy room.

Once there was a little girl called Mira and she loved to play outside. One day, Mira spotted a net in the garden and she was super excited. She wanted to use it to play a game with her friends.

Mira's friends came over to the garden and they all tried to figure out how to play with the net. "Let's play 'catch!'" Mira said. Everyone agreed and the game began. 

However, it quickly became clear that the net had a rip in it and it wouldn't hold up very well. Mira had a great idea. She said, "Let's get creative and use the net to find a way to fix it!" 

The friends worked together to repair the net and eventually they managed to fix it by using some leaves and pieces of string. 

Everyone cheered with joy. Mira was so proud that they had managed to fix the net together. From then on, every time they would spot the net, they would remember the creative way they had worked together to solve the problem.

Once upon a time there was a factory that made fake toys. The toys looked real, but they were not. One day a little girl named Jacky came to the factory. She saw a big box that was rolling around. Jacky opened the box, and there was an old rusty toy car inside! 

Jacky picked up the car with a big smile and said, "Cool!" She pushed the car around the factory, then decided to take it home.

On the way home, one of the tires of the car fell off. Jacky looked sad, and so she stopped at a store to buy another tire. She looked at all the tires, but none of them fit her toy car. 

But then, Jacky saw a tire that was shaped like a bubble! She asked the shopkeeper, "Is this tire real?" 

The shopkeeper smiled and said, "No, it's just a fake tire. But it will fit perfectly on your toy car! Take it home and have fun rolling around the house!" 

Jacky was so happy. She thanked the shopkeeper and took the fake tire home. She quickly put it on her toy car, and off she went rolling around the house!

Once upon a time, there was a wild bunny. The bunny was pale and had big feet. He liked to bounce all around the meadow. He would jump and hop and have lots of fun. He would go bouncing and playing from morning till night. He was so happy and carefree!

One day, he saw something shiny in the leaves. He went to take a closer look and saw a sparkly ring. The bunny picked it up in his big teeth and started to bounce away with it. 

Soon a tall woman appeared, and the bunny stopped to look at her. She told the bunny that the ring belonged to her grandchild. She said if the bunny gave it back, she would reward him with more bounces.

The bunny was happy and hopped around a few times before giving the ring back. The woman thanked the bunny and said that he could come back whenever he wanted and bounce around in the meadow.

The bunny was so happy and thanked the woman before hopping away. He enjoyed bouncing around the meadow from then on, and was always careful to keep an eye out for anything shiny!

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy lived in a small house in the forest with his family. One day, Timmy went out to play and he saw a big factory in the distance. He was curious and decided to go see what it was.

When he got closer to the factory, he felt something tickling his nose. Suddenly, he sneezed so loudly that he woke up the nearby animals. A kind old owl saw Timmy and asked him what was wrong. Timmy explained that he sneezed because of the smell coming from the factory.

The owl, being very wise, told Timmy that the factory was making the air dirty and that it was not good for anyone. Timmy felt sad and wanted to help. So, he went back to his little house and told his family about the factory. Together, they came up with a plan to talk to the humans who owned the factory and ask them to be more humble and stop polluting the air. And they lived happily ever after.

Steve was playing and he heard his dad say "it's time to follow me and go on vacation". Steve was excited as he followed his dad to the car. Steve could see people in colorful clothes, delicious smells and happy faces.

Steve and his dad went on a plane for the first time. The air was fresh and the sky was blue. Steve loved looking out of the window at the clouds. His dad said it was a fair day for a vacation!

At the end of their journey, Steve and his dad arrived at their vacation spot. It was so beautiful with lush green trees and a crystal clear lake. The sun was shining and it was warm.

Steve enjoyed running and jumping around. He also liked making castles in the sand. His dad watched him and smiled with joy.

At the end of their vacation, Steve and his dad went to the airport to fly back home. Steve's dad said that it had been a fair vacation. Steve smiled and said he wanted to go back soon!

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a daddy and their daughter. The daughter was only three years old. She was happy and loved to explore.

One day, the mommy and daddy brought their daughter to the store. There were lots of things to look at and the daughter wanted to explore everywhere. The mommy and daddy said it was better to crawl so she wouldn't hurt herself.

The daughter smiled and started to crawl around the store. She looked at everything and thought it was so much fun.

After a little while, the daughter came across a toy. It was a teddy bear. Its eyes were shiny and they sparkled in the light. The mommy and daddy smiled. It was cheap so they let their daughter keep it.

The daughter hugged the bear tight. â€œThank youâ€, she said with glee. She was so happy she wanted to crawl all the way home.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the living room. There is a big armchair in the living room. It is soft and cozy. Lily and Ben both want to sit on the armchair.

"Me first!" Lily says. She runs to the armchair and jumps on it.

"No, me first!" Ben says. He runs after Lily and tries to push her off.

"Stop it!" Lily says. She holds on to the armchair.

"Move!" Ben says. He pulls Lily's hair.

"Ow!" Lily says. She kicks Ben's leg.

They make a lot of noise. They yell and cry and fight. They do not share the armchair.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the living room. She sees Lily and Ben on the armchair. She is not happy.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks. She looks at Lily and Ben.

They stop fighting. They look at Mom. They are quiet.

"We want to sit on the armchair," Lily says.

"But there is only one armchair," Mom says.

Lily and Ben look at the armchair. They look at each other. They have to decide.

"Can we take turns?" Lily asks.

"OK," Ben says.

They nod. They smile. They hug.

Mom smiles too. She is happy.

"Good job," Mom says. She claps her hands.

Lily and Ben take turns. They sit on the armchair. They read a book. They sing a song. They are not noisy. They are nice. They share the armchair.

Once there was a fisherman who lived by a purple sea. He loved being near the sea and would spend his days fishing.
One day he made a special promise to the sea. The sea wanted the fisherman to share his love and joy so the fisherman promised to do that.
He made a big boat out of purple wood and started showing people the beauty of the sea and its creatures. Everywhere he went, the people loved it and welcomed him with smiles. They often brought him gifts for his boat, so that it would stay purple and beautiful.
The fisherman kept his promise and shared his love with everyone. The sea was so pleased that it continued to bring him delicious fishes each morning. The fisherman was so happy and often thanked the sea for being so kind to him.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved figuring out things. She was very creative. Her parents saw all the happy things she was doing and wanted to give her a special treat. So one day they decided to give her a present.

The present was a big box, with a padlock on it. The little girl was so excited! She quickly asked her parents what was inside. But they just smiled and said she had to unlock it to find out.

The little girl thought and thought about how to unlock the box. She tried many different things but nothing would work. After awhile her parents helped her to solve the puzzle. They showed her how to turn the key and twist it until the padlock clicked open.

When she opened the box, the little girl was so happy! Inside was a brand new toy that she could play with. She was so thankful to her parents for giving her such a creative and special gift.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and cuddle with her teddy bear. One day, her mommy and daddy decided to light a fire in the fireplace to keep the house warm.

Lily's mommy warned her not to get too close to the fireplace because it was very hot. "I dare you to touch it," said Lily's big brother, Jack. But Lily knew it was dangerous and didn't want to get burned.

Later that night, Lily's family sat around the fireplace and roasted marshmallows. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise coming from the chimney. It was a bird that had gotten stuck and couldn't get out! Jack tried to grab it, but it was too high up.

Lily had an idea. She grabbed her teddy bear and held it up to the chimney. The bird saw the teddy bear and flew towards it, finally escaping the fireplace. Everyone cheered and Lily felt proud of herself for being brave and helping the bird. And even though the fireplace was now covered in soot and ash, no one thought it was disgusting because they were all happy the bird was safe.

Once upon a time, there was a hammer. It was very special. It was so beautiful that everyone wanted to take it. 

One day a little boy saw it. He wanted it so much that he decided to take it. He picked it up and carried it away.

The little boy was so happy with his hammer that he took it everywhere with him. Everywhere he went, people marveled at the beautiful hammer.

The little boy used his hammer to build all sorts of things. He even used it to make a surprise for his Mom. He hammered and hammered until it was finished. When it was done, it was the most beautiful thing the little boy had ever seen.

The little boy was so proud of his hammer and all the things that he could make with it. He could hardly believe his own luck. And the hammer was never forgotten.

Lily liked to play with her toys on the big cushion in the living room. She had a doll, a bear, a car and a ball. She made them talk and move and have fun. One day, she saw a fly on the cushion. It was not moving. Lily touched it with her finger. It was dead.

Lily felt sad for the fly. She wanted to help it. She ran to the kitchen and got a cup of water. She poured some water on the fly. Maybe it was thirsty, she thought. But the fly did not wake up. It was still dead.

Lily got an idea. She ran to her room and got a blanket. She wrapped the fly in the blanket and put it on the cushion. She said, "Good night, fly. I hope you have good dreams." Then she got her doll and hugged it. She said, "Thank you, doll, for being my friend. You are not dead. You are alive and happy."

Lily's mom came into the living room and saw Lily and her doll on the cushion. She smiled and said, "What are you doing, Lily?" Lily looked up and said, "I am playing with my toys, mom. And I am saying thank you to them. They are good toys. They make me happy."

Lily's mom sat down next to Lily and said, "That's very nice of you, Lily. It's good to say thank you to the things and people that make you happy. And it's good to be kind to the things and people that are not happy. Like the fly. You tried to help the fly, didn't you?" Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. But the fly was dead. I could not make it alive. I was sad."

Lily's mom hugged Lily and said, "I know, Lily. Sometimes things die and we can't do anything about it. It's okay to be sad. But it's also okay to be happy. Because you have a lot of things and people that love you. Like me. And dad. And your toys. And the cushion. And the sun. And the moon. And the stars. And many more. Can you say thank you to them, too?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, mom. Thank you, mom. Thank you, dad. Thank you, toys. Thank you, cushion. Thank you, sun. Thank you, moon. Thank you, stars. Thank you, thank you, thank you."

Once upon a time there was a dog named Spot. He was a very happy pup and loved to play with his friends. One day Spot and his friends went for a walk in the park. They had lots of fun running around and playing games. 

Spot's friend Lola said, "Let's go for a walk and explore!" 

Spot took off running and Lola followed. They went all around the park and before they knew it, it was getting dark. 

Lola said, "Let's go home now, Spot." 

Spot didn't want to go home, so he took off running again. Lola shouted, "Spot, come back, heel!" 

Spot slowed down and remembered that he had to listen when someone said "heel" so he slowly made his way back to Lola. He walked next to her with a long leash and stayed close. 

When they got home, Spot was so proud that he had listened to Lola and stayed close. From then on he remembered to take "heel" very seriously!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat rice for dinner every day. One day, her mom made a lovely bowl of rice with some vegetables. Lily sat down to eat, but she didn't feel like eating the vegetables.

"I don't want to eat the vegetables," Lily said.

"But they're good for you," her mom urged.

Lily didn't want to listen, but her mom kept urging her to eat the vegetables. Finally, Lily took a bite and realized they were actually delicious.

"Yum, these are really good!" Lily said with a smile.

From that day on, Lily always ate her vegetables with her lovely bowl of rice.

Ben and Lily were going to the zoo with their mom. They were very happy and excited. They wanted to see the lions, the monkeys, and the elephants. Mom said they had a surprise for them at the zoo, but she would not tell them what it was. She said they had to guess.

"Is it a new animal?" Ben asked.

"Is it a big toy?" Lily asked.

Mom smiled and said, "You will see when we get there. It is something very special."

Ben and Lily were anxious to find out. They tried to guess all the way to the zoo. They looked out the window and saw cars, trees, and houses. They did not see anything that looked like a surprise.

When they got to the zoo, Mom bought the tickets and gave them a map. She said, "Follow me. I will show you the surprise. It is at the end of this path."

Ben and Lily followed Mom. They saw many animals on the way. They saw the lions, the monkeys, and the elephants. They were happy, but they still wanted to see the surprise.

They reached the end of the path. There was a big gate with a sign that said, "Penguin View". Mom opened the gate and said, "Here we are. This is the surprise. We can go inside and see the penguins."

Ben and Lily gasped. They loved penguins. They had seen them on TV, but they had never seen them in real life. They ran inside the gate and saw a big pool with many penguins. The penguins were swimming, diving, and sliding on the ice. They were black and white and very cute.

Ben and Lily were amazed. They clapped and laughed. They thanked Mom for the surprise. They said, "This is the best view ever. We love the penguins. They are so fun and cool."

Mom hugged them and said, "I'm glad you like it. I knew you would. I guessed right."

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to play outside with his friends, but one day he found a big hole in the ground. It was so deep that he couldn't see the bottom. 

Benny knew he shouldn't go near the hole because it was very harsh and dangerous. But he wanted to know how deep it was, so he decided to count how many hops it would take to get to the bottom. 

Benny hopped and hopped, counting each hop until he reached the bottom. When he got there, he found a treasure chest filled with carrots! Benny was so happy and he knew he had found a great number of carrots. 

From that day on, Benny knew that even though something might seem harsh or dangerous, it could lead to a great reward if he was brave enough to explore it.

Once upon a time, there was a big, red basketball. It loved to play with kids in the park. One day, it got wet because a careless boy left it in the rain. The basketball did not like being wet. It wanted to be dry.

The sun saw the wet basketball and felt sad. The sun wanted to help. So, it shined very bright and warm. The basketball started to feel dry and happy. It was excited to play with the kids again.

Later, the kids came back to the park. They saw the dry basketball and were very happy. They played with the basketball all day long. The careless boy said sorry for leaving it in the rain. The basketball forgave him, and they all had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear. The big bear lived in a big forest. One day, the big bear found a nail on the ground. The big bear picked up the nail and looked at it. The nail was very sharp. The big bear decided to fold the nail in half so it wouldn't hurt anyone. The big bear was very happy that he could help keep his friends safe.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jane and Fred. They lived far away from each other so they only wrote letters. One day Fred wrote to Jane with a special pen. The pen had ink inside of it that changed colour. Jane was so excited!

She opened the letter to see the beautiful ink inside. It was very slow to move and it made the most beautiful patterns. When the ink finally finished moving Jane said, "Wow! That's so cool!"

Jane wrote to Fred with the same kind of pen. She sent it off in the post and waited and waited. Finally the letter arrived and sure enough inside was the special ink again. Fred opened the letter and smiled when he saw the pattern the ink had made.

He said, "That looks so beautiful! Jane is so clever!â€ 
They kept writing back and forth with their special ink pen, each one amazed by the different patterns it created. 

The two friends had so much fun making things with the ink pen that their letters became very long!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to jog in the park with her mommy. One day, while they were jogging, they saw a little bird who looked very hungry. 

Lily asked her mommy, "Can we feed the bird, please?" 

Her mommy said, "Sure, let's give the bird some bread crumbs." 

Lily felt very happy that they could help the bird. But suddenly, she saw her friend from school watching them. Lily was ashamed because she thought her friend might make fun of her for feeding a bird. 

Her mommy noticed how Lily felt and said, "Don't be ashamed, Lily. It's a good thing to help others, even if they are just little birds." 

Lily smiled and felt proud that she could help the little bird.

Lily and Ben are playing with blocks. They like to build towers and houses and cars. Lily has a lot of red blocks and Ben has a lot of blue blocks. They share some yellow and green blocks.

"Look at my tower!" Lily says. "It is very tall and strong. It can touch the sky!"

Ben looks at Lily's tower. He thinks it is too tall and not strong. He wants to make his tower taller and stronger. He takes some more blocks and puts them on top of his tower.

"Look at my tower!" Ben says. "It is taller and stronger than yours. It can touch the stars!"

Lily looks at Ben's tower. She thinks it is too silly and not stable. She sees that Ben's tower is leaning to one side. She has an idea. She takes a yellow block and throws it at Ben's tower.

"Oops!" Lily says. "I am sorry. I did not mean to do that."

Ben's tower falls down with a loud crash. The blocks scatter all over the floor. Ben is angry and sad. He cries.

"Why did you do that?" Ben says. "You are mean. You broke my tower!"

Lily feels bad. She did not want to make Ben cry. She wants to make him happy. She has another idea. She takes some blocks and makes a funny face with them. She puts them in front of Ben.

"Look at this!" Lily says. "It is a silly face. It has a big nose and a small mouth and two eyes that are not the same. It is funny. Do you like it?"

Ben looks at the silly face. He stops crying. He sees that Lily is trying to make him laugh. He thinks the silly face is funny. He smiles.

"I like it!" Ben says. "It is very silly. Can I make one too?"

Lily nods. She gives Ben some blocks. They make more silly faces with the blocks. They laugh and play. They are friends again. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only three years old and loved exploring the garden. One day she was looking around the old shed when she saw a cobweb in the corner. It was filthy and full of dirt.

'What is that?' she said, not understanding what it was.

A voice then echoed from behind her. It was her mum.

'That Lucy is a cobweb. It's made by a spider,' she said.

Lucy wrinkled her nose. 'Why is it so filthy?'

'That's because the spiders catch flies and they are very dirty,' her mum told her.

Lucy nodded and smiled. Now she understood.

Mom and Dad raised the little girl. They helped her have a safe home with furniture for comfort. Mom and Dad showed the little girl how to keep herself safe. She was careful not to touch any of the furniture without Mom and Dad there.

One day, Dad said he was going to raise something. The little girl was curious, so she followed. Dad was raising a new bed for the little girl. It was so special! Together, Dad and the little girl moved the furniture and put the new bed in just the right spot. The little girl was amazed. She couldn't wait to sleep in her safe and cozy new bed.

Mom and Dad watched proudly as the little girl giggled with glee. She thanked them for making her home so safe and comfortable. The little girl had never felt so happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to take showers because it made her feel clean and comfortable. One day, while taking a shower, she saw a beautiful butterfly outside the window. She admired the butterfly's pretty wings and wished she could fly like it.

The next day, Lily went to the park and saw a group of kids playing with a big ball. She admired how they played together and wanted to join in. She ran over and asked if she could play too. The kids welcomed her and they all had fun together.

As the sun began to set, Lily went home and snuggled up in her cozy bed. She thought about the butterfly and the kids at the park and felt happy. She admired the beauty of the world around her and fell asleep with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet rat named Ratty. Ratty was very cute and loved to play with Lily. One day, Lily went to the park with Ratty. While playing, Ratty ran away and got hurt. Lily was sad and wanted to help Ratty. She took Ratty to the vet who said that Ratty needed a bandage. The bandage would include some medicine to make Ratty feel better. After a few days, Ratty was all better and Lily was happy again.

Anna and Ben are playing with their baby brother, Sam. Sam is very small and cute, but he is also very persistent. He wants to grab everything he sees, even if it is not his.

"Look, Sam, this is a ball. You can roll it and bounce it," Anna says, showing him a red ball. She rolls it to him gently, and he smiles and tries to catch it.

"No, Sam, this is a book. You can read it and learn new words," Ben says, holding a colorful book. He opens it and points to a picture of a dog. "This is a dog. It says woof-woof."

Sam reaches for the book, but Ben pulls it away. "No, Sam, this is mine. You have the ball."

Sam frowns and starts to cry. He does not want the ball. He wants the book.

"Ben, don't be mean. Share with Sam. He is just curious," Anna says, taking the book from Ben. She gives it to Sam, who stops crying and laughs. He likes the book.

"Fine, I don't care. I have the ball," Ben says, rolling the ball away. He pretends he is not interested in the book.

But Sam is persistent. He crawls after Ben, dragging the book with him. He wants to share the book with Ben. He thinks Ben will like it too.

"Sam, leave me alone. I don't want the book. I want the ball," Ben says, pushing Sam away.

Sam does not give up. He keeps crawling and laughing. He thinks it is a game.

"Sam, stop it. You are annoying me," Ben says, getting angry.

Anna watches them and laughs too. She thinks they are funny. She loves her baby brother and her big brother. She knows they love each other too, even if they fight sometimes. She decides to join them and play with the ball and the book. She thinks they will have more fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to work. One day, she decided to help her mommy in the kitchen. She took a modest dish and filled it with water. Then, she found a sponge and started to wash the dishes. She worked so hard and scrubbed until her hands hurt. But she was so proud of her work that she smiled the whole time. 

When she finished washing the dishes, she took the dish to the counter and wiped it off. After that, she put the dish away. Lily was very excited to be able to help her mommy with working.

The next day, Lily wanted to help even more. This time, she brought a modest dish of food to the table. Her mommy smiled and praised Lily for being so kind and helpful. Lily was so happy to work and help her family.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sara. She was so excited because she had a package. She could not wait to open it and when the package arrived, she was ready. As soon as she opened the package, she screamed with joy. Inside there were lots of toys - dolls, trucks and puzzles - everything she wanted! She was so happy that she started to run around the room and jumped with joy, screaming. Sara had so much fun playing with her new toys. She smiled and laughed all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing dress-up and would often use a hanger to hang her princess dresses. One day, she found a heavy hammer in her dad's toolbox. She thought it looked like a fun toy and decided to play with it.

As she swung the hammer around, she accidentally struck the hanger holding her favorite dress. The hanger broke and the dress fell to the ground. Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. She knew she shouldn't have played with the hammer.

The moral of the story is that we should always be careful when playing with things that can be dangerous. Sometimes, accidents happen and we need to learn from them. Lily learned her lesson and promised to never play with tools again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing in her yard with her toys. One day, she was running around and accidentally bumped into a rock. It hurt her foot and she started crying.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toy cars and trucks. They like to make noises and pretend they are driving fast. Lily has a red car and Ben has a blue truck.

Tom and Sue are twins. They like to play with their toys and talk to each other. Sometimes they repeat what the other one says, like a game.

Sue hears him and says, "Ouch, my tummy hurts!" She repeats what he says, but she does not know he is in pain. She thinks it is part of the game.

Tom says, "No, Sue, it is not a game. I need help. I need Mommy." He repeats what he says, hoping she will understand.

Sue hears him and says, "No, Sue, it is not a game. I need help. I need Mommy." She repeats what he says, but she does not know he is serious. She thinks he is still playing.

Tom gets angry and says, "Stop repeating me, Sue! You are not helpful. You are silly!" He repeats what he says, trying to make her stop.

Sue hears him and says, "Stop repeating me, Sue! You are not helpful. You are silly!" She repeats what he says, but she does not know he is angry. She thinks he is joking.

Tom cries and says, "Mommy, Mommy, where are you?" He repeats what he says, looking for their mother.

Sue hears him and says, "Mommy, Mommy, where are you?" She repeats what he says, following him.

Then, Mommy comes and sees them. She sees the balloon and the tears. She hugs them and says, "What is wrong, my darlings?"

Tom says, "Mommy, I have gas. It hurts. Sue repeats me. She is not helpful. She is silly." He repeats what he says, pointing at Sue.

Sue says, "Mommy, I have gas. It hurts. Sue repeats me. She is not helpful. She is silly." She repeats what he says, pointing at herself.

Mommy smiles and says, "Oh, my darlings, you are both helpful and silly. You have gas because you blew the balloon too much. It is not good for your tummy. Next time, blow less and share more. And don't repeat each other when someone is in pain. Repeat only when someone is happy or funny. Do you understand?"

Tom and Sue nod and say, "Yes, Mommy, we understand." They repeat what she says, but this time they mean it. They hug Mommy and say, "We love you, Mommy." They repeat what they say, but this time they are happy.

One day, they had a fight over who could play with Rex. Ben said he saw him first, and Sam said he was his turn. They both pulled on Rex's neck, trying to take him away from each other. They did not listen to their mom, who told them to share and be nice. They pulled and pulled, until Rex's neck split in two. They both gasped and let go of Rex. They looked at the broken toy, and saw that his scales were fake. They were just stickers that peeled off easily.

They felt very sad and sorry. They realized that they had ruined their favorite toy, and hurt each other's feelings. They hugged and said they were sorry. They decided to glue Rex's neck back together, and find some new stickers for his scales. They learned that fighting over toys was not worth it, and that they should love and respect each other. They also learned that some things are not what they seem, and that they should be careful with their toys. They promised to play nicely with Rex and their other dinosaurs, and to share and take turns. They were happy again, and so was Rex.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly little girl. She liked to explore and see new things. One day, she decided to take a walk. As she was walking, she saw a strange symbol in the grass. She stopped to take a closer look.

The symbol was a friendly shape which made the little girl smile. She reached down and held the symbol in her hand. She kept it safe and kept on walking.

The symbol made the little girl feel happy and excited. She couldn't wait to tell her mom about it. When she got back home, she showed her mom the symbol. Her mom was really surprised!

The symbol was special to the little girl and her mom. It was like a reminder that they were both very friendly. The little girl still has the symbol and holds onto it tight. Whenever she looks at it, she remembers her special day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys every evening. One day, her mom brought home a new toy for her. It was a shiny red car.

Lily was very happy and she said, "Mommy, can we play with my new car tonight?"

Her mom replied, "Of course, Lily! We can play together."

That evening, Lily and her mom played with the new car until it was time for bed. Lily was so happy that she fell asleep with a big smile on her face. From that day on, Lily played with her new toy car every evening with her mom.

Once upon a time there were two bears. They were best friends and loved to play together. One day, the two friends were walking in the forest when they noticed a basket full of apples. 

The first bear said, "Let's take the apples and share them."

But the second bear wasn't sure. He didn't want to share the apples. He wanted them all for himself. He pinched one of the apples and said, "You can't have one! They are all mine!"

The first bear was jealous. He wanted an apple too. He pinched one of the apples and said to his friend, "You have to share. We can both eat an apple."

The second bear smiled. He knew that his best friend was right. He was happy to share the apples. They each ate an apple and had a wonderful time. The end.

Once there was a giraffe and a snake. The two were best friends. Every day they would work together.

One day the giraffe found a present. It was tucked away in the corner. It was very special and unique. 

The snake asked, "What is it?". 

The giraffe replied, "It's an original present. I think it might be for us!" 

The two were so excited. They opened the present together. Inside was a new toy that they hadn't seen before. 

The snake said, "Let's work together and play with it!" 

So the two friends worked together to enjoy their new present. They had lots of fun!

Once upon a time, in a small house, Mom and Dad were sitting at the table. They wanted to drink coffee. Dad wanted strong coffee, but Mom insisted on weak coffee. They talked about it for a bit.

Mom made the weak coffee and put it on the table. Dad was not happy, but he drank it anyway. They talked a little more and smiled at each other.

Then, a big wind came and blew the door open. The wind was so strong that it knocked the weak coffee off the table. The coffee spilled all over the floor. Mom and Dad were sad because they had no more coffee to drink. The day did not end well for them.

There was a bear named Bob who lived in a cave in the woods. Every day, he would go out and look for food. One day, Bob saw something hanging from a tree, it was a strange symbol. He wasn't sure what it was, but he decided to take it. 

Back in his cave, Bob looked closely at the symbol. It was made out of a rough material and he couldn't work out what it was. He looked all around his cave, and noticed a big, empty space on the wall. He decided to hang the symbol up there.

The symbol glowed in the cave and looked very special. Bob was proud of his new possession, and he never took it down. After a while, Bob's friends saw it and asked what it was. Bob told them it was a special symbol that he found in the woods, and he felt proud of it every time he saw it.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Kate. She was only three years old, but was already very smart. She was always eager to learn new things!

One day, she went to a special school. In the school, she met other children her age and they had lots of fun learning together. Some children already knew a lot, so they were able to learn quickly. But some of the children didn't understand things as easily, and they needed more help.

Kate was very patient with her friends. She taught them the things she knew and helped themwith the things they didn't understand. She saw that some of the children were poor learners, so she gave them extra help.

With Kate's help, all the children were able to learn well. By the end, none of them were poor learners anymore! The whole class was very proud of Kate for her patience and effort. She was so happy that she was able to help her friends!

Once there was a clever deer. He was always thinking of ways he could use things around him. One day he was walking outside and saw a huge pile of leaves. He had an idea! He decided to use the leaves to make a bed. He carefully arranged them so they were nice and cozy.

He laid down and soon he was snoring. Soon other deer came by to see what was happening. They were amazed! They wanted the same cozy bed too. So the clever deer showed them how to use the leaves to make beds of their own.

They were all so happy and cozy in their beds. They jumped and danced around in joy. The other deer thanked the clever deer for showing them how to use the leaves. It was an amazing day!

Jimmy was walking along the path, carrying a big box. The sun was starting to rise, so the grass was sparkly and golden. Jimmy was feeling a bit uncomfortable because the box was heavy. 

Then Jimmy saw a rabbit hopping along the path. He stopped to admire the little creature with its soft fur. The rabbit stopped hopping and looked up at Jimmy with its big eyes. 

Jimmy asked the rabbit: "Do you want to help me carry this box? It's very heavy."

The rabbit shook its head and said: "I'm sorry, it's too big for me!"

So Jimmy took a deep breath and kept on carrying the box. As the sun got brighter and brighter, Jimmy felt a bit stronger. Eventually, the box was heavy no more and Jimmy reached his destination. 

The sunrise was beautiful, and Jimmy was happy he'd made it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and dress up in pretty clothes. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help clean up her closet. Lily was excited to see what was inside.

As they started to clean, Lily found a box of toys that she had forgotten about. She looked through them and found a teddy bear that she really liked. She told her mom that it was interesting and she wanted to keep it.

Her mom said that the teddy bear was very old and might be valuable. Lily didn't understand what that meant, but she knew she wanted to keep it anyway. She put it on her bed and hugged it tight. From that day on, the teddy bear became her favorite toy.

Charlie and Louis were very good friends. They were both three years old and loved to play together. One day, Charlie had a creative idea. He wanted to play a game with the pole in the backyard.

So, Charlie clapped his hands to get Louis's attention. Once Louis came over, Charlie explained the game to him. He said that they could use the pole to make a castle and then use their imaginations to play a fun game.

Louis was really excited to try the game. He and Charlie grabbed the pole and started to build. They put it in the middle of the yard and imagined that it was their very own castle.

Inside their castle, the boys imagined all kinds of fun things. They pretended to fight dragons and save princesses. They used their imaginations to find ways to overcome any difficult situation.

After a few hours of play, the boys were exhausted. They said goodbye to their castle and clapped their hands one last time. They had had a creative adventure!

Lily and Ben are friends. They live in a big city with many cars and people. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big black dog in the park. The dog is friendly and wants to play.

"Hi, dog!" Lily says. She pets the dog's head. The dog wags its tail.

"Can we run with the dog, mom?" Ben asks. His mom nods and smiles.

"Okay, but be careful. Stay close to us," she says.

Lily and Ben run with the dog. They have fun. The dog runs fast and jumps over the grass. Lily and Ben laugh and follow the dog. They feel happy.

But then, the dog sees a cat. The cat is small and gray. The dog barks and chases the cat. The cat runs away.

"Wait, dog! Come back!" Lily and Ben shout. They run after the dog. But the dog is faster. The dog runs out of the park and into the city.

"Stop, dog! Stop!" Lily and Ben cry. They are scared. The city is loud and busy. There are many cars and people. They can't see the dog.

"Where is the dog?" Lily asks. She holds Ben's hand.

"I don't know," Ben says. He looks around.

They see their moms. Their moms are worried. They run to Lily and Ben and hug them.

"Are you okay?" their moms ask.

"Yes, mom. But the dog is gone," Lily says.

"The dog ran away. We couldn't catch him," Ben says.

Their moms sigh and shake their heads.

"That was a bad dog. He should not run away from his owner," one mom says.

"Maybe he was lost. Maybe he was looking for his home," the other mom says.

Lily and Ben feel sad. They liked the dog. They hope the dog is okay.

"Can we find the dog, mom?" Lily asks.

"Maybe, honey. But it's hard to find a dog in the city. There are many dogs here," her mom says.

"Maybe we can ask someone. Maybe someone knows the dog," Ben says.

"Maybe, sweetie. But we have to go home now. It's getting late," his mom says.

Lily and Ben nod. They say goodbye to the dog in their hearts. They hope the dog finds his home. They hope the dog is happy. They walk with their moms to the bus. They go home. They are tired. They sleep. They dream of the dog.

Tom and Sam were friends. They liked to play with cars and balls. One day, they saw a big cake on the table. It looked yummy. They wanted to eat some.

"Let's take some cake," Tom said. "No one will know."

"But Mom said no cake before dinner," Sam said. "She will be mad."

"Who cares?" Tom said. "She is not here. Come on, it will be fun."

Tom and Sam went to the table. They took a big knife. They cut a big piece of cake. They put it on a plate. They ran to the sofa. They ate the cake. It was sweet and soft. They smiled.

But they did not see the man in the corner. He was bald. He had a big camera. He was taking pictures of them. He worked for a newspaper. He was looking for a story.

He saw Tom and Sam steal the cake. He thought they were bad boys. He took many pictures of them. He wrote a story about them. He called them "The Cake Thieves". He put the story and the pictures in the newspaper.

The next day, Tom and Sam's mom saw the newspaper. She was very angry. She showed them the story and the pictures. She scolded them. She said they were naughty and dishonest. She said they had to say sorry and give back the cake. She said they had no dessert for a week.

Tom and Sam felt very bad. They cried. They wished they had not stolen the cake. They learned their lesson. They never stole again.

Once upon a time there lived a kind and gentle girl. Every day the girl would remains in her home with her mum and dad. She loved them both very much and she knew in her heart that they cared for her.

One summer, the girl went to the park with her family. While they were there, they heard a strange sound coming from the bush. The girl's mum and dad were surprised, so they asked their daughter to go and take a look.

The little girl bravely stepped into the bush and soon discovered a tiny, furry cat. The cat seemed scared and alone, so the girl decided to pick it up. As soon as she did, the cat spoke to her in a gentle voice. It told her that it was a deaf cat, who had been abandoned. The three year old girl felt a little sad, but she wanted to help the cat.

So she and her family decided to remain the cat and look after it. Everyday the girl would spend time with the cat and she soon realised how sweet and loving the cat was. Her heart was warmed and she was happy to have the little deaf cat in her life.

The little girl and the cat remain friends and she knew that the feeling of love and care would remain between them forever.

Maggie went to the park with her mom. It was a sunny day, but Maggie was feeling miserable. Suddenly she saw a beautiful crystal lying in the grass. She ran over to it and picked it up. It shone in the sunlight and Maggie knew it was special.

Maggie was so happy that she ran back to her mom and showed her the crystal. Her mom smiled and hugged her. Maggie was glad to have the crystal that made her happy.

But then Maggie accidentally dropped the crystal and it broke into many pieces. She started to cry. She felt so sad and miserable. Her mom came over and hugged her tight.
