"It is ok", her mom said. Maggie knew that even though the crystal was broken, it had still made her happy for a little time. She dried her eyes, and her mom and her went home. Even though the crystal was broken, Maggie still remembered the wonderful feeling she'd felt when she found it.

Sara and Ben like to play in the park. They run, slide, swing and laugh. They also like to look for pebbles. Pebbles are small and hard and have different colors and shapes. Sara and Ben have a game. They try to find pebbles that remind them of something.

One day, Sara finds a pebble that is orange and round. She shows it to Ben and says, "Look, this pebble reminds me of an orange. It is the same color and shape. Do you like oranges?" Ben nods and says, "Yes, I like oranges. They are sweet and juicy. Can I see your pebble?" Sara gives him the pebble and he holds it in his hand.

Ben looks around and sees a pebble that is white and flat. He picks it up and says, "Look, this pebble reminds me of a paper. It is the same color and shape. Do you like paper?" Sara nods and says, "Yes, I like paper. I can draw and write on it. Can I see your pebble?" Ben gives her the pebble and she holds it in her hand.

They keep playing and finding more pebbles that remind them of different things. They find pebbles that remind them of a leaf, a star, a cookie, a ball and a flower. They have fun and learn new words. They put all their pebbles in a bag and take them home. They show their pebbles to their mom and dad and tell them what they remind them of. Their mom and dad smile and hug them. They are proud of Sara and Ben. They say, "You are very smart and creative. We love you and your pebbles." Sara and Ben are happy and say, "We love you too. And we love our pebbles."

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with a crack in the trunk. They want to see what is inside the crack.

"Let's stand on this rock and look inside the crack," Anna says.

"OK, but be careful," Ben says.

They climb on the rock and peek into the crack. They see a nest with three baby birds. The baby birds are fluffy and yellow. They open their mouths and make noises.

"Wow, look at the baby birds! They are so cute!" Anna says.

"They are impressive! I wonder where their mom is," Ben says.

Suddenly, they hear a loud squawk. They look up and see a big bird flying towards them. It is the mom bird. She is angry and scared. She thinks Anna and Ben want to hurt her babies.

"Uh-oh, we have to go!" Ben says.

They jump off the rock and run away. The mom bird chases them for a while, then goes back to her nest. Anna and Ben are safe, but they are also sorry.

"We didn't mean to bother the baby birds. We just wanted to see them," Anna says.

"Me too. Maybe we can come back another day and watch them from far away," Ben says.

They hug each other and go home. They learned a lesson. They should not touch or disturb wild animals. They should respect and admire them.

Once upon a time, in a land full of trees, there was a little cherry tree. The cherry tree was very sad because it did not have any friends. All the other trees were big and strong, but the cherry tree was small and weak. The cherry tree was envious of the big trees.

One day, the cherry tree felt a tickle in its branches. It was a little spring wind. The wind told the cherry tree not to be sad. The wind said, "You are special because you have sweet cherries that everyone loves." The cherry tree started to feel a little better.

As time went on, the cherry tree grew more and more cherries. All the animals in the land came to eat the cherries and play under the cherry tree. The cherry tree was happy because it had many friends now. The cherry tree learned that being different can be a good thing. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lilly. Lilly was very excited and enthusiastic about learning spells. She wanted to be a powerful magician like her mother.

One day, Lilly asked her mother if she could learn a special spell. Her mother smiled and said, "Yes, I promise I will teach you a special spell."

Lilly was so happy that she jumped up and down. "When can I start?" she asked.

Her mother said, "Tomorrow, I will teach you the spell. Then you can practice until you have it down." 

Lilly was so excited that she couldn't stop smiling. She said to her mother, "I promise I will practice as hard as I can." 

The next day, Lilly started to learn the spell. She quickly got the hang of it and soon was performing the spell with enthusiasm. 

Lilly was so proud of herself for learning the spell so quickly. She hugged her mother and said, "Thank you for teaching me. I promise I will practice every day so I can be the best magician ever."

And that is the story about how Lilly learned a special spell with enthusiasm and kept her promise to practice every day.

Once upon a time, there was a zebra named Ziggy. Ziggy was very patient and liked to eat grass all day. One day, Ziggy saw a little girl walking by and he smiled at her. The little girl was happy to see Ziggy and she said, "Hi, Ziggy! You're so pretty!" 

Ziggy smiled again and said, "Thank you, little girl. Would you like to play with me?" 

The little girl nodded her head and said, "Yes, please!" They played together for a while and had so much fun. The little girl was so happy that she hugged Ziggy and said, "You're my best friend, Ziggy!" 

Ziggy smiled once more and said, "You're my best friend too, little girl." From that day on, Ziggy and the little girl played together every day and had many adventures.

Sam and Max were brothers who lived on a big ranch with many animals. They liked to play with the horses, cows, and dogs, but they did not like to do their chores. One day, their mom told them to clean their room and help with the dishes, but they did not listen. They ran outside and played with the horses instead.

"Look, Max, I can ride this horse without a saddle!" Sam said, jumping on a brown horse.

"Wow, Sam, you are so brave!" Max said, clapping his hands.

But the horse did not like Sam. He bucked and kicked and threw Sam off his back. Sam landed on a pile of cow poop. He was dirty and smelly and hurt.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Sam cried.

Max laughed and pointed at Sam. "Ha, ha, ha! You are so silly, Sam! You look like a cow poop!"

But then, their mom came out and saw them. She was very angry. She scolded them for being naughty and lazy. She took them inside and made them take a bath and clean their room and do the dishes. She also said they could not play with the horses for a week. She punished them for being bad.

Sam and Max were very sad and embarrassed. They wished they had listened to their mom. They learned their lesson the hard way.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little dog named Max. Max had a toy bone that he loved to play with all day. One day, Max was playing with his toy bone when he heard a noise outside. He ran to the window and saw a big cat. Max knew that he had to be brave and protect his toy bone.

Max went outside to face the big cat. The big cat saw Max's toy bone and wanted it too. They both started to pull on the bone with their mouths, but Max didn't want to surrender his favorite toy. Max pulled harder and harder, but the big cat was very strong. Max started to feel tired and worried that he might lose his toy bone.

Then, Max had an idea. He let go of the toy bone with his mouth and quickly grabbed it with his front leg. The big cat was surprised and didn't know what to do. Max used his leg to hold the toy bone and ran back inside his house. The big cat couldn't catch Max, and he saved his toy bone. Max learned that sometimes, being smart is better than being strong. And from that day on, Max never had to worry about surrendering his toy bone again.

Jack and his mom were walking down the street. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. Jack said, "What's that, Mommy?" His mom replied, "It's a fan, Jack. It's making a lot of noise." Jack said, "I'm confused, what's a fan?" His mom picked him up and said, "A fan passes air. It's like a breeze, but stronger." Jack smiled and asked, "Can I touch it?" His mom said, "Of course. Pass your hand slowly over it and see what happens!" Jack slowly passed his hand over the fan and felt a refreshing cool breeze. He was so excited! He said, "Wow! I love the fan!" His mom laughed and said, "Yes, fans are pretty cool!"

Once upon a time, there was a generous horn. It would snap every time someone walked by. One day, a little boy heard the horn snap and he was curious. He snuck around the corner to see what was making the sound.

When he got closer he saw a old, friendly man. The man was holding the generous horn and playing a cheerful tune. The boy was so excited that he started to dance and clap his hands.

The boy asked the man if he could try the generous horn. The man said, "of course, go ahead". The boy smiled and put the horn up to his lips. He took in a deep breath, and then he snapped.

The sound of the generous horn filled the air. Everyone around stopped and smiled. The boy was so proud that he could make the horn snap.

The man smiled and told the boy, "now you are a part of the band". From that day forward, the boy and the man would play the generous horn loud and proud together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to run and play with his friends. One day, he and his friends went to the park to play. They ran around and laughed a lot.

Timmy's mommy told him that he needed to eat healthy food to make his muscles grow big and strong. So, Timmy ate lots of fruits and vegetables.

But sometimes, Timmy could be a little naughty. He would run away from his mommy when she tried to catch him. But when she finally caught him, they would both laugh together.

Once upon a time, there was a hippo. She stayed in the river all day and all night long. One day, the hippo had an idea. She decided to explore the forest near the river.

When the hippo was walking through the forest, she saw a rabbit. The rabbit said, "Hi Hippo, why are you so far from the river?" The hippo replied, "I have come to explore the forest. I am curious to see what this new land has to offer."

The rabbit warned the hippo, "Be careful, there's a lot of danger out here. You should remain in the river." The hippo thanked the rabbit, but she wanted to explore. So the hippo said goodbye and continued her adventure.

Unfortunately, the hippo encountered some trouble in the forest. She encountered a fierce lion. The lion roared and said, "You must leave my forest now!" The hippo was scared and quickly ran back to the river.

When the hippo returned to the river she was glad that she had listened to the rabbit's advice to remain in the river. The moral of the story is that it's important to listen to the advice of others. They might be able to provide us with important insights that could save us from danger.

Once upon a time, there was a generous man. He liked to spoil his daughter with lots of nice things. One day, he had a surprise for her, but it was a secret. He brought her to the stairs, where he had hidden something special. 

The daughter was so excited to see what it was. When she looked under the stairs, she found a new toy! She was so happy and thanked her dad for being so generous. 

The two of them played together with the toy all afternoon. It was so much fun! Every day, the generous dad would spoil his daughter in some special way. 

The end!

Once upon a time, there was an ancient owl. The owl lived alone in the forest and it liked to measure things. Every day, it measured the trees and the animals. It counted the leaves and measured the rocks. One day, it measured a butterfly and the butterfly flew away. The owl kept on measuring things, each one carefully. 

Then one day, it found something amazing! It was a tiny castle made of twigs and leaves. It was so small, the owl had to use a feather to measure it. When the owl opened the door, a group of animals came out. They were so surprised to see the owl measuring their castle. 

The animals asked the owl to measure them too. So the owl flew around them, counting and measuring as it went. When it was done, everyone cheered. They thanked the owl for coming and measuring the castle, and they asked it to come back soon. 

The ancient owl was so happy. It had found a special place in the forest, and it had made some new friends. From then on, the owl measured everything with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jane. Jane was really hungry, and wanted to eat something.
She walked to the kitchen and looked in the fridge. She saw something that made her eyes open wide. It was a weird pizza! She never saw one before.

Jane was excited and picked it up. She leaned over the counter and took a big bite. It was delicious! She ate the whole pizza in no time. 

Once she was done, she felt very full. She leaned back in her chair and smiled a big, happy smile. 

Jane was so thankful to have found the weird pizza. She thought it was the best thing she ever had. From then on, she was always on the lookout for weird pizzas.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she found a shiny rock on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her mom.

"Look, Mommy! I found a pretty rock!" Lily said.

"That's lovely, sweetie," her mom replied. "Let's go inside and wash it off in the sink."

Lily followed her mom inside and watched as she turned on the faucet. She put the rock under the water and gently rubbed it with her fingers. When she was done, she handed it back to Lily.

"Wow! It looks even more beautiful now!" Lily exclaimed.

"Yes, it's the original color," her mom said with a smile.

Lily was so happy with her new treasure and she kept it in her pocket all day long. She loved how it sparkled in the sunlight and how it felt smooth in her hand. She couldn't wait to show it to her friends at preschool the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily found a shiny coin on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

"Look what I got, Timmy! It's a coin!" said Lily.

"Wow, that's so cool! You're so strong for finding it," replied Timmy.

Lily felt proud of herself for being strong and finding the coin. She decided to save it in her piggy bank at home. From that day on, Lily always looked for coins when she played outside with her friends. She wanted to get more coins and become even stronger.

The sun was shining on a fine Sunday. It was the perfect day to fly!

Two birds woke up early to see the sunrise. They were excited to go on an adventure.

The birds flapped their wings and went up, up, up into the sky. They flew over the trees and watched their shadows below.

Suddenly, they saw beautiful butterflies flying around them. As they watched the butterflies, they kept flying higher and higher.

Soon, the birds saw a rainbow ahead. The colors were so bright and pretty! They flew through the rainbow, ready for a new adventure.

They kept flying until they saw the sun set. Then they flew down and landed back in the tree where they started. The birds had a wonderful Sunday together, they were so happy and proud of their adventure!

The sun was shining in the sky and Jenny was feeling so excited. She was waiting with her Mom at the station for the train to arrive. Suddenly they heard the sound of the train coming and Jenny started to feel very anxious. 

"It's almost here, Jenny," said Mom. 

They waited at the station and soon the train arrived. They got on the big train and it slowly started moving. After a while they arrived at their destination, another station.

When they got off the train, Jenny was surprised to see someone she hadn't seen in a very long time - her Grandma! Mom and Grandma were hugging and crying together and Jenny was so happy to see Grandma.

"It's so nice to meet you again, Grandma," said Jenny. Grandma smiled and gave Jenny a big hug. Jenny was so glad that she and Mom had come to the station to meet Grandma. Even though she had been feeling anxious before the train arrived, Jenny was very happy now.

Once upon a time there was a famous balloon. It was big, round and sparkly and it floated in the sky. Its beautiful colours made it stand out from all the other balloons.

One windy day, the balloon got caught in a tree. It couldn't free itself and was stuck.

"Oh no," thought the balloon. "What should I do?"

Just then, a little boy came by. He noticed the balloon and said, "Don't worry, I can help you!"

He went to his garden shed, and came back with a long cable. He grabbed hold of the balloon and carefully attached the cable to it.

"There," the boy said, "now you're free to fly again."

The balloon thanked the boy and floated away. He waved goodbye and watched the balloon go higher and higher until it disappeared into the clouds. The boy smiled as he knew that he'd made the famous balloon very happy.

Once there was a boy named Alex. He was only 3 years old but he was brave. He was scared of monsters but wanted to be bossy and brave. One day his mommy said they were going to a dance. Alex was excited but he was scared too.

When they got to the dance, Alex saw some people dancing. He watched them and wanted to join but he was scared. He sat in a corner and watched everyone. Then something scary happened! A monster jumped out of the shadows!

Everyone screamed and ran away but Alex didn't move. He was brave and he said "Go away scary monster!" The monster was startled and ran away. Everyone looked at Alex and clapped. He was so brave.

The people laughed and danced and Alex joined in. He bounced and twirled and felt like a bossy brave boy. Then he looked up and smiled. He beat the scary monster and had a wonderful time at the dance.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. Jane had a special camera that she liked to take pictures with.

On hot summer days, Jane liked to take her camera and explore the park. She would look around and find interesting things to take pictures of. One day when she was looking around, Jane saw a family of ducks. She snapped some great photos of them with her camera!

As Jane continued exploring the park, she spotted a group of kids playing by a busy street. They all looked like they belonged together. She took a few pictures of the kids, but was careful not to get too close to the busy street.

When Jane got home, she showed her mom all the photos she had taken. Her mom was so proud of her for discovering interesting things, and taking amazing photos of them. 

They both had a lot of fun looking through the pictures, and remembering the fun day Jane had exploring the park!

One day, a little boy named Tim and his dog, Spot, went for a walk. They saw a big tree and wanted to play near it. Tim was happy, but Spot was scared. Spot saw something behind the tree and did not want to go closer.

Tim said to Spot, "Don't be scared, I am here with you." They walked closer to the tree and saw a small bird. The bird had a hurt wing and could not fly. Tim and Spot wanted to help the bird.

They found a soft place for the bird to settle. Tim gave the bird some food, and Spot stayed with the bird on the left side to keep it safe. The bird was not scared anymore because Tim and Spot were there to help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to color with her crayons. One day, she found a pretty picture of a flower and wanted to hang it up on her wall. 

Lily asked her mommy for help and together they got some tape to attach the picture to the wall. Lily was so happy to see her colorful flower on her wall. 

Later that day, Lily was feeling a little sad. She was scared of the thunderstorm outside. Her mommy hugged her and told her to take deep breaths to stay calm. Lily closed her eyes and breathed in and out. Soon, she felt much better and fell asleep with her colorful flower watching over her. The end.

Once there was a girl named Maya. She was three years old. One day, Maya and her mom went to a store. Maya saw a pretty cup. It was bright blue with stars all around. She felt so excited. She asked her mom to buy it for her. 

Mom smiled and said, "Sure, this cup looks great. Let's get it for you."

Maya was so happy she could hardly contain herself. She grabbed the cup and hugged it tight. Then she said thank you to her Mom.

On the way home, Maya held the cup tightly in her hands. She felt so happy and excited, like she was the luckiest girl in the world. When she reached home, she put the cup on her shelf and smiled. It made her feel great.

One day, Tommy was hungry. He looked around his house, but he couldn't find any food. Suddenly, Tommy heard someone call his name. It was his friend Emma. She was inviting Tommy to come visit her family's new building.

"Come on Tommy, let's go! My brothers are building it now," said Emma.

So, Tommy went with Emma. When they got there, the building was almost finished. It was really big and exciting. The brothers had done a great job!

Emma's family was so happy to see Tommy. They invited him to stay for lunch. Tommy was so excited. He ate a big, delicious lunch! After lunch, Emma showed Tommy around the building. She was so proud of her brothers for building it.

It was a great day for Tommy. He was happy to have been invited to a new building and to meet Emma's family. Plus, he was no longer hungry!

Jimmy was an really busy boy. Every day he was looking for adventure.
One day, he was outside playing when a strange big man appeared from behind a tree. He was bald, with a big red nose and a shiny nail on his finger. 
Jimmy was surprised and a little scared, but the man smiled and started to talk to him. He said he was a magical man and could make special things appear just by clicking his nail. 
Jimmy was so excited! The man clicked his nail and magcally, a giant ice cream appeared! Jimmy was so happy he ate the whole thing. 
The magical man waved goodbye and then he was gone. Jimmy never saw him again, but he always remembered the special day.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sarah. She loved to imagine things. One day she imagined that she was standing in front of a big plate of spaghetti. She imagined the spaghetti was long and yummy. It was the best spaghetti ever!

Sarah loved the taste of spaghetti. She wanted to eat it, so she grabbed a fork and started eating. It was so delicious that she ate it all. She was full and happy.

But then she started feeling competitive. She wanted to know if she could eat even more spaghetti! So she imagined a big bowl of spaghetti was in front of her. This time it was even bigger than before! It was a big challenge for Sarah.

Sarah had to be brave and eat it all. But she was brave and she ate the whole bowl of spaghetti! She was so proud of herself. She had managed to eat the biggest bowl of spaghetti!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, he found a caterpillar crawling on the ground. 

Tim said, "Hello little caterpillar, what are you doing?" 

The caterpillar replied, "I am trying to be a butterfly. I need to eat lots of leaves and grow big and thick." 

Tim watched as the caterpillar ate and ate. Soon, the caterpillar grew an inch longer and Tim exclaimed, "Wow, you're getting bigger!" 

The caterpillar smiled and said, "Yes, I am growing so I can be a beautiful butterfly one day." Tim was so happy to have made a new friend and couldn't wait to see the caterpillar transform into a butterfly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, she was feeling very cold in her bed. So, she asked her mommy to bring her a blanket. Her mommy brought her a cozy blanket that made her feel warm and happy.

As she was snuggling under her blanket, she started to imagine a magical world where everything was made of candy. She imagined candy trees, candy houses, and candy animals. It was a very fun and sweet dream.

In the morning, Lily woke up and saw that her blanket was not just any blanket. It was a special blanket that could make her dreams come true. She felt very lucky and grateful to have such a modest and wonderful blanket. From that day on, she always took her blanket with her wherever she went, just in case she wanted to start dreaming again.

Once upon a time there was a brave boy named Tom. Tom was playing in the park when he heard a strange voice behind him. He turned around curiously, and saw an old man.

The old man asked him what his name was. Tom was brave, and he didn't want to be scared, so he told the old man his name.

The old man smiled and told Tom his name was George. Tom smiled and said hello. George asked him if he wanted to play a game.

Tom said yes and they both went to a nearby tree. George asked Tom to close his eyes. Tom was a bit scared, but he was brave and so he did as George said.

When Tom opened his eyes, he saw that George had a present for him! It was a toy car. Tom was excited and thanked George for the present.

George asked Tom what the kindest thing he'd ever done was. Tom thought for a moment, and then replied that he'd once helped a bird who had hurt its wing.

George told Tom he'd been very brave and kind. Tom smiled, thanked George and ran off to play with his new car.

Once upon a time there was a bear. He was a nice bear and wanted to be fair. He wanted to give everyone the same.

The bear had an idea, he wanted to take a stick and attach something special to the end. He found some beautiful ribbons, cut them into small pieces and attached one piece to the end of the stick. 

He called his friends and they all lined up. The bear handed out the stick with the ribbon attached to the end and he said, "This is so that everyone gets the same and it will be fair." 

The bear's friends were so happy, they hugged the bear and thanked him for being so kind. From that day onwards, everyone was happy and fair.

Once upon a time two friends, Joe and Jenny, were out at the pond having a grand time.

Joe was splashing in the water, lying on his back and feeling the sunshine on his face. Jenny was looking for crickets.

Jenny eventually found one and she shouted to Joe, "Look Joe!"

Joe opened his eyes and saw the small cricket with its antennae twitching.

Joe said, "He's so distant!"

Jenny giggled. Then she scooped up the cricket in her little hand and said, "Let's splash!"

Joe and Jenny both ran into the pond and started splashing each other. 

In his mind, Joe imagined they were in a distant land, free and happy, just the two of them.

Little Andy was playing in the garden one sunny day when he heard a loud trumpet. He trotted over to see what it was. He arrived in the field, and noticed a bright yellow duck playing a trumpet. The duck quacked, "Hi Andy! Would you like to play with me? I'm practising to be a trumpet player!" Andy giggled and replied, "Yes, I would!"

The duck smiled, and held out her trumpet for Andy. She said, "Go on, have a try. Just push your lips together and blow." Andy put his lips together and blew gently. To his surprise, out came a loud sound! The duck laughed, "Good job! Keep blowing like that and you'll get better. Let's have a game. Ready, set, go!"

The duck started to quack and Andy had to use his trumpet to keep up with the quacks. Whenever the duck quacked, Andy had to yield a note from his trumpet. They carried on playing like this for a while and Andy became more and more alert. He was getting better at playing the trumpet. After a while, they both got tired and the duck said it was time to go. Andy thanked her for teaching him how to play the trumpet and promised to come back again. He waved goodbye and ran off, feeling very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing baseball with his friends. They would throw the ball and hit it with a bat. Timmy's favorite player was his dad. He was the best at hitting the ball.

One day, Timmy and his friends went to the park to play baseball. They chose a spot to play and started to create their own field. They used sticks and rocks to make the bases. Timmy was in charge of making the pitcher's mound. He dug a hole and filled it with dirt.

As they were playing, Timmy's dad came to watch. He saw that the field was filthy and needed some cleaning. He asked Timmy and his friends if they wanted to help him clean it up. They all said yes and started picking up the trash and throwing it away.

After they finished cleaning, Timmy's dad noticed that the field looked much better. He said, "Now we have a clean field to play on." Timmy and his friends were happy and continued playing baseball. From that day on, they made sure to keep their field clean so they could play on it every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jake. Jake was three years old and he loved to do two things: point and eat peanuts. One day, he was walking down the street with his mother, when he saw something very incredible. It was a large circus tent! He stopped and pointed at the tent and said, "Look, Mommy! What's that?" His mother replied, "That is a circus tent, Jake." Jake was so excited he jumped up and down and shouted, "I want to go to the circus!" 

So, his mother took him on a little adventure to the circus that day. He saw a big elephant and little monkeys, but what he was waiting for were the peanuts. By the time they made it to the peanut stand, Jake was jumping up and down like a little popcorn. He couldn't believe it! The peanuts looked incredible! He asked the man for a bag, and the man gave him a handful of peanuts. Then Jake pointed to the sky and shouted with joy, "Yay, peanuts!" 

Jake has had an incredible day with his mom and his peanuts. He pointed at the circus tent one last time before they went back home. From that day onwards, Jake would never forget the incredible and magical day he spent at the circus.

One sunny day, Jessi went for a walk in the forest. She saw a furry fox and asked it what it was doing. The fox didn't say anything, but it just shrugged. Jessi figured it was looking for food in the soil. 

Jessi wanted to help the fox, so she opened her backpack and took out an apple. She held it out to the fox and said, "Here you go!" 

The fox didn't move. Jessi wondered why, so she said, "It's okay. You can have it." 

The fox still didn't move. So Jessi shrugged and said, "Well, I guess you don't want it."

The fox quickly took the apple from Jessi's hand and ran away. Jessi smiled and waved goodbye. She had made a new furry friend in the forest!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures with her mom and dad. One day, they went for a drive in the car. Dad had a special paper called a license that allowed him to drive the car. 

As they drove down the road, Lily saw something unusual on the side of the street. It was a big, purple balloon! She asked her mom and dad if they could stop and get it. Dad pulled over and got out of the car. He tried to grab the balloon, but it suddenly disappeared! 

Lily was sad that she couldn't have the balloon, but she was also confused. Where did it go? Mom and dad explained that sometimes things can disappear and we don't know where they go. They continued on their drive, but Lily couldn't stop thinking about the unusual disappearing balloon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his favorite toy car. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy wanted to play with Timmy's toy car, but Timmy didn't want to share.

"I want to play with my car!" said Timmy.

"But I want to play too," said Billy.

Timmy got angry and decided to destroy his toy car so that Billy couldn't play with it. He hit it with a thick stick and it broke into pieces. Suddenly, a spark flew out of the broken car and started a fire. The fire grew bigger and bigger until it destroyed Timmy's entire house.

Timmy and Billy were very scared as they watched the fire destroy everything they knew. They knew they had made a big mistake by not sharing and playing nicely. From that day on, Timmy and Billy learned to always share and be kind to each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing with her toys when she heard a loud noise. She looked out the window and saw a big, scary dog. Lily was frightened and ran to her mom. 

"Mommy, I'm scared!" Lily cried. 

"It's okay, sweetie," her mom said, picking her up. "Let's go inside and I'll make you some cookies." 

Lily felt better and went to the kitchen with her mom. While her mom was cutting the cookies, Lily touched her ear and said, "Mommy, my ear hurts." 

Her mom looked at her ear and saw a little scratch. She put a band-aid on it and gave Lily a cookie. Lily smiled and forgot all about the scary dog.

Today Ann and Toby walked to the park. Ann was very happy. When they arrived, Toby saw a pink bird. He pointed excitedly and said "Look Ann"! 

Ann was also excited to see the pink bird. Ann and Toby watched the little bird fly around. Suddenly, Ann and Toby saw two more pink birds, but these birds were fighting. They were squawking and trying to peck each other. 

Ann was scared and wanted to go home, but Toby was fascinated by the birds. He wanted to stay and watch. Ann said no, they had to leave. So, Ann and Toby turned and started to walk away from the park. 

Ann and Toby talked about the pink birds all the way home. They were both very excited about the fight they saw. Ann and Toby liked the pretty pink birds and still talk about them today.

Once upon a time there was a quiet stove. It was all alone in the corner of the kitchen. The stove felt so sad. One day, the stove had an idea. He decided to invite all his friends to his house.

The stove went outside and looked around. He saw a table, a chair and a lamp. He invited all of them to his house and they quickly accepted. 

The new friends were all excited to see each other. Then they all united around the stove. They talked, laughed and sang together. Finally, the stove was no longer sad. It was happy to be with all its friends.

From then on, everyone in the kitchen was happy and united. They spent many happy days together and the stove was never lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help wash the dishes. Timmy didn't want to because he thought it was a bad job. 

"Timmy, please help me wash the dishes," said Timmy's mom.

"I don't want to. It's a bad job," replied Timmy.

"It's not a bad job. It's an important job. We need clean dishes to eat off of," explained Timmy's mom.

Timmy thought about it and decided to help his mom wash the dishes. He realized it wasn't such a bad job after all.

Henry had a car. Every day he put fuel in it to make it go faster. 

One day, Henry wanted to make his car go even faster. So he asked his friend Lisa for some help.

"Can you help me make my car go faster?" Henry asked.

"Yes," said Lisa. "I think if we put more fuel in it, we can improve it."

So Lisa and Henry put more fuel in the car, and then they went for a drive. The car went faster than ever, and Henry was very happy.

But then something strange happened. The smell from the car became sour.

"That's strange," said Henry. "What's happening?"

"I think the fuel isn't the right kind," said Lisa. "We need to get some better fuel so we can improve the car again."

So they went and got better fuel, and Henry put it in the car. Now the car ran smoother and faster than ever, and it smelled nice too. 

Henry and Lisa were very happy. They had improved Henry's car, and it was working perfectly.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a hotel. This hotel was not a good hotel. People said it was a bad hotel. In the hotel, there lived a cat named Max.

One day, Max saw a big cup on the floor. It was full of a yummy drink. Max wanted to drink it. He said, "I want to drink this yummy drink!" So, Max started to drink the drink from the cup.

Suddenly, a big dog named Sam came into the hotel. Sam saw Max drinking the drink. Sam was not happy. He said, "That is my drink! You are a bad cat!" Sam chased Max out of the hotel. Max was sad and thirsty. He could not drink the yummy drink anymore, and he had to find a new place to live.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But today, they have to go to a big event with their mom and dad. The event is for their dad's work. Sara and Ben do not want to go. They think it will be boring and noisy.

"Mom, can we stay home?" Sara asks.

"No, you have to come with us. It will be fun, I promise. You will meet new people and see new things," Mom says.

"But we like our toys. We do not like new people. They are scary and loud," Ben says.

"Please, do not be silly. You have to be polite and nice. Dad is very proud of his work and he wants to show you off. Maybe you will find some other kids to play with there," Mom says.

Sara and Ben sigh. They put on their coats and shoes. They follow Mom and Dad to the car. They are not happy.

The event is in a big hall. There are many people there. They are all wearing fancy clothes and talking and laughing. Sara and Ben feel shy and small. They hold Mom and Dad's hands. They see a table with cookies and juice. They want some.

"Can we have some cookies, Mom?" Sara asks.

"Sure, but only one each. And be careful not to spill your juice," Mom says.

Sara and Ben take a cookie and a cup of juice. They look around for a place to sit. They see a corner with some chairs and a big plant. They go there.

They eat their cookies and drink their juice. They are still bored. They wish they had their toys. They see a big red ball on the floor. It looks like fun.

"Look, a ball!" Ben says.

"Let's play with it!" Sara says.

They put down their cups and run to the ball. They kick it and throw it and catch it. They laugh and giggle. They do not see the man who is standing next to the ball. He is holding a microphone. He is about to speak to the people.

"Hello, everyone. Thank you for coming to this important event. I am very honored to introduce our guest speaker, who is a very distinguished and respected leader in our field. He is also my boss and my friend. Please welcome..." the man says.

But before he can finish, the ball hits him in the face. He drops the microphone. It makes a loud noise. Everyone looks at him. They see Sara and Ben. They are shocked and angry.

"Who are these kids? How did they get here? What are they doing?" the people say.

Sara and Ben are scared. They did not mean to hurt the man. They did not know he was there. They run back to their corner. They hide behind the plant. They cry.

Mom and Dad hear the noise. They see what happened. They are embarrassed and sorry. They go to the man. They apologize. They go to Sara and Ben. They hug them. They scold them.

"What were you thinking? You cannot play with a ball here. You cannot interrupt the speech. You cannot hit the man. You have to be quiet and respectful. You have to say sorry," Mom and Dad say.

Sara and Ben say sorry. They are very sorry. They do not like the event. They do not like the people. They do not like the ball. They want to go home. They want their toys. They want to play in their room. They hope the event will end soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard with her favorite toy, a stuffed bunny named Binky. One day, while playing, Binky accidentally fell over the fence and into the neighbor's yard.

Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, she saw an adorable puppy named Max marching towards her. Max asked, "What's wrong, Lily?"

Lily told Max about Binky and how he was stuck in the neighbor's yard. Max offered to help and together they marched over to the fence. Max was able to jump over the fence and retrieve Binky. Lily was so happy and thanked Max for his help. From then on, Max and Lily became the best of friends and played together every day in the backyard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat sweet and juicy fruits, but she didn't like prunes. One day, her mommy gave her a prune to eat, but she refused to eat it. She said, "I don't want to eat this prune, mommy. It's not sweet and juicy like the other fruits."

Her mommy told her that she needed to eat it because it was good for her tummy. But Lily didn't want to accept it. She cried and said, "No, no, no!" Her mommy tried to explain to her that sometimes we need to eat things we don't like to be healthy and strong.

Finally, Lily decided to be a big girl and accept the prune. She took a bite and realized it wasn't so bad after all. She even said, "This prune is pretty tasty!" Her mommy was proud of her for trying something new and being tidy by cleaning up after herself. From that day on, Lily learned to accept new foods and be a healthy and strong little girl.

One day, a little girl named Sally was walking in the park. She had a perfect day planned. As she walked, she noticed a beautiful flower. She walked over to it and carefully picked it. She reached into her pocket and pulled out a paintbrush. As she carefully painted the flower, she heard a tiny voice. "Hey Sally!".

Sally looked around and saw a tiny fairy. The fairy smiled at Sally and said, "I would like to give you a gift. I know the perfect word, do you want to hear it?" Sally nodded eagerly.

The fairy said her gift was to pinch her nose three times and say the word â€œstarlightâ€. Sally thanked the fairy and did as she said. Suddenly, there was a little twinkle in the air and a star appeared right above her. Sally was so excited that she gave the fairy a big hug.

The fairy smiled and said, "Remember, starlight is a perfect word to make your wishes come true!". Sally thanked the fairy and said goodbye. She carefully put the flower in her pocket, and skipped off to continue her perfect day.

Adam lived in a fancy house near a swamp. Every day he would go out and explore the swamp, looking for treasure and looking for new adventures. His parents encouraged him to explore and make new friends, to help him learn and grow. 

One afternoon, Adam came home unusually excited. He ran straight to his mom to tell her about a new discovery he had made. 

"Mom," he said, "I met a crocodile today and he said he wanted to be my friend!" 

His mom smiled and encouraged him, telling him that making new friends was a great way to have fun in the swamp. Adam thanked his mom and ran back to the swamp, ready to have adventures with his new friend.

Once upon a time, there lived a girl. She was just three years old and very tidy. Every day, she would clean up her room and make sure everything was in its place. One day, she was cleaning her room when she saw something shiny. She picked it up and saw it was a penny!

She was so excited. She wanted to show it to her mom. She shouted: "Mom! Look!"

Her mom came in. The girl showed her the penny. Her mom smiled and said, "Wow! What a tidy penny. You can keep it safe in your room."

The girl nodded, and put the penny in her drawer. Then, she shut the drawer tightly.

The girl was so happy that she had a shiny penny. She hugged it and thanked her mom for letting her keep it. From then on, she kept her room very tidy so she could keep her penny safe.

Lily liked to create things with her play-dough. She made balls, snakes, flowers and cakes. She was very proud of her creations and showed them to her mom and dad.

One day, she wanted to make something new. She looked around the kitchen and saw a big piece of beef on the counter. It was warm and red and smelled good. Lily thought it would be fun to make a play-dough beef. She took some brown play-dough and shaped it like the beef. She put some green play-dough on top to make parsley. She smiled and put her play-dough beef next to the real beef.

But then, her big brother Tom came into the kitchen. He was hungry and wanted a snack. He saw the two pieces of beef and thought they were both real. He grabbed the play-dough beef and took a big bite. He spat it out and made a face. He was angry and yelled at Lily.

"Lily, this is not beef, this is play-dough! You tricked me! You are a bad sister!"

Lily was scared and sad. She did not mean to trick Tom. She just wanted to create something new. She started to cry and ran to her mom.

Mom heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw the play-dough beef and the real beef and understood what happened. She hugged Lily and comforted her.

"Lily, it's okay. You did not do anything wrong. You were just playing and being creative. Tom did not know it was play-dough. He was just hungry and made a mistake. He is sorry, right Tom?"

Tom felt bad for making Lily cry. He realized she was not a bad sister. He was just a silly brother. He apologized to Lily and gave her a hug.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to yell at you. You are a good sister. You are very creative. Can I play with your play-dough too?"

Lily smiled and nodded. She forgave Tom and shared her play-dough with him. They played together and made more things. They had fun and were happy. Mom smiled and watched them. She was proud of her children. She put the real beef in the oven and made a warm and yummy dinner for them.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah was so shy that she would never speak up. Nobody knew what she was like or what she was thinking.

One day Cynthia, Sarah's best friend, came over. Cynthia asked Sarah if they could bake something together. Sarah was scared, but she said yes. 

They gathered all the ingredients, and carefully measured them. They placed everything into the bowl, and stirred until it was nice and creamy. Then they put it all into the oven.

The smell was amazing! Cynthia and Sarah waited until the timer buzzed to a big zero. Out came the delicious cake. It was golden brown, and smelled so good.

Cynthia and Sarah smiled at each other. They were so happy. That day, Sarah had become braver and less shy. They shared the cake and enjoyed it together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went out to play even though it was raining. She didn't have an umbrella, so she got all wet.

Lily's mom saw her and said, "Oh no, Lily! You're all wet! You'll catch a cold and suffer."

Lily replied, "I don't hurt, Mommy. I just got wet. Can I still play outside?"

Her mom said, "No, Lily. You have to come inside and dry off. You don't want to suffer from being sick." So, Lily went inside and changed into dry clothes. She felt much better and was happy to play inside with her toys.

Honey was very excited. She was outside with Mommy and Daddy who had a big surprise for her. Suddenly, a funny looking bike appeared. It had two wheels and one seat and a funny round thing on the front. Honey climbed on and Daddy told her to grab the funny round thing, which was the pedal. She tried to push it and the bike started moving forward. Honey was so delighted; she couldn't believe she was riding a bike. 

Mommy and Daddy took her to the ice cream parlor for a delicious treat. Honey had a bubble gum flavored ice cream and was amazed how yummy it was. She gobbled it up, just in time to ride her bike home. Honey was so proud of herself for riding her bike and for eating her delicious ice-cream. As she pedaled back home with Mommy and Daddy following close behind, Honey smiled from ear to ear.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved parties. But today, her party was disgusting. Food was everywhere and it looked very messy. The girl was sad and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, an idea came to her. She ran to the kitchen, grabbed a cloth and some soap, and started to wipe the mess away. Wipe, wipe, wipe. She worked very hard and soon the mess was gone.

The girl was happy and wanted to call her friends to come back and enjoy the party. When they arrived, they all had a wonderful time because the girl had successfully wiped away the disgusting mess!

Once upon a time, there was an ancient vegetable garden. In the garden there grew lots of juicy and delicious vegetables.

One day a little girl named Anna came to the garden. She was wearing a yellow dress and had a big smile on her face. She was so excited because she had never seen such a beautiful vegetable garden before.

Anna started picking some of the juiciest vegetables she could find. But then suddenly, she heard an ear-piercing scream coming from the garden. Startled, she dropped her basket of veggies and quickly looked around to see what was happening.

Just a few feet away were two little boys who were screaming with excitement. They had seen the biggest carrot they had ever seen in their lives! Anna couldn't help but smile as the two boys happily ran towards the ancient carrot.

And that's how Anna discovered the wonderful ancient vegetable garden.

Once there was a messy lizard. He wanted to move around the garden. He saw a beautiful flower and said to himself, "I can move that way." So the lizard moved towards the flower. 

He saw a big tree and said to himself, "I can move that way." So the lizard moved towards the tree. 

Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was a ladybug. The ladybug said, "Where are you going?" The lizard said, "I'm moving around the garden." 

The ladybug said, "Would you like help?" The lizard said, "Yes please!" So the ladybug and the lizard moved around the garden together. 

They found a muddy puddle and the ladybug said, "Let's move that way." So they moved towards the puddle and made a mess. But they had a lot of fun!

One day, Sam was walking in the park. He saw a wide green field, with a carrot patch surrounded by a fence. He wanted to pick some carrots, so he ran over to the patch. But when he got there, he saw that the fence was too high. He wanted to quit, so he started crying. 

Just then, he heard a voice. He looked around and saw an old man. The man took Sam's hand, and then he walked to the other side of the carrot patch. There was a wide gate, and the old man opened it for Sam.

Sam was so happy; he could finally pick the carrots. He ran into the patch and grabbed his basket. Soon he was picking carrots like crazy. He ate some, too; they were so sweet!

When the basket was full, it was time for Sam to quit. He gave the man a big hug, thanked him, and then walked back home. He had a big basket of carrots and the best adventure ever!

Sam was a curious boy who liked to examine everything he saw. One day, he found a big onion in the kitchen. He wondered what it was and how it smelled. He picked up the onion and peeled off the brown skin. He saw many white layers inside.

He wanted to know more, so he brought the onion to his nose and sniffed it. It smelled very strong and made his eyes water. He sneezed and rubbed his eyes. He felt a burning pain in his eyes and nose. He dropped the onion and cried.

His mom heard him and ran to the kitchen. She saw him holding his face and the onion on the floor. She knew what happened and felt sorry for him. She hugged him and took him to the sink. She washed his eyes and nose with water. She told him the onion was a food that made people cry. She said he should not examine it with his nose. She gave him a cookie and a kiss.

Sam learned his lesson and never examined an onion again. He still liked to be curious, but he was more careful. He asked his mom before he touched anything new. He did not want to cry or hurt himself again. He was a smart boy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy aeroplane. He would pretend to fly it up high in the sky and make loud airplane noises. One day, Timmy's toy aeroplane got dirty because he played with it in the mud. 

Timmy's mom saw that the toy aeroplane was dirty and told him that they needed to clean it. So, they went to the kitchen sink and washed it with soap and water. After it was clean, Timmy wanted to play with it again, but his mom said it was time to go outside and sail his toy boat in the pond. 

Timmy was sad that he couldn't play with his toy aeroplane anymore, but he had fun sailing his toy boat in the pond. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Max. She had an incredible pole that she liked to use to adventure with. Every day, Max would borrow her pole and go on a new adventure in the woods. 

One day, while Max was exploring, she noticed something strange. Someone had borrowed her pole and was not bringing it back! Max was very upset and did not know what to do. 

The next day, Max decided to follow the clues she had noticed to find out who had borrowed her pole. She followed the clues until they led to a mysterious old house.

Max bravely knocked on the door. To her surprise, an incredible shape-shifting dragon answered. It seemed to be using Max's pole to fly around!

Max politely asked the dragon to return her pole. The dragon was so surprised by Max's courage that it decided to give it back. Max was so relieved and thanked the dragon for returning her pole. 

Max learned an important lesson that day; it pays to be brave!

Once upon a time, in a small house, lived a girl named Lily. She loved tea very much. Every day, she would drink tea with her mom and dad. They would sit and laugh together. They were a very happy family.

One day, a big, fearful bird saw Lily's tea. The bird wanted the tea for itself. So, when Lily was not looking, the bird flew down and stole her tea. Lily was very sad. She did not know what to do. Her mom and dad told her not to be sad, but Lily missed her tea.

The next day, Lily saw the bird again. She told the bird that stealing was bad. The bird felt sorry and gave the tea back to Lily. From that day on, the bird never stole again. Lily, her mom, and her dad were happy again. They learned that it was important to be kind and not to steal from others.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Bob and Jane. They were very close and liked to play together. One day, they were playing in the dark woods. Bob suddenly stumbled upon a funny-looking rock, and he asked Jane to come take a look.

When Jane saw the rock, she said, "This is the start of something special!" Bob agreed, and they decided to unite the funny-looking rock with the trees around it. 

Jane said, "Let's make a campfire. That way, we can stay warm in the dark woods." 

Bob and Jane got together the twigs and pieces of wood and put them around the rock. Then, Bob looked in his pocket and found a big, red match. He struck the match and the campfire came to life!

Bob and Jane laughed and shared stories by the campfire that night. They were happy to be so united in the dark woods. The start of this wonderful adventure will not be forgotten.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane had a friend named Joe who was very selfish. Every time Joe would come over to play, he would take all of Jane's toys without asking and leave her nothing to play with.

This made Jane very sad, so she would weep. But she was too scared to tell Joe how she felt.

One day Joe came over with a new toy: it was a spike. He showed it off to Jane and then took away all of her toys again. Jane stared down at the ground and her eyes filled with tears.

Joe saw this and started to feel a little bit guilty. He offered Jane the spike so they could both play together. Jane smiled and hugged it tight.

Joe saw that Jane was happy, and felt much better. From then on, Joe was a lot less selfish and they both had lots of fun playing together!

Once upon a time, there was a sour apple. The apple was angry and wanted to go on an adventure. It saw a friendly bird and asked, â€œDo you have some string?â€ The bird said, â€œYes, I do! Here you goâ€.

The apple took the string and zipped it around his body. Then, he said goodbye to the bird and flew away. He zoomed through the air, faster and faster. As he flew, he saw other animals, like a bear and a fox.

When the apple finished his adventure, he found himself back in the same place he started. He flew around the tree a few more times and then un-zipped his string. He smiled and said, â€œThat was fun!â€

Once upon a time, there was a brown bird who lived in a tree. One day, the bird heard a strange noise coming from far away. At first, the bird did not recognize the noise, but then it realized it was the sound of a telephone ringing!

The bird flew away to find the telephone. It flew over a lake, a flowery meadow and a dark forest before finally spotting the telephone in a nearby field. The bird landed and looked around, but couldn't find anyone around. 

It tapped the telephone with its beak, wondering what to do next. Suddenly, the telephone stopped ringing and started to make different sounds. Puzzled, the bird stepped back and listened. After a few seconds, it recognized a voice speaking. The bird thought it was the most wonderful thing it had ever heard!

Tim and Lily were going on a trip with Mom and Dad. They were very happy. They packed their bags and toys and got in the car. Mom said, "We are going to the lake. It is very big and blue. You can swim and play there."

Tim and Lily liked the lake. They had been there before. They remembered the fish and the ducks and the sand. They wanted to see them again. They looked out the window and saw the trees and the hills and the sky. They sang songs and played games.

But then the car made a loud noise. It stopped on the road. Mom and Dad got out and looked at the car. They looked worried. Tim and Lily stayed in the car. They did not know what was wrong. They felt scared.

Dad came back and said, "The car is broken. We have to wait for help. It may take a long time. I'm sorry, kids. We may not get to the lake today."

Tim and Lily felt sad. They wanted to go to the lake. They did not want to wait in the car. They did not want to miss the fun. They started to cry.

Mom came back and said, "Don't cry, kids. We can still have fun. We can tell stories and draw pictures and eat snacks. We can make the best of it. We can remain happy and hopeful. Maybe we can go to the lake tomorrow."

Tim and Lily wiped their tears. They listened to Mom. They decided to try to have fun. They told stories and drew pictures and ate snacks. They laughed and smiled. They remained happy and hopeful. They hoped to go to the lake tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dream about purple flowers and butterflies. One night, she had a dream about a big tiger. 

In her dream, the tiger was very friendly and they played together. When she woke up, she told her mommy about her dream. "Mommy, I had a dream about a tiger. He was purple and we played together," Lily said. 

Her mommy smiled and said, "That sounds like a fun dream, Lily. Tigers are big and strong, but they can also be very gentle." Lily smiled and said, "Yes, he was very gentle in my dream." 

From that day on, Lily loved to dream about the purple tiger. She would tell her friends about her dream and they would all smile and listen. Lily knew that dreams can come true and that anything is possible in her imagination.

Once upon a time, there was an old lady. She had a big book with lots of words called a dictionary. Every day, she would read it to learn new words. 

One day, a little girl came to visit the old lady. The girl saw the dictionary and asked what it was. The old lady said, "It's a big book with lots of words to help me learn." 

The little girl was curious and asked if she could read it too. The old lady smiled and said, "Of course, you can read it too. It's never too early or too late to learn new words." 

And so, the little girl and the old lady sat together and read the dictionary, learning new words and having fun. From that day on, the little girl loved to read and learn new things.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. They were having fun and laughing.

But then they saw a big cat with spots on its fur. It was a leopard. The leopard was hungry and looking for food. It saw Tom and Lily and their ball. It wanted to eat them.

"Look, Lily, a big cat!" Tom said. "It is incredible!"

"No, Tom, it is not a cat, it is a leopard!" Lily said. "It is dangerous! We have to run!"

But it was too late. The leopard was faster than them. It jumped on Tom and bit him. Tom screamed and dropped the ball. Lily was scared and tried to run away. But the leopard saw her and chased her. It caught her and bit her too. Lily screamed and cried.

The leopard ate Tom and Lily and their ball. It was full and happy. It left the park and went back to the forest. Nobody saw what happened. Nobody helped Tom and Lily. They were gone. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big pig. The pig was very colorful, with pink and purple spots all over its body. The pig liked to play in the mud and eat apples. One day, the pig finished eating all the apples in the orchard. The pig was very happy and went to take a nap in the shade of a big tree.

Lily was shy. She did not like to talk to new people. She liked to play with her dolls and make things with yarn. She had a big box of yarn in many colors.

One day, she saw a new girl in her class. Her name was Anna. Anna had a big smile and long brown hair. She wore a pretty sweater with flowers on it. Lily liked her sweater, but she was too shy to say hello.

At recess, Lily sat on a bench and took out some yarn. She wanted to make a sweater for her doll. She knew how to make loops and knots with the yarn. She liked to see the sweater grow.

Anna saw Lily and walked over to her. She said, "Hi, I'm Anna. What are you making?"

Lily looked up and felt scared. She did not know what to say. She held her yarn and her doll.

Anna smiled and said, "Is that a sweater for your doll? It's very nice. I like to make things with yarn, too. Can I sit with you and make something?"

Lily nodded and moved over a little. She felt a bit less shy. She said, "I'm Lily. This is my doll, Rose. What do you want to make?"

Anna said, "Maybe I can make a hat for my doll, Daisy. She has a blue dress. What color do you have?"

Lily said, "I have blue, too. And pink, and yellow, and green. You can use any color you want."

Anna said, "Thank you. You are very kind. Can we be friends?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, we can be friends."

They sat together and made things with yarn. They talked and laughed. Lily was not shy anymore. She was happy. She had a new friend.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jane. Jane loved to go outside and play all day. One day outside it was so, so hot. Jane felt like she was melting! She wanted to cool off, so she decided to take a swim. 

Jane grabbed her trusty, yellow comb and started to move quickly to the lake. She was moving so fast, the wind blew through her hair. When she arrived at the lake, she plopped in the cool water and swam around for a while.

After her swim, Jane got out of the lake and grabbed her comb. She combed her wet hair and then she started to move back home. Jane could feel the warmth of the sun as she moved and kicked up sand with her feet. 

When Jane arrived back home, she was tired and happy. She had a fun day in the hot sun and was ready to get some rest. The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Brianna. She was only three years old and loved to play outside with her friends. Every day, she would support them to do something fun, like drawing or skipping.

One day, Brianna was feeling a bit upset. She wanted to eat a sausage but she had none in her kitchen. She asked her mom if she could have a sausage, but her mom said no. Brianna was very upset and went to find her friends to make her feel better.

Her friends gave her lots of support and made her feel better. They all went to the store together and bought some sausages for Brianna. She was so happy and was smiling from ear to ear.

From that day on, Brianna and her friends always supported each other and had lots of fun together. They always ate sausages and never got upset again!

Once there was a little boy named Bobby. Bobby was three-years-old and very lazy. He wanted to explore the sky, so he lay down in the grass and stared up above.

Suddenly, he saw something streak across the sky. Bobby eventually figured out that it was a comet. He was so amazed that he wished he could touch it!

Then a magical thing happened. A star flew down from the sky and was right in front of Bobby. It sparkled and glowed and Bobby was so surprised. The star said something to him. It said, â€œI am here to heal you.â€

Bobby was so happy! He felt like he had been blessed by this magical star. He knew that the comet and the star were somehow connected and he believed in their power to heal him.

And so, Bobby was healed in his heart and he felt better in his soul. His laziness had disappeared and he now felt motivated to explore the sky. He thanked the comet and the star and said goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and see all the pretty flowers. One day, she saw a mysterious box on the sidewalk. She wondered what was inside. 

Lily decided to trade her favorite toy for the mysterious box. When she opened it, she saw a beautiful necklace with a shiny diamond. She was so happy! 

But then, Lily realized that the necklace belonged to her neighbor. She felt bad for trading for something that wasn't hers. So, she went to her neighbor and gave back the necklace. Her neighbor was happy and gave Lily a big hug. 

From that day on, Lily learned that it's not good to trade for things that don't belong to you. She continued to see all the pretty flowers outside and played with her favorite toy.

Sara was a girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a doll, a ball, a car and a bear. She played with them every day in her room. She made them talk to each other and have fun.

One day, Sara was playing with her bear. She pretended that he was her friend and they went to the park. She said, "Hello, bear. Do you want to go on the slide?" The bear nodded and said, "Yes, Sara. I like the slide. It is fast and fun." Sara smiled and took the bear to the slide. She put him on the top and pushed him down. The bear laughed and said, "Whee! That was fun. Thank you, Sara."

Sara and the bear played on the slide for a long time. They also played on the swings, the seesaw and the sandbox. They had a lot of fun. But soon, Sara felt tired. She yawned and said, "I am sleepy, bear. Let's go home." The bear yawned too and said, "Me too, Sara. Let's go home and take a nap."

Sara and the bear walked back to her room. They saw that Sara's mom was waiting for them. She said, "Hello, Sara. Hello, bear. Did you have fun at the park?" Sara nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We had fun. But we are sleepy now. Can we take a nap?" Sara's mom smiled and said, "Of course, Sara. You can take a nap. But first, you need to wash your hands and face. You are dirty and smelly from playing." Sara said, "Okay, mom. I will wash my hands and face. But what about the bear? He is dirty and smelly too." Sara's mom said, "Don't worry, Sara. I will wash the bear for you. He needs a bath too. Then he will be clean and soft again."

Sara and the bear washed their hands and face. Then Sara's mom took the bear and put him in the sink. She used soap and water to wash him. She rinsed him and dried him with a towel. She gave him back to Sara and said, "Here you go, Sara. Your bear is clean and soft now. He smells good too." Sara hugged the bear and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I love you and I love the bear." Sara's mom said, "I love you too, Sara. And I love the bear too. Now, let's go to your bed and take a nap. You need to rest after playing so much." Sara and the bear said, "Okay, mom. Let's go to bed and take a nap." They followed Sara's mom to the bed. They snuggled under the blanket and closed their eyes. They fell asleep and dreamed of the park. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toy cars and trucks all day long. One day, he went outside to play with his friend, Sally.

Sally said, "I want to win this race!" Timmy replied, "I don't mind if you win, as long as we have fun." They started racing their toy cars down the hill. Sally's car was faster, and she won the race.

Timmy felt a little bitter about losing, but Sally said, "Don't worry, we can race again and again. Winning is not important, having fun with our friends is." Timmy smiled and agreed, and they continued to play together happily.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily was playing in her room when she noticed a shiny knob on her dresser. She thought it looked lovely and decided to turn it.

When she turned the knob, a secret compartment opened up! Inside, she found a magical wand. She waved it around and suddenly, all of her toys came to life! Her teddy bear started dancing and her dolls started singing.

Lily was so happy and grateful for her lovely surprise. She knew that she would always remember the special knob on her dresser that brought her so much joy. From that day on, she made sure to always notice the little things that could bring her happiness. The end.

Lila and Ben are playing in the farm. They see a big gray bull in the field. The bull has horns and a ring in his nose. He looks angry.

"Let's go closer and say hello to the bull," Ben says. He likes animals.

"No, Ben, that's not a good idea. The bull might hurt us. He is not friendly like the cows," Lila says. She is scared of the bull.

But Ben does not listen to Lila. He runs to the fence and climbs over it. He walks towards the bull. He wants to touch him.

"Ben, come back! You are in danger!" Lila shouts. She follows him and tries to pull him away.

The bull sees Ben and Lila. He snorts and lowers his head. He charges at them. He is very fast.

Lila and Ben are very afraid. They run back to the fence. But the bull is faster. He is almost on them.

Lila remembers what her dad told her. If a bull chases you, you have to kneel down and stay still. Maybe he will think you are a rock and leave you alone.

Lila kneels down and covers her head with her arms. She hopes the bull will not see her.

Ben sees Lila kneel down. He does not understand why she does that. He thinks she is giving up. He keeps running to the fence. He thinks he can make it.

But he is wrong. The bull catches up with him. He hits him with his horns. He tosses him in the air. He makes him fly.

Ben screams. He is hurt. He falls to the ground. He does not move.

Lila sees what happens to Ben. She cries. She is very sad. She wishes she could help him.

The bull sees Lila. He does not care about her. He thinks she is a rock. He walks away. He goes back to his grass.

Lila gets up. She runs to Ben. She hugs him. She calls for help.

Dad hears Lila's cries. He comes to the field. He sees Ben and Lila. He sees the bull. He understands what happened.

He is very angry at the bull. He is very worried about Ben. He is very proud of Lila.

He picks up Ben and carries him to the car. He takes him to the doctor. He hopes he will be okay.

He tells Lila she is very brave. She did the right thing. She saved her life.

He tells her he loves her. He hugs her. He takes her home.

He tells her they will never go near the bull again. He tells her the bull is very bad. He tells her he will find a new home for him.

Lila nods. She agrees. She does not like the bull. She likes Ben.

She hopes he will get better soon. She wants to play with him again. She loves him.

Once there was a wealthy duck who loved to swim. He would swim around the pond every day. One day, he decided to take an adventure and swim to the top of a nearby cliff. He was so excited to explore what the cliff was like.

The cliff was high and steep. The wealthy duck had to work extra hard in order to make it to the top. But, he was determined and kept swimming. Eventually, he made it to the top of the cliff and was so proud of himself!

At the top, the duck had the most amazing view. He could see the pond far below and he felt so happy and free. From then on, the wealthy duck visited the cliff every day. He would swim to the top and enjoy the wonderful view of the pond below.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toy shark in the bathtub. One day, he tried to whistle a song while playing with his shark.

His mom heard him and said, "Timmy, that's a nice whistle! Are you having fun with your shark?"

Timmy replied, "Yes, Mommy! Shark is so fit and strong. He can swim very fast in the water."

Suddenly, the toy shark fell into the water and Timmy couldn't reach it. He started to cry.

"Don't worry, Timmy," said his mom. "I'll help you get your shark back."

She whistled a tune and magically, the shark jumped out of the water and back into Timmy's hands.

Timmy was so happy and thanked his mom. From then on, he never forgot to whistle a tune whenever he played with his shark in the bathtub.

Edward and his mum were out for a walk. Edward wanted to explore, and his mum said it was ok, so she permitted him to wander around.

Edward found some jam on the ground! He wasn't sure where it had come from, but he was excited to pick it up. His mum said it wasn't safe to eat, so she asked him to put it back. Edward didn't want to, but his mum let him keep the jam if he promised to sit in the grass and enjoy the peaceful afternoon.

Edward smiled and sat in the grass. He examined the jam in his hand and stroked it softly. Then, he held it up and said 'Mum, can I make a wish on it?'.

His mum smiled and nodded. 'Yes,' she said, 'you can make a wish if you'd like. I'm sure it will come true!'

Edward nodded and closed his eyes. He wished for something wonderful and held the jam up in front of him. Then, he put it back where he found it and continued his peaceful walk.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her family. One day, Lily went for a walk in the park. She saw a butterfly and started to chase it. Suddenly, she stumbled and fell down. She was scared and started to cry.

A kind lady saw her and came to help. She asked Lily what was wrong. Lily told her that she had fallen down. The lady comforted her and said, "It's okay to stumble sometimes. It's normal. But what's important is that you get up and keep going."

Lily wondered about what the lady had said. She realized that it was true. Everyone makes mistakes and falls down sometimes, but it's important to keep trying and never give up. From that day on, Lily tried to be brave and not be afraid of stumbling. She learned that it's part of life and it's okay to make mistakes.

Once upon a time there was a three year old girl named Lily. She was a very creative and imaginative little girl. One day, when she was walking in the park, she spotted something very interesting. She saw a beautiful symbol made out of twigs and leaves.

Lily was very excited, and she carefully picked up the symbol. When she looked closer, she saw that it was an original symbol. She had never seen something so beautiful before.

Suddenly, Lily heard a voice behind her. It was an old man. He said, "That is a special symbol, young one. I want you to have it."

Lily smiled. She was so pleased the old man was offering her the symbol. She quickly accepted, thanked the old man and ran off with the symbol to show her friends what she had found.

From that day on, whenever Lily wanted to remember the symbol, she only had to look at her hand and feel the original symbol that she had accepted from the old man.

Once there was a person who didn't like anything. She hated the way people looked and the way they talked. She even hated the way food tasted. It was like nothing was good enough for her.

One day she had to go somewhere fancy. She was so unhappy, she wore dark clothing and had a frown on her face. When she got there she saw that everyone was having a wonderful time. They were all dressed nicely and laughing with each other.

The person looked around at all the fancy decorations and felt even more angry. She couldn't stand it anymore and shouted, "I hate this place!"

Everyone stopped and stared at her. No one had ever seen anyone act so unpleasantly in this place. They were all a bit shocked and some of the children began to cry. The person felt a little bit bad, but still didn't want to stay. So she quickly left and never came back.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because today was her friend's birthday party. She put on her favorite gray dress and asked her mom to help her tie her hair with a pink ribbon. 

When they arrived at the party, there were lots of balloons and yummy treats. Lily saw her friend and ran over to give her a big hug. They played games and danced to music. 

During the party, Lily wanted some candy that was on a table that was too high for her to reach. She asked her mom for help and her mom picked her up so she could grab some candy. Lily was very happy and had a great time at the party.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends went on an adventure in the forest. They walked and walked until they found a dark cave. 

Lily's friend said, "Let's go inside!" But Lily was scared. She said, "It's too dark in there, I can't see anything." Her friend said, "Don't worry, I'll point my flashlight in the cave." 

So, they went inside the cave. It was very dark but the flashlight helped them see. They found a treasure chest! But when they opened it, they found a scary monster inside. The monster was not modest and attacked them. Lily and her friends ran away as fast as they could. 

When they got out of the cave, they were safe but scared. Lily said, "I don't want to go on adventures anymore." Her friend said, "Me neither." And they all went home.

Sara and Ben like to play with their toys. They have many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, animals, and more. Sometimes they share their toys, and sometimes they say "mine!" and do not want to share.

One day, they decide to sort their toys by color. Sara puts all the red toys in one pile, and Ben puts all the blue toys in another pile. They are happy with their sorting.

But then they see a weird toy. It is a green car with pink wheels and yellow spots. They do not know whose toy it is. They both want it, because it is weird and different.

"Mine!" Sara says, and grabs the toy.

"No, mine!" Ben says, and pulls the toy.

They start to fight over the weird toy. They tug and shout and cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to see what is wrong. She sees Sara and Ben fighting over the weird toy.

"Stop, stop!" Mom says. "Why are you fighting over this toy?"

"Mine!" Sara and Ben say at the same time.

Mom shakes her head. She picks up the weird toy and looks at it.

"This is not your toy," Mom says. "This is a toy I bought for your cousin Lily. She is coming to visit tomorrow, and I wanted to give her a special gift. This toy is not yours, it is hers."

Sara and Ben feel ashamed. They did not know the toy was for Lily. They say sorry to Mom and to each other.
