Mom smiles and hugs them. She says, "It is okay to like weird toys, but it is not okay to fight over them. You have many toys of your own, and you can share them with Lily when she comes. Maybe she will share her weird toy with you, too. But you have to ask nicely, and say please and thank you."

Sara and Ben nod and agree. They say they will be nice to Lily and share their toys. They put the weird toy back in the box and finish sorting their toys by color. They are happy with their sorting, and with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, a big hurricane came to their town. The wind was blowing very hard and the rain was pouring down.

Timmy's mom called him inside the house to stay safe. "Timmy, come inside now. It's not safe to play outside during a hurricane," she said. "But Mom, I want to play with my friends," Timmy replied.

"No, Timmy. It's too dangerous. The hurricane is too strong," his mom said. "But Mom, can we count how many raindrops fall during the hurricane?" Timmy asked. "Sure, Timmy. Let's do that together," his mom said with a playful smile. So, they sat inside and counted the number of raindrops falling outside during the hurricane.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy named Spike. Spike was a lucky dinosaur with a big spike on his back. Tim and Spike were best friends. They played together every day.

One sunny day, Tim and Spike went to the park. They saw a little girl crying. Tim wanted to help her. He asked her what was wrong. The girl said she lost her toy. Tim and Spike wanted to make her feel better.

Tim offered to help the girl find her toy. The girl said thank you. Tim, Spike, and the girl looked everywhere. They were lucky because they found the toy under a big tree. The girl was so happy. Tim, Spike, and the girl played together all day long.

Once there was a violin. The violin was pale. The violin wanted to play a song. So the violin started to play. The music was beautiful. But the violin could not finish the song.

Then, a small girl came along. She was three years old. She heard the violin's song and wanted to help. She closed her eyes and listened. Then she knew what to do.

The little girl picked up the violin. She held it softly and plucked the strings. The music was perfect! The violin finished its song.

The little girl smiled. She knew the violin was happy too. She put it down gently and waved goodbye. The little girl and the pale violin were friends now.

One day, a powerful steel machine came to life. It could speak, and everyone was very afraid. The machine said, "I want to be friends with everyone". Even though everyone was scared, they were also curious. So, they asked the machine what it wanted to show them.

The machine replied, â€œI want to make a place for everyone to be safe and happy.â€ Everyone was so excited! They started to work with the machine and soon enough, a beautiful city was built. Everyone was so proud of what the powerful machine helped them do.

The people and the machine were now friends and they decided to have a party! They danced and spoke with each other and thanked the machine for all its hard work. From then on, the city was safe and happy. The machine had made their dreams come true.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very hungry and wanted to eat his favorite food, pizza. But his mom said that they didn't have any pizza left in the house. Timmy was sad and didn't know what to do.

Then Timmy had an idea. He asked his mom if they could go to a pizza place to get some pizza. His mom said yes and they went to the pizza place. But when they got there, they saw that there was a long line and they had to wait for a long time. Timmy's hunger was increasing and he was getting very impatient.

Finally, they got to the front of the line and ordered their pizza. They took it home and Timmy was very happy. He ate his pizza and his hunger went away. Timmy learned that sometimes you have to wait for things you want, but it's worth it in the end.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but they did not like to share them. They always fought over who got to play with what, and they made a lot of noise and mess.

One day, their mom said, "We are going to the store to buy a new rug for the living room. You can come with me, or you can stay home with dad. But you have to clean up your toys first."

Ben and Lily did not want to clean up their toys. They wanted to keep playing. They said, "No, we don't want to go to the store. We want to stay home with dad."

Their mom said, "Okay, but you have to promise to clean up your toys before I come back. And don't fight, or dad will be grumpy."

Ben and Lily said, "Okay, okay, we promise." But they did not mean it. As soon as their mom left, they started to play again. They did not clean up their toys. They did not share. They did not listen to their dad. They made him very grumpy.

When their mom came back, she saw the mess and the noise. She was very angry. She said, "Ben and Lily, you did not keep your promise. You did not clean up your toys. You did not behave. You made dad grumpy. You are not nice."

She took away their toys and put them in a box. She said, "You cannot play with your toys until you learn to share and be nice. And you have to help me put the new rug in the living room."

Ben and Lily felt very sad. They realized they had been selfish and naughty. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We are sorry, dad. We want to be nice. We want to share. We want to help."

They helped their mom put the new rug in the living room. It was a soft and colorful rug. They liked it very much. They said, "Wow, mom, this is a nice rug. Can we play on it?"

Their mom said, "Yes, you can play on it, but only if you share and be nice. And you have to clean up your toys after you play."

Ben and Lily agreed. They said, "Okay, mom, we will share and be nice. And we will clean up our toys. Thank you for the nice rug."

They hugged their mom and dad. They were not grumpy anymore. They were happy. They learned that sharing and being nice is better than fighting and being naughty. They played on the new rug with their toys, and they had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big cupboard in a small house. Inside the cupboard, there were many things like plates, cups, and bowls. One day, a little girl named Lily was playing with her toys in the living room when her mom called out to her.

"Come help me in the kitchen, Lily," her mom said.

Lily got up and walked to the kitchen. Her mom asked her to get a big cup from the cupboard. Lily opened the cupboard and looked for the big cup. She found it and took it to her mom.

"Good job, Lily! Now, can you leave the cup on the counter?" her mom asked.

Lily put the cup on the counter and smiled. "I like helping you, Mommy," she said.

"I like it when you help me too, Lily," her mom replied, giving her a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy vendor. He sold ice cream in a big truck. He would stay in one place all day and not move. 

One day, a little girl came to buy an ice cream from the lazy vendor. She asked him to move his truck closer to her house, but he didn't want to. He said he was too lazy to move. 

The little girl was sad because she really wanted an ice cream. But then, she had an idea. She ran to her house and got her wagon. She pulled the wagon to the lazy vendor's truck and asked him to put the ice cream in her wagon. 

The lazy vendor was surprised but he did it. The little girl was so happy! She thanked the lazy vendor and went home with her ice cream. From then on, the lazy vendor realized that he could sell more ice cream if he moved around. So he started driving his truck to different places.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, mom said, "Amy, let's make some cookies!" Amy was very excited and said, "Yes, mom!"

First, they had to mix the dough. Amy poured some flour, sugar, and eggs into a big bowl. Then, she mixed it all together with her hands. It was a harmless and fun thing to do. The dough felt soft and squishy.

When the dough was ready, Amy and her mom rolled it out on the table. They used cookie cutters to make fun shapes like stars, hearts, and circles. Then, they put the cookies in the oven to bake. Soon, the whole house smelled like yummy cookies. Amy and her mom enjoyed eating the delicious cookies they made together.

Once upon a time, there was a prince. He was very nervous because he had something to do. He let the people around him help him. He let the birds tell him stories. He let the animals give him advice. He was so nervous, he could barely sleep.

Finally, the prince let the wind guide him to the place he needed to go. When he arrived, he was so happy he forgot to be nervous. The people cheered for him and clapped.

The prince let everyone give him a big hug. Then, he thanked them all.

Now the prince was brave and not nervous at all. He was ready to take on the world!

Tommy was walking in the park and he observed a bird chirping up in a tree. He smiled and ran over to take a closer look. 

"Hello," said the little bird. "My name is Bella. What's yours?"

Tommy smiled and said, "My name is Tommy. I love birds!"

Bella smiled back. "I love people too! I can teach you some of my bird songs if you like."

Tommy laughed and said, "Yes please!"

So Bella sang her best songs while Tommy observed her closely. Then a little girl walked over. She was poor and had only a few birds perched on a stick.

"Where did you get these birds?" asked Tommy.

"I found them outside my house," said the little girl. "I found some eggs too, but there's not enough love coming from my home. So I wanted to make sure these birds found a good home. Would you like them?"

Tommy smiled and said, "I would love to give them a home. What do you think, Bella?"

Bella smiled and said, "I think that's a very kind thing for you to do. I'm sure these little birds will be happy with you."

So Tommy took the little birds home and he spent all day watching them, singing his songs and giving them lots of love.

Once there was a girl called Lucy. She was three years old and was feeling very sleepy. She was wearing a blue dress and had red lips. She pulled out a box filled with matches. She knew how to play a game with the matches. She had to match the heads of the matches together. She smiled when she matched all the heads together.

Then she made the matches into a house shape. She thought it was very pretty. She tried to make a lip shape with the matches. She made it look like a fish. It was a fun game for her.

When she finished all of her matching games, she was feeling very sleepy. She laid down on her bed and went to sleep. She had a long day so she rested until the morning. What a fun time she had playing with the matches!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wandered through the forest. She peered around each tree looking for something special. As she kept walking, she noticed a post and stopped to take a look. It was open and she looked inside. There was a small bird! She gasped in wonder and stepped closer. The little bird flew into the air, chirping away. She smiled and watched it fly. She wondered if the bird would come back and she looked up in the sky hoping to see it again. Then she knew what she must do and she wandered the forest searching for an open post that the bird might have gone to. She never forgot the adventure that day and she will forever wander the forest in search of a post that's open. 

The End

Once upon a time there was a little elephant. She was so quiet and gentle. Every day she liked to rub her trunk on a big tree in the park. She would pat it softly and make the leaves rustle. 

One day when the elephant was rubbing her trunk, she heard a noise coming from the grass. She stopped rubbing and looked around. To her surprise, she saw a little bug scurrying around. 

The elephant was so curious about the bug, she stood still and watched him for a while. She followed the bug and watched it hop around the park. She got closer and closer as it climbed onto a leaf and rubbed its belly. 

The elephant found it so funny, she started to giggle. Then, she bent her trunk down close to the bug and blew it gently. The bug felt so safe with the elephant, they were both very quiet. The elephant wanted to play and took the bug in her trunk and started to rub it softly. 

The bug tickled and started to giggle too. The elephant was so happy and wished to keep the bug forever. But, she knew she had to take care of the bug and put it back in the grass. The bug waved goodbye and the elephant smiled. She knew they would always be friends.

Once there was a man and a small girl. The girl was only 3 years old and was called Alice. She wanted to go on an adventure.

The man took Alice to the river. He showed her a big boat that she could sit on and play.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Lily. She liked to explore, so one day she went walking in the forest.

Lily saw a tree. It was filthy, covered in mud and leaves. She wanted to drink from it, so she cupped her hands and bent down near the tree.

But then, a voice came from behind her.

"What are you doing there?" the voice asked.

Lily turned around and saw a giant. He was tall and strong.

Lily was scared. She said, "I was just gonna drink from the tree."

The giant smiled. He said, "You don't want to drink from that tree. It's filthy. Come, I'll show you a better one."

The giant led Lily to another tree. This one was nice and clean. He told Lily to drink all she wanted and she did.

Afterward, the giant and Lily said goodbye. Lily thanked the giant and said, "I'm glad I met you!"

And she went home happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear pretty dresses. One day, she saw a new dress in the store. It was so pretty and pink. She wanted it so much.

Lily asked her mom, "Can we get that dress, please?" Her mom replied, "We can't buy it now, but if you save your money, you can gain enough to buy it later."

Lily thought about it and decided to save her money. She did chores around the house and earned some money. After a few weeks, she had enough to buy the dress. She was so happy and couldn't wait to wear it. When she tried it on, she felt so pretty and the dress was so tasty.

Marlon was only three years old but he already knew that he wanted to be an astronaut one day. Every night he would look up at the stars and dream about floating around in the sky. He decided to make a spaceship out of cardboard.

Marlon was so excited. He chose a nice spot in the garden to launch his spaceship and asked his mum to push him up in it. His mum laughed and was happy to help him.

When they got to the top, Marlon didn't know what to do. He was scared and wished he had asked his mum for a few tips. He started flapping his arms up and down quickly and was surprised to see that he hadn't moved an inch!

Suddenly, Marlon realised that he was missing something very important - oxygen. He had been so excited about taking off that he had forgotten this essential item! He looked down at his mum and felt a wave of regret as he watched her shaking her head in disappointment.

Marlon's mum hugged him tightly and said, "Don't worry, Marlon. You'll be a great astronaut one day!" Marlon smiled and hugged her back. He now knew that he needed to remember the right things when making his spaceship!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and eat candy. One day, Lily's mom cooked dinner and put salt on the food. Lily didn't like it and made a sad face.

Her mom asked, "What's wrong, Lily? Don't you like the food?" 

Lily replied, "No, Mommy. It's too salty. Can I have some candy instead?"

Her mom said, "No, Lily. You need to eat your dinner. I dare you to try it again and see if you like it." 

Lily took a small bite and to her surprise, it tasted good! She smiled and ate the rest of her dinner happily.

Once upon a time, Tom the bear was walking through the forest. He was looking for something special and exciting, but he hadn't seen anything yet.

Suddenly, Tom saw a spark in the distance. He got closer and closer until he realized it was a flame!

The flame was bright and warm. He wondered what he should do.

Tom looked around and noticed there were many other furry animals in the forest. He decided to invite them to join him and the flame.

Tom said, "Come, friends! Join me around this warm flame!"

There were two hairy squirrels eager to cuddle up together and keep warm. There were two rabbits who were so excited to join the group. A friendly fox even joined in.

They all snuggled together and stayed warm around the flame that night. They had so much fun playing and telling stories around the fire.

Tom smiled and said, "Thanks for coming to my flame party, friends!"

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with blocks and make towers. One day, they find a new box of blocks. The blocks have symbols on them. Some have stars, some have circles, some have squares.

"Look, Tom, these blocks are different!" Lily says. "They have symbols. What do they mean?"

"I don't know, Lily. Maybe they are a code. Maybe we can use them to send messages," Tom says.

They start to build towers with the blocks. They try to make patterns with the symbols. They have fun.

But then, Lily's mom comes. She says it is time to go home. She says they have to clean up the blocks.

"Can we leave them like this, mom?" Lily asks. "We are making a code. We want to finish it."

"No, Lily, you have to be obedient. You have to put the blocks back in the box. You can play with them another day," Lily's mom says.

Lily and Tom are sad. They like their code. They don't want to break their towers.

But they are obedient. They listen to Lily's mom. They put the blocks back in the box. They say goodbye to each other.

"Maybe we can play with the blocks again tomorrow," Tom says.

"Maybe we can find out what the symbols mean," Lily says.

They smile. They are still friends. They still like to play with blocks.

Molly was a happy little girl who loved to hug everyone she met. One day she went to the store with her mommy to buy something special. They looked around and Molly saw something orange! It was an orange, so sweet and juicy. Molly asked her mommy if she could have it and mommy said yes. Molly was so happy, she hugged it tight and said thank you.

On their way home Molly and her mommy stopped by the park. Molly wanted to show her orange to all her friends. She held it up and showed it to them. Everyone said it was so sweet. They were so excited to see it that they all came to give Molly a hug.

Molly was so excited and happy to have her sweet orange and to be showered with hugs from all her friends. It was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was an attractive mill. It had tall walls, a big wheel and lots of birds who sang along as it spun. The mill was very important because it prevented the town from running out of food. 

One day, when the mill was spinning, some naughty cows wandered past. They stumbled into the mill and caused a lot of trouble, making a huge mess inside. 

The mill worker was very angry and called for the mayor. However, the mayor knew that the cows were just being curious and needed help to get out of the mill. 

So he asked the mill worker to get the cows safely out, and then asked a few children to help clean up the mess. 

After all was finished, the mill worker and mayor were very happy because they had prevented any more damage to the mill. 

From then on, the mill worked hard and everyone in town knew to stay away from it, to prevent any more accidents.

Once upon a time there was a small furry mouse. It lived in a cozy house in the woods. The small mouse liked to explore and have adventures.

One day, the mouse decided to start on an adventure. He packed some cheese and grabbed a stick. The stick was perfect for poking into holes and spotting tasty snacks.

The mouse started walking through the forest. The leaves rustled in the wind and the trees looked so tall. The mouse soon noticed something strange. The stick was getting bigger and bigger!

The mouse stopped to take a closer look. The stick had turned into a furry animal! The mouse was so excited, but the animal had gone to sleep. The mouse decided to name him Stick.

From then on, Stick and the little mouse were the best of friends. They traveled through the woods, looking for more adventures. Together, they found lots of fun and surprises!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a nice note that she wanted to show her friend, Max. So, she went to Max's house and knocked on the door. Max opened the door and said, "Hi, Lily! What do you have there?" 

Lily replied, "I have a nice note for you to see." 

Max took the note and said, "This is great! But I want to keep it forever." 

Lily said, "No, Max. We can share it. We can separate it and each keep a piece." 

Max thought about it and said, "Okay, that's a good idea. Let's do that." 

So, they separated the note and each kept a piece. They were both happy and their friendship continued to grow. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a crazy girl. Her name was Molly and she was 3 years old. Every day, Molly liked to make a salad. She did this by cutting up the vegetables. She would use a sharp knife to cut the carrots and tomatoes. She would also chop the lettuce and cucumber too. Molly enjoyed putting them all together in a bowl and mixing them up. Then she'd enjoy eating the salad.

One day, Molly was in the kitchen, getting ready to make her salad. She took the knife, but she wasn't really paying attention. She was thinking about something else. Suddenly, she accidently cut her hand with the knife. It hurt a lot because she had made a mistake. Molly started to cry. 

Luckily, her mom came and saw what had happened. She was very worried but quickly took care of Molly's hand. With a bandage, she carefully wrapped up Molly's hand and made it all better. She was so relieved that Molly was okay! 

After that, Molly was more careful when cutting her salad. And she always remembered to focus on what she was doing. Even though it was a little scary, Molly was happy that she had learned such an important lesson.

Once upon a time there was a twig. The twig was old and broken and wanted to be made better. So it asked around for help. But nobody wanted to help it because it was too small for them to care about.

The twig was sad and wondered what it could do. Then it thought of a plan. It asked a bird if it could help. The bird was clever and agreed.

The bird found some small tools and started to fix the twig. It repaired the twigâ€™s broken pieces until it was as good as new. The twig was so happy!

The bird then realised that many people had been ignorant of the twigâ€™s pain. The bird made a promise to help others who needed it.

The twig was very proud of the bird and thanked it for the help. From then on, the twig and the bird were the best of friends, always helping and supporting each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to skip and play outside with her friends. One day, Lily's mom bought her a big bag of candy. Lily was so happy and ate all the candy in one day. But, the next day, Lily got a shock when she woke up with a tummy ache. 

Lily's friend, Jack, came to play with her and noticed that Lily wasn't feeling well. "What happened?" Jack asked. "I ate too much candy and now my tummy hurts," Lily replied. Jack said, "Oh no, you spoiled your tummy by eating too much candy. Next time, you should only eat a little bit at a time." 

Lily realized that Jack was right and promised to be more careful next time. From that day on, Lily learned to enjoy her treats in moderation and never spoiled her tummy again. The moral of the story is to always be mindful of how much you eat and to take care of your body.

Carla picked up her cuddly toy bear. It was adorable. She loved to squeeze it tight and feel its soft fur against her skin. She was never without it! 

One day, Carla put the bear near the window. Then clouds appeared in the sky, and rain started to fall. Carla watched as steam rose up from the warm rain. 

Suddenly, a gust of wind blew the window open. The bear flew away! Carla tried to catch it, but it was lost. 
Carla was very sad. She had lost her most beloved and adorable friend.

One day, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was three years old and loved exploring. 

She was playing in her garden one sunny day and she admired the beautiful flowers, the butterflies and the trees. As she walked around, she came to the stairs, which were colorful. Daisy thought they looked so fancy and she wanted to try walking up them. 

Daisy took her first step and admired how pretty the stairs were with all the colorful hues. Then she walked up one more step and admired how the steps changed color as she went. After Daisy went up a few more steps, she reached the top and felt very proud of herself. 

Daisy admired the stairs until she got to the end and wanted to go down again. Step by step, Daisy slowly but surely walked down the stairs, admiring the colors along the way. 

Once Daisy made it back to the bottom of the stairs, she appreciated how pretty and colorful the stairs were. She smiled with delight and went off on her next exploration.

Once upon a time, there was a river where a little otter lived. The otter was very useful because he could catch fish to eat. One day, a little girl came to the river and saw the otter swimming. She said, "Hello, otter! You appear very happy today."

The otter replied, "Yes, I am happy because I caught a lot of fish today. They are very tasty!"

The little girl smiled and said, "You are such a useful otter. Can you catch some fish for me too?"

The otter agreed and caught some fish for the little girl. She was very happy and said, "Thank you, otter! You are my new friend."

From that day on, the little girl would often visit the river to play with her new friend, the useful otter. They would swim together and catch fish for each other. They had a lot of fun together and were very happy.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Peter and Sarah. Peter and Sarah always liked to gather together and go on adventures. One day they decided to go exploring on the other side of the forest. 

As they travelled along to the other side, Sarah noticed a large pile of disgusting things. She didn't like the way it looked and so decided not to go any closer. Peter however, thought the pile looked really interesting, so he decided to gather up some of the things and take them with him. 

But as they continued along the path, they noticed that the further they went, the more gross and disgusting the things became. Eventually, the path was so full of disgusting things that they couldn't go any further. 

Realising the importance of taking care of the environment, Peter and Sarah decided to use their knowledge and contribute to the forest. With that, the two friends gathered up the disgusting things, and placed them in a bin nearby. 

At the end of the day, they realized that they were not the only ones who were going to benefit from the clean and tidy forest. The moral of the story is that we have to take care of our environment and not create more mess.

Once there was a little girl named Mia. She was 3 years old and loved playing with mixers. One day, Mia's mum called her into the kitchen. When she arrived, she saw a huge, clean mixer on the counter. 

"Look, Mia," said her mum. "This mixer is for you!" 

Mia's eyes lit up with excitement and she gave her mum a big hug. "Thank you, mum," she replied.

Mia and her mum played together all day with the mixer. They made fruit smoothies, delicious cakes and all kinds of tasty treats. They laughed and had so much fun!

When it was time to go, Mia gave her mum a big hug and said cheerfully,"Goodbye! See you tomorrow!"

Mia's mum smiled and gently replied, "Goodbye, sweetheart. I'll see you then!"

Once upon a time, there was a girl who wanted to find something special. She went on a walk in a dark forest. As she walked, she saw something glimmering between the trees. She stopped and looked closer. It was a string. 

She pulled the string until it was all the way out and it led her to a big tree. She looked around, but saw nothing else. She took the string in her hands and walked around the tree. 

Suddenly, a door opened in the tree. The girl was very excited and stepped inside. Inside, she found a beautiful surprise - a box filled with golden stars! The girl smiled and put the stars in her pocket. 

The girl thanked the tree for the surprise and said goodbye. She closed the door and, holding the string in her hands, ran all the way home. She will never forget the dark forest and all the surprises it held for her.

The little girl was busy by the tree. She had a zipper in her hands and was looking for something. Suddenly, she saw a big bear coming down the hill. She was so scared, she dropped the zipper! The big bear saw the zipper and started to destroy it. The little girl was so sad. She wanted to keep her zipper, but the bear was too strong. The bear kept destroying until there was nothing left of the zipper. The little girl was so busy trying to save her zipper, but it was too late. She ran away quickly, and the bear never came back.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go on walks with her mom and dad. One day, they decided to go on a hike in the mountains. They packed snacks and water and started their journey. 

As they were walking, Lily noticed a man jogging towards them. He seemed very happy and full of energy. "Hello!" he said. "What a beautiful landscape we have here!" 

Lily's dad smiled and replied, "Yes, it's amazing. We love coming here." 

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It sounded like a tree falling. They looked up and saw a big rock rolling down the mountain. They quickly realized it was heading their way. They all started to run, but Lily's mom tripped and fell. 

The man who was jogging quickly ran towards them and helped Lily's mom get up. They all made it to safety, but they were very scared. "Thank you so much for helping us," said Lily's dad. "You saved us from being dead." 

The man smiled and said, "No problem. I'm just glad everyone is okay." From that day on, Lily and her family always remembered to be careful when they went on hikes in the mountains.

Sam had a new black camera. She liked to take pictures of her family, her toys, and even her pets.

One day, Sam was putting on her dress when her mom said, "no Sam, it's time for bed!" Sam was tired and wanted to play with her camera before bed, but her mom wouldn't let her.

Sam pouted and said, "please mom, I just want to take one picture!" Her mom firmly said, "no Sam, it's time to go to sleep." 

Sam sighed, feeling sad and frustrated that she couldn't use her new camera. But her mom had a plan. She said, "okay, Sam, tomorrow we'll play with the camera. How does that sound?"

Sam perked up at the invitation. She smiled, gave her mom a hug, and said, "okay, I'll dress for bed now!"

Once upon a time, there was a rich fireman. He was strong and brave. One day he had to save a cat from a high tree. He put on his fireman suit and went to save the cat. He climbed the tree and dropped the cat onto the ground. The little cat was safe!

The fireman wandered off, trying to find his way home. He soon realised he was lost. He looked around and couldn't find his way back. Then, he spotted a rich house. He knocked on the door and the nice people inside gave him some food and a bed.

The fireman thanked them and on his way home the next day, he dropped a bag of money that he found in the street, into their mailbox as a way to say thank you.

The rich fireman was happy he could help these nice people, and he thanked his lucky stars he found his way home.

Once upon a time, a little girl called Rose was walking in the forest. Suddenly, she spotted something twinkling around a tree. Rose looked closely and it was a piece of string. She reached out to grab it, but it flew away and got stuck in a tree!

Rose called out, â€œWho can help me?â€

Suddenly, a kind man appeared. He said, â€œI can help you.â€ He had a calm face and warm eyes.

The man grabbed a ladder and carefully climbed up the tree. He rescued the string and handed it to Rose.

â€œThank you!â€ said Rose.

The man smiled and said, â€œAnytime. Have a lovely day.â€ He then disappeared into the forest.

Rose was so happy to have the string. She twirled it around her fingers and raced home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to run in the park with his friends. One day, Timmy saw a fancy rake in his neighbor's yard. He asked his neighbor if he could use the rake to help clean up the leaves in his own yard. His neighbor said yes, and Timmy was very happy. Timmy ran back to his yard with the fancy rake and started to clean up the leaves. He worked very hard and soon his yard was all clean. Timmy was proud of himself and ran back to his neighbor's yard to return the fancy rake. The neighbor was happy to see that Timmy had done a good job and thanked him. Timmy felt very happy and ran back to his house to tell his parents about his day.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely hook. He was so lonely that he used to mention his loneliness to everyone he met. One day, he was walking down a path when he heard a voice. He looked around, but he couldn't see anyone. Then, he looked up and saw a butterfly in the sky. The butterfly told him that she had seen a beach which was full of lively hooks having fun. The lonely hook was very excited to hear this and thanked the butterfly before hopping off in the direction she had mentioned.

When the lonely hook arrived at the beach, he was amazed by how many hooks were playing and having fun. He quickly made new friends, and they all had the most wonderful time. They ran around, built sandcastles, and splashed in the water. The lonely hook was no longer lonely and from that day onwards, he always remembered to mention the butterfly who had showed him to this special place.

Gus was a nosy boy. His mom always warned him not to be so nosy but he just couldn't help it. Today he was exploring the grocery store. He had never been in one before. 

Gus started to wander around the aisles. He glanced down every aisle, poking his head into each one. Suddenly an old lady appeared and started scolding him. Gus was so scared he just shrugged and ran away. 

Gus kept on running until he wasn't sure where he was. He stopped to catch his breath but he had no idea how to get back home. He started to cry, feeling scared and alone. 

Gus got more and more lost. He had been wandering for hours when the sun started setting. Suddenly he started to feel very tired and was about to fall asleep when he heard noises coming toward him. 

Gus opened his eyes and saw a group of grown-ups coming his way. He knew he was in trouble. He wanted to run away again, but there was nowhere to go. The grown-ups grabbed him and he had to go with them, never to be heard from again.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl. She wanted to see if she could do things that were tough, so her mum dared her. One day she decided to take the dare and baked a cake. Everyone was so surprised at how good it was and said it was incredible.

But the brave girl didn't want to stop there. She wanted to do something else that was tough, so her mum dared her again. This time she decided to take the dare to tell the truth. The brave girl was scared but she found the courage to speak the truth.

Everyone was so impressed at the brave girl's courage. They said she was incredible for telling the truth even though it was so scary. Everyone cheered for the brave girl and praised her for being so courageous.

The brave girl was so happy to face her fears and take the dares. She was proud of herself that she had the courage to do two incredible things.

The little girl was playing in the garden when she saw a butterfly. She was so excited and chased after it. She followed it everywhere, but it was just too fast. She wanted to reach out and grab it, but it was always out of sight. 

Suddenly, a big scary dog appeared. He barked and growled loudly. He was very bossy and refused to let the little girl near the butterfly. She felt scared and stepped back. 

Fortunately, the girl's mom was nearby and came to her rescue. She gave the dog a stern look and told him to go away. He refused again, but the mom did not give up and kept scolding him. Finally, he decided to go and the little girl was able to go back to chasing the butterfly.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was very restless and wanted something to do. So he decided to go to the park. When he arrived at the park, he saw a big, round, sausage. It was big enough for him to hug. So he grabbed it tight and hugged it. He smiled, feeling happy that he had something to hug.

He hugged it so much until he was tired. When he was tired, he sat down. He felt cozy with the sausage by his side. He closed his eyes and felt very peaceful. He fell asleep with the sausage still in his arms.

When he woke up, the sausage was still there. He smiled and gave the sausage one final hug before he went home.

One day, there was a generous man. He had an ice cream cone. He saw a little girl who was 3 years old. He stepped up to her and said, "Hello little one, do you like ice cream?"

The little girl smiled and nodded. The generous man said, "It would be my pleasure to give you my cone". He handed the cone to the little girl and she said, "Thank you!"

The little girl was so happy. She closed her eyes and took a big lick of ice cream. It was so delicious. She opened her eyes and said, "This is the best ice cream ever!"

The generous man smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it."

The little girl smiled back and said, "Thank you very much. You are so generous."

The generous man nodded and said, "You're welcome". 

The little girl finished her cone and thanked the generous man again before she skipped off.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to hop. They hopped on the grass, on the sand, on the rocks. They hopped fast and slow, high and low, far and near. They had fun hopping together.

One day, they saw a sign that said: Hop Race. Win a big toy. They wanted to join the race and win the toy. They went to the start line and waited for the sound. They were nervous. They hoped they could hop well.

The sound came and they started to hop. They hopped as fast as they could. They passed other kids who hopped too. They saw the finish line and the big toy. They hopped harder and harder.

Lily and Ben reached the finish line at the same time. They looked at each other and smiled. They had both won the race. They had both won the toy. They were happy. They hugged and said:

"We did it! We hopped well! We are good friends!"

They shared the toy and played with it. They hopped some more. They had fun hopping together.

Once upon a time, there was a big, squishy jello. It was green and it liked to play. One day it wanted to explore, so it decided to go underground. It stretched itself across the ground and snuggled down into a hole.

The jello found it was quite tight and hard down there. But it kept squeezing between the rocks and gravel. It kept feeling around until it bumped into something. Its eyes opened wide in surprise.

It was another squishy jello. It was blue and the same size as the first one. The first jello was so excited and they squeezed each other in a big hug.

They decided to explore together and after a while they found a big, warm cave. They made a cozy home and lived happily ever after.

A big hot sun was shining in the sky. Two friends saw it and decided to go outside. They wanted to have fun in the warm weather.

The two friends started to play chase and they got very hot. One of the friends found an old rag lying in the grass. He decided to throw it in the air and try to catch it.

His friend got mad and picked up the rag. He wanted to keep it for himself. He started shouting and tried to pull it away from his friend.

This made the other friend very angry. He also wanted the rag and a fight started! They pushed and pulled each other trying to take the rag away.

Eventually one of them got it. Both were so tired that they decided to stop fighting. They took a break and decided to find something else to do.

Once upon a time there was a little sheep. He lived all by himself and he ached to have a friend. One day while he was walking around, he stumbled upon a farm. The farmer saw him and said, â€œWhat are you doing here little sheep?â€ The sheep was so happy to have a talked to and quickly said, â€œIâ€™m looking for a friend.â€ The farmer smiled and told the sheep he could stay with him if he helped on the farm. The sheep gladly said yes and the farmer smiled.

The sheep quickly moved in and started helping the farmer. Every day, the farmer taught him how to cook and soon enough the sheep became a master chef. One day the farmer said to the sheep, â€œLetâ€™s go and show everyone how good of a cook you are!â€

So the sheep followed the farmer to the town square and he was so proud to show everyone what he had cooked. But when he arrived and the people saw him, they all started laughing. The sheep felt ashamed. But the farmer patted him on the back and said, â€œEveryone has their first time cooking, donâ€™t be ashamed!â€ The people stopped laughing and started clapping and the sheep was so proud. He had made a friend, and found something he was good at.

Once upon a time, there was an important pigeon named Polly. Polly was a special pigeon, and every day she would keep flying high in the sky. Everyday, she would go very far from her home to find food for her family. She was very brave. 

One day, Polly was flying very high up in the sky, and she couldn't find her way back home. She kept flying for a very long time, until she saw something special - a farm! She flew down to the farm, and the farmer was so happy to see her. He gave her some food and a nice place to stay. 

The farmer kept an eye on Polly, and then he gave her a very special gift - her own family! From then on, Polly kept coming back to the farm every day to find food for her new family. The farmer was very happy with Polly, and they became very good friends. 

Polly was an important pigeon in the farmer's life, and he kept her safe always. She was a very special bird!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Sam. He loved to explore. Today, he wanted to go for a walk in the woods to find a creek. So he said goodbye to his parents and started walking.

On his way, Sam heard a noise coming from the trees. When he looked between the branches he saw an amazing sight. A group of frogs were jumping from stone to stone in the creek.

Sam wanted to stay and watch but he didn't want to delay his adventure, so he said goodbye to the frogs and continued his walk. 

Later, he came across a tall mountain and said, "Wow, that's amazing!" He was quite happy and excited. 

He followed the creek until he reached his parents house. When he walked inside he said, "Mummy, look I found a creek! It was amazing!"

His Mummy smiled and said, "I'm glad you had a great adventure, Sam."

One day, Toby had a big event. He was so excited! He put on his special outfit and waved goodbye to Mommy. At the event, Toby saw many people. Everyone was working and having a good time.

Toby noticed a smelly food cart and his mouth started to water. He asked one of the workers what kind of food they had. "We have hot dogs and hamburgers," said the worker. Toby wanted to try a hot dog.

He ordered the hot dog and waited. When his order was ready, Toby took a big bite. But something was not right. "It tastes yucky," he said.

The worker laughed. "That's because the hot dog is smelly," he said. Toby was so embarrassed! He thanked the worker and quickly went home. Mommy laughed when she heard the story. From then on, Toby was more careful when choosing his food!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance to the rhythm of the music. One day, Lily's friend asked her to perform in front of many people. Lily felt scared and didn't know what to do. Her mom told her to be brave and try her best.

Lily's mom also recommended that she practice every day to get better. Lily listened to her mom and practiced every day. She felt more confident and brave. Finally, the day of the performance arrived. Lily danced to the rhythm of the music and did a great job. Everyone clapped and cheered for her. Lily felt very happy and proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful girl named Lucy. She liked to wander through the country. One day, she went for a long walk. She saw many different things along the way.

Lucy saw a river, with lots of big, green trees on the edge, birds hopping around and big, fluffy clouds in the sky. Then, she saw a castle. She wandered up to the castle to explore. When she got close, she saw someone near the gate. It was a big, friendly dog.

"Hello," said Lucy.

The dog looked up and smiled. "Hello," said the dog. "My name is Max. What's your name?"

"My name is Lucy," said Lucy. "I'm wandering through this country."

Max barked happily. "I'd be glad to show you around!"

So Lucy and Max went on a journey together and saw many wonderful things. Everywhere they went, people and animals said hello to them. Lucy had a great time and felt very cheerful. 

At the end of their journey, Max said goodbye and went back to the castle. Lucy waved to him and went on her way. She was happy she had such a fun adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved to help her mommy. One day, her mommy said, â€œWill you help me make squash?â€ The little girl smiled and said, â€œYes!â€

So the little girl and her mommy went to the kitchen. The mommy showed the little girl how to make the squash. The little girl washed the squash and chopped it into small pieces.

Next, the mommy and the little girl put the squash into a pot with some water. They put it on the stove to make it nice and hot. The little girl stirred the squash while the mommy watched. The cooking squash smelled yummy!

Finally, the squash was done cooking. The little girl and her mommy put the squash on a plate. Then they added some butter and salt. The squash looked and smelled yummy and safe.

The little girl and her mommy ate the squash together. It was delicious. The little girl was so proud that she could help make it with her mommy.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Mary. Mary was so happy, because she was going to marry her best friend. On the day of the wedding, everyone was so excited.

Mary looked so beautiful in her pretty dress. Her friend was wearing a white suit and he looked so handsome. They looked so happy together. 

When it was time for the reception, everyone enjoyed the party. There was delicious food, and one of the treats was yogurt. It was very smooth and tasted so yummy. 

Mary and her friend loved the yogurt so much, they fed each other. Everyone clapped and cheered for them. Then the music started so that everyone could dance. 

It was the best day ever and Mary and her friend married and were very happy together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had hair as yellow as the sun, and a smile that shone brighter than all the stars in the sky. The little girl requested her mum to open the drawer in the kitchen. Her mum obliged, and the little girl let out an excited yelp of joy.

Inside the drawer, there were amazing things! Bars of chocolate, colourful plastic badges, and a toy car. The little girl was so excited that she couldn't pick just one thing. She took out all of the amazing items in the drawer and placed them on the kitchen table.

She smiled and thanked her mum as she raced out of the kitchen with her treasures. The little girl was so happy with the amazing items in the drawer that she told all of her friends in the playground about it. Everyone was so excited to come visit her and explore the drawer!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. One night Lucy was very sleepy, so she lay down in her crib. She wanted to go to sleep, but she was cold. 

Suddenly, Lucy saw something in her crib. It was a fake blanket! It looked like a real one, but it was made out of cloth. 

Lucy wrapped the fake blanket around her and got very warm. She lay in her crib and smiled with happiness. She soon fell asleep and had a wonderful dream. 

The next morning, Lucy woke up and put the fake blanket away. Then she lay back down in her crib and had a nice warm nap. 

The end!

One day, Tommy's mum asked him to collect a task. Tommy was a brilliant three-year-old and he was excited to do the task.

He put on his shoes and went outside. He looked around the garden to see what he had to collect. He saw a few stones and some leaves. Then, he noticed a few pieces of wood and some twigs.

He collected the stones, leaves and twigs. He put them all in a big bucket so he could take them into the house.

When Tommy finished collecting the task, he felt very proud! He had done a brilliant job collecting everything on his own.

Tommy was excited to show his mum the task he had collected. She was so happy to see Tommy's work and she gave him a big hug. Tommy was very pleased - it had been fun collecting the task!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to climb trees, but he was too short to reach the branches. One day, he found an axe in the shed and decided to use it to chop down a tree. 

"Timmy, what are you doing with that axe?" asked his mom. 

"I'm going to chop down a tree so I can climb it," Timmy replied politely. 

His mom explained that chopping down trees was dangerous and that he could hurt himself. She suggested that he ask his dad for help instead. 

Later that day, Timmy's dad helped him climb a tall tree in the backyard. Timmy was so happy that he thanked his dad politely. From that day on, Timmy never used the axe to chop down trees again.

Once upon a time there was a curious little girl. She loved to explore and build things. One day she went on a walk and found something unusual. It was a big horn! She thought it was so cool.

She decided to take the horn home with her. There she built a special horn house for it, with a door and windows. She played with the horn every day, making more and more noise until she had made all sorts of unusual sounds.

Every day the little girl built something new with the horn. She was so happy and felt so proud of her creations. It was a lot of fun!

Soon enough, the little girl had built a special home for her horn and they were best friends. Every day they played together and created new and unusual sounds. It was a happy time!

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max loved to dig in the dirt and play with his ball. One day, Max's owner noticed that he was feeling very tired and weak. She took him to the vet, who said that Max needed more power in his body to feel better.

Max's owner decided to give him special food that would raise his power. She also gave him lots of love and cuddles. After a few days, Max started to feel much better! He had more power to play with his ball and dig in the dirt.

But one day, Max got very dirty from digging in a filthy mud puddle. His owner didn't mind, though. She knew that even though Max was filthy, he was still her lovable dog. And Max was happy, because he got to play in the mud and feel the power of being a dog!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat waffles for breakfast every day. One morning, she asked her mom for waffles, but her mom said no because she had been misbehaving. Lily was sad and angry, but she knew she had to be good to get her waffles.

Later that day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. One of her friends, a boy named Timmy, was being mean to the other kids. Lily told him to stop, but he wouldn't listen. When the teacher saw what was happening, she punished Timmy by making him sit on the bench for a few minutes.

After that, Lily felt proud of herself for standing up to Timmy and doing the right thing. She learned that even if she didn't get what she wanted, being good and kind to others was always the best choice. And the next day, her mom made her some delicious waffles for breakfast.

Lily and Tom were hungry. They wanted to eat soup for lunch. Mom said she would make soup for them. She went to the kitchen and put a pot on the stove.

Lily and Tom followed Mom to the kitchen. They saw a big spoon on the counter. It was shiny and silver. Lily liked shiny things. She wanted to play with the spoon.

"Can I have the spoon, Mom?" Lily asked.

"No, Lily, that spoon is for the soup. You can have another spoon to play with," Mom said.

But Lily did not listen. She reached for the shiny spoon when Mom was not looking. She grabbed it and ran away.

Tom saw Lily run away with the spoon. He was confused. Why did Lily take the spoon? He wanted to help Mom with the soup. He ran after Lily.

"Lily, give back the spoon! Mom needs it for the soup!" Tom shouted.

Lily did not want to give back the spoon. She liked the shiny spoon. She ran to her room and hid under the bed.

Tom followed Lily to her room. He looked under the bed. He saw Lily and the spoon.

"Lily, please give back the spoon. The soup will be ready soon. We can share the soup and eat it with our own spoons," Tom said.

Lily looked at Tom. She saw that he was sad. She felt sorry for Tom. She did not want to make him sad. She decided to give back the spoon.

"Okay, Tom, I will give back the spoon. I'm sorry I took it. I just liked the shiny spoon," Lily said.

She gave the spoon to Tom. Tom smiled and thanked her. He took the spoon to the kitchen and gave it to Mom.

Mom was happy to see the spoon. She stirred the soup with the spoon. She smelled the soup. It was hot and yummy.

"Soup is ready, Lily and Tom! Come and eat!" Mom called.

Lily and Tom ran to the kitchen. They sat at the table and waited for Mom to serve them soup. They each got a bowl of soup and a spoon. They ate the soup and enjoyed it.

They were not hungry anymore. They were happy. They liked soup. They liked Mom. They liked each other. They learned to share. They learned to listen. They learned to say sorry. They learned to shine.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy lived in a small house with her mommy and daddy. She loved to play in the park near her house. In the park, there was a modest fountain. Amy liked to watch the water go up and down.

One sunny day, Amy went to the park with her mommy. They saw a small bird near the fountain. Amy wanted to peek at the bird. She walked slowly and quietly to the bird. The bird looked at Amy and said, "Hi, I am Timmy the bird. Do you want to play with me?"

Amy was so happy to have a new friend. She said, "Yes, Timmy! Let's play together." Amy and Timmy played near the fountain all day. They splashed in the water and had lots of fun. When it was time to go home, Amy said, "Bye, Timmy! See you tomorrow!"

Once upon a time, there was a nice fox. The fox wanted to make a new friend, so she picked up an attractive bone and ventured into the forest.

The fox saw a bear, and called out, "Hi! Do you want to be my friend?" 

The bear smiled and said, "Yes, I would like to be your friend. But first you have to reach me."

The fox was confused. She didn't know what "reach" meant. So the bear laughed and said, "Reach means to stretch out your arms like this."

The fox watched as the bear stretched out his arms, and she tried to do the same. She felt silly, but soon enough the fox was able to reach the bear.

The fox and bear hugged, and from that day forward, they were the best of friends. Every day, they would reach for each other, and remind themselves of their newfound friendship.

Jen and Ben were twins who liked to play in the attic. They found many old things there, like hats and books and toys. One day, they saw a big chest in the corner. It was covered with dust and had a lock on it.

"Let's open it!" Jen said. "Maybe there is a treasure inside!"

"But how?" Ben asked. "We don't have a key."

Jen looked around and saw a small hole in the wall. She peeked inside and saw something shiny. She reached in and pulled out a key.

"Look, Ben, I found a key!" she whispered. "Maybe it fits the chest!"

They ran to the chest and tried the key. It turned and clicked. They lifted the lid and gasped. Inside, there was a beautiful dress, a pair of shoes, a necklace and a crown. They were all made of ice and sparkled in the light.

"Wow, they are so pretty!" Jen said. "Can I try them on?"

"OK, but be careful," Ben said. "They look very icy and cold."

Jen put on the dress, the shoes, the necklace and the crown. She felt like a princess. She twirled and danced in the attic. Ben clapped and cheered.

Suddenly, they heard a loud voice from downstairs.

"Jen! Ben! Time for lunch!" their mom called.

"Uh-oh, we have to go," Ben said. "Quick, put the things back in the chest!"

Jen nodded and took off the dress, the shoes, the necklace and the crown. She put them back in the chest and closed the lid. They ran downstairs, leaving the chest behind.

They never told anyone about their icy secret. But sometimes, they would go back to the attic and play with the ice things again. They wondered who made them and why they were in the chest. But they never found out. They just enjoyed their magic.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends were playing tag when they heard a loud noise. They looked and saw that a little bird had fallen out of its nest and was on the ground.

Timmy knew he had to help the bird, so he carefully picked it up and took it to his mom. His mom said the bird was hurt and needed to go to the vet. Timmy was sad, but he knew he had saved the bird's life.

Later that day, Timmy went back to the park to play with his friends. They were having fun until they saw a big, filthy dog running towards them. Timmy was scared, but he remembered how he had saved the bird earlier that day. He knew he had to be brave and save his friends from the dog. So, he stood in front of his friends and yelled at the dog to go away. The dog listened and ran off.

Timmy and his friends were safe and happy. They went home and had lunch at noon. Timmy felt proud of himself for being a hero and saving the day.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl who had a favorite scarf. Her mom always tied it very tight around her neck, and she loved it. One day, she went outside to play and when she came back, the scarf was not there anymore. She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find it. Tears filled her eyes and she started to cry.

Her mom saw her crying and asked what was wrong. The girl told her mom about the scarf. Suddenly, her mom bent down and felt around on the ground. She found the scarf! The girl was so excited and hugged her mom very tight.

The mom tied the scarf around the little girl's neck and smiled. She said that she would never lose the scarf again. The little girl wiped her tears away, smiled, and ran off to play. She wore her scarf everywhere, and never forgot to keep it tight.

Once upon a time, there was a funny little frog named Fred. Fred liked to jump and play with his friends in the pond. One day, Fred found a stick. He thought it was a weapon, but it was just a stick.

Fred showed the stick to his friend, the fish. "Look at my weapon!" said Fred. The fish looked at the stick and laughed. "That's not a weapon, that's a stick!" said the fish. "You can't order anyone with that!"

Fred felt silly, but he still had fun playing with the stick. He and the fish took turns tossing the stick in the water and watching it float. They had a great day playing together, and they learned that a stick can be fun, even if it's not a weapon.

Once upon a time, there was a playful little girl named Lily. Lily loved to explore and test things - she found it very fun!

One day, Lily wanted to explore and test something new. She saw a bottle and knew she had to try it! She opened up the top and looked inside. There was nothing inside but air.

Lily decided to test it further. She grabbed the bottle and ran around the room. She shook it and spun it around. She laughed as the bottle made funny noises.

Lily then went outside and tested her bottle some more. She threw it in the air and watched it tumble back down. She blew into the bottle and made music.

Lily had so much fun testing her bottle and discovering the different things it could do. From that day onwards, she never stopped testing and exploring - it was her favorite thing to do!

Once upon a time, there was a kind boy named Tim. Tim lived in a small village near a big forest. Tim loved to play in the forest and collect lumber. One day, Tim went to the forest and found a big pile of lumber. He was so happy and started to collect it.

Suddenly, a big bear appeared and scared Tim. The bear was angry and said, "Why are you taking my lumber? I will punish you!" Tim was scared and said, "I didn't know it was yours. I'm sorry. Please don't punish me."

The bear thought for a moment and said, "Okay, I won't punish you this time. But next time, make sure you ask before taking my lumber." Tim nodded his head and thanked the bear for being kind. From that day on, Tim always asked before taking lumber from the forest.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the pool. Lily can swim very well. Ben is learning to swim. He is persistent. He tries hard every day.

One day, Lily and Ben see a big piece of cheese floating in the pool. They are curious. They want to taste it. They swim towards it.

"Who put cheese in the pool?" Lily asks.

"I don't know. Maybe it fell from the sky," Ben says.

They reach the cheese. They take a bite. It is not cheese. It is soap. It tastes bad. They spit it out.

"Yuck! This is not cheese. This is soap. It makes bubbles in my mouth," Lily says.

"Me too. It is icky. Let's throw it away," Ben says.

They throw the soap out of the pool. They rinse their mouths with water. They laugh.

"That was a silly cheese. It tricked us," Lily says.

"Yes, it did. But we are smart. We know cheese is not soap," Ben says.

They swim away. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a ship. It was a big, strong ship. It sailed through the blue sky and the bright sea.

The ship had a job. It had to observe the land and take pictures. It was also very flexible. It could move quickly and make big turns.

One day, the ship spotted something big and bright on the sea. It flew closer to observe. It was an island! The island was full of trees, animals and plants - it was so exciting!

The ship took lots of pictures of the island. It used its flexible wings to fly up and over the island. It was such a fun day!

At the end of the day, the ship flew back to its home. It had done its job and taken lots of amazing pictures.

Sara liked to play with her dolls in the park. She had many dolls and she gave them names and clothes. She was happy when she played with her dolls.

One day, a boy came to the park. He had a big truck and he made loud noises. He said, "Vroom, vroom, crash, bang!" He drove his truck near Sara and her dolls. He did not see them and he hit them with his truck. Sara's dolls fell down and some of their clothes came off.

Sara was sad and angry. She said, "Hey, you are bad! You hurt my dolls! Go away!" The boy stopped his truck and looked at Sara. He said, "Sorry, I did not see your dolls. I like to play with my truck. It is fun and loud."

Sara said, "But your truck is not fun for me. It is loud and scary. It makes me and my dolls unhappy. You should play somewhere else." The boy said, "But I like this park. It has grass and trees and flowers. And I want to play with you. You have many dolls. They are pretty and soft. Can I play with you and your dolls?"

Sara thought for a moment. She did not like the boy's truck, but she liked the park too. And she liked to play with other children. She said, "OK, you can play with me and my dolls. One day, a little girl was talking to her mommy. She said, "Mommy, why do I have to worry? What is worry?" Her mommy said, "Worry is when you feel sad and scared about something." The little girl said, "Oh, ok. What can I do if I worry?"

Her mommy said, "Well, one thing you can do is look at a picture. A picture can make you feel better if you're worried, because it helps you to feel calm. So just look at a picture that you like, and it will make you feel better."

The little girl said, "Ok!" She went to get a picture from her bedroom. She picked out a dirty, old picture that she liked. She looked at it and smiled. She was no longer worried. 

The little girl stuck the picture on her wall. She looked at it every day when she was feeling scared or worried. The picture helped her to feel brave, strong, and happy.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park. She saw her friend Tom playing with a hoop. Lily wanted to play with the hoop too. She asked Tom, "Can you give me the hoop, please?" Tom said, "No, I am playing with it now."

Lily wanted to play with her scooter. She liked to go fast and make turns. She put on her helmet and went outside. She saw her friend Ben on the sidewalk. He had a ball.

Once upon a time there was a mommy cat and a baby cat. They both had big eyes and fluffy fur. The baby cat was so cute and original. The mommy cat loved her baby cat so very much. Every morning the mommy cat would rock the baby cat in her arms. The baby cat felt so cozy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved animals so much! One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a beautiful dove. The dove was white and had pretty feathers. Lily thought the dove was sweet.

Once upon a time, there was a bee who liked to dream. He dreamed of flying and exploring the world, but the other bees said he was too slow. He sat on a leaf and sighed. Once upon a time, there was a smart little mouse named Timmy. Timmy lived in a cozy hole in the wall of a big house. One day, Timmy saw a big sack in the kitchen. He wanted to explore it, but it was too high up. So, Timmy climbed inch by inch up a chair to reach the sack.

Once upon a time, there was a pond. In the pond there lived a fierce creature. He liked to swim around and kept all of the other creatures in the pond away. Every day, he swam around and around, looking for something to share.

Once upon a time, two friends were walking through the woods. It was getting dark and it was getting scary. Suddenly the two friends heard a noise. It sounded like something was rising.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the snow. One day, he went outside and it was very cold. He forgot his coat and he started to freeze. His mom said, "Timmy, always wear your coat when it's cold outside. It will keep you warm."

Once upon a time, there was a dirty dog named Max. Max liked to dig in the mud and play with his friends. One day, Max found a big, shiny thing in the dirt. It was an axe. Max did not know what it was, but he thought it was fun to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a baby who lived in a house with his mommy and daddy. They loved him very much and wanted him to be very happy.

Once upon a time there was a large thumb. The thumb was very insistent and wanted to do something fun. So it decided to go on an adventure.

The frog grabbed the thumb with its long, slimy tongue and tugged it into the pond. The thumb was so excited that it could finally explore the deep pool.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved the summer. He loved to go outside and play in the warm sun. He often made cheerful toys with the sand, and he practiced singing and dancing for his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Dave. Dave was three years old. Dave liked to learn about life. One day, he asked his mom what life was like. His mom told him it was a very attractive thing and it was important to understand it. Dave thought that sounded interesting. So, he decided to go outside and explore life. 

He found the most fascinating thing he had ever seen. It was a big, colorful butterfly. Dave thought the butterfly looked very attractive. He wanted to understand how it was alive. He watched the butterfly as it flew gracefully in the sunlight. Dave was amazed by the beauty of life.

Then, he heard a buzzing sound and saw a little bee. Dave wanted to understand how the bee could fly. He watched the bee as it flew around and around. Dave was so inspired by how much life he saw around him. 

Finally, Dave came to a conclusion. Life was a beautiful and fascinating thing. Dave was so happy he had the chance to understand it. He ran back to his mom to tell her about all the amazing things he had learned about life.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey. The monkey liked to eat bananas. One day, the monkey went for a jog in the jungle. The monkey saw a big, fine banana tree. The monkey climbed up the tree and ate some bananas. The monkey was happy and went home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big, pink cat. The cat was very proud. She liked to walk around the town and show off her pretty pink fur. Everyone would look at her and smile. The pink cat was very happy.

One day, the pink cat heard a little bird singing. The bird had a beautiful voice. The cat wanted to hear more, so she followed the sound. She found the bird sitting on a tree branch, singing a happy song.

The pink cat and the little bird became friends. They played together every day. The cat was proud to have a friend with such a pretty voice. The bird was happy to have a big, pink friend. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there lived a painter. He was a very clumsy painter and often knocked things over when he was working. One day he was painting a window when he accidentally knocked over his paint bucket.

"Oh no!" he cried as he watched the paint spill all over the floor.

Just then his friend, a goat, came over to help him. "Let's leave the mess for now," the goat said. "Come on, I know a better place to paint."

The painter agreed, so he left the spilled paint and followed the goat. As they walked, the goat pointed out things for the painter to paint. Soon enough, they reached the more perfect spot for the painter to work. 

The painter smiled and thanked his friend. He unpacked his painting supplies and began to work. The clumsy painter was careful not to tip over his paint bucket this time. He continued to paint until the sun was setting and he was finished.

The painter smiled as he admired his work. He waved goodbye to his friend and headed home with a happy heart.

Once upon a time there was a poor temple. The temple was very old and had many broken pieces. People used to come and pray.

One day, a little girl called Amy came to visit the temple. She looked around and imagined what it must have been like when the temple was first built. She closed her eyes and saw colourful flags and animals roaming around the temple.

Amy wanted to help the poor temple, so she decided to take some of her pocket money and use it to buy some flowers and new flags. She decorated the temple and suddenly it seemed very bright and beautiful.

People started to come to the temple again, and were amazed by the changes. They thanked Amy for her hard work and thanked her for bringing life back to the old temple.

Amy had done a wonderful job and was very proud of herself. She had imagined a better temple and with a little hard work and help from her community, Amy had made her dream come true.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Pete. He was only three years old and always wanted to help his dad. One day, Pete's dad said, "Time to load the truck, Pete!" So Pete went out to the truck and started loading it with boxes.

Pete was having trouble lifting the heavy boxes, so his dad came out and said, "Here, let me help." He picked up the biggest box, and Pete was so happy to help.

Pete ran to the shed to get the hammer so they could seal the box shut. His dad patiently waited while Pete looked for the hammer. When Pete finally found it, he said excitedly, "Here it is!"

His dad said, "Thank you Pete, now let's get to work and load the truck."

Pete was eager to help, so he impatiently began hammering the box shut. His dad stopped him and said, "Pete, let me help. You need to be careful, you could break the hammer."

Pete smiled and let his dad take over. Together, they loaded the truck and were able to finish just in time for the big trip.

Once, there was a boy called Tom. He liked to go outside and run around his garden. One day, he noticed that some of his toys were gone. He wondered where they had gone.

He saw a fox with a toy in his mouth, going over the fence. Tom wanted to get his toy back. He was very sad. But then he had a great idea! He got a camera and he recorded the fox.

The next day, the fox was back again. But this time, Tom was ready. He had built a new fence around his garden. The fox could no longer get in. Tom was very proud of his fence. It was very tall and very fine.

Tom was so happy and proud. He recorded it so he could show it to all his friends. He was sure that they would love to see it, just like he did.

Once upon a time, in a big pond, there lived an alligator. His name was Al. Al was an incredible alligator who had many friends.

One day, Al and his friends played in the pond. They splashed and laughed. The sun was warm and everyone was happy. Al's friends were glad that he was so incredible and fun.

As the sun went down, Al and his friends went home. They said "bye" and hugged. Al was happy to have such good friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sarah. She loved to skip. She skipped everywhere - inside her house, outside her house, around the block and even in the rain!

Today, Sarah wanted to skip in the kitchen. She skipped around the table and hopped over to the faucet. It was bright purple and made Sarah so happy. She felt silly, so she talked to the faucet.

"Hi, Faucet," she said. "You're so purple! I love skipping around you."

The faucet wasn't very loud, but it answered in a small voice.

"Thank you, Sarah," it said. "I like it when you skip. Please keep skipping around me."

So Sarah kept skipping around the faucet. Faster and faster she skipped until the faucet was a blur of purple spinning around her. She giggled and skipped and twirled until she was too tired to keep going.

"That was so much fun," Sarah said and gave the faucet a big smile. "Let's skip again soon!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe. He was a happy three year old. One day, Joe was looking at his calendar. He frowned. Something didn't smell right. It was smelly!

He asked his mom, "What that smell?"

"Honey, it's the trash!" His mom replied.

Joe frowned again. He was confused. He asked, "Why it smelly?"

His mom smiled. "It's time to take out the garbage. Come help me, Joe."

Joe shook his head. He was still confused but he followed his mom. Together they took out the smelly garbage and threw it out in the trash bin.

Joe's mom smiled. "See, that wasn't so hard. Now the smell is gone!"

Joe smiled and gave his mom a big hug. He was happy that the smelly trash was gone. And he learned an important lesson about taking out the garbage.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lucy. One day, her mummy gave her a string. Lucy was very happy. She loved to play with the string. She moved it from side to side, making different shapes. Sadly, the string broke. Lucy was sad. She pouted and frowned.

Mummy gave Lucy some glue. She showed Lucy how to use it and also gave her a paintbrush. Together they glued the string back together. When the glue and string were dry, Lucy showed her mummy the new string. It was shiny and fixed.

Lucy was happy again. She thanked her mummy and put the string away safely. Her mummy was pleased that Lucy had fixed her broken string.

Once upon a time, in a fair, sunny land, there was a big bear named Bob. Bob loved to eat honey. He would find honey in the trees and eat it all day. The sweet taste made him very happy.

One day, Bob met a small bee named Betty. Betty did not like Bob, because he ate all the honey. She would say, "I hate that you take our honey, Bob." But Bob did not care. He just wanted to eat more honey.

Betty wanted to teach Bob a lesson. She gathered all her bee friends and they made a plan. The next time Bob tried to eat honey, the bees buzzed and stung him. It hurt, and Bob ran away. He learned to share the honey with the bees and not be greedy. From that day on, Bob and Betty became friends, and they all lived happily in the fair, sunny land.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard. It was big and green with smooth grass. Lily liked to run and jump around in it.

One day, Lily saw her neighbor's toy and she wanted to play with it. She asked her neighbor if she could play with it, but the neighbor said no. Lily was sad and went back to her backyard. 

But then, Lily remembered something her mom had told her. She remembered that it's not nice to take things that don't belong to you. Lily decided to be a good girl and not take her neighbor's toy. She gained something very important that day - the value of being honest and respectful.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little angel. She wanted to fly around the world and make it a better place. She had seen many people fighting and not being nice to each other and she wanted to fix it.

So one day she flew down to earth, and saw a group of people around a big tree. They were all yelling and not listening to each other. 

The brave angel flew towards a little boy standing near the tree.

"What's wrong?" asked the angel.

The boy looked at her, surprised. Then he said, "My friends and I were playing, but we can't agree how to fix our game. Nobody can find an idea that works."

The angel thought for a moment. Then she said, "Let's make a picture instead! Then everyone can work together and make something beautiful to remember your day."

The boy smiled and told his friends. They all started working together, drawing pictures and making up stories. Soon they had made a wonderful mural on the side of the tree.

The brave angel flew away, knowing she had done something to make the world a little bit better.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bunny named Rosie. Rosie was glad because she had lots of friends to play with. One day, Rosie and her friends went to a field to play. The sun was very bright and Rosie had to blink her eyes a lot. Suddenly, Rosie saw a big pink flower in the field. She was so happy to see it that she started to hop towards it. When she got closer, she saw that the flower was as big as her! Rosie was so glad to have found such a beautiful flower. She blinked her eyes again and again, looking at the pink petals.
