Rosie's friends came over and saw the flower too. They were all amazed and glad to see it. From that day on, Rosie and her friends visited the pink flower often, and they were always glad to see it.

David was so excited for his new bed. He ran through the toy store and pointed with excitement at the bright yellow bed that he wanted to buy. His mom smiled and decided to buy it for him. 

When they got home they put the bed together in David's room. He was so proud of it and spent a few hours playing with his toys in it. 

But as the night grew darker, David started to be tired so his mom decided it was time for bed. She tucked him in, but when she closed the door, David thought he saw some things move around in his bed. He was scared so he decided to ignore it. 

In the morning, when David woke up, he saw his room was a big mess. His bed was the messiest of all, with toys everywhere. David was very sad because he knew his mom wouldn't be happy. He had decided to invite some of his toys into his bed and that is why it was such a mess. 

He knew he had made a bad decision and he didn't know how his mom would react. She was very angry when she saw the mess and knew it was all because of David's decision. He was so sorry that he couldn't undo what he had done.

Once upon a time there was a perfect little mouse. The mouse lived in a big, tall tree. One day, the mouse wanted to find some food. So, the mouse ran and ran, looking for something to eat.

But then, the mouse saw a scary cat coming closer and closer! The mouse was scared and ran away. But the cat was very fast. The mouse was about to be caught!

But then, a kind knight came and saved the mouse! The knight scooped up the mouse up in his arms, and quickly took it away from the cat.

The mouse was so happy and thanked the knight for saving it. From then on, the mouse was very safe and happy to be alive. The knight had saved the perfect little mouse!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint with her fingers and make colorful pictures. One day, she decided to paint her leg with her favorite color, pink. She thought it looked beautiful and graceful.

But then, she accidentally spilled paint all over the floor. Her mom slipped on it and hurt her leg. Lily felt very sad and guilty. She apologized to her mom and tried to clean up the mess, but it was too late. Her mom had to go to the hospital and get a cast on her leg.

Lily learned that even though painting can be fun, it's important to be careful and not make a mess. She promised to always be more careful in the future.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a peanut on the ground. Tom picks it up and looks at it.

"What is this?" he asks Mia.

Mia knows what it is. She likes to eat peanuts. She explains to Tom.

"This is a peanut. It is a kind of food. You can eat it, but you have to peel it first. It has a rough skin that you have to take off. Inside, it has a soft and yummy part. Do you want to try?"

Tom is curious. He wants to try the peanut. He tries to peel it, but it is hard. He asks Mia for help.

"Can you help me peel it? It is too rough for me."

Mia helps Tom peel the peanut. She gives him half of it. They both eat it and smile.

"Mmm, this is good. Thank you for explaining, Mia. You are a good friend."

Tom and Mia are happy. They share the other half of the peanut. Then they go back to playing in the park. They have fun.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She always felt a bit lonely. One day, she was walking down the street and saw a pastry shop. It was the most beautiful place she had ever seen. She wanted to go inside, so she slowly leaned forward and opened the door.

Inside, the pastry shop was full of delicious goodies. She could smell the sweet smell of pastry. She smiled, feeling much less lonely.

She decided to get herself a treat. She leaned forward and stared at all the pastries in the display case. She saw a pink macaron and could not resist. She handed her money to the storekeeper and received the delicious macaron.

Sarah sat down outside the store and ate her macaron. She felt so happy and content that she didn't want to leave. But soon enough, the sun began to set. She picked up her bag, leaned forward, and waved goodbye to the storekeeper.

The next day, Sarah returned to the pastry shop. Her macaron had made her feel less lonely, after all. She leaned forward, opened the door, and stepped inside.

Once there was a girl named Letty. She was three years old and liked to play. She was playing with her toys one day when she heard a noise. She was scared.

Suddenly, a big coin appeared. It was shining in the sun. She wanted to add it to her toy collection, so she reached out her hand and grabbed it.

Letty was so happy to have a new coin. She played with it all day and showed it to all the people she knew. She even pretended it was magical.

At the end of the day, Letty put the coin in a special box with all her other toys. She knew that she would have something special to add to her collection.

Tom and Lily love to perform for their family. They like to sing, dance and tell jokes. They make everyone laugh and clap.

One day, they decide to perform outside in nature. They find a big tree and use it as a stage. They pick some flowers and leaves and make costumes. They invite their mom, dad and dog to watch.

Tom sings a song about a funny frog. He hops and croaks and sticks out his tongue. Lily dances a dance about a funny bird. She flaps and chirps and spins around. They both tell jokes about funny animals. They make their family laugh and clap.

They have so much fun performing in nature. They hug their mom, dad and dog and say thank you. They are happy and proud. They love to perform.

George and Rachel were playing catch in the backyard. George was so excited that he stopped to yawn. Suddenly, a flood of water came rushing down the street. Rachel felt embarrassed and wanted to hide, but George wanted to play in the water. He yelled, "Let's go in!" So, Rachel took a deep breath, held onto George's hand, and they jumped into the flood! They laughed and jumped up and down while the water covered their toes. After they were done, they both felt tired and Rachel even yawned again. George and Rachel were so happy with their adventure, they couldn't wait to tell their parents all about it.

Lily and Ben were twins who loved to visit the sea. They liked to watch the big boats and the small fish. They also liked to play with the sand and the shells.

One day, they saw a shiny thing in the water. It was an anchor. It was very big and heavy. Lily and Ben wanted to touch it.

"Let's go and see the anchor," Lily said.

"But it is too deep," Ben said. "We can't swim there."

Lily was brave. She said, "We can use this rope. It is long and strong. We can tie it to the anchor and pull it out."

Ben was scared. He said, "No, Lily, it is too hard. We might get hurt. And what if the boat comes back and wants the anchor?"

Lily did not listen. She took the rope and ran to the water. She threw the rope over the anchor and tried to pull it out. But the anchor was too heavy. Lily could not move it. She pulled and pulled, but the rope only got tighter around her hand.

"Help, Ben, help!" Lily cried. "The rope is hurting me. I can't get free."

Ben heard Lily's cry. He was scared, but he was also brave. He ran to the water and saw Lily's hand. He took a knife from his pocket and cut the rope. He freed Lily's hand and hugged her.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked.

"Yes, Ben, I'm okay. Thank you for saving me. You are very brave," Lily said.

They ran back to the shore and told their mom what happened. Their mom was angry and worried. She scolded them for being foolish and careless. She also hugged them and kissed them. She was glad they were safe.

She said, "Lily and Ben, you are brave, but you are also silly. You should never play with things that are not yours. And you should never go near the water without me. The sea is beautiful, but it is also dangerous. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "Yes, mom, we understand. We are sorry. We love you."

They learned their lesson. They never played with the anchor again. They still liked to visit the sea, but they always stayed with their mom. They also always said hello to the boat and the fish. They were happy and careful.

Once upon a time there was a bald man who wanted to build something special. He worked very hard on it every day and when he was finished, he had built a big medal. He was so proud of his medal and he wanted to show it off! 

He brought the medal to a show and everyone was so impressed. They all clapped and smiled and said that he had done an amazing job. The bald man felt really happy and everyone wanted to take pictures with his medal. 

The bald man had built something really special and his medal was now famous! He was so proud that he had made it himself and it was a great reminder that with hard work, you could achieve anything.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who wanted to buy something special. He had a rare barn and wanted to give it an extra sparkle. So he went out to buy the perfect thing.

The farmer searched and searched, but nothing seemed quite right. Then, he stumbled upon something quite unique - a shiny diamond! It was so rare, the farmer knew this was the perfect thing to put in his barn.

The farmer bought the diamond and took it back to his barn. To his surprise, when the diamond was placed in the barn it lit up the entire space â€“ like a never ending twinkle! Everyone who had visited the farm was in awe of this magical sight. The barn had become rarer than ever before!

The farmer was so happy with his purchase. He now had a truly special barn, better than ever before. And so, the farmer and the diamond lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to clap her hands and dance around. One day, Lily went to a lecture with her mom. The lecture was about being kind to others. 

But Lily thought the lecture was weird. She didn't understand why they needed to talk about being kind. She already knew how to be kind! 

After the lecture, Lily and her mom went to the park. There, they saw a boy who was sad because he had lost his toy. Lily remembered the lecture and decided to be kind. She helped the boy look for his toy and they found it together. 

Lily realized that even though she already knew how to be kind, it was important to hear the lecture and be reminded of it. From then on, she always listened carefully to the lectures and tried to be kind to everyone she met.

Once upon a time, there was a big orange tree. The tree had lots of oranges on it. The oranges were so yummy and juicy. 

One day, a little girl came by the tree. She saw the oranges and wanted to eat them. She waved at the tree and said "Hi tree, can I have an orange please?" 

The tree was very kind and rich with oranges. It gave the little girl an orange to eat. The little girl was very happy and said "Thank you, tree. This orange is so yummy!" She ate the orange and then went on her way. 

From that day on, the little girl would come back to the orange tree and wave hello. The tree was always happy to see her and would give her more oranges to eat. The little girl loved the orange tree and the yummy oranges it gave her.

Once upon a time, there was a big, furry bear named Bobo. Bobo was a very nice bear who lived in the woods. One day, he looked up at the sky and saw the big, round moon. Bobo thought the moon was very pretty.

Bobo wanted to show his friend, Bunny, the moon. He went to Bunny's house and said, "Bunny, come see the big moon!" Bunny hopped outside and looked at the moon. Bunny said, "Wow, Bobo! The moon is so pretty!"

But then, Bobo did something silly. He tried to jump up and touch the moon. He jumped and jumped, but he couldn't reach it. Bunny laughed and said, "Silly Bobo, you can't touch the moon!" Bobo felt embarrass, but he laughed too. They both had fun looking at the moon together.

One day, a white owl lived in a big tree. The white owl loved to fly at night and look for food. The white owl had a friend, a small brown mouse. They liked to play together in the forest.

One day, the white owl saw a big, red apple on the ground. The white owl wanted to share the apple with the small brown mouse. But the apple was not good. It was old and it had started to rot. The white owl did not know that the apple was bad.

The white owl and the small brown mouse ate the bad apple. Soon, they both felt sick. They were very sad because they could not play together in the forest anymore. The white owl and the small brown mouse learned that they should not eat food that is old and rotten.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. He was 3 years old and loved playing outside with his friends.

One day, Jack and his friends had a big fight. At first, Jack was brave and tried to sort things out. But soon, he became embarrassed and his cheeks turned red. 

Jack's friends could see how sad he looked, so they decided to forgive him and stop fighting. Jack smiled and said "Thank you, I'm happy we solved this without a fight."

Everyone smiled and ran off to play. From that day on, Jack was excited to go out and play with his friends again.

Jane had a zebra. She loved it very much. But one day, the zebra had to leave. Jane was sad and she was very embarrassed. She didn't want the zebra to go. She asked her mom why the zebra had to leave. Mom said the zebra was going to a new home, so it could make more friends. Jane felt better knowing the zebra was just going away for a little while. She said goodbye to the zebra, and wished it a safe trip. 

Now, Jane remembers the zebra with fondness. She knows that it has found new friends, and is happy in its new home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys every day. One day, she found a playful puppy in her yard. Lily wanted to play with the puppy, but the puppy was too small and couldn't lift its paw.

Lily said, "I wish you could play with me, little puppy."

The puppy barked and said, "I want to play too, but I can't lift my paw."

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Let's play catch with this ball. You can use your nose to push it to me."

The puppy was excited and they played catch for hours. They became best friends and played together every day. Lily learned that even if someone can't do something, there is always a way to have fun and play together.

Once there was a little boy. His name was Tom. Tom was very selfish. He never wanted to share his lunch, even if his friends asked. 

One day, Tom went to school and brought his lunch with him. All of his friends were eating the same lunch, but Tom kept his lunch all to himself. 

Tom's friends felt bad because they didn't have their own lunch and didn't get to eat. They asked to have a bit of Tom's lunch, but he said no. 

Tom felt like his lunch belonged only to him and he didn't want to share it. 

His teacher saw what was happening and told Tom that sharing was important and that everyone should have a chance to eat. Tom thought about it and slowly, he started to share his lunch. 

He soon realised that when you share your lunch, everyone belongs and feels like they are part of the group. So, from that day on, Tom always made sure to share his lunch with everyone.

Mommy told Frannie to go to bed, but she didn't want to quit playing with her toy. She kept playing and playing with it, until it grew very dead. She started to cry, because she wanted her toy to be alive again. 

Mommy held her and said, "It's ok Frannie, we can find you a new toy." She dried Frannie's tears and looked around the room until she found a new toy, a beautiful car. 

Frannie was so happy, she hugged Mommy and said, "Thank you Mommy!" She was so excited to play with the new car, that she forgot all about the old toy. She quickly quit crying and enjoyed playing with her new car.

Once upon a time there was a big exam. It was hard for some of the kids, but not for Susie. She was going to pass it easily!

Susie studied hard for the exam. Every day she printed out notes so she could learn them. Slowly and steadily, she was learning more and more.

On the day of the exam, Susie felt soft and calm. She carefully printed her answers and smiled when she was done. She knew she had done well.

When the results came out, Susie was very proud. She had gotten the highest marks in the class! Everyone was so proud of her. They cheered and hugged her, and Susie was the happiest girl in the world!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She was three and she loved to bake. Every day, she would put on her bright red apron and bake all sorts of things in her kitchen. 

One day, Mia said to her mom "I'm gonna bake a heel, Mommy! Can you help me?" Her mom said "Yes, I can help you bake a heel. What kind of heel do you want?" Mia said, "I want a black heel. Can you get the ingredients we need?"

Her mom went to the grocery store and got all the ingredients they needed to make the black heel. 

When they got home, they started mixing the ingredients and put it in the oven. While they waited, Mia's mom said "Be careful, the heel might be hot when it's done." 

Mia said "I can't wait to see the black heel!" finally, the black heel was done. It smelled delicious. They both took it out of the oven and they both looked at the beautiful black heel. Mia was so happy she couldn't contain herself.

They both tasted the delicious heel. It was hot and sweet, just like Mia had dreamed.  Mia smiled and said, "I love it!" 

Mia and her mom shared the black heel and enjoyed it together. It was the best heel Mia had ever baked.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot liked to gaze at the big, blue sky. He liked to see the white clouds and the bright sun.

One day, Spot went for a walk. He found a path in the forest. The path was long, but Spot felt safe. He liked to walk on the path and see the pretty trees.

As Spot walked on the path, he met a big, friendly bear. The bear said, "Hello, Spot! Let's be friends." Spot and the bear walked on the path together, feeling safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her marbles. One day, she found a big, shiny marble that was very flexible. She could squish it and it would bounce back to its original shape. 

Lily decided to show her marble to her pet cat, Mittens. She fed Mittens some cat food and then showed her the marble. Mittens was very interested and Lily let her play with it for a little while. 

After a while, Lily took the marble back and put it in her pocket. She went outside to play with her friends and they all played with marbles together. Lily's friends were amazed by her flexible marble and they all wanted one too. 

Lily was happy to share her marble with her friends and they all had fun playing with it. When it was time to go home, Lily put the marble back in her pocket and said goodbye to her friends. She couldn't wait to play with her marble again tomorrow. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. One day, he found a big cabinet in his house. He opened it and saw a lot of colorful jars inside. Timmy wanted to touch them, but his mom told him to be careful.

Timmy tried to be careful, but he accidentally knocked over one of the jars. It made a loud sound and his mom came running. She was very angry and told Timmy to go to his room. Timmy felt sad and wished he had been more careful.

The lesson Timmy learned was to always listen to his mom and be careful. He promised to be more careful in the future. From that day on, Timmy would clap his hands whenever he remembered to be careful.

Lily and Sam love to play theater. They have a big box that they put in the living room. They cut out a hole for the stage. They use their toys and clothes to make the actors and the costumes. They invite their mom and dad to watch their show.

Today, they are doing a show about a princess and a dragon. Lily is the princess and Sam is the dragon. Lily wears a pink dress and a crown. Sam wears a green shirt and a mask. They make up the story as they go along. The princess is sad because the dragon took her castle. The dragon is lonely because he has no friends. They talk and sing and act.

Mom and dad clap and cheer. They are very proud of Lily and Sam. They say they are very good at theater. They give them a hug and a kiss. They also give them a generous gift. They put two tickets in their hands. The tickets are for a real theater show. Lily and Sam are very happy and excited. They say thank you and they love you. They can't wait to see the real theater show. They put their tickets in a safe place. They hug their mom and dad again. They are very lucky to have such a generous family.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw pictures in his notebook. His notebook was hard and had a red cover. One day, Timmy's little sister, Lily, wanted to draw in his notebook too. But Timmy didn't want her to because he thought she would ruin his drawings.

Lily felt sad and didn't understand why Timmy wouldn't share. So, she decided to measure her own notebook to show Timmy that it was just as good as his. But Timmy still didn't want to share. This made Lily very upset and she started to cry.

Their mom came in and saw what was happening. She explained to Timmy that it was important to share and that Lily's notebook was just as special as his. Timmy finally understood and they all ended up drawing together in Lily's notebook. From that day on, Timmy learned to share and they all had fun drawing together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she saw her friend, Timmy, spraying water from a bottle. Lily asked, "Can I spray too?"

Timmy said, "Sure, let's spray the flowers!" They sprayed the flowers and had fun. Suddenly, they heard a bell ringing. It was time to go home. 

Lily's mom asked, "Did you have fun today, Lily?" Lily replied, "Yes, we sprayed the flowers and heard a bell." Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you had an organized playtime with your friends."

Once upon a time there was a smart girl named Sam. She was very intelligent and loved to play, dance and run. One day she decided to ignore her friends and go to the park on her own.

At the park, Sam saw many other kids playing and laughing. She wanted to join in the fun too, but they ignored her. Feeling lonely, Sam watched the other kids playing, and felt more and more sad until finally she went home.

That night, Sam made a plan. She decided that tomorrow she would be brave, so that when she went back to the park her friends would no longer ignore her.

The next day, Sam went back to the park and said hello to everyone. They were surprised and welcomed her with open arms. From then on, no one ignored Sam again. They all had fun playing together and soon became best friends. 

Sam was proud of herself for being brave and making friends. She proved that being intelligent and positive can help turn a bad day into a fun one.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Bob and Sally. They liked to play games together. One day they were playing a game that was very tough. Bob wanted to keep playing but Sally thought it was too hard and wanted to quit. 

Bob tried to talk Sally into staying, but she just shook her head. She said she was tired and wanted to quit. Bob felt disappointed, but still wanted to be friends. So he promised Sally they could find another game later. 

That made Sally smile. She said goodbye to Bob and they hugged. Bob said they should find an easier game the next time they played. Sally agreed with Bob and went home. 

Bob went to find a new game and soon found one that was fun but not too tough. Now he and Sally can play this game together and have lots of fun. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy who liked to daydream. Every day, she would close her eyes and pretend to be a star of her own movie and she was always so happy!

One day, Daisy told her mommy about her dreams. â€œMummy, I want to be in a real film!â€ She said. â€œOh, Daisy, thatâ€™s a big dreamâ€ her mommy said. â€œBut if youâ€™re persistent, you can make it happen!â€

Then, Daisy and her mommy went to the park and Daisy imagined what a real film would be like. She thought about all the people who would help make it come alive. She felt so excited!

The next day, Daisy wrote a letter to a famous movie director and asked for his help to bring her dreams to life.

Months passed and Daisy almost forgot about her letter but then, one day, the director wrote back! He said he could help Daisy make her dream come true!

Today, Daisy is living her dream and she is one of the stars in her very own movie! Daisy is so proud of her hard work and her persistence really paid off!

Once upon a time, there was a garden. It was special, because it was full of wonderful things like flowers, butterflies, bees and birds. Every day, the garden looked more and more beautiful.

One morning, the garden keeper had an idea. He decided to scatter some special seeds all over the garden. Then he watered the garden and waited for them to grow.

The seeds soon turned into tall, bright flowers. Everyone was so happy and said that the garden keeper had been very successful.

Now, when people walk by the garden, they look at the beautiful flowers and remember how the garden keeper scattered the seeds. The garden is a happy place, full of beauty and life.

Once upon a time there was a dog. His name was Max. He was a very brave dog. He loved to protect his family. Max had an important job. His job was to guard the number. He had the number hidden in his collar.

Max was very funny. He liked to play in the park with the kids. He liked to bark and make them laugh. 

One day Max heard a strange noise outside. He went outside to see what it was. There was a big mean bear. He wanted to get the number from Max. Max kept barking and growling. He was trying to protect the number.

The little kids in the neighbourhood were scared. They asked Max to help them. Max barked and scared away the bear. The kids were very happy. 

Max was the bravest and funniest dog ever! He protected the number and the kids were safe.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named May who had a pet rabbit. May loved her rabbit and enjoyed playing with her every day.

One day, the rabbit spotted something new in the backyard. She dug a dry hole in the ground with her paws and found something shiny. May ran over to the rabbit, looked in the hole, and saw it was full of carrots! 

May was so excited that she asked the rabbit, "do you want to share the carrots?" But the rabbit shook her head and said, "No! I hate carrots, they're yucky!"

May laughed and said, "Well, if you don't want the carrots, can I have them?" But the rabbit said, "No, I don't want them either. The hole is mine and I found it first!"

May huffed and puffed but knew the rabbit had found the hole and it was only fair. So she said, "OK, we will both keep the hole and you can do whatever you want with it."

The rabbit proudly hopped away, knowing her hole was safe, and May and her rabbit played happily the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Alex. She was only three years old and loved running around outside.

One day, Alex went to the park. She climbed a tree and perched high in the branches. From her vantage point, she looked down and saw something sparkly around the base of the tree. 

Alex carefully climbed down and noticed it was a spirit made of shiny silver stars. The spirit smiled brightly at Alex and said, "Hello, my name is John. I am very, very busy but I wanted to say hi." Alex was so excited to meet the spirit! 

John asked Alex if she wanted to join him on an adventure. She happily agreed, so the two set off. They went for a long walk, then stopped for a nap under a big tree. After a few minutes, the two were up and running again. Alex had the best time spending the day with John!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and her favorite toy was a pink teddy bear. One day, she went to the park with her mom and lost her teddy bear.

Lily was very sad and cried a lot. Her mom tried to comfort her and said, "Don't worry, we will find your teddy bear. Let's look for it together." They searched the park but couldn't find the teddy bear anywhere.

Suddenly, Lily saw a pale man with a hat walking away from them. She pointed at him and said, "Mommy, that man has my teddy bear!" But it was too late, the man had already left with the teddy bear.

Lily's mom tried to prevent her from chasing after the man, but Lily was too upset and ran after him. Unfortunately, the man was too fast and Lily couldn't catch up. She returned to her mom crying even more.

From that day on, Lily learned to take better care of her things and never let them out of her sight. But she never forgot her favorite teddy bear and always wondered where it went.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was so excited, and she had something very special to do. She went to the shop with her mom. 

The little girl saw something she wanted to buy, it was a rabbit. She asked Mom if she could buy it, and Mom said yes.

The rabbit was so friendly! The little girl was so happy. She hugged it and said, "Hi, Rabbit, I'm your friend."

The rabbit was so happy too. The little girl took it home and she fed it and played with it. The rabbit was so happy to have a new friend.

The little girl and the rabbit became the best of friends. They had so much fun, playing together and cuddling up at night. They were the best of friends forever.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old and very curious.

One day Sarah went to her favorite store with her mom. When they got there, Sarah saw lots of new things. She wanted to try them all, but her mom said no. Sarah started to get upset and refused to leave.

The store staff noticed Sarah and wanted to help. They found a warm, soft blanket and offered it to Sarah. She instantly stopped crying and hugged the blanket. 

The store staff asked Sarah if she wanted to try any of the new toys. She shook her head and said "no". The staff smiled and said, "It's okay if you refuse. We understand." Sarah gave them a big smile and she and her mom left the store. 

Sarah was very happy. She had a warm, soft blanket and she knew the store staff really cared.

Ben and Sam were brothers. They liked to play in their room with their toys. But sometimes they fought over the toys. One day, Ben wanted to play with the big truck, but Sam had it. Ben tried to take it from Sam, but Sam was stronger. He pushed Ben away and said, "No, it's mine!"

Ben was angry. He looked around the room and saw a cloth. He had an idea. He grabbed the cloth and ran to the door. He locked the door with the cloth. He said, "Ha, ha, now you can't get out!"

Sam was scared. He banged on the door and shouted, "Let me out, Ben! Let me out!" But Ben did not listen. He laughed and played with the truck. He thought he was smart.

But he did not know that Mom was coming. She heard the noise and went to the room. She tried to open the door, but it was locked. She asked, "What's going on in there? Who locked the door?"

Ben heard Mom's voice and felt sorry. He realized he was mean to Sam. He said, "I did, Mom. I'm sorry. I locked the door with a cloth."

Mom said, "That was not nice, Ben. You should not lock your brother in the room. You should share your toys. Now, take the cloth off the door and open it."

Ben did what Mom said. He took the cloth off the door and opened it. He saw Sam crying. He said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I was wrong. Do you want to play with the truck?"

Sam nodded and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Ben. I forgive you. Can we play together?"

Ben said, "Yes, we can. I love you, Sam."

They hugged and played with the truck. Mom was happy. She said, "That's better. I'm proud of you, boys. Now, be nice to each other."

The bald man sat in his chair, holding a journal. He was wearing a big, red hat and looked very serious. He read the journal for a long time. Suddenly, he began to cry. His cries were so loud that everyone in the room stopped what they were doing to look at him. 

The bald man kept reading the journal. He cried and cried until his face was all wet and his clothes were all wet too. No one knew what was wrong. Then, the bald man took a deep breath and said, "It's all been a terrible mistake, there's no way to fix it."

The bald man walked out of the room, never to return. Everyone was very worried. What had happened? What was in the journal? No one knew. They all just sat there, feeling sad and worried. 

The bad ending of the story was the bald man's strange behavior and words. What had been the mistake he had made? Would anyone ever find out?

Once upon a time there lived a boy named Joe. Every day Joe would go to the store to get food and drinks. Every day Joe's heart felt a bit heavier because the store was so boring.

One day, Joe decided to go to the store with a plan. He wanted to make the store a bit more fun. When he got there, he looked around. Suddenly, he had an idea.

He asked the cashier, "Can I borrow some crayons?" The cashier said, "Yes, you can." So Joe took the crayons and went around the store. He put a different colour on each shelf. 

When Joe was finished, he stepped back to admire his work. He saw that the store was more pretty and colourful than it had been before. Joe's heart felt happy and much lighter. 

From then on, Joe went to the store with his crayons every week to keep it colourful, and to make sure his heart stayed light.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very sleepy and wanted to go to bed. Her mommy said, "Lily, it's time to sleep now." Lily replied, "Okay, mommy."

As she was sleeping, she heard a loud noise. She woke up and saw a big fire outside her window. She shouted, "Mommy, there's a fire!" Her mommy quickly woke up and called the firefighters.

The firefighters came and put out the fire. Lily was very scared but happy that everyone was safe. Her mommy hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. You're safe now." Lily felt better and went back to sleep.

Once upon a time, there was a tall bookcase. It was filled to the brim with books and other things. Every morning, a little girl with curly brown hair would come to the bookcase and count the things inside it. She would number the books, the stuffed animals, and other objects. She loved to number everything.

One day, her mommy asked her to put all the things away neatly. So, the little girl started using her numbers. She picked up the books and put them on the shelves, counting each one as she went. She counted the stuffed animals and put them in the drawers, counting each one as she placed it inside.

When she was done, she looked at the bookcase and was so proud of herself. She had done a great job of counting and organizing everything. Now it was neat and tidy and she was very happy with her work.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, books, and more. But sometimes their toys are messy. Mom says they have to sort their toys before they can watch TV.

Lily and Ben start to sort their toys. Lily puts the dolls in a pink basket. Ben puts the cars in a blue box. They work together to sort the blocks by color and shape. They put the books on the shelf.

"Look, Mom, we sorted our toys!" Lily says. She is proud of her work.

"Good job, Lily and Ben!" Mom says. She smiles and gives them a hug. "You are very helpful and smart. I love you both."

Lily and Ben hug Mom back. They feel happy and warm. They think Mom is the best.

"Can we watch TV now?" Ben asks.

"Sure, you can watch TV for a little while. But first, let me show you something." Mom says. She takes them to the window and points outside.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily says. She sees a big rainbow in the sky. It has many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.

"It's so pretty!" Ben says. He likes the rainbow.

"It's adorable!" Mom says. She hugs Lily and Ben again. "Just like you two."

Mum and Dad had an exciting surprise for Sarah and her brother, Ben.
Dad said, "Come and look what I've got!" 
He lifted up a box, and there was a new light bulb inside. Sarah and Ben each held one end and lifted it together. Then Dad said, "This light bulb will make your room nice and clean."
Sarah and Ben were so happy and they ran to their room to fit it. 
Mum was watching them with a big smile. She said, "I'm sure your room looks nice and clean now!"
Sarah and Ben both nodded enthusiastically. Then they switched on the light and the room filled with a warm, inviting glow.
From that day on, Sarah and Ben loved telling their friends how their room was so bright and clean.

The windy day was quiet and still. Little Timmy decided to take a walk. As he walked he found something smelly. It was a box! Curious, he opened it to explore. Suddenly a giant dragon flew out of the box! Timmy was so scared, he stood there and couldn't move.

"RRAAAAAAAAWR!" The dragon bellowed.

"I am here to strike!"

Timmy was so scared, he didn't know what to do. Suddenly he heard a wise old voice. It said,

"Do not be afraid, Timmy. Strike the dragon with your courage."

So Timmy gathered up all his courage and shouted,

"No! You will not strike me!"

The dragon was so surprised. He flew away, never to be seen again.

The windy day was quiet again and Timmy felt proud of his bravery.

Once upon a time, there was a big box in the park. A little boy named Tim saw it and wanted to open it. He thought there might be something impressive inside. 

Tim asked his friend, Jane, "Do you want to help me open the box?" Jane said, "Yes! Let's open it together!" So, they both pushed and pulled the box to open it. 

When the box was open, they found a lot of colorful balloons inside. They were so happy with the result! Tim and Jane played with the balloons all day and shared them with their friends. Everyone had a great time.

One day, mommy and daddy took Tom to the park. Tom was very happy. He saw some birds flying in the sky and some squirrels running around. Then he saw something shiny on the ground. It was a copper penny! Tom shouted with delight and ran to pick it up.

Mommy smiled at him and said, "Let's organize your penny with the others!"

Tom ran back over to where his parents were sitting. They had a jar there with other pennies in it. Tom carefully put his penny in the jar and Daddy said, "Let's add another penny to it every day and by the end of the year, we'll have a nice collection. We can be happy together!"

Tom smiled and hugged his parents. He was so lucky to have such a great family. He couldn't wait to organize more pennies with them!

Once upon a time there was a black cat named Pit. Pit was a very curious cat. One day, Pit decided he wanted to explore a big black pit he had seen in the yard. 

Pit's mommy saw him walking towards the pit and shouted, "No, Pit! Don't go in there!" 

But Pit was already standing at the edge of the pit, so he looked up and said, "What is down there?" 

His mommy replied, "It's a big, deep, dark pit. I don't want you to go down there, so please don't." 

But Pit couldn't help himself. He wanted to know what was down there. So he put one paw in and then another and soon he was down in the pit. It was very dark inside, so he felt around. Soon, he found a big black mouse! 

Pit was so excited that he quickly put the mouse in his pocket and climbed back out of the pit. He raced home to show his mommy the mouse. 

His mommy was so pleased with what Pit had done that she gave him a hug and said, "That was very brave of you to go in the pit, Pit!"

Once upon a time, there was a loud man. He wanted to find treasure. So he went looking for it everywhere. He asked everyone, "Where is the treasure?"

One day, the man saw a little girl. He asked her, "Where is the treasure?" But the girl just shook her head and said nothing.

The man got very angry. He shouted, "Come with me! I want to show you where the treasure is!" The little girl was scared. She came with the man and he took her to a dark, scary cave.

The loud man said, "This is where the treasure is!" But, when the man opened the cave, there was nothing inside.

The little girl was so upset. She said, "There is no treasure here!" But the loud man just laughed and said, "Ha ha! You will never find treasure! You will never be rich!" and he walked away, leaving the little girl all alone in the dark.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Susie. She went to the mall with her mom and dad. When they got there, Susie saw a fake toy and shouted, "I want it!"

Her mom said, "No, Susie. It's fake. We need to get a real one."

Susie didn't like that and started to shout even louder, "I WANT IT!"

Her dad laughed and said, "Let's go find the real one!" 

So they all went off to find the real toy. Susie found it very quickly and shouted, "I found it!"

"That's great, Susie! Let's get it!," said her mom, and off they went to check out. 

When they got home, Susie was very happy. She smiled and hugged her new toy and said, "I love it! Thank you, Mom and Dad!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lizzie. She was only three years old, but she loved to explore.

One day, Lizzie was in her backyard when she came across a small, fragile island. It was perfect for exploring! She quickly scampered onto the island and began to explore.

Suddenly, Lizzie noticed that the island was starting to move! She was so surprised and asked, "What is happening?"

Her dad was watching her from the backyard and said, "It looks like you found a magical island, Lizzie! You can slide it!" 

Lizzie smiled and said, "Really? Cool!" She then grabbed the island and happily slide it across the grass. She had so much fun exploring her own little island. 

The end!

Once upon a time there was a happy boy. He loved to explore the world around him. One day he was looking around his backyard and saw a frog. He wanted to take a closer look. So, he bent down to examine it. 

The frog suddenly began to sing a song. The boy was amazed by the sound and listened very carefully. The song was slow and sweet. He asked the frog, "What is that song?" 

The frog answered, "It is a song of friendship. It is a sweet reminder that friends can be found in the most unexpected places." 

The boy smiled and thanked the frog. From then on, he always examined the world around him in hopes of finding more new friends. The end.

Tim and Kim like to play in the garden. They have a big jar with a lid. They catch bugs and put them in the jar. They want to see how big the bugs are.

One day, they find a cricket in the grass. It is green and brown and has long legs. It makes a loud noise with its wings. Tim and Kim are excited. They want to measure the cricket.

They put the cricket in the jar and close the lid. They get a ruler and a pencil. They draw a line on the jar with the pencil. They say, "This is how long the cricket is."

They look at the ruler. They see the numbers on the ruler. They try to count the numbers. They say, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. The cricket is seven long."

They are happy. They have measured the cricket. They open the lid and let the cricket go. The cricket jumps away and makes a loud noise. Tim and Kim say, "Bye, cricket. You are very noisy and very long."

Once upon a time, there was a brave hero who had an important mission to deliver. He was given a big box, and the box was zero. He had to make sure it got to its destination perfectly.

So the brave hero set off on his journey. He walked, he hopped, he skipped a lot too. But soon he got very tired and felt like he had a long way left to go.

But then a magical thing happened. Just as he started to get really tired, something landed in front of him. It was a giant bird! The giant bird said "Hop on my back and I will deliver the zero box to your destination."

The brave hero was so happy that he hopped straight onto the giant bird's back. He held the box tightly and the giant bird flew off. Soon they arrived at their destination and delivered the box perfectly. 

The brave hero was very impressed with the perfect job the giant bird did, and thanked him for his help. They both flew off in different directions and the brave hero went back home feeling very proud of himself. The end.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and stories with their cars, dolls and blocks. They did not hear their mom calling them for lunch.

"Ben, Lily, come to the kitchen, it's time to eat!" their mom said again, louder this time.

Ben and Lily looked at each other and smiled. They liked lunch, but they liked playing more. They decided to hide behind the couch and pretend they did not hear their mom.

"Where are they?" their mom wondered, looking around the living room. She saw their toys on the floor, but not her children. She walked to the couch and lifted the cushion. She saw Ben and Lily giggling and holding their hands over their mouths.

"Boo!" she said, making them jump. "I found you, you silly kids! Why did you not come when I called you?"

Ben and Lily looked at their mom with big eyes. They did not know what to say. They forgot to listen to their mom. They forgot to obey her.

"We are sorry, mom," they said together. "We were playing and we forgot."

Their mom smiled and hugged them. She was not angry, but she wanted them to learn. She was a smart lady and she loved her children.

"It's okay, I forgive you," she said. "But next time, please come when I call you. Lunch is important for your health and growth. And I don't want you to miss it."

Ben and Lily nodded and said they understood. They followed their mom to the kitchen and ate their lunch. They thanked their mom for the food and for finding them. They did not forget to say "I love you".

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a room with a door and a special thing called a knob. The knob was round and shiny and it helped her open and close the door. 

One day, Lily's mommy came to her room and saw that the door was not closed. She said, "Lily, please close the door so the cold air won't come in." Lily got up and turned the knob until the door was closed perfectly. 

Lily was happy because she did a good job closing the door. She loved her knob and knew how to use it to keep her room warm and cozy. From that day on, Lily always made sure to close the door with the perfect knob.

Lily and Tom were playing with their dolls in the garden. They had a tea party with cups and plates and cookies. Lily was very careful with her doll, because it was delicate. She had a pink dress and a hat with flowers.

"Can I hold your doll, Lily?" Tom asked. He liked the hat with flowers.

"Okay, but be gentle. She is delicate," Lily said. She gave her doll to Tom.

Tom took the doll and looked at her. He tried to put the hat on his head, but it was too small. He pulled it hard and it ripped.

"Oh no! You broke my hat!" Lily cried. She took her doll back and saw the rip. She was very sad and angry.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to," Tom said. He felt bad for making Lily cry.

"You have to pay for my hat. It was my favorite," Lily said.

"How can I pay for it? I don't have money," Tom said.

"You can pay with your cookies. Give me all your cookies," Lily said.

"But I'm hungry. Can I keep one cookie?" Tom asked.

"No. You have to give me all your cookies. That's the deal," Lily said.

Tom sighed. He liked his cookies, but he wanted to make Lily happy. He gave her all his cookies and said sorry again.

Lily took the cookies and smiled. She was still sad about her hat, but she liked the cookies. She ate one and gave one to her doll.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend," Lily said.

"You're welcome, Lily. Can we still play?" Tom asked.

"Okay. But next time, be careful with my doll. She is delicate," Lily said.

They hugged and played some more. They had fun in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she saw her friend Emma playing on a swing. Lily wanted to play on the swing too, but there was only one swing.

Lily said, "Emma, can I play on the swing too?"

Emma said, "Sure, but you have to wait your turn. I'm not finished yet."

Lily waited patiently for her turn. While she waited, she saw a spider hanging from a web. She thought it was cool how the spider made a network of webs to catch its food.

When it was Lily's turn to play on the swing, Emma watched her. Emma felt a little jealous because she wanted to play on the swing again. But she didn't say anything, and Lily had fun swinging back and forth.

Once upon a time, there was a goat. The goat was very friendly and liked to play with the children. One day, a little girl came to see the goat. "Can I play with your goat?" she asked the farmer. "Yes, you can," he replied. "Just be careful and don't let him eat too much grass."

The little girl played with the goat for a while. She petted him and let him nibble on her dress. "You're such a friendly goat," she said. "I wish I had a goat like you." The goat bleated happily in response.

After a while, the little girl had to go home. "Goodbye, friendly goat," she said. "I'll come back and play with you again soon." The goat watched her go, then went back to his grazing. He was happy to have made a new friend.

Lily wanted to dress her doll in a new outfit. She looked for some yarn in her toy box. She found a pink yarn and a blue yarn. She liked both colors.

She asked her mom, "Mom, can you help me make a dress for my doll?"

Mom smiled and said, "Sure, Lily. We can use the yarn to knit a dress. Do you want to learn how to knit?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want to make a pretty dress."

Mom and Lily sat on the couch and took out some needles. Mom showed Lily how to hold the yarn and the needles. She said, "You have to make loops with the yarn and slide them on the needles. Then you have to pull the yarn through the loops. That's how you knit."

Lily tried to follow Mom's instructions. She made some loops and slid them on the needles. She pulled the yarn through the loops. She was proud of herself. She said, "Look, Mom. I'm knitting."

Mom praised Lily and said, "You're doing great, Lily. Keep going. You'll have a dress for your doll soon."

Lily and Mom knitted together for a while. They made a small dress with pink and blue stripes. Lily was happy. She said, "Thank you, Mom. You're the best."

Mom hugged Lily and said, "You're welcome, Lily. You're very clever."

Lily put the dress on her doll. She said, "You look beautiful, doll. Do you like your new dress?"

The doll smiled and said, "I love it, Lily. You're very kind."

Lily and her doll played happily. They didn't mind the gloomy weather outside. They had fun inside with their yarn and needles.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a mule. The mule was very strong and helped the farmer with his work. One day, the farmer asked his son to pour some water into the mule's bucket. The son was very excited to help and poured the water carefully.

But, suddenly the mule kicked the bucket and spilled all the water. The son felt ashamed because he thought he did something wrong. But the farmer told him that it was not his fault and the mule was just being naughty. The son felt better and continued to help his father with the mule.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with trains. They had many toy trains and tracks in their room. They liked to make long rails and run their trains on them. They also liked to watch real trains go by on the big rail near their house.

One day, they received a big box from their grandma. They opened it and saw a new train set. It had a shiny engine, some cars, and a bridge. They were very happy and thanked their grandma on the phone. They wanted to try their new train set right away.

They set up the bridge on the floor and put the engine and the cars on it. They pushed a button and the train started to move. It made a funny sound, like a whistle. Tom and Lily laughed and clapped. They watched the train go over the bridge and back.

But then, something bad happened. The bridge was not very strong. It broke in the middle and the train fell down. The engine and the cars smashed on the floor. Tom and Lily were shocked and sad. They cried and hugged each other.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken train and the bridge. She felt sorry for Tom and Lily. She said, "Oh, no! Your new train set is ruined! I'm so sorry, my darlings. Maybe we can fix it or get a new one. Don't cry, it's not your fault."

But Tom and Lily did not stop crying. They loved their new train set and they did not want to lose it. They wished they had never received it. They wished they had played with their old trains and tracks instead. They learned a hard lesson. Sometimes, new things are not better than old things. And sometimes, funny things are not fun at all.

Sophia and her mom were looking for their house when they noticed a wolf nearby. As Sophia looked on with wide eyes, her mom explained, "That wolf is impressive Sophia; it must have been wandering around here for a while".

At that moment, the wolf ran up to them and sat down in front of Sophia and her mom. Sophia couldn't believe her eyes and whispered, "Mommy, what does it want?". Her mom smiled and explained, "Maybe it just wanted us to admire how impressive it is".

Sophia was amazed and cautiously reached out to pet the wolf. After a few moments, the wolf nuzzled her hand, then trotted away. 

Sophia's mom told her what a special moment it was they had just shared, and the two of them continued their journey home.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big pond with many ducks and fish. They wanted to feed them some bread, so they asked their mom for some.

"Here you go, boys. But be careful, don't go too close to the water. There might be an alligator hiding there," their mom said.

Ben and Sam nodded and ran to the pond. They threw some bread to the ducks and fish, who came to eat. They were having fun, but soon they ran out of bread.

"Let's go back to mom and get more bread," Sam said.

"No, I want to stay here. Look, there is a big log in the water. Maybe we can stand on it and see more ducks and fish," Ben said.

He pointed to a long, brown thing in the water. Sam thought it looked like a log, too. He followed Ben to the edge of the pond.

"Be careful, Ben. Don't drop in the water. It might be hot," Sam said.

Ben laughed. "Don't be silly, Sam. The water is not hot. It is cool and nice. Watch me, I can stand on the log."

He stepped on the log, but it was not a log. It was an alligator. The alligator opened its big mouth and snapped at Ben. Ben screamed and jumped back. He dropped his hat in the water.

"Help, help! It's an alligator!" Ben cried.

Sam was scared, too. He ran to their mom and told her what happened. Their mom came to the pond and saw the alligator. She grabbed Ben and hugged him.

"Are you okay, Ben? You are very lucky. The alligator could have hurt you. You should have listened to me and stayed away from the water," she said.

Ben was sorry. He realized he was wrong. He hugged his mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was foolish. I should have listened to you. I won't go near the water again."

Sam hugged his brother and said, "I'm sorry, too, Ben. I should have stopped you. I'm glad you are safe."

Their mom smiled and said, "It's okay, boys. I'm glad you are safe, too. Let's go home and have some ice cream. But remember, always be careful and listen to your mom."

Ben and Sam learned their lesson. They never went near the water again. They also never saw their hat again. The alligator kept it as a souvenir.

Molly was very excited, as she was ready to explore the maze. She was with her parents, holding their hands and wondering what secrets the maze held. Molly's parents had been talking about mazes for days and Molly was eager to see one in real life.

Molly went further and further into the maze, taking each turn and discovering more and more twists and turns. Each corner was an adventure. Eventually, after a few turns, Molly became tired and a bit scared - she had been in the maze for what seemed like forever.

Molly's dad saw the tired look on her face and said, "Don't worry Molly, we'll surrender and go home."

Molly was relieved. She grabbed her parent's hands and they left the maze. Molly felt sure that one day she'd be brave enough to explore a maze again. 

As they left, Molly took one last look back. She felt excited to explore the maze one day and find out where each turn would lead her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who lived in a valley. She loved to play outside and explore the mountains. One day, she met a bald eagle named Eddie.

"Hello, Eddie! You have no hair on your head!" Lily said.

"Yes, I know. But I am still a strong and brave eagle," Eddie replied.

Lily and Eddie became friends and flew around the valley together. But one day, they saw a big black bear who was very angry. 

"We need to find a safe place to hide," Eddie mentioned to Lily.

They flew to a nearby cave and hid inside. The bear couldn't find them and eventually left. Lily and Eddie were relieved.

"Thank you for protecting me, Eddie," Lily said.

"You are my friend and I will always keep you safe," Eddie replied.

From that day on, Lily and Eddie continued to explore the valley together and had many more adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside. One day, Timmy went to the park with his mom. At the park, Timmy saw some kids playing catch with a ball. Timmy wanted to play too, but he didn't have a ball. 

One of the kids saw Timmy and said, "Hey, do you want to play with us?" Timmy was happy and said, "Yes please!" The kid said, "But we only have one ball. Do you have anything we can use to play with?" Timmy thought for a moment and said, "I have a net!" 

The kids were confused and asked, "What do we do with a net?" Timmy said, "We can use it to catch the ball when we throw it!" The kids thought that was a fair idea, so they used the net to play catch with Timmy. They all had so much fun playing together that they didn't even notice the time passing by. When it was time for Timmy to go home, he said goodbye to his new friends and went home happy.

One day, there was a little boy who wanted to go and play outside. He looked out the window and saw a sunny day. He couldn't guess what it was like outside but he knew it was warm. He went outside and found a tree with lots of shade. He felt so comfortable in the shade that he fell asleep. Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was his dad, telling him to be careful in the shade. The little boy was being careless and he had almost fallen asleep. His dad laughed and the little boy laughed too. That day, the little boy learnt to be careful so he wouldn't get hurt in the shade.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little girl called Susie. Her mummy said it was time to leave the park. Susie didn't want to leave and started to cry.

Mummy said she was being bad and gave her a lemon as a punishment. She tried to smile as she took it from her mummy.

"This lemon is too sour," said Susie.

"Hold it in your mouth longer, it might help," said Mummy.

So Susie did what her mummy said, and after a while the lemon started to taste nice.

Mummy said "See! That wasn't so bad was it?" And Susie smiled and said, "No it wasn't!"

One day, Tom was very eager. He did not know why, but he wanted to find out.

He asked his mum, â€œWhat is my surprise?â€

She smiled and said, â€œLetâ€™s go and see!â€

Tom and his mum went outside. They walked together until they came to a park. In the park, Tom could see a big tree with lots of colourful balloons around it.

Tom was so excited and ran to the tree. He had the best surprise ever! A puppy was sitting underneath the tree, just for him!

Tom was so happy. He hugged the puppy and named it Coco.

Tom was eager for many more surprises like this one!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy loved pieces, so one day she decided to go and pick some pieces in the hot sun. She looked around, but she could not find any pieces. She was feeling sad.

Just then, she saw a rainbow in the sky. She followed the rainbow and it led her to a little house. When she opened the door, she saw a big pile of pieces. Daisy was so happy! She trusted the rainbow and it led her to pieces. 

She spent the day happily playing with the pieces. She had fun building castles and towers with them. When Daisy was finished, she was happy and warm from playing in the hot sun. 

She never forgot the day that the rainbow showed her the pieces. She learned to trust. And she liked to remember that special day.

Once upon a time, there was a big and powerful lion. He lived in a hut made of sticks and leaves in the jungle. One day, the lion went out to hunt for his dinner. He saw a small rabbit and tried to strike it with his paw, but the rabbit was too quick and ran away.

The lion was very hungry, so he decided to keep looking for food. He walked around the jungle and saw a group of monkeys eating bananas. The lion thought he could strike them and take their bananas, but the monkeys were too high up in the trees.

The lion was getting very tired and hungry. He went back to his hut and lay down to rest. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise outside. He got up and saw that a storm was coming. The wind was so powerful that it knocked down some of the trees around his hut. The lion was scared, but he felt safe inside his hut.

Steve was a leopard who was very nosy. He always wanted to peek into windows and see what was happening inside. One day he was feeling very sleepy and he decided to take a nap. He laid down under a shady tree and before he knew it, he was fast asleep.

Soon, Steve started to yawn. He opened his mouth wide and took a big, deep yawn. He felt much better now and decided to look around. All of a sudden, he spotted something from the corner of his eye. "What is that?" he thought.

He quietly snuck up to the window and peeked inside. There, he saw a little boy having his afternoon nap. He couldn't believe his eyes - the little boy was yawning just like him!  He watched in amazement as the boy stretched out his arms and yawned again.

Steve smiled and thought to himself, "It looks like I'm not the only nosy leopard taking naps around here!"

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who promised to always be together. They were so happy, but one day something scary happened. They met a monster!

The monster was big and loud, and he asked the two friends to leave their happy place. But the two best friends promised each other to stay brave.

Suddenly, a nice big bird flew down from the sky. He promised to help them. He made funny sounds and faces at the monster, and the monster ran away!

The two friends hugged the nice big bird and thanked him for saving them. They promised to always remember how kind and brave the bird was and to always stay together.

One day, a little girl named Lucy discovered a yellow pond. It was sparkling in the sun and filled with fish. Lucy was curious. She wanted to know what was in the water. She put her hand in the pond and felt something cold and slimy! It was a frog! It was yellow too! Lucy was so excited that she squealed with joy. She then lifted the frog out of the pond and admired its beauty. It blinked at her with its big eyes and made a funny sound. Then it hopped away. From that day on, the yellow pond was one of Lucy's favorite places. She often returned to discover what new surprises the pond would offer her.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with numbers. They have cards with numbers on them. One day, they want to play a new game.

"Let's prepare a cake with numbers," Lily says.

"How do we do that?" Ben asks.

"We need a big paper, some crayons, and scissors. We can draw a cake and cut out numbers to put on it," Lily explains.

They find the things they need and start to work. They draw a big cake with orange frosting and sprinkles. They cut out numbers from one to ten. They have fun putting the numbers on the cake.

"Look, our cake is ready!" Lily says.

"It looks yummy!" Ben says.

They count the numbers on the cake. They have one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and ten.

"Wait, we forgot something," Lily says.

"What did we forget?" Ben asks.

"We forgot zero. Zero is a number too," Lily says.

"Where can we put zero?" Ben asks.

"Let's put it on top of the cake. It can be a candle," Lily says.

They cut out a zero and stick it on the cake. They pretend to blow it out.

"Happy number cake day!" they say to each other.

They laugh and hug. They love their cake with numbers.

One day, a big mosquito came to a little town. It was not nice. It wanted to bite everyone. The people in the town did not like the mosquito. They wanted to prevent it from biting them.

A smart girl named Lily had an idea. She told everyone to use a special cream. The cream would make the mosquito not want to bite them. Everyone put the cream on their arms and legs. They hoped it would stop the mosquito.

The mosquito tried to bite the people, but it did not like the cream. It flew away, sad and hungry. The people in the town were happy. They stopped the mosquito and no one was dead. They thanked Lily for her smart idea.

One day Mommy, Daddy and Sarah went out to the beach. Sarah was very excited to find shells. She started looking up and down the beach and found some very interesting ones. Mommy asked Sarah which shell she thought was the most special. Sarah picked up a shiny white shell and said, "This one! Look at it shine!"

Daddy was very proud of Sarah and said, "You found a beautiful shell! Good job!"

Sarah smiled and said, "I'm going to keep it forever."

Mommy smiled and said, "I'm sure it will make you very happy each time you look at it." 

Sarah nodded and looked at the beautiful shell with a big grin on her face. She was so proud to have found such a special shell. She was sure it would always make her feel happy.

One day, a 3 year old boy named Zack was playing in his garden. Suddenly, he noticed a spike. He was very curious and decided to investigate. 

He walked closer to the spike and saw that it was a very sweet looking flower! Zack was amazed at how something so small could look so beautiful.

He asked the flower, "What are you?" 

The flower replied, "I am a spike. I become sweeter when it's sunny and I get bigger too."

Zack smiled and said, "Wow! Thank you for telling me about you. You're so pretty."

The flower smiled back at him and said, "You're welcome, Zack. I'm glad you like me." 

And from that day forward, Zack and the spike were the best of friends. Every day, Zack would visit the spike and give it some water from the garden hose so it could become even sweeter!

Once there was a boy called Jack. He was only three years old. One day Jack went for a walk with his mom. They walked and walked until they came to a tall tree. Jack was happy because the tall tree was his favorite. 

Suddenly, Jack realized he couldn't hear anything. He looked around and saw that everything was silent and still. He felt strong and happy in the silence.

"Mommy," he said, "it's so quiet here." His mom smiled and said, "That's why it's so special." Jack understood and enjoyed the silence for many minutes.

When it was time to go, Jack was sad. But he knew he'd come back one day and realize the silence again.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He liked to watch his toys. One day, he saw a strange figure. He felt a bit guilty and he hid behind his sofa. Then, the figure started to move. He poked his head out and watched. It was his mom! She was moving his toys around the room. The boy was so happy that all he felt was joy--no more guilty feeling! He ran out and hugged his mom. From then on, every time he saw a figure coming in, he knew it was his mom watching him.

Anna and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. They had a jar with some ants and worms inside.

"Look, Ben, I found a big beetle!" Anna said, holding up a shiny black bug.

"Wow, let me see!" Ben said, reaching for the beetle.

But as he touched it, the beetle opened its wings and flew away. Anna and Ben screamed and ran away from the beetle.

They bumped into a rock and fell down. They looked up and saw something on the rock. It was a lizard. It had green scales and a long tail. It stared at them with its small black eyes.

"Ah, a lizard!" Anna said, panicking. She did not like lizards. She thought they were disgusting and scary.

"Shh, don't move. Maybe it will go away," Ben said, trying to be brave.

But the lizard did not go away. It opened its mouth and showed its sharp teeth. It hissed and flicked its tongue.

"Help, help!" Anna and Ben shouted, crying. They wanted their mom and dad to come and save them from the lizard.

They heard footsteps and saw their mom and dad running towards them. They picked them up and hugged them.

"What's wrong, sweeties? What scared you?" their mom asked, worried.

"The lizard, the lizard!" Anna and Ben said, pointing at the rock.

Their mom and dad looked at the rock and laughed. They saw the lizard, but it was not a real lizard. It was a toy lizard. Someone had left it on the rock as a joke.

"It's okay, it's not a real lizard. It's just a toy. See?" their dad said, picking up the toy lizard and showing it to them.

Anna and Ben looked at the toy lizard and felt silly. They realized they had been afraid of nothing. They laughed too and hugged their mom and dad.

"Sorry, we were silly. We thought it was a real lizard," Anna said.

"It's okay, we all get scared sometimes. But you don't have to be afraid of lizards. They are not disgusting. They are just animals. They won't hurt you if you leave them alone," their mom said.

"Really? Can we see a real lizard?" Ben asked, curious.

"Sure, maybe we can find one in the garden. But don't touch them, just look at them. They are very interesting and beautiful," their dad said.

"Okay, let's go find a real lizard!" Anna and Ben said, excited.

They put the toy lizard back on the rock and went with their mom and dad to look for a real lizard in the garden. They learned that lizards were not so bad after all. They had fun and forgot about the beetle.

Once there was a little boy named George. He was always so happy and eager to explore. Everywhere he went, he followed his urge. 

One day, George decided to visit his neighbor, who had a farm. His neighbor had all sorts of animals like chickens, ducks and cows. When George saw them, he was so excited and he wanted to feed them!

So, George went out to the barn and grabbed a handful of sweet, juicy apples. He couldn't wait to see the animals' happy faces when he offered them the food! 

George approached the chickens first, who were so excited to get a snack from George. He couldn't stop smiling as he watched them eat, and he even shared a little of his apples with the cows. 

When George was done feeding the animals, his neighbor thanked him. George was filled with joy and he thanked his neighbor in return. He was so happy that he had been able to witness everything and help out. He couldn't wait to come back to the farm again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wander around her backyard and explore. One day, she saw a big, angry dog coming towards her. Lily was scared and her knee started to hurt.

Lily's mommy came outside and saw the dog. She quickly picked up Lily and took her inside. Lily's mommy called the dog's owner and they came to get the dog. From that day on, Lily was careful when she wandered around outside.

A few days later, Lily was playing with her toys when she heard a knock at the door. It was the dog's owner! They brought over a big bag of treats for Lily and apologized for their dog scaring her. Lily was happy and her knee felt better, and she learned that sometimes even angry things can have a happy ending.

Once upon a time, there was a tall man. He was walking down a long hallway. He came to an exit and he wanted to keep going. He looked for a way out, but he couldn't find one.

He looked up and saw a very tall door. He wanted to keep walking so he opened the door. He walked through the door, and then he saw a huge staircase. Again, he wanted to keep walking, so he walked up the stairs.

At the top of the stairs was another tall door. He opened it and he saw a big moon in the sky. He was so happy to find the exit. He was glad he was able to keep going and find the way out. He thanked the moon and went back down the stairs. He never forgot the tall exit that he found.

Once upon a time there was a mole who lived in a gloomy forest. He liked to cover himself in dirt so he blended in with his surroundings.

One day, the mole was feeling a bit lonely, so he decided to explore the forest to find some other animals. He saw a scarlet bird perched on a branch and a funny little rabbit hopping around the bushes.

But then the mole noticed something even more exciting â€“ a sunny meadow full of wildflowers! He scampered across the meadow, stopping to smell the flowers and jumping around in the sun. He had never felt so happy!

Suddenly, he felt a heavy rain start to fall and he quickly ran back to the gloomy forest to take cover. He burrowed into the dirt and soon he was dry and warm again.

The mole stayed in his forest for a long time, but he would often remember that sunny meadow and all the wonderful flowers he had seen.

Once upon a time, there was a bad man. He carried a cross and hated to share. One day, he was mad and decided to burn the cross. The cross started to burn and it made the bad man sad. He realised that he had done a bad thing.

The bad man started to cry. He had made a mistake and now he felt bad. He was sorry for burning the cross. 

Suddenly, a kind fairy appeared. She saw what had happened and said that it was okay. She waved her wand and suddenly the cross was whole again. The bad man was so happy. He thanked the kind fairy and promised he would never burn the cross again. 

The bad man now shares and is always kind to everyone. He never forgets what the kind fairy did for him and is always grateful.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump on the grass. The grass was green and soft. But some parts of the grass were brown and dry. Lila and Tom wondered why.

They saw a man with a big hose. He was spraying water on the grass. He wore a hat and a shirt with a flower on it. Lila and Tom were curious. They ran to the man and said hello.

"Hello, little ones. What are you doing here?" the man asked.

"We are playing on the grass. But why is some grass brown and dry?" Lila asked.

"Well, the grass needs water to grow and stay green. Sometimes, the sun is too hot and the rain is too little. Then the grass gets thirsty and sad. That's why I'm here. I'm trying to restore the grass. Do you know what restore means?" the man explained.

Lila and Tom shook their heads. They did not know what restore meant.

"Restore means to make something good again. Like when you fix a broken toy or heal a hurt knee. I'm giving water to the grass so it can be happy and green again. Do you want to help me?" the man offered.

Lila and Tom nodded. They liked to help. The man gave them each a small hose. They sprayed water on the grass with the man. They had fun and learned a new word. They helped to restore the grass.

Once upon a time, there was a vehicle. It was a tough vehicle and it needed help. It had to make it up a big hill. The vehicle could not make it up the hill on its own. So, a friend came to help.

The friend was very encouraging. He said, â€œCome on, vehicle. You can do it! You are tough!â€

And with the encouraging words of his friend, the vehicle was able to make it up the hill! Everyone cheered for the vehicle and the friend was so proud of the vehicle for being so tough.

After the vehicle made it up the hill, the two friends high-fived each other. They were so happy and the vehicle was so proud. It had made it up the hill!

Tom and Jen were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. Sometimes, they helped their dad with the grill, where he cooked meat and corn for dinner. They knew the grill was hot and they had to be careful.

One day, Tom and Jen were playing with their toy cars in the sandbox. They pretended they were racing on a track. Tom had a red car and Jen had a blue car. They made zooming and honking noises as they moved their cars around. Tom wanted to win the race, so he pushed his car faster and faster. Jen tried to catch up, but Tom was too quick.

Tom saw the grill nearby and had an idea. He thought he could make his car go even faster if he put it on the grill. He did not think about how hot the grill was or how it could hurt his car. He ran to the grill and threw his car on it. He shouted, "Look, Jen, my car is on fire! I win!"

Jen saw what Tom did and felt scared and sad. She knew the grill was dangerous and she loved her brother. She did not want him to get burned or lose his car. She ran to the grill and tried to grab Tom's car. But the car was too hot and it burned her hand. She screamed and dropped the car. She started to cry.

Tom heard Jen's scream and saw her hand. He realized he had done a bad thing. He felt sorry and ashamed. He ran to Jen and hugged her. He said, "I'm sorry, Jen, I'm sorry. I was silly and mean. Are you okay?"

Jen felt Tom's hug and heard his words. She knew he was sorry and he loved her. She felt compassionate and forgave him. She said, "It's okay, Tom, it's okay. I love you. But don't do that again, okay?"

Tom and Jen went inside and told their dad what happened. Their dad was angry and worried. He scolded Tom for being reckless and careless. He praised Jen for being brave and kind. He took them to the bathroom and put some cream and a bandage on Jen's hand. He said, "You two are lucky it was not worse. You have to be careful with the grill. It can burn you and your things. You have to respect it and listen to me. Do you understand?"

Tom and Jen nodded and said, "Yes, dad, we understand. We're sorry. We won't do it again."

Their dad hugged them and said, "I love you both. Now, let's go have some dinner. I have some meat and corn for you. And some ice cream for dessert."

Tom and Jen smiled and said, "Yay, ice cream!" They followed their dad to the kitchen and ate their dinner. They learned their lesson and never played with the grill again.

Once there was a boy who had a cabinet. It was very special to him because he built it all by himself. He was so proud of how independent he was! 

One day, the boy heard a loud noise coming from the cabinet. It was so loud that he thought it was about to break! So he quickly marched over and opened the cabinet to see what was happening inside.
