When he looked in, he saw a small mouse. It was shaking and scurrying around the cabinet. The boy was so surprised that he wanted to catch it! He decided to strike at it with his hand, but the mouse got away just in time. 

The boy decided to leave the cabinet open overnight, so that the mouse could find its way out. The next day, the boy was happy to see that the mouse had gone. His cabinet was safe, and he was still very proud of how independent he was.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Angel, a soft doll with wings and a halo. Lily loved to hug Angel and pretend she was flying with her in the sky.

One day, Lily's brother Tom came into her room. He was bored and wanted to play with Lily. He saw Angel on the bed and grabbed her. "What is this?" he asked. "It looks silly."

Lily was angry. She ran to Tom and tried to take Angel back. "No, Tom, that's my doll!" she said. "Her name is Angel and she is very nice. Give her back!"

Tom did not listen. He laughed and pulled Angel's wings. "She is not nice, she is boring. Look, her wings are falling off. She is not a real angel."

Lily felt very sad. She slapped Tom on the face. "Stop it, Tom, you are mean!" she shouted. "You hurt Angel and you hurt me. Go away!"

Tom was surprised and hurt. He dropped Angel and ran out of the room. He had a red mark on his face where Lily slapped him. He started to cry.

Lily picked up Angel and hugged her. She saw that one of her wings was torn. She felt sorry for Angel and for Tom. She knew she should not have slapped him. She decided to say sorry to him and to share her dolls with him. She hoped he would be nice to her and to Angel.

The moral of the story is: Do not hurt others or their things. Be kind and share with your siblings. Slapping is not a good way to solve problems.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the field near their house. The field has many flowers and butterflies. Anna and Ben run and laugh and chase the butterflies.

"Look, Ben, a yellow flower!" Anna says. She picks the flower and gives it to Ben. "It is for you, Ben. You are my friend."

"Thank you, Anna. You are my friend too." Ben says. He smiles and puts the flower in his hair. "You are pretty, Anna. Like the flower."

Anna and Ben hug and kiss. They are happy. They sit on the grass and watch the sky. The sky is blue and has white clouds. Anna and Ben make shapes with the clouds.

"I see a bunny, Anna. Do you see it?" Ben asks.

"Yes, Ben, I see it. And I see a star. Do you see it?" Anna asks.

"Yes, Anna, I see it. And I see a heart. Do you see it?" Ben asks.

"Yes, Ben, I see it. And I see you. You are in my heart." Anna says.

Anna and Ben kiss again. They are very happy. They are also very tired. They lie on the grass and close their eyes. They fall asleep in the field. They dream of flowers and butterflies and stars and hearts. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a small post. The post was fragile and needed to be held carefully. One day, a little girl named Jane decided to pick it up. She held it very carefully and walked across the street. 

Once she had the post in her hands, she looked around to see if anyone was watching. Luckily, no one was around. Jane quietly placed the post in the front yard of her house. She smiled, feeling proud of herself.

The following day, Jane got out of bed early. She wanted to make sure no one had moved the post. When she arrived at her house, the post was still there. She was so relieved! She carefully picked up the post and safely put it back in its place. 

From that day, Jane took turns with her friends holding the post until it no longer needed protecting. The fragile post was safe and the children were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. Her name was Jane, and she wanted to be happy. But she was very sad because there was something terrible on her shelf. It was a monster, and it scared her a lot. 

Every day, Jane looked up at the monster on her shelf and was too scared to do anything. She cried a lot and couldn't sleep.

One night, Jane had an idea. She decided to hope that the monster would go away. So, she closed her eyes and said the magic word: "Hope!"

The next morning, Jane opened her eyes and looked up. The monster was gone! Jane smiled and was very happy. She had hoped with all her might, and it worked!

The End.

Raquel ran out of the house, into the big backyard, with a smile on her face. In her hand, she held her yellow ball. She looked up at the sky and saw a kite so high. She wanted to try flying it. 

Raquel asked her mom, "Can I fly the kite?" Mom said, "Let's give it a try." They started walking to the big field. 

When they reached the field, mom showed Raquel how to hold the kite in her palm and with a big push, it was flying in the sky! Raquel couldn't believe how high it had gone. She stared at the kite as it flew around and around.

Mom said, "You did a great job flying it!" Raquel smiled and said, "Can we do it again tomorrow?" Mom laughed and said, "Of course!" 

Raquel was so happy that she had mastered flying the kite. The next day she asked if she could fly it again, and again, and again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Bop. Bop loved to hop all day long. He would hop in the grass, hop on the dirt, and hop with his friends. Bop was very brave and liked to hop high and far.

One day, Bop and his friends were playing near the big tree. They were hopping and laughing, having lots of fun. Then, it was time for dinner. Bop's mom called him and his friends to come eat. They all hopped back to Bop's home.

At dinner, Bop and his friends ate yummy food. They had carrots, lettuce, and apples. Bop's mom told them stories about brave bunnies who hopped very high and very far. Bop and his friends listened and smiled. They wanted to be brave like the bunnies in the stories.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to play hide and seek with his friends in the forest. One day, Benny found a big leaf and decided to use it to hide from his friends.

Tommy was playing with his toy car outside in the sunshine. He kept zooming it around and around and it was so much fun.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but they always wanted more. They asked their mom and dad for new toys every day. Mom and dad said no, because they had enough toys and they should be happy with what they had. But Lily and Ben did not listen. They cried and whined and threw tantrums. They said they were not happy and they wanted more toys.

One day, mom and dad had to go to work and they left Lily and Ben with their grandma. Grandma was very kind and gentle. She made them pancakes for breakfast and read them stories. She also gave them a big box of toys that she had saved from when mom and dad were little. Lily and Ben were very excited. They opened the box and saw many toys that they had never seen before. There were cars and dolls and puzzles and books and blocks and animals. Lily and Ben grabbed the toys and ran to their room. They did not say thank you to grandma. They did not share the toys with each other. They fought and snatched and broke the toys. They made a big mess in their room.

Grandma heard the noise and came to their room. She saw the toys scattered and torn and ruined. She saw Lily and Ben crying and yelling. She was very sad and angry. She said, "Lily and Ben, you have spoiled the toys that I gave you. You have spoiled the fun that you could have had. You have spoiled the day that we could have spent together. You have been very selfish and ungrateful. You do not deserve these toys. You need to learn to be happy with what you have and to share and care for others. Now you have to clean up this mess and put the toys back in the box. And you have to say sorry to me and to each other. And you have to sit in the corner and think about what you have done. No more toys for you today."

Lily and Ben felt very ashamed and sorry. They did what grandma said. They cleaned up the mess and put the toys back in the box. They said sorry to grandma and to each other. They sat in the corner and thought about what they had done. They realized that they had been very bad and that they had hurt grandma and themselves. They wished they had been more kind and thankful and happy. They wished they had played nicely with the toys and with each other. They wished they had spent more time with grandma and listened to her stories.

The rest of the day was very quiet and boring. There was no more noise and fun and laughter. There was only silence and sadness and regret. Lily and Ben learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that being greedy and spoiled can make you lose what you have and what you love. They learned that being happy and grateful and sharing can make you gain more than you expect. They learned that being good and respectful and loving can make you and others happy. They learned that sometimes, less is more.

The little one said goodbye and went off to play. From that day on, the little one was no longer scared and new that the police would always help.

Once upon a time there was a silver fish. He was very adventurous and wanted to explore the big blue ocean. He swam and swam, looking for a new place to explore.

One day he came across a place he had never seen before. It was a shiny, silver cave! The fish was so excited that he swam inside. As he did, he felt something strange on his tail. He had been weighed down!

He looked around and saw that the cave was full of small silver coins. He realized that he had been weighed down with all the coins the cave contained. The fish was so happy that he started to swim around the cave with all the silver coins.

The adventurous fish had an amazing time in his silver cave and he visited it often. Every time he swam inside, he was weighed down with silver coins. What an amazing adventure he had!

One day, a boy and a girl were playing in the park. They saw a big bush with red berries. The boy said, "Let's split the berries and eat them. They look yummy." The girl said, "No, we don't know if they are good or bad. Maybe they are sour or bitter or make us sick. We should ask mom or dad first."

But the boy did not listen. He was foolish and greedy. He ran to the bush and picked some berries. He split them with his teeth and put them in his mouth. He made a face and spat them out. They were very sour and bitter and made his tongue hurt. He cried and said, "Ow, ow, ow! These berries are bad! They hurt my mouth!"

The girl ran to him and said, "I told you not to eat them. You were foolish and did not listen. Now you have to drink some water and wash your mouth. Come, I will help you." She took his hand and led him to a fountain. She gave him some water and said, "Next time, listen to me and be careful. Don't eat things you don't know."

The boy said, "I'm sorry, I was foolish and greedy. Thank you for helping me. You are a good friend. Next time, I will listen to you and be careful. Don't eat things I don't know." He hugged her and said, "You are welcome. You are a good friend too. Let's go and play something else." They smiled and ran to the swings. They had fun and forgot about the bad berries. They learned a lesson and never ate things they didn't know again.

Once there was a mighty man who lived in the forest. Every day he used to go fishing in the nearby lake and collect coins. One day he got a dare from his friends to jump off a cliff and swim across the lake. The man thought it was an impossible task, but he was brave and decided to take up the challenge. He took a deep breath and jumped off the cliff into the lake below. With a mighty splash he swam across the lake to the other side. There he found a huge pile of coins lying on the ground. He was so surprised to see a treasure of coins that he jumped out of the lake and ran back home to show his friends the coins. From then on the man never took up a dare without thinking twice.

Tik and Tuk were two small frogs. They were walking down a path when they spotted an old temple in the distance. The temple had been there for ages.

"Wow, look at it," said Tik to Tuk.

"Yes, it looks very alert," said Tuk.

What could it be? They thought.

So, they hopped closer to the temple and peeked in. Inside, they saw something very strange. It was a huge rock floating in the air!

The rock was swaying gently from side to side and making a gentle rocking sound.

Tik and Tuk were so surprised, but the rock looked so peaceful and beautiful.

They decided to stay and watch for a while, so they hopped up onto the stone and began to rock right along with it. 

They felt so happy and relaxed, like they were part of the temple.

They stayed there, rocking back and forth in harmony, until the sun started to set. 

Then, they hopped back home with a happy smile. Because they knew that they had discovered something amazing - the power of the alert temple.

Once there was a young girl called Kate. One day, Kate was playing in the garden when she suddenly tripped and hurt her leg. She started crying and felt really sad.

Her mum came outside and said, "Oh no, Kate! You need a bandage. Let's get you one".

Kate shook her head and said, "No! I don't need a bandage".

Mum said, "Yes, Kate. You were so silly running around and now you need a bandage. Off we go".

Kate said, "No! I don't want to go! I don't need a bandage".

Mum said, "Oh Kate, you might not want a bandage now, but you need one, so let's go!"

Finally, Kate realised her mum was right and said, "Ok, I need a bandage".

So they went to the store and got a bandage for Kate. She put it on and felt much better. 
Mum said, "See, it's not so bad to admit that you need help sometimes".

Kate smiled and said, "Yes, I'm glad I'm still young enough to get away with silly things".

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pretty dress and loved to play outside. One day, she went to the park to swing on the swings. She saw her friend, Timmy, and they started to play together.

Suddenly, Lily felt an itch on her arm. She scratched and scratched, but it wouldn't go away. Timmy saw her and asked, "Are you okay, Lily?" Lily replied, "I have an itch and it won't stop!"

Timmy laughed and said, "I know how to make it go away. Let's go play in the sand!" Lily smiled and they ran to the sandbox. They played and laughed together until the sun went down. From that day on, Lily knew that when she had an itch, all she had to do was play with her friend Timmy and the itch would disappear.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, she found a shiny silver necklace in her mom's jewelry box. She asked her mom if she could wear it, but her mom said it was a secret and she couldn't wear it yet.

Lily was sad and her mom noticed that she was hurt. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. One day, when you're older, I'll give you the necklace and it will be our secret."

Years passed and Lily grew up. She remembered the necklace and asked her mom about it. Her mom smiled and said, "I've been waiting for this day. Let me go get it." When her mom came back, she gave Lily the necklace and said, "I've been polishing it all these years, just for you." Lily put on the necklace and felt so special. She knew it was their little secret.

One day, Mommy and Freddy went to the park. They saw a big crane. They were excited. Mommy said, "Look, Freddy! That crane is so big!"

Mommy and Freddy filled the crane with sand. Freddy picked up some little rocks and put them in the sand. Mommy added some spicy herbs. They even made a sand castle.

Next, they saw birds flying. Freddy said, "Mommy, look at the crane's neck! It looks like a giant bird". Mommy laughed and said, "Yes, it does".

Mommy and Freddy continued playing with the crane. They filled the sand up to the top of the crane. When the crane was full, Mommy and Freddy hugged each other.

The end.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with their scooters in the park. Anna has a pink scooter and Ben has a blue scooter. They zoom around the grass and the trees, laughing and having fun.

One day, they see a new boy in the park. He has a big, shiny scooter. It has lights and sounds and stickers. Anna and Ben feel curious. They want to see the new scooter. They go to the new boy and say hello.

"Hi, I'm Anna and this is Ben. We like your scooter. Can we try it?" Anna asks.

The new boy looks at them and frowns. He does not feel friendly. He feels mean. He says, "No, you can't. This is my scooter. Go away. You have silly scooters. They are small and dirty and boring."

Anna and Ben feel sad and angry. They do not like the new boy. They think he is rude and selfish. They say, "Your scooter is not nice. It is loud and ugly and silly. You are not nice. You are mean and greedy and nasty."

The new boy feels mad and hurt. He does not like Anna and Ben. He thinks they are mean and jealous. He says, "You are liars. My scooter is the best. You are the worst. You are stupid and dumb and lame."

Then, he does something very bad. He pushes Anna and Ben off their scooters. He grabs their scooters and runs away. He laughs and says, "Ha ha, now I have three scooters. You have none. You are losers. I am the winner."

Anna and Ben feel shocked and scared. They fall to the ground and cry. They do not have their scooters. They do not have their fun. They do not have their friend. They have nothing. They feel very, very sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to dress. Each morning, she chose the prettiest dress for that day. Today, she chose a dress with lots of pink and purple stripes. 

On the way to school, she saw a matching hat. She was so excited that she dressed it on her head. She especially liked how it made her look very pretty. 

When she arrived at school, she showed her friends her matching hat. She twirled and danced, feeling so excited about her new look. 

Unfortunately, the day was a bit rough. It started to rain and the wind was so strong. Her pretty dress and matching hat were both ruined. 

The little girl was very sad. But then she looked up at the sky and saw a beautiful rainbow. She soon forgot all her worries and started to dream of her next dress to dress.

Once upon a time, a colorful bird named Bob lived in a big tree. Bob loved to fly in the sunshine and fill the sky with his beautiful songs. One day, he saw a little girl named Sue playing in the park.

"Hi Sue!" said Bob, "Do you want to play with me in the sunshine?" Sue looked up and smiled. "Yes, Bob! Let's play together!" So, they played and had fun under the warm sunshine.

But then, dark clouds came and covered the sky. The sunshine was gone. Bob and Sue were sad. They could not play anymore. They said goodbye and went back to their homes. The day ended with no more sunshine and fun.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see big clouds in the sky. They hear loud noises. They feel cold wind.

"It is a storm!" Tom says. "We should go home."

"Yes, let's go!" Sue says. They hold hands and run.

But the path is rough. There are rocks and sticks. Tom stumbles on a rock. He falls down. He hurts his knee. He cries.

"Tom, are you okay?" Sue asks. She helps him get up.

"It hurts!" Tom says. He shows his knee. There is blood.

Sue hugs him. "Don't worry, Tom. I have a band-aid in my pocket. I will put it on your knee. It will make it better."

She takes out a band-aid and sticks it on his knee. Tom smiles.

"Thank you, Sue. You are a good friend."

They hug again. Then they walk home. The storm is over. The sun comes out. They see a rainbow.

"Look, Tom! A rainbow!" Sue says. "It is so pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Tom says. "Maybe it is a sign that everything will be okay."

They smile and hold hands. They are happy. They are friends.

Tom was a man who liked to work on his car. He had a big car that made loud noises when he drove it. He had many tools that he used to fix his car. He was happy when his car worked well.

One day, Tom wanted to go for a drive. He put on his hat and his coat and went to his car. He tried to start his car, but it did not work. He tried again and again, but nothing happened. He was very angry and sad. He said, "Why does my car not work? I need to go for a drive!"

He got out of his car and opened the hood. He looked inside and saw a lot of wires and parts. He did not know what was wrong. He took his tools and tried to fix his car. He hit and twisted and pulled and pushed, but nothing changed. He was very frustrated and tired. He said, "This is too hard! I do not know how to fix my car!"

He threw his tools on the ground and sat on the hood. He sighed and looked at the sky. He wished he had a friend who could help him. He wished he had a new car that worked well. He wished he could go for a drive.

But he had no friend, no new car, and no drive. He had only his broken car, his tools, and his hat and coat. He was very lonely and unhappy. He said, "This is the worst day ever! I hate my car!"

He stayed on the hood and sighed. He did not see the big truck that was coming down the road. He did not hear the loud horn that warned him. He did not feel the crash that smashed his car and him. He did not know that he was dead. He had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to carry things around with him wherever he went. One day, Timmy found a newspaper on the ground. It was big and had lots of words on it. Timmy thought it was cool and decided to carry it with him.

As Timmy walked around with the newspaper, he saw a big dog running towards him. The dog looked dangerous because it was barking loudly and had sharp teeth. Timmy was scared, but he remembered he had the newspaper with him. He held it up and the dog ran away because it was scared of the newspaper.

Timmy was happy that he had the newspaper with him because it helped him stay safe from the dangerous dog. He continued to carry it with him everywhere he went and showed it to all of his friends. They thought it was cool too! The end.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little mouse. She loved adding wood to her cozy little house. She would go out and find small pieces of wood, then carefully add them to her collection. 

One day, she noticed a pile of wood that was much bigger than the wood she usually added to her house. She was so nosy that she decided to climb the pile and check it out. When she reached the top, she discovered a big strong tree.

She thought it was the most beautiful tree she had ever seen, so she decided to add it to her house. She started to gnaw away at the base of the tree until it was loose enough to move. 

The little mouse was so excited and proud of the huge tree she had added to her small, cozy house. She proudly sat and admired her work, feeling very happy and content.

One day, Timmy was playing with his friends in the park. They were running and dancing and having a great time.

Suddenly, they saw a small rabbit through the bushes. It was fragile and timid.

The children squealed in delight and ran towards the rabbit, wanting to play with it.

"Let's celebrate," Timmy said. "Let's give the rabbit a party!"

His friends cheered and clapped their hands.

The children slowly approached the rabbit and made it a special party. They decorated the area with paper streamers, and provided the rabbit with yummy fruit snacks.

The rabbit stayed to enjoy the delicious treats and the children showed their love and respect for the small creature.

At the end of the day, the rabbit hopped away into the bush, feeling happy and safe.

The children hugged each other and celebrated the wonderful moment they had shared.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, her mommy told her they were going to clean the attic. Lily was very excited because she had never been up there before.

When they got to the attic, they found a big box. Inside the box, there was a letter. The letter said that Lily's family was very wealthy and they were going to receive a lot of money. Lily didn't understand what "wealthy" meant, but she knew it was something good because her mommy and daddy were very happy.

After they read the letter, they went back downstairs and had a big celebration. They danced and sang and Lily felt very happy. She didn't know what the letter said, but she knew it was something special.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mommy. When they arrived, they saw a long line of children waiting to enter the playground. The line was so busy that Lily thought they would never get to play.

Lily asked her mommy, "How long is the line?" Her mommy replied, "It's a very busy day, so we have to wait our turn." Lily looked at the other children and said, "I wish we could skip the line and go in faster."

Just then, a little boy turned around and said, "Hey, do you want to play with us?" Lily was so happy and excited that she forgot all about the line. They played together and had so much fun that they didn't even notice when it was their turn to enter the playground. When they finally went inside, Lily turned to the little boy and said, "Thank you for letting me play with you. You made my day!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Kim. She was three years old and had bright, twinkling eyes.

Kim wanted to explore the world, so she started walking down a path. It felt like a distant journey already!

Suddenly, she saw a cell. It was small, with tiny little doors on it. Kim's eyes twinkled even brighter as she ran towards it.

"What's this?" Kim asked.

A voice from inside the cell replied, "I'm a rabbit! Can you please squeeze my door open?"

Kim used all her little fingers to try and squeeze the door open. After a few tries, she finally did it and the rabbit ran away to freedom.

Kim laughed with joy and gave one last tiny squeeze to the door before going back on her distant journey.

Once there was a 3 year old girl. She was called Lauren. In her bedroom there was a toybox. Today, Lauren wanted to open it.

"Mummy, can I open the toybox?" she asked. 

Mummy smiled. "Yes, of course you can. But be careful."

Lauren put her hands on the box and opened it. Inside, there were lots of exciting things. She saw a ball, a teddy bear and a jigsaw puzzle. She wanted to take them all out! 

Mummy said, "Be careful when you put your hands in the box." 

Lauren was careful. She put her hands in the box, one at a time. She carefully took out the ball and the teddy bear. But when she tried to take out the jigsaw puzzle, it was stuck. 

"Mummy, the jigsaw puzzle is stuck!" Lauren said. 

Mummy smiled and said, "It's ok. Be patient and be careful. Pull gently and it will come out!"

So Lauren pulled gently and the jigsaw puzzle came out. She was so excited! 

Mummy said, "Put everything back carefully and we can play with it all later." 

Lauren put everything back in the toybox. They would play with the toybox later. Until then, Lauren would go back to playing with her

John watched a bug crawl across the grass. He was careful not to hurt it. His mom smiled as she watched him.

Mom picked up the little bug and put it inside her case. She explained that it would be safer inside.

John was upset. He wanted the bug to stay outside and play. He began to cry.

Mom gave John a hug, and she sighed. She said that she was sorry, but it was safer inside the case.

John smiled. He still missed the little bug, but he understood why mom was being so careful.

John and mom hugged again. Mom thanked John for understanding, and they went on to play some more.

Anna and Ben were twins. They liked to play and laugh together. But they did not like to get haircuts. They thought haircuts were scary. They did not want to go to the salon with Mom.

"Come on, kids, it's time to go," Mom said. "You need a haircut. Your hair is too long and messy."

"No, Mom, no!" Anna and Ben said. They ran and hid under the bed. They hoped Mom would not find them.

But Mom was smart. She knew where they were. She smiled and said, "Okay, if you don't want to go, I have a surprise for you. I have a lovely gift for you. Do you want to see it?"

Anna and Ben were curious. They liked surprises. They liked gifts. They crawled out from under the bed. They followed Mom to the living room.

There, they saw a big box with a bow. Mom said, "This is for you. Go ahead, open it."

Anna and Ben were excited. They tore the paper and lifted the lid. They gasped. Inside the box, there was a pair of scissors, a comb, and a mirror.

"Surprise!" Mom said. "Now you can give each other a haircut. Isn't that fun?"

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They looked at the scissors. They looked at Mom. They did not think it was fun. They thought it was scary. They wished they had gone to the salon. They said, "Sorry, Mom, we changed our minds. Can we please go to the salon?"

Once upon a time, there was a baby named Lily. She had a crib that was very big and empty. Every night, her mommy would put her in the crib and sing her a lullaby. But Lily noticed that the crib was not shiny and clean like her toys. 

One day, Lily's mommy went to the store and bought a special polish for the crib. Lily watched as her mommy rubbed the polish all over the crib until it was shiny and new. Lily was so happy that she jumped up and down in her crib.

That night, when Lily's mommy put her in the crib, Lily noticed something different. She felt like she was sleeping on a cloud! The crib was so smooth and shiny that it felt like magic. Lily knew that she would sleep soundly every night in her beautiful crib.

Once upon a time there was a poor little boy who was playing in the park. He was running and jumping around, when he stumbled upon the patch of grass. He tried to get up but fell again.

Suddenly a kind woman wearing a towel on her head, came over to help him. With her gentle hands, she helped the little boy stand up. 

"Are you OK? said the kind woman

The little boy nodded, smiled, and thanked the woman for helping him.

The kind woman was very happy to help the little boy. She patted him on the head with her towel, and then she went on her way. 

The little boy was very thankful to the kind woman for helping him up. He will never forget the warm feeling he felt when she patted him on the head with her towel. He was so happy. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lily. She was very scared at night because she heard noises in her room.

One night, Lily heard louder noises coming from her closet. She was so scared that she started to cry. Then she heard a small voice coming from her closet.

"Help me, Lily," it said. "I need to escape from here."

Lily was even more scared but she was brave. She opened the closet and saw a little mouse. The mouse was scared too.

"Please help me," it said. "I'm trying to escape but I'm stuck here."

Lily was very brave and she reached her hand inside the closet to help the mouse. She grabbed the mouse gently and put it outside the window. 

The mouse was very happy and thanked Lily. Then it ran away into the night. 

Lily was happy that she had helped the mouse and she was no longer scared at night. She went to bed feeling brave and safe.

Once upon a time there was a brave little boy, who always wanted to go swimming in the sea. He was eager to go and explore all the big waves. On the way, he noticed a big, scary shark swimming near him. He was very scared, so he began to yell with excitement!

The shark was also very excited, it began to jump and pull out of the water. The little boy thought it was so fun, that he started to yell even louder, encouraging the shark to come closer.

So eventually, the brave little boy and the shark became the best of friends. Every few days they would meet in the sea and have a big swim together. The little boy was always so excited to see his new friend, and would yell louder than ever when they met.

Once upon a time, there was a strong little boy. He loved to explore his house. One day, he decided to explore the kitchen. He saw a big stove and he wanted to grab it to see how strong he was. 

He gripped the stove tightly with both hands and pulled with all of his might, but he could not move it. He kept pulling and pulling, but it was just too heavy. He started to feel frustrated, but then he thought of a new idea.

The little boy grabbed a chair, put it beside the stove, and climbed up to get a better grip. He tried one last time to grab the stove and this time, he was able to push it across the kitchen floor! He was so happy that he managed to do it, and it made him feel strong and proud. 

The boy smiled and knew that he had explored the kitchen in style!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to run fast and play outside. One day, Timmy saw his big brother practicing for a race. Timmy wanted to race too, but he didn't know how.

"Can you teach me how to race like you?" Timmy asked his brother.

"Sure, little brother. First, you need to run as fast as you can," his brother replied.

Timmy tried his best to run fast, but he kept falling down. His brother helped him up and said, "Don't worry, I'm glad you're trying. Keep practicing and you'll get better." 

From that day on, Timmy practiced every day with his brother. He ran faster and faster until one day, he won his very first race. Timmy was so glad that he learned how to race and he thanked his brother for teaching him.

Once upon a time there were two silly little birds. They were always quarrelling. One day, they decided to play with a net. They each held onto a corner and ran around in circles with it. It was so much fun!

But then they started quarrelling again. They fought so hard that the net got tangled. They couldn't undo it, no matter how hard they tried.

They decided to go find help. They flew around the garden looking for someone who could help them. Finally, they found a little girl and asked her for help.

The little girl was happy to help the silly little birds. She untangled the net in no time. The birds thanked her and flew away, never to quarrel again.

Sophia was very tired after a long day. She had been polishing all day, and hadn't much free time to play.

Sophia looked out the window. She saw the most beautiful sunset. She wanted to go outside to see it up close.

Sophia asked her mom, "Can I go out and see the sunset?"

Her mom replied, "No, not now. Its getting dark and you're tired - you must rest."

Sophia nodded and said, "Ok, I'll stay inside and rest. But can I still polish something?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can polish a few things. That way you can still enjoy the sunset from here."

So Sophia polished her toys while watching the beautiful sunset. She was so happy and relaxed. As the sun set, Sophia lay down and fell asleep.

Once upon a time there was a happy girl named Lisa. She loved to play with all her toys. One day, Lisa was playing with her blocks and she made a shape. But she was not careful and accidentally knocked the shape down. 

Lisa started to cry, but then she remembered something special. A wise person had told her that it was important to forgive. So she decided to forgive herself for making a mistake and keep playing.

Lisa started to build the shape again and she was very patient. It took longer but she was able to make it. She was very happy that she was able to rebuild the shape and she knew it was because she had learned to forgive. 

The End.

Lily liked to draw with crayons. She had many colors and made creative pictures of animals, flowers and stars. She put her pictures on the wall of her room with tape. She was proud of her art.

One day, she found a new crayon in the drawer. It was shiny and silver. She wanted to try it on her paper. She took it to her desk and started to draw. But the crayon did not make a mark. It was hard and cold. She rubbed it harder on the paper, but nothing happened.

She wondered what would happen if she heated the crayon. She saw a candle on the table. It had a flame that was hot and bright. She thought maybe the crayon would melt and make a mark if she put it near the flame. She was curious and did not think of the danger.

She held the crayon over the candle. She saw it start to melt and drip. She was excited and moved it closer to the paper. But then, something bad happened. The paper caught fire. It burned quickly and made a lot of smoke. Lily was scared and dropped the crayon and the paper. She ran to the door and screamed for help.

The smoke set off the alarm. It made a loud noise that hurt her ears. Her mom and dad heard the alarm and ran to her room. They saw the fire and grabbed a blanket. They threw the blanket over the fire and put it out. They hugged Lily and asked her what happened. Lily told them the truth. She was sorry and cried. Her mom and dad were angry and worried, but they were also glad that she was safe. They told her never to play with fire or candles again. They took her to the living room and gave her a glass of water. They looked at her pictures on the wall. They said they were creative and beautiful, but they also said she needed to be careful and smart. Lily nodded and said she learned her lesson. She said she loved them and thanked them for saving her. They said they loved her too and kissed her. They were happy that the fire did not spread and that no one was hurt. They decided to buy her some new crayons and paper, but not the shiny and silver ones.

A boy and his mom went to the park. The boy liked to play on the swings and the slide. He saw a big dog with a ball in his mouth. The boy wanted to play with the dog and the ball. He ran to the dog and tried to take the ball.

"Stop, boy, stop!" his mom shouted. "The dog is not yours. He may bite you!"

But the boy did not listen. He grabbed the ball from the dog's mouth. The dog did not like that. He growled and barked. He jumped on the boy and bit his arm. The boy dropped the ball and cried.

"Help, help!" his mom screamed. She ran to the boy and the dog. She tried to pull the dog away. But the dog was too strong. He bit the mom's leg. She fell to the ground and cried.

A man came to help. He was the dog's owner. He was wise. He knew how to calm the dog. He called the dog's name and gave him a treat. The dog let go of the mom and the boy. He wagged his tail and ate the treat.

"I'm so sorry," the man said. "My dog is not bad. He just loves his ball. He thought you wanted to take it away from him."

The mom and the boy were hurt. They had blood on their clothes. They needed a doctor. The man said he would pay for the doctor. He said he was sorry again.

But the mom and the boy were not happy. They were scared and sad. They did not want to play with the dog or the ball. They did not want to go to the park. They wanted to go home. They cried.

Once in a season, the sun began to glow. It glowed brighter and brighter until it lit up the sky.

"Oh wow!" said a little boy as he saw the sun. "It's so bright!"

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, it's a very normal thing. The sun glows every day."

The boy grinned and said, "But it's really really really special today!"

His mom laughed and said, "Yes, it's special today, because the sun glows in all kinds of different colors. Look closely, and you'll see the colors!"

The boy gasped and said, "Really? I can see colors in the sun?" He watched closely, and sure enough, he could see colors like yellow, orange, and red in the sun's glow.

"That's so cool!" the boy said.

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, it sure is. The sun glows in all kinds of colors every single season."

The boy smiled and said, "I love it when the sun glows!"

Once upon a time there was a hairy mule. He lived in a field and ate lots of yummy grass. One day something very exciting happened. The mule went to the beach with his friend the horse. They splashed in the water and had lots of fun! The mule ran and ran until he was very tired. Then he stopped to rest and looked out over the ocean. It was a beautiful day and the mule smiled happily. After that, he and the horse went home. They had a great time and were happy to be back in their green field. The End.

Once upon a time there was a nice fairy. She was very small and hid in the garden.

One day when the sun was shining, a little boy named Timmy went to the garden. He saw something sparkling in the grass. Timmy was curious and bent down to take a closer look. 

He said, "Wow! Is that a fairy?"

The fairy blinked and nodded. She said, "Yes, it is me! My name is Rose."

Timmy smiled. He asked Rose, "Do you want to play with me?"

Rose giggled. She said, "Yes, let's have some fun!"

So Timmy and Rose played together in the garden all afternoon. When it was time to go home, Timmy said goodbye and thanked Rose for such a fun day.

The little fairy waved goodbye and said, "You're welcome! I hope to see you again soon!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play with her toys and eat candy. One day, Lily went to the store with her mommy. They walked around and looked at all the things in the store. 

Suddenly, Lily saw a boy who was being very naughty. He was throwing things and making a mess. Lily's mommy told her to stay away from the naughty boy. 

When they were done shopping, Lily and her mommy went to the exit. They saw a man who was wearing a big bow tie. Lily thought it looked funny and she laughed. Then, they went home and had some ice cream. The end.

Sparky was lost and alone. He had been walking for hours with no sign of shelter. He sighed and shrugged his shoulders.

As Sparky was walking he heard voices coming from behind a bush. He peered through the leaves and saw a group of children. He was nervous and wanted to run away, but he stayed and watched them play.

The children noticed Sparky and asked him to join them. They were very friendly and welcoming. Sparky wanted to stay and play but he was still scared and hesitant.

The children asked Sparky why he was so scared and alone. He looked down and shrugged his shoulders. He was too scared to speak.

The children were understanding and told Sparky he could stay with them. They showed him to their small shelter and told him he can stay as long as he needs. Sparky was so thankful for their kindness, even when he had been so ignorant and scared.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She wanted to find something special, so she looked everywhere. She looked in her garden, but nothing was there. Then she looked in the park. Suddenly she saw something shining on the ground! She bent down and picked it up. It was a golden star! Sarah was so happy.

She wanted to find out what the reward was, so she asked her Mom. Mom said that the reward was a tasty treat! Sarah was so excited. She went to the kitchen and Mom gave her a yummy ice cream. It was so tasty!

Sarah was so happy that she found a special reward. She was sure that she wouldn't forget this day, and she was now ever so lucky to have such a tasty treat.

Once upon a time, there was a great knot. This knot was so big and strong that it could not be broken. One day, a small girl had a dream about the knot. In her dream, it was talking to her and teaching her amazing things. She dreamt about flying into the sky and going on an exciting adventure.

The little girl woke up with a smile on her face. She couldn't believe that great knot had talked to her in her dream. She wanted to keep the knot with her always to remember her dream. So, she put her big knot in her pocket. Everywhere she went, she kept the knot close by.

The little girl would always remember her dream and the great knot that was a part of it. She kept the knot with her until she was a grown up. She would look at it and remember the amazing dream she had when she was a little girl.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to draw pictures with her crayons. One day, she went to her mom and said, "Mom, I want more crayons. Can we go to the store and get some?"

Her mom said, "Sure, Lily. Let's go to the store and get some new crayons for you."

When they got to the store, Lily found a big box of crayons with lots of colors. She was so happy and said, "Mom, I want this box of crayons. Can we get it?"

Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. You were successful in finding the crayons you wanted. Let's go home and draw some pictures." And they went home and drew lots of pictures with Lily's new crayons.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He was the youngest sibling and often got jealous when his sister and brother were given special opportunities.

One day, Jack's mom said that if he wanted to join in on the fun they were having, he had to help clean up the park. Jack agreed that it would be fun and put on his cleaning gloves.

Jack started to clean but it was taking too long. He watched as his siblings finished quickly and started to play. Jack became jealous. He wanted to join in but he still had so much to do.

Then suddenly, Jack's mom told them about a shortcut. She said that if he cut the grass at the park, he could clean faster. Jack couldn't believe his ears! He quickly grabbed the scissors and started to cut the grass super fast.

Before he knew it, Jack had finished cleaning the park. He ran to where his siblings were playing and finally got to have some fun. He was so happy that he found the shortcut.

Once upon a time, there was a clever girl. Her name was Paige. She liked to spin and she was very good at it.

One day, Paige went to a special place to spin. She spun faster and faster. A bright, fun light shone all around her and amazing music filled the air! 

When she stopped spinning, Paige was filled with special power. She felt so strong and special.

Paige knew that the spinning had given her this special power. She thanked the special place for showing her and decided to go back soon to spin again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the green grass. He had a big blue ball that he liked to throw and catch. One day, Timmy played with his ball all day long until the sun started to set. He knew it was time to go inside and finish his dinner.

Timmy's mom called him inside and he quickly ran to the table. He saw that his plate had green broccoli on it. He didn't like broccoli, but he knew he had to eat it all to finish his dinner. After he finished his broccoli, his mom gave him a piece of blueberry pie for dessert. Timmy loved blueberry pie and he ate it all up until there was nothing left. Then, he went to bed feeling happy and full.

Jill and Tom were going to a show. They were very happy. They put on their clean clothes and shoes. Mom and Dad drove them to the big hall. There were many people and seats.

"Can we sit in the front?" Jill asked.

"Sorry, honey, those seats are for the VIPs," Dad said.

"What are VIPs?" Tom wondered.

"They are very important people who pay a lot of money to see the show," Mom explained.

Jill and Tom were not very important people, but they did not mind. They found some nice seats in the middle. They waited for the show to start.

Soon, the lights went down and the curtain went up. The show was about a princess and a dragon. The princess was very brave and smart. She tricked the dragon and saved the kingdom. The dragon was very funny and silly. He made everyone laugh.

Jill and Tom liked the show very much. They clapped their hands and cheered. They applauded the princess and the dragon. They also applauded the other actors and the music.

At the end of the show, the princess and the dragon came to the front of the stage. They bowed and smiled. They saw Jill and Tom in the crowd. They waved at them.

"Hey, you two, come here!" the princess called.

Jill and Tom were surprised. They looked at Mom and Dad. Mom and Dad nodded. They got up and walked to the stage.

The princess and the dragon hugged them and gave them flowers. They said they were the best audience ever. They said they wanted to make them VIPs for the day. They invited them to go backstage and see the costumes and props.

Jill and Tom were very happy. They thanked the princess and the dragon. They followed them to the open door behind the curtain. They saw many things and people. They had a lot of fun.

Mom and Dad were very proud. They took pictures and videos. They said it was a very special day. They said they were very lucky to have such wonderful kids.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to play. Everywhere she went she would find something new and exciting to play with.

One day the little girl was playing in the garden when she found a strange passport. The passport looked weird and she wondered where it had come from. The passport belonged to a magical mermaid who had been visiting the garden.

The little girl wanted to show the passport to her family, so she put it in her pocket and went inside. But when she went to show her family the passport, there was no sign of it anywhere.

The little girl looked everywhere but there was no sign of the passport. She asked her family if they had seen the passport, but they hadn't seen it. Suddenly, the little girl heard a voice coming from the garden. It was the magical mermaid, who thanked the little girl for finding her passport. 

The little girl was so happy to have found the passport and the magical mermaid was grateful to get it back. They played in the garden together until it was time for the mermaid to return home. 

From that day forward the little girl was never without her passport, always ready to explore new and exciting places.

One day, a little boy named Tim saw a hole in the ceiling. He wanted to repair it. He told his mom, "Mom, there is a hole in the ceiling. Can we fix it?"

His mom said, "Yes, Tim. We will fix it tomorrow. But for now, be alert and don't go near the hole."

The next day, Tim's dad came with a ladder. He climbed up and fixed the hole in the ceiling. Tim was very happy. He said, "Thank you, Dad! Now the ceiling is all better!"

Later that day, Tim and his mom heard a noise. They were alert and looked around. They saw a bird that had flown into the house. The bird had come through the hole in the ceiling before it was fixed.

Tim's mom said, "Good thing we fixed the hole, or more birds might come in!" Tim was happy that he helped repair the ceiling and keep the birds outside.

Once upon a time there was a little duck who was feeling very sad. She had no friends and was always alone.

One day, she heard a voice calling out her name. It was a kind voice that said, "Hello little duck. Welcome!"

The little duck was so surprised, she didn't know where the voice was coming from. Then she looked up to the sky and saw the most beautiful bird she had ever seen.

The bird was bright and colorful and its wings were spread open. The bird smiled at her and spoke, "Welcome, little duck. I'm glad you're here."

The little duck was now so happy. She said, "Thank you! I'm so glad to be here."

The bird said, "Let's go swimming. This lake is so wet and it's a perfect day for a dip."

The little duck was so excited and they both flew into the lake and had a great time.

The little duck's life had changed forever because of that kind bird and she will always be thankful for the welcome she was given.

On Wednesday, Sam and Lily went to the park with Mom. They saw a big slide and a swing and a sandbox. Sam wanted to try the slide, but Lily was nervous. She did not like to go fast or high.

"Come on, Lily, it is fun!" Sam urged. He climbed up the ladder and slid down with a whoop. He smiled and waved at Lily.

Lily shook her head. She hugged Mom's leg and said, "No, thank you. I like the swing better."

Mom smiled and said, "That is okay, Lily. You can do what you like. Maybe another day you will try the slide."

She took Lily to the swing and pushed her gently. Lily felt happy and relaxed. She liked to swing back and forth and feel the breeze.

Sam came over and said, "Can I swing too, Mom?"

Mom nodded and said, "Sure, Sam. There is another swing next to Lily. You can take turns."

Sam and Lily swung together and laughed. They had fun at the park on Wednesday.

Once upon a time, there was a little boat named Daisy. Daisy loved to sail in the big blue sea. One day, Daisy noticed a big anchor in the water. She wanted to play with it, but she knew it was too heavy. 

Daisy asked her friend, a seagull named Lucky, to help her. Lucky flew down and picked up the anchor with his strong wings. Daisy was so happy and grateful to have a friend like Lucky. 

As they continued to sail, Daisy and Lucky saw many other boats struggling with their anchors. They decided to help them too. Daisy and Lucky learned that helping others is important and makes them feel good inside. They felt lucky to have each other and to be able to help others.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved the sea. She loved to swim and explore its depths. Every day she would visit the shore looking for new discoveries. One day, she spotted something strange in the water. It was a jellyfish! She had never seen a jellyfish before and was very excited. She wanted to get closer to see it better but she knew she had to be careful. She slowly moved closer but the jellyfish began to drift away. Suddenly she noticed it was crying. She was so sad to see the jellyfish weep. She wished she could help it but she did not know how. She gently touched the jellyfish and whispered that she was sorry. The jellyfish stopped crying and slowly smiled at her. It was then, that she knew she had made a new friend. They spent the day playing together and the jellyfish taught her all about the sea. It was a wonderful day.

Once upon a time there was an ostrich named Sam. He was fit and active and he loved to run. He ran every day around the farm, and the other animals would cheer him on.

One day, Sam was running faster and harder than ever before. He went faster than he meant to and tripped over a rock. He hurt his foot and couldn't run anymore. Sam cried and said, "My foot hurts, who will fix it for me?"

Just then, an elephant came walking by. He said to Sam, "I know how to fix your foot. I can make it strong again. Would you like me to try?" Sam nodded his head yes and the elephant said, "Let me get to work!"

The elephant got some herbs from the farmer and put them on Sam's foot. He rubbed them in and said, "Now your foot should feel fit in no time!" And sure enough, it did! Sam thanked the elephant and said, "Now I can run again!" The elephant smiled and said, "You're welcome!"

Sam was quite happy, and ran around the farm as fast as ever. He always remembered to thank the elephant for fixing him, and he still runs around the farm everyday with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Grace. Grace was very sad because she couldn't find the truth. Everywhere she looked she couldn't seem to find it, so she asked her mom what she should do.

Her mom said to her, "truth can be hard to find, but if you take your time and do your best, you'll find it". Grace thought about it and decided to try.

So she took a deep breath and started looking. She looked inside and outside, in the trees and the sky, but she still couldn't find it. She felt sad and wanted to give up.

But then, suddenly, she heard a whisper in her ear. She listened carefully and it said, "look inside your heart and you'll find the truth". Grace was surprised but decided to try it.

So she took another deep breath and closed her eyes. She focused on her heart and after some time she felt something. It was warm and peaceful, like a hug. She opened her eyes and realized that she had found the truth! She felt amazing and happy.

Grace was so glad she had decided to do her best and look inside her heart because that's where she found the truth.

Once upon a time, there was a messy robot. People imagined how wonderful it would be to have a robot living with them. So, the people built the robot.

When the robot was finished, it looked so messy! Its wires, lines and parts were all jumbled up. Nobody knew what to do, so the robot just stayed messy.

One day, a little girl named Louise saw the robot. She wanted to help the robot be tidy. So, she spent time cleaning it, sorting the lines and putting its parts in the right places.

When Louise was finished, the robot was so neat! Everyone was so proud of Louise and they all celebrated with big smiles on their faces.

The robot will always remember the messy and neat moments with Louise and her friends.

Once upon a time there was a boy. His name was Sam. He had a store. He was very ready to open it.

One day, he was at the store when he heard a noise. He was scared and started to tremble. He said to himself, "What is this noise?"

Then, a little girl appeared. She said, "Hi Sam, I am Lucy." Sam was surprised but smiled. 

He asked, "Where did that noise come from?" Lucy said, "I made it. I wanted to surprise you."
Sam stopped trembling and said, "Thank you, it was a nice surprise". 

Lucy smiled and they both had fun at the store. They were very ready to explore the store together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, she saw a beautiful doll in the store. She asked her mommy if she could have it, but her mommy said it had a high price.

Lily really wanted the doll, so she decided to save her money. She helped her mommy with the chores and got some money in return. After a few weeks, she had enough money to buy the doll. She was so happy that she could finally spend her money on something she really wanted.

Lily went back to the store and bought the doll. She hugged it tightly and thanked her mommy for teaching her the value of money. From that day on, Lily learned that if she saved her money, she could buy things she really wanted, even if they had a high price.

Once upon a time, there was a man called Bob. Bob lived in a big city. He was very worried because he had broken a law. He thought he was in big trouble! So he went to the court to see the judge.

Bob was very scared. The judge asked him why he had broken the law. Bob told the truth. He said he was sorry. The judge looked at Bob carefully. He said he will receive an important decision. 

Bob went home. He was very worried. He didn't know what to do. He waited and waited.

A few days later Bob walked to the post box. Inside he found a letter from the court. He opened the letter and it said he did not have to go to prison. Bob was so happy. He had received a good decision!

Once upon a time, there was a special little girl named Lucy.

Every day, Lucy liked to go to the playground by herself. She always felt so happy running around and playing with all her friends.

Today, Lucy was especially brave and decided to try the big slide all by herself. She nervously placed her hands on the sides and started to climb.

As she neared the top, she heard a voice from the top, â€œYou can do it Lucy! I urge you to try it!â€

Lucy looked up and saw her mommy at the top of the slide. She smiled and shouted back, â€œYouâ€™re right mommy! I can do it!â€

At the end, Lucy cheered with excitement and ran to her mom, â€œMommy, that was the best ride ever!â€

Mom smiled, â€œIâ€™m so proud of you, Lucy. Now whoâ€™s ready for ice cream?â€
